entries.zh: 虞有勇力，騰之被害，虞逐豐，豐投水而死。
entries.en: Yu avenged his father driving Feng into the river.
entries.literal: Yu had courage and strength; when Teng was harmed Yu pursued Feng who threw himself in water and died.

entries.zh: 是日，虞及矯、紹並钜鹿太守崔曼、車騎長史羊恆、從事中郎蔡克等又為豐餘黨所害，及諸名家流移依鄴者，死亡並盡。
entries.en: The bloodbath wiped Julu officials and refugee clans at Ye.
entries.literal: That same day Yu together with Jiao and Shao and Julu governor Cui Man chariot-and-cavalry chief clerk Yang Heng consultant Cai Ke were again harmed by Feng's remaining faction and renowned families taking refuge at Ye perished altogether.

entries.zh: 初，鄴中雖府庫虛竭，而騰資用甚饒。
entries.en: Ye's arsenals stood empty yet Teng hoarded wealth.
entries.literal: At first though Ye granaries were exhausted Teng's private wealth was very ample.

entries.zh: 性儉嗇，無所振惠，臨急，乃賜將士米可數升，帛各丈尺，是以人不為用，遂致於禍。
entries.en: His miserly handfuls of grain and cloth bought no loyalty and brought disaster.
entries.literal: By nature stingy he showed no generosity; facing crisis he then gifted officers several sheng of rice and bolts only one zhang therefore men would not serve him and ruin followed.

entries.zh: 及苟晞救鄴，桑還平陽。
entries.en: Gou Xi's relief sent Ji Sang back toward Pingyang.
entries.literal: When Gou Xi relieved Ye Sang returned to Pingyang.

entries.zh: 于時盛夏，屍爛壞不可復識，騰及三子骸骨不獲。
entries.en: It was midsummer, and the corpses had decayed beyond recognition; the remains of Teng and his three sons could not be recovered.
entries.literal: It was then deep summer; corpses rotted beyond recognition and Teng's and his three sons' bones could not be recovered.

entries.zh: 庶子確立。
entries.en: His son by a secondary consort, Sima Que, succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son by a secondary consort, Que, succeeded him.

entries.zh: 南陽王模，字元表，少好學，與元帝及范陽王虓俱有稱於宗室。
entries.en: Mo, styled Yuanbiao, studied hard alongside Sima Rui and Sima Xiao.
entries.literal: Prince of Nanyang Mo courtesy Yuanbiao in youth loved learning and together with Yuan Di and Prince Xiao of Fanyang was praised within the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 初封平昌公。
entries.en: He began as Pingchang duke.
entries.literal: At first enfeoffed Duke of Pingchang.

entries.zh: 惠帝末，拜冗從僕射，累遷太子庶子、員外散騎常侍。
entries.en: Late Hui's reign brought chariot master through heir staff to supernumerary cavalry attendant.
entries.literal: Late Emperor Hui he was appointed supernumerary chariot master and progressively promoted heir-apparent household aide and supernumerary irregular cavalry attendant.

entries.zh: 成都王穎奔長安，東海王越以模為北中郎將，鎮鄴。
entries.en: Ying's flight west left Mo northern gentleman at Ye under Yue.
entries.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Ying fled to Chang'an Prince of Donghai Yue appointed Mo Northern Gentlemen General guarding Ye.

entries.zh: 永興初，成都王穎故帳下督公師籓、樓權、郝昌等攻鄴，模左右謀應之。
entries.en: Yongxing opened with Gongshi Fan's siege and traitors inside Ye.
entries.literal: Early Yongxing Chengdu Prince Ying's former overseer Gongshi Fan Lou Quan Hao Chang and others attacked Ye; Mo's attendants plotted to respond within.

entries.zh: 廣平太守丁邵率眾救模，范陽王虓又遣兗州刺史苟晞援之，籓等散走。
entries.en: Ding Shao and Gou Xi lifted the siege and routed Fan.
entries.literal: Guangping governor Ding Shao led hosts relieving Mo; Prince Xiao of Fanyang again dispatched Yan Inspector Gou Xi aiding them; Fan and others scattered and fled.

entries.zh: 遷鎮東大將軍，鎮許昌。
entries.en: He became guarding-east marshal at Xuchang.
entries.literal: Mo was promoted Guarding East Grand Marshal stationed Xuchang.

entries.zh: 進爵南陽王。
entries.en: Promoted to Prince of Nanyang.
entries.literal: He advanced noble rank Prince of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 永嘉初，轉征西大將軍、開府、都督秦雍梁益諸軍事，代河間王顒鎮關中。
entries.en: Yongjia gave him four-province western command replacing Sima Yong.
entries.literal: Early Yongjia he transferred western expedition grand marshal independent headquarters supervising Qin Yong Liang Yi military affairs replacing Prince of Hejian Yong guarding Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 模感丁邵之德，敕國人為邵生立碑。
entries.en: He memorialized Ding Shao with a standing stone.
entries.literal: Mo grateful for Ding Shao's virtue ordered his people erect a living monument to Shao.

entries.zh: 時關中饑荒，百姓相噉，加以疾癘，盜賊公行。
entries.en: Famine cannibalism plague and brigandage ravaged Guanzhong.
entries.literal: At that time Guanzhong starved; commoners devoured one another; pestilence added; bandits operated openly.

entries.zh: 模力不能制，乃鑄銅人鐘鼎為釜器以易穀，議者非之。
entries.en: He melted ritual bronzes for grain swaps—widely condemned.
entries.literal: Mo's strength could not control it so he cast bronze men bells and tripods into cauldrons to trade for grain; critics condemned this.

entries.zh: 東海王越表徵模為司空，遣中書監傅祗代之。
entries.en: Yue summoned Mo to minister of works under Fu Zhi.
entries.literal: Prince of Donghai Yue memorialized summoning Mo as Minister of Works sending Palace Library Director Fu Zhi to replace him.

entries.zh: 模謀臣淳於定說模曰：「關中天府之國，霸王之地。
entries.en: Mo's strategist Chunyu Ding advised Mo saying 'Guanzhong is heaven's storehouse—the ground of hegemons.
entries.literal: Mo's strategist Chunyu Ding advised Mo saying 'Guanzhong is heaven's storehouse—the ground of hegemons.

entries.zh: 今以不能綏撫而還，既於聲望有虧，又公兄弟唱起大事，而並在朝廷，若自強則有專權之罪，弱則受制於人，非公之利也。」
entries.en: Now unable to soothe and returning damages your renown; moreover your lordship's brothers launched great affairs yet both remain at court—if you strengthen yourself you incur monopolizing guilt; if weak you fall under others' control—not to your advantage.'
entries.literal: Now unable to soothe and returning damages your renown; moreover your lordship's brothers launched great affairs yet both remain at court—if you strengthen yourself you incur monopolizing guilt; if weak you fall under others' control—not to your advantage.'

entries.zh: 模納其言，不就徵。
entries.en: Mo stayed put ignoring the recall.
entries.literal: Mo accepted his words and did not obey the summons.

entries.zh: 表遣世子保為西中郎將、東羌校尉，鎮上邽，秦州刺史裴苞距之。
entries.en: He sent heir Bao to Shanggui against Pei Bao's block.
entries.literal: He memorialized dispatching heir-apparent Bao as Western Gentlemen General Eastern Qiang colonel guarding Shanggui; Qin Inspector Pei Bao resisted.

entries.zh: 模使帳下都尉陳安率眾攻苞，苞奔安定。
entries.en: Chen An drove Pei Bao to Anding.
entries.literal: Mo ordered household Commandant Chen An leading hosts attacking Bao; Bao fled Anding.

entries.zh: 太守賈疋以郡迎苞，模遣軍司謝班伐疋，疋退盧水。
entries.en: Jia Ya's welcome drew Xie Ban until Ya fled to Lushui.
entries.literal: Governor Jia Ya of the commandery welcomed Bao with the district; Mo dispatched army director Xie Ban attacking Ya; Ya withdrew to Lushui.

entries.zh: 其年，進位太尉、大都督。
entries.en: Same year brought grand commandant and supreme command.
entries.literal: That year he advanced Grand Commandant grand commander.

entries.zh: 河間王顒表立成都王穎為太弟，為王浚所破，挾天子還洛陽。
entries.en: Yong's heir plot collapsed under Wang Jun forcing return east.
entries.literal: Prince of Hejian Yong memorialized establishing Chengdu Prince Ying heir-apparent; defeated by Wang Jun he escorted Son of Heaven back Luoyang.

entries.zh: 虓與東平王楙、鎮東將軍周馥等上言曰：自湣懷被害，皇儲不建，委重前相，輒失臣節。
entries.en: Xiao, together with King Mao of Dongping, General Who Guards the East Zhou Fu, and others, submitted words, saying: Since Minhuai was harmed, the imperial heir has not been established. Weighty responsibility was entrusted to the former minister, and he then lost the duty of a subject.
entries.literal: Xiao, together with King Mao of Dongping, General Who Guards the East Zhou Fu, and others, submitted words, saying: Since Minhuai was harmed, the imperial heir has not been established. Weighty responsibility was entrusted to the former minister, and he then lost the duty of a subject.

entries.zh: 是以前年太宰與臣，永惟社稷之貳，不可久空，所以共啟成都王穎，以為國副。
entries.en: Therefore in the previous year the Grand Steward and we your servants long considered that the deputy of the altars of soil and grain could not remain vacant for long, and for this reason we jointly proposed King Ying of Chengdu to be deputy to the state.
entries.literal: Therefore in the previous year the Grand Steward and we your servants long considered that the deputy of the altars of soil and grain could not remain vacant for long, and for this reason we jointly proposed King Ying of Chengdu to be deputy to the state.

entries.zh: 受重之後，而弗克負荷。
entries.en: After receiving this weighty charge, he was unable to bear it.
entries.literal: After receiving this weighty charge, he was unable to bear it.

entries.zh: 「小人勿用」，而以為腹心。
entries.en: "Do not employ petty men," yet he made them his trusted intimates.
entries.literal: "Do not employ petty men," yet he made them his trusted intimates.

entries.zh: 骨肉宜敦，而猜佻薦至，險詖宜遠，而讒說殄行。
entries.en: Flesh-and-blood kin should have been treated with thick affection, yet suspicion and frivolity arrived repeatedly; dangerous and slanting men should have been kept distant, yet slanderous talk destroyed conduct.
entries.literal: Flesh-and-blood kin should have been treated with thick affection, yet suspicion and frivolity arrived repeatedly; dangerous and slanting men should have been kept distant, yet slanderous talk destroyed conduct.

entries.zh: 此皆臣等不聰不明，失所宗賴。
entries.en: All this was because we your servants were neither perceptive nor clear-sighted and lost the one on whom we relied.
entries.literal: All this was because we your servants were neither perceptive nor clear-sighted and lost the one on whom we relied.

entries.zh: 遂令陛下謬于降授，雖戮臣等，不足以謝天下。
entries.en: We then caused Your Majesty to err in lowering and granting rank; even if you executed us, it would not be enough to apologize to all under Heaven.
entries.literal: We then caused Your Majesty to err in lowering and granting rank; even if you executed us, it would not be enough to apologize to all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 今大駕還宮，文武空曠，制度荒破，靡有孑遺，臣等雖劣，足匡王室。
entries.en: Now the great carriage has returned to the palace, civil and military offices are empty, institutions are ruined and broken, and nothing remains. Although we your servants are inferior, we are enough to help correct the royal house.
entries.literal: Now the great carriage has returned to the palace, civil and military offices are empty, institutions are ruined and broken, and nothing remains. Although we your servants are inferior, we are enough to help correct the royal house.

entries.zh: 而道路之言，謂張方與臣等不同。
entries.en: But talk on the roads says that Zhang Fang is not of one mind with us.
entries.literal: But talk on the roads says that Zhang Fang is not of one mind with us.

entries.zh: 既惜所在興異，又乙太宰惇德允元，著於具瞻，每當義節，輒為社稷宗盟之先。
entries.en: We both regret that differences are arising where he is, and also because the Grand Steward is sincere in virtue and truly principal, visible to all who look up to him; whenever righteousness and integrity are at stake, he always stands first among the great allies of the altars of soil and grain.
entries.literal: We both regret that differences are arising where he is, and also because the Grand Steward is sincere in virtue and truly principal, visible to all who look up to him; whenever righteousness and integrity are at stake, he always stands first among the great allies of the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 張方受其指教，為國效節。
entries.en: Zhang Fang received his direction and instruction and showed integrity for the state.
entries.literal: Zhang Fang received his direction and instruction and showed integrity for the state.

entries.zh: 昔年之舉，有死無貳。
entries.en: In last year's action, he had death before him and no second loyalty.
entries.literal: In last year's action, he had death before him and no second loyalty.

entries.zh: 此即太宰之良將，陛下之忠臣。
entries.en: He is therefore a good general of the Grand Steward and a loyal subject of Your Majesty.
entries.literal: He is therefore a good general of the Grand Steward and a loyal subject of Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 但以受性強毅，不達變通，遂守前志，已致紛紜。
entries.en: It is only because his nature is forceful and resolute and he does not understand adaptation that he kept to his former intention and has already caused confusion.
entries.literal: It is only because his nature is forceful and resolute and he does not understand adaptation that he kept to his former intention and has already caused confusion.

entries.zh: 然退思惟，既是其不易之節，且慮事翻之後，為天下所罪，故不即西還耳。
entries.en: Yet when we withdraw and think on it, this is already his unchanging integrity, and he also worries that after affairs reverse, he will be blamed by all under Heaven; therefore he has not immediately returned west.
entries.literal: Yet when we withdraw and think on it, this is already his unchanging integrity, and he also worries that after affairs reverse, he will be blamed by all under Heaven; therefore he has not immediately returned west.

entries.zh: 原其本事，實無深責。
entries.en: When the root of the matter is traced, there is in fact no deep blame.
entries.literal: When the root of the matter is traced, there is in fact no deep blame.

entries.zh: 臣聞先代明主，未嘗不全護功臣，令福流子孫。
entries.en: We your servants have heard that enlightened rulers of earlier generations always preserved and protected meritorious ministers and made blessings flow to their descendants.
entries.literal: We your servants have heard that enlightened rulers of earlier generations always preserved and protected meritorious ministers and made blessings flow to their descendants.

entries.zh: 自中間以來，陛下功臣初無全者，非獨人才皆劣，其於取禍，實由朝廷策之失宜，不相容恕。
entries.en: Since the recent troubled period, none of Your Majesty's meritorious ministers has been preserved. This is not only because the men were all inferior; their incurring disaster has truly come from the court's policies losing what was fitting and from failure to tolerate and forgive one another.
entries.literal: Since the recent troubled period, none of Your Majesty's meritorious ministers has been preserved. This is not only because the men were all inferior; their incurring disaster has truly come from the court's policies losing what was fitting and from failure to tolerate and forgive one another.

entries.zh: 以一旦之咎，喪其積年之勳，既違《周禮》議功之典，且使天下之人莫敢復為陛下致節者。
entries.en: To lose accumulated years of merit because of one day's fault both violates the Zhouli canon of deliberating on merit and makes the people of the realm no longer dare to give their utmost loyalty for Your Majesty.
entries.literal: To lose accumulated years of merit because of one day's fault both violates the Zhouli canon of deliberating on merit and makes the people of the realm no longer dare to give their utmost loyalty for Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 臣等此言，豈獨為一張方，實為社稷遠計，欲令功臣長守富貴。
entries.en: These words of ours are not only for one Zhang Fang; they are truly a long-range plan for the altars of soil and grain, wishing to let meritorious ministers long keep wealth and honor.
entries.literal: These words of ours are not only for one Zhang Fang; they are truly a long-range plan for the altars of soil and grain, wishing to let meritorious ministers long keep wealth and honor.

entries.zh: 臣愚以為宜委太宰以關右之任，一方事重，及自州郡已下，選舉授任，一皆仰成。
entries.en: In our foolish view, it is fitting to entrust the Grand Steward with responsibility west of the passes. Affairs in that region are weighty, and from provinces and commanderies downward, selection, recommendation, appointment, and assignment should all look up to him for completion.
entries.literal: In our foolish view, it is fitting to entrust the Grand Steward with responsibility west of the passes. Affairs in that region are weighty, and from provinces and commanderies downward, selection, recommendation, appointment, and assignment should all look up to him for completion.

entries.zh: 若朝之大事，廢興損益，每輒疇諮。
entries.en: As for great affairs of the court, abolitions, establishments, reductions, and additions, each should be consulted with him.
entries.literal: As for great affairs of the court, abolitions, establishments, reductions, and additions, each should be consulted with him.

entries.zh: 此則二伯述職，周召分陝之義，陛下復行於今時。
entries.en: This would be Your Majesty carrying out again in the present age the meaning of the two regional chiefs reporting on their duties and of Zhou and Shao dividing Shaan.
entries.literal: This would be Your Majesty carrying out again in the present age the meaning of the two regional chiefs reporting on their duties and of Zhou and Shao dividing Shaan.

entries.zh: 遣方還郡，令群後申志，時定王室。
entries.en: Send Fang back to his commandery, let the assembled nobles extend their intentions, and in time settle the royal house.
entries.literal: Send Fang back to his commandery, let the assembled nobles extend their intentions, and in time settle the royal house.

entries.zh: 所加方官，請悉如舊。
entries.en: As for the offices added to Fang, we request that all be as before.
entries.literal: As for the offices added to Fang, we request that all be as before.

entries.zh: 此則忠臣義士有勸，功臣必全矣。
entries.en: Then loyal ministers and righteous men will have encouragement, and meritorious ministers will surely be preserved.
entries.literal: Then loyal ministers and righteous men will have encouragement, and meritorious ministers will surely be preserved.

entries.zh: 司徒戎，異姓之賢；
entries.en: Minister over the Masses Rong is a worthy of a different surname.
entries.literal: Minister over the Masses Rong is a worthy of a different surname.

entries.zh: 司空越，公族之望，並忠國愛主，小心翼翼，宜幹機事，委以朝政。
entries.en: Minister of Works Yue is the hope of the imperial clan. Both are loyal to the state and love the ruler, careful and reverent, and should manage key affairs and be entrusted with court government.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Yue is the hope of the imperial clan. Both are loyal to the state and love the ruler, careful and reverent, and should manage key affairs and be entrusted with court government.

entries.zh: 安北將軍王浚佐命之胤，率身履道，忠亮清正，遠近所推。
entries.en: General Who Pacifies the North Wang Jun is a descendant of one who assisted the mandate; he leads himself according to the Way, is loyal, bright, clear, and correct, and is recommended by those near and far.
entries.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Wang Jun is a descendant of one who assisted the mandate; he leads himself according to the Way, is loyal, bright, clear, and correct, and is recommended by those near and far.

entries.zh: 如今日之大舉，實有定社稷之勳，此是臣等所以歎息歸高也。
entries.en: In a great undertaking like today's, he truly has merit in settling the altars of soil and grain; this is why we sigh in admiration and return high praise to him.
entries.literal: In a great undertaking like today's, he truly has merit in settling the altars of soil and grain; this is why we sigh in admiration and return high praise to him.

entries.zh: 浚宜特崇重之，以副群望，遂撫幽朔，長為北籓。
entries.en: Jun should be specially exalted and honored in order to meet the hopes of the multitude, then pacify You and the northern lands and long serve as the northern shield.
entries.literal: Jun should be specially exalted and honored in order to meet the hopes of the multitude, then pacify You and the northern lands and long serve as the northern shield.

entries.zh: 臣等竭力扞城，籓屏皇家，陛下垂拱，而四海自正。
entries.en: We your servants will exhaust our strength as defending walls and act as screens for the imperial house, while Your Majesty lets your robes hang and folds your hands, and the four seas will correct themselves.
entries.literal: We your servants will exhaust our strength as defending walls and act as screens for the imperial house, while Your Majesty lets your robes hang and folds your hands, and the four seas will correct themselves.

entries.zh: 則四祖之業，必隆於今，日月之暉，昧而復曜。
entries.en: Then the enterprise of the Four Ancestors will surely flourish today, and the radiance of sun and moon, once dimmed, will shine again.
entries.literal: Then the enterprise of the Four Ancestors will surely flourish today, and the radiance of sun and moon, once dimmed, will shine again.

entries.zh: 乞垂三思，察臣所言。
entries.en: We beg you to lower threefold thought and examine what we your servants have said.
entries.literal: We beg you to lower threefold thought and examine what we your servants have said.

entries.zh: 又可以臣表西示太宰。
entries.en: You may also show our memorial westward to the Grand Steward.
entries.literal: You may also show our memorial westward to the Grand Steward.

entries.zh: 又表曰：「成都王失道，為奸邪所誤，論王之身，不宜深責。
entries.en: Again memorializing 'Chengdu Prince lost the Way misled by wicked favorites judging the prince's person ought not be deeply blamed.
entries.literal: Again memorializing 'Chengdu Prince lost the Way misled by wicked favorites judging the prince's person ought not be deeply blamed.

entries.zh: 且先帝遺體，陛下群弟，自元康以來，罪戮相等，實海內所為匈匈，而臣等所以痛心。
entries.en: Moreover former emperor's bodily heirs Your Majesty's junior brothers since Yuankang executions match in toll truly why realm churns and why we ache.
entries.literal: Moreover former emperor's bodily heirs Your Majesty's junior brothers since Yuankang executions match in toll truly why realm churns and why we ache.

entries.zh: 今廢成都，更封一邑，宜其必許。
entries.en: Now deposing Chengdu changing enfeoffment one canton he ought surely consent.
entries.literal: Now deposing Chengdu changing enfeoffment one canton he ought surely consent.

entries.zh: 若廢黜尋有禍害，既傷陛下矜慈之恩，又令遠近恆謂公族無復骨肉之情，此實臣等內省悲慚，無顏于四海也。
entries.en: If deposition soon brings calamity it wounds Your Majesty's compassionate grace and lets far and near forever say the ducal kin lack flesh-and-blood feeling—truly our inward shame without face before the realm.
entries.literal: If deposition soon brings calamity it wounds Your Majesty's compassionate grace and lets far and near forever say the ducal kin lack flesh-and-blood feeling—truly our inward shame without face before the realm.

entries.zh: 乞陛下察臣忠款。」
entries.en: We beg Your Majesty to perceive our loyal sincerity."
entries.literal: We beg Your Majesty to perceive our loyal sincerity."

entries.zh: 於是虓先率眾自許屯于滎陽。
entries.en: Xiao marched to Xingyang first.
entries.literal: Thereupon Xiao first led hosts from Xu camping at Xingyang.

entries.zh: 濟南惠王遂，字子伯，宣帝弟魏鴻臚丞恂之子也。
entries.en: Sima Sui, styled Zibo, was Sima Xun's son—Sima Yi's nephew.
entries.literal: Prince Hui of Jinan Sui courtesy Zibo was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Grand Herald Assistant Xun.

entries.zh: 仕魏關內侯，進封平昌亭侯，曆典軍郎將，
entries.en: Under Wei he rose from secondary marquis to Pingchang ting through army posts.
entries.literal: Serving Wei district marquis within passes advanced Marquis of Pingchang precinct successively holding army corps captain.

entries.zh: 景元二年，轉封武城鄉侯、督鄴城守諸軍事、北中郎將。
entries.en: In the second year of Jingyuan, Shifted to Wucheng township marquis guarding Ye as northern gentleman.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jingyuan, Transferred enfeoffment Wucheng village marquis supervising Ye garrison Northern Gentlemen General.

entries.zh: 五等建，封祝阿伯，累遷冠軍將軍。
entries.en: Five-rank reform made him Zhu'e baron then champion general.
entries.literal: When five ranks were established enfeoffed Baron of Zhu'e progressively Champion General.

entries.zh: 武帝受禪，封濟南王。
entries.en: Sima Yan created Jinan prince.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Jinan.

entries.zh: 泰始二年薨。
entries.en: He died in the second year of Taishi.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taishi, he died.

entries.zh: 二子：耽、緝。
entries.en: Sons Dan and Ji.
entries.literal: Two sons: Dan and Ji.

entries.zh: 耽嗣立，咸寧三年徙為中山王。
entries.en: Dan succeeded to the title, and in Xianning year three he was transferred to be Prince of Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Dan succeeded to the title, and in Xianning year three he was transferred to be Prince of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 是年薨，無子，緝繼。
entries.en: Dan died childless same year; Ji followed.

entries.zh: 舒有威重德望，祿賜散之九族，家無餘財。
entries.en: Shu combined moral authority with high prestige; stipends and gifts he shared across his entire kindred, leaving nothing hoarded at home.
entries.literal: Shu had awesome weight and virtuous repute; stipends and gifts he scattered among the nine kinships; the household had no surplus wealth.

entries.zh: 陳留周震累為諸府所辟，辟書既下，公輒喪亡，僉號震為殺公掾，莫有辟者。
entries.en: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu had been summoned again and again, yet each time the appointment was issued his patron died; people called him the adjutant who killed his superiors, and no one would hire him.
entries.literal: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu repeatedly was summoned by various bureaus; once the summons letter had descended, the grandee always died; all called Zhen the adjutant who kills lords, and there was none who summoned him.

entries.zh: 舒乃命之，而竟無患，識者以此稱其達命。
entries.en: Shu summoned him nonetheless, and no misfortune followed; observers praised this as proof of Shu's grasp of fate.
entries.literal: Shu then ordered him, and in the end there was no calamity; those who knew praised him on this account as comprehending destiny.

entries.zh: 以年老，每稱疾遜位。
entries.en: In old age he often pleaded illness in order to resign.
entries.literal: Because of old age, he repeatedly claimed illness to yield position.

entries.zh: 中復暫起，署兗州中正，尋又稱疾。
entries.en: He briefly returned to office as middle appraiser for Yan Province, then again pleaded sickness.
entries.literal: In the middle again he briefly rose, was appointed middle appraiser of Yan Province, and presently again claimed illness.

entries.zh: 尚書左丞郤詵與舒書曰：「公久疾小差，視事是也，唯上所念。
entries.en: Xi Shen, left assistant in the Secretariat, wrote: "You have been ill a long time but are a little better; resuming duty is what the throne expects.
entries.literal: Xi Shen, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, wrote Shu a letter, saying, "You have long been ill and slightly improved; attending to affairs is right — it is what those above think of.

entries.zh: 何竟起訖還臥，曲身回法，甚失具瞻之望。
entries.en: Why rise only to go straight back to bed, bending every rule? You disappoint the court that looks to you for guidance.
entries.literal: Why altogether rise and finish and return to bed, bending the body and twisting the law — greatly losing the expectation of being looked up to.

entries.zh: 公少立巍巍，一旦棄之，可不惜哉！」
entries.en: You built a towering reputation in youth—to throw it away now would be a bitter waste!"
entries.literal: You from youth established towering height; in one morning to cast it — can it not be pitied!"

entries.zh: 舒稱疾如初。
entries.en: Shu pleaded illness as stubbornly as before.
entries.literal: Shu claimed illness as at first.

entries.zh: 後以災異遜位，帝不聽。
entries.en: Later he cited portents and offered to retire, but the emperor would not hear of it.
entries.literal: Later because of disasters and anomalies he yielded position; the emperor did not listen.

entries.zh: 後因正旦朝罷還第，表送章綬。
entries.en: Then, after New Year's court, he went home and submitted his seals and ribbons of office.
entries.literal: Later because on New Year's dawn court finished he returned to mansion and memorialized sending seals and ribbons.

entries.zh: 帝手詔敦勉。
entries.en: The emperor answered with a personal edict urging him to stay.
entries.literal: The emperor by hand edict earnestly urged him.

entries.zh: 而舒執意彌固，乃下詔曰：「司徒、劇陽子舒，體道弘粹，思量經遠，忠肅居正，在公盡規。
entries.en: Shu only dug in harder, so the throne issued an edict: "Minister of Education and Viscount of Ji, Wei Shu, embodies the Way in its pure breadth; his plans look far ahead; he is loyal, grave, and upright, and in office he has never stinted honest counsel.
entries.literal: Yet Shu held his intent more firm; then an edict was issued, saying, "Minister of Education, Viscount of Ji, Shu embodies the Way in broad purity, thought and measure reach far, loyal and reverent he holds to the straight, in public he exhausts regulation.

entries.zh: 入管銓衡，官人允敘；
entries.en: Within the ministry he balanced appointments so that every post went to a fitting man;
entries.literal: Within he managed the balance of appointments, ranking officials in suitable order;

entries.zh: 出贊袞職，敷弘五教。
entries.en: without he aided the highest councils and spread the five teachings of moral order.
entries.literal: without he assisted the ducal robe office, spread and enlarged the five teachings.

entries.zh: 惠訓播流，德聲茂著，可謂朝之俊乂者也。
entries.en: His gentle instruction has spread everywhere and his virtuous name shines bright—he is truly one of the great pillars of the court.
entries.literal: Kind instruction spreads and flows; virtuous fame flourishes bright — he may be called the court's outstanding talent.

entries.zh: 而屢執沖讓，辭旨懇誠，申覽反覆，省用憮然。
entries.en: Yet he presses his modest resignations again and again, and each memorial is so earnest that, reading them back and forth, I must grieve.
entries.literal: Yet repeatedly he presses modest yielding; his words' intent is earnest and sincere; extending and viewing back and forth, examining it I am sorrowful.

entries.zh: 蓋成人之美，先典所與，難違至情。
entries.en: Ancient canons praise those who crown another man's excellence, and I cannot lightly set aside such heartfelt devotion.
entries.literal: For crowning others' excellence is what former canons grant; it is hard to reject utmost feeling.

entries.zh: 今聽其所執，以劇陽子就第，位同三司，祿賜如前。
entries.en: I therefore grant what he asks: he may retire to his mansion as viscount of Ji with rank equal to the Three Dukes and stipends as before.
entries.literal: Now I listen to what he insists on: as Viscount of Ji he goes to mansion, rank equal to Three Dukes, stipends and gifts as before.

entries.zh: 几杖不朝，賜錢百萬，床帳簟褥自副。
entries.en: He need not attend court; he receives a million cash, with bed-curtains, fine mats, and bedding supplied.
entries.literal: With folding-stool and staff not attending court; bestowed one million cash; bed curtains, bamboo mats, bedding self-attached.

entries.zh: 以舍人四人為劇陽子舍人，置官騎十人。
entries.en: Four chamberlains shall attend him as householders of the viscount of Ji, with ten mounted escorts.
entries.literal: With four chamberlains as householders to the Viscount of Ji, establish official riders ten men.

entries.zh: 使光祿勳奉策，主者詳案典禮，令皆如舊制。」
entries.en: Let the master of ceremonies present the rescript, and let the bureaus review the statutes so every detail follows precedent."
entries.literal: Cause the Master of Ceremonies to bear the rescript; those in charge shall in detail examine canonical rites, ordering all like old regulations."

entries.zh: 於是賜安車駟馬，門施行馬。
entries.en: He was then granted a secure carriage and four-horse team, and a mounting-block was set at his gate.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was bestowed secure carriage and four-horse team; at the gate was applied riding horse block.

entries.zh: 舒為事必先行而後言，遜位之際，莫有知者。
entries.en: Shu always acted before he spoke; when he resigned, no one had seen it coming.
entries.literal: Shu in doing affairs always first acted and afterward spoke; at the juncture of yielding position, there was none who knew.

entries.zh: 時論以為晉興以來，三公能辭榮善終者，未之有也。
entries.en: Public opinion held that since the founding of Jin no holder of the three highest posts had refused honor and finished his career with such dignity.
entries.literal: Contemporary discussion held that since Jin's rise, among Three Dukes able to decline glory and end well, there had not been such.

entries.zh: 司空衛瓘與舒書曰：「每與足下共論此事，日日未果，可謂瞻之在前，忽焉在後矣。」
entries.en: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote him, "We spoke of this again and again yet never settled it—truly it was always 'right before our eyes,' then 'gone in an instant,' as the saying goes."
entries.literal: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote Shu a letter, saying, "Whenever with you I together discussed this matter, day by day not yet fruit — it may be called 'it seemed before the eyes, suddenly afterward."

entries.zh: 太熙元年薨，時年八十二。
entries.en: He died in the first year of Taixi, aged eighty-two.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taixi he died; at the time his years were eighty-two.

entries.zh: 帝甚傷悼，賵賻優厚，諡曰康。
entries.en: The emperor grieved deeply, sent lavish funeral gifts, and gave him the posthumous name Kang, "Peaceful."
entries.literal: The emperor greatly mourned; funeral gifts were generous and thick; his posthumous name was Kang.

entries.zh: 劉寔，字子真，平原高唐人也。
entries.en: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, was a native of Gaotang in Pingyuan commandery.
entries.literal: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, was a man of Gaotang in Pingyuan.

entries.zh: 漢濟北惠王壽之後也，父廣，斥丘令。
entries.en: He descended from Prince Hui of Jibei, named Shou, under the Han; his father Guang had been magistrate of Chiqiu.
entries.literal: He was a descendant of Han Prince Hui of Jibei, Shou; his father Guang was magistrate of Chiqiu.

entries.zh: 寔少貧苦，賣牛衣以自給。
entries.en: He grew up in grinding poverty and sold winter straw mats for cattle to keep himself fed.
entries.literal: Shi in youth was poor and bitter, selling cattle straw cloaks to supply himself.

entries.zh: 然好學，手約繩，口誦書，博通古今。
entries.en: Yet he loved study, knotting cord to tally his lessons while he recited texts aloud, until he mastered the classical corpus past and present.
entries.literal: Yet he loved learning, hand grasping cord, mouth chanting books, broadly penetrating ancient and modern.

entries.zh: 清身潔己，行無瑕玷。
entries.en: He kept his person and conduct spotless, without a blemish on his record.
entries.literal: He purified the body and cleansed himself; conduct had no flaw or stain.

entries.zh: 郡察孝廉，州舉秀才，皆不行。
entries.en: The commandery nominated him Filial and Incorrupt and the province as flourishing talent; he declined both.
entries.literal: The commandery investigated him Filial and Incorrupt, the province raised him Flourishing Talent; all he did not go.

entries.zh: 以計吏入洛，調為河南尹丞，遷尚書郎、廷尉正。
entries.en: He went to Luoyang as a commandery accounts clerk, was transferred to assistant intendant of Henan, then rose to gentleman of the masters of writing and director in the court of justice.
entries.literal: As accounts clerk he entered Luoyang, was transferred Assistant to the Intendant of Henan, promoted Secretariat gentleman, Director of Justice.

entries.zh: 後曆吏部郎，參文帝相國軍事，封循陽子。
entries.en: He later served as personnel ministry gentleman, joined the military staff of Prince Wen's chancellery, and was enfeoffed as viscount of Xun.
entries.literal: Later he successively was Personnel Ministry gentleman, participated in Prince Wen's chancellor of state military affairs, and was enfeoffed viscount of Xun.

entries.zh: 鐘會、鄧艾之伐蜀也，有客問寔曰：「二將其平蜀乎？」
entries.en: During Zhong Hui and Deng Ai's invasion of Shu, a visitor asked Liu Shi, "Will those two generals conquer Shu?"
entries.literal: When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai campaigned against Shu, a guest asked Shi, saying, "The two generals — will they pacify Shu?"

entries.zh: 寔曰：「破蜀必矣，而皆不還。」
entries.en: Shi replied, "They will break Shu, yet neither will come back alive."
entries.literal: Shi said, "Breaking Shu is certain, yet both will not return."

entries.zh: 客問其故，笑而不答，竟如其言。
entries.en: When pressed for his reasons he only smiled and said nothing—and events proved him right.
entries.literal: The guest asked the reason; he laughed and did not answer; in the end it was as his words.

entries.zh: 寔之先見，皆此類也。
entries.en: His foresight was often of this order.
entries.literal: Shi's foresight was all of this kind.

entries.zh: 以世多進趣，廉遜道闕，乃著《崇讓論》以矯之。
entries.en: Seeing his contemporaries scramble for advancement while modesty vanished, he wrote the "Treatise on Honoring Yielding" to set matters right.
entries.literal: Because the age had much advancing and rushing, the way of integrity and yielding was lacking, therefore he composed "Treatise on Honoring Yielding" to correct it.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: It begins:
entries.literal: Its words said:

entries.zh: 在朝之人不務相讓久矣，天下化之。
entries.en: Courtiers have long ceased to practice mutual deference, and the whole realm has taken its tone from them.
entries.literal: Men at court long have not exerted themselves in yielding to one another; the realm has been transformed thereby.

entries.zh: 自魏代以來，登進辟命之士，及在職之吏，臨見受敘，雖自辭不能，終莫肯讓有勝己者。
entries.en: Since the Wei era, every man summoned to office or promoted on appointment, even when he protests his unfitness, still refuses in the end to yield to anyone better qualified.
entries.literal: From Wei times onward, gentlemen who ascended in advancement and summons appointments, and clerks in office, facing audience and receiving order, although themselves declining inability, to the end none were willing to yield to those who surpassed themselves.

entries.zh: 夫推讓之風息，爭競之心生。
entries.en: When deference dies, the scramble for place begins.
entries.literal: When the wind of pushing yielding ceases, the mind of striving and competition arises.

entries.zh: 孔子曰，上興讓則下不爭，明讓不興下必爭也。
entries.en: Confucius said, "When superiors honor yielding, inferiors do not fight among themselves"—which shows that without yielding below, contention is inevitable.
entries.literal: Confucius said, when those above raise yielding then those below do not contend; it clarifies that when yielding does not rise, those below must contend.

entries.zh: 推讓之道興，則賢能之人日見推舉；
entries.en: When yielding prevails, able men are advanced every day;
entries.literal: When the way of pushing yielding rises, then worthy and able men day by day are seen pushed and raised;

entries.zh: 爭競之心生，則賢能之人日見謗毀。
entries.en: when contention rules, they are slandered every day.
entries.literal: when the mind of striving and competition arises, then worthy and able men day by day are seen slandered and destroyed.

entries.zh: 夫爭者之欲自先，甚惡能者之先，不能無毀也。
entries.en: A man who fights for precedence loathes anyone ahead of him who is more capable, and slander follows inevitably.
entries.literal: As for contenders' desire to put themselves first, they greatly hate able men's going first; they cannot be without destruction.

entries.zh: 故孔墨不能免世之謗己，況不及孔墨者乎！
entries.en: Even Confucius and Mozi could not escape slander—what hope have lesser men?
entries.literal: Therefore even Kong and Mo could not escape the age's slandering them, how much more those who do not reach Kong and Mo!

entries.zh: 議者僉然言，世少高名之才，朝廷不有大才之人可以為大官者。
entries.en: Critics all insist that the age lacks men of towering reputation and that the court has no great talent fit for high office.
entries.literal: Discussers all alike say, the age lacks high-named talent; the court does not have great-talent men who can become great officials.

entries.zh: 山澤人小官吏亦復雲，朝廷之士雖有大官名德，皆不及往時人也。
entries.en: Rustics and petty clerks echo the charge that today's grandees, however eminent their titles, fall short of men of earlier generations.
entries.literal: Mountain-marsh men and petty clerks also again say, court gentlemen although they have great office name and virtue, all do not reach men of former times.

entries.zh: 餘以為此二言皆失之矣。
entries.en: Both judgments miss the mark.
entries.literal: I hold that these two sayings both miss it.

entries.zh: 非時獨乏賢也，時不貴讓。
entries.en: The problem is not a sudden dearth of worthies but that the age no longer esteems yielding.
entries.literal: It is not that the age alone lacks worthies; the age does not honor yielding.

entries.zh: 一人有先眾之譽，毀必隨之，名不得成使之然也。
entries.en: Let a single man win praise above the rest, and malice dogs his steps; no good name can stand under such pressure.
entries.literal: When one man has reputation ahead of the crowd, destruction must follow him; names cannot be completed — this makes it so.

entries.zh: 雖令稷契復存，亦不復能全其名矣。
entries.en: Even if Ji and Xie walked the earth again, they could not keep their reputations intact.
entries.literal: Even if Ji and Xie again lived, they also could not again complete their names.

entries.zh: 能否混雜，優劣不分，士無素定之價，官職有缺，主選之吏不知所用，但案官次而舉之。
entries.en: Able and useless are jumbled together with no clear ranking, so gentlemen carry no settled market value; when a vacancy opens, the appointing clerk has no idea whom to choose and simply promotes the next man in line.
entries.literal: Able and unable are mixed in confusion, excellence and inferiority are not divided; gentlemen have no plain-settled price; when offices have vacancies, masters of selection clerks do not know whom to use, but only examine official order and raise them.

entries.zh: 同才之人先用者，非勢家之子，則必為有勢者之所念也。
entries.en: Among equals the first to win appointment is either a son of the mighty or a protégé of the mighty.
entries.literal: Among men of same talent, those first used are either not sons of powerful houses, then they must be those whom the powerful think of.

entries.zh: 非能獨賢，因其先用之資，而復遷之無已。
entries.en: Not because they alone deserve it, but because early preferment becomes a ladder of endless promotions.
entries.literal: It is not that they alone are worthy; because of their first-used capital, again they are transferred without end.

entries.zh: 遷之無已，不勝其任之病發矣。
entries.en: Promote such men without end and you soon see them collapse under duties they cannot bear.
entries.literal: Transferring without end, the sickness of not bearing their duties arises.

entries.zh: 觀在官之人，政績無聞，自非勢家之子，率多因資次而進也。
entries.en: Look at officials today: few have any record of real achievement; unless they are sons of great houses, they have usually climbed sheerly by seniority.
entries.literal: Observe men in office: administrative achievement is unheard of; unless they are sons of powerful houses, mostly many advance because of qualifications in order.

entries.zh: 古之聖王之化天下，所以貴讓者，欲以出賢才，息爭競也。
entries.en: The sage kings of old transformed the world by honoring deference because they wanted worthy men to come forward and strife to fall silent.
entries.literal: The ancient sage kings' transforming the realm — the reason they honored yielding was that they wished thereby to bring forth worthy talent and rest striving and competition.

entries.zh: 夫人情莫不欲已之賢也，故勸令讓賢以自明賢也，豈假讓不賢哉！
entries.en: Every man wishes to be thought worthy, so the sage kings urged men to yield place to the better qualified and thus prove their own worth—never to pretend humility while yielding to the unworthy!
entries.literal: As for human feeling, none does not wish himself worthy; therefore they urged ordering yielding worthies thereby to self-manifest worthiness — how was it feigned yielding to the unworthy!

entries.zh: 故讓道興，賢能之人不求而自出矣，至公之舉自立矣，百官之副亦豫具矣。
entries.en: When yielding is honored, able men step forward unbidden, the most impartial choices make themselves, and the whole chain of secondary offices fills of its own accord.
entries.literal: Therefore when the way of yielding rises, worthy and able men without seeking come forth of themselves; utmost impartial selection stands of itself; the hundred officials' deputies are also prepared in advance.

entries.zh: 一官缺，擇眾官所讓最多者而用之，審之道也。
entries.en: When a post opens, appoint the man to whom the greatest number of colleagues have already deferred—that is the sure way to choose well.
entries.literal: When one office is vacant, choose among the host of officials the one whom most have yielded to and use him — this is the way of carefulness.

entries.zh: 在朝之士相讓於上，草廬之人咸皆化之，推賢讓能之風從此生矣。
entries.en: Courtiers defer to one another before the throne, recluses take the lesson from them, and a wind of recommending the worthy and yielding to the able springs up everywhere.
entries.literal: Gentlemen at court yield to one another above; men in thatched huts all are transformed by it; the wind of pushing worthies and yielding to ability from this arises.

entries.zh: 為一國所讓，則一國士也；
entries.en: The man a whole state agrees to honor is that state's true gentleman;
entries.literal: If by one state yielded to, then he is that state's gentleman;

entries.zh: 天下所共推，則天下士也。
entries.en: the man the whole realm presses forward is the gentleman of the realm.
entries.literal: if by the realm jointly pushed, then he is the realm's gentleman.

entries.zh: 推讓之風行，則賢與不肖灼然殊矣。
entries.en: Once yielding becomes the fashion, worthy and unworthy stand out as clearly as fire and ice.
entries.literal: When the wind of pushing yielding is practiced, then worthy and unworthy are scorchingly distinct.

entries.zh: 此道之行，在上者無所用其心，因成清議，隨之而已。
entries.en: Under such a system those on high need not scheme; pure public opinion takes shape of itself, and they have only to follow it.
entries.literal: When this way is practiced, those above have no need to use their hearts; thereby pure discussion is completed, and they follow it only.

entries.zh: 故曰，蕩蕩乎堯之為君，莫之能名。
entries.en: Hence the saying, "Vast was Yao as ruler—no one could put a name to his art."
entries.literal: Therefore it is said, vast vast was Yao as lord — none could name him.

entries.zh: 言天下自安矣，不見堯所以化之，故不能名也。
entries.en: The realm was at peace of itself; people could not point to what Yao had done to change them, and so they could not describe his government.
entries.literal: It means the realm was self-at peace; they did not see whereby Yao transformed it, therefore could not name it.

entries.zh: 又曰，舜禹之有天下而不與焉，無為而化者其舜也歟。
entries.en: It is also said that Shun and Yu possessed the empire yet seemed not to grasp it; perhaps Shun was the one who ruled without acting.
entries.literal: Again it is said, Shun and Yu had the realm yet did not participate therein; by non-action transforming — was it not Shun!

entries.zh: 賢人相讓于朝，大才之人恆在大官，小人不爭於野，天下無事矣。
entries.en: Worthy men defer to one another at court, great talent always fills high office, petty men do not squabble in the countryside, and the realm is untroubled.
entries.literal: Worthy men yield to one another at court; great-talent men always are in great offices; petty men do not contend in the wilds; the realm has no affairs.

entries.zh: 以賢才化無事，至道興矣。
entries.en: When worthies bring about an age without crises, the highest Way prevails.
entries.literal: By worthy talent transforming to no affairs, the utmost Way rises.

entries.zh: 已仰其成，復何與焉！
entries.en: The ruler has only to trust the outcome—what need has he to meddle?
entries.literal: Already looking up to its completion, what further participation!

entries.zh: 故可以歌《南風》之詩，彈五弦之琴也。
entries.en: That is why he could sing the "South Wind" and strum the five-string lute in peace.
entries.literal: Therefore he could sing the "South Wind" poem, pluck the five-stringed zither.

entries.zh: 成此功者非有他，崇讓之所致耳。
entries.en: No other art produced that achievement—only the honoring of yielding did.
entries.literal: Completing this achievement had nothing else; it was what honoring yielding brought about only.

entries.zh: 孔子曰，能以禮讓為國，則不難也。
entries.en: Confucius said, "To govern a state by ritual and deference presents no difficulty."
entries.literal: Confucius said, if able by ritual yielding to govern the state, then it is not difficult.

entries.zh: 向令天下貴讓，士必由於見讓而後名成，名成而官乃得用之。
entries.en: Suppose the realm honored deference: a man would first win recommendation through others' yielding to him, build a reputation on that, and only then receive appointment.
entries.literal: Suppose we ordered the realm to honor yielding; gentlemen must by being seen yielded to afterward complete their names, names completed and then offices could use them.

entries.zh: 諸名行不立之人，在官無政績之稱，讓之者必矣，官無因得而用之也。
entries.en: Men of no established reputation who leave no record of achievement in office would find plenty of colleagues ready to yield to them, and no bureau could justify hiring them.
entries.literal: The various men whose names and conduct are not established, in office have no praise of administrative achievement — those who yield to them will be certain; offices have no cause thereby to use them.

entries.zh: 所以見用不息者，由讓道廢，因資用人之有失久矣。
entries.en: The endless parade of unfit appointees comes from the death of yielding and from long reliance on seniority instead of merit.
entries.literal: The reason those seen employed without cease is because the way of yielding was abolished; relying on seniority to employ men has missed the mark for a long time.

entries.zh: 故自漢魏以來，時開大舉，令眾官各舉所知，唯才所任，不限階次，如此者甚數矣。
entries.en: Since Han and Wei the court has often ordered a general nomination: every official recommends men he knows, with talent the sole criterion and rank ignored—such campaigns have been many.
entries.literal: Therefore from Han and Wei onward, times opened great selections, ordering the host of officials each to raise those they knew, only talent being entrusted, not limited by rank order — such cases have been very numerous.

entries.zh: 其所舉必有當者，不聞時有擢用，不知何誰最賢故也。
entries.en: Some nominees must be suitable, yet we never hear of timely promotions from these lists—because no one can tell who is truly the best.
entries.literal: Among those raised there must be suitable ones, yet we do not hear timely promotions and selections — because we do not know who is most worthy.

entries.zh: 所舉必有不當，而罪不加，不知何誰最不肖也。
entries.en: Some nominees must be unsuitable, yet no one is punished—because no one can tell who is the worst.
entries.literal: Among those raised there must be unsuitable ones, yet punishment is not applied — because we do not know who is most unworthy.

entries.zh: 所以不可得知，由當時之人莫肯相推，賢愚之名不別，令其如此。
entries.en: The reason is that contemporaries will not recommend one another, worthy and foolish look alike, and the system ends in this confusion.
entries.literal: The reason it cannot be known is because men of the time none were willing to defer to one another; names of worthy and foolish are not distinguished, ordering it to be thus.

entries.zh: 舉者知在上者察不能審，故敢漫舉而進之。
entries.en: Nominators know superiors cannot vet every name, so they toss lists together without care.
entries.literal: Those who raise know those above examine yet cannot be careful; therefore they dare carelessly to raise and advance them.

entries.zh: 或舉所賢，因及所念，一頓而至，人數猥多，各言所舉者賢，加之高狀，相似如一，難得而分矣。
entries.en: Some push their favorites and tag along their cronies; names arrive in heaps, every sponsor swears his pick is brilliant and piles on the same lofty phrases, so the court cannot sort them out.
entries.literal: Some raise those they esteem, thereby reaching those they favor; in one batch they arrive, the number of persons very many; each says those he raised are worthy, adding them high descriptions, similar as one — hard to obtain and divide.

entries.zh: 參錯相亂，真偽同貫，更復由此而甚。
entries.en: Truth and falsehood are jumbled in one bundle, and the tangle only grows worse.
entries.literal: Mixed and crossed they mutually confuse; true and false share one string; again from this it becomes extreme.

entries.zh: 雖舉者不能盡忠之罪，亦由上開聽察之路濫，令其爾也。
entries.en: Nominators share the blame for disloyalty, yet the throne has opened so wide a gate for rumor that the mess was inevitable.
entries.literal: Although it is also the nominators' crime of not exhausting loyalty, it is also because those above opened the road of listening and examining to flood, ordering it to be thus.

entries.zh: 昔齊王好聽竽聲，必令三百人合吹而後聽之，廩以數人之俸。
entries.en: Once the King of Qi loved the sound of the yu and insisted that three hundred players blow together before he would listen, paying them the rations of several men each.
entries.literal: Formerly the King of Qi loved listening to yu pipes, and always ordered three hundred men jointly to blow before he listened, granarying them several men's stipends.

entries.zh: 南郭先生不知吹竽者也，以三百人合吹可以容其不知，因請為王吹竽，虛食數人之俸。
entries.en: Master Nanguo could not play at all, but hid inside a chorus of three hundred and drew several men's pay for doing nothing.
entries.literal: Master Nanguo was one who did not know how to blow the yu; because three hundred men jointly blowing could contain his not knowing, therefore he requested to blow yu for the king, vainly eating several men's stipends.

entries.zh: 嗣王覺而改之，難彰先王之過。
entries.en: When the new king saw through the trick, he wished to reform the practice yet hesitated to shame his father.
entries.literal: The succeeding king perceived and changed it, finding it hard to display the former king's fault.

entries.zh: 乃下令曰：「吾之好聞竽聲有甚于先王，欲一一列而聽之。」
entries.en: So he proclaimed, "I love the yu even more than my father did; I mean to hear each musician play in turn."
entries.literal: Then he issued an order, saying, "My liking to hear yu sound is greater than the former king's; I wish each one in row to play and I will listen."

entries.zh: 先生于此逃矣。
entries.en: At that the fellow fled the kingdom.
entries.literal: The master at this fled.

entries.zh: 推賢之風不立，濫舉之法不改，則南郭先生之徒盈於朝矣。
entries.en: Until we honor real recommendation and stop indiscriminate lists, the court will swarm with Nanguos.
entries.literal: If the wind of pushing worthies is not established, if the law of reckless raising is not changed, then disciples of Master Nanguo fill the court.

entries.zh: 才高守道之士日退，馳走有勢之門日多矣。
entries.en: Talented men who keep their integrity withdraw further each day, while toadies at great houses grow more numerous.
entries.literal: Men of high talent who keep the Way daily withdraw; those who gallop to powerful gates daily increase.

entries.zh: 雖國有典刑，弗能禁矣。
entries.en: Even the full code cannot check it.
entries.literal: Although the state has statutes and punishments, it cannot forbid it.

entries.zh: 竊以為改此俗甚易耳。
entries.en: I believe this custom could be changed with ease.
entries.literal: I privately hold that changing this custom is very easy.

entries.zh: 何以知之？
entries.en: Why do I say so?
entries.literal: By what is it known?

entries.zh: 夫一時在官之人，雖雜有凡猥之才，其中賢明者亦多矣，豈可謂皆不知讓賢為貴邪！
entries.en: The men in office at any moment, though many are mediocre, include a host of able and upright men—surely they all know that yielding to the better man is the honorable course!
entries.literal: As for men in office at one time, although mixed with vulgar and base talent, among them the worthy and bright are also many — how can it be said they all do not know yielding to worthies is noble!

entries.zh: 直以其時皆不讓，習以成俗，故遂不為耳。
entries.en: They do not yield only because no one yields now; habit has frozen into custom, and so they follow along.
entries.literal: Straight because at that time all did not yield, habit thereby completed custom, therefore in the end they did not do it.

entries.zh: 人臣初除，皆通表上聞，名之謝章，所由來尚矣。
entries.en: Every new appointee submits a memorial of thanks to the throne—a practice of great antiquity.
entries.literal: When ministers are first appointed, all pass memorials upward to be heard; naming them thanks memorials — the origin thereof is long.

entries.zh: 原謝章之本意，欲進賢能以謝國恩也。
entries.en: The original purpose of that memorial was to recommend worthier men in gratitude for imperial favor.
entries.literal: Tracing the thanks memorial's root intent, it desired to advance worthy ability thereby to thank state grace.

entries.zh: 昔舜以禹為司空，禹拜稽首，讓於稷契及咎繇。
entries.en: When Shun made Yu minister of works, Yu kowtowed and yielded the honor to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao.
entries.literal: Formerly Shun made Yu Minister of Works; Yu bowed touching forehead, yielding to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao.

entries.zh: 使益為虞官，讓於硃虎、熊、羆。
entries.en: Shun made Yi warden of forests and marshes; Yi deferred to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.
entries.literal: He made Yi forest officer, yielding to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.

entries.zh: 使伯夷典三禮，讓于夔龍。
entries.en: When Boyi was put in charge of the three classes of rites, he yielded to Kui and Long.
entries.literal: He made Boyi manage the three rites, yielding to Kui and Long.

entries.zh: 唐虞之時，眾官初除，莫不皆讓也。
entries.en: Under Yao and Shun every first appointment was accompanied by such deferrals.
entries.literal: In the time of Tang and Yu, when the host of officials were first appointed, none did not all yield.

entries.zh: 謝章之義，蓋取於此。
entries.en: The memorial of thanks took its meaning from that age.
entries.literal: The meaning of the thanks memorial, probably was taken from this.

entries.zh: 《書》記之者，欲以永世作則。
entries.en: The Book of Documents set down these acts so later ages would have a model.
entries.literal: The Documents records them, desiring thereby for endless ages to make a model.

entries.zh: 季世所用，不賢不能讓賢，虛謝見用之恩而已。
entries.en: In a decadent age the unworthy cannot yield to worthier men; the memorial becomes an empty gesture of thanks.
entries.literal: What declining ages use: not worthy, unable to yield to worthies — empty thanks for the grace of being used only.

entries.zh: 相承不變，習俗之失也。
entries.en: Generation after generation never changed the form—only the spirit was lost.
entries.literal: Handed down unchanged — it is the loss of habit and custom.

entries.zh: 夫讓道不興之弊，非徒賢人在下位，不得時進也，國之良臣荷重任者，亦將以漸受罪退矣。
entries.en: When yielding dies, the harm is not only that able men stuck below cannot rise; even good ministers who bear the heaviest burdens will step by step be hounded from office.
entries.literal: The harm when the way of yielding does not rise is not only that worthy men in lower positions cannot advance in time; the state's good ministers bearing heavy burden also will by degrees suffer blame and withdraw.

entries.zh: 何以知其然也？
entries.en: How do we know this is true?
entries.literal: By what do we know it is so?

entries.zh: 孔子以為顏氏之子不貳過耳，明非聖人皆有過。
entries.en: Confucius said even Yan Hui never repeated a mistake—meaning everyone short of a sage errs sometimes.
entries.literal: Confucius held that the Yan clan's son merely did not repeat a fault — making clear that all who are not sages have faults.

entries.zh: 寵貴之地欲之者多矣，惡賢能者塞其路，其過而毀之者亦多矣。
entries.en: Everyone covets high favor; rivals who hate true talent block the path, and many seize on small slips to ruin a man.
entries.literal: In places of favor and nobility, those who desire them are many; those who hate worthies and able men block their road; those who for their faults destroy them are also many.

entries.zh: 夫謗毀之生，非徒空設，必因人之微過而甚之者也。
entries.en: Slander is never spun from thin air; it always seizes some tiny fault and blows it out of proportion.
entries.literal: As for slander and destruction arising, it is not merely empty establishment; it must be because of men's slight faults that they exaggerate them.

entries.zh: 譭謗之言數聞，在上者雖欲弗納，不能不杖所聞，因事之來而微察之也，無以，其驗至矣。
entries.en: When calumny is repeated often enough, the ruler may wish to ignore it yet cannot help leaning on what he hears; each new incident invites scrutiny, and in time the charges seem proved.
entries.literal: Words of ruinous slander repeatedly are heard; those above although they wish not to accept, must lean on what they hear, because affairs come and they slightly examine them; having no other means, the verification arrives.

entries.zh: 得其驗，安得不理其罪。
entries.en: Once it looks verified, how can the throne fail to punish?
entries.literal: Having obtained the verification, how can they not handle their crimes?

entries.zh: 若知而縱之，王之威日衰，令之不行自此始矣。
entries.en: To know guilt and overlook it drains royal authority and marks the moment when decrees cease to bite.
entries.literal: If knowing yet indulging them, the king's awe daily wanes; orders not being practiced from this begin.

entries.zh: 知而皆理之，受罪退者稍多，大臣有不自固之心。
entries.en: If every charge is prosecuted, dismissed ministers multiply and great officers lose confidence in their own survival.
entries.literal: If knowing and all handling them, those who suffer punishment and withdraw gradually become many, great ministers have hearts not self-firm.

entries.zh: 夫賢才不進，貴臣日疏，此有國者之深憂也。
entries.en: Blocked promotion of talent and estrangement of loyal ministers are a ruler's deepest fears.
entries.literal: When worthy talent does not advance and honored ministers daily grow distant, this is what those who hold the state deeply worry about.

entries.zh: 《詩》曰：「受祿不讓，至於已斯亡。」
entries.en: The Classic of Poetry says, "He took his salary without yielding—unto himself came ruin."
entries.literal: The Odes says, "Receiving emolument without yielding — to the point of self, then perishing."

entries.zh: 不讓之人憂亡不暇，而望其益國朝，不亦難乎！
entries.en: Men who never yield are too busy saving their own skins to strengthen the state—can we expect much from them?
entries.literal: Men who do not yield worry about perishing without leisure, yet hope they benefit state and court — is it not difficult!

entries.zh: 夫敘用之官得通章表者，其讓賢推能乃通，其不能有所讓徒費簡紙者，皆絕不通。
entries.en: Let every bureau that may submit memorials accept only those that name worthier men to replace the writer; any memorial that yields no one and wastes paper should be rejected unread.
entries.literal: As for appointment offices that can pass memorials, if their yielding worthies and pushing ability then pass; those who cannot have anything to yield, vainly wasting bamboo slips and paper — all cut off and not pass.

entries.zh: 人臣初除，各思推賢能而讓之矣，讓之文付主者掌之。
entries.en: On first appointment each man should propose a worthier candidate; the text of his deferral goes to the keeper of records.
entries.literal: When ministers are first appointed, each thinks to push worthy ability and yield to them; the texts of yielding are handed to the chief keeper to hold.

entries.zh: 三司有缺，擇三司所讓最多者而用之。
entries.en: When a seat among the Three Dukes falls vacant, choose the man to whom the three have most often deferred.
entries.literal: When the Three Dukes have a vacancy, choose among what the Three Dukes yielded to most and use him.

entries.zh: 此為一公缺，三公已豫選之矣。
entries.en: Thus one grandee's vacancy is filled from names the three have already ranked.
entries.literal: This is: one duke vacant, the Three Dukes have already pre-selected him.

entries.zh: 且主選之吏，不必任公而選三公，不如令三公自共選一公為詳也。
entries.en: It is needless to charge the personnel bureau with picking the Three Dukes; better let the three jointly choose their own colleague—that is surer.
entries.literal: Moreover appointment clerks need not entrust the duke to select the Three Dukes — it is not as good as ordering the Three Dukes themselves jointly to select one duke, which is more detailed.

entries.zh: 四征缺，擇四征所讓最多而用之，此為一征缺，四征已豫選之矣，必詳於停缺而令主者選四征也。
entries.en: When a Four Expeditions command opens, pick the man most often yielded to by the four commanders—so one vacancy is filled from lists the four have already filed, a far sounder method than leaving the post empty while some clerk picks among four nominees.
entries.literal: When a Four Expeditions post is vacant, choose among what the four expeditions yielded to most and use him; this is: one expedition vacant, the four expeditions have already pre-selected him — it must be more detailed than halting the vacancy and ordering the chief to select the four expeditions.

entries.zh: 尚書缺，擇尚書所讓最多者而用之，此為八尚書共選一尚書，詳于臨缺令主者選八尚書也。
entries.en: When a minister of the masters of writing is needed, take the man most deferred to by the eight ministers—eight colleagues choose one, which beats leaving a gap and letting a single clerk juggle eight names.
entries.literal: When a Masters of Writing post is vacant, choose among what the Masters of Writing yielded to most and use him; this is: the eight Masters of Writing jointly select one Master of Writing — more detailed than on facing vacancy ordering the chief to select eight Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 郡守缺，擇眾郡所讓最多者而用之，詳于任主者令選百郡守也。
entries.en: When a commandery governorship opens, choose the man most often yielded to across the commanderies—far better than asking one appointing officer to rank a hundred magistrates.
entries.literal: When a commandery governor is vacant, choose among what the host of commanderies yielded to most and use him — more detailed than entrusting the chief to order selection of a hundred commandery governors.

entries.zh: 夫以眾官百郡之讓，與主者共相比，不可同歲而論也。
entries.en: The judgment of hundreds of deferring officials cannot be mentioned in the same breath as one clerk's guess.
entries.literal: To use the yielding of the host of officials and hundred commanderies, compared with the chief together — they cannot be spoken of in the same year.

entries.zh: 雖復令三府參舉官，本不委以舉選之任，各不能以根其心也。
entries.en: Even when the three bureaus are ordered to deliberate on nominations, they are not truly charged with selection, so none commits his judgment.
entries.literal: Although again ordering the Three Offices jointly to deliberate on raising officials, fundamentally they were not entrusted with the duty of raising and selecting; each cannot thereby root his heart.

entries.zh: 其所用心者裁之不二三，但令主者案官次而舉之，不用精也。
entries.en: They give the matter a moment's thought, then tell the appointing clerk to go by seniority—no care for quality.
entries.literal: What they use heart on cuts it not two or three; only ordering the chief to examine official order and raise them — not using refinement.

entries.zh: 賢愚皆讓，百姓耳目盡為國耳目。
entries.en: When worthy and foolish alike must defer to someone else, every commoner's eyes and ears become the eyes and ears of the state.
entries.literal: Worthy and foolish all yield; the hundred surnames' ears and eyes all become the state's ears and eyes.

entries.zh: 夫人情爭則欲毀己所不知，讓則競推於勝己。
entries.en: In a scramble men slander what they do not understand; in yielding they compete to lift up whoever surpasses them.
entries.literal: As for human feeling: when striving, then they wish to destroy what they themselves do not know; when yielding, then they compete to push toward those who surpass themselves.

entries.zh: 故世爭則毀譽交錯，優劣不分，難得而讓也。
entries.en: When the age is contentious, praise and blame tangle until no one can tell who excels—deference becomes impossible.
entries.literal: Therefore when the age strives, praise and blame cross confused; excellence and inferiority are not divided — hard to obtain yielding.

entries.zh: 時讓則賢智顯出，能否之美歷歷相次，不可得而亂也。
entries.en: When yielding is the fashion, talent stands out and able and useless line up in clear order—no confusion possible.
entries.literal: When yielding in the age, then worthy wisdom appears; the beauty of able and unable is clear, succeeding in order — cannot be obtained and confused.

entries.zh: 當此時也，能退身修已者，讓之者多矣。
entries.en: In such an hour, any man who steps back to cultivate himself will find many ready to yield him place.
entries.literal: At this time, those able to withdraw the body and cultivate themselves — those who yield to them are many.

entries.zh: 雖欲守貧賤，不可得也。
entries.en: Even if he wished to remain poor and obscure, he could not.
entries.literal: Although wishing to keep poverty and low status, it cannot be obtained.

entries.zh: 馳騖進趣而欲人見讓，猶卻行而求前也。
entries.en: To scramble for promotion and still expect others to defer is like walking backward and hoping to advance.
entries.literal: Galloping and rushing advancement and wishing others to see yielding to oneself — is like walking backward yet seeking forward.

entries.zh: 夫如此，愚智咸知進身求通，非修之於己則無由矣。
entries.en: Then fool and sage alike see that to rise they must polish themselves—there is no other road.
entries.literal: If thus, foolish and wise alike know advancing the body and seeking penetration — if not cultivating in oneself then there is no way.

entries.zh: 游外求者，於此相隨而歸矣。
entries.en: Men who chase outside connections will come home to self-cultivation instead.
entries.literal: Those who roam outside seeking — at this follow one another and return.

entries.zh: 浮聲虛論，不禁而自息矣。
entries.en: Empty rumor and hollow debate die away without a ban.
entries.literal: Floating sounds and empty discussions, without forbidding, of themselves cease.

entries.zh: 人人無所用其心，任眾人之議，而天下自化矣。
entries.en: No one needs to scheme; trust public discussion, and the realm orders itself.
entries.literal: Each man has nowhere to use his heart; entrust the host of men's discussions, and the realm transforms itself.

entries.zh: 不言之化行，巍巍之美於此著矣。
entries.en: Silent transformation takes hold, and the majesty of good rule shows forth.
entries.literal: Non-speaking transformation is practiced; the lofty beauty here is manifest.

entries.zh: 讓可以致此，豈可不務之哉！
entries.en: Yielding can achieve this—how can we fail to pursue it?
entries.literal: Yielding can bring this about — how can it not be urgently pursued!

entries.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「范宣子之讓，其下皆讓。
entries.en: The Zuo commentary says, "When Fan Xuanzi yielded, his subordinates yielded in turn.
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn Tradition says, "Fan Xuanzi's yielding — his subordinates all yielded.

entries.zh: 欒黶雖汰，弗敢違也。
entries.en: Even the arrogant Luan Yan did not dare refuse.
entries.literal: Luan Yan although extravagant, did not dare disobey.

entries.zh: 晉國以平，數世賴之。」
entries.en: Jin was pacified thereby, and generations reaped the benefit."
entries.literal: Jin state thereby was pacified; several ages relied on it."

entries.zh: 上世之化也，君子尚能而讓其下，小人力農以事其上，上下有禮，讒慝遠黜，由不爭也。
entries.en: Such was the transformation of high antiquity: gentlemen honored ability and deferred to inferiors, while commoners bent to the plow to serve their betters; rank observed ritual, slander and malice were driven off, and all because men did not fight for place.
entries.literal: Upper ages' transformation: the gentleman esteems ability and yields to those below; petty men exert strength in farming to serve those above; above and below have ritual; slander and evil are distantly banished — from not contending.

entries.zh: 及其亂也，國家之弊，恆必由之。
entries.en: When that order breaks down, the state's sickness always stems from the same cause.
entries.literal: Reaching their disorder, the state's ills, always must come from this.

entries.zh: 篤論了了如此。
entries.en: The argument stands clear as this.
entries.literal: The firm discussion is clear thus.

entries.zh: 在朝君子典選大官，能不以人廢言，舉而行之，各以讓賢舉能為先務，則群才猥出，能否殊別，蓋世之功，莫大於此。
entries.en: If the great officers who control appointments will not dismiss good counsel because of its source, but put these measures into practice and make yielding to worthier men their first duty, talent will pour forth, able and useless will stand apart, and no achievement could match it for an age.
entries.literal: Gentlemen at court who manage selection and great officials, if able not because of the person to discard words, raise and put them in practice, each taking yielding to worthies and raising ability as first task, then host of talents will swarm forth, able and unable will be sharply distinguished — age-surpassing achievement, nothing greater than this.

entries.zh: 泰始初，進爵為伯，累遷少府。
entries.en: Early in Taishi his noble rank rose to earl, and he was promoted step by step to privy treasurer.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he advanced in noble rank to earl, by accumulated transfers became Privy Treasurer.

entries.zh: 咸甯中為太常。
entries.en: During the Xianning era he served as minister of ceremonies.
entries.literal: In Xianning he was Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 轉尚書。
entries.en: He was transferred to the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 杜預之伐吳也，寔以本官行鎮南軍司。
entries.en: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Liu Shi, still in his current post, served as army director on the southern pacification staff.
entries.literal: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu, Shi by his original office acted as Army Director of the Southern Pacification command.

entries.zh: 初，寔妻盧氏生子躋而卒，華氏將以女妻之。
entries.en: Earlier, Shi's wife of the Lu clan bore a son, Ji, then died; the Hua family wished to give him a daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: Earlier, Shi's wife the Lu clan bore a son Ji and died; the Hua clan was about to take a daughter and marry her to him.

entries.zh: 寔弟智諫曰：「華家類貪，必破門戶。」
entries.en: His brother Zhi warned him, "The Huas are a grasping clan; they will ruin our house."
entries.literal: Shi's younger brother Zhi remonstrated, saying, "The Hua clan is by kind greedy; they will surely break the household gate."

entries.zh: 辭之不得，竟婚華氏而生子夏。
entries.en: Shi could not refuse the match; he married a Hua daughter and fathered a son named Xia.
entries.literal: Declining it he could not obtain; in the end he married the Hua clan and bore a son Xia.

entries.zh: 寔竟坐夏受賂，免官。
entries.en: In the end Shi lost his office because Xia took bribes.
entries.literal: Shi in the end, because Xia was convicted of accepting bribes, was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 頃之為大司農，又以夏罪免。
entries.en: Soon he was named grand minister of agriculture, then dismissed again over Xia's crimes.
entries.literal: Before long he was Grand Minister of Agriculture, again because of Xia's crime dismissed.

entries.zh: 寔每還州裏，鄉人載酒肉以候之。
entries.en: Whenever Shi returned to his home district, villagers brought wine and meat to greet him.
entries.literal: Whenever Shi returned to the commandery district, townsmen loaded wine and meat to await him.

entries.zh: 寔難逆其意，輒共啖而返其餘。
entries.en: Unwilling to refuse their kindness outright, he would share a little of the feast and send the rest back.
entries.literal: Shi found it hard to go against their intent, then always together ate and returned the remainder.

entries.zh: 或謂寔曰：「君行高一世，而諸子不能遵。
entries.en: Someone said to him, "Your conduct towers above the age, yet your sons will not follow your example.
entries.literal: Someone said to Shi, "Your conduct is high above one age, yet the various sons cannot follow.

entries.zh: 何不旦夕切磋，使知過而自改邪！」
entries.en: Why not lecture them day and night until they see their faults and mend their ways?"
entries.literal: Why not morning and evening cut and polish, causing them to know fault and themselves reform!"

entries.zh: 寔曰：「吾之所行，是所聞見，不相祖習，豈復教誨之所得乎！」
entries.en: Shi answered, "What I do rests on what I myself saw and heard; my sons have not walked the same path—how could mere lecturing reach them now?"
entries.literal: Shi said, "What I practice is what I heard and saw; we do not mutually imitate and practice — how again could instruction and teaching obtain it!"

entries.zh: 世以寔言為當。
entries.en: People of the time judged his reply sound.
entries.literal: The age held Shi's words correct.

entries.zh: 後起為國子祭酒、散騎常侍。
entries.en: Later he was recalled as libationer of the imperial academy and cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: Later he rose as Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 湣懷太子初封廣陵王，高選師友，以寔為師。
entries.en: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first enfeoffed as prince of Guangling, the court chose his tutors with care and named Shi his principal teacher.
entries.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, highly selecting teachers and friends, they made Shi his teacher.

entries.zh: 元康初，進爵為侯，累遷太子太保，加侍中、特進、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領冀州都督。
entries.en: Early in Yuankang his rank rose to marquis; he rose through junior tutor to the heir apparent to the added titles of palace attendant, specially advanced, grand master of the right of splendid carriage, and opener of a bureau with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, while commanding military affairs in Ji Province.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuankang he advanced in noble rank to marquis, by accumulated transfers became Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, added Palace Attendant, Specially Advanced, Grand Master of the Right of Splendid Carriage, Opener of Office with parity of the Three Dukes, concurrently Area Commander of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 九年，策拜司空，遷太保，轉太傅。
entries.en: In the ninth year of the era he received the rescript as minister of works, then moved up to grand guardian and finally grand tutor.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was rescript-appointed Minister of Works, transferred Grand Guardian, transferred Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 太安初，寔以老病遜位，賜安車駟馬、錢百萬，以侯就第。
entries.en: Early in the Tai'an era he resigned on grounds of age and illness; the court granted him a secure carriage, four-horse team, a million cash, and permission to retire to his mansion as a marquis.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tai'an, Shi because of old age and illness yielded position; he was bestowed secure carriage and four-horse team, one million cash, and as marquis went to mansion.

entries.zh: 及長沙成都之相攻也，寔為軍人所掠，潛歸鄉里。
entries.en: When the princes of Changsha and Chengdu turned on each other, soldiers plundered him and he slipped away to his home district.
entries.literal: When Changsha and Chengdu mutually attacked, Shi was plundered by soldiers and secretly returned to his home village.

entries.zh: 惠帝崩，寔赴山陵。
entries.en: When Emperor Hui died, Shi went to attend at the imperial mausoleum.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui died; Shi went to the imperial mausoleum.

entries.zh: 懷帝即位，復授太尉。
entries.en: When Emperor Huai succeeded to the throne, he again appointed Shi as grand commandant.
entries.literal: Emperor Huai took the throne and again appointed him Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 寔自陳年老，固辭，不許。
entries.en: Shi pleaded old age and firmly declined the post, but the court would not allow it.
entries.literal: Shi himself stated he was old in years, firmly declined, and was not permitted.

entries.zh: 左丞劉坦上言曰：「夫堂高級遠，主尊相貴。
entries.en: Left Deputy Liu Tan submitted a memorial, saying, "When the hall is high, the steps are far; when the sovereign is honored, the minister is exalted.
entries.literal: Left Deputy Liu Tan submitted a memorial saying, "When the hall is high the steps are far; the lord is honored and the minister noble.

entries.zh: 是以古之哲王莫不師其元臣，崇養老之教，訓示四海，使少長有禮。
entries.en: For this reason the wise kings of antiquity all looked to their chief ministers as teachers, honored the instruction to nurture the aged, and taught all within the seas so that young and old alike observed proper ritual.
entries.literal: Therefore the wise kings of antiquity all took their chief ministers as teachers, esteemed the teaching of nurturing the old, instructed and displayed to the four seas, making young and old have ritual.

entries.zh: 七十致仕，亦所以優異舊德，厲廉高之風。
entries.en: Retirement at seventy was likewise meant to honor aged virtue and sharpen the standards of integrity and lofty conduct.
entries.literal: Retiring from office at seventy was also a means to specially distinguish old virtue and sharpen the wind of integrity and loftiness.

entries.zh: 太尉寔體清素之操，執不渝之潔，懸車告老，二十餘年，浩然之志，老而彌篤。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Shi embodies pure and simple conduct and unwavering integrity; he hung up his carriage and announced retirement more than twenty years ago, and his vast resolve has grown only firmer with age.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Shi embodies pure and simple conduct, holds unchanging integrity, hung up his cart and announced old age for more than twenty years; his vast resolve grows firmer as he ages.

entries.zh: 可謂國之碩老，邦之宗模。
entries.en: He may truly be called a venerable pillar of the state and a model for the realm.
entries.literal: He may be called the state's venerable elder and the dynasty's model.

entries.zh: 臣聞老者不以筋力為禮，寔年逾九十，命在日制，遂自扶輿，冒險而至，展哀山陵，致敬闕庭，大臣之節備矣。
entries.en: I have heard that the aged are not judged by physical strength in matters of ritual. Shi is past ninety and his days are numbered, yet he supported himself into his carriage, braved the dangers of the road, mourned at the imperial tombs, and paid homage at court—the full conduct of a great minister.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that the aged are not measured by sinew and strength in ritual; Shi is past ninety, his life measured in days, yet he supported himself into his carriage, came through danger, displayed mourning at the mausoleum, and paid respect at the palace court—the full measure of a great minister's conduct.

entries.zh: 聖詔殷勤，必使寔正位上臺，光飪鼎實，斷章敦喻，經涉二年。
entries.en: Imperial rescripts urged him earnestly, insisting that Shi take his proper seat at the highest level of government to bring glory to the state and sustain its substance; edict after edict pressed him for two years.
entries.literal: The sacred edict was earnest, insisting that Shi take his proper place on the high terrace, illumine the tripod and nourish its substance; section upon section of rescripts urged him, spanning two years.

entries.zh: 而寔頻上露板，辭旨懇誠。
entries.en: Yet Shi repeatedly submitted open memorials, and the sincerity of his refusal was unmistakable.
entries.literal: Yet Shi repeatedly submitted open memorials; the purport of his refusal was earnest and sincere.

entries.zh: 臣以為古之養老，以不事為優，不以吏之為重，謂宜聽寔所守。」
