entries.literal: Hong invited him back to the province, asked what he rode; he answered, "Plainly I have foot ailment; lately I ride a blue litter—still enough to return myself."

entries.zh: 乃令一門生二兒共轝之至州，而言笑賞適，不覺其有羨于華軒也。
entries.en: Students carried his chair; he chatted as if no shame.
entries.literal: Then he ordered one student and two sons together to carry him to the province, yet talking and laughing at ease, not letting them feel he envied splendid carriages.

entries.zh: 弘後欲見，輒于林澤間候之。
entries.en: Wang met him only in the wilds.
entries.literal: Hong afterward when wishing to see him, then waited for him among woods and marshes.

entries.zh: 至於酒米乏絕，亦時相贍。
entries.en: Wang sent grain when the larder ran dry.
entries.literal: As for when wine and rice failed, sometimes he also supplied him.

entries.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；
entries.en: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.
entries.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;

entries.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。
entries.en: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.
entries.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.

entries.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；
entries.en: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;
entries.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;

entries.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。
entries.en: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.
entries.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.

entries.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；
entries.en: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;
entries.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;

entries.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。
entries.en: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.
entries.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.

entries.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。
entries.en: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.
entries.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.

entries.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。
entries.en: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.
entries.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?

entries.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！
entries.en: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.
entries.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?

entries.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。
entries.en: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.
entries.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.

entries.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。
entries.en: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.
entries.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.

entries.zh: 古者帝王，乃生奇類、淳維，伯禹之苗裔，豈異類哉？
entries.en: Ancient emperors counted even alien lines like Chunwei among the descendants of Great Yu—hardly a separate species.
entries.literal: Of old the August Lords and Kings gave birth to strange stocks such as Chunwei, lineal descendants of Lord Yu—how could they be a different kind?

entries.zh: 反首衣皮，餐膻飲湩，而震驚中域，其來自遠。
entries.en: They wore furs, ate mutton, drank kumiss, yet convulsed the heartland—their roots lay deep in antiquity.
entries.literal: They turned their heads, wore pelts, ate rank flesh and drank curds, yet shook the central domains; their coming lay far in the past.

entries.zh: 天未悔禍，種落彌繁。
entries.en: Heaven had not yet called off the scourge, and their clans multiplied.
entries.literal: Heaven had not yet repented the disaster, and their tribes grew ever more numerous.

entries.zh: 其風俗險詖，性靈馳突，前史載之，亦以詳備。
entries.en: Their ways were sly and abrupt, their natures fierce—earlier histories already told the tale in exhaustive detail.
entries.literal: Their customs were crafty and crooked, their temperaments headstrong; earlier histories recorded them in full detail.

entries.zh: 軒帝患其干紀，所以徂征；
entries.en: The Yellow Emperor feared they would break the cosmic order and campaigned against them;
entries.literal: The Yellow Emperor worried that they would violate the norm, and therefore marched against them;

entries.zh: 武王竄以荒服，同乎禽獸。
entries.en: King Wu pushed them into the outermost wilds, no better than beasts in policy.
entries.literal: King Wu banished them to the wild outer zone, treating them like birds and beasts.

entries.zh: 而於露寒之野，候月覘風，睹隙揚埃，乘間騁暴，邊城不得緩帶，百姓靡有室家。
entries.en: Yet on the open steppe they watched seasons and winds, struck whenever a crack appeared, and raided at will—so frontier garrisons never rested and the people lost hearth and home.
entries.literal: Yet on the steppes of dew and cold they watched the moon and spied the wind, seized gaps and raised dust, exploited openings to run riot; border cities could not loosen their belts, and commoners had no homes.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「微管仲，吾其被髮左衽矣。」
entries.en: Confucius said, "Without Guan Zhong we should all have gone unbound-haired with robes buttoned left—barbarians."
entries.literal: Confucius said, "Without Guan Zhong, I would let my hair down and button my robe on the left."

entries.zh: 此言能教訓卒伍，整齊車甲，邊埸既伏，境內以安。
entries.en: He meant a minister who could train troops, fit out armies, quiet the frontier, and secure the interior.
entries.literal: This speaks of one who could drill the ranks, align chariots and armour, so that the border submitted and the interior was calm.

entries.zh: 然則燕築造陽之郊，秦塹臨洮之險，登天山，絕地脈，苞玄菟，款黃河，所以防夷狄之亂中華，其備豫如此。
entries.en: So Yan walled Zaoyang, Qin ditched Lintao, climbed the Heavenly Mountain, choked the passes, wrapped Xuandu, and bent the Yellow River into a shield—every device to keep the barbarians from China.
entries.literal: Thus Yan built walls at Zaoyang's outskirts, Qin trenched the peril of Lintao, ascended Heaven Mountain, cut the earth's veins, embraced Xuandu, and bowed to the Yellow River—all to guard the Hua heartland from the Di and Yi, with precautions so thorough.

entries.zh: 漢宣帝初納呼韓，居之亭鄣，委以候望，始寬戎狄。
entries.en: Han Xuandi first admitted Huhanye, lodged him inside the beacon line, and gave him scout duty—opening the door to the steppe peoples.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Han Xuandi he admitted Huhanye, housed him in signal towers and stockades, entrusted him with watch duties, and first relaxed control over the Rong and Di.

entries.zh: 光武亦以南庭數萬徙入西河，後亦轉至五原，連延七郡。
entries.en: Guangwu likewise resettled tens of thousands of southern Xiongnu into Xihe, later spreading them through Wuyuan across seven commanderies.
entries.literal: Guangwu also moved several tens of thousands of the southern court into Xihe, later shifted them to Wuyuan, stretching across seven commanderies.

entries.zh: 董卓之亂，則汾晉之郊蕭然矣。
entries.en: When Dong Zhuo wrecked the capital, the Fen and Jin borderlands were stripped bare.
entries.literal: At the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, then the Fen and Jin hinterlands were desolate.

entries.zh: 郭欽騰箋于武帝，江統獻策于惠皇，皆以為魏處戎夷，繡居都鄙，請移沙塞之表，定一殷周之服。
entries.en: Guo Qin petitioned Emperor Wu and Jiang Tong briefed Emperor Hui, both arguing that Wei had lodged barbarians inside the inner districts and urging their removal beyond the deserts to restore the classical inner-outer divide.
entries.literal: Guo Qin sent a memorial soaring to Emperor Wu, and Jiang Tong offered strategy to Emperor Hui; both held that Wei had quartered Rong and Yi embroidered among capital and district, and requested moving them beyond the sandy wastes to fix the single garment-zone of Yin and Zhou.

entries.zh: 統則憂諸並部，欽則慮在盟津。
entries.en: Jiang Tong feared the clustered Bing garrisons; Guo Qin eyed the Mengjin crossing.
entries.literal: Tong worried about the Bing provinces together; Qin fretted over the Meng ford.

entries.zh: 言猶自口，元海已至。
entries.en: Their warnings were barely spoken when Liu Yuan was already at the gates.
entries.literal: The words were still in their mouths, yet Yuanhai had already arrived.

entries.zh: 語曰「失以豪厘」，晉卿大夫之辱也。
entries.en: The proverb says, "An error begins by a hair's breadth"; Jin's great officers earned that reproach.
entries.literal: The saying runs, 'Loss begins from a hair's breadth'—it is the shame of Jin's ministers and grandees.

entries.zh: 聰之誓兵，東兼齊地；
entries.en: When Liu Cong mobilized eastward he swallowed the old Qi domain;
entries.literal: When Cong swore in the troops, he annexed the Qi lands eastward;

entries.zh: 曜之馳旆，西逾隴山，覆沒兩京，蒸徒百萬。
entries.en: when Liu Yao drove west past Longshan, he toppled both capitals and trampled a million subjects.
entries.literal: when Yao flew his banners, he crossed Long Mountain westward, overthrew the two capitals, and steamed a million thralls.

entries.zh: 天子陵江禦物，分據地險，回首中原，力不能救，劃長淮以北，大抵棄之。
entries.en: The emperor fled across the Yangzi to stem the tide, clung to river defences, gazed back at the north he could not save, and yielded everything north of the Huai.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven crossed the Yangzi to stem the flood, split and held perilous ground, turned his head toward the central plain yet lacked strength to save it, and north of the long Huai was largely abandoned.

entries.zh: 胡人利我艱虞，分鑣起亂；
entries.en: The steppe peoples seized on Jin's distress and rose in every quarter;
entries.literal: The Hu profited from our distress and raised rebellion on every road;

entries.zh: 晉臣或阻兵遐遠，接武效尤。
entries.en: Jin commanders likewise froze armies far away and copied their treason.
entries.literal: Jin ministers too blocked troops in distant corners and followed suit one after another.

entries.zh: 豹妻呼延氏，魏嘉平中祈子于龍門，俄而有一大魚，頂有二角，軒鬐躍鱗而至祭所，久之乃去。
entries.en: Lady Huyan prayed at Longmen during Wei Jiaping; a huge horned fish with towering fins flopped up to the altar and then swam away.
entries.literal: Bao's wife the Lady Huyan, in the Wei Jiaping era prayed for a child at Longmen; presently a great fish with two horns on its head, high fins and leaping scales, came to the sacrifice place and after a long while departed.

entries.zh: 巫覡皆異之，曰：「此嘉祥也。」
entries.en: The shamans cried an omen: "This is heaven-sent good fortune."
entries.literal: The shamans all marvelled, saying, "This is an auspicious portent."

entries.zh: 其夜夢旦所見魚變為人，左手把一物，大如半雞子，光景非常，授呼延氏，曰：「此是日精，服之生貴子。」
entries.en: That night she dreamed the fish turned into a man who pressed into her palm a sun-bright pearl, saying, "Swallow this essence of the day-star and you will bear a lord among men."
entries.literal: That night she dreamed the fish seen at dawn became a man, holding in his left hand an object the size of half a chicken egg, of extraordinary radiance; he gave it to Lady Huyan, saying, "This is the essence of the sun; swallow it and you will bear a noble son."

entries.zh: 寤而告豹，豹曰：「吉徵也。
entries.en: She woke and told Liu Bao, who said, "Heaven favours us.
entries.literal: Awakening she told Bao, who said, "It is a lucky sign.

entries.zh: 吾昔從邯鄲張冏母司徒氏相，云吾當有貴子孫，三世必大昌，仿像相符矣。」
entries.en: Mother Situ of Handan once read my face and promised noble grandsons and three generations of glory—this fits that prophecy."
entries.literal: Long ago the diviner Mother Situ of Handan Zhang Jiong told me I would have noble descendants, and for three generations there would be great flourishing—it seems to match."

entries.zh: 自是十三月而生元海，左手文有其名，遂以名焉。
entries.en: Thirteen months later she bore Liu Yuan; his left palm bore the characters of his name, so they called him Yuan.
entries.literal: From this after thirteen months she bore Yuanhai; on his left hand were characters forming his name, and therefore he was so named.

entries.zh: 齠齔英慧，七歲遭母憂，擗踴號叫，哀感旁鄰，宗族部落咸共歎賞。
entries.en: Even as a child he showed genius; at seven he mourned his mother with such tearing grief that neighbours wept; kinsmen and tribesmen marvelled.
entries.literal: In childhood he was bright; at seven he met mourning for his mother, beat his breast and wailed until grief touched the neighbours; clan and tribe together sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 時司空太原王昶聞而嘉之，並遣吊賻。
entries.en: Minister of Works Wang Chang of Taiyuan heard the tale, praised the boy, and sent funeral gifts.
entries.literal: At the time Minister of Works Wang Chang of Taiyuan heard and praised him, and also sent condolences and gifts.

entries.zh: 幼好學，師事上党崔游，習《毛詩》、《京氏易》、《馬氏尚書》，尤好《春秋左氏傳》、《孫吳兵法》，略皆誦之，《史》、《漢》、諸子，無不綜覽。
entries.en: He loved books early, studied under Cui You of Shangdang, mastered the Mao Odes, Jing Changes, Ma Rong's Documents, devoured Zuo's Spring and Autumn commentary and the Sunzi-Wuzi military classics, and read widely in the histories and philosophers.
entries.literal: In youth he loved study, took as teacher Cui You of Shangdang, studied Mao's Odes, Jing's Changes, Ma's Documents, and especially loved Zuo's Tradition of the Spring and Autumn and the Sun and Wu Art of War—he could recite them all in outline—and comprehensively surveyed the Records, Han, and the masters.

entries.zh: 嘗謂同門生硃紀、範隆曰：「吾每觀書傳，常鄙隨陸無武，降灌無文。
entries.en: He once told Zhu Ji and Fan Long, "Reading history I always scoff that Sui He and Lu Jia had no sword, while Zhou Bo and Guan Ying had no brush.
entries.literal: Once he said to fellow students Zhu Ji and Fan Long, "Whenever I read histories I always despise Sui He and Lu Jia for lacking martial prowess, and Zhou Bo and Guan Ying for lacking literary polish.

entries.zh: 道由人弘，一物之不知者，固君子之所恥也。
entries.en: The Way spreads through human effort; ignorance of even one art is a gentleman's shame.
entries.literal: The Way is enlarged by men; not to know a single thing is indeed what a gentleman should be ashamed of.

entries.zh: 二生遇高皇而不能建封侯之業，兩公屬太宗而不能開庠序之美，惜哉！」
entries.en: Those worthies served Han's founder yet never matched his martial glory, and aided Wenjing yet never spread culture—what a waste!"
entries.literal: The two students met the High Founder yet could not build a marquis's achievement; the two dukes served the Founding Ancestor yet could not open the beauty of schools—how regrettable!"

entries.zh: 於是遂學武事，妙絕於眾，猿臂善射，膂力過人。
entries.en: So he drilled in arms, outshone every comrade, shot like Yi, and wielded strength beyond mortal measure.
entries.literal: Thereupon he studied military affairs, was wondrously supreme among the host, had ape arms and excelled at archery, and his strength surpassed others.

entries.zh: 姿儀魁偉，身長八尺四寸，須長三尺餘，當心有赤毫毛三根，長三尺六寸。
entries.en: He was a giant of eight feet four inches with a three-foot beard and three crimson hairs three feet six inches long on his breast.
entries.literal: His bearing was lofty and grand; he stood eight chi four cun tall, his beard over three chi long, and on his breast were three red down hairs three chi six cun long.

entries.zh: 有屯留崔懿之、襄陵公師彧等，皆善相人，及見元海，驚而相謂曰：「此人形貌非常，吾所未見也。」
entries.en: Physiognomists such as Cui Yizhi and Gongshi Yu gasped when they saw him: "We have never read a face like his."
entries.literal: There were Cui Yizhi of Tunliu, Gongshi Yu of Xiangling, and others, all skilled at physiognomy; when they saw Yuanhai they started and said to each other, "This man's form and bearing are extraordinary—we have never seen the like."

entries.zh: 於是深相崇敬，推分結恩。
entries.en: They pledged him deep respect, broke bread with him, and swore friendship.
entries.literal: Thereupon they deeply revered him, sharing portions and knotting kindness.

entries.zh: 太原王渾虛襟友之，命子濟拜焉。
entries.en: Wang Hun of Taiyuan befriended him openly and told his son Wang Ji to treat him as elder.
entries.literal: Wang Hun of Taiyuan opened his bosom as friend and ordered his son Ji to bow to him.

entries.zh: 會豹卒，以元海代為左部帥。
entries.en: When Liu Bao died Liu Yuan succeeded him as left-section chief.
entries.literal: When Bao died, Yuanhai was appointed in his stead as commander of the left section.

entries.zh: 太康末，拜北部都尉。
entries.en: Late in Taikang he became northern commandant.
entries.literal: At the end of Taikang he was appointed northern commandant.

entries.zh: 明刑法，禁奸邪，輕財好施，推誠接物，五部俊傑無不至者。
entries.en: He enforced the code, crushed crime, spent freely, dealt honestly, and every notable of the five Xiongnu hosts rallied to him.
entries.literal: He clarified penal law, prohibited wickedness, was light with wealth and fond of giving, extended sincerity in receiving people, and there was no outstanding man of the five sections who did not come.

entries.zh: 幽冀名儒，後門秀士，不遠千里，亦皆遊焉。
entries.en: Confucian stars from You and Ji and poor scholars crossed a thousand li to sit at his feet.
entries.literal: Famous Ru of You and Ji, talented men from rear gates, not shying a thousand li, all also came to study with him.

entries.zh: 楊駿輔政，以元海為建威將軍、五部大都督，封漢光鄉侯。
entries.en: Regent Yang Jun named him General Who Establishes Might, commander-in-chief of the five sections, and marquis of Hanguang township.
entries.literal: When Yang Jun assisted the government, he made Yuanhai General Who Establishes Might, grand commander of the five sections, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Han'guang village.

entries.zh: 元康末，坐部人叛出塞免官。
entries.en: Yuankang's end saw him cashiered when his tribesmen broke for the steppe.
entries.literal: At the end of Yuankang he lost office because his tribesmen rebelled and fled beyond the pass.

entries.zh: 成都王穎鎮鄴，表元海行甯朔將軍、監五部軍事。
entries.en: While Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, was stationed at Ye, he memorialized a request to appoint Yuanhai acting General Who Pacifies the North with supervision over the military affairs of the five divisions.
entries.literal: The Prince of Chengdu, Ying, was stationed at Ye and memorialized a request to appoint Yuanhai acting General Who Pacifies the North, with supervision over the military affairs of the five divisions.

entries.zh: 惠帝失馭，寇盜蜂起，元海從祖故北部都尉、左賢王劉宣等竊議曰：「昔我先人與漢約為兄弟，憂泰同之。
entries.en: As Emperor Hui lost control, Liu Xuan, former northern commandant and left worthy king, whispered with kinsmen: "Our ancestors swore brotherhood with Han and shared its fate.
entries.literal: Emperor Hui lost the reins; bandits sprang like wasps; Yuanhai's granduncle, the former northern commandant and Left Worthy King Liu Xuan, and others secretly deliberated, saying, "Formerly our forefathers covenanted with Han as brothers, sharing joy and peril alike.

entries.zh: 自漢亡以來，魏晉代興，我單于雖有虛號，無復尺土之業，自諸王侯，降同編戶。
entries.en: Since Han fell we have kept a hollow title while every prince sank to commoner status on Jin registers.
entries.literal: Since Han fell, Wei and Jin rose in turn; our Shanyu, though he kept an empty title, no longer had an enterprise of a foot of soil; from the various princes and marquises downward he was reduced to the same as registered households.

entries.zh: 今司馬氏骨肉相殘，四海鼎沸，興邦復業，此其時矣。
entries.en: Now the Simas tear one another apart while the realm boils—this is the moment to refound our line.
entries.literal: Now the Sima clan flesh and blood devour one another and the four seas boil; to raise a state and restore an enterprise—this is the time.

entries.zh: 左賢王元海姿器絕人，幹宇超世。
entries.en: Left Worthy King Liu Yuan's presence and scope outshine every man of his day.
entries.literal: Left Worthy King Yuanhai's mien and capacity surpass others, and his stem and canopy transcend the age.

entries.zh: 天若不恢崇單于，終不虛生此人也。」
entries.en: Heaven would not have bred such a man unless it meant to exalt our Shanyu again."
entries.literal: If Heaven does not intend to exalt the Shanyu, in the end it would not vainly have born this man."

entries.zh: 於是密共推元海為大單于。
entries.en: They secretly elected Liu Yuan great Shanyu.
entries.literal: Thereupon they secretly together pushed Yuanhai as great Shanyu.

entries.zh: 乃使其党呼延攸詣鄴，以謀告之。
entries.en: They sent Huyan You to Ye with the plan.
entries.literal: They then sent their partisan Huyan You to Ye to report the plot to him.

entries.zh: 元海請歸會葬，穎弗許。
entries.en: Liu Yuan begged leave to mourn; Sima Ying refused.
entries.literal: Yuanhai requested leave to return for a funeral assembly; Ying did not permit.

entries.zh: 乃令攸先歸，告宣等招集五部，引會宜陽諸胡，聲言應穎，實背之也。
entries.en: Huyan You raced home to rally the five sections and Yiyang Hu, claiming they would help Sima Ying while plotting the opposite.
entries.literal: They then ordered You to return first, telling Xuan and the others to gather the five sections and muster the various Hu at Yiyang, declaring they would answer Ying, but in truth betrayed him.

entries.zh: 穎為皇太弟，以元海為太弟屯騎校尉。
entries.en: When Sima Ying became crown younger brother, Liu Yuan became his garrison-cavalry colonel.
entries.literal: When Ying became imperial younger brother, he made Yuanhai Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry of the imperial younger brother.

entries.zh: 惠帝伐穎，次於蕩陰，穎假元海輔國將軍、督北城守事。
entries.en: During Emperor Hui's march on Dangyin, Sima Ying put Liu Yuan in charge of the northern wall.
entries.literal: When Emperor Hui attacked Ying and halted at Dangyin, Ying made Yuanhai acting General Who Supports the State and supervised defence of the north wall.

entries.zh: 及六軍敗績，穎以元海為冠軍將軍，封盧奴伯。
entries.en: After the six armies collapsed Sima Ying named him General Who Crowns the Army and baron of Lunu.
entries.literal: When the six armies were routed, Ying made Yuanhai General Who Crowns the Army and enfeoffed him as Baron of Lunu.

entries.zh: 并州刺史東嬴公騰、安北將軍王浚，起兵伐穎，元海說穎曰：「今二鎮跋扈，眾餘十萬，恐非宿衛及近都士庶所能禦之，請為殿下還說五部，以赴國難。」
entries.en: When Bingzhou governor Sima Teng and Wang Jun raised troops against Sima Ying with more than a hundred thousand men, Liu Yuan advised Ying: "The two commands are now overbearing, and I fear neither the palace guard nor the people near the capital can withstand them. Let me return for Your Highness and persuade the five Xiongnu divisions to answer the state's crisis."
entries.literal: Governor of Bing Sima Teng of Dongying and General Who Guards the North Wang Jun raised troops to attack Ying; Yuanhai counselled Ying, saying, "Now the two garrisons are overbearing; their hosts exceed a hundred thousand—I fear neither the palace guard nor the gentry near the capital can withstand them; I beg leave for Your Highness to return and persuade the five sections to answer the state's disaster."

entries.zh: 穎曰：「五部之眾可保發已不？
entries.en: Sima Ying asked, "Can you actually raise those five hosts?
entries.literal: Ying said, "Can the host of the five sections be guaranteed to mobilize?

entries.zh: 縱能發之，鮮卑、烏丸勁速如風雲，何易可當邪？
entries.en: Even if you can, Xianbei and Wuhuan move like storms—who stops them once loosed?
entries.literal: Even if they can be mobilized, Xianbei and Wuhuan are fierce and swift as wind and cloud—how can they easily be resisted?

entries.zh: 吾欲奉乘輿還洛陽，避其鋒銳，徐傳檄天下，以逆順制之。
entries.en: I mean to escort the throne to Luoyang, dodge their spearpoint, then call the realm to arms on right and wrong.
entries.literal: I wish to escort the imperial carriage back to Luoyang, avoid their sharp edge, then slowly transmit summons across All-under-Heaven and control them with obedience and rebellion.

entries.zh: 君意何如？」
entries.en: What do you counsel?"
entries.literal: What is your intent?"

entries.zh: 元海曰：「殿下武皇帝之子，有殊勳於王室，威恩光洽，四海欽風，孰不思為殿下沒命投軀者哉，何難發之有乎！
entries.en: Liu Yuan answered, "You are Sima Yan's son, beloved across the realm—every warrior would die for you; raising the tribes is no hard task.
entries.literal: Yuanhai said, "Your Highness is Martial Emperor's son and has extraordinary merit toward the royal house; awe and kindness shine everywhere, and the four seas admire your wind—who would not think to die and cast aside his body for Your Highness—what difficulty is there in mobilizing them!

entries.zh: 王浚豎子，東嬴疏屬，豈能與殿下爭衡邪！
entries.en: Wang Jun is a pup and Sima Teng a cadet branch—neither can rival you.
entries.literal: Wang Jun is a stripling; Dongying is a distant cousin—how can they match Your Highness!

entries.zh: 殿下一發鄴宮，示弱於人，洛陽可復至乎？
entries.en: Flee Ye once and you advertise weakness—will Luoyang ever welcome you back?
entries.literal: If Your Highness once leaves the Ye palace, you show weakness to men—can Luoyang be regained?

entries.zh: 縱達洛陽，威權不復在殿下也。
entries.en: Even in Luoyang you would hold no real power.
entries.literal: Even if you reach Luoyang, awesome authority will no longer be with Your Highness.

entries.zh: 紙檄尺書，誰為人奉之！
entries.en: Who would heed a sheaf of edicts from a discrowned prince!
entries.literal: Paper summons an inch long—who will obey them!

entries.zh: 且東胡之悍不逾五部，願殿下勉撫士眾，靖以鎮之，當為殿下以二部摧東嬴，三部梟王浚，二豎之首可指日而懸矣。」
entries.en: The eastern tribes are no tougher than our horsemen—stay in Ye, steady the army, and I will smash Sima Teng with two wings and take Wang Jun's head with three; both puppets will swing from the gate in days."
entries.literal: Moreover the eastern Hu are not fiercer than the five sections; I hope Your Highness will encourage and soothe the soldiers and quiet them to hold the city—I will for Your Highness with two sections crush Dongying and with three sections behead Wang Jun; the two striplings' heads can be hung within days."

entries.zh: 穎悅，拜元海為北單于、參丞相軍事。
entries.en: Sima Ying cheered up, named Liu Yuan northern Shanyu, and attached him to the chancellor's staff.
entries.literal: Ying was pleased, appointed Yuanhai northern Shanyu, and joined him to the staff of the minister of state.

entries.zh: 元海至左國城，劉宣等上大單于之號，二旬之間，眾已五萬，都于離石。
entries.en: At Zuoguocheng Liu Xuan proclaimed him great Shanyu; inside twenty days fifty thousand men gathered with capital at Lishi.
entries.literal: Yuanhai reached Zuoguocheng; Liu Xuan and others presented the title of great Shanyu; within twenty days the host already numbered fifty thousand, with capital at Lishi.

entries.zh: 王浚使將軍祁弘率鮮卑攻鄴，穎敗，挾天子南奔洛陽。
entries.en: Wang Jun's general Qi Hong drove Xianbei against Ye; Sima Ying fled south clutching the emperor.
entries.literal: Wang Jun sent General Qi Hong leading Xianbei to attack Ye; Ying was defeated, seized the Son of Heaven, and fled south to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 元海曰：「穎不用吾言，逆自奔潰，真奴才也。
entries.en: Liu Yuan sneered, "Sima Ying ignored my counsel and ran—little better than a bondsman.
entries.literal: Yuanhai said, "Ying did not use my words and contrary-wise fled in collapse—he is a true slave.

entries.zh: 然吾與其有言矣，不可不救。」
entries.en: Still I promised him aid and must move."
entries.literal: Yet I had an agreement with him and cannot fail to save him."

entries.zh: 於是命右於陸王劉景、左獨鹿王劉延年等率步騎二萬，將討鮮卑。
entries.en: He ordered Liu Jing and Liu Yannian forward with twenty thousand riders—ostensibly against the Xianbei.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ordered King of the Right Yulu Liu Jing, King of the Left Duliu Liu Yannian, and others to lead twenty thousand foot and horse, about to attack the Xianbei.

entries.zh: 劉宣等固諫曰：「晉為無道，奴隸禦我，是以右賢王猛不勝其忿。
entries.en: Liu Xuan blocked him: "Jin treats us like driven slaves—remember how Right Worthy Meng rose in fury.
entries.literal: Liu Xuan and others firmly remonstrated, saying, "Jin is without the Way; slaves drive us—therefore the Right Worthy King Meng could not bear his rage.

entries.zh: 屬晉綱未馳，大事不遂，右賢塗地，單于之恥也。
entries.en: Jin's grip was still tight then, and our rising failed—our people's blood is still the Shanyu's shame.
entries.literal: When Jin's net had not yet slackened, the great matter did not succeed; the Right Worthy was crushed to earth—it was the Shanyu's shame.

entries.zh: 今司馬氏父子兄弟自相魚肉，此天厭晉德，授之於我。
entries.en: Now the Simas devour their own—Heaven has turned from Jin and hands us the mandate.
entries.literal: Now the Sima father, sons, and brothers devour one another like fish flesh—Heaven tires of Jin's virtue and hands it to us.

entries.zh: 單于積德在躬，為晉人所服，方當興我邦族，復呼韓邪之業，鮮卑、烏丸可以為援，奈何距之而拯仇敵！
entries.en: You already command Jin's awe; rebuild our nation and Huhanye's glory—use the steppe peoples, do not waste your strength saving a foe.
entries.literal: The Shanyu has stored virtue in his person and is obeyed by Jin men; you should raise our tribal nation, restore Huhanye's enterprise—Xianbei and Wuhuan can be allies—how turn them away to rescue an enemy!

entries.zh: 今天假手於我，不可違也。
entries.en: Heaven lends us this chance—we dare not refuse.
entries.literal: Now Heaven lends its hand to us—it cannot be disobeyed.

entries.zh: 違天不祥，逆眾不濟；
entries.en: Defy Heaven and fortune flees; defy your warriors and nothing succeeds;
entries.literal: To disobey Heaven is inauspicious; to oppose the multitude will not succeed;

entries.zh: 天與不取，反受其咎。
entries.en: Reject Heaven's gift and you earn its curse.
entries.literal: Heaven gives and you do not take—instead you receive its blame.

entries.zh: 願單于勿疑。」
entries.en: Do not hesitate, Shanyu."
entries.literal: I beg the Shanyu not to doubt."

entries.zh: 元海曰：「善。
entries.en: Liu Yuan said, "Well spoken.
entries.literal: Yuanhai said, "Good.

entries.zh: 當為崇岡峻阜，何能為培塿乎！
entries.en: We aim to be mountain ranges, not molehills.
entries.literal: We ought to be high ridges and steep mounds—how can we be mere hillocks!

entries.zh: 夫帝王豈有常哉，大禹出於西戎，文王生於東夷，顧惟德所授耳。
entries.en: Thrones never stay fixed: Yu rose from western tribes, Wen from eastern barbarians—virtue alone decides who rules.
entries.literal: For emperors and kings—how can there be constancy? Great Yu came from the western Rong; King Wen was born among the eastern Yi—it depends only on whom virtue invests.

entries.zh: 今見眾十餘萬，皆一當晉十，鼓行而摧亂晉，猶拉枯耳。
entries.en: I command a hundred thousand, each man worth ten Jin soldiers; marching on Luoyang will splinter them like dry twigs.
entries.literal: Now I see a host of over a hundred thousand, each one worth ten Jin soldiers; beating the drum and advancing to crush chaotic Jin is like snapping dead wood.

entries.zh: 上可成漢高之業，下不失為魏氏。
entries.en: Best case I match Han Gaozu; worst I still rival Cao Wei.
entries.literal: Above I can complete Gaozu's enterprise; below I will not fall short of the house of Wei.

entries.zh: 雖然，晉人未必同我。
entries.en: Yet Jin subjects may not flock to us.
entries.literal: Even so, Jin men will not necessarily join me.

entries.zh: 漢有天下世長，恩德結于人心，是以昭烈崎嶇於一州之地，而能抗衡於天下。
entries.en: Han ruled long enough that the people still love its memory—Liu Bei clung to one province yet defied the world.
entries.literal: Han possessed the realm for generations long; kindness and virtue knotted in human hearts; therefore Zhaolie, twisted on one province's ground, could yet resist All-under-Heaven.

entries.zh: 吾又漢氏之甥，約為兄弟，兄亡弟紹，不亦可乎？
entries.en: We are sworn brothers to the Liu house; when the elder line fell should not the younger inherit?
entries.literal: I am moreover Han's nephew by marriage, covenanted as brothers; the elder died and the younger continues—is that not fitting?

entries.zh: 且可稱漢，追尊後主，以懷人望。」
entries.en: Call our state Han, enshrine the last Han emperor, and the hearts of the people will follow."
entries.literal: Moreover one may style the state Han, posthumously honour the last lord, and thereby embrace human hope."

entries.zh: 乃遷于左國城，遠人歸附者數萬。
entries.en: He shifted to Zuoguocheng and tens of thousands of far wanderers joined him.
entries.literal: Thereupon he moved to Zuoguocheng, and distant people who attached numbered in the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 永興元年，元海乃為壇於南郊，僭即漢王位，下令曰：「昔我太祖高皇帝以神武應期，廓開大業。
entries.en: In Yongxing year one Liu Yuan built an altar in the southern suburb, usurped the title King of Han, and issued an order: "Formerly our Grand Progenitor, the High Emperor, answered the age with divine arms and opened a vast enterprise.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongxing Yuanhai then built an altar south of the suburbs and usurped accession as King of Han, ordering, "Formerly our Grand Progenitor the High Emperor, by divine martialness answered the period and opened the great enterprise.

entries.zh: 太宗孝文皇帝重以明德，升平漢道。
entries.en: Han Wendi lifted the realm with pure virtue.
entries.literal: The Founding Ancestor, Emperor Wen of Filial Piety, again by bright virtue elevated the Han Way to peace.

entries.zh: 世宗孝武皇帝拓土攘夷，地過唐日。
entries.en: Han Wudi widened the map beyond even Tang's reach.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Filial Piety, Shizong, expanded the soil and pushed the Yi; the land passed Tang days.

entries.zh: 中宗孝宣皇帝搜揚俊乂，多士盈朝。
entries.en: Han Xuandi filled court with talent he sought out.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety, Zhongzong, searched out and raised the excellent, so that many shi filled the court.

entries.zh: 是我祖宗道邁三王，功高五帝，故卜年倍于夏商，卜世過於姬氏。
entries.en: So Han virtue outshone the Three Kings and merit topped the Five Thearchs—its allotted years doubled Xia and Shang, its generations outlasted Zhou.
entries.literal: Thus our forefathers' Way overtook the Three Kings and merit topped the Five Thearchs; therefore the divined years doubled Xia and Shang, and the divined generations surpassed the Ji clan.

entries.zh: 而元成多僻，哀平短祚，賊臣王莽，滔天篡逆。
entries.en: Later emperors slipped; Ai and Ping died young; Wang Mang usurped the throne.
entries.literal: Yet Yuancheng were many depraved, Ai and Ping had short fates, and the traitorous minister Wang Mang swelled to heaven and usurped in rebellion.

entries.zh: 我世祖光武皇帝誕資聖武，恢復鴻基，祀漢配天，不失舊物，俾三光晦而復明，神器幽而復顯。
entries.en: Guangwu restored Han, realigned heaven and earth, and brought back the sun, moon, and stars.
entries.literal: Our Shizu, Emperor Guangwu of the Han, was born with sacred martialness, restored the great foundation, sacrificed to Han and matched Heaven, not losing old tokens, so that the three luminaries, having darkened, again brightened, and the divine vessel, having been hidden, again appeared.

entries.zh: 顯宗孝明皇帝、肅宗孝章皇帝累葉重暉，炎光再闡。
entries.en: Ming and Zhang emperors relit Han's fire generation after generation.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming of Filial Piety, Xianzong, and Emperor Zhang of Filial Piety, Suzong, piled generation on generation of doubled radiance, and the fiery light again blazed.

entries.zh: 自和安已後，皇綱漸頹，天步艱難，國統頻絕。
entries.en: After He and An the dynasty frayed, heaven's course faltered, and the succession snapped again and again.
entries.literal: From He and An onward the imperial net gradually collapsed, heaven's step was hard, and the state's thread repeatedly broke.

entries.zh: 黃巾海沸於九州，群閹毒流于四海，董卓因之肆其猖勃，曹操父子凶逆相尋。
entries.en: Yellow Turbans boiled across the nine regions, eunuchs poisoned every quarter, Dong Zhuo ran wild, and the Caos seized power in turn.
entries.literal: Yellow Turbans seethed like sea foam in the Nine Provinces; packs of eunuchs poisoned the four seas; Dong Zhuo thereupon let loose his raging arrogance; Cao Cao father and son followed each other in vicious rebellion.

entries.zh: 故孝湣委棄萬國，昭烈播越岷蜀，冀否終有泰，旋軫舊京。
entries.en: Han emperors fled the realm; Liu Bei held Shu, hoping fate would turn and Luoyang return.
entries.literal: Therefore Xiaomin cast aside the myriad states, and Zhaolie wandered Min and Shu, hoping that the bad end would have a good turn and the capital could be turned again.

entries.zh: 何圖天未悔禍，後帝窘辱。
entries.en: Yet heaven still refused mercy and the last Han child met humiliation.
entries.literal: Who could have thought Heaven had not yet repented the disaster, and the later emperor met shame and insult.

entries.zh: 自社稷淪喪，宗廟之不血食四十年於茲矣。
entries.en: Forty years now the Han shrines have gone hungry.
entries.literal: From the altars' ruin and loss, the ancestral temples have gone without blood sacrifice for forty years to this point.

entries.zh: 今天誘其衷，悔禍皇漢，使司馬氏父子兄弟迭相殘滅。
entries.en: Now heaven stirs pity, repents toward Han, and sets the Simas at one another's throats.
entries.literal: Now Heaven opens their bosoms, repents the disaster toward august Han, and makes the Sima father, sons, and brothers destroy one another in turn.

entries.zh: 黎庶塗炭，靡所控告。
entries.en: The common folk burn in mud and ash with no court to hear them.
entries.literal: The black-haired people are smeared in mud and charcoal, with nowhere to cry their complaint.

entries.zh: 孤今猥為群公所推，紹修三祖之業。
entries.en: I am pressed by you lords to renew the work of Han's three founders.
entries.literal: I, alone, am now vulgarly pushed by the host of dukes to continue and repair the enterprise of the three ancestors.

entries.zh: 顧茲尪暗，戰惶靡厝。
entries.en: I am small and weak and tremble at the charge.
entries.literal: Looking at this dim dullness, I tremble and have no place to put myself.

entries.zh: 但以大恥未雪，社稷無主，銜膽棲冰，勉從群議。」
entries.en: Yet because the great shame remains unavenged and the altars of state have no master, I swallow gall and dwell on ice, reluctantly following the counsel of the multitude."
entries.literal: Yet because the great shame is not yet washed away and the altars lack a master, holding gall and dwelling on ice, I reluctantly follow the host's deliberation."

entries.zh: 乃赦其境內，年號元熙，追尊劉禪為孝懷皇帝，立漢高祖以下三祖五宗神主而祭之。
entries.en: He proclaimed an amnesty within his territory, adopted the era name Yuanxi, posthumously honored Liu Shan as Emperor Xiaohuai, and established and sacrificed to the spirit tablets of Han Gaozu and the other emperors among Han's three founding ancestors and five honored ancestors.
entries.literal: Thereupon he amnestied his territory, adopted the era name Yuanxi, posthumously honored Liu Shan as Emperor Xiaohuai, and established and sacrificed to the spirit tablets of Han Gaozu and the other emperors among Han's three founding ancestors and five honored ancestors.

entries.zh: 立其妻呼延氏為王后。
entries.en: He named Lady Huyan queen.
entries.literal: He established his wife Lady Huyan as queen.

entries.zh: 置百官，以劉宣為丞相，崔游為御史大夫，劉宏為太尉，其餘拜授各有差。
entries.en: He formed a government: Liu Xuan chancellor, Cui You censor-in-chief, Liu Hong grand commandant, and the rest ranked by merit.
entries.literal: He set up the hundred offices, making Liu Xuan chancellor, Cui You imperial counsellor, Liu Hong grand commandant, and the rest received appointments each according to rank.

entries.zh: 東嬴公騰使將軍聶玄討之，戰於大陵，玄師敗績，騰懼，率并州二萬餘戶下山東，遂所在為寇。
entries.en: Sima Teng sent Nie Xuan against him, lost at Daling, then fled Bing with twenty thousand families eastward, leaving the province to chaos.
entries.literal: Dongying Duke Teng sent General Nie Xuan to attack him; they fought at Daling; Xuan's army was routed; Teng, in fear, led more than twenty thousand households of Bingzhou down to Shandong, and thereupon everywhere became bandits.

entries.zh: 元海遣其建武將軍劉曜寇太原、泫氏、屯留、長子、中都，皆陷之。
entries.en: Liu Yuan sent Liu Yao to storm Taiyuan, Xuan, Tunliu, Changzi, and Zhongdu—all fell.
entries.literal: Yuanhai sent his General Who Establishes Might Liu Yao to raid Taiyuan, Xuan, Tunliu, Changzi, and Zhongdu—all fell.

entries.zh: 二年，騰又遣司馬瑜、周良、石鮮等討之，次於離石汾城。
entries.en: Next year Sima Teng sent Sima Yu, Zhou Liang, and Shi Xian to Lishi's Fencheng.
entries.literal: In the second year Teng again sent Sima Yu, Zhou Liang, Shi Xian, and others to attack him, halting at Fencheng of Lishi.

entries.zh: 元海遣其武牙將軍劉欽等六軍距瑜等，四戰，瑜皆敗，欽振旅而歸。
entries.en: Liu Yuan sent Liu Qin with six hosts; after four battles Jin fled and Liu Qin marched home in triumph.
entries.literal: Yuanhai sent his General Who Martial Fangs Liu Qin and six armies to oppose Yu and the others; after four battles Yu was defeated each time, and Qin returned with drums beating.

entries.zh: 是歲，離石大饑，遷于黎亭，以就邸閣穀，留其太尉劉宏、護軍馬景守離石，使大司農卜豫運糧以給之。
entries.en: Famine struck Lishi, so the court moved to Liting granaries while Liu Hong and Ma Jing held Lishi and Bu Yu shipped grain.
entries.literal: That year Lishi suffered great famine; they moved to Liting to draw on granary grain, leaving Grand Commandant Liu Hong and Protector Ma Jing to guard Lishi, and ordered Grand Minister of Agriculture Bu Yu to transport grain to supply them.

entries.zh: 以其前將軍劉景為使持節、征討大都督、大將軍，要擊并州刺史劉琨于版橋，為琨所敗，琨遂據晉陽。
entries.en: He sent Liu Jing to ambush Liu Kun at Banqiao; Liu Kun crushed him and took Jinyang.
entries.literal: He made his former general Liu Jing credential-holder, grand commander for conquest, grand general, and intercepted Bing Governor Liu Kun at Banqiao; he was defeated by Kun, and Kun thereupon occupied Jinyang.

entries.zh: 其侍中劉殷、王育進諫元海曰：「殿下自起兵以來，漸已一周，而顓守偏方，王威未震。
entries.en: Liu Yin and Wang Yu urged him: "A year has passed and you still hug one corner—your majesty has not yet thundered abroad.
entries.literal: His attendants Liu Yin and Wang Yu advanced remonstrance to Yuanhai, saying, "Since Your Highness raised troops it has gradually been a full cycle, yet you only hold a corner; kingly awe has not yet shaken.

entries.zh: 誠能命將四出，決機一擲，梟劉琨，定河東，建帝號，鼓行而南，克長安而都之，以關中之眾席捲洛陽，如指掌耳。
entries.en: Send four columns, kill Liu Kun, secure Hedong, proclaim the throne, march on Chang'an, then sweep from the passes to Luoyang like turning your hand.
entries.literal: If you truly can order generals to go out on four sides, cast the die once, behead Liu Kun, settle Hedong, establish an imperial title, beat the drum southward, take Chang'an as capital, then with the hosts of Guanzhong roll up Luoyang—it is like turning the palm.

entries.zh: 此高皇帝之所以創啟鴻基，克殄強楚者也。」
entries.en: That was Gaozu's road to crush Chu."
entries.literal: This is how the High Emperor opened the great foundation and utterly destroyed mighty Chu."

entries.zh: 元海悅曰：「此孤心也。」
entries.en: Liu Yuan cried, "That is my own mind too."
entries.literal: Yuanhai, pleased, said, "This is Our heart."

entries.zh: 遂進據河東，攻寇蒲阪、平陽，皆陷之。
entries.en: He drove into Hedong, stormed Puyin and Pingyang, and took both.
entries.literal: Thereupon he advanced and occupied Hedong, attacked and raided Puyin and Pingyang, and both fell.

entries.zh: 元海遂入都蒲子，河東、平陽屬縣壘壁盡降。
entries.en: He moved the capital to Puzi; every fort in Hedong and Pingyang opened its gates.
entries.literal: Yuanhai thereupon entered and made his capital at Puzi; fortified camps of the counties of Hedong and Pingyang all surrendered.

entries.zh: 時汲桑起兵趙魏，上郡四部鮮卑陸逐延、氏酋大單于征、東萊王彌及石勒等並相次降之，元海悉署其官爵，
entries.en: Ji Sang rose in Zhao-Wei; Xianbei, Di, Wang Mi, and Shi Le came over in turn; Liu Yuan handed each a title.
entries.literal: At that time Ji Sang raised troops in Zhao and Wei; Lüzhuyan of the four Xianbei sections of Shangjun, Di chief Great-Shanyu Zheng, Wang Mi of Donglai, and Shi Le in succession each surrendered to him; Yuanhai all appointed their offices and noble ranks,

entries.zh: 劉宣，字士則。
entries.en: Liu Xuan, courtesy name Shize.
entries.literal: Liu Xuan, style Shize.

entries.zh: 朴鈍少言，好學修潔。
entries.en: He was quiet, plain-spoken, bookish, and scrupulously clean.
entries.literal: He was plain, dull, and sparing of speech, loved study and cultivated purity.

entries.zh: 師事樂安孫炎，沈精積思，不舍晝夜，好《毛詩》、《左氏傳》。
entries.en: He studied under Sun Yan of Le'an with obsessive focus, loving the Mao Odes and Zuo commentary.
entries.literal: He took as teacher Sun Yan of Le'an, sinking his essence and piling thought, not quitting day or night, loving Mao's Odes and Zuo's Tradition.

entries.zh: 炎每歎之曰：「宣若遇漢武，當逾于金日磾也。」
entries.en: Sun Yan often sighed over him, saying, "Had Xuan met Emperor Wu of Han, he would have surpassed Jin Midi."
entries.literal: Yan always sighed of him, saying, "If Xuan had met Han Wudi, he would have surpassed Jin Midi."

entries.zh: 學成而返，不出門閭蓋數年。
entries.en: When his course finished he stayed home for years without stepping past his gate.
entries.literal: When study was completed he returned, not going out his gate for several years.

entries.zh: 每讀《漢書》，至《蕭何》、《鄧禹傳》，未曾不反覆詠之，曰：「大丈夫若遭二祖，終不令二公獨擅美於前矣。」
entries.en: Reading the Book of Han chapters on Xiao He and Deng Yu he would chant, "Had I served Han's founders I would not leave those two alone the laurels."
entries.literal: Whenever he read the Han Documents, reaching the treatises on Xiao He and Deng Yu, he never failed repeatedly to intone them, saying, "If a great husband met the two Founders, in the end he would not let the two dukes alone monopolize beauty before them."

entries.zh: 并州刺史王廣言之于武帝，帝召見，嘉其占對，因曰：「吾未見宣，謂廣言虛耳。
entries.en: Bing governor Wang Guang praised him to Sima Yan, who interviewed Liu Xuan and said, "I thought Wang Guang exaggerated.
entries.literal: The Governor of Bing, Wang Guang, spoke of him to Emperor Wu; the Emperor summoned and saw him, praised his answers, and therefore said, "We had not yet seen Xuan and thought Guang's words empty.

entries.zh: 今見其進止風儀，真所謂如圭如璋，觀其性質，足能撫集本部。」
entries.en: Seeing his carriage I know the proverb 'like jade tablets'—he can truly pacify his people."
entries.literal: Now seeing his advance and retreat, wind and bearing, he is truly called like jade, like fine jade; observing his nature and substance, he is sufficient to soothe and gather his native command."

entries.zh: 乃以宣為右部都督，特給赤幛曲蓋。
entries.en: Sima Yan named him right-section commander with crimson pennant and curved awning.
entries.literal: Thereupon he made Xuan commander of the right section, specially granting red pennant and curved canopy.

entries.zh: 蒞官清恪，所部懷之。
entries.en: He governed cleanly and his tribes loved him.
entries.literal: When he took office he was pure and scrupulous; those under his command cherished him.

entries.zh: 元海即王位，宣之謀也，故特荷尊重，勳戚莫二，軍國內外靡不專之。
entries.en: Liu Yuan's kingship was Liu Xuan's design, so he alone enjoyed supreme trust—no kinsman or minister rivalled his authority.
entries.literal: When Yuanhai assumed the kingly title it was Xuan's stratagem; therefore he alone bore utmost respect; among meritorious kin there was no second; none within or without the army and state did not defer to him.

entries.zh: 劉元海（子和） 劉宣
entries.en: Liu Yuanhai (with his son He) and Liu Xuan.
entries.literal: Liu Yuanhai (son: He) and Liu Xuan.

entries.en: (His son He)
entries.literal: (Son: He)

entries.zh: 劉宣
entries.en: Liu Xuan.
entries.literal: Liu Xuan.

entries.zh: 慕容廆，字弈洛瑰，昌黎棘城鮮卑人也。
entries.en: A Xianbei leader from Jicheng in Changli, style Yiluogui.
entries.literal: Murong Hui, courtesy name Yiluogui, was a Xianbei of Jicheng in Changli.

entries.zh: 其先有熊氏之苗裔，世居北夷，邑于紫蒙之野，號曰東胡。
entries.en: They claimed Youxiong ancestry, lived beyond the frontier at Zimeng, and were known as Eastern Hu.
entries.literal: His ancestors were descendants of the Youxiong clan; for generations they dwelt among the northern tribes, built their seat in the wilds of Zimeng, and were called Eastern Hu.

entries.zh: 其後與匈奴並盛，控弦之士二十餘萬，風俗官號與匈奴略同。
entries.en: They matched the Xiongnu in strength—two hundred thousand horsemen with parallel customs.
entries.literal: Later they rose alongside the Xiongnu with more than two hundred thousand bowmen; customs and titles broadly matched the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 秦漢之際為匈奴所敗，分保鮮卑山，因以為號。
entries.en: Early Han defeat drove them onto Xianbei Mountain and gave them their tribal name.
entries.literal: At the Qin-Han transition the Xiongnu defeated them; they split off to hold Mount Xianbei and took that name.

entries.zh: 曾祖莫護跋，魏初率其諸部入居遼西，從宣帝伐公孫氏有功，拜率義王，始建國於棘城之北。
entries.en: Mohuba earned Wei's trust against the Gongsuns and planted Murong power north of Jicheng.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Mohuba in early Wei led his tribes into western Liaoxi, followed Emperor Xuan on campaign against the Gongsun clan, earned merit, was enfeoffed Prince of Shuaiyi, and first founded a state north of Jicheng.

entries.zh: 時燕代多冠步搖冠，莫護跋見而好之，乃斂發襲冠，諸部因呼之為步搖，其後音訛，遂為慕容焉。
entries.en: A hat nicknamed him Buyao until listeners corrupted it into Murong.
entries.literal: In Yan and Dai many wore buyao crowns; Mohuba admired them, tucked his hair under such a crown, and the tribes called him Buyao—later slip of the tongue turned the name into Murong.

entries.zh: 或云慕二儀之德，繼三光之容，遂以慕容為氏。
entries.en: Another etymology ties Murong to reverence for Heaven, Earth, and the luminaries.
entries.literal: Another tale says they revered the virtue of the Two Principles and the radiance of the Three Lights, hence the surname Murong.

entries.zh: 祖木延，左賢王。
entries.en: Muyan served as Left Wise Prince.
entries.literal: His grandfather Muyan held the title Left Wise Prince.

entries.zh: 父涉歸，以全柳城之功，進拜鮮卑單于，遷邑於遼東北，於是漸慕諸夏之風矣。
entries.en: Shegui won the Shanyu title for Liucheng and guided the clan toward Chinese ways.
entries.literal: His father Shegui, for preserving Liucheng intact, was promoted Xianbei Shanyu and moved the seat northeast into Liaodong; there they gradually admired Central Plains refinement.

entries.zh: 廆幼而魁岸，美姿貌，身長八尺，雄傑有大度。
entries.en: Even young he stood eight chi tall—striking, heroic, broad.
entries.literal: From youth Hui was imposing and handsome, eight chi tall, heroic and magnanimous.

entries.zh: 安北將軍張華雅有知人之鑒，廆童丱時往謁之，華甚歎異，謂曰：「君至長必為命世之器，匡難濟時者也。」
entries.en: Zhang Hua said, "When you grow up you will be an instrument for the age—one who rectifies disaster and aids the times."
entries.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Zhang Hua was famed for judging men; while still a boy Hui visited him. Hua marveled and said, "When grown you will be an instrument for the age—one who rectifies disaster and aids the times."

entries.zh: 因以所服簪幘遺廆，結殷勤而別。
entries.en: He gave Hui his cap pin and turban as farewell gifts.
entries.literal: Thereupon he gave Hui his own hairpin and turban as gifts and parted with earnest warmth.

entries.zh: 涉歸死，其弟耐篡位，將謀殺廆，廆亡潛以避禍。
entries.en: Uncle Nai seized power and hunted him until kinsmen restored Hui.
entries.literal: When Shegui died, his younger brother Nai seized the throne and plotted to murder Hui; Hui fled into hiding to escape harm.

entries.zh: 後國人殺耐，迎廆立之。
entries.en: The tribe slew Nai and enthroned Hui.
entries.literal: Later the tribes killed Nai and welcomed Hui to the throne.

entries.zh: 初，涉歸有憾于宇文鮮卑，廆將修先君之怨，表請討之。
entries.en: He sought imperial blessing to avenge Shegui's feud with the Yuwen.
entries.literal: At first Shegui had quarreled with the Yuwen Xianbei; Hui meant to settle his father's score and memorialized for permission to attack.

entries.zh: 武帝弗許。
entries.en: The western Jin court refused.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu forbade it.

entries.zh: 廆怒，入寇遼西，殺略甚眾。
entries.en: He lashed out with raids across western Liaoxi.
entries.literal: Angered, Hui raided western Liaoxi and slaughtered widely.

entries.zh: 帝遣幽州諸軍討廆，戰於肥如，廆眾大敗。
entries.en: Imperial troops routed him at Feiru.
entries.literal: The emperor dispatched Youzhou forces against him; they fought at Feiru and Hui's army was routed.

entries.zh: 自後復掠昌黎，每歲不絕。
entries.en: He kept harassing Changli afterward.
entries.literal: Afterward he again pillaged Changli year after year without cease.

entries.zh: 又率眾東伐扶余，扶余王依慮自殺，廆夷其國城，驅萬餘人而歸。
entries.en: He shattered Buyeo, drove its king to suicide, and dragged captives home.
entries.literal: He also led hosts east against Buyeo; King Yilü of Buyeo killed himself; Hui leveled the capital, drove off ten thousand captives, and returned.

entries.zh: 東夷校尉何龕遣督護賈沈將迎立依慮之子為王，廆遣其將孫丁率騎邀之。
entries.en: He Kan tried to crown a new Buyeo king while Murong ambushed the escort.
entries.literal: Colonel of the Eastern Yi He Kan sent protector Jia Shen to install Yilü's son as king; Hui sent general Sun Ding with cavalry to intercept.

entries.zh: 沈力戰斬丁，遂復扶余之國。
entries.en: Jia Shen killed Sun Ding and restored Buyeo.
entries.literal: Shen fought hard, beheaded Ding, and restored Buyeo's kingdom.

entries.zh: 廆謀於其眾曰：「吾先公以來世奉中國，且華裔理殊，強弱固別，豈能與晉競乎？
entries.en: He urged submission to Jin, saying, "Since our forefathers we have honored China; Chinese and barbarian orders differ and strength is uneven—how can we vie with Jin?
entries.literal: Hui consulted his followers: "Since our forefathers we have honored China; Chinese and barbarian orders differ and strength is uneven—how can we vie with Jin?

entries.zh: 何為不和以害吾百姓邪！」
entries.en: Why not make peace rather than harm our people!"
entries.literal: Why not make peace rather than harm our people!"

entries.zh: 乃遣使來降。
entries.en: He sent envoys west to surrender.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys to surrender.

entries.zh: 帝嘉之，拜為鮮卑都督。
entries.en: The court named him commander over the Xianbei.
entries.literal: The emperor praised him and appointed him Xianbei Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 廆致敬於東夷府，巾衣詣門，抗士大夫之禮。
entries.en: He appeared at He Kan's yamen in scholar dress.
entries.literal: Hui paid respects at the Eastern Yi headquarters, wearing civilian cap and robe at the gate like a scholar-official.

entries.zh: 何龕嚴兵引見，廆乃改服戎衣而入。
entries.en: When Kan lined up troops, Hui donned armor instead.
entries.literal: Kan arrayed troops for the audience; Hui changed into armor before entering.

entries.zh: 人問其故，廆曰：「主人不以禮，賓復何為哉！」
entries.en: He said, "If the host shows no courtesy, what should a guest do!"
entries.literal: Asked why, Hui said, "If the host shows no courtesy, what should a guest do!"

entries.zh: 龕聞而慚之，彌加敬憚。
entries.en: Kan swallowed his pride and deferred.
entries.literal: Kan, ashamed, treated him with deeper awe.

entries.zh: 時東胡宇文鮮卑段部以廆威德日廣，懼有吞併之計，因為寇掠，往來不絕。
entries.en: Yuwen and Duan rivals feared annexation and raided endlessly.
entries.literal: Then the Yuwen and Duan branches of Eastern Hu Xianbei, fearing Hui's spreading might meant annexation, raided ceaselessly.

entries.zh: 廆卑辭厚幣以撫之。
entries.en: He bought quiet with gifts and soft words.
entries.literal: Hui answered them with humble words and lavish gifts.

entries.zh: 懷帝蒙塵于平陽，王浚承制以廆為散騎常侍、冠軍將軍、前鋒大都督、大單于，廆不受。
entries.en: Wang Jun's honors could not buy him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Huai suffered at Pingyang, Wang Jun by interim authority offered Hui supernumerary attendant, Champion General, Forward Marshal, Great Shanyu—Hui declined.

entries.zh: 建興中，湣帝遣使拜廆鎮軍將軍、昌黎、遼東二國公。
entries.en: Emperor Min offered guard-general rank and twin ducal patents.
entries.literal: During Jianxing Emperor Min sent envoys to appoint Hui General Who Guards the Army and duke of Changli and Liaodong.

entries.zh: 建武初，元帝承制拜廆假節、散騎常侍、都督遼左雜夷流人諸軍事、龍驤將軍、大單于、昌黎公，廆讓而不受。
entries.en: Early in Jianwu, Emperor Yuan, acting under provisional authority, appointed Hui Bearer of the Staff, Supernumerary Palace Attendant, commander of the Liaozuo mixed tribes and displaced people, General of Dragon Soaring, Great Shanyu, and Duke of Changli; Hui declined and would not accept.
entries.literal: Early in Jianwu Yuan-di by interim authority appointed Hui Bearer of Staff, Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Area Commander of Liaozuo miscellaneous barbarians and displaced persons, General of Dragon Soaring, Great Shanyu, Duke of Changli—Hui demurred.

entries.zh: 征虜將軍魯昌說廆曰：「今兩京傾沒，天子蒙塵，琅邪承制江東，實人命所系。
entries.en: Lu Chang argued only imperial seals could awe rival tribes, saying, "Both capitals have fallen and the Son of Heaven wanders; Langye rules Jiangdong by interim decree—the mandate of life and death rests there.
entries.literal: General Who Conquers the Enemy Lu Chang urged Hui: "Both capitals have fallen and the Son of Heaven wanders; Langye rules Jiangdong by interim decree—the mandate of life and death rests there.

entries.zh: 明公雄據海朔，跨總一方，而諸部猶怙眾稱兵，未遵道化者，蓋以官非王命，又自以為強。
entries.en: Murong prestige needed Jiankang's mandate.
entries.literal: My lord towers over the northern sea yet tribes still bear arms because your offices lack imperial seals and each thinks himself strongest.

entries.zh: 今宜通使琅邪，勸承大統，然後敷宣帝命，以伐有罪，誰敢不從！」
entries.en: Send envoys to Langye urging enthronement, then proclaim imperial orders and punish the guilty—who would disobey?"
entries.literal: Send envoys to Langye urging enthronement, then proclaim imperial orders and punish the guilty—who would disobey?"

entries.zh: 廆善之，乃遣其長史王濟浮海勸進。
entries.en: He sent Wang Ji across the sea to urge enthronement.
entries.literal: Hui approved and dispatched chief clerk Wang Ji by sea to urge Yuan-di to take the throne.

entries.zh: 及帝即尊位，遣謁者陶遼重申前命，授廆將軍、單于，廆固辭公封。
entries.en: Ming's envoy Tao Liao could not force ducal robes on him.
entries.literal: After the emperor assumed the throne, envoy Tao Liao renewed earlier commissions as general and Shanyu; Hui firmly declined ducal investiture.

entries.zh: 天祚有晉，挺授英傑。
entries.en: Divine aid sustained Jin survivors.
entries.literal: Heaven blesses Jin and raises heroes.

entries.zh: 車騎將軍慕容廆自弱冠蒞國，忠於王室，明允恭肅，志在立勳。
entries.en: Petition praised Murong youth and loyalty.
entries.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Murong Hui since youth held his country loyal to the royal house—trustworthy, reverent, resolved on merit.

entries.zh: 屬海內分崩，皇輿遷幸，元皇中興，初唱大業，肅祖繼統，蕩平江外。
entries.en: Southern courts sustained mandate.
entries.literal: As the realm shattered and the imperial carriage shifted, Yuan-di revived enterprise midstream and Su zu continued, sweeping peace beyond the river.

entries.zh: 廆雖限以山海，隔以羯寇，翹首引領，系心京師，常假寤寐，欲憂國忘身。
entries.en: Murong fixation on restoration despite barriers.
entries.literal: Though mountains and seas fence Hui from Jie bandits he cranes his neck toward capital, hearts tied to Luoyang, sleepless with longing to forget self for state.

entries.zh: 貢篚相尋，連舟載路，戎不稅駕，動成義舉。
entries.en: Steady tribute demonstrated virtue.
entries.literal: Tribute baskets followed one another and barges jammed the route—without pausing harness he acted righteously.

entries.zh: 今羯寇滔天，怙其丑類，樹基趙、魏，跨略燕、齊。
entries.en: Shi's realm sprawled north.
entries.literal: Now Jie flood heaven; relying on rabble they rooted Zhao-Wei and span Yan-Qi.

entries.zh: 廆雖率義眾，誅討大逆，然管仲相齊，猶曰寵不足以禦下，況廆輔翼王室，有匡霸之功，而位卑爵輕，九命未加，非所以寵異籓翰，敦獎殊勳者也。
entries.en: Petition argued Murong deserved kingly rank to command allies.
entries.literal: Though Hui leads righteous hosts punishing great rebellion, even Guan Zhong aiding Qi said petty favors cannot command subordinates—how much less Hui aiding royal house with hegemonic merit yet low rank and light fiefs without nine honors—not how to exalt a frontier pillar or reward extraordinary deeds.

entries.zh: 毖之與三國謀伐廆也，瞻固諫以為不可，毖不從。
entries.en: Zhan warned against Cui Bi's triple alliance; Bi ignored him.
entries.literal: When Bi plotted with three states to strike Murong Hui, Zhan remonstrated firmly that it must not be done—Bi refused to listen.

entries.zh: 及毖奔敗，瞻隨眾降於廆。
entries.en: After Bi's rout Zhan submitted with the refugees.
entries.literal: When Bi fled in defeat Zhan joined the crowd surrendering to Hui.

entries.zh: 廆署為將軍，瞻稱疾不起。
entries.en: Murong named him general; Zhan feigned sickness.
entries.literal: Hui appointed him general but Zhan pleaded illness and would not take office.

entries.zh: 廆敬其姿器，數臨候之，撫其心曰：「君之疾在此，不在餘也。
entries.en: Murong pressed him personally, saying, "Your ailment lies here, nowhere else.
entries.literal: Hui respected his stature and repeatedly visited, pressing a hand to his chest: "Your ailment lies here, nowhere else.

entries.zh: 今天子播越，四海分崩，蒼生紛擾，莫知所系，孤思與諸君匡復帝室，翦鯨豕於二京，迎天子于吳、會，廓清八表，侔勳古烈，此孤之心也，孤之願也。
entries.en: Murong proclaimed plans to sweep bandits from Luoyang and Chang'an and escort Jin home.
entries.literal: Today the Son of Heaven wanders, the realm splinters, the people drift anchorless—I desire with you gentlemen to restore the imperial house, cut whale-like foes from both capitals, welcome the emperor at Wu and Kuaiji, cleanse the eight quarters, rival ancient heroes—that is my heart and wish.

entries.zh: 君中州大族，冠冕之餘，宜痛心疾首，枕戈待旦，柰何以華夷之異，有懷介然。
entries.en: He urged Zhan to shed ethnic prejudice for restoration.
entries.literal: You stem from great houses of the Central Plain, remnants of titled courts—you should ache with rage and sleep beside spears awaiting dawn—how can Chinese versus barbarian divide your loyalty?

entries.zh: 且大禹出於西羌，文王生於東夷，但問志略何如耳，豈以殊俗不可降心乎！」
entries.en: Moreover Yu the Great rose from western Qiang; King Wen was born among eastern Yi—only ambition matters—must foreign customs block sincere hearts!"
entries.literal: Moreover Yu the Great rose from western Qiang; King Wen was born among eastern Yi—only ambition matters—must foreign customs block sincere hearts!"

entries.zh: 瞻仍辭疾篤，廆深不平之。
entries.en: Zhan stayed "ill"; Murong grew bitter.
entries.literal: Zhan still pleaded grave illness; Hui nursed deep resentment.

entries.zh: 瞻又與宋該有隙，該陰勸廆除之。
entries.en: Song Gai baited Murong to execute Zhan.
entries.literal: Zhan also quarreled with Song Gai; Gai secretly urged Hui to kill him.

entries.zh: 瞻聞其言，彌不自安，遂以憂死。
entries.en: Word of the plot terrified Zhan to death.
entries.literal: When Zhan heard he grew ever more fearful and died of anxiety.

entries.zh: 時二京傾覆，幽、冀淪陷，廆刑政修明，虛懷引納，流亡士庶多繈負歸之。
entries.en: Clear rule drew refugee elites carrying children on their backs.
entries.literal: As both capitals collapsed and You-Ji fell, Hui governed clearly and welcomed exiles; scholars and commoners arrived carrying children on their backs.

entries.zh: 廆乃立郡以統流人，冀州人為冀陽郡，豫州人為成周郡，青州人為營丘郡，并州人為唐國郡。
entries.en: Hui therefore established commanderies to govern the displaced people: those from Ji Province became Jiyang Commandery, those from Yu Province Chengzhou Commandery, those from Qing Province Yingqiu Commandery, and those from Bing Province Tangguo Commandery.
entries.literal: He founded commanderies for the displaced—Jiyang for Ji refugees, Chengzhou for Yu, Yingqiu for Qing, Tangguo for Bing.

entries.zh: 於是推舉賢才，委以庶政，以河東裴嶷、代郡魯昌、北平陽耽為謀主，北海逢羨、廣平遊邃、北平西方虔、渤海封抽、西河宋奭、河東裴開為股肱，渤海封弈、平原宋該、安定皇甫岌、蘭陵繆愷以文章才俊任居樞要，會稽硃左車、太山胡毋翼、魯國孔纂以舊德清重引為賓友，平原劉贊儒學該通，引為東庠祭酒，其世子皝率國胄束修受業焉。
entries.en: He therefore promoted men of talent and entrusted them with government: Pei Yi of Hedong, Lu Chang of Dai, and Yang Dan of Beiping served as his chief advisers; Feng Xian of Beihai, You Sui of Guangping, Xifang Qian of Beiping, Feng Chou of Bohai, Song Shi of Xihe, and Pei Kai of Hedong were his arms and legs; Feng Yi of Bohai, Song Gai of Pingyuan, Huangfu Ji of Anding, and Miao Kai of Lanling, all distinguished for literary talent and ability, held key posts; Zhu Zuoche of Kuaiji, Humu Yi of Taishan, and Kong Zuan of Lu, respected for their old virtue and pure standing, were brought in as guests and friends; and Liu Zan of Pingyuan, broadly learned in the classics, was appointed libationer of the Eastern Academy, where his heir Murong Huang led the sons of the state in bringing tuition gifts and receiving instruction.
entries.literal: He promoted worthies to routine administration: Hedong Pei Yi, Dai commandery Lu Chang, Beiping Yang Dan as strategists; Beihai Feng Xian, Guangping You Sui, Beiping Xifang Qian, Bohai Feng Chou, Xihe Song Shi, Hedong Pei Kai as arms and legs; Bohai Feng Yi, Pingyuan Song Gai, Anding Huangfu Ji, Lanling Miao Kai held literary portfolios; Kuaiji Zhu Zuoche, Taishan Humu Yi, Lu state Kong Zuan served as honored guests; Pingyuan Liu Zan's erudition made him Libationer of the eastern school where heir Huang studied.

entries.zh: 廆覽政之暇，親臨聽之，於是路有頌聲，禮讓興矣。
entries.en: He audited the school himself until courtesy songs filled the roads.
entries.literal: When governance permitted, Hui attended lectures himself; songs of praise spread and courtesy flourished.

entries.zh: 裴嶷，字文冀，河東聞喜人也。
entries.en: Pei Yi bio opens—style Wenji, Hedong Wenxi.
entries.literal: Pei Yi, courtesy name Wenji, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.

entries.zh: 父昶，司隸校尉。
entries.en: Father Pei Chang held metropolitan colonel rank.
entries.literal: His father Chang had been Colonel Director of Retainers.

entries.zh: 嶷清方有幹略，累遷至中書侍郎，轉給事黃門郎、滎陽太守。
entries.en: Yi was upright, principled, and capable in administration; he rose through repeated promotions to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, then became Yellow-Gate Gentleman and governor of Xingyang.
entries.literal: Yi was upright and capable, rising to gentleman of the palace secretariat, then Huangmen gent., governor of Xingyang.

entries.zh: 屬天下亂，嶷兄武先為玄菟太守，嶷遂求為昌黎太守。
entries.en: He pursued Changli post near Murong.
entries.literal: As the realm collapsed his elder brother Wu first governed Xuandu; Yi sought appointment as Changli governor.

entries.zh: 至郡，久之，武卒，嶷被征，乃將武子開送喪俱南。
entries.en: Death recalled him with nephew Kai.
entries.literal: Long after reaching the commandery Wu died; Yi was recalled—escorting Wu's son Kai south for mourning.

entries.zh: 既達遼西，道路梗塞，乃與開投廆。
entries.en: Liaoxi obstruction drove him to Murong.
entries.literal: Reaching Liaoxi the roads were blocked so he and Kai joined Murong Hui.

entries.zh: 時諸流寓之士見廆草創，並懷去就。
entries.en: Early refugees wavered over Murong's regime.
entries.literal: Then refugee gentlemen saw Murong still founding his state and hesitated whether to stay.

entries.zh: 嶷首定名分，為群士啟行。
entries.en: Pei Yi imposed order on refugee protocols.
entries.literal: Yi first fixed hierarchy of ranks and opened the way for scholars.

entries.zh: 廆甚悅，以嶷為長史，委以軍國之謀。
entries.en: Murong made him chief strategist.
entries.literal: Hui rejoiced, appointed Yi chief clerk, entrusting civil and military counsel.

entries.zh: 君侯植根江陽，發曜荊、衡，杖葉公之權，有包胥之志，而令白公、伍員殆得極其暴，竊為丘明恥之。
entries.en: He urged Tao Kan to emulate Chu loyalists against barbarians.
entries.literal: You, lord, are rooted along the Yangzi, shine between Jing and Heng, wield Lord Ye's authority and harbor Shen Baoxu's resolve—yet Bai Gong and Wu Yuan ran riot—history would shame Qiu Ming.

entries.zh: 區區楚國子重之徒，猶恥君弱、群臣不及先大夫，厲己戒眾，以服陳、鄭；
entries.en: He cited Spring and Autumn shame-forged virtue.
entries.literal: Even Chu ministers like Zichong were ashamed when their lord was weak and officers fell short of earlier leaders—they disciplined themselves to humble Chen and Zheng.

entries.zh: 越之種蠡尚能弼佐句踐，取威黃池；
entries.en: Wu-Yue precedent proved peripheral grit could win.
entries.literal: Yue's Zhongli and Fan Li still aided Goujian to glory at Huangchi.

entries.zh: 況今吳土英賢比肩，而不輔翼聖主，陵江北伐。
entries.en: He contrasted Wu talent with southern lethargy.
entries.literal: How much more today Wu soil teams with heroes—yet none assists the sage sovereign to sweep north.

entries.zh: 以義聲之直，討逆暴之羯，檄命舊邦之士，招懷存本之人，豈不若因風振落，頓阪走輪哉！
entries.en: Northern expedition should sweep Shi Le easily.
entries.literal: With righteous prestige you could punish cruel Jie bandits, issue orders to old heartlands, summon homesick people—is it not like shaking leaves in wind or wheels racing downhill!

entries.zh: 且孫氏之初，以長沙之眾摧破董卓，志匡漢室。
entries.en: Sun Jian's loyalty anchored Wu rise.
entries.literal: Moreover Sun's house began by crushing Dong Zhuo with Changsha's host and aiming to restore Han.

entries.zh: 雖中遇寇害，雅志不遂，原其心誠，乃忽身命。
entries.en: Sun lineage sacrifice deserved respect.
entries.literal: Though mid-course setbacks thwarted noble aims, judging original intent they threw away life for loyalty.

entries.zh: 及權據揚、越，外杖周、張，內馮顧、陸，距魏亦壁，克取襄陽。
entries.en: Sun Quan's teamwork humbled northern power.
entries.literal: When Sun Quan held Yang and Yue, Zhou Yu and Zhang Zhao outside, Gu Yong and Lu Xun inside, he checked Wei at the river and seized Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 自茲以降，世主相襲，咸能侵逼徐、豫，令魏朝旰食。
entries.en: Successive Wu kings threatened central plains.
entries.literal: Thereafter each ruler inherited ambition and pressed Xu and Yu so Wei ate meals late with worry.

entries.zh: 不知今之江表為賢俊匿智，藏其勇略邪？
entries.en: He challenged southern elites to show courage.
entries.literal: Do today's Jiangnan talents hide wisdom and bury valor?

entries.zh: 將呂蒙、淩統高蹤曠世哉？
entries.en: He invoked Wu's famed commanders.
entries.literal: Are they inferior to Lü Meng and Ling Tong?

entries.zh: 況今凶羯虐暴，中州人士逼迫勢促，其顛沛之危，甚於累卵。
entries.en: Northern Chinese suffered imminent ruin under Shi.
entries.literal: Moreover vicious Jie tyranny squeezes central-plain families worse than stacked eggs.

entries.zh: 假號之強，眾心所去，敵有釁矣，易可震盪。
entries.en: Shi Le's regime was brittle.
entries.literal: The false emperor's might lacks popular support; enemies show cracks—easy to shake apart.

entries.zh: 王郎、袁術雖自詐偽，皆基淺根微，禍不旋踵，此皆君侯之所聞見者矣。
entries.en: Pseudo-emperors fell quickly before true mandate.
entries.literal: Wang Lang and Yuan Shu were frauds yet shallow-rooted—their doom swift; all this you yourself have witnessed.

entries.zh: 慕容廆
entries.en: Murong Hui
entries.literal: Murong Hui

entries.zh: 封弈等以皝任重位輕，宜稱燕王，皝於是以咸康三年僭即王位，赦其境內。
entries.en: Feng Yi and others, holding that Huang’s burden was heavy while his rank was light, urged him to style himself King of Yan; Huang thereupon in the third year of Xiankang illegitimately assumed the kingship and pardoned those within his borders.
entries.literal: Feng Yi and others because Huang’s burden was weighty yet rank was light, ought to style King of Yan; Huang thereupon in the third year of Xiankang illegitimately assumed kingship, pardoned those within his borders.

entries.zh: 以封弈為國相，韓壽為司馬，裴開、陽騖、王寓、李洪、杜群、宋該、劉瞻、石琮、皇甫真、陽協、宋晃、平熙、張泓等並為列卿將帥。
entries.en: He named Feng Yi chancellor, Han Shou marshal, and distributed ministerial and command posts among Pei Kai, Yang Wu, and the rest.
entries.literal: Made Feng Yi state chancellor, Han Shou marshal, Pei Kai, Yang Wu, Wang Yu, Li Hong, Du Qun, Song Gai, Liu Zhan, Shi Cong, Huangfu Zhen, Yang Xie, Song Huang, Ping Xi, Zhang Hong and others concurrently ministers and generals.

entries.zh: 起文昌殿，乘金根車，駕六馬，出入稱警蹕。
entries.en: He built Wenchang Hall, rode the six-horse imperial carriage, and received full royal escorts.
entries.literal: Raised the Wenchang Hall, rode the gold-root carriage, harnessed six horses, going out and entering called out “clear the way.”

entries.zh: 以其妻段氏為王后，世子俊為太子，皆如魏武、晉文輔政故事。
entries.en: He made Lady Duan queen and Murong Jun crown prince, citing Cao Cao and Sima Zhao as precedents.
entries.literal: Made his wife Lady Duan queen, heir apparent Jun crown prince, all like Wei Wu and Jin Wen’s precedent of assisting government.

entries.zh: 若親黨后族，必有傾辱之禍。
entries.en: when they favored kin and the empress's clan, overthrow and humiliation were sure to follow.
entries.literal: If they favored kin and the empress's clan, disaster of overthrow and humiliation was sure to follow.

entries.zh: 是以周之申伯號稱賢舅，以其身籓於外，不握朝權。
entries.en: Shen Bo of Zhou was praised as a worthy maternal uncle because he held a frontier fief and did not grasp court power.
entries.literal: Therefore Shen Bo of Zhou was called the worthy maternal uncle, because he was enfeoffed outside as a frontier lord and did not hold court power.

entries.zh: 降及秦昭，足為令主，委信二舅，幾至亂國。
entries.en: Even King Zhao of Qin, a capable ruler, trusted his two maternal uncles and nearly ruined the state.
entries.literal: Descending to King Zhao of Qin, who was enough to be called a fine ruler, he entrusted his two maternal uncles and nearly brought the state to disorder.

entries.zh: 逮于漢武，推重田蚡，萬機之要，無不決之。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Han elevated Tian Fen until every vital decision passed through him.
entries.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, who elevated Tian Fen, none of the myriad affairs' essentials went undecided by him.

entries.zh: 及蚡死後，切齒追恨。
entries.en: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in bitter regret.
entries.literal: When Fen died, he gnashed his teeth in later regret.

entries.zh: 成帝暗弱，不能自立，內惑豔妻，外恣五舅，卒令王莽坐取帝位。
entries.en: Emperor Cheng was weak and could not stand alone; beguiled within by a beautiful consort and indulging the five maternal uncles without, he finally let Wang Mang seize the throne.
entries.literal: Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang sit and take the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 每覽斯事，孰不痛惋！
entries.en: Reading such cases, who does not feel pain and regret!
entries.literal: Each time one reads these affairs, who does not feel pain and regret!

entries.zh: 設使舅氏賢若穰侯、王鳳，則但聞有二臣，不聞有二主。
entries.en: If maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang or Wang Feng, one would hear of two ministers, not two rulers.
entries.literal: Suppose the maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang and Wang Feng, then one would only hear of two ministers, not two lords.

entries.zh: 若其不才，則有竇憲、梁冀之禍。
entries.en: If they lacked talent, disasters like those of Dou Xian and Liang Ji followed.
entries.literal: If they lacked talent, there were the disasters of Dou Xian and Liang Ji.

entries.zh: 凡此成敗，亦既然矣。
entries.en: The lesson of these successes and failures is already plain.
entries.literal: All these successes and failures are already thus clear.

entries.zh: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
entries.en: Change course in time and collapse can be avoided.
entries.literal: If one could change course, one could avoid overturn and collapse.

entries.zh: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
entries.en: Your Majesty is heaven-born to exalt Jin's Way, yet the state has met repeated calamity; grief presses on every side, and recalling the past still burns.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side; recalling past affairs, to this day one burns with anguish.

entries.zh: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
entries.en: The root cause was the late Minister of Works Yu Liang: as chief maternal uncle he wielded overwhelming power, judged subordinates harshly, and insulted frontier generals until Su Jun and Zu Yue, unable to bear their rage, ruined the state.
entries.literal: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.

entries.zh: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager has died in indignation.
entries.literal: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.

entries.zh: 若社稷不靈，人神無助，豺狼之心當可極邪！
entries.en: Had the altars not been numinous and heaven not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!
entries.literal: If the altars were not numinous and men and spirits gave no aid, would the heart of wolves and jackals be allowed to reach its limit!

entries.zh: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
entries.en: Past affairs are not forgotten, yet Yu Bing as directorate counselor and left general, with his brothers, inwardly holds the pivot and outwardly commands armies, unmatched among ministers.
entries.literal: Past affairs are not forgotten, the model for later affairs, yet Directorate Counselor and Left General Yu Bing and others inwardly hold the pivot, outwardly hold supreme command; brothers stand side by side, no minister has a peer.

entries.zh: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
entries.en: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his brothers ought to withdraw of their own accord.
entries.literal: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to withdraw.

entries.zh: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
entries.en: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in frontier states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
entries.literal: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with frontier states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.

entries.zh: 如此，榮辱何從而生！
entries.en: Then whence would honor or disgrace arise!
entries.literal: Thus, from what would honor and disgrace arise!

entries.zh: 噂𠴲何辭而起！
entries.en: Whence would slander spring!
entries.literal: From what words would slander and calumny spring!

entries.zh: 往者惟亮一人，宿有名望，尚致世變，況今居之者素無聞焉！
entries.en: Formerly Yu Liang alone, though long renowned, still brought turmoil; how much more those who hold power today and were never heard of before!
entries.literal: Formerly there was only Yu Liang alone, long with a name of standing, yet still he brought change to the age; how much more those who hold the posts today, who from the first had no renown!

entries.zh: 且人情易惑，難以戶告，縱今陛下無私于彼，天下之人誰謂不私乎！
entries.en: Human feelings are easily swayed and cannot be told house to house; even if Your Majesty is impartial, who in the realm will believe it!
entries.literal: Moreover human feelings are easily confused and hard to tell door to door; even if Your Majesty today has no partiality toward them, who in the realm would say there is none!

entries.zh: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
entries.en: Bing and I differ in rank and station, yet as kin of the state I ought by rights to yield and rejoice at the occasion.
entries.literal: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and name, are far apart in origin and position, and moreover are kin of the state; by reason one ought to yield and rejoice to suit the occasion.

entries.zh: 臣獨矯抗此言者，上為陛下，退為冰計，疾苟容之臣，坐鑒得失。
