entries.en: I speak against the tide alone: for Your Majesty above and for Bing's sake below, hating ministers who only flatter and judging gain and loss plainly.
entries.literal: Your servant alone presses this contrary speech: for Your Majesty above, for Bing's sake below; despising ministers who only accommodate; sitting in judgment of gain and loss.

entries.zh: 顛而不扶，焉用彼相！
entries.en: If one does not right what is overturned, of what use is that minister!
entries.literal: If one does not right what is overturned, what use is that minister!

entries.zh: 昔徐福陳霍氏之戒，宣帝不從，至令忠臣更為逆族，良由察之不審，防之無漸。
entries.en: Formerly Xu Fu warned against the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not heed him, and loyal ministers became a traitorous house because he did not examine carefully or guard against gradual encroachment.
entries.literal: Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and prevention had no gradual steps.

entries.zh: 臣今所陳，可謂防漸矣。
entries.en: What I now set forth is prevention at the first sign.
entries.literal: What your servant now sets forth may be called prevention at the first sign.

entries.zh: 但恐陛下不明臣之忠，不用臣之計，事過之日，更處焦爛之後耳。
entries.en: I fear only that Your Majesty may not see my loyalty or use my plan, and that after disaster passes you will again stand amid the ashes.
entries.literal: Only fearing that Your Majesty may not understand your servant's loyalty and may not use your servant's plan; after the affair has passed, one will again be in the charred wreckage.

entries.zh: 昔王章、劉向每上封事，未嘗不指斥王氏，故令二子或死或刑。
entries.en: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang denounced the Wang clan in every sealed memorial and ended dead or punished.
entries.literal: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang, each time they submitted sealed memorials, never failed to denounce the Wang clan, so both men ended dead or under punishment.

entries.zh: 谷永、張禹依違不對，故容身苟免，取譏於世。
entries.en: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and preserved themselves, winning only the age's ridicule.
entries.literal: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and did not answer directly, so they preserved themselves and escaped, drawing ridicule from the age.

entries.zh: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
entries.en: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold supreme command, worry day and night how to repay the state, and can only destroy enemies abroad and offer loyal remonstrance within.
entries.literal: Your servant wears disheveled hair in a foreign land, holds the rank of supreme general, worries day and night and knows not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.

entries.zh: 臣若不言，誰當言者！
entries.en: If I do not speak, who will!
entries.literal: If your servant does not speak, who will speak!

entries.zh: 咸康七年，皝遷都龍城。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Xiankang, he moved his capital to Longcheng.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang, Huang moved the capital to Longcheng.

entries.zh: 率勁卒四萬，入自南陝，以伐宇文、高句麗，又使翰及子垂為前鋒，遣長史王寓等勒眾萬五千，從北置而進。
entries.en: He took forty thousand veterans through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and Murong Chui as van while Wang Yu led fifteen thousand from Beizhi.
entries.literal: Led picked soldiers forty thousand, entered from the southern defile to campaign against Yuwen and Goguryeo; again had Han and son Chui as vanguard, sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others leading host fifteen thousand to advance from Beizhi.

entries.zh: 高句麗王釗謂皝軍之從北路也，乃遣其弟武統精銳五萬距北置，躬率弱卒以防南陝。
entries.en: King Gao Zhen assumed the main thrust would come from the north, sent fifty thousand under his brother Wu to Beizhi, and held the southern defile with weaker troops.
entries.literal: Goguryeo King Zhen thought Huang’s army came by the northern route; thereupon sent his younger brother Wu leading picked fifty thousand to block Beizhi; personally led weak soldiers to guard the southern defile.

entries.zh: 翰與釗戰於木底，大敗之，乘勝遂入丸都，釗單馬而遁。
entries.en: Murong Han routed him at Mudi, pressed into Wandu, and Zhen fled alone on horseback.
entries.literal: Han fought Zhen at Mudi, greatly defeated them, rode victory then entered Wandu; Zhen single horse fled.

entries.zh: 皝掘釗父利墓，載其屍並其母妻珍寶，掠男女五萬餘口，焚其宮室，毀丸都而歸。
entries.en: Huang opened Gao Zhen’s father Li’s tomb, carried off the corpse together with Zhen’s mother, wife, and treasures, plundered more than fifty thousand men and women, fired the palaces, and razed Wandu.
entries.literal: Huang dug Zhen’s father Li’s tomb, loaded his corpse together with his mother, wife, and treasures, plundered over fifty thousand male and female, burned his palace chambers, destroyed Wandu and returned.

entries.zh: 明年，釗遣使稱臣于皝，貢其方物，乃歸其父屍。
entries.en: The next year Gao Zhen sent envoys declaring himself a subject of Huang, offered local products, and Huang then returned his father’s corpse.
entries.literal: The next year, Zhen sent envoys declaring subject to Huang, offered their local products, then returned his father’s corpse.

entries.zh: 時鮮卑單于段眷為晉驃騎大將軍、遼西公，雅好人物，虛心延裕。
entries.en: Duan Juan, Xianbei chieftain and Jin general, sought him eagerly.
entries.literal: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi; by nature he loved men of talent and humbly invited Yu.

entries.zh: 裕謂友人成泮曰：「仲尼喜佛肸之召，以匏瓜自喻，伊尹亦稱何事非君，何使非民，聖賢尚如此，況吾曹乎！
entries.en: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a gourd; Yi Yin too said, 'What affair is not that of the lord? What people are not his subjects?' Even sages were thus, how much more we!
entries.literal: Yu told friend Cheng Pan, saying: “Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi’s summons, used the gourd as metaphor; Yi Yin also said what affair is not lord, what people not subjects—even sages were thus; how much more our sort!

entries.zh: 眷今召我，豈徒然哉！」
entries.en: Duan Juan’s summons is no empty gesture!”
entries.literal: Juan now summons me—how could it be vain!”

entries.zh: 泮曰：「今華夏分崩，九州幅裂，軌跡所及，易水而已。
entries.en: Cheng Pan replied, “China is shattered; beyond the Yi River there is no refuge.
entries.literal: Pan said: “Now Huaxia split and crumbling, the nine provinces in tatters, where tracks reach is only to the Yi River.

entries.zh: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。
entries.en: To hide and wait for peace is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
entries.literal: Desiring to recline and await the great penetration—waiting for the Yellow River to clear—is waiting for the river to clear.

entries.zh: 人壽幾何？
entries.en: How long is a life?
entries.literal: Human life how much?

entries.zh: 古人以為白駒之歎。
entries.en: The ancients sighed at time’s white colt.
entries.literal: The ancients took this as the white colt’s sigh.

entries.zh: 少遊有雲，郡掾足以廕後，況國相乎！
entries.en: Even a county post can bless one’s heirs—let alone chancellor.
entries.literal: Shao You said, a commandery aide suffices to shade posterity—how much more a state chancellor!

entries.zh: 卿追蹤伊、孔，抑亦知機其神也。」
entries.en: You follow Confucius and Yi Yin—you know when Heaven calls.”
entries.literal: You trace Yi and Kong, or also know the moment’s spirit.”

entries.zh: 裕乃應之。
entries.en: Yang Yu accepted Duan Juan’s offer.
entries.literal: Yu thereupon answered him.

entries.zh: 拜郎中令、中軍將軍，處上卿位。
entries.en: He was named palace director and central army general, ranking among the highest ministers.
entries.literal: Appointed Palace Director, Central Army General, occupying the upper minister’s seat.

entries.zh: 曆事段氏五主，甚見尊重。
entries.en: He served five successive Duan lords and won deep respect.
entries.literal: Passed through serving the Duan house’s five lords, greatly was respected.

entries.zh: 慕容皝
entries.en: Murong Huang.
entries.literal: Murong Huang.

entries.zh: 始廆以武帝太康六年稱公，至暐四世。
entries.en: Murong Gui first received the ducal title in the sixth year of Taikang under Jin Wudi; to Murong Wei was four generations.
entries.literal: At first Gui in Emperor Wu's sixth year of Taikang was called duke; reaching Wei was four generations.

entries.zh: 暐在位一十一年，以海西公太和五年滅，通廆、皝凡八十五年。
entries.en: Murong Wei reigned eleven years; the state fell in the fifth year of Taihe under the Duke of Haixi—eighty-five years in all from Murong Gui and Murong Huang.
entries.literal: Wei on the throne eleven years; with Duke of Haixi in the fifth year of Taihe destroyed—through Gui and Huang altogether eighty-five years.

entries.zh: 慕容暐
entries.en: Murong Wei
entries.literal: Murong Wei (section heading).

entries.zh: 初，張遇自許昌來降，健納遇後母韓氏為昭儀，每於眾中謂遇曰：「卿，吾子也。」
entries.en: At first, when Zhang Yu surrendered from Xuchang, Jian had taken Yu’s stepmother Lady Han as an honored concubine and often said to Yu in public: “You are my son.”
entries.literal: At first, when Zhang Yu had surrendered from Xuchang, Jian had taken Yu’s stepmother Lady Han as an honored concubine and often said in public: “You are my son.”

entries.zh: 遇慚恨，引關中諸將欲以雍州歸順，乃與健中黃門劉晃謀夜襲健，事覺，遇害。
entries.en: Burning with shame, Yu rallied Guanzhong’s commanders to deliver Yong to Jin and conspired with Liu Huang to ambush Jian; the scheme surfaced and Yu died for it.
entries.literal: Yu was ashamed and resentful; he drew in the Guanzhong generals intending to hand Yong Province to Jin, and plotted with palace attendant Liu Huang to strike Jian by night; the plot leaked and Yu was killed.

entries.zh: 於是孔特起池陽，劉珍、夏侯顯起鄠，喬景起雍，胡陽赤起司竹，呼延毒起霸城，眾數萬人，並遣使詣征西桓溫、中軍殷浩請救。
entries.en: Revolt flared: Kong Te at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyan Du at Bashicheng—each mustered tens of thousands—and all begged Huan Wen and Yin Hao for relief.
entries.literal: Thereupon Kong Te rose at Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian at Hu, Qiao Jing at Yong, Hu Yangchi at Sizhu, Huyan Du at Bashicheng—each with tens of thousands—and all sent envoys to General Who Conquers the West Huan Wen and Central Army commander Yin Hao begging rescue.

entries.zh: 苻洪
entries.en: Fu Hong
entries.literal: Fu Hong

entries.zh: 是時安西呂光自西域還師，至於宜禾，堅涼州刺史梁熙謀閉境距之。
entries.en: Meanwhile Lü Guang, general who pacifies the west, was marching home from the Western Regions and had reached Yihe; Liang Xi, inspector of Liangzhou under Fu Jian, meant to shut the frontier and block his entry.
entries.literal: At this time the General Who Pacifies the West Lü Guang was returning his army from the Western Regions and reached Yihe; Liang Xi, Fu Jian's Inspector of Liangzhou, planned to close the border and keep him out.

entries.zh: 高昌太守楊翰言於熙曰：「呂光新定西國，兵強氣銳，其鋒不可當也。
entries.en: Yang Han, administrator of Gaochang, warned Liang Xi: "Lü Guang has just brought the west under his hand; his soldiers are fresh and fierce, and nothing can stand in the path of his thrust.
entries.literal: The Administrator of Gaochang Yang Han spoke to Xi, saying: "Lü Guang has newly subdued the western lands; his troops are strong and his morale keen, and the edge of his advance cannot be withstood.

entries.zh: 度其事意，必有異圖。
entries.en: Judging from how things are moving, he must be nursing ambitions beyond a simple homecoming.
entries.literal: Considering the drift of events, he is sure to harbor other designs.

entries.zh: 且今關中擾亂，京師存亡未知，自河已西迄於流沙，地方萬里，帶甲十萬，鼎峙之勢實在今日。
entries.en: Moreover Guanzhong is chaos and the fate of the capital uncertain; west of the Yellow River stretches ten thousand li of ground to the desert's edge, garrisoned by a hundred thousand men—if ever there was a moment for contending powers to face one another, it is this.
entries.literal: Moreover the Guanzhong is in turmoil, and whether the capital survives is unknown; from the Yellow River westward to the shifting sands, the territory is ten thousand li, with a hundred thousand armored men—the time for a tripartite standoff is truly now.

entries.zh: 若光出流沙，其勢難測。
entries.en: Once Lü Guang breaks out of the western wastes, no one can tell what he will do next.
entries.literal: If Lü Guang emerges from the desert, his movements will be hard to predict.

entries.zh: 高梧穀口，水險之要，宜先守之而奪其水。
entries.en: Gaowu Gorge is a defile where water and ground favor the defender; hold it first and deny him water.
entries.literal: Gaowu Gorge is a choke point of water and terrain; you should seize it first and cut off his water supply.

entries.zh: 彼既窮渴，自然投戈。
entries.en: Thirst and exhaustion will do your work for you—they will throw down their arms of their own accord.
entries.literal: When they are exhausted and parched, they will naturally cast aside their weapons.

entries.zh: 如其以遠不守，伊吾之關亦可距也。
entries.en: Even if he scorns to contest that distant ground, the Yiwu barrier can still block him.
entries.literal: If he disdains to hold that distant line, the pass at Yiwu can still bar him.

entries.zh: 若度此二要，雖有子房之策，難為計矣。
entries.en: Let him through both choke points, and not even Zhang Liang's cunning could save your position.
entries.literal: If he passes these two critical points, even with a Zhang Liang's stratagems you will find no remedy.

entries.zh: 地有所必爭，真此機也。」
entries.en: Some ground must be contested at any cost; the opportunity is now."
entries.literal: There are positions that must be fought for—this is the moment."

entries.zh: 熙弗從。
entries.en: Liang Xi refused to listen.
entries.literal: Xi did not follow this advice.

entries.zh: 美水令犍為張統說熙曰：「主上傾國南討，覆敗而還。
entries.en: Zhang Tong of Qianwei, magistrate of Meishui, said to Liang Xi: "Our lord emptied the kingdom for a southern campaign and returned in defeat.
entries.literal: The magistrate of Meishui, Zhang Tong of Qianwei, urged Xi, saying: "The sovereign raised the whole realm for a southern expedition and came back in ruin.

entries.zh: 慕容垂擅兵河北，泓、沖寇逼京師，丁零雜虜，跋扈關、洛，州郡奸豪，所在風扇，王綱弛絕，人懷利己。
entries.en: Murong Chui holds the Hebei plain; Murong Hong and Murong Chong threaten the capital; Dingling and other tribes rampage through Guanzhong and the Luoyang region; local magnates everywhere take the cue to rebel; imperial authority frays and every hand reaches for advantage.
entries.literal: Murong Chui wields arms north of the Yellow River; Hong and Chong press the capital; Dingling and mixed barbarians run riot in Guan and Luo; unscrupulous strongmen in every province rise like windblown grass; the royal net hangs slack and each man seeks his private gain.

entries.zh: 今呂光回師，將軍何以抗也？」
entries.en: Lü Guang is marching home at the head of a seasoned host—how do you mean to stop him?"
entries.literal: Now Lü Guang is leading his army back—how will you, General, resist him?"

entries.zh: 熙曰：「誠深憂之，未知計之所出。」
entries.en: Liang Xi answered, "The danger weighs on me, yet I see no clear course."
entries.literal: Xi said: "I am deeply troubled, but I do not know what plan to adopt."

entries.zh: 統曰：「光雄果勇毅，明略絕人，今以蕩西域之威，擁歸師之銳，鋒若猛火之盛于原，弗可敵也。
entries.en: Zhang Tong replied, "Lü Guang is a fighter of rare courage and cunning; fresh from conquering the west and leading veterans homeward, he strikes like wildfire across dry grass—you cannot meet him head-on.
entries.literal: Tong said: "Lü Guang is bold, resolute, and brave beyond ordinary men; now, with the prestige of having swept the Western Regions and the keen edge of a homecoming army, his spearhead is like a fierce fire racing across the plain—he cannot be opposed.

entries.zh: 將軍世受殊恩，忠誠夙著，立勳王室，宜在於今。
entries.en: Your family has enjoyed extraordinary grace, your devotion has never been in doubt, and you have served the throne with distinction—now is the hour to prove it again.
entries.literal: The General's house has received singular favor for generations, your loyalty has long been manifest, and you have raised achievements for the royal house—this is the moment to show it.

entries.zh: 行唐公洛，上之從弟，勇冠一時。
entries.en: The duke of Xingtang, Fu Luo, is the emperor's cousin on the father's side and the foremost warrior of his day.
entries.literal: The Duke of Xingtang, Luo, is His Majesty's younger cousin by the same grandfather; his valor is unmatched in the age.

entries.zh: 為將軍計者，莫若奉為盟主，以攝眾望，推忠義以總率群豪，則光無異心也。
entries.en: The wise course is to recognize Fu Luo as leader of the alliance and win the people's hope, then gather the heroes under the banner of duty—so Lü Guang finds no opening for disloyalty.
entries.literal: For the General's planning, nothing would be better than to acknowledge him as covenant lord to gather popular expectation, and to rally the bold with loyalty and righteousness—then Lü Guang will have no separate ambition.

entries.zh: 資其精銳，東兼毛興，連王統、楊璧，集四州之眾，掃凶逆于諸夏，甯帝室於關中，此桓文之舉也。」
entries.en: Use his elite columns to drive east, link with Mao Xing, Wang Tong, and Yang Bi, combine the armies of four provinces, clear the heartland of traitors, and set the dynasty right in Guanzhong—work worthy of Duke Huan or Duke Wen."
entries.literal: With his picked troops strike east to absorb Mao Xing, join Wang Tong and Yang Bi, assemble the hosts of four provinces, sweep the rebels from the central plains, and restore the imperial house in Guanzhong—this is the deed of a Huan or a Wen."

entries.zh: 熙又不從。
entries.en: Liang Xi still would not take the advice.
entries.literal: Again Xi did not follow.

entries.zh: 殺洛於西海，以子胤為鷹揚將軍，率眾五萬距光於酒泉。
entries.en: Instead he executed Fu Luo at Xihai, named his son Yin general who spreads might, and sent fifty thousand soldiers to block Lü Guang at Jiuquan.
entries.literal: He killed Luo at Xihai, appointed his son Yin General Who Spreads Might, and led fifty thousand men to oppose Lü Guang at Jiuquan.

entries.zh: 敦煌太守姚靜、晉昌太守李純以郡降光。
entries.en: Yao Jing of Dunhuang and Li Chun of Jinchang yielded their prefectures to Lü Guang.
entries.literal: The Administrator of Dunhuang Yao Jing and the Administrator of Jinchang Li Chun surrendered their commanderies to Lü Guang.

entries.zh: 胤及光戰于安彌，為光所敗。
entries.en: Fu Yin met Lü Guang at Anmi and was routed.
entries.literal: Yin fought Lü Guang at Anmi and was defeated by him.

entries.zh: 武威太守彭濟執熙迎光，光殺之。
entries.en: Peng Ji, administrator of Wuwei, took Liang Xi prisoner and opened the gates to Lü Guang, who then put Liang Xi to death.
entries.literal: The Administrator of Wuwei Peng Ji seized Xi and welcomed Lü Guang; Lü Guang killed Xi.

entries.zh: 建威、西郡太守索泮，奮威、督洪池已南諸軍事、酒泉太守宋皓等，並為光所殺。
entries.en: Suo Pan, who held Jianwei and the western commandery, Song Hao of Jiuquan—who served as general who rouses might and directed troops south of Hongchi—and others likewise fell to Lü Guang's blade.
entries.literal: Suo Pan, administrator of Jianwei and Xijun, and Song Hao, administrator of Jiuquan who held the office of general who rouses might and supervised military affairs south of Hongchi Pool, together with others, were all killed by Lü Guang.

entries.zh: 堅尚書令、魏昌公苻纂自關中來奔，拜太尉，進封東海王。
entries.en: Fu Zuan, Fu Jian's director of the secretariat and duke of Weichang, arrived as a refugee from Guanzhong; Fu Pi named him grand commandant and raised him to prince of Donghai.
entries.literal: Fu Jian's Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Weichang Fu Zuan came fleeing from Guanzhong and was appointed Grand Commandant, advanced to Prince of Donghai.

entries.zh: 以中山太守王兗為平東將軍、平州刺史、阜城侯，苻定為征東將軍、冀州牧、高城侯，苻紹為鎮東將軍、督冀州諸軍事、重合侯，苻謨為征西將軍、幽州牧、高邑侯，苻亮為鎮北大將軍、督幽、并二州諸軍事，並進爵郡公。
entries.en: Wang Yan of Zhongshan became general who pacifies the east, inspector of Pingzhou, and marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding general who conquers the east, governor of Jizhou, and marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao general who guards the east, with overall command in Jizhou, and marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo general who conquers the west, governor of Youzhou, and marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang general who guards the north, with joint authority over You and Bing—all were promoted to commandery dukes.
entries.literal: He made the Administrator of Zhongshan Wang Yan General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Pingzhou, and Marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding General Who Conquers the East, Governor of Jizhou, and Marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao General Who Guards the East, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Jizhou, and Marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Youzhou, and Marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang General Who Guards the North, Commander of Military Affairs in You and Bing, and all were advanced in noble rank to Dukes of commanderies.

entries.zh: 定、紹據信都，謨、亮先據常山，慕容垂之圍鄴城也，並降于垂，聞丕稱尊號，遣使謝罪。
entries.en: Fu Ding and Fu Shao held Xindu while Fu Mo and Fu Liang had seized Changshan first; both pairs had gone over to Murong Chui when he invested Ye, yet when Fu Pi declared himself emperor they dispatched messengers begging forgiveness.
entries.literal: Ding and Shao held Xindu; Mo and Liang had first occupied Changshan; when Murong Chui besieged Ye they had both surrendered to Chui, but on hearing that Fu Pi had assumed the imperial title they sent envoys to apologize.

entries.zh: 王兗固守博陵，與垂相持。
entries.en: Wang Yan shut himself in Boling and held the line against Murong Chui.
entries.literal: Wang Yan stubbornly defended Boling against Chui.

entries.zh: 左將軍竇沖、秦州刺史王統、河州刺史毛興、益州刺史王廣、南秦州刺史楊璧、衛將軍楊定，並據隴右，遣使招丕，請討姚萇。
entries.en: Dou Chong, general of the left; Wang Tong, inspector of Qinzhou; Mao Xing, inspector of Hezhou; Wang Guang, inspector of Yizhou; Yang Bi, inspector of south Qinzhou; and Yang Ding, general of the guards, each held ground in Longyou and wrote to Fu Pi offering to strike Yao Chang.
entries.literal: The General of the Left Dou Chong, the Inspector of Qinzhou Wang Tong, the Inspector of Hezhou Mao Xing, the Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang, the Inspector of South Qinzhou Yang Bi, and the General of the Guards Yang Ding all held Longyou and sent envoys to summon Fu Pi, asking to campaign against Yao Chang.

entries.zh: 丕大悅，以定為驃騎大將軍、雍州牧，沖為征西大將軍、梁州牧，統鎮西大將軍，興車騎大將軍，璧征南大將軍，並開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，廣安西將軍，皆進位州牧。
entries.en: Fu Pi was delighted: Yang Ding became grand general of agile cavalry and governor of Yongzhou; Dou Chong grand general who conquers the west and governor of Liangzhou; Wang Tong grand general who guards the west; Mao Xing grand general of chariots and cavalry; Yang Bi grand general who conquers the south—each with an independent headquarters and honors matching the three dukes, plus the title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; Wang Guang became general who pacifies the west; all were raised to governorships.
entries.literal: Fu Pi was greatly pleased; he made Yang Ding Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Yongzhou, Chong Grand General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Liangzhou, Tong Grand General Who Guards the West, Xing Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bi Grand General Who Conquers the South, all with the privilege of opening a general's office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Guang General Who Pacifies the West, all advanced to the position of provincial governor.

entries.zh: 先是，慕容驎攻王兗於博陵，至是糧竭矢盡，郡功曹張猗逾城聚眾應驎。
entries.en: Before this, Murong Lin had been besieging Wang Yan in Boling; supplies and arrows ran out, and Zhang Yi, the county merit clerk, scaled the walls, raised a band of followers, and opened the city to Lin.
entries.literal: Earlier, Murong Lin had attacked Wang Yan at Boling; by now grain and arrows were exhausted, and the county merit officer Zhang Yi climbed the wall, gathered a crowd, and went over to Lin.

entries.zh: 袞臨城數之曰：「卿，秦之人也。
entries.en: Wang Yan appeared on the battlements and cried out, "You were born a subject of Qin.
entries.literal: Yan stood on the wall and rebuked him, saying: "You are a man of Qin.

entries.zh: 吾，卿之君也。
entries.en: I am the lord you serve.
entries.literal: I am your lord.

entries.zh: 起眾應賊，號稱義兵，何名實相違之甚！
entries.en: You rouse the people for the rebels yet name it a loyal host—never was deed and title so at odds!
entries.literal: You raised a host to answer the bandit and call it a righteous army—how far name and fact are twisted!

entries.zh: 卿兄往合鄉宗，親逐城主，天地不容，為世大戮。
entries.en: Your brother once mustered the clan, chased the lawful governor from the walls, and earned the scorn of heaven and earth—a public enemy while he lived.
entries.literal: Your elder brother once joined your village kin, personally drove out the city's master; heaven and earth would not shelter him—he became the great criminal of his age.

entries.zh: 身滅未幾，卿復續之。
entries.en: He has scarcely paid for his crimes in the grave, and you follow in his footsteps.
entries.literal: His person was destroyed not long ago, and you have taken up his course.

entries.zh: 卿見為吾吏，親尋干戈，競為戎首，為爾君者，不亦難乎！
entries.en: You served under my banner, then seized weapons with your own hands and led the alien host—what lord could forgive such a thing?
entries.literal: You have been my officer, yet you personally took up arms and strove to be chief among the barbarians—for your lord, is that not hard indeed!

entries.zh: 今人何取卿一切之功，寧能忘卿不忠不孝之事！
entries.en: Men may praise your little coup today, but they will not forget that you are faithless to your prince and heartless toward your kin!
entries.literal: What do men value in your petty moment of glory—can they forget your deeds of disloyalty and unfilial impiety!

entries.zh: 古人有雲，求忠臣必出孝子之門，卿母在城，不能顧之，何忠義之可望！
entries.en: The old proverb runs that loyal servants come from filial homes; your mother is trapped in this town while you betray it—where is your duty or your honor?
entries.literal: The ancients said, seek loyal ministers among the households of filial sons; your mother is inside the city and you do not care for her—what loyalty or righteousness can be expected!

entries.zh: 惡不絕世，卿之謂也。
entries.en: They say wickedness outlives a single life—you prove the saying.
entries.literal: Evil does not die with the generation—this is said of you.

entries.zh: 不圖中州禮義之邦邦，而卿門風若斯。
entries.en: I never thought to see, in the heartland where rites and duty are taught, a family sink to such conduct as yours.
entries.literal: I did not expect that in the Central Plains, the land of ritual and propriety, the conduct of your clan should be thus.

entries.zh: 卿去老母如脫屣，吾復何論哉！」
entries.en: You abandoned your old mother like a pair of worn-out sandals—I have nothing left to say to you!"
entries.literal: You cast off your aged mother as one casts off worn shoes—what more is there for me to say!"

entries.zh: 既而城陷，兗及固安侯苻鑒，並為驎所殺。
entries.en: The city soon fell; Wang Yan and Fu Jian, marquis of Gu'an, were both slain by Murong Lin.
entries.literal: Soon the city fell; Yan and the Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian were both killed by Lin.

entries.zh: 登以竇沖為車騎大將軍、南秦州牧，楊定為大將軍、益州牧，楊璧為司空、梁州牧。
entries.en: Fu Deng named Dou Chong grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of south Qinzhou, Yang Ding grand general and governor of Yizhou, Yang Bi minister of works and governor of Liangzhou.
entries.literal: Deng made Dou Chong Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of South Qinzhou, Yang Ding Grand General and Governor of Yizhou, Yang Bi Minister of Works and Governor of Liangzhou.

entries.zh: 登收合餘兵，退據胡空堡，遣使齎書加竇沖大司馬、驃騎將軍、前鋒大都督、都督隴東諸軍事，楊定左丞相、上大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，楊璧大將軍、都督隴右諸軍事。
entries.en: Fu Deng regrouped at Hu Kong's fort and promoted Dou Chong to grand marshal and Yang Ding to left chancellor with full military authority, Yang Bi to grand general over Longyou.
entries.literal: Deng gathered the remaining troops, withdrew to occupy Hu Kong's fort, sent envoys bearing documents to advance Dou Chong to Grand Marshal, General of Agile Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Longdong, Yang Ding to Left Chancellor, Supreme Grand General, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Yang Bi to Grand General, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Longyou.

entries.zh: 遣沖率見眾為先驅，自繁川趣長安。
entries.en: Dou Chong led the van toward Chang'an from Fanchuan.
entries.literal: He dispatched Chong to lead the troops at hand as vanguard, himself going from Fanchuan toward Chang'an.

entries.zh: 登率眾從新平逕據新豐之千戶固。
entries.en: Fu Deng cut through Xinping and seized Qianhu fort at Xinfeng.
entries.literal: Deng led the host from Xinping by a direct route to occupy Qianhu Fort of Xinfeng.

entries.zh: 使定率隴上諸軍為其後繼，璧留守仇池。
entries.en: Yang Ding was to follow with the Long uplands levies; Yang Bi stayed to hold Qiuqi.
entries.literal: He ordered Ding to lead the various armies on Longshang as his rear support, while Bi remained to guard Qiuqi.

entries.zh: 又命其并州刺史楊政、冀州刺史楊楷率所統大會長安。
entries.en: Yang Zheng of Bingzhou and Yang Kai of Jizhou were to march on Chang'an for the general muster.
entries.literal: He also ordered his Inspector of Bingzhou Yang Zheng and Inspector of Jizhou Yang Kai to lead their commands in a great rendezvous at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 萇遣其將軍王破虜略地秦州，楊定及破虜戰于清水之格奴阪，大敗之。
entries.en: Yao Chang's Wang Polu raided Qinzhou until Yang Ding shattered him at Genu Ford on the Qingshui.
entries.literal: Chang sent his general Wang Polu to seize territory in Qinzhou; Yang Ding and Polu fought at Genu Slope on the Qingshui, and Ding inflicted a great defeat on him.

entries.zh: 登攻張龍世於鴦泉堡，姚萇救之，登引退。
entries.en: Fu Deng besieged Zhang Longshi at Yuanquan until Yao Chang relieved him, forcing Fu Deng to pull back.
entries.literal: Deng attacked Zhang Longshi at Yuanquan Fort; Yao Chang came to save him, and Deng led a withdrawal.

entries.zh: 萇密遣其將任瓫、宗度詐為內應，遣使招登，許開門納之。
entries.en: Yao Chang secretly ordered Ren Chong and Zong Du to feign treason and invite Fu Deng inside the walls.
entries.literal: Chang secretly sent his generals Ren Chong and Zong Du to pretend to be inner collaborators, dispatched envoys to summon Deng, promising to open the gates and admit him.

entries.zh: 登以為然。
entries.en: Fu Deng believed the ruse.
entries.literal: Deng believed it was so.

entries.zh: 雷惡地馳謂登曰：「姚萇多計略，善御人，必為奸變，願深宜詳思。」
entries.en: Lei Edi galloped up to warn him: "Yao Chang is cunning and knows how to bind men—he will betray you; think twice."
entries.literal: Lei Edi rode in haste and said to Deng: "Yao Chang is full of stratagems and skilled at controlling men; he is sure to work a treacherous turn—I pray you think it through most carefully."

entries.zh: 登乃止。
entries.en: Fu Deng called off the attempt.
entries.literal: Deng thereupon stopped.

entries.zh: 萇聞惡地之詣登也，謂諸將曰：「此羌多奸智，今其詣登，事必無成。」
entries.en: Yao Chang told his officers, "That Qiang is sly; now that he has warned Fu Deng, the trap is sprung for nothing."
entries.literal: When Chang heard that Edi had gone to Deng, he said to his generals: "This Qiang is full of treacherous cleverness; now that he has gone to Deng, the affair is sure not to succeed."

entries.zh: 登聞萇懸門以待之，大驚，謂左右曰：「雷征東其殆聖乎！
entries.en: Learning that Yao Chang had lifted the portcullis in ambush, Fu Deng gasped to his staff, "Lei the east-conquering general must be clairvoyant!
entries.literal: Deng heard that Chang had raised the drawbridge to await him, was greatly startled, and said to those at his side: "Lei, General Who Conquers the East, is perhaps a sage!

entries.zh: 微此公，朕幾為豎子所誤。」
entries.en: Without him I would have walked into that boy's snare."
entries.literal: Without this lord, I would almost have been misled by the stripling."

entries.zh: 萇攻陷新羅堡。
entries.en: Yao Chang then took Xinluo fort.
entries.literal: Chang attacked and captured Xinluo Fort.

entries.zh: 萇撫風太守齊益男奔登。
entries.en: Qi Yinan, governor of Fufeng under Yao Chang, defected to Fu Deng.
entries.literal: Chang's Administrator of Fufeng Qi Yinan fled to Deng.

entries.zh: 登將軍路柴、強武等並以眾降於萇。
entries.en: Lu Chai, Qiang Wu, and other Fu Deng commanders went over to Yao Chang with their troops.
entries.literal: Fu Deng's generals Lu Chai, Qiang Wu, and others all led their hosts to surrender to Chang.

entries.zh: 登攻萇將張業生於隴東，萇救之，不克而退。
entries.en: Fu Deng struck Zhang Yesheng in Longdong; Yao Chang tried to help but retired without breaking the siege.
entries.literal: Deng attacked Chang's general Zhang Yesheng in Longdong; Chang came to his rescue, could not overcome him, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 登將軍魏褐飛攻姚當成於杏城，為萇所殺。
entries.en: Wei Hefei besieged Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng and died at Yao Chang's hand.
entries.literal: Fu Deng's general Wei Hefei attacked Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng and was killed by Chang.

entries.zh: 苻丕 苻登
entries.en: This chapter records Fu Pi and Fu Deng.
entries.literal: Fu Pi; Fu Deng.

entries.zh: 流人郭斁等千餘人執晉堂邑內史劉仕降於襄，朝延大震，以吏部尚書周閔為中軍將軍，緣江備守。
entries.en: When wanderers under Gu Yi seized Tangyi's interior minister Liu Shi and handed him to Xiang, the court reeled and named Zhou Min of the personnel ministry general of the central army to brace the Yangzi.
entries.literal: More than a thousand displaced persons led by Gu Yi seized Jin's interior administrator of Tangyi, Liu Shi, and surrendered him to Xiang; the court trembled greatly and appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min central army general to guard the river line.

entries.zh: 襄將佐部眾皆北人，咸勸襄北還。
entries.en: Every adviser and soldier hailed from the north and clamored to march home.
entries.literal: Xiang's staff and following were all northerners; all urged Xiang to return north.

entries.zh: 襄方軌北引，自稱大將軍、大單于，進攻外黃，為晉邊將所敗。
entries.en: He formed ranks for a northern march, proclaimed himself grand general and grand Shanyu, struck Waihuang, and stumbled against Jin frontier troops.
entries.literal: Xiang drove north in ordered columns, styled himself Grand General and Grand Shanyu, attacked Waihuang, and was defeated by Jin border generals.

entries.zh: 襄收散卒而勤撫恤之，於是復振。
entries.en: He rallied stragglers and tended them patiently until his army breathed again.
entries.literal: He gathered scattered soldiers and diligently comforted them; thereby he revived.

entries.zh: 乃據許昌，將如河東以圖關右，自許遂攻洛陽，逾月不克。
entries.en: Seizing Xuchang, he aimed at Hedong and the greater Guanzhong design; from there he threw columns at Luoyang yet failed for a full month.
entries.literal: Thereupon he occupied Xuchang; he intended to go to Hedong to plan Guanzhong; from Xu he attacked Luoyang but could not take it within a month.

entries.zh: 其長史王亮諫襄曰：「公英略蓋天下，士眾思效力命，不可損威勞眾，守此孤城。
entries.en: Chief clerk Wang Liang warned him: "Your genius outmatches the age and men ache to die for you—do not squander awe besieging one stubborn town.
entries.literal: His chief clerk Wang Liang remonstrated with Xiang: "Your lordship's strategy overshadows the realm; soldiers long to spend their lives for you—you cannot waste prestige and tire the host guarding this lone city.

entries.zh: 宜還河北，以弘遠略。」
entries.en: Withdraw north of the river and reopen the wider campaign."
entries.literal: You ought to return north of the Yellow River to enlarge distant designs."

entries.zh: 襄曰：「洛陽雖小，山河四塞之固，亦是用武之地。
entries.en: Xiang answered, "Luoyang looks small yet sits locked by river and hill—it remains a battlefield worth holding.
entries.literal: Xiang said: "Though Luoyang is small, its mountains and rivers form four barriers—it too is ground for arms.

entries.zh: 吾欲先據洛陽，然後開建大業。」
entries.en: I mean to take Luoyang first, then unfold the larger enterprise."
entries.literal: I desire first to seize Luoyang, then open and establish great enterprise."

entries.zh: 俄而亮卒，襄哭之甚慟，曰：「天將不欲成吾事乎？
entries.en: Wang Liang died soon after; Xiang mourned wildly and cried, "Does Heaven deny my purpose?
entries.literal: Shortly Liang died; Xiang wept exceedingly bitterly and said: "Does Heaven refuse to complete my affair?

entries.zh: 王亮舍我去也！」
entries.en: Has Wang Liang abandoned me?"
entries.literal: Wang Liang has left me!"

entries.zh: 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇
entries.en: Biographies of Yao Yizhong, his son Yao Xiang, and his son Yao Chang.
entries.literal: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang.

entries.zh: 安南強熙、鎮遠楊多叛，推竇沖為盟主，所在擾亂。
entries.en: Qiang Xi, general who pacifies the south, and Yang Duo rebelled, made Dou Chong their leader, and stirred the region.
entries.literal: The General Who Pacifies the South Qiang Xi and Yang Duo, general who guards the distance, rebelled, raised Dou Chong as covenant lord, and everywhere disturbed and rebelled.

entries.zh: 興率諸將討之，軍次武功，多兄子良國殺多而降。
entries.en: Yao Xing marched to suppress them; at Wugong Yang Duo's nephew Liangguo killed him and surrendered.
entries.literal: Xing led the generals to punish them; the army halted at Wugong; Duo's elder brother's son Liangguo killed Duo and surrendered.

entries.zh: 沖弟彰武與沖離貳，沖奔強熙。
entries.en: Dou Chong's brother Zhangwu turned on him, and Dou Chong fled to Qiang Xi.
entries.literal: Chong's younger brother Zhangwu broke with Chong; Chong fled to Qiang Xi.

entries.zh: 熙聞興將至，率戶二千奔秦州。
entries.en: Qiang Xi took two thousand households to Qinzhou when he learned Yao Xing was coming.
entries.literal: Xi, hearing Xing was about to arrive, led two thousand households in flight to Qinzhou.

entries.zh: 竇沖走汧川，汧川氐仇高執送之。
entries.en: Dou Chong ran to the Qian valley; the Di chief Qiu Gao seized him and handed him over.
entries.literal: Dou Chong fled to Qian River; the Di of Qian River Qiu Gao seized him and sent him in.

entries.zh: 沖從弟統率其眾降於興。
entries.en: Dou Tong, Dou Chong's cousin, brought his men to Yao Xing.
entries.literal: Chong's younger cousin Tong led his host to surrender to Xing.

entries.zh: 時劉裕誅桓玄，迎復安帝，玄衛將軍、新安王桓謙，臨原王桓怡，雍州刺史桓蔚，左衛將軍桓謐，中書令桓胤，將軍何澹之等奔於興。
entries.en: Huan Xuan's kinsmen and He Danzhi fled to Yao Xing after Liu Yu restored Jin.
entries.literal: At the time Liu Yu had executed Huan Xuan, welcomed and restored Emperor An; Xuan's Guard General and Prince of Xin'an Huan Qian, Prince of Linyuan Huan Yi, Inspector of Yongzhou Huan Wei, General of the Left Guard Huan Mi, Director of the Secretariat Huan Yin, General He Danzhi, and others fled to Xing.

entries.zh: 劉裕遣大參軍衡凱之詣姚顯，請通和，顯遣吉默報之，自是聘使不絕。
entries.en: Liu Yu and Yao Xing exchanged peace envoys through Yao Xian.
entries.literal: Liu Yu sent senior staff officer Heng Kaizhi to Yao Xian begging open peace; Xian sent Ji Mo to answer him; from this envoys on friendly missions were unceasing.

entries.zh: 晉求南鄉諸郡，興許之。
entries.en: Jin asked for Nanxiang; Yao Xing agreed.
entries.literal: Jin begged the commanderies of Nanxiang; Xing granted them.

entries.zh: 群臣咸諫以為不可，興曰：「天下之善一也，劉裕拔萃起微，匡輔晉室，吾何惜數郡而不成其美乎！」
entries.en: Ministers objected; Yao Xing said, "The good under heaven is one; Liu Yu, outstanding from humble beginnings, aids and supports the Jin house—why should I begrudge several commanderies and not complete his beauty!"
entries.literal: The host of ministers all remonstrated that it could not be done; Xing said: "The good under heaven is one; Liu Yu, outstanding from humble beginnings, aids and supports the Jin house—why should I begrudge several commanderies and not complete his beauty!"

entries.zh: 遂割南鄉、順陽、新野、舞陰等十二郡歸於晉。
entries.en: He yielded twelve prefectures including Nanxiang and Shunyang.
entries.literal: Thereupon he ceded Nanxiang, Shunyang, Xinye, Wuyin, and twelve other commanderies to Jin.

entries.zh: 禿髮傉檀獻興馬三千匹，羊三萬頭。
entries.en: Tufa Nutan presented Yao Xing three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.
entries.literal: Tufa Nutan presented Xing three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.

entries.zh: 興以為忠於己，乃署傉檀為涼州刺史，征涼州刺史王尚還長安。
entries.en: Thinking it loyalty, Yao Xing swapped Wang Shang for Tufa Nutan as governor of Liangzhou.
entries.literal: Xing thought him loyal to himself and thereupon appointed Nutan Inspector of Liangzhou, summoning Inspector of Liangzhou Wang Shang back to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 涼州人申屠英等二百餘人，遣主簿胡威詣興，請留尚，興弗許。
entries.en: More than two hundred men of Liangzhou, including Shentu Ying, sent chief clerk Hu Wei to Yao Xing, begging to retain Wang Shang; Xing refused.
entries.literal: More than two hundred men of Liangzhou such as Shentu Ying sent chief clerk Hu Wei to Xing begging to retain Shang; Xing did not permit it.

entries.zh: 引威見之，威流涕謂興曰：「臣州奉國五年，王威不接，銜膽棲冰、孤城獨守者，仰恃陛下威靈，俯杖良牧惠化。
entries.en: Hu Wei wept and said, "My province has served the state five years without royal majesty drawing near; those who hold gall and dwell on ice, alone guarding a solitary city, look up to Your Majesty's awesome spirit and down to a good shepherd's kindly rule.
entries.literal: He led Wei in audience; Wei wept and said to Xing: "My province has served the state five years without royal majesty drawing near; those who hold gall and dwell on ice, alone guarding a solitary city, look up relying on Your Majesty's awesome spirit and look down leaning on a good shepherd's kindly transformation.

entries.zh: 忽違天人之心，以華土資狄。
entries.en: Now you hand Chinese land to barbarians.
entries.literal: Suddenly to go against the hearts of heaven and men and with Chinese soil aid the Di.

entries.zh: 若傉檀才望應代，臣豈敢言。
entries.en: If Tufa Nutan were fit to rule, I would be silent.
entries.literal: If Nutan's talent and reputation fitted succession, how would your subject dare speak.

entries.zh: 竊聞乃以臣等貿馬三千匹，羊三萬口，如所傳實者，是為棄人貴畜。
entries.en: Rumor says you sold us for livestock—that values animals over people.
entries.literal: Privately I hear it is because you traded us for three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep—if the rumor is true, this is discarding men and prizing beasts.

entries.zh: 苟以馬供軍國，直煩尚書一符，三千餘家戶輸一匹，朝下夕辦，何故以一方委此奸胡！
entries.en: A requisition could raise the horses; why give a province to aliens?
entries.literal: If horses were wanted for army and state, it would suffice for the secretariat to issue one tally and more than three thousand households each render one hide—morning order, evening done—why entrust a whole region to this treacherous Hu!

entries.zh: 昔漢武傾天下之資，開建河西，隔絕諸戎，斷匈奴右臂，所以終能屠大宛王毋寡。
entries.en: Emperor Wu built Hexi to break the Xiongnu and take Dayuan.
entries.literal: In the past Han Wu tilted the realm's resources to open Hexi, cut off the various Rong, severed the Xiongnu's right arm—therefore in the end he could slaughter the King of Dayuan, Wugua.

entries.zh: 今陛下方布政玉門，流化西域，奈何以五郡之地資之犬嚴狁，忠誠華族棄之虐虜！
entries.en: You mean to civilize the west yet you feed five commanderies to Xianyun and abandon Chinese loyalty!
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty is just spreading government at Jade Gate, extending transformation to the Western Regions—how can you with the land of five commanderies aid these dog Xianyun and cast off loyal Chinese clans to cruel captives!

entries.zh: 非但臣州裏塗炭，懼方為聖朝旰食之憂。」
entries.en: Liangzhou will burn and the court will pay."
entries.literal: It is not only that my province will be smeared with mud and charcoal—I fear it will become the sagely court's worry of eating only at noon and night."

entries.zh: 興乃遣西平人車普馳止王尚，又遣使喻傉檀。
entries.en: Yao Xing sent Che Pu to recall Wang Shang and wrote Tufa Nutan.
entries.literal: Xing thereupon sent Che Pu of Xiping in haste to stop Wang Shang, and also sent envoys to instruct Nutan.

entries.zh: 會傉檀已至姑臧，普以狀先告之。
entries.en: Che Pu met Tufa Nutan already at Guzang.
entries.literal: It happened that Nutan had already reached Guzang; Pu reported the situation to him first.

entries.zh: 傉檀懼，脅遣王尚，遂入姑臧。
entries.en: Tufa Nutan forced Wang Shang out and took Guzang.
entries.literal: Nutan feared, coerced Shang's departure, and thereupon entered Guzang.

entries.zh: 興覽之大悅，謂其黃門侍郎姚文祖曰：「卿知宗敞乎？」
entries.en: Yao Xing read the memorial and was greatly pleased; he asked Yao Wenzu about Zong Chang.
entries.literal: Xing read it and was greatly pleased, saying to his Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Yao Wenzu: "Do you know Zong Chang?"

entries.zh: 文祖曰：「與臣州裏，西方之英雋。」
entries.en: He is our countryman and a western star."
entries.literal: Wenzu said: "He is of my province; a splendid talent of the west."

entries.zh: 興曰：「有表理王尚，文義甚佳，當王尚研思耳。」
entries.en: This petition for Wang Shang is brilliant—Wang Shang must have drafted it."
entries.literal: Xing said: "There is a memorial reasoning Wang Shang; the literary sense is very fine—it must be Wang Shang's polished thought."

entries.zh: 文祖曰：「尚在南台，禁止不與賓客交通，敞寓於楊桓，非尚明矣。」
entries.en: Yao Wenzu said, "Wang Shang is at the south terrace, forbidden to traffic with guests; Zong Chang lodges with Yang Huan—clearly Wang did not write it."
entries.literal: Wenzu said: "Shang is at the south terrace, forbidden to traffic with guests; Chang lodges with Yang Huan—not Shang is clear."

entries.zh: 興曰：「若爾，桓為措思乎？」
entries.en: Yang Huan then?"
entries.literal: Xing said: "If so, did Huan set the thought?"

entries.zh: 文祖曰：「西方評敞甚重，優於楊桓。
entries.en: Yao Wenzu said, "The west ranks Zong Chang very high, above Yang Huan.
entries.literal: Wenzu said: "The west ranks Chang very high, above Yang Huan.

entries.zh: 敞昔與呂超周旋，陛下試可問之。」
entries.en: Zong Chang formerly associated with Lü Chao—Your Majesty may try asking him."
entries.literal: Chang formerly circled with Lü Chao—Your Majesty may try asking him."

entries.zh: 興因謂超曰：「宗敞文才何如？
entries.en: He asked Lü Chao, "How is Zong Chang's literary talent?
entries.literal: Xing thereupon said to Chao: "How is Zong Chang's literary talent?

entries.zh: 可是誰輩？」
entries.en: Who is his peer?"
entries.literal: To what company does he belong?"

entries.zh: 超曰：「敞在西土，時論甚美，方敞魏之陳、徐，晉之潘、陸。」
entries.en: Lü Chao said, "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen Lin and Xu Gan of Wei, Pan Yue and Lu Ji of Jin."
entries.literal: Chao said: "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen and Xu of Wei, Pan and Lu of Jin."

entries.zh: 即以表示超曰：「涼州小地，寧有此才乎？」
entries.en: He showed the memorial: could Liangzhou produce this?"
entries.literal: Thereupon he showed the memorial to Chao, saying: "Can a small land like Liangzhou have such talent?"

entries.zh: 超曰：「臣以敞余文比之，未足稱多。
entries.en: Lü Chao said, "Compared to his other writings this does not count for much.
entries.literal: Chao said: "Your subject comparing Chang's remaining writings—this does not count as much.

entries.zh: 琳琅出於昆嶺，明珠生於海濱，若必以地求人，則文命大夏之棄夫，姬昌東夷之擯士。
entries.en: Genius is not geography—Yu and Wen Wang came from humble ground.
entries.literal: Fine jade comes from Kun range, bright pearls from the sea shore—if you must seek men by locality, then Wenming was a cast-off man of great Xia, Jichang a rejected scholar of eastern Yi.

entries.zh: 但當問其文彩何如，不可以區宇格物。」
entries.en: Judge the prose, not the map."
entries.literal: You should only ask how the literary color is; you cannot use region to measure things."

entries.zh: 興悅，赦尚之罪，以為尚書。
entries.en: Yao Xing freed Wang Shang and named him director of the secretariat.
entries.literal: Xing was pleased, pardoned Shang's crime, and made him Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 姚興
entries.en: Biography of Yao Xing.
entries.literal: Yao Xing.

entries.en: The first installment of the account.
entries.literal: (Part One)

entries.zh: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓，次於彭城，遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡入自淮、肥，攻漆丘、項城，將軍沈林子自汴入河，攻倉垣。
entries.en: Soon Liu Yu of Jin massed at Pengcheng and sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e through Huai-Fei against Qiqiu and Xiangcheng while Shen Linzi struck Cangyuan from Bian.
entries.literal: Before long Jin Grand Commandant Liu Yu commanded the great host to campaign against Hong, halted at Pengcheng, sent General Who Wins the Championship Tan Daoji and General Who Soars like Dragon Wang Zhen'e in from Huai and Fei to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng, General Shen Linzi from Bian into the He to attack Cangyuan.

entries.zh: 泓將王苟生以漆丘降鎮惡，徐州刺史姚掌以項城降道濟，王師遂入潁口，所至多降服。
entries.en: Wang Gousheng yielded Qiqiu to Wang Zhen'e, Yao Zhang yielded Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji, and the Jin host poured through Yingkou almost unopposed.
entries.literal: Hong's general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Zhen'e; Xuzhou Inspector Yao Zhang surrendered Xiangcheng to Daoji; the royal army then entered Yingkou, and wherever it went there was surrender.

entries.zh: 惟新蔡太守董遵固守不降，道濟攻破之，縛遵而致諸軍門。
entries.en: Only Dong Zun of Xin'cai held out until Tan Daoji stormed the city and bound him before the camp.
entries.literal: Only Xin'cai Grand Administrator Dong Zun firmly guarded and would not surrender; Daoji broke him, bound Zun, and brought him to the army gate.

entries.zh: 遵厲色曰：「古之王者伐國，待士以禮。
entries.en: Dong Zun snapped: "Ancient kings campaigned with courtesy toward worthy foes.
entries.literal: Zun in stern color said, "Kings of old in campaigning against states treated knights with ritual.

entries.zh: 君奈何以不義行師，待國土以非禮乎。」
entries.en: How dare you wage an unjust war and dishonor a loyal governor?"
entries.literal: How can you, sir, march with unrighteous conduct and treat a state's knights without ritual."

entries.zh: 道濟怒殺之。
entries.en: Tan Daoji killed him in fury.
entries.literal: Daoji in anger killed him.

entries.zh: 姚紹聞王師之至，還長安，言於泓曰：「晉師已過許昌，豫州、安定孤遠，卒難救衛，宜遷諸鎮戶內實京畿，可得精兵十萬，足以橫行天下。
entries.en: Yao Shao raced back to warn Yao Hong: "Jin is past Xuchang—Yuzhou and Anding are too far to save. Move frontier households into the capital for a hundred thousand veterans.
entries.literal: When Yao Shao heard the royal army had arrived, he returned to Chang'an and said to Hong, "The Jin army has passed Xuchang; Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and far; in the end hard to rescue—it is fitting to move the garrison households inward to fill the capital region; you can obtain crack troops of one hundred thousand, enough to range across the realm.

entries.zh: 假使二寇交侵，無深害也。
entries.en: Even if Bobo and Jin strike together, a thick core can absorb the blow.
entries.literal: Even if the two bandits jointly invade, there is no deep harm.

entries.zh: 如其不爾，晉侵豫州，勃勃寇安定者，將若之何！
entries.en: Otherwise Jin will chew Yuzhou while Bobo gnaws Anding—what then?
entries.literal: If it is not so—Jin invading Yuzhou and Bobo raiding Anding—what is to be done!

entries.zh: 事機已至，宜在速決。」
entries.en: The hour demands a fast decision."
entries.literal: The moment of affairs has arrived; it is fitting to decide with speed."

entries.zh: 其左僕射梁喜曰：「齊公恢雄勇有威名，為嶺北所憚，鎮人已與勃勃深仇，理應守死無貳，勃勃終不能棄安定遠寇京畿。
entries.en: Liang Xi argued: "Yao Hui terrifies the north; his garrisons hate Bobo and will die before yielding—Bobo cannot skip Anding to strike the core.
entries.literal: His left vice-director Liang Xi said, "Duke of Qi Hui is fierce and brave and has an awesome name, feared north of the ridge; the garrison people already have deep hatred with Bobo, by principle ought to guard unto death without second mind—Bobo in the end cannot abandon Anding and raid the capital region far.

entries.zh: 若無安定，虜馬必及於郿、雍。
entries.en: Lose Anding and enemy horsemen will reach Mei and Yong.
entries.literal: If there is no Anding, enemy horses will surely reach Mei and Yong.

entries.zh: 今關中兵馬足距晉師，豈可未有憂危先自削損也。」
entries.en: Guanzhong can still face Jin—why cripple yourself before the crisis?"
entries.literal: Now Guanzhong troops and horses are enough to stop the Jin army—how can one, not yet having worry and peril, first wound oneself by cutting away!"

entries.zh: 泓從之。
entries.en: Yao Hong sided with Liang Xi.
entries.literal: Hong followed him.

entries.zh: 吏部郎懿橫密言於泓曰：「齊公恢于廣平之難有忠勳于陛下，自陛下龍飛紹統，未有殊賞以答其意。
entries.en: Personnel clerk Yi Heng whispered: "Yao Hui saved you at Guangping yet has never been richly rewarded.
entries.literal: Personnel Director Yi Heng secretly said to Hong, "Duke of Qi Hui at the Guangping crisis had loyal merit toward Your Majesty; since Your Majesty's dragon flight and succession, there has been no special reward to answer his intent.

entries.zh: 今外則致之死地，內則不豫朝權，安定人自以孤危逼寇，欲思南遷者十室而九，若擁精兵四萬，鼓行而向京師，得不為社稷之累乎！
entries.en: Now outside he is cast into a dead place, and inside he does not share court power; the men of Anding think themselves isolated and pressed by the raider—nine houses in ten wish to move south. If he rallies forty thousand crack troops and drums his march on the capital, would that not burden the altars?
entries.literal: Now outside he is cast into a dead place, inside he does not share court power; Anding men themselves think isolated and endangered by the raider—those who wish to think of moving south are nine houses in ten—if he rallies crack troops of forty thousand and drums his march toward the capital, could it not be a burden on the altars!

entries.zh: 宜征還朝廷，以慰其心。」
entries.en: Recall him to the capital to calm him."
entries.literal: It is fitting to summon him back to court to comfort his mind."

entries.zh: 泓曰：「恢若懷不逞之心，征之適所以速禍耳。」
entries.en: Yao Hong said: "If Yao Hui is disloyal, recalling him would only hasten revolt."
entries.literal: Hong said, "If Hui harbors a mind of unfulfilled ambition, summoning him would only hasten disaster."

entries.zh: 又不從。
entries.en: He refused again.
entries.literal: Again he did not follow.

entries.zh: 檀道濟、沈林子攻拔襄邑堡，建威薛帛奔河東。
entries.en: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi took Xiangyi; Xue Bo ran to Hedong.
entries.literal: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi attacked and took Xiangyi stockade; Jianwei Xue Bo fled to Hedong.

entries.zh: 道濟白陝北渡，攻蒲阪，使將軍苟卓攻匈奴堡，為泓甯東姚成都所敗。
entries.en: Tan Daoji crossed north against Puban; Gou Zhuo lost to Yao Chengdu at Xiongnu Fort.
entries.literal: Daoji crossed north from Shan, attacked Puban, sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort, and was defeated by Hong's General Who Calms the East Yao Chengdu.

entries.zh: 泓遣姚驢救蒲阪，胡翼度據潼關。
entries.en: Yao Hong sent Yao Lü to Puban and Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.
entries.literal: Hong sent Yao Lü to rescue Puban; Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 泓進紹太宰、大將軍、大都督、都督中外諸軍事、假黃鋮，改封魯公，侍中、司隸、宗正、節錄並如故，朝之大政皆往決焉。
entries.en: Yao Hong made Yao Shao supreme commander with the yellow axe and Lu dukedom, leaving all war policy to him.
entries.literal: Hong advanced Shao to grand tutor, grand general, grand commander-in-chief, commander of all military affairs within and without, granted yellow battle-axe, changed enfeoffment to duke of Lu—palace attendant, director of Sizhou, director of clan affairs, holding seal and tallies as before; great court policy all went to decide there.

entries.zh: 紹固辭，弗許。
entries.en: Yao Shao refused the honors; Yao Hong insisted.
entries.literal: Shao firmly declined; he was not permitted.

entries.zh: 於是遣紹率武衛姚鸞等步騎五萬，距王師於潼關。
entries.en: He sent Yao Shao with fifty thousand men to Tong Pass.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent Shao leading Martial Guard Yao Luan and others, fifty thousand foot and horse, to block the royal army at Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 姚驢與并州刺史尹昭為表裏之勢，夾攻道濟。
entries.en: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao hit Tan Daoji from two sides.
entries.literal: Yao Lü and Bingzhou Inspector Yin Zhao formed inner-outer posture and jointly attacked Daoji.

entries.zh: 道濟深壁不戰，沈林子說道濟曰：「今蒲阪城堅池浚，非可卒克，攻之傷眾，守之引日，不如棄之，先事潼關。
entries.en: Shen Linzi urged Tan Daoji, saying, "Puban is walled and moated too strong for a quick assault; attacking bleeds the army, holding it wastes days. Abandon it and strike Tong Pass first.
entries.literal: Daoji kept deep walls and did not fight; Shen Linzi persuaded Daoji, saying, "Now Puban city is firm and moat deep—not to be taken in haste; attacking it wounds the host, guarding it draws out days—better to abandon it and first strike Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 潼關天限，形勝之地，鎮惡孤軍，勢危力寡，若使姚紹據之，則難圖矣。
entries.en: Tong Pass is Heaven's barrier, a place of advantageous terrain; Zhen'e is an isolated army, his situation perilous and his force small—if Yao Shao is allowed to hold it, he will be hard to deal with.
entries.literal: Tong Pass is Heaven's barrier, a place of terrain's advantage; Zhen'e is an isolated army, situation perilous and force small—if you let Yao Shao hold it, it will be hard to plan.

entries.zh: 如克潼關，紹可不戰而服。」
entries.en: Seize the pass and Yao Shao will submit without fighting."
entries.literal: If you take Tong Pass, Shao can be subdued without battle."

entries.zh: 道濟從之，乃棄蒲阪，南向潼關。
entries.en: Tan Daoji gave up Puban and marched on Tong Pass.
entries.literal: Daoji followed it, then abandoned Puban and went south toward Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 姚贊率禁兵七千，自渭北而東，進據蒲津。
entries.en: Yao Zan took seven thousand palace guards to Pu ford.
entries.literal: Yao Zan led seven thousand household troops from north of the Wei eastward and advanced to occupy Pu ford.

entries.zh: 劉裕使沈田子及傅弘之率眾萬餘人入上洛，所在多委城鎮奔長安。
entries.en: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo; towns collapsed toward the capital.
entries.literal: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi leading more than ten thousand to enter Shangluo; place after place mostly abandoned cities and towns and fled to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 田子等進及青泥，姚紹方陣而前，以距道濟。
entries.en: Shen Tianzi reached Qingni while Yao Shao advanced to face Tan Daoji.
entries.literal: Tianzi and others advanced as far as Qingni; Yao Shao formed square array and advanced to block Daoji.

entries.zh: 道濟固壘不戰，紹乃攻其西營，不克，遂以大眾逼之。
entries.en: Tan Daoji stayed behind walls; Yao Shao stormed his west camp, failed, then massed against him.
entries.literal: Daoji kept firm ramparts and did not fight; Shao then attacked his western camp, did not take it, then pressed with the great host.

entries.zh: 道濟率王敬、沈林子等逆沖紹軍，將士驚散，引還定城。
entries.en: Tan Daoji led Wang Jing, Shen Linzi, and others in a straight charge at Shao's army; Shao's officers and soldiers were startled and scattered and drew back to Dingcheng.
entries.literal: Daoji led Wang Chong, Shen Linzi and others to charge straight at Shao's army; officers and soldiers startled and scattered, drew back to Dingcheng.

entries.zh: 紹留姚鸞守險，絕道濟糧道。
entries.en: Yao Shao left Yao Luan to choke Tan Daoji's supply line.
entries.literal: Shao left Yao Luan guarding the narrows, cutting Daoji's grain road.

entries.zh: 時裕別將姚珍入自子午，竇霸入自洛穀，眾各數千人。
entries.en: Liu Yu's columns entered from Ziwu and Luogu valleys.
entries.literal: At the time Liu Yu's separate general Yao Zhen entered from Ziwu, Dou Ba entered from Luogu, each several thousand.

entries.zh: 泓遣姚萬距霸，姚彊距珍。
entries.en: Yao Hong sent Yao Wan and Yao Qiang to meet them.
entries.literal: Hong sent Yao Wan to block Ba, Yao Qiang to block Zhen.

entries.zh: 姚鸞遣將尹雅與道濟司馬徐琰于潼關南，為琰所獲，送之劉裕。
entries.en: Yin Ya was captured by Xu Yan and sent to Liu Yu.
entries.literal: Yao Luan sent general Yin Ya against Daoji's major Xu Yan south of Tong Pass; Ya was seized by Yan and sent to Liu Yu.

entries.zh: 裕以雅前叛，欲殺之。
entries.en: Liu Yu meant to execute Yin Ya for past treason.
entries.literal: Yu because Ya had formerly rebelled, wished to kill him.

entries.zh: 雅曰：「前活本在望外，今死寧不甘心。
entries.en: Yin Ya said: "You spared me once; now I will not beg like a coward.
entries.literal: Ya said, "Formerly living was already beyond expectation; now death surely I do not willingly accept.

entries.zh: 明公將以大義平天下，豈可使秦無守信之臣乎！」
entries.en: You claim to conquer by virtue—do not kill the one Qin man who keeps faith!"
entries.literal: The enlightened lord will use great righteousness to pacify the realm—how can you make Qin lack a faithful subject!"

entries.zh: 裕嘉而免之。
entries.en: Liu Yu admired him and let him live.
entries.literal: Yu praised him and spared him.

entries.zh: 泓遣給事黃門侍郎姚和都屯于堯柳，以備田子。
entries.en: Yao Hong posted Yao Hedou at Yaoliu against Shen Tianzi.
entries.literal: Hong sent attendant gentleman Huangmen Yao Hedou to camp at Yaoliu to prepare for Tianzi.

entries.zh: 姚紹謂諸將曰：「道濟等遠來送死，眾旅不多，嬰壘自固者，正欲曠日持久，以待繼援耳。
entries.en: Yao Shao told his generals: "Jin hugs its walls waiting for reinforcements.
entries.literal: Yao Shao said to the generals, "Daoji and others have come from afar to deliver death; their hosts are not many; hugging ramparts and self-fortifying—they only wish to prolong days and months to await follow-up relief.

entries.zh: 吾欲分軍還據閿鄉，以絕其糧運，不至一月，道濟之首可懸之麾下矣。
entries.en: Send a column to Wenxiang to sever their supplies and Tan Daoji's head will be on your pole within a month.
entries.literal: I wish to divide the army and return to hold Wenxiang to cut their grain transport—within not one month, Daoji's head can hang beneath the banner.

entries.zh: 濟等既沒，裕計自沮。」
entries.en: Kill Tan Daoji and Liu Yu loses his spear point."
entries.literal: Once Ji and others are gone, Yu's plan will naturally be blocked."

entries.zh: 諸將咸以為然。
entries.en: The generals agreed.
entries.literal: All generals all thought it right.

entries.zh: 其將胡翼度曰：「軍勢宜集不可以分，若偏師不利，人心駭懼，胡可以戰！」
entries.en: Hu Yidu objected: "Split the army and one defeat routs every heart—you cannot fight divided."
entries.literal: His general Hu Yidu said, "Army momentum ought to be gathered and cannot be divided; if a partial army is not successful, human hearts will be terrified with alarm—how then can we fight!"

entries.zh: 紹乃止。
entries.en: Yao Shao dropped his plan to split the army.
entries.literal: Shao then desisted.

entries.zh: 薛帛據河曲以叛。
entries.en: Xue Bo rebelled from the river bend.
entries.literal: Xue Bo occupied the river bend in revolt.

entries.zh: 紹分道置諸軍為掎角之勢，遣輔國胡翼度據東原，武衛姚鸞營于大路，與晉軍相接。
entries.en: Yao Shao spread his wings: Hu Yidu on the east plain, Yao Luan on the main road, pressing Jin.
entries.literal: Shao divided roads and set various armies in horn-and-flank posture, sent General Who Supports the State Hu Yidu to hold the eastern plain, Martial Guard Yao Luan to camp on the great road, connecting with the Jin army.

entries.zh: 沈林子簡精銳銜枚夜襲之，鸞眾潰戰死，士卒死者九千餘人。
entries.en: Shen Linzi night-attacked; Yao Luan fell with nine thousand men.
entries.literal: Shen Linzi picked crack troops, held mouthpieces for a night raid; Luan's host broke in battle and died; more than nine thousand soldiers died.

entries.zh: 姚贊屯於河上，遣恢武姚難運蒲阪穀以給其軍，至香城，為王師所敗。
entries.en: Yao Zan tried to ship grain from Puban but Jin smashed the train at Xiangcheng.
entries.literal: Yao Zan camped on the river, sent General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to transport Puban grain to supply the army; reaching Xiangcheng, he was defeated by the royal army.

entries.zh: 時泓遣姚諶守堯柳，姚和都討薛帛於河東，聞王師要難，乃兼道赴救，未至而難敗，固破裕裨將于河曲，遂屯蒲阪。
entries.en: Yao Chen raced to save Yao Nan, missed him, but beat a Jin column in the bend and held Puban.
entries.literal: At the time Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu, Yao Hedou campaigned against Xue Bo in Hedong; hearing the royal army was intercepting Nan, they hurried by combined roads to rescue; before arriving Nan was defeated, yet they broke Liu Yu's lieutenant at the river bend, then camped at Puban.

entries.zh: 姚贊為林子所敗，單馬奔定城。
entries.en: Yao Zan fled alone to Dingcheng after Shen Linzi routed him.
entries.literal: Yao Zan was defeated by Linzi, alone on horseback fled to Dingcheng.

entries.zh: 紹遣左長史姚洽及姚墨蠡等率騎三千屯于河北之九原，欲絕道濟諸縣租輸。
entries.en: Yao Shao sent Yao Qia to Jiuyuan to choke Tan Daoji's supply convoys.
entries.literal: Shao sent left chief clerk Yao Qia and Yao Moli and others leading three thousand horse to camp at Jiuyuan north of the He, wishing to cut off Daoji's county rent convoys.

entries.zh: 洽辭曰：「夫小敵之堅，大敵之擒。
entries.en: Yao Qia refused: "A small force that stands stubborn becomes bait.
entries.literal: Qia declined, saying, "The firmness of a small enemy is the great enemy's catch.

entries.zh: 今兵眾單弱，而遠在河外，雖明公神武，然鞭短勢殊，恐無所及。」
entries.en: We are too few and too far—even you cannot stretch a whip across the river."
entries.literal: Now the troops are few and weak and far beyond the river—though the enlightened lord is divinely martial, yet the whip is short and the power situation unequal—I fear there is no reaching them."

entries.zh: 紹不聽。
entries.en: Yao Shao ignored him.
entries.literal: Shao did not listen.

entries.zh: 沈林子率眾八千，耍洽於河上，洽戰死，眾皆沒。
entries.en: Shen Linzi destroyed Yao Qia on the riverbank.
entries.literal: Shen Linzi led eight thousand hosts, intercepted Qia on the river; Qia died in battle, the host all perished.

entries.zh: 紹聞洽等敗，忿恚發病，托姚贊以後事，使姚難屯關西，紹嘔血而死。
entries.en: Yao Shao died of rage and bleeding after Yao Qia's loss.
entries.literal: When Shao heard Qia and others were defeated, anger and vexation brought illness; he entrusted later affairs to Yao Zan, sent Yao Nan to camp west of the pass; Shao vomited blood and died.

entries.zh: 泓以晉師之逼，遣使乞師于魏。
entries.en: Yao Hong begged Northern Wei for aid against Jin.
entries.literal: Because the Jin army pressed, Hong sent envoys begging troops from Wei.

entries.zh: 魏遣司徒、南平公拔拔嵩，正直將軍、安平公乙旃眷，進據河內，遊擊將軍王洛生屯於河東，為泓聲援。
entries.en: Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, Straight General Duke of Anping Yizhan Juan, and Raiding General Wang Luosheng to occupy Henei and Hedong as support for Yao Hong.
entries.literal: Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, Straight General Duke of Anping Yizhan Juan, and Raiding General Wang Luosheng; they advanced to occupy Henei, and Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong, as sounding support for Hong.

entries.zh: 劉裕次於陝城，遣沈林子率精兵萬餘，越山開道，會沈田子等於青泥，將攻堯柳。
entries.en: Liu Yu halted at Shan city and sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand crack troops over the mountains to join Shen Tianzi and others at Qingni, intending to attack Yaoliu.
entries.literal: Liu Yu halted at Shan city, sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand crack troops to cross mountains opening roads, join Shen Tianzi and others at Qingni, planning to attack Yaoliu.

entries.zh: 泓使姚裕率步騎八千距之，泓躬將大眾繼發。
entries.en: Yao Hong marched with Yao Yu to meet them.
entries.literal: Hong sent Yao Yu with eight thousand foot and horse to block them; Hong personally led the great host to follow.

entries.zh: 裕為田子所敗，泓退次於灞上，關中郡縣多潛通于王師。
entries.en: Yao Yu lost to Shen Tianzi; Yao Hong fell back to Bashang as towns went over to Jin.
entries.literal: Yu was defeated by Tianzi; Hong drew back to camp at Bashang; many Guanzhong counties secretly communicated with the royal army.

entries.zh: 劉裕至潼關，遣將軍硃超石、徐猗之會薛帛于河北，以攻蒲阪。
entries.en: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yi to join Xue Bo north of the He to attack Puban.
entries.literal: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass, sent generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yi to join Xue Bo north of the He to attack Puban.

entries.zh: 姚贊距裕于關西，姚難屯於香城。
entries.en: Yao Zan faced Liu Yu; Yao Nan held Xiangcheng.
entries.literal: Yao Zan blocked Yu west of the pass; Yao Nan camped at Xiangcheng.

entries.zh: 裕遣王鎮惡、王敬自秋社西渡渭，以逼難軍。
entries.en: Liu Yu sent Wang Zhen'e and Wang Jing west from Qiushe to cross the Wei, pressing Nan's army.
entries.literal: Yu sent Wang Zhen'e and Wang Chong west from Qiushe to cross the Wei, pressing Nan's army.

entries.zh: 鎮東姚璞及姚和都擊敗猗之等於蒲阪，猗之遇害，超石棄其眾奔於潼關。
entries.en: Yao Pu crushed Jin at Puban; Xu Yi died and Zhu Chaoshi ran.
entries.literal: General Who Conquers the East Yao Pu and Yao Hedou defeated Yi and others at Puban; Yi met death; Chaoshi abandoned his host and fled to Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 姚贊遣司馬休之及司馬國璠自軹關向河內，引魏軍以躡裕後。
entries.en: Yao Zan sent Sima Xiuzhi and Sima Guofan from Zhiguan toward Henei, drawing Wei troops to fall on Liu Yu's rear.
entries.literal: Yao Zan sent Sima Xiuzhi and Sima Guofan from Zhiguan toward Henei, drawing Wei troops to tread on Yu's rear.

entries.zh: 姚難既為鎮惡所逼，引師而西。
entries.en: Yao Nan retreated west before Wang Zhen'e.
entries.literal: Nan, already pressed by Zhen'e, drew the army westward.

entries.zh: 時大霖雨，渭水泛溢，贊等不得北渡。
entries.en: Floods blocked Yao Zan from crossing the Wei.
entries.literal: At the time great rains fell in succession, the Wei overflowed; Zan and others could not cross north.

entries.zh: 鎮惡水陸兼進，追及姚難。
entries.en: Wang Zhen'e overtook Yao Nan in the flood season.
entries.literal: Zhen'e advanced by water and land together, caught up with Yao Nan.

entries.zh: 泓自灞上還軍，次於石橋以援之。
entries.en: Yao Hong rushed to Stone Bridge to help.
entries.literal: Hong returned the army from Bashang, halted at Stone Bridge to aid him.

entries.zh: 贊退屯鄭城。
entries.en: Yao Zan fell back to Zheng.
entries.literal: Zan drew back to camp at Zheng city.

entries.zh: 鎮北姚彊率郡人數千，與姚難陣於涇上，以距鎮惡。
entries.en: Yao Qiang joined Yao Nan on the Jing River line.
entries.literal: General Who Conquers the North Yao Qiang led several thousand commandery people and with Yao Nan formed array on the Jing to block Zhen'e.

entries.zh: 鎮惡遣毛德祖擊彊，大敗，彊戰死，難遁還長安。
entries.en: Mao Dezu killed Yao Qiang; Yao Nan bolted for Chang'an.
entries.literal: Zhen'e sent Mao Dezu to strike Qiang, greatly defeated him; Qiang died in battle; Nan fled back to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 劉裕進據鄭城。
entries.en: Liu Yu took Zheng.
entries.literal: Liu Yu advanced and occupied Zheng city.

entries.zh: 泓使姚裕、尚書龐統屯兵宮中，姚洸屯於灃西，尚書姚白瓜徙四軍雜戶入長安，姚丕守渭橋，胡翼度屯石積，姚贊屯霸東，泓軍於逍遙園。
entries.en: Yao Hong sent Yao Yu and the minister Pang Tong to station troops in the palace, Yao Guang to garrison west of Feng, the minister Yao Baigua to move the mixed households of the four armies into Chang'an, Yao Pi to guard the Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu to garrison Shiji, Yao Zan to garrison east of the Ba, while Hong himself encamped at Xiaoyao Garden.
entries.literal: Hong sent Yao Yu and Minister Pang Tong to camp troops in the palace, Yao Guang west of the Feng, Minister Yao Baigua moved four-army miscellaneous households into Chang'an, Yao Pi guarded Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu camped at Stone Accumulation, Yao Zan east of Ba; Hong encamped at Free-Roam Garden.

entries.zh: 鎮惡夾渭進兵，破姚丕於渭橋。
entries.en: Wang Zhen'e shattered Yao Pi at the Wei bridge.
entries.literal: Zhen'e advanced troops on both sides of the Wei, defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.

entries.zh: 泓自逍遙園赴之，逼水地狹，因丕之敗，遂相踐而退。
entries.en: Yao Hong's relief column stampeded itself in the narrow river flats.
entries.literal: Hong went from Free-Roam Garden to aid him; pressed by water, ground narrow, because of Pi's defeat, they trampled each other in retreat.

entries.zh: 姚諶及前軍姚烈、左衛姚寶安、散騎王帛、建武姚進、揚威姚蠔、尚書右丞孫玄等皆死於陣，泓單馬還宮。
entries.en: Yao Chen; Yao Lie of the Vanguard; Yao Bao'an of the Left Guard; Cavalier Attendant Wang Bo; General Who Establishes Martial Might Yao Jin; General Who Displays Might Yao Hao; Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Sun Xuan; and the others all died in battle. Yao Hong rode back to the palace alone.
entries.literal: Yao Chen and forward army Yao Lie, left guard Yao Bao'an, supernumerary Wang Bo, Jianwei Yao Jin, General Who Displays Might Yao Hao, right aide Sun Xuan and others all died in formation; Hong alone on horseback returned to the palace.

entries.zh: 鎮惡入自平朔門，泓與姚裕等數百騎出奔于石橋。
entries.en: Wang Zhen'e broke Pingshuo Gate; Yao Hong fled toward Stone Bridge.
entries.literal: Zhen'e entered from Pingshuo Gate; Hong with Yao Yu and several hundred horse fled out toward Stone Bridge.

entries.zh: 贊聞泓之敗也，召將士告之，眾皆以刀擊地，攘袂大泣。
entries.en: Yao Zan's men wept and beat the ground when they heard the news.
entries.literal: When Zan heard of Hong's defeat, he summoned officers and soldiers and told them; all struck the earth with knives, pulled sleeves and wept greatly.

entries.zh: 胡翼度先與劉裕陰通，是日棄眾奔裕。
entries.en: Hu Yidu defected to Liu Yu.
entries.literal: Hu Yidu had earlier secretly communicated with Liu Yu; that day he abandoned the host and fled to Yu.

entries.zh: 贊夜率諸軍，將會泓于石橋，王師已固諸門，贊軍不得入，眾皆驚散。
entries.en: Yao Zan could not re-enter the sealed capital.
entries.literal: Zan by night led all armies, planning to join Hong at Stone Bridge; the royal army had already secured all gates; Zan's army could not enter; the host all startled and scattered.

entries.zh: 姚萇以孝武太元九年僭立，至泓三世，以安帝義熙十三年而滅，凡三十二年。
entries.en: From Yao Chang's usurpation in the ninth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu to the fall in the thirteenth year of Yixi under Emperor An, the Later Qin lasted three reigns and thirty-two years.
entries.literal: Yao Chang presumptuously rose in the ninth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu; down to Hong three generations; in the thirteenth year of Yixi under Emperor An they perished—thirty-two years in all.

entries.zh: 元子以庸懦之質，屬傾擾之餘，內難方殷，外禦斯輟。
entries.en: Yao Hong was weak when kin tore the realm apart and Jin struck.
entries.literal: Yuanzi with a mediocre and timid substance, amid the aftermath of overturn and turmoil, inner disaster just raging, outer defense then ceased.

entries.zh: 王師杖順，弭節而下長安；
entries.en: Jin marched in righteousness and took Chang'an;
entries.literal: The royal army wielded obedience, lowered the pace and descended on Chang'an;

entries.zh: 凶嗣失圖，系組而降軹道。
entries.en: the last heir bound himself at Zhidao.
entries.literal: the wicked heir lost his plan, tied cord and surrendered at Zhidao.

entries.zh: 物極則反，抑斯之謂歟！
entries.en: Thus the wheel turns: extremes invite reversal.
entries.literal: Things extreme then reverse—does this say it!

entries.zh: 泓計無所出，謀欲降於裕。
entries.en: Yao Hong decided to surrender to Liu Yu.
entries.literal: Hong had no plan left, plotted wishing to surrender to Yu.

entries.zh: 其子佛念，年十一，謂泓曰：「晉人將逞其欲，終必不全，願自裁決。」
entries.en: His eleven-year-old son Yao Fonian said: "Surrender will not save us—better to die cleanly."
entries.literal: His son Fonian, age eleven, said to Hong, "The Jin people will indulge their desires to the end—you will surely not be preserved whole; I wish to decide for myself."

entries.zh: 泓憮然不答。
entries.en: Yao Hong could not answer.
entries.literal: Hong looked mournful and did not answer.

entries.zh: 佛念遂登宮牆自投而死。
entries.en: Yao Fonian leaped from the palace wall.
entries.literal: Fonian then climbed the palace wall and threw himself down to die.

entries.zh: 泓將妻子詣壘門而降。
entries.en: Yao Hong brought his family to Liu Yu's camp and yielded.
entries.literal: Hong led wife and children to the camp gate and surrendered.

entries.zh: 贊率宗室子弟百餘人亦降於裕，裕盡殺之，余宗遷於江南。
entries.en: Liu Yu slaughtered the surrendered Yao princes and deported the clan to the south.
entries.literal: Zan led more than a hundred sons and nephews of the imperial clan also to surrender to Yu; Yu killed them all; the rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangzi.

entries.zh: 送泓于建康市斬之，時年三十，在位二年。
entries.en: Yao Hong was executed in the Jiankang market at thirty after two years' reign.
entries.literal: They sent Hong to Jiankang market and beheaded him; he was thirty years old, on the throne two years.

entries.zh: 建康百里之內，草木皆燋死焉。
entries.en: Within a hundred li of Jiankang, grass and trees all scorched dead.
entries.literal: Within a hundred li of Jiankang, grass and trees all scorched dead.

entries.zh: 姚泓
entries.en: Yao Hong.
entries.literal: Section heading: Yao Hong.

entries.zh: 至是，慕容寶自龍城南奔至黎陽，遣其中黃門令趙思召慕容鍾來迎。
entries.en: Murong Bao then fled south from Longcheng to Liyang and dispatched Zhao Si, his central palace gate director, to call Murong Zhong to escort him.
entries.literal: At this point Murong Bao fled south from Longcheng to Liyang and sent his central yellow-gate director Zhao Si to summon Murong Zhong to come welcome him.

entries.zh: 鍾本首議勸德稱尊號，聞而惡之，執思付獄，馳使白狀。
entries.en: Murong Zhong, who had first urged Murong De to take the throne, took offense, jailed Zhao Si, and sent a courier to inform Murong De.
entries.literal: Murong Zhong had originally been first to urge Murong De to assume the exalted title, and when he heard this he hated it, seized Zhao Si and handed him to prison, and galloped a messenger to report the situation.

entries.zh: 德謂其下曰：「卿等前以社稷大計，勸吾攝政。
entries.en: Murong De told his subordinates: “Earlier, for the great plan of the altars of state, you urged me to take the regency.
entries.literal: Murong De told his subordinates: “Earlier, for the great plan of the altars of state, you urged me to take the regency.

entries.zh: 吾亦以嗣帝奔亡，人神曠主，故權順群議，以系眾望。
entries.en: I also, because the heir emperor had fled and men and spirits lacked a lord, temporarily followed the counsel of the crowd in order to hold the hopes of the multitude.
entries.literal: I also, because the heir emperor had fled and men and spirits lacked a lord, temporarily followed the counsel of the crowd in order to hold the hopes of the multitude.

entries.zh: 今天方悔禍，嗣帝得還，吾將具駕奉迎，謝罪行闕，然後角巾私第，卿等以為何如？」
entries.en: Now Heaven is beginning to repent of the calamity, and the heir emperor may return. I will prepare my carriage to welcome him, apologize for my crimes at the traveling palace, and afterward retire in a scholar’s headcloth to a private house. What do you think?”
entries.literal: Now Heaven is beginning to repent of the calamity, and the heir emperor may return. I will prepare my carriage to welcome him, apologize for my crimes at the traveling palace, and afterward retire in a scholar’s headcloth to a private house. What do you think?”

entries.zh: 其黃門侍郎張華進曰：「夫爭奪之世，非雄才不振；
entries.en: His Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Zhang Hua stepped forward and said: “In an age of struggle, only heroic talent can rouse the realm;
entries.literal: His Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Zhang Hua stepped forward and said: “In an age of struggle, only heroic talent can rouse the realm;

entries.zh: 從橫之時，豈懦夫能濟！
entries.en: in a time of maneuvering, how could a coward accomplish rescue?
entries.literal: in a time of maneuvering, how could a coward accomplish rescue?

entries.zh: 陛下若蹈匹婦之仁，舍天授之業，威權一去，則身首不保，何退讓之有乎！」
entries.en: If Your Majesty treads the kindness of a common woman, abandons the enterprise bestowed by Heaven, and lets authority and awe depart, then body and head will not be preserved. What room is there for yielding?”
entries.literal: If Your Majesty treads the kindness of a common woman, abandons the enterprise bestowed by Heaven, and lets authority and awe depart, then body and head will not be preserved. What room is there for yielding?”

entries.zh: 德曰：「吾以古人逆取順守，其道未足，所以中路徘徊，悵然未決耳。」
entries.en: Murong De said: “I considered how the ancients seized power against the current and guarded it in accord with right, but my way is not yet sufficient; that is why I halted midway in hesitation, despondent and undecided.”
entries.literal: Murong De said: “I considered how the ancients seized power against the current and guarded it in accord with right, but my way is not yet sufficient; that is why I halted midway in hesitation, despondent and undecided.”

entries.zh: 慕輿護請馳問寶虛實，德流涕而遣之。
entries.en: Yu Hu volunteered to ride north and learn Murong Bao's true situation; Murong De sent him off in tears.
entries.literal: Yu Hu requested to gallop and inquire into Murong Bao's truth and falsehood, and Murong De wept as he sent him.

entries.zh: 乃率壯士數百，隨思而北，因謀殺寶。
entries.en: He led hundreds of picked men north with Zhao Si plotting to murder Murong Bao.
entries.literal: Yu Hu then led several hundred stalwarts and followed Zhao Si northward and plotted to kill Murong Bao.

entries.zh: 初，寶遣思之後，知德攝位，懼而北奔。
entries.en: After dispatching Zhao Si, Murong Bao had learned of Murong De's assumption of power and fled north in fear.
entries.literal: Earlier, after Murong Bao had sent Zhao Si, he learned that Murong De had taken the position and was afraid and fled north.

entries.zh: 護至無所見，執思而還。
entries.en: Yu Hu found no sign of Murong Bao, seized Zhao Si, and came back.
entries.literal: When Yu Hu arrived he saw nothing, seized Zhao Si, and returned.

entries.zh: 德以思閑習典故，將任之。
entries.en: Murong De intended to employ Zhao Si for his knowledge of court precedent.
entries.literal: Murong De, because Zhao Si was versed in precedents and stories, was about to employ him.

entries.zh: 思曰：「昔關羽見重曹公，猶不忘先主之恩。
entries.en: Zhao Si said: “Formerly Guan Yu was esteemed by Cao Cao, yet still did not forget his former lord’s kindness.
entries.literal: Zhao Si said: “Formerly Guan Yu was esteemed by Cao Cao, yet still did not forget his former lord’s kindness.

entries.zh: 思雖刑餘賤隸，荷國寵靈，犬馬有心，而況人乎！
entries.en: Though I, Si, am a mutilated and base slave, I have received the state’s favor. Dogs and horses have hearts; how much more men!
entries.literal: Though I, Si, am a mutilated and base slave, I have received the state’s favor. Dogs and horses have hearts; how much more men!

entries.zh: 乞還就上，以明微節。」
entries.en: I beg to return to my sovereign in order to make clear my slight integrity.”
entries.literal: I beg to return to my sovereign in order to make clear my slight integrity.”

entries.zh: 德固留之，思怒曰：「周室衰微，晉、鄭夾輔；
entries.en: Murong De firmly detained him. Si grew angry and said: “When the Zhou house declined, Jin and Zheng supported it on either side;
entries.literal: Murong De firmly detained him. Si grew angry and said: “When the Zhou house declined, Jin and Zheng supported it on either side;
