entries.zh: 漢有七國之難，實賴梁王。
entries.en: when Han suffered the trouble of the seven states, it truly relied on the Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: when Han suffered the trouble of the seven states, it truly relied on the Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 殿下親則叔父，位則上臺，不能率先群後以匡王室，而幸根本之傾為趙倫之事。
entries.en: Your Highness, in kinship, is the emperor’s uncle, and in rank you stand among the highest ministers, yet you cannot lead the lords in aiding the royal house, but instead rejoice in the collapse of the root and foundation and act like Zhao Lun.
entries.literal: Your Highness, in kinship, is the emperor’s uncle, and in rank you stand among the highest ministers, yet you cannot lead the lords in aiding the royal house, but instead rejoice in the collapse of the root and foundation and act like Zhao Lun.

entries.zh: 思雖無申胥哭秦之效，猶慕君賓不生莽世。」
entries.en: Though I, Si, lack Shen Baoxu’s effect of weeping at Qin, I still admire Junbin for refusing to live in Wang Mang’s age.”
entries.literal: Though I, Si, lack Shen Baoxu’s effect of weeping at Qin, I still admire Junbin for refusing to live in Wang Mang’s age.”

entries.zh: 德怒，斬之。
entries.en: Murong De flew into a rage and had him executed.
entries.literal: De was angry and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 初，寶之至黎陽也，和長史李辯勸和納之，和不從。
entries.en: When Murong Bao came to Liyang, chief clerk Li Bian urged Murong He to admit him, but Murong He refused.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Murong Bao reached Liyang, He's chief clerk Li Bian urged He to take Bao in, and He refused.

entries.zh: 辯懼謀泄，乃引晉軍至管城，冀德親率師，於後作亂。
entries.en: Li Bian feared exposure, drew Jin troops to Guancheng, and hoped Murong De would take the field himself so Li Bian could raise revolt behind him.
entries.literal: Bian feared the plot would leak, so drew Jin troops to Guancheng, hoping De would personally lead the army and he could raise trouble in the rear.

entries.zh: 會德不出，愈不自安。
entries.en: Murong De did not march, and Li Bian grew still more anxious.
entries.literal: But De did not go out, and Bian grew even more uneasy.

entries.zh: 及德此行也，辯又勸和反，和不從。
entries.en: When Murong De set out on this campaign, Li Bian again pressed Murong He to revolt, and Murong He again refused.
entries.literal: On this expedition of De's, Bian again urged He to rebel, and He refused.

entries.zh: 辯怒，殺和，以滑台降于魏。
entries.en: Li Bian slew Murong He in rage and handed Huatai over to Wei.
entries.literal: Bian in anger killed He and surrendered Huatai to Wei.

entries.zh: 時將士家悉在城內，德將攻之，韓范言於德曰：「魏師已入城，據國成資，客主之勢，翻然復異，人情既危，不可以戰。
entries.en: At that time officers' and soldiers' families were all inside the city; De was about to attack when Han Fan said to De, 'Wei troops have entered the city, hold the state and its resources; guest and host are reversed, hearts are shaken, and we cannot fight.
entries.literal: At that time officers' and soldiers' families were all inside the city; De was about to attack when Han Fan said to De, 'Wei troops have entered the city, hold the state and its resources; guest and host are reversed, hearts are shaken, and we cannot fight.

entries.zh: 宜先據一方，為關中之基，然後畜力而圖之，計之上也。」
entries.en: We should first seize a region as a base for Guanzhong, then store strength and plan against them; that is the best plan.'
entries.literal: We should first seize a region as a base for Guanzhong, then store strength and plan against them; that is the best plan.'

entries.zh: 德乃止。
entries.en: Murong De called off the assault.
entries.literal: De then stopped.

entries.zh: 德右衛將軍慕容雲斬李辯，率將士家累二萬餘人而出，三軍慶悅。
entries.en: Right Guard general Murong Yun executed Li Bian and led out over twenty thousand dependents, to the army's delight.
entries.literal: De's Right Guard general Murong Yun beheaded Li Bian, led more than twenty thousand officers' and soldiers' dependents out, and the three armies rejoiced.

entries.zh: 德謀於眾曰：「苻廣雖平，而撫軍失據，進有強敵，退無所托，計將安出？」
entries.en: De consulted the host, saying, 'Though Fu Guang is crushed, the Pacification headquarters has lost its footing; advancing we face strong foes, retreating we have nowhere to lean; what plan should we take?'
entries.literal: De consulted the host, saying, 'Though Fu Guang is crushed, the Pacification headquarters has lost its footing; advancing we face strong foes, retreating we have nowhere to lean; what plan should we take?'

entries.zh: 張華進曰：「彭城阻帶山川，楚之舊都，地險人殷，可攻而據之，以為基本。」
entries.en: Zhang Hua stepped forward, saying, 'Pengcheng is girded by mountains and rivers, the old Chu capital; the ground is defensible and the people abundant; we can attack and hold it as our foundation.'
entries.literal: Zhang Hua stepped forward, saying, 'Pengcheng is girded by mountains and rivers, the old Chu capital; the ground is defensible and the people abundant; we can attack and hold it as our foundation.'

entries.zh: 慕容鐘、慕輿護、封逞、韓𧨳等固勸攻滑台，潘聰曰：「滑台四通八達，非帝王之居。
entries.en: Murong Zhong, Muyu Hu, Feng Cheng, Han Fan, and others strongly urged attacking Huatai; Pan Cong said, 'Huatai is a crossroads, not a place for an emperor to dwell.
entries.literal: Murong Zhong, Muyu Hu, Feng Cheng, Han Fan, and others strongly urged attacking Huatai; Pan Cong said, 'Huatai is a crossroads, not a place for an emperor to dwell.

entries.zh: 且北通大魏，西接強秦，此二國者，未可以高枕而待之。
entries.en: Moreover it opens north to Great Wei and west joins strong Qin; these two states are not to be awaited lying easy on a pillow.
entries.literal: Moreover it opens north to Great Wei and west joins strong Qin; these two states are not to be awaited lying easy on a pillow.

entries.zh: 彭城土曠人稀，地平無險，晉之歸鎮，必距王師。
entries.en: Pengcheng has broad fields and thin population, flat ground without natural barriers; Jin's returning garrison is sure to block our royal army.
entries.literal: Pengcheng has broad fields and thin population, flat ground without natural barriers; Jin's returning garrison is sure to block our royal army.

entries.zh: 又密邇江、淮，水路通浚，秋夏霖潦，千里為湖。
entries.en: It also hugs the Yangzi and Huai; waterways reach Jun, and in autumn and summer rains turn a thousand li into lakes.
entries.literal: It also hugs the Yangzi and Huai; waterways reach Jun, and in autumn and summer rains turn a thousand li into lakes.

entries.zh: 且水戰國之所短，吳之所長，今雖克之，非久安之計也。
entries.en: Moreover water war is our state's short suit and Wu's long suit; even if we take it now, it is no plan for lasting peace.
entries.literal: Moreover water war is our state's short suit and Wu's long suit; even if we take it now, it is no plan for lasting peace.

entries.zh: 青、齊沃壤，號曰東秦，土方二千，戶餘十萬，四塞之固，負海之饒，可謂用武之國。
entries.en: Qing and Qi are fertile soil called Eastern Qin, two thousand li square, more than a hundred thousand households, boxed by four passes, rich with the sea; it may be called a land for wielding arms.
entries.literal: Qing and Qi are fertile soil called Eastern Qin, two thousand li square, more than a hundred thousand households, boxed by four passes, rich with the sea; it may be called a land for wielding arms.

entries.zh: 三齊英傑，蓄志以待，孰不思得明主以立尺寸之功！
entries.en: The heroes of the three Qi have stored their will and wait; who does not long for a wise lord to win even slight merit!
entries.literal: The heroes of the three Qi have stored their will and wait; who does not long for a wise lord to win even slight merit!

entries.zh: 廣固者，曹嶷之所營，山川阻峻，足為帝王之都。
entries.en: Guanggu was built by Cao Yi; its mountains and streams are steep enough for an emperor's capital.
entries.literal: Guanggu was built by Cao Yi; its mountains and streams are steep enough for an emperor's capital.

entries.zh: 宜遣辯士馳說于前，大兵繼進於後，避閭渾昔負國恩，必翻然向化。
entries.en: We should send eloquent men ahead to persuade them, then follow with a great army; Pilü Hun, who once betrayed the state's grace, is sure to turn toward civilization.
entries.literal: We should send eloquent men ahead to persuade them, then follow with a great army; Pilü Hun, who once betrayed the state's grace, is sure to turn toward civilization.

entries.zh: 如其守迷不順，大軍臨之，自然瓦解。
entries.en: If he clings to delusion and will not submit, when the great host reaches him he will naturally crumble.
entries.literal: If he clings to delusion and will not submit, when the great host reaches him he will naturally crumble.

entries.zh: 既據之後，閉關養銳，伺隙而動，此亦二漢之有關中、河內也。」
entries.en: Once we hold it, close the passes and nurse our edge, move when a gap opens; this too is like the two Han holding Guanzhong and Henei.'
entries.literal: Once we hold it, close the passes and nurse our edge, move when a gap opens; this too is like the two Han holding Guanzhong and Henei.'

entries.zh: 德猶豫未決。
entries.en: Murong De remained undecided.
entries.literal: De still hesitated and could not decide.

entries.zh: 沙門郎公素知占候，德因訪其所適。
entries.en: Murong De consulted the monk Lang Gong, versed in astrology.
entries.literal: The monk Lang Gong was skilled in divination; De therefore asked him where they should go.

entries.zh: 郎曰：「敬覽三策，潘尚書之議可謂興邦之術矣。
entries.en: Lang said, 'I have reviewed the three plans; Minister Pan's counsel may be called a method to raise the state.
entries.literal: Lang said, 'I have reviewed the three plans; Minister Pan's counsel may be called a method to raise the state.

entries.zh: 今歲初，長星起于奎婁，遂掃虛危，而虛危，齊之分野，除舊佈新之象。
entries.en: At the year's start a long comet rose in Kui and Lou, then swept Xu and Wei; Xu and Wei are Qi's field division, an omen of removing the old and spreading the new.
entries.literal: At the year's start a long comet rose in Kui and Lou, then swept Xu and Wei; Xu and Wei are Qi's field division, an omen of removing the old and spreading the new.

entries.zh: 宜先定舊魯，巡撫琅邪，待秋風戒節，然後北圍臨齊，天之道也。」
entries.en: We should first secure old Lu, pacify Langye on tour, wait until the autumn wind sets the season, then invest Linqi from the north; that is Heaven's way.'
entries.literal: We should first secure old Lu, pacify Langye on tour, wait until the autumn wind sets the season, then invest Linqi from the north; that is Heaven's way.'

entries.zh: 德大悅，引師而南，兗州北鄙諸縣悉降，置守宰以撫之。
entries.en: Murong De marched south, winning the north of Yanzhou and installing officials.
entries.literal: De was greatly pleased, led the army south, and all counties on the northern border of Yanzhou submitted; he set governors to soothe them.

entries.zh: 存問高年，軍無私掠，百姓安之，牛酒屬路。
entries.en: His troops refrained from looting, elders were cared for, and locals brought food and drink to the road.
entries.literal: He inquired after the aged, the army took no private plunder, the common people were at peace, and oxen and wine lined the roads.

entries.zh: 德母兄先在長安，遣平原人杜弘如長安問存否，弘曰：「臣至長安，若不奉太后動止，便即西如張掖，以死為效。
entries.en: De's mother and elder brother were first in Chang'an; he sent Pingyuan man Du Hong to Chang'an to ask whether they still lived, and Hong said, 'If I reach Chang'an and do not bring back news of the empress dowager's condition, I will go west to Zhangye and die to prove my loyalty.
entries.literal: De's mother and elder brother were first in Chang'an; he sent Pingyuan man Du Hong to Chang'an to ask whether they still lived, and Hong said, 'If I reach Chang'an and do not bring back news of the empress dowager's condition, I will go west to Zhangye and die to prove my loyalty.

entries.zh: 臣父雄年逾六十，未沾榮貴，乞本縣之祿，以申烏鳥之情。」
entries.en: My father Xiong is past sixty and has not tasted honor; I beg the salary of our home county to express the crow's filial heart.'
entries.literal: My father Xiong is past sixty and has not tasted honor; I beg the salary of our home county to express the crow's filial heart.'

entries.zh: 張華進曰：「杜弘未行而求祿，要利情深，不可使也。」
entries.en: Zhang Hua stepped forward, saying, 'Du Hong has not yet gone but seeks salary; his desire for profit runs deep; he cannot be used.'
entries.literal: Zhang Hua stepped forward, saying, 'Du Hong has not yet gone but seeks salary; his desire for profit runs deep; he cannot be used.'

entries.zh: 德曰：「吾方散所輕之財，招所重之死，況為親尊而可吝乎！
entries.en: De said, 'I am now scattering the wealth I lightly esteem to recruit the deaths I heavily value; how could I be stingy for a revered kinsman?
entries.literal: De said, 'I am now scattering the wealth I lightly esteem to recruit the deaths I heavily value; how could I be stingy for a revered kinsman?

entries.zh: 且弘為君迎親，為父求祿，雖外如要利，內實忠孝。」
entries.en: Moreover Hong goes for the ruler to welcome kin and for his father seeks salary; though outwardly like seeking profit, inwardly it is loyalty and filial piety.'
entries.literal: Moreover Hong goes for the ruler to welcome kin and for his father seeks salary; though outwardly like seeking profit, inwardly it is loyalty and filial piety.'

entries.zh: 乃以雄為平原令。
entries.en: Murong De named Du Xiong magistrate of Pingyuan.
entries.literal: He therefore appointed Xiong governor of Pingyuan.

entries.zh: 弘至張掖，為盜所殺，德聞而悲之，厚撫其妻子。
entries.en: Du Hong was killed by bandits at Zhangye; Murong De mourned him and richly aided his family.
entries.literal: Hong reached Zhangye and was killed by bandits; De heard and grieved, treating his wife and children generously.

entries.zh: 明年，德如齊城，登營丘，望晏嬰塚，顧謂左右曰：「禮，大夫不逼城葬。
entries.en: The next year De went to Qi city, climbed Yingqiu, gazed on Yan Ying's mound, and said to those around him, 'By ritual a great officer is not buried pressing the city wall.
entries.literal: The next year De went to Qi city, climbed Yingqiu, gazed on Yan Ying's mound, and said to those around him, 'By ritual a great officer is not buried pressing the city wall.

entries.zh: 平仲古之賢人，達禮者也，而生居近市，死葬近城，豈有意乎？」
entries.en: Pingzhong was a worthy of old, one who understood ritual, yet lived near the market in life and is buried near the city in death; did he intend it?'
entries.literal: Pingzhong was a worthy of old, one who understood ritual, yet lived near the market in life and is buried near the city in death; did he intend it?'

entries.zh: 青州秀才晏謨對曰：「孔子稱臣先人平仲賢，則賢矣。
entries.en: Qingzhou xiucai Yan Mo replied, 'Confucius called my ancestor Pingzhong worthy; worthy he was.
entries.literal: Qingzhou xiucai Yan Mo replied, 'Confucius called my ancestor Pingzhong worthy; worthy he was.

entries.zh: 豈不知高其梁，豐其禮？
entries.en: Could he not have known to raise his ridgepole and enrich his rites?
entries.literal: Could he not have known to raise his ridgepole and enrich his rites?

entries.zh: 蓋政在家門，故儉以矯世。
entries.en: In sum government was in the family gate, therefore he used frugality to correct the age.
entries.literal: In sum government was in the family gate, therefore he used frugality to correct the age.

entries.zh: 存居湫隘，卒豈擇地而葬乎！
entries.en: He lived in a cramped low place; at death could he choose ground to bury!
entries.literal: He lived in a cramped low place; at death could he choose ground to bury!

entries.zh: 所以不遠門者，猶冀悟平生意也。」
entries.en: The reason he did not distance the gate was still hoping to awaken Pingzhong's intent in life.'
entries.literal: The reason he did not distance the gate was still hoping to awaken Pingzhong's intent in life.'

entries.zh: 遂以謨從至漢城陽景王廟，宴庶老于申池，北登社首山，東望鼎足，因目牛山而歎曰：「古無不死！」
entries.en: Thereupon he took Yan Mo along to the temple of Prince Jing of Chengyang at Hancheng, feasted the common elders at Shen Pool, climbed north Mount Sheshou, looked east at the tripod legs of terrain, then gazed at Mount Niu and sighed, saying, 'From antiquity there has been no not dying!'
entries.literal: Thereupon he took Yan Mo along to the temple of Prince Jing of Chengyang at Hancheng, feasted the common elders at Shen Pool, climbed north Mount Sheshou, looked east at the tripod legs of terrain, then gazed at Mount Niu and sighed, saying, 'From antiquity there has been no not dying!'

entries.zh: 愴然有終焉之志。
entries.en: He was overcome with melancholy and half wished to end his days there.
entries.literal: He was mournful and had the will to end there.

entries.zh: 遂問謨以齊之山川丘陵，賢哲舊事。
entries.en: He quizzed Yan Mo on Qi's geography and famous stories.
entries.literal: Thereupon he asked Yan Mo about Qi mountains and rivers, mounds and hills, worthies and ancient affairs.

entries.zh: 謨曆對詳辯，畫地成圖。
entries.en: Yan Mo answered in fluent detail and sketched a map in the dust.
entries.literal: Yan Mo answered in sequence, detailed and disputatious, and drew lines on the ground to make a map.

entries.zh: 德深嘉之，拜尚書郎。
entries.en: Murong De was so impressed he named him a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: De deeply praised him and appointed him gentleman of the masters of writing.

entries.zh: 立冶于商山，置鹽官于烏常澤，以廣軍國之用。
entries.en: He opened ironworks on Mount Shang and salt monopolies at Wuchang Marsh to swell the army's coffers.
entries.literal: He set up smelting works on Mount Shang and salt offices at Wuchang Marsh to broaden military and state use.

entries.zh: 慕容德
entries.en: Murong De.
entries.literal: Murong De.

entries.zh: 陽九數纏，永康多難。
entries.en: “Ill-starred cycles and Yongkang’s woes—”
entries.literal: The yang-nine reckonings twine; Yongkang knew many hardships.

entries.zh: 自北都傾陷，典章淪滅，律令法憲，靡有存者。
entries.en: “—toppled the northern capital and swallowed the law.”
entries.literal: Since the northern capital overturned, canons sank away; statutes, ordinances, laws, and models—none survive.

entries.zh: 綱理天下，此焉為本，既不能導之以德，必須齊之以刑。
entries.en: “Rule needs law; without moral sway, use the rod.”
entries.literal: To order the All-under-Heaven, this is the root; since we cannot guide them with virtue, we must even them with punishments.

entries.zh: 且虞舜大聖，猶命咎繇作士，刑之不可已已也如是！
entries.en: “Even Shun set Gao Yao over justice—punishment is inescapable.”
entries.literal: Moreover Shun the great sage still ordered Gao Yao to be minister of crime—thus punishments cannot be stopped, stopped like this!

entries.zh: 先帝季興，大業草創，兵革尚繁，未遑修制。
entries.en: “Our founder was too busy fighting to codify law.”
entries.literal: The former emperor in his last rise, great enterprise still in the grass-creation stage, arms and armor still numerous, had no leisure to repair institutions.

entries.zh: 朕猥以不德，嗣承大統，撫禦寡方，至蕭牆釁發，遂戎馬生郊，典儀寢廢。
entries.en: “We inherited chaos, misruled until kin turned blades and armies trampled the suburbs.”
entries.literal: We, mean in virtue, have inherited the great line, ruled and restrained without method, until trouble sprang within the bed curtain; then war-horses foaled in the suburbs and ceremony slept abandoned.

entries.zh: 今四境無虞，所宜修定，尚書可召集公卿。
entries.en: “Now the frontiers are quiet—time to legislate; summon the ministers.”
entries.literal: Now the four marches are without alarm; it is fitting to repair and fix; the Secretariat may summon the dukes and ministers.

entries.zh: 至如不忠不孝若封嵩之輩，梟斬不足以痛之，宜致烹轘之法，亦可附之律條，納以大辟之科。
entries.en: “Traitors like Feng Song deserve boiling and tearing, not mere beheading—write it into the code.”
entries.literal: As for the disloyal and unfilial like Feng Song’s sort, beheading and display are not enough to pain them; boiling and tearing by cart should be applied; these too may be attached to the statutes, folded into the capital-crime articles.

entries.zh: 肉刑者，乃先聖之經，不刊之典，漢文易之，輕重乖度。
entries.en: “Mutilation was sage law; Han Wendi’s mercy upset proportion.”
entries.literal: Corporal punishment is the classic of former sages, an unalterable model; Emperor Wen of Han changed it, and light and heavy lost measure.

entries.zh: 今犯罪彌多，死者稍眾。
entries.en: “Crime swells; executions mount.”
entries.literal: Now crimes grow ever more numerous; the dead become somewhat more many.

entries.zh: 肉刑之於化也，濟育既廣，懲慘尤深，光壽、建興中二祖已議復之，未及而晏駕。
entries.en: “Mutilation both deters and redeems; two late kings meant to revive it but died too soon.”
entries.literal: As for corporal punishment in transformation, its nurturing aid is already broad, its deterrent cruelty especially deep; in Guangshou and Jianxing the two ancestors already debated restoring it, but before it could happen they died on the road.

entries.zh: 其令博士已上參考舊事，依《呂刑》及漢、魏、晉律令，消息增損，議成燕律。
entries.en: “Let scholars draft new Yan law from the Lü Xing and Han–Wei–Jin codes.”
entries.literal: Order erudites and above to consult former affairs, follow the ‘Lü Xing’ and Han, Wei, and Jin statutes and ordinances, adjust by increase and decrease, deliberate and complete Yan law.

entries.zh: 五刑之屬三千，而罪莫大於不孝。
entries.en: “Of three thousand clauses, none tops unfilial crime.”
entries.literal: Among the three thousand articles of the five punishments, no crime is greater than unfilial piety.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「非聖人者無法，非孝者無親，此大亂之道也。」
entries.en: Confucius said: “Those who deny sages have no law; those who deny filial piety have no kin—this is the way of great disorder.”
entries.literal: Confucius said: “Those who deny sages have no law; those who deny filial piety have no kin—this is the way of great disorder.”

entries.zh: 轘裂之刑，烹煮之戮，雖不在五品之例，然亦行之自古。
entries.en: Cart-tearing and cauldron killings, though outside the “five punishments,” are ancient tools.
entries.literal: Punishment of tearing by cart and boiling execution, though not in the five grades, have also been practiced since antiquity.

entries.zh: 渠彌之轘，著之《春秋》；
entries.en: Qumi, minister to Duke Zhuang of Zheng, was executed by chariot-tearing, as recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
entries.literal: Qumi’s tearing is written in the ‘Spring and Autumn’;

entries.zh: 哀公之烹，爰自中代。
entries.en: Duke Ai’s boiling belongs to middle antiquity.
entries.literal: Duke Ai’s boiling comes from middle antiquity.

entries.zh: 世宗都齊，亦湣刑罰失中，咨嗟寢食。
entries.en: Our Shizong at Qi likewise fretted when justice skewed.
entries.literal: When Shizong made Qi his capital, he too lamented that punishments had lost their proper measure, sighing over it even as he ate and slept.

entries.zh: 王者之有刑糾，猶人之左右手焉。
entries.en: Law to a king is like two hands to a man.
entries.literal: For a king to have punishments to correct is like a man’s left and right hands.

entries.zh: 故孔子曰：「刑罰不中，則人無所措手足。」
entries.en: Therefore Confucius said: “When punishments miss the mean, the people have nowhere to put hand or foot.”
entries.literal: Therefore Confucius said: “When punishments miss the mean, the people have nowhere to put hand or foot.”

entries.zh: 是以蕭何定法令而受封，叔孫通以制儀為奉常。
entries.en: Xiao He and Shusun Tong won honor for codifying law and rite.
entries.literal: Therefore Xiao He fixed statutes and received enfeoffment; Shu Sun Tong by making ritual became minister of ceremonies.

entries.zh: 立功立事，古之所重。
entries.en: Great deeds mattered to the ancients.
entries.literal: To establish merit and affairs is what antiquity prized.

entries.zh: 其明議損益，以成一代准式。
entries.en: Debate amendments until we have a model code.
entries.literal: Let them clarify increase and decrease to complete a generation’s standard model.

entries.zh: 周、漢有貢士之條，魏立九品之選，二者孰愈，亦可詳聞。
entries.en: Compare Zhou–Han recommendation to Wei’s nine ranks.
entries.literal: Zhou and Han had articles for presenting scholars; Wei established nine-rank selection—which of the two is better may also be reported in detail.

entries.zh: 超母妻既先在長安，為姚興所拘，責超稱籓，求太樂諸伎，若不可，使送吳口千人。
entries.en: Yao Xing detained Murong Chao's mother and wife, demanding that Chao declare himself a vassal and surrender the Grand Music performers; failing that, he was to send a thousand people from Wu.
entries.literal: Chao’s mother and wife, since they were earlier in Chang’an, were detained by Yao Xing; Xing demanded Chao declare vassalage and send the Grand Music performers; if not, send a thousand Wu captives.

entries.zh: 超下書遣群臣詳議。
entries.en: Murong Chao asked his court for options.
entries.literal: Chao issued an edict ordering the host of ministers to deliberate in detail.

entries.zh: 左僕射段暉議曰：「太上囚楚，高祖不回。
entries.en: Left Vice Director Duan Hui argued: “When the Grand Supreme was imprisoned in Chu, the High Ancestor did not bend.
entries.literal: Left Vice Director Duan Hui argued: “When the Grand Supreme was imprisoned in Chu, the High Ancestor did not bend.

entries.zh: 今陛下嗣守社稷，不宜以私親之故而降統天之尊。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty inherits and guards the altars of soil and grain; you ought not, because of private kinship, lower the honor that unifies heaven.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty inherits and guards the altars of soil and grain; you ought not, because of private kinship, lower the honor that unifies heaven.

entries.zh: 又太樂諸伎，皆是前世伶人，不可與彼，使移風易俗，宜掠吳口與之。」
entries.en: Moreover the Grand Music performers are all former entertainers of prior ages—you cannot give them to him; let him shift custom by moving—better to raid Wu captives and give him those.”
entries.literal: Moreover the Grand Music performers are all former entertainers of prior ages—you cannot give them to him; let him shift custom by moving—better to raid Wu captives and give him those.”

entries.zh: 尚書張華曰：「若侵掠吳邊，必成鄰怨。
entries.en: Minister Zhang Hua said: “If we raid Jin’s border, we are sure to complete neighborly resentment.
entries.literal: Minister Zhang Hua said: “If we raid Jin’s border, we are sure to complete neighborly resentment.

entries.zh: 此既能往，彼亦能來，兵連禍結，非國之福也。
entries.en: This side can go there, that side can also come; arms linked and disaster knotted is not the state’s blessing.
entries.literal: This side can go there, that side can also come; arms linked and disaster knotted is not the state’s blessing.

entries.zh: 昔孫權重黎庶之命，屈己以臣魏；
entries.en: Anciently Sun Quan weighted the lives of the black-haired masses and bent himself to serve Wei;
entries.literal: Anciently Sun Quan weighted the lives of the black-haired masses and bent himself to serve Wei;

entries.zh: 惠施惜愛子之頭，舍志以尊齊。
entries.en: Hui Shi pitied his beloved son’s head and set aside his intent to honor Qi.
entries.literal: Hui Shi pitied his beloved son’s head and set aside his intent to honor Qi.

entries.zh: 況陛下慈德在秦，方寸崩亂，宜暫降大號，以申至孝之情。
entries.en: Moreover Your Majesty’s kindly virtue lies in Qin; your heart is shattered in chaos—you ought temporarily to lower the great title to extend utmost filial feeling.
entries.literal: Moreover Your Majesty’s kindly virtue lies in Qin; your heart is shattered in chaos—you ought temporarily to lower the great title to extend utmost filial feeling.

entries.zh: 權變之道，典謨所許。
entries.en: The way of weighing change is what the canons permit.
entries.literal: The way of weighing change is what the canons permit.

entries.zh: 韓范智能回物，辯足傾人，昔與姚興俱為秦太子中舍人，可遣將命，降號修和。
entries.en: Han Fan’s intelligence can turn things, his eloquence enough to sway men; anciently he and Yao Xing were both attendants in the Eastern Palace of Qin—you can send him on mission to lower the title and repair peace.
entries.literal: Han Fan’s intelligence can turn things, his eloquence enough to sway men; anciently he and Yao Xing were both attendants in the Eastern Palace of Qin—you can send him on mission to lower the title and repair peace.

entries.zh: 所謂屈於一人之下，申于萬人之上也。」
entries.en: This is what is called bowing beneath one man to stretch above ten thousand.”
entries.literal: This is what is called bowing beneath one man to stretch above ten thousand.”

entries.zh: 超大悅曰：「張尚書得吾心矣。」
entries.en: Chao was greatly pleased and said: “Director Zhang has gotten Our heart.”
entries.literal: Chao was greatly pleased and said: “Director Zhang has gotten Our heart.”

entries.zh: 使范聘於興。
entries.en: He sent Han Fan to Yao Xing.
entries.literal: He sent Fan on embassy to Xing.

entries.zh: 及至長安，興謂範曰：「封愷前來，燕王與朕抗禮。
entries.en: When he reached Chang’an, Xing said to Fan: “Feng Kai came before; the Yan king treated Us as an equal by ritual.
entries.literal: When he reached Chang’an, Xing said to Fan: “Feng Kai came before; the Yan king treated Us as an equal by ritual.

entries.zh: 及卿至也，款然而附。
entries.en: When you arrived he attached himself warmly.
entries.literal: When you arrived he attached himself warmly.

entries.zh: 為依春秋以小事大之義？
entries.en: Is it following the Spring and Autumn meaning of the small serving the great?
entries.literal: Is it following the Spring and Autumn meaning of the small serving the great?

entries.zh: 為當專以孝敬為母屈也？」
entries.en: Or is it solely bending in filial respect for the mother?”
entries.literal: Or is it solely bending in filial respect for the mother?”

entries.zh: 範曰：「周爵五等，公侯異品，小大之禮，因而生焉。
entries.en: Fan said: “Zhou’s nobility had five ranks; dukes and marquises differed in grade; rites of great and small arose from this.
entries.literal: Fan said: “Zhou’s nobility had five ranks; dukes and marquises differed in grade; rites of great and small arose from this.

entries.zh: 今陛下命世龍興，光宅西秦，本朝主上承祖宗遺烈，定鼎東齊，中分天曜，南面並帝。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty, a dragon risen to command the age, shines in western Qin; our court’s sovereign inherits the fierce legacy of ancestors, fixes the cauldron in eastern Qi; you split heaven’s radiance, face south, and both are emperors.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty, a dragon risen to command the age, shines in western Qin; our court’s sovereign inherits the fierce legacy of ancestors, fixes the cauldron in eastern Qi; you split heaven’s radiance, face south, and both are emperors.

entries.zh: 通聘結好，義尚廉沖，便至矜誕，苟折行人，殊似吳、晉爭盟，滕、薛競長，恐傷大秦堂堂之盛，有損皇燕巍巍之美，彼我俱失，竊未安之。」
entries.en: Envoys exchange visits and knot friendship; the right meaning favors modesty—yet you strut and boast, casually humiliate the traveler—much like Wu and Jin vying in covenant, Teng and Xue competing for seniority; I fear it wounds great Qin’s majestic splendor and damages royal Yan’s towering grace; both sides lose—I privately am not at ease.”
entries.literal: Envoys exchange visits and knot friendship; the right meaning favors modesty—yet you strut and boast, casually humiliate the traveler—much like Wu and Jin vying in covenant, Teng and Xue competing for seniority; I fear it wounds great Qin’s majestic splendor and damages royal Yan’s towering grace; both sides lose—I privately am not at ease.”

entries.zh: 興怒曰：「若如卿言，便是非為大小而來。」
entries.en: Xing angrily said: “If it were as you say, then they did not come for reasons of great and small.”
entries.literal: Xing angrily said: “If it were as you say, then they did not come for reasons of great and small.”

entries.zh: 範曰：「雖由大小之義，亦緣寡君純孝過於重華，願陛下體敬親之道，霈然垂湣。」
entries.en: Fan said: “Though the meaning of great and small is involved, it is also because our poor ruler’s pure filial piety surpasses Shun’s; I hope Your Majesty will embody reverence for kin and pour forth pity.”
entries.literal: Fan said: “Though the meaning of great and small is involved, it is also because our poor ruler’s pure filial piety surpasses Shun’s; I hope Your Majesty will embody reverence for kin and pour forth pity.”

entries.zh: 興曰：「吾久不見賈生，自謂過之，今不及矣。」
entries.en: Xing said: “Long have I not seen Jia Yi; I thought myself his better—now I do not reach him.”
entries.literal: Xing said: “Long have I not seen Jia Yi; I thought myself his better—now I do not reach him.”

entries.zh: 於是為范設舊交之禮，申敘平生，謂範曰：「燕王在此，朕亦見之，風表乃可，於機辯未也。」
entries.en: Thereupon he treated Fan with the rites of an old acquaintance, narrating their whole lives, and said to Fan: “The Yan king here—We have also seen him; his bearing is passable, but in sharp debate he is not yet there.”
entries.literal: Thereupon he treated Fan with the rites of an old acquaintance, narrating their whole lives, and said to Fan: “The Yan king here—We have also seen him; his bearing is passable, but in sharp debate he is not yet there.”

entries.zh: 範曰：「大辯若訥，聖人美之，況爾日龍潛鳳戢，和光同塵，若使負日月而行，則無繼天之業矣。」
entries.en: Fan said: “Great eloquence seems dull—the sage prized it; moreover that day the dragon hid and the phoenix folded, blending gleam with dust; had he shouldered sun and moon in his walk, there would be no enterprise to continue heaven.”
entries.literal: Fan said: “Great eloquence seems dull—the sage prized it; moreover that day the dragon hid and the phoenix folded, blending gleam with dust; had he shouldered sun and moon in his walk, there would be no enterprise to continue heaven.”

entries.zh: 興笑曰：「可謂使乎延譽者也。」
entries.en: Xing laughed and said: “You may be called one who on embassy spreads praise.”
entries.literal: Xing laughed and said: “You may be called one who on embassy spreads praise.”

entries.zh: 範承間逞說，姚興大悅，賜范千金，許以超母妻還之。
entries.en: Han Fan pressed his case; Yao Xing relented, paid him, and promised the hostages back.
entries.literal: Fan seized the interval to press his persuasion; Yao Xing was greatly pleased, gifted Fan a thousand in gold, and promised to return Chao’s mother and wife.

entries.zh: 慕容凝自梁父奔于姚興，言於興曰：「燕王稱籓，本非推德，權為母屈耳。
entries.en: Murong Ning fled from Liangfu to Yao Xing and said to Xing: “The Yan king’s declaration of vassalage was not from yielding virtue—it was a temporary bend for his mother.
entries.literal: Murong Ning fled from Liangfu to Yao Xing and said to Xing: “The Yan king’s declaration of vassalage was not from yielding virtue—it was a temporary bend for his mother.

entries.zh: 古之帝王尚興師征質，豈可虛還其母乎！
entries.en: Ancient emperors still raised armies to demand hostages—how can you hollowly return his mother!
entries.literal: Ancient emperors still raised armies to demand hostages—how can you hollowly return his mother!

entries.zh: 母若一還，必不復臣也。
entries.en: If the mother returns once, he will surely not again be a subject.
entries.literal: If the mother returns once, he will surely not again be a subject.

entries.zh: 宜先制其送伎，然後歸之。」
entries.en: You ought first to seize the performers he is to send, then return her.”
entries.literal: You ought first to seize the performers he is to send, then return her.”

entries.zh: 興意乃變，遣使聘於超。
entries.en: Yao Xing wavered and reopened talks.
entries.literal: Xing’s intent then changed; he sent envoys on a friendly visit to Chao.

entries.zh: 超遣其僕射張華、給事中宗正元入長安，送太樂伎一百二十人于姚興。
entries.en: Murong Chao sent Zhang Hua and Zong Zhengyuan with a hundred twenty court musicians.
entries.literal: Chao sent his Vice Director Zhang Hua and Supervising Secretary Zong Zhengyuan to Chang’an, delivering a hundred twenty Grand Music performers to Yao Xing.

entries.zh: 興大悅，延華入宴。
entries.en: Yao Xing feasted Zhang Hua.
entries.literal: Xing was greatly pleased and drew Hua into a banquet.

entries.zh: 酒酣，樂作，興黃門侍郎尹雅謂華曰：「昔殷之將亡，樂師歸周；
entries.en: When the wine was deep and music began, Xing’s gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Yin Ya said to Hua: “Anciently when Yin was about to perish, the music masters went to Zhou;
entries.literal: When the wine was deep and music began, Xing’s gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Yin Ya said to Hua: “Anciently when Yin was about to perish, the music masters went to Zhou;

entries.zh: 今皇秦道盛，燕樂來庭。
entries.en: now imperial Qin’s Way flourishes and Yan’s music comes to court.
entries.literal: now imperial Qin’s Way flourishes and Yan’s music comes to court.

entries.zh: 廢興之兆，見於此矣。」
entries.en: The omens of decline and rise appear in this.”
entries.literal: The omens of decline and rise appear in this.”

entries.zh: 華曰：「自古帝王，為道不同，權譎之理，會于功成。
entries.en: Hua said: “From antiquity emperors have differed in their Way; the pattern of weighing stratagem meets in merit accomplished.
entries.literal: Hua said: “From antiquity emperors have differed in their Way; the pattern of weighing stratagem meets in merit accomplished.

entries.zh: 故老子曰：'將欲取之，必先與之。
entries.en: Therefore Laozi says: ‘If you would take, you must first give.’
entries.literal: Therefore Laozi says: ‘If you would take, you must first give.’

entries.zh: '今總章西入，必由餘東歸，禍福之驗，此其兆乎！」
entries.en: Now the Zongzhang musicians have gone west; surely You Yu will return east. Is this not an omen of fortune and disaster?"
entries.literal: Now Zongzhang has entered the west; surely You Yu will return east. Is this not the sign of fortune and disaster?"

entries.zh: 興怒曰：「昔齊、楚競辯，二國連師。
entries.en: Xing angrily said: “Anciently Qi and Chu debated rhetoric; the two states linked armies.
entries.literal: Xing angrily said: “Anciently Qi and Chu debated rhetoric; the two states linked armies.

entries.zh: 卿小國之臣，何敢抗衡朝士！」
entries.en: You, a minister of a small state—how dare you stand up to courtiers!”
entries.literal: You, a minister of a small state—how dare you stand up to courtiers!”

entries.zh: 華遜辭曰：「奉使之始，實願交歡上國，上國既遺小國之臣，辱及寡君社稷，臣亦何心，而不仰酬！」
entries.en: Hua deferentially said: “When the mission began, I truly wished to befriend the superior state; the superior state has now disdained the small state’s minister and insulted even our poor ruler’s altars—how could your servant lack heart and not answer upward!”
entries.literal: Hua deferentially said: “When the mission began, I truly wished to befriend the superior state; the superior state has now disdained the small state’s minister and insulted even our poor ruler’s altars—how could your servant lack heart and not answer upward!”

entries.zh: 興善之，於是還超母妻，
entries.en: Yao Xing relented and freed Murong Chao’s family.
entries.literal: Xing approved of this; thereupon he returned Chao’s mother and wife.

entries.zh: 尚書都令史王儼諂事五樓，遷尚書郎，出為濟南太守，入為尚書左丞，時人為之語曰：「欲得侯，事五樓。」
entries.en: Secretariat chief clerk Wang Yan fawned on Wulou, was promoted ministerial secretary, went out as governor of Jinan, came in as left aide to the minister—people of the time made a saying: “If you want a marquis, serve Wulou.”
entries.literal: Secretariat chief clerk Wang Yan fawned on Wulou, was promoted ministerial secretary, went out as governor of Jinan, came in as left aide to the minister—people of the time made a saying: “If you want a marquis, serve Wulou.”

entries.zh: 又遣公孫歸等率騎三千入寇濟南，執太守趙元，略男女千餘人而去。
entries.en: He again sent Gongsun Gui and others with three thousand cavalry to raid Jinan, capture Administrator Zhao Yuan, and carry off more than a thousand men and women.
entries.literal: He again sent Gongsun Gui and others leading three thousand horse to raid Jinan, seized Governor Zhao Yuan, and carried off more than a thousand men and women.

entries.zh: 劉裕率師將討之，超引見群臣于節陽殿，議距王師。
entries.en: As Liu Yu marched, Murong Chao convened council at Jieyang Hall.
entries.literal: Liu Yu led an army about to punish him; Chao led out the host of ministers in the Jieyang Hall to debate resisting the royal army.

entries.zh: 公孫五樓曰：「吳兵輕果，所利在戰，初鋒勇銳，不可爭也。
entries.en: Gongsun Wulou said: “Wu’s troops are light and decisive; what they profit from is battle; the first clash is brave and sharp—it cannot be contested.
entries.literal: Gongsun Wulou said: “Wu’s troops are light and decisive; what they profit from is battle; the first clash is brave and sharp—it cannot be contested.

entries.zh: 宜據大峴，使不得入，曠日延時，沮其銳氣。
entries.en: You ought to hold Daxian Pass and keep them from entering; stretch days and lengthen time, sap their keen edge.
entries.literal: You ought to hold Daxian Pass and keep them from entering; stretch days and lengthen time, sap their keen edge.

entries.zh: 可徐簡精騎二千，循海而南。
entries.en: You may leisurely select two thousand picked horse and follow the sea south.
entries.literal: You may leisurely select two thousand picked horse and follow the sea south.

entries.zh: 絕其糧運，別敕段暉率兗州之軍，緣山東下。
entries.en: Cut their grain transport; separately order Duan Hui to lead Yan Province’s army down along the mountains east.
entries.literal: Cut their grain transport; separately order Duan Hui to lead Yan Province’s army down along the mountains east.

entries.zh: 腹背擊之，上策也。
entries.en: Strike them belly and back—the upper strategy.
entries.literal: Strike them belly and back—the upper strategy.

entries.zh: 各命守宰，依險自固，校其資儲之外，餘悉焚蕩，芟除粟苗，使敵無所資。
entries.en: Order each defender to hold fast by natural barriers, and besides what their stores allow, burn all else, cut the grain shoots, so the enemy has nothing to draw on.
entries.literal: Order each defender to hold fast by natural barriers, and besides what their stores allow, burn all else, cut the grain shoots, so the enemy has nothing to draw on.

entries.zh: 堅壁清野，以待其釁，中策也。
entries.en: Strong walls and cleared fields, awaiting their fault—the middle strategy.
entries.literal: Strong walls and cleared fields, awaiting their fault—the middle strategy.

entries.zh: 縱賊入峴，出城逆戰，下策也。」
entries.en: Let the bandits enter the pass and meet them outside the city in battle—the lower strategy.”
entries.literal: Let the bandits enter the pass and meet them outside the city in battle—the lower strategy.”

entries.zh: 超曰：「京都殷盛，戶口眾多，非可一時入守。
entries.en: Chao said: “The capital is populous and rich; households and mouths are many—not possible to enter and defend in one moment.
entries.literal: Chao said: “The capital is populous and rich; households and mouths are many—not possible to enter and defend in one moment.

entries.zh: 青苗布野，非可卒芟。
entries.en: Green shoots blanket the wilds—not possible to cut down at once.
entries.literal: Green shoots blanket the wilds—not possible to cut down at once.

entries.zh: 設使芟苗城守，以全性命，朕所不能。
entries.en: Suppose we cut the shoots and defend the city to preserve life—that is something We cannot do.
entries.literal: Suppose we cut the shoots and defend the city to preserve life—that is something We cannot do.

entries.zh: 今據五州之強，帶山河之固，戰車萬乘，鐵馬萬群，縱令過峴，至於平地，徐以精騎踐之，此成擒也。」
entries.en: Now relying on the strength of five provinces, girded by mountains and rivers’ solidity, war chariots in myriads, armored horse in myriads—even if they cross the pass and reach level ground, We will slowly use picked horse to trample them—this is assured capture.”
entries.literal: Now relying on the strength of five provinces, girded by mountains and rivers’ solidity, war chariots in myriads, armored horse in myriads—even if they cross the pass and reach level ground, We will slowly use picked horse to trample them—this is assured capture.”

entries.zh: 賀賴盧苦諫，不從，退謂五樓曰：「上不用吾計，亡無日矣。」
entries.en: Helailu remonstrated bitterly; he did not follow; he withdrew and said to Wulou: “The sovereign will not use my plan—destruction is not far off.”
entries.literal: Helailu remonstrated bitterly; he did not follow; he withdrew and said to Wulou: “The sovereign will not use my plan—destruction is not far off.”

entries.zh: 慕容鎮曰：「若如聖旨，必須平原用馬為便，宜出峴逆戰，戰而不勝，猶可退守。
entries.en: Murong Zhen said: “If it follows Your Sagely intent, on level ground using horse is convenient; you ought to go out of the pass and meet them in battle—if battle does not succeed, you may still withdraw and defend.
entries.literal: Murong Zhen said: “If it follows Your Sagely intent, on level ground using horse is convenient; you ought to go out of the pass and meet them in battle—if battle does not succeed, you may still withdraw and defend.

entries.zh: 不宜縱敵入峴，自貽窘逼。
entries.en: It is not right to let the enemy into the pass and bring embarrassment and pressure on yourself.
entries.literal: It is not right to let the enemy into the pass and bring embarrassment and pressure on yourself.

entries.zh: 昔成安君不守井陘之關，終屈于韓信；
entries.en: Anciently Chengan Jun did not guard the barrier of Jingxing and in the end submitted to Han Xin;
entries.literal: Anciently Chengan Jun did not guard the barrier of Jingxing and in the end submitted to Han Xin;

entries.zh: 諸葛瞻不據束馬之險，卒擒于鄧艾。
entries.en: Zhuge Zhan did not hold the peril of Shuma and in the end was captured by Deng Ai.
entries.literal: Zhuge Zhan did not hold the peril of Shuma and in the end was captured by Deng Ai.

entries.zh: 臣以為天時不如地利，阻守大峴，策之上也。」
entries.en: Your servant thinks heaven’s timing is not as good as earth’s advantage; blocking and holding Daxian is the top of strategies.”
entries.literal: Your servant thinks heaven’s timing is not as good as earth’s advantage; blocking and holding Daxian is the top of strategies.”

entries.zh: 超不從。
entries.en: Murong Chao refused.
entries.literal: Chao did not follow.

entries.zh: 鎮出，謂韓𧨳曰：「主上既不能芟苗守險，又不肯徙人逃寇，酷似劉璋矣。
entries.en: When Zhen came out, he said to Han Zhuo: “The sovereign can neither cut the shoots and hold the peril, nor will he move the people to flee the bandits—he closely resembles Liu Zhang.
entries.literal: When Zhen came out, he said to Han Zhuo: “The sovereign can neither cut the shoots and hold the peril, nor will he move the people to flee the bandits—he closely resembles Liu Zhang.

entries.zh: 今年國滅，吾必死之，卿等中華之士，復為文身矣。」
entries.en: This year when the state is destroyed, I am sure to die for it; you gentlemen, scholars of the Hua heartland, will again become tattooed bodies.”
entries.literal: This year when the state is destroyed, I am sure to die for it; you gentlemen, scholars of the Hua heartland, will again become tattooed bodies.”

entries.zh: 超聞而大怒，收鎮下獄。
entries.en: Murong Chao jailed Murong Zhen.
entries.literal: When Chao heard it he was greatly angry and seized Zhen and cast him into prison.

entries.zh: 乃攝莒、梁父二戍，修城隍，簡士馬，畜銳以待之。
entries.en: He pulled in Ju and Liangfu garrisons and dug in.
entries.literal: He then drew in the two garrisons of Ju and Liangfu, repaired walls and moats, selected troops and horse, and stored keen edge to await them.

entries.zh: 其夏，王師次東莞，超遣其左軍段暉、輔國賀賴盧等六將步騎五萬，進據臨朐。
entries.en: That summer, the imperial army encamped at Dongguan. Chao sent six generals, including his Left Army commander Duan Hui and General Who Assists the State Helailu, with fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to occupy Linqu.
entries.literal: That summer the royal army halted at Dongguan; Chao sent his left army Duan Hui, assistant state Helailu, and six other generals with fifty thousand foot and horse to advance and hold Linqu.

entries.zh: 俄而王師度峴，超懼，率卒四萬就暉等於臨朐，謂公孫五樓曰：「宜進據川源，晉軍至而失水，亦不能戰矣。」
entries.en: Presently the royal army crossed the pass; Chao feared, led forty thousand troops to join Hui and the others at Linqu, and said to Gongsun Wulou: “You ought to advance and hold the river sources—when the Jin army arrives and loses water, they cannot fight either.”
entries.literal: Presently the royal army crossed the pass; Chao feared, led forty thousand troops to join Hui and the others at Linqu, and said to Gongsun Wulou: “You ought to advance and hold the river sources—when the Jin army arrives and loses water, they cannot fight either.”

entries.zh: 五樓馳騎據之。
entries.en: Gongsun Wulou raced to the fords.
entries.literal: Wulou galloped horse to seize them.

entries.zh: 劉裕前驅將軍孟龍符已至川源，五樓戰敗而返。
entries.en: Meng Longfu held the water; Gongsun Wulou fled.
entries.literal: Liu Yu’s vanguard general Meng Longfu had already reached the river sources; Wulou was defeated in battle and returned.

entries.zh: 裕遣諮議參軍檀韶率銳卒攻破臨朐，超大懼，單騎奔段暉于城南。
entries.en: Tan Shao stormed Linqu; Murong Chao bolted to Duan Hui.
entries.literal: Yu sent staff adviser Tan Shao leading picked troops to break Linqu; Chao was greatly afraid, fled alone on horse to Duan Hui south of the wall.

entries.zh: 暉眾又戰敗，裕軍人斬暉。
entries.en: Duan Hui’s line broke; Liu Yu’s men killed him.
entries.literal: Hui’s host was again defeated in battle; Yu’s soldiers beheaded Hui.

entries.zh: 超又奔還廣固，徙郭內人入保小城，使其尚書郎張綱乞師于姚興。
entries.en: Murong Chao shrank into Guanggu’s inner town and sent Zhang Gang to Qin for aid.
entries.literal: Chao again fled back to Guanggu, moved the people inside the outer wall into the lesser city for protection, and sent his ministerial secretary Zhang Gang to beg troops from Yao Xing.

entries.zh: 赦慕容鎮，進錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事。
entries.en: He freed Murong Zhen and made him chief minister and supreme commander.
entries.literal: He pardoned Murong Zhen, promoted him recorder of the Secretariat and area commander of all military affairs at court and in the field.

entries.zh: 引見群臣，謝之曰：「朕嗣奉成業，不能委賢任善，而專固自由，覆水不收，悔將何及！
entries.en: He led out the host of ministers, apologized to them, saying: “We have inherited and upheld the completed enterprise, unable to delegate worthies and employ the good, but stubbornly free in Our own way—spilled water is not gathered; what regret can reach it!
entries.literal: He led out the host of ministers, apologized to them, saying: “We have inherited and upheld the completed enterprise, unable to delegate worthies and employ the good, but stubbornly free in Our own way—spilled water is not gathered; what regret can reach it!

entries.zh: 智士逞謀，必在事危，忠臣立節，亦在臨難，諸君其勉思六奇，共濟艱運。」
entries.en: Wise men deploy stratagem surely when affairs are perilous; loyal ministers establish integrity also on facing disaster—may you all strive to think the six marvels and together ford hard fate.”
entries.literal: Wise men deploy stratagem surely when affairs are perilous; loyal ministers establish integrity also on facing disaster—may you all strive to think the six marvels and together ford hard fate.”

entries.zh: 鎮進曰：「百姓之心，系於一人。
entries.en: Zhen stepped forward and said: “The hearts of the hundred surnames hang on one man.
entries.literal: Zhen stepped forward and said: “The hearts of the hundred surnames hang on one man.

entries.zh: 陛下既躬率六軍，身先奔敗，群臣解心，士庶喪氣，內外之情，不可復恃。
entries.en: Your Majesty has already personally led the six armies and taken the lead in rout; the host of ministers’ hearts are undone, gentry and common lose breath; inside and outside feelings cannot again be relied on.
entries.literal: Your Majesty has already personally led the six armies and taken the lead in rout; the host of ministers’ hearts are undone, gentry and common lose breath; inside and outside feelings cannot again be relied on.

entries.zh: 如聞西秦自有內難，恐不暇分兵救人，正當更決一戰，以爭天命。
entries.en: As I hear, western Qin has its own internal troubles—I fear they have no leisure to divide troops to save others; you ought rightly to decide another battle to contest heaven’s mandate.
entries.literal: As I hear, western Qin has its own internal troubles—I fear they have no leisure to divide troops to save others; you ought rightly to decide another battle to contest heaven’s mandate.

entries.zh: 今散卒還者，猶有數萬，可悉出金帛、宮女，餌令一戰。
entries.en: Now scattered soldiers returning still number in the tens of thousands—you can bring out all gold, silks, and palace women as bait to force one battle.
entries.literal: Now scattered soldiers returning still number in the tens of thousands—you can bring out all gold, silks, and palace women as bait to force one battle.

entries.zh: 天若相我，足以破賊。
entries.en: If heaven assists us, it is enough to break the bandits.
entries.literal: If heaven assists us, it is enough to break the bandits.

entries.zh: 如其不濟，死尚為美，不可閉門坐受圍擊。」
entries.en: If it does not succeed, death is still beautiful; you cannot close the gates and sit receiving siege blows.”
entries.literal: If it does not succeed, death is still beautiful; you cannot close the gates and sit receiving siege blows.”

entries.zh: 司徒慕容惠曰：「不然。
entries.en: Minister of education Murong Hui said: “It is not so.
entries.literal: Minister of education Murong Hui said: “It is not so.

entries.zh: 今晉軍乘勝，有陵人之氣，敗軍之將，何以禦之！
entries.en: Now the Jin army rides victory and has the air of lording over others—how can a defeated host’s general oppose it!
entries.literal: Now the Jin army rides victory and has the air of lording over others—how can a defeated host’s general oppose it!

entries.zh: 秦雖與勃勃相持，不足為患。
entries.en: Though Qin is locked with Bobo, it is not enough to count as worry.
entries.literal: Though Qin is locked with Bobo, it is not enough to count as worry.

entries.zh: 且二國連橫，勢成脣齒，今有寇難，秦必救我。
entries.en: Moreover the two states are joined in horizontal alliance; the situation forms lips and teeth—now there is raider disaster, Qin is sure to save us.
entries.literal: Moreover the two states are joined in horizontal alliance; the situation forms lips and teeth—now there is raider disaster, Qin is sure to save us.

entries.zh: 但自古乞援，不遣大臣則不致重兵，是以趙隸三請，楚師不出；
entries.en: From antiquity, when seeking aid, failure to send a senior minister has meant failure to obtain a large relief force. Thus Zhao petitioned three times, yet no army came from Chu;
entries.literal: But from antiquity when begging aid, if you do not send a great minister you do not draw heavy troops—therefore Zhao’s thrice begging indentured no Chu army;

entries.zh: 平原一使，援至從成。
entries.en: one mission from Pingyuan and aid arrived and success followed.
entries.literal: one mission from Pingyuan and aid arrived and success followed.

entries.zh: 尚書令韓范德望具瞻，燕秦所重，宜遣乞援，以濟時難。」
entries.en: Minister Secretary Han Fan’s virtue and gaze are looked up to by both Yan and Qin—you ought to send him to beg aid to ford the hour’s hardship.”
entries.literal: Minister Secretary Han Fan’s virtue and gaze are looked up to by both Yan and Qin—you ought to send him to beg aid to ford the hour’s hardship.”

entries.zh: 於是遣范與王蒲乞師于姚興。
entries.en: He dispatched Han Fan and Wang Pu to Yao Xing.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent Fan and Wang Pu to beg troops from Yao Xing.

entries.zh: 未幾，裕師圍城，四面皆合。
entries.en: Before long, Liu Yu's army surrounded the city on all sides.
entries.literal: Before long, Yu’s army surrounded the city; on four sides all joined.

entries.zh: 人有竊告裕軍曰：「若得張綱為攻具者，城乃可得耳。」
entries.en: Someone secretly told the Yu army: “If you could get Zhang Gang to make siege engines, the city could be taken.”
entries.literal: Someone secretly told the Yu army: “If you could get Zhang Gang to make siege engines, the city could be taken.”

entries.zh: 是月，綱自長安歸，遂奔於裕。
entries.en: That month Zhang Gang returned from Chang’an and defected to Liu Yu.
entries.literal: That month, Gang returned from Chang’an and thereupon fled to Yu.

entries.zh: 裕令綱周城大呼曰：「勃勃大破秦軍，無兵相救。」
entries.en: Yu ordered Gang to circle the wall and shout loudly: “Bobo has crushed Qin’s army—there are no troops to save you.”
entries.literal: Yu ordered Gang to circle the wall and shout loudly: “Bobo has crushed Qin’s army—there are no troops to save you.”

entries.zh: 超怒，伏弩射之，乃退。
entries.en: Chao grew angry and had concealed crossbowmen shoot at Zhang Gang, forcing him to withdraw.
entries.literal: Chao grew angry, laid ambush crossbows and shot at him; he then withdrew.

entries.zh: 右僕射張華、中丞封愷並為裕軍所獲。
entries.en: Zhang Hua and Feng Kai fell prisoner.
entries.literal: Right Vice Director Zhang Hua and the Palace Aide to the Censor-in-chief Feng Kai were both captured by Yu’s army.

entries.zh: 裕令華、愷與超書，勸令早降。
entries.en: Liu Yu made them write Murong Chao to yield.
entries.literal: Yu ordered Hua and Kai to write Chao a letter urging early surrender.

entries.zh: 超乃遺裕書，請為籓臣，以大峴為界，並獻馬千區，以通和好，裕弗許。
entries.en: Murong Chao offered vassalage, Daxian as border, and a thousand horses; Liu Yu refused.
entries.literal: Chao then sent Yu a letter, asking to be a vassal minister, with Daxian Pass as the boundary, and offered a thousand teams of horses to open good relations; Yu did not consent.

entries.zh: 江南繼兵相尋而至。
entries.en: Fresh Jin regiments kept landing from the south.
entries.literal: South of the Yangzi reinforcements arrived one after another.

entries.zh: 尚書張俊自長安還，又降於裕，說容曰：「今燕人所以固守者，外杖韓范，冀得秦援。
entries.en: Minister Zhang Jun returned from Chang’an and again surrendered to Yu, saying to Yu: “Now the reason Yan men stubbornly defend is they outwardly lean on Han Fan, hoping to gain Qin’s rescue.
entries.literal: Minister Zhang Jun returned from Chang’an and again surrendered to Yu, saying to Yu: “Now the reason Yan men stubbornly defend is they outwardly lean on Han Fan, hoping to gain Qin’s rescue.

entries.zh: 范既時望，又與姚興舊昵，若勃勃敗後，秦必救燕，宜密信誘範，啖以重利，范來則燕人絕望，自然降矣。」
entries.en: Fan is both the man of the hour and old-intimate with Yao Xing; if after Bobo’s defeat Qin is sure to save Yan, you ought secretly to write enticing Fan with rich profit—when Fan comes the Yan men will despair and naturally surrender.”
entries.literal: Fan is both the man of the hour and old-intimate with Yao Xing; if after Bobo’s defeat Qin is sure to save Yan, you ought secretly to write enticing Fan with rich profit—when Fan comes the Yan men will despair and naturally surrender.”

entries.zh: 裕從之，表範為散騎常侍，遺範書以招之。
entries.en: Liu Yu offered Han Fan a Jin title and a letter.
entries.literal: Yu followed this, memorialized Fan as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and sent Fan a letter to summon him.

entries.zh: 時姚興乃遣其將姚強率步騎一萬，隨範就其將姚紹於洛陽，並兵來援。
entries.en: At that time Yao Xing sent his general Yao Qiang with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to accompany Han Fan to Luoyang, join forces with Yao Shao, and come to the rescue.
entries.literal: At that time Yao Xing then sent his general Yao Qiang leading ten thousand foot and horse to follow Fan and join his general Yao Shao at Luoyang, merging troops to come to the rescue.

entries.zh: 會赫連勃勃大破秦軍，興追強還長安。
entries.en: Helian Bobo routed Qin; Yao Xing recalled the relief column.
entries.literal: It happened that Helian Bobo crushed Qin’s army; Xing recalled Qiang to Chang’an.

entries.zh: 範歎曰：「天其滅燕乎！」
entries.en: Fan sighed: “Is Heaven about to extinguish Yan!”
entries.literal: Fan sighed: “Is Heaven about to extinguish Yan!”

entries.zh: 會得裕書，遂降於裕。
entries.en: He read Liu Yu’s offer and defected.
entries.literal: When he received Yu’s letter, he thereupon surrendered to Yu.

entries.zh: 裕謂範曰：「卿欲立申包胥之功，何以虛還也？」
entries.en: Yu said to Fan: “You wished to establish Shen Baoxu’s merit—why return empty?”
entries.literal: Yu said to Fan: “You wished to establish Shen Baoxu’s merit—why return empty?”

entries.zh: 範曰：「自亡祖司空世荷燕寵，故泣血秦庭，冀匡禍難。
entries.en: Fan said: “Since my late grandfather the minister of works, generations have borne Yan’s favor; therefore I wept blood in Qin’s court, hoping to right disaster.
entries.literal: Fan said: “Since my late grandfather the minister of works, generations have borne Yan’s favor; therefore I wept blood in Qin’s court, hoping to right disaster.

entries.zh: 屬西朝多故，丹誠無效，可謂天喪弊邑而贊明公。
entries.en: It fell out that the western court had many troubles, and my crimson loyalty had no effect—one may say Heaven destroyed our poor town to aid the enlightened duke.
entries.literal: It fell out that the western court had many troubles, and my crimson loyalty had no effect—one may say Heaven destroyed our poor town to aid the enlightened duke.

entries.zh: 智者見機而作，敢不至乎！」
entries.en: The wise see the moment and act—how dare I not arrive!”
entries.literal: The wise see the moment and act—how dare I not arrive!”

entries.zh: 翌日，裕將範循城，由是人情離駭，無復固志，裕謂範曰：「卿宜至城下，告以禍福。」
entries.en: The next day Yu led Fan around the wall; on that account human hearts split in terror, none again had firm will; Yu said to Fan: “You ought to go below the wall and announce fortune and disaster.”
entries.literal: The next day Yu led Fan around the wall; on that account human hearts split in terror, none again had firm will; Yu said to Fan: “You ought to go below the wall and announce fortune and disaster.”

entries.zh: 範曰：「雖蒙殊寵，猶未忍謀燕。」
entries.en: Fan said: “Though I have received extraordinary favor, I still cannot bear to plot against Yan.”
entries.literal: Fan said: “Though I have received extraordinary favor, I still cannot bear to plot against Yan.”

entries.zh: 裕嘉而不強，左右勸超誅範家，以止後叛。
entries.en: Liu Yu respected his silence; courtiers begged Murong Chao to slaughter Han Fan’s kin.
entries.literal: Yu praised him and did not force him; those at Chao’s side urged Chao to execute Fan’s family to stop later defections.

entries.zh: 超知敗在旦夕，又弟𧨳盡忠無貳，故不罪焉。
entries.en: Murong Chao spared Han Fan’s people because his brother Han Zhuo stayed loyal.
entries.literal: Chao knew defeat was at dawn or dusk, and moreover younger brother Han Zhuo was utterly loyal without twofold intent; therefore he did not punish them.

entries.zh: 是歲東萊雨血，廣固城門鬼夜哭。
entries.en: Blood rain fell; ghosts wailed at the gates.
entries.literal: That year Donglai rained blood; Guanggu’s city gates heard ghosts weep by night.

entries.zh: 明年朔旦，超登天門，朝群臣於城上，殺馬以饗將士，文武皆有遷授。
entries.en: On New Year’s dawn he feasted the garrison on horseflesh and handed out ranks.
entries.literal: The next year on new moon dawn Chao ascended the Heavenly Gate, faced the host of ministers atop the wall, slaughtered horses to feast generals and officers; civil and martial all received promotions.

entries.zh: 超幸姬魏夫人從超登城，見王師之盛，握超手而相對泣，韓𧨳諫曰：「陛下遭百六之會，正是勉強之秋，而反對女子悲泣，何其鄙也！」
entries.en: Chao’s favored concubine Lady Wei followed Chao onto the wall; seeing the royal army’s might, she grasped Chao’s hand and wept face to face; Han Zhuo remonstrated: “Your Majesty meets the hundred-six conjunction—this is exactly the season to strive hard—yet you face a woman weeping—how base!”
entries.literal: Chao’s favored concubine Lady Wei followed Chao onto the wall; seeing the royal army’s might, she grasped Chao’s hand and wept face to face; Han Zhuo remonstrated: “Your Majesty meets the hundred-six conjunction—this is exactly the season to strive hard—yet you face a woman weeping—how base!”

entries.zh: 超拭目謝之。
entries.en: Murong Chao wiped his tears and thanked him.
entries.literal: Chao wiped his eyes and thanked him.

entries.zh: 其尚書令董銳勸超出降，超大怒，系之於獄。
entries.en: Minister Secretary Dong Rui advised surrender; Murong Chao jailed him.
entries.literal: His minister secretary Dong Rui urged Chao to go out and surrender; Chao grew greatly angry and bound him in prison.

entries.zh: 於是賀賴盧、公孫五樓為地道出戰王師，不利。
entries.en: Helailu and Gongsun Wulou sallied by tunnel and lost.
entries.literal: Thereupon Helailu and Gongsun Wulou dug a tunnel to go out and fight the royal army; it went ill.

entries.zh: 河間人玄文說裕曰：「昔趙攻曹嶷，望氣者以為澠水帶城，非可攻拔，若塞五龍口，城必自陷。
entries.en: A man of Hejian, Xuan Wen, said to Yu: “Anciently when Zhao attacked Cao Yi, the qi-watcher thought the Mian River girdled the city and it could not be stormed; if you block the Wulong mouth, the city is sure to collapse of itself.
entries.literal: A man of Hejian, Xuan Wen, said to Yu: “Anciently when Zhao attacked Cao Yi, the qi-watcher thought the Mian River girdled the city and it could not be stormed; if you block the Wulong mouth, the city is sure to collapse of itself.

entries.zh: 石季龍從之，而嶷請降。
entries.en: Shi Hu followed this, and Yi asked to surrender.
entries.literal: Shi Hu followed this, and Yi asked to surrender.

entries.zh: 後慕容恪之圍段龕，亦如之，而龕降。
entries.en: Later when Murong Ke besieged Duan Kan, he did likewise, and Kan surrendered.
entries.literal: Later when Murong Ke besieged Duan Kan, he did likewise, and Kan surrendered.

entries.zh: 降後無幾，又震開之。
entries.en: Not long after surrender, it again quaked open.
entries.literal: Not long after surrender, it again quaked open.

entries.zh: 今舊基猶在，可塞之。」
entries.en: Now the old foundation still exists—you can block it.”
entries.literal: Now the old foundation still exists—you can block it.”

entries.zh: 裕從其言。
entries.en: Liu Yu dammed the water.
entries.literal: Yu followed his words.

entries.zh: 至是，城中男女患腳弱病者太半。
entries.en: Half the city sickened with leg-rot.
entries.literal: At this point more than half the men and women in the city suffered foot-weakness illness.

entries.zh: 超輦而升城，尚書悅壽言於超曰：「天地不仁，助寇為虐，戰士尪病，日就凋隕，守困窮城，息望外援，天時人事，亦可知矣。
entries.en: Chao was carried in a palanquin up the wall; Minister Yue Shou spoke to Chao: “Heaven and earth are not humane—they aid the bandit in cruelty; warriors are wasted and sick, daily nearing withering fall; we guard a poor exhausted city, breath stopped waiting for outside aid—heaven’s timing and human affairs are also knowable.
entries.literal: Chao was carried in a palanquin up the wall; Minister Yue Shou spoke to Chao: “Heaven and earth are not humane—they aid the bandit in cruelty; warriors are wasted and sick, daily nearing withering fall; we guard a poor exhausted city, breath stopped waiting for outside aid—heaven’s timing and human affairs are also knowable.

entries.zh: 苟曆運有終，堯、舜降位，轉禍為福，聖達以先。
entries.en: If the allotted reign has an end, Yao and Shun yielded the throne—turning disaster to fortune is what the sage and clear do first.
entries.literal: If the allotted reign has an end, Yao and Shun yielded the throne—turning disaster to fortune is what the sage and clear do first.

entries.zh: 宜追許、鄭之蹤，以全宗廟之重。」
entries.en: You ought to follow the tracks of Xu and Zheng to preserve the weight of the ancestral temple.”
entries.literal: You ought to follow the tracks of Xu and Zheng to preserve the weight of the ancestral temple.”

entries.zh: 超歎曰：「廢興，命也。
entries.en: Chao sighed: “Decline and rise are fate.
entries.literal: Chao sighed: “Decline and rise are fate.

entries.zh: 吾寧奮劍決死，不能銜璧求生。」
entries.en: I would rather brandish the sword and decide death than hold the jade disk and beg life.”
entries.literal: I would rather brandish the sword and decide death than hold the jade disk and beg life.”

entries.zh: 於是張綱為裕造沖車，覆以版屋，蒙之以皮，並設諸奇巧，城上火石弓矢無所施用；
entries.en: Zhang Gang built armored rams impervious to missiles.
entries.literal: Thereupon Zhang Gang for Yu made battering rams, roofed with plank houses, covered in hide, and installed every clever device—on the wall fire, stones, and bows had nothing they could apply;

entries.zh: 又為飛樓、懸梯、木幔之屬，遙臨城上。
entries.en: He added siege towers and mantlets.
entries.literal: he also made flying towers, hanging ladders, wooden screens, and the like, overlooking the wall from afar.

entries.zh: 超大怒，懸其母而支解之。
entries.en: Murong Chao butchered Zhang Gang’s mother in rage.
entries.literal: Chao grew greatly angry, hung up Gang’s mother and dismembered her.

entries.zh: 城中出降者相繼。
entries.en: Defectors streamed out.
entries.literal: Those who came out of the city to surrender followed one another.

entries.zh: 裕四面進攻，殺傷其眾，悅壽遂開門以納王師。
entries.en: Liu Yu stormed every face; Yue Shou opened the gates.
entries.literal: Yu attacked on four sides, killing and wounding his host; Yue Shou then opened the gate to admit the royal army.

entries.zh: 超與左右數十騎出亡，為裕軍所執。
entries.en: Murong Chao fled with dozens of riders and was caught.
entries.literal: Chao with several tens of horse of his attendants fled out and was seized by Yu’s army.

entries.zh: 裕數之以不降之狀，超神色自若，一無所言，惟以母托劉敬宣而已。
entries.en: Liu Yu rebuked him; Murong Chao stayed silent, begging only that his mother be given to Liu Jingxuan.
entries.literal: Yu enumerated his crimes of not surrendering; Chao’s spirit and bearing were self-possessed, he said nothing at all, only entrusted his mother to Liu Jingxuan.

entries.zh: 送建康市斬之，時年二十六。
entries.en: They executed him at twenty-six in the Jiankang marketplace.
entries.literal: He was sent to Jiankang market and beheaded, aged twenty-six.

entries.zh: 及德死，以義熙元年僭嗣偽位，大赦境內，改元曰太上。
entries.en: After Murong De died, in the first year of Yixi he usurped succession to the false throne, pardoned his territory, and changed the era name to Taishang.
entries.literal: When De died, in the first year of Yixi he usurped succession to the false throne, declared a general amnesty within his territory, and changed the era name to Taishang.

entries.zh: 慕容超
entries.en: Murong Chao
entries.literal: Murong Chao

entries.zh: 傉檀來伐，蒙遜敗之於若厚塢。
entries.en: When Nutan invaded, Mengxun defeated him at Ruohouwu.
entries.literal: Nutan came to attack; Mengxun defeated him at Ruohouwu.

entries.zh: 傉檀湟河太守文支據湟川，護軍成宜侯率眾降之。
entries.en: Wen Zhi, Nutan's governor on the Huang River, held the Huangchuan, while Cheng Yi, guard commander, brought his command over to Mengxun.
entries.literal: Nutan's Huanghe governor Wen Zhi held the Huangchuan; guard commander Marquis Cheng Yi led the host to submit.

entries.zh: 署文支鎮東大將軍、廣武太守、振武侯，成宜侯為振威將軍、湟川太守，以殿中將軍王建為湟河太守。
entries.en: He named Wen Zhi grand general of the east, governor of Guangwu, and marquis of Zhenwu; Cheng Yi general who rouses might and governor of Huangchuan; and Wang Jian of the palace guard as governor of the Huang River.
entries.literal: He appointed Wen Zhi grand general who guards the east, governor of Guangwu, marquis of Zhenwu; Cheng Yi as general who rouses might, governor of Huangchuan; and palace general Wang Jian as Huanghe governor.

entries.zh: 蒙遜下書曰：「古先哲王應期撥亂者，莫不經略八表，然後光闡純風。
entries.en: Mengxun proclaimed, "The sage kings of old who met their hour and quelled chaos always secured the outer marches before they spread pure rule.
entries.literal: Mengxun issued a writ saying: "Ancient sage kings who answered the period and set right disorder, none did not plan the eight outer regions, then afterward brightly open pure wind.

entries.zh: 孤雖智非靖難，職在濟時，而狡虜傉檀鴟峙舊京，毒加夷夏。
entries.en: Though I am no master of saving the age, it is my charge to aid the times, while that bandit Nutan perches like an owl on the old capital and poisons Chinese and barbarian alike.
entries.literal: I, although wisdom is not that which quiets disaster, duty lies in aiding the times, yet the crafty captive Nutan owl-perches on the old capital, poison reaching Yi and Xia.

entries.zh: 東苑之戮，酷甚長平，邊城之禍，害深獫狁。
entries.en: The massacre in the eastern park outdid Changping; the harm to the frontier ran deeper than the Xianyun raids.
entries.literal: The slaughter in the eastern park was crueler than Changping; the border cities' disaster harmed deeper than the Xianyun.

entries.zh: 每念蒼生之無辜，是以不遑啟處，身疲甲胄，體倦風塵。
entries.en: Whenever I think of the innocent people, I cannot rest; I wear armor until I drop and ride the dust without pause.
entries.literal: Each time I think of the dark people's guiltlessness, therefore I have no leisure to rest; body weary in armor, form tired in wind and dust.

entries.zh: 雖傾其巢穴，傉檀猶未授首。
entries.en: Though I have torn up his lair, Nutan still lives.
entries.literal: Although I have overturned his nest, Nutan still has not offered his head.

entries.zh: 傉檀弟文支追項伯歸漢之義，據彼重籓，請為臣妾。
entries.en: His brother Wen Zhi, like Xiang Bo who went over to Han, holds a key bastion and begs to become my subject.
entries.literal: Nutan's younger brother Wen Zhi, tracing Xiang Bo's meaning in returning to Han, holds that heavy screen and requests to be minister and concubine.

entries.zh: 自西平已南，連城繼順。
entries.en: South of Xiping the walled towns surrender in a chain.
entries.literal: From Xiping south, linked cities in succession submit.

entries.zh: 惟傉檀窮獸，守死樂都。
entries.en: Only Nutan, a beast at bay, clings to Ledu.
entries.literal: Only Nutan, cornered beast, guards death at Ledu.

entries.zh: 四支既落，命豈久全！
entries.en: With his limbs cut away, how long can he last!
entries.literal: The four limbs already fallen—how can life long endure!

entries.zh: 五緯之會已應，清一之期無賒，方散馬金山，黎元永逸。
entries.en: The conjunction of the five planets answers our rise; the day of unification is near—then we shall turn the horses loose at Jinshan and the people know lasting peace.
entries.literal: The five cords' conjunction already responds; the pure-one's term not distant—then I shall loose horses at Jin Mountain and the black-haired people rest forever.

entries.zh: 可露布遠近，咸使聞知。」
entries.en: Let this be proclaimed far and wide so every ear may hear."
entries.literal: May a bulletin be spread far and near, all causing to hear and know."

entries.zh: 晉益州刺史硃齡石遣使來聘。
entries.en: Zhu Lingshi, governor of Yi for the Eastern Jin, sent envoys on a courtesy mission.
entries.literal: Jin's governor of Yi, Zhu Lingshi, dispatched envoys to visit.

entries.zh: 蒙遜遣舍人黃迅報聘益州，因表曰：「上天降禍，四海分崩，靈耀擁于南裔，蒼生沒於醜虜。
entries.en: Mengxun sent the houseman Huang Xun to return the courtesy visit to Yi and submitted a memorial: "Heaven has scourged the realm; the empire is broken; the royal sun hangs over the south while the people lie under barbarian hooves.
entries.literal: Mengxun sent houseman Huang Xun to return the visit to Yi and submitted a memorial saying: "Heaven above sent disaster; the four seas split apart; the numinous radiance is stalled in the southern marches while the black-haired sink among ugly captives.

entries.zh: 陛下累聖重光，道邁周、漢，純風所被，八表宅心。
entries.en: Your Majesty, sage upon sage, surpasses Zhou and Han; wherever your virtue reaches, the eight quarters turn their hearts to you.
entries.literal: Your Majesty, piled sage and repeated light, the Way surpasses Zhou and Han; the pure wind's covering—within the eight extremities all dwell in heart.

entries.zh: 臣雖被髮邊徼，才非時雋，謬為河右遺黎推為盟主。
entries.en: I, though a tribesman on the frontier and no genius of the age, have been chosen leader by the people west of the River.
entries.literal: Your subject, although hair unbound on the border, talent not the age's outstanding, wrongly am by Hexi's surviving people pushed as covenant lord.

entries.zh: 臣之先人，世荷恩寵，雖曆夷險，執義不回，傾首陽，乃心王室。
entries.en: My forebears received your grace generation after generation; through every trial they kept faith and never turned their faces from the Jin sun.
entries.literal: Your subject's ancestors, generation receiving grace and favor, although passing through barbarian peril, held righteousness and did not turn; bowing to the sun, then heart in the royal house.

entries.zh: 去冬益州刺史硃齡石遣使詣臣，始具朝廷休問。
entries.en: Last winter Zhu Lingshi's envoy brought me word of the court's health and favor.
entries.literal: Last winter Governor of Yi Zhu Lingshi sent an envoy to your subject, beginning fully to convey the court's good rest and inquiry.

entries.zh: 承車騎將軍劉裕秣馬揮戈，以中原為事，可謂天贊大晉，篤生英輔。
entries.en: I hear Liu Yu, general of chariots and cavalry, is shoeing horses and raising spears for the Central Plain—surely Heaven aids great Jin and has sent a true champion.
entries.literal: I hear the chariot-and-cavalry general Liu Yu is rubbing horses and wielding spears, taking the central plains as his affair—this can be called Heaven aiding great Jin, richly producing heroic assistant.

entries.zh: 臣聞少康之興大夏，光武之復漢業，皆奮劍而起，眾無一旅，猶能成配天之功，著《車攻》之詠。
entries.en: I recall how Shaokang restored Xia and Guangwu rebuilt Han with a sword in hand and barely a regiment, yet their deeds matched Heaven and were sung in the ode Chegong.
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that Shaokang's raising Great Xia, Guangwu's restoring Han enterprise, both grasped sword and rose, the host not one brigade, still were able to complete merit matching Heaven, manifest the ode Chegong's chant.

entries.zh: 陛下據全楚之地，擁荊、揚之銳，而可垂拱晏然，棄二京以資戎虜！
entries.en: You hold all of Chu and the spear-points of Jing and Yang—can you sit idle and yield the two capitals to the nomads!
entries.literal: Your Majesty occupies all Chu land, holds Jing and Yang's keen edge—yet can hang sleeves in ease, abandon the two capitals to supply barbarian captives!

entries.zh: 若六軍北軫，克復有期，臣請率河西戎為晉右翼前驅。」
entries.en: When the six hosts wheel north and a day of reconquest is set, I beg to lead the Rong of the west river as the vanguard on your right wing."
entries.literal: If the six armies turn north and recovery has a date, your subject begs to lead the Hexi Rong as Jin's right wing and vanguard."

entries.zh: 蒙遜聞劉裕滅姚泓，怒甚。
entries.en: When word came that Liu Yu had destroyed Yao Hong, Mengxun flew into a rage.
entries.literal: Mengxun heard Liu Yu had extinguished Yao Hong, was very angry.

entries.zh: 門下校郎劉祥言事于蒙遜，蒙遜曰：「汝聞劉裕入關，敢研研然也！」
entries.en: Liu Xiang offered advice; Mengxun snarled, "You heard that Liu Yu had entered the passes and grew insolent!"
entries.literal: Gatehouse collating officer Liu Xiang spoke on affairs to Mengxun; Mengxun said: "You heard Liu Yu enter the passes, dare to be so pleased with yourself!"

entries.zh: 遂殺之。
entries.en: He had Liu Xiang killed.
entries.literal: Thereupon killed him.

entries.zh: 其峻暴如是。
entries.en: Such was his harsh and violent temper.
entries.literal: His severity and violence were like this.

entries.zh: 顧謂左右曰：「古之行師，不犯歲鎮所在。
entries.en: He told his attendants, "The ancients never campaigned against the station of the year star and the garrison planet.
entries.literal: He turned and said to left and right: "Of old when marching armies, one did not offend against the year star and the garrison star's seat.

entries.zh: 姚氏舜後，軒轅之苗裔也。
entries.en: The Yao clan are Shun's line and the blood of the Yellow Thearch.
entries.literal: The Yao house is Shun's posterity, Xuanyuan's descendants.

entries.zh: 今鎮星在軒轅，而裕滅之，亦不能久守關中。」
entries.en: The garrison star now stands in Xuanyuan, yet Liu Yu has destroyed Qin—he too will not long hold Guanzhong."
entries.literal: Now the garrison star is in Xuanyuan, yet Yu destroyed them—also cannot long hold Guanzhong."

entries.zh: 蒙遜為李士業敗于解支澗，復收散卒欲戰。
entries.en: Mengxun was routed by Li Shiye at Jiezhi Creek and tried to rally his broken troops for another round.
entries.literal: Mengxun was by Li Shiye defeated at Jiezhi Stream, again gathered scattered soldiers desiring to fight.

entries.zh: 前將軍成都諫曰：「臣聞高祖有彭城之敗，終成大漢，宜旋師以為後圖。」
entries.en: Juqu Chengdu urged him, "Even the Han founder lost at Pengcheng yet built the dynasty—you should withdraw and plan again."
entries.literal: Vanguard general Chengdu remonstrated saying: "Your subject has heard the High Ancestor had Pengcheng's defeat, yet in the end completed great Han—fit to turn the army for later planning.

entries.zh: 蒙遜從之，城建康而歸。
entries.en: Mengxun agreed, walled Jiankang, and marched home.
entries.literal: Mengxun followed it, encamped at Jiankang commandery and returned.

entries.zh: 沮渠蒙遜
entries.en: Juqu Mengxun.
entries.literal: Juqu Mengxun.

entries.zh: 勃勃聞姚泓將姚嵩與氐王楊盛相持，率騎四萬襲上邽，未至而嵩為盛所殺。
entries.en: Hearing Yao Hong's general Yao Song fought the Di king Yang Sheng, Bobo led forty thousand horse to raid Shanggui; Song was killed before he arrived.
entries.literal: Bobo heard that Yao Hong's general Yao Song was locked in struggle with the Di king Yang Sheng; he led forty thousand horsemen to raid Shanggui, but before he arrived Song was killed by Sheng.

entries.zh: 勃勃攻上邽，二旬克之，殺泓秦州剌史姚平都及將士五千人，毀城而去。
entries.en: Bobo took Shanggui in twenty days, killed Governor Yao Pingdu and five thousand men, razed the city, and withdrew.
entries.literal: Bobo attacked Shanggui; in twenty days he took it, killed Hong's Qin Province governor Yao Pingdu and five thousand officers and soldiers, destroyed the city, and departed.

entries.zh: 進攻陰密，又殺興將姚良子及將士萬餘人。
entries.en: He attacked Yinmi and killed Xing's general Yao Liangzi and more than ten thousand soldiers.
entries.literal: He advanced to attack Yinmi and again killed Xing's general Yao Liangzi and more than ten thousand officers and soldiers.

entries.zh: 以其子昌為使持節、前將軍、雍州刺史，鎮陰密。
entries.en: He made his son Chang Bearer of the Staff, Forward General, and Governor of Yong Province, garrisoning Yinmi.
entries.literal: He made his son Chang Bearer of the Staff, Forward General, and Governor of Yong Province, garrisoning Yinmi.

entries.zh: 泓將姚恢棄安定，奔于長安，安定人胡儼、華韜率戶五萬據安定，降於勃勃。
entries.en: Yao Hui abandoned Anding for Chang'an; Hu Yan and Hua Tao held Anding with fifty thousand households and surrendered to Bobo.
entries.literal: Hong's general Yao Hui abandoned Anding and fled to Chang'an; the men of Anding, Hu Yan and Hua Tao, led fifty thousand households to hold Anding and surrender to Bobo.

entries.zh: 以儼為侍中，韜為尚書，留鎮東羊苟兒鎮之，配以鮮卑五千。
entries.en: He made Yan Attendant-in-Ordinary and Tao Master of Writing, left the General Who Garrisons the East, Yang Gou'er, to garrison Anding with five thousand Xianbei.
entries.literal: He made Yan Attendant-in-Ordinary and Tao Master of Writing, left the General Who Garrisons the East, Yang Gou'er, to garrison it, and assigned five thousand Xianbei.

entries.zh: 進攻泓將姚諶於雍城，諶奔長安。
entries.en: He attacked Yao Chen at Yongcheng; Chen fled to Chang'an.
entries.literal: He advanced to attack Hong's general Yao Chen at Yongcheng; Chen fled to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 勃勃進師次郿城，泓遣其將姚紹來距，勃勃退如安定。
entries.en: Bobo encamped at Mei; Hong sent Yao Shao against him; Bobo withdrew to Anding.
entries.literal: Bobo advanced and encamped at Mei; Hong sent his general Yao Shao to resist; Bobo withdrew toward Anding.

entries.zh: 胡儼等襲殺苟兒，以城降泓。
entries.en: Hu Yan killed Gou'er and surrendered the city to Hong.
entries.literal: Hu Yan and the others raided and killed Gou'er, surrendering the city to Hong.

entries.zh: 勃勃引歸杏城，笑謂群臣曰：「劉裕伐秦，水陸兼進，且裕有高世之略，姚泓豈能自固！
entries.en: Bobo withdrew to Xingcheng and laughed: "Liu Yu attacks Qin by land and sea with stratagems beyond his age—how can Yao Hong stand alone?
entries.literal: Bobo withdrew to Xingcheng and said to his ministers with a laugh: "Liu Yu attacks Qin by land and water together, and Yu has stratagems transcending the age—how can Yao Hong hold firm by himself!

entries.zh: 吾驗以天時人事，必當克之。
entries.en: By heaven's signs and human affairs he is sure to win.
