entries.literal: I test it by heaven's seasons and human affairs—he is sure to conquer.

entries.zh: 又其兄弟內叛，安可以距人！
entries.en: His brothers rebel within—how can he resist outsiders?
entries.literal: Moreover his brothers rebel within—how can he resist others!

entries.zh: 裕既克長安，利在速返，正可留子弟及諸將守關中。
entries.en: Once Yu takes Chang'an he will hurry home, leaving only sons and generals to hold Guanzhong.
entries.literal: When Yu has taken Chang'an, his profit lies in swift return; he can only leave sons and younger brothers and the generals to hold Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 待裕發軫，吾取之若拾芥耳，不足復勞吾士馬。」
entries.en: When Yu departs I shall take it like picking up a mustard seed—no need to weary my army."
entries.literal: Wait until Yu sets out and I shall take it like picking up a mustard stalk—no need again to weary my officers and horses."

entries.zh: 於是秣馬厲兵，休養士卒。
entries.en: He fed horses, sharpened weapons, and rested his troops.
entries.literal: Thereupon he fed horses and sharpened weapons, resting and nurturing officers and soldiers.

entries.zh: 尋進據安定，姚泓嶺北鎮戍郡縣悉降，勃勃於是盡有嶺北之地。
entries.en: He seized Anding; Hong's garrisons north of the mountains all surrendered, and Bobo held the north.
entries.literal: Presently he advanced and held Anding; Yao Hong's garrison commanderies and counties north of the mountains all surrendered, and Bobo thereupon fully possessed the lands north of the mountains.

entries.zh: 俄而劉裕滅泓，入于長安，遣使遺勃勃書，請通和好，約為兄弟。
entries.en: Liu Yu destroyed Hong, entered Chang'an, and sent envoys proposing brotherhood with Bobo.
entries.literal: Before long Liu Yu destroyed Hong and entered Chang'an; he sent envoys with a letter to Bobo requesting good relations and covenanting as brothers.

entries.zh: 勃勃命其中書侍郎皇甫徽為文而陰誦之，召裕使前，口授舍人為書，封以答裕。
entries.en: Bobo ordered his Palace Secretariat Attendant Huangfu Hui to compose a text and memorize it secretly; he summoned Yu's envoy forward, dictated it orally to a clerk to write, sealed it, and returned it to Yu.
entries.literal: Bobo ordered his Palace Secretariat Attendant Huangfu Hui to compose a text and memorize it secretly; he summoned Yu's envoy forward, dictated it orally to his document clerk to write, sealed it, and returned it to Yu.

entries.zh: 裕覽其文而奇之，使者又言勃勃容儀瑰偉，英武絕人。
entries.en: Yu read the letter and marveled; the envoy said Bobo's bearing was magnificent and his valor unmatched.
entries.literal: Yu read the text and marveled at it; the envoy also said Bobo's bearing was magnificent and his martial prowess unmatched.

entries.zh: 裕歎曰：「吾所不如也！」
entries.en: Yu sighed: "I am not his equal!"
entries.literal: Yu sighed and said: "I am not his equal!"

entries.zh: 既而勃勃還統萬，裕留子義真鎮長安而還。
entries.en: Bobo returned to Tongwan; Yu left his son Yizhen at Chang'an and went home.
entries.literal: Presently Bobo returned to Tongwan; Yu left his son Yizhen to garrison Chang'an and returned.

entries.zh: 勃勃聞之，大悅，謂王買德曰：「朕將進圖長安，卿試言取之方略。」
entries.en: Bobo was delighted and asked Wang Maide: "I mean to take Chang'an—tell me how."
entries.literal: When Bobo heard this he was greatly pleased and said to Wang Maide: "I shall advance to take Chang'an—try to speak the strategy for taking it."

entries.zh: 買德曰：「劉裕滅秦，所謂以亂平亂，未有德政以濟蒼生。
entries.en: Maide said: "Liu Yu ended Qin by disorder, not by virtue—the people have no relief.
entries.literal: Maide said: "Liu Yu destroyed Qin—what is called using disorder to pacify disorder; there is no virtuous government to aid the black-haired masses.

entries.zh: 關中形勝之地，而以弱才小兒守之，非經遠之規也。
entries.en: Guanzhong is strategic ground, guarded by a weak boy—not a far-sighted plan.
entries.literal: Guanzhong is terrain of strategic advantage, yet a weak talent and small child guard it—not a plan reaching far.

entries.zh: 狼狽而返者，欲速成篡事耳，無暇有意于中原。
entries.en: He hurries home to usurp the throne and has no time for the central plains.
entries.literal: He returns in distress because he wishes to hurry the matter of usurpation and has no leisure to care for the central plains.

entries.zh: 陛下以順伐逆，義貫幽顯，百姓以君命望陛下義旗之至，以日為歲矣。
entries.en: Your Majesty attacks rebellion with justice; the people have awaited your banner for years.
entries.literal: Your Majesty with obedience attacks rebellion, righteousness penetrating the hidden and manifest; the hundred surnames await Your Majesty's banner of righteous army as if counting days by years.

entries.zh: 青泥、上洛，南師之沖要，宜置遊兵斷其去來之路。
entries.en: Qingni and Shangluo are the southern army's vital passes—set roaming troops to cut their retreat.
entries.literal: Qingni and Shangluo are the vital passes of the southern army—you should set roaming troops to cut their coming and going.

entries.zh: 然後杜潼關，塞崤、陝，絕其水陸之道。
entries.en: Then block Tong Pass and Xiao and Shan and cut their roads by land and water.
entries.literal: Then block Tong Pass, seal Xiao and Shan, and cut their water and land roads.

entries.zh: 陛下聲檄長安，申布恩澤，三輔父老皆壺漿以迎王師矣。
entries.en: Proclaim grace at Chang'an and the three auxiliaries will welcome you with wine.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's proclamation at Chang'an, spreading grace— the elders of the three auxiliaries will all bring wine and broth to welcome the royal army.

entries.zh: 義真獨坐空城，逃竄無所，一旬之間必面縛麾下，所謂兵不血刃，不戰而自定也。」
entries.en: Yizhen sits in an empty city with nowhere to flee; within ten days he will bind himself before you—arms without blood, victory without battle."
entries.literal: Yizhen sits alone in an empty city with nowhere to flee; within ten days he is sure to bind himself before your majesty's horse—what is called arms without bloody blades, settled without fighting."

entries.zh: 勃勃善之，以子璝都督前鋒諸軍事，領撫軍大將軍，率騎二萬南伐長安，前將軍赫連昌屯兵潼關，以買德為撫軍右長史，南斷青泥，勃勃率大軍繼發。
entries.en: Bobo approved: Gui led twenty thousand horse on Chang'an, Chang held Tong Pass, Maide blocked Qingni, and Bobo followed with the main army.
entries.literal: Bobo approved; he made his son Gui commander of the vanguard armies, Pacification Grand General, leading twenty thousand horse south to attack Chang'an; the Forward General Helian Chang encamped at Tong Pass; Maide was made Pacification Right Chief Clerk to cut Qingni in the south; Bobo followed with the great army.

entries.zh: 璝至渭陽，降者屬路。
entries.en: Gui reached Weiyang; surrenderers lined the road.
entries.literal: Gui reached Weiyang; those who surrendered lined the road.

entries.zh: 義真遣龍驤將軍沈田子率眾逆戰，不利而退，屯劉回堡。
entries.en: Yizhen sent the Dragon-Soaring General Shen Tianzi against him; Tianzi was beaten back to Liuhui Fort.
entries.literal: Yizhen sent the Dragon-Soaring General Shen Tianzi to lead the host to meet in battle; he was unsuccessful and withdrew, encamping at Liuhui Fort.

entries.zh: 田子與義真司馬王鎮惡不平，因鎮惡出城，遂殺之。
entries.en: Tianzi quarreled with Yizhen's marshal Wang Zhen'e and killed him when he left the city.
entries.literal: Tianzi and Yizhen's Marshal Wang Zhen'e were at odds; because Zhen'e left the city, Tianzi killed him.

entries.zh: 義真又殺田子。
entries.en: Yizhen then killed Tianzi.
entries.literal: Yizhen also killed Tianzi.

entries.zh: 於是悉召外軍入於城中，閉門距守。
entries.en: He recalled all outside troops, shut the gates, and held the city.
entries.literal: Thereupon he summoned all external armies into the city, shut the gates, and held in defense.

entries.zh: 關中郡縣悉降。
entries.en: Guanzhong's commanderies and counties surrendered.
entries.literal: Commanderies and counties of Guanzhong all surrendered.

entries.zh: 璝夜襲長安，不克。
entries.en: Gui raided Chang'an by night and failed.
entries.literal: Gui raided Chang'an by night and could not take it.

entries.zh: 勃勃進據咸陽，長安樵采路絕。
entries.en: Bobo took Xianyang; Chang'an's supply roads were cut.
entries.literal: Bobo advanced and held Xianyang; the fuel-gathering roads of Chang'an were cut.

entries.zh: 劉裕聞之，大懼，乃召義真東鎮洛陽，以硃齡石為雍州刺史，守長安。
entries.en: Liu Yu in alarm recalled Yizhen to Luoyang and sent Zhu Lingshi to hold Chang'an.
entries.literal: When Liu Yu heard he was greatly afraid; he summoned Yizhen east to garrison Luoyang and made Zhu Lingshi Governor of Yong to hold Chang'an.

entries.zh: 義真大掠而東，至於灞上，百姓遂逐齡石，而迎勃勃入于長安。
entries.en: Yizhen plundered as he fled east; at Bashang the people expelled Lingshi and welcomed Bobo into Chang'an.
entries.literal: Yizhen plundered greatly as he went east; when he reached Bashang the common people drove out Lingshi and welcomed Bobo into Chang'an.

entries.zh: 璝率眾三萬追擊義真，王師敗績，義真單馬而遁。
entries.en: Gui pursued Yizhen with thirty thousand; the Jin army was routed and Yizhen escaped alone.
entries.literal: Gui led thirty thousand to pursue Yizhen; the royal army was defeated and Yizhen fled on a single horse.

entries.zh: 買德獲晉甯朔將軍傅弘之、輔國將軍蒯恩、義真司馬毛脩之於青泥，積人頭以為京觀。
entries.en: Maide captured the Jin General of Pacifying the North Fu Hongzhi, the Pacification General Kuai En, and Yizhen's Marshal Mao Xiuzhi at Qingni and piled heads into a victory mound.
entries.literal: Maide captured the Jin General of Pacifying the North Fu Hongzhi, the Pacification General Kuai En, and Yizhen's Marshal Mao Xiuzhi at Qingni and piled heads into a mound.

entries.zh: 於是勃勃大饗將士于長安，舉觴謂王買德曰：「卿往日之言，一周而果效，可謂算無遺策矣。
entries.en: Bobo feasted his officers in Chang'an and told Maide: "Your words of former days bore fruit after one year's circuit—no strategy left unused.
entries.literal: Thereupon Bobo held a great feast for officers at Chang'an, raised his cup and said to Wang Maide: "Your words of other days bore fruit after one year's circuit—one may call it a plan without leftover strategy.

entries.zh: 雖宗廟社稷之靈，亦卿謀獻之力也。
entries.en: The ancestral spirits helped—but so did your counsel.
entries.literal: Though the spirits of the ancestral temple and altars also had your plotting contribution.

entries.zh: 此觴所集，非卿而誰！」
entries.en: This cup is for you alone!"
entries.literal: This cup gathers—not you, who else!"

entries.zh: 於是拜買德都官尚書，加冠軍將軍，封河陽侯。
entries.en: He made Maide director of the masters of writing, champion general, and marquis of Heyang.
entries.literal: Thereupon he appointed Maide Director of the Masters of Writing, added Champion General, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Heyang.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：赫連勃勃犬熏醜種類，入居邊宇，屬中壤分崩，緣間肆慝，控弦鳴鏑，據有朔方。
entries.en: The historian writes: Helian Bobo was a barbarian breed who seized the north when the central plains split, sounding bow and whistle across Shuofang.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Helian Bobo was a dog-stench ugly species who entered and dwelt in the border territories; when the central plains split apart he seized the interval and unleashed wickedness, controlling the bent bow and sounding the arrow-whistle, holding Shuofang.

entries.zh: 遂乃法玄象以開宮，擬神京而建社，竊先王之徽號，備中國之禮容，驅駕英賢，窺窬天下。
entries.en: He patterned palaces on the divine capital, stole kings' titles, aped Chinese ritual, and eyed the realm.
entries.literal: Thereupon he patterned the dark image to open palaces, modeled the divine capital to build the altars, stole the honored titles of former kings, prepared the ritual and bearing of China, drove and harnessed worthy men, and peered covetously at the realm.

entries.zh: 然其器識高爽，風骨魁奇，姚興睹之而醉心，宋祖聞之而動色。
entries.en: Yet his insight was keen and his bearing remarkable; Yao Xing marveled and Liu Yu was stirred.
entries.literal: Yet his capacity and insight were lofty and clear, his wind and bone outstanding and strange; Yao Xing saw him and was intoxicated in heart, Emperor Wu of Song heard and was moved in countenance.

entries.zh: 豈陰山之韞異氣，不然何以致斯乎！
entries.en: Did the Yin Mountains breed strange spirit—how else produce such a man!
entries.literal: Was it that the Yin Mountains stored strange breath—if not, how reach this!

entries.zh: 雖雄略過人，而凶殘未革，飾非距諫，酷害朝臣，部內囂然，忠良捲舌。
entries.en: Though his strategy surpassed others, cruelty remained; he rejected remonstrance and harmed ministers until loyalty fell silent.
entries.literal: Though his bold strategy surpassed others, his fierce cruelty was not reformed; he adorned wrong and rejected remonstrance, cruelly harmed court ministers; within the departments there was clamor and loyal men curled their tongues.

entries.zh: 滅亡之禍，宜在厥身，猶及其嗣，非不幸也。
entries.en: Destruction should have fallen on him alone—yet it reached his heirs; that was no accident.
entries.literal: The calamity of extinction should have been on his person—yet it reached his heirs; this was not misfortune.

entries.zh: 赫連勃勃
entries.en: Helian Bobo
entries.literal: Helian Bobo

entries.zh: 三月乙丑朔。
entries.en: The third month opened on yichou.
entries.literal: Third month, yichou new moon.

entries.zh: 戊辰，詔常參官寒食拜墓，在畿內聽假日往還，他州府奏取進止。
entries.en: Cold Food grave visits were regulated for capital officials on wuchen.
entries.literal: On wuchen an edict: regular-attendance officials may visit graves at Cold Food — within the capital circuit they are permitted holiday travel back and forth; other prefectures and circuits memorialized for decision.

entries.zh: 辛未，御史中丞武元衡奏：「中書門下御史台五品已上官、尚書省四品已上、諸司正三品已上、從三品職事官、東都留守、轉運鹽鐵節度觀察使、團練防禦招討經略等使、河南尹、同華州刺史、諸衛將軍三品已上官除授，皆入合謝，其餘官許于宣政南班拜訖便退。」
entries.en: On xinwei Wu Yuanheng, vice censor-in-chief, memorialized: "Officials of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Censorate of fifth rank and above, the Department of State Affairs of fourth rank and above, all offices of full third rank and above, acting officials of the third rank, the eastern capital defender, transport and salt-and-iron commissioners, military, observation, training, defense, punitive, and strategy commissioners, the prefect of Henan, the prefects of Tongzhou and Huazhou, and generals of the guards of third rank and above shall all enter the hall to give thanks when appointed. The remaining officials may bow in the southern row at Xuanzheng and then withdraw."
entries.literal: On xinwei Vice Censor-in-Chief Wu Yuanheng memorialized: "Officials of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Censorate of fifth rank and above, the Department of State Affairs of fourth rank and above, all regular third rank and above, acting third rank and above, eastern capital regent, transport and salt commissioners, military observation commissioners, defense and campaign commissioners, Governor of Henan, Governors of Tong and Hua, generals of the guards of third rank and above — on appointment all enter the hall to give thanks; other officials are permitted to bow at the southern court of Xuanzheng and withdraw."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「如此例中有加使及職掌並准此。」
entries.en: An edict said: "Where this precedent includes added commissioners and duties, all follow this."
entries.literal: An edict said: "Where this precedent includes added commissioners and duties, all follow this."

entries.zh: 又「兵部、吏部、禮部貢院官員，每舉選限內，有十月至二月不奉朝參。
entries.en: Also: "Personnel of the War, Personnel, and Rites examination bureaus — within each selection limit, from the tenth month to the second month do not attend court.
entries.literal: Also: "Personnel of the War, Personnel, and Rites examination bureaus — within each selection limit, from the tenth month to the second month do not attend court.

entries.zh: 若稱事繁，則中書門下、御史台、度支、京兆府公事至重，朝謁如常。
entries.en: If they claim affairs are numerous, then the Secretariat-Chancellery, Censorate, revenue office, and metropolitan government have affairs to the utmost — court attendance as usual.
entries.literal: If they claim affairs are numerous, then the Secretariat-Chancellery, Censorate, revenue office, and metropolitan government have affairs to the utmost — court attendance as usual.

entries.zh: 況旬節已賜歸休，又許分日，一月之內，才奉十日朝參，甚暑甚寒，又蒙矜放。
entries.en: Moreover seasonal holidays already grant return rest, and divided days are also permitted — within one month they attend court only ten days; in great heat and great cold they are also shown compassion.
entries.literal: Moreover seasonal holidays already grant return rest, and divided days are also permitted — within one month they attend court only ten days; in great heat and great cold they are also shown compassion.

entries.zh: 臣求故實，以為王顏任中丞日嘗論其事，舉對甚詳。
entries.en: Your subject seeks former precedent and holds that when Wang Yan held the censorate he once discussed this matter and answered in great detail.
entries.literal: Your subject seeks former precedent and holds that when Wang Yan held the censorate he once discussed this matter and answered in great detail.

entries.zh: 伏請准貞元十二年四月二十七日敕，永為常式。」
entries.en: I humbly ask that the edict of Zhenyuan 12, fourth month, twenty-seventh day, be followed forever as constant form."
entries.literal: I humbly ask that the edict of Zhenyuan 12, fourth month, twenty-seventh day, be followed forever as constant form."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The throne agreed.
entries.literal: It was followed.

entries.zh: 丙子，嚴礪收梓州。
entries.en: Yan Li took Zizhou on bingzi.
entries.literal: On bingzi Yan Li recovered Zizhou.

entries.zh: 丁丑，制削奪劉辟在身官爵。
entries.en: Liu Pi was stripped of rank on dingchou.
entries.literal: On dingchou an order stripped Liu Pi of all offices held in life.

entries.zh: 先是韓全義入朝，令其甥楊惠琳知留後，俄有詔除李演為節度，代全義。
entries.en: Han Quanyi's nephew Yang Huilin had held the command until Li Yan was appointed.
entries.literal: Earlier Han Quanyi entered court; he ordered his nephew Yang Huilin to act as regent; soon an edict appointed Li Yan military commissioner in his stead.

entries.zh: 演赴任，惠琳據城叛，詔發河東、天德兵誅之。
entries.en: Yang Huilin rebelled when Li Yan arrived; imperial troops were sent.
entries.literal: Yan went to his post; Huilin held the city in rebellion; an edict sent Hedong and Tiande troops to execute him.

entries.zh: 辛巳，夏州兵馬使張承金斬惠琳，傳首以獻。
entries.en: Zhang Chengjin killed Huilin and presented his head on xinsi.
entries.literal: On xinsi Xiazhou army commander Zhang Chengjin beheaded Huilin and sent the head as tribute.

entries.zh: 壬辰，大行太上皇德妃董氏卒。
entries.en: Lady Dong, Shunzong's consort, died on renchen.
entries.literal: On renchen the late Retired Emperor's Virtuous Consort Lady Dong died.

entries.zh: 以右神策行營節度高崇文檢校兵部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度。
entries.en: Gao Chongwen, military commissioner of the Right Divine Strategy field command, was made acting minister of war, prefect of Zizhou, and military commissioner of Jiannan East.
entries.literal: Gao Chongwen, military commissioner of the Right Divine Strategy field command, was made acting minister of war, prefect of Zizhou, and military commissioner of Jiannan East.

entries.zh: 戊戌，以安南經略副使張舟為安南都護、本管經略使。
entries.en: Zhang Zhou took Annan on wuxu.
entries.literal: On wuxu Zhang Zhou, Annan pacification vice commissioner, was made Protector-General of Annan and circuit commissioner.

entries.zh: 己亥，以前劍南東川節度使韋丹為晉絳觀察使。
entries.en: Wei Dan went to the Jin-He circuit on jihai.
entries.literal: On jihai former eastern Sichuan military commissioner Wei Dan was made Jin-He observer.

entries.zh: 壬寅，以前安南經略使趙昌為廣州刺史、嶺南節度使。
entries.en: On renyin Zhao Chang, former strategy commissioner of Annan, was made prefect of Guangzhou and military commissioner of Lingnan.
entries.literal: On renyin Zhao Chang, former strategy commissioner of Annan, was made prefect of Guangzhou and military commissioner of Lingnan.

entries.zh: 癸卯，前嶺南節度使徐申卒。
entries.en: Xu Shen died on guimao.
entries.literal: On guimao former Lingnan military commissioner Xu Shen died.

entries.zh: 丙午，命宰臣監試製舉人于尚書省，以制舉人先朝所征，不欲親試也。
entries.en: Ministers supervised the decree exam rather than the emperor on bingwu.
entries.literal: On bingwu the councillors were ordered to supervise examination of decree-examination candidates at the Department of State Affairs — because decree candidates were summoned by the former dynasty and he did not wish to examine personally.

entries.zh: 丁未，以檢校司空、平章事杜祐為司徒，所司備禮冊拜，平章事如故；
entries.en: Du You became Minister of Education on dingwei while keeping the council;
entries.literal: On dingwei Du You, acting Master of Works and Grand Councillor, was made Minister of Education; the relevant offices prepared rites for enfeoffment and bowing; Grand Councillor as before;

entries.zh: 罷領度支、鹽鐵、轉運等使，從其讓也，仍以兵部侍即李巽代領其任。
entries.en: he yielded fiscal posts to Li Xun.
entries.literal: he ceased leading revenue, salt, iron, and transport commissions — following his declination — and Vice Minister of War Li Xun was still made to lead those duties.

entries.zh: 戊申，以隴右經略使、秦州經略使、秦州刺史劉澭為保義軍節度使。
entries.en: On wushen Liu Yong, strategy commissioner of Longyou and Qinzhou and prefect of Qinzhou, was made military commissioner of Baoyi Army.
entries.literal: On wushen Liu Yong, strategy commissioner of Longyou and Qinzhou and prefect of Qinzhou, was made military commissioner of Baoyi Army.

entries.zh: 賑浙東米十萬石。
entries.en: Zhedong received famine relief grain.
entries.literal: Zhedong was given 100,000 piculs of relief grain.

entries.zh: 己未，武元衡奏，常參官兼御史大夫、中丞者，准檢校省官例，立在本品同類之上。
entries.en: Wu Yuanheng fixed precedence for censor-concurrents on jiwei.
entries.literal: On jiwei Wu Yuanheng memorialized: regular-attendance officials who are concurrent Censor-in-Chief or vice censor — follow the precedent for acting provincial officials, standing above others of the same original rank.

entries.zh: 壬戌，邵王約薨。
entries.en: Prince Yue of Shao died on renxu.
entries.literal: On renxu Prince of Shao Yue died.

entries.zh: 武元衡奏：「正衙待制官，本置此官以備問。
entries.en: Wu Yuanheng memorialized: "Regular-attendance awaiting-order officials — originally this office was established to prepare for questioning.
entries.literal: Wu Yuanheng memorialized: "Regular-attendance awaiting-order officials — originally this office was established to prepare for questioning.

entries.zh: 比來正衙多不奏事。
entries.en: Recently at regular court many do not present business.
entries.literal: Recently at regular court many do not present business.

entries.zh: 自今後請以尚書省六品以上職事官、東宮師傅賓詹、王傅等，每坐日令兩人待制，退朝，詔于延英候對。」
entries.en: From now on let officials of the Department of State Affairs of sixth rank and above with substantive posts, eastern palace tutors, companions, and princes' tutors — each court day two await order; after court, order them to wait at Yanying for audience."
entries.literal: From now on let officials of the Department of State Affairs of sixth rank and above with substantive posts, eastern palace tutors, companions, and princes' tutors — each court day two await order; after court, order them to wait at Yanying for audience."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The throne agreed.
entries.literal: It was followed.

entries.zh: 順宗至德大聖大安孝皇帝諱誦，德宗長子，母昭德皇后王氏。
entries.en: Shunzong, the Filial Emperor Song, was Dezong's eldest son; his mother was Empress Zhaode Wang.
entries.literal: Emperor Shunzong, posthumous title To the Utmost Virtue Great Sage Great Peace Filial, taboo name Song, eldest son of Dezong; mother Empress Zhaode, née Wang.

entries.zh: 上元二年正月生於長安之東內。
entries.en: He was born in the eastern palace quarter of Chang'an in Shangyuan 2.
entries.literal: In the first month of Shangyuan 2 he was born in the Eastern Inner Palace at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 大曆十四年六月，封宣王。
entries.en: In Dali 14 he received the title Prince of Xuan.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of Dali 14 he was enfeoffed Prince of Xuan.

entries.zh: 建中元年正月丁卯，立為皇太子。
entries.en: He became crown prince on dingmao in the first month of Jianzhong 1.
entries.literal: In the first month of Jianzhong 1, on dingmao, he was installed as heir apparent.

entries.zh: 侍中裴耀卿、中書令張九齡、禮部尚書李林甫等奏曰：「外族之親，禮無厭降。
entries.en: Chief Attendant Pei Yaoqing, Grand Counselor Zhang Jiuling, Minister of Rites Li Linfu, and others wrote: "External kin are not subject to ritual demotion.
entries.literal: Attendant-in-chief Pei Yaoqing, Grand Counselor Zhang Jiuling, Minister of Rites Li Linfu, and others memorialized, saying: "Kin of the external clan—in ritual there is no suppressed demotion.

entries.zh: 外甥既為舅母制服，舅母還合報之。
entries.en: A nephew already mourns his aunt by marriage; she in turn should return the obligation.
entries.literal: The sister's son already wears mourning for the mother's brother's wife; the mother's brother's wife in turn ought to return it.

entries.zh: 夫外甥既為報服，則與夫之姨舅，以類是同，外甥之妻，不得無服。
entries.en: If a nephew wears return mourning, the same logic covers the husband's aunts and uncles; a nephew's wife cannot go without dress.
entries.literal: Since the sister's son already wears return mourning, then with the husband's mother's brothers and sisters it is the same by category; the sister's son's wife cannot be without mourning.

entries.zh: 所增者頗廣，所引者漸疏。
entries.en: What is added grows wide; what is cited grows remote.
entries.literal: What is added is rather broad; what is cited grows ever more distant.

entries.zh: 微臣愚蒙，猶有未達。」
entries.en: We, foolish and ignorant petty officials, still do not fully grasp it."
entries.literal: We, foolish and ignorant petty officials, still do not fully grasp it."

entries.zh: 玄宗又手製答曰：「從服有六，此其一也。降殺之制，禮無明文。此皆自身率親，用為制服。所有存抑，儘是推恩。朕情有未安，故令詳議，非欲苟求變古，以示不同。卿等以為『外族之親，禮無厭降，報服之制，所引甚疏』。且姨舅者，屬從之至近也，以親言之，則亦姑伯之匹敵也。豈有所引者疏，而降所親者服？又婦，從夫者也。夫之姨舅，夫既有服，從夫而服，由是睦親。實欲令不肖者企及，賢者俯就。卿等宜熟詳之。」耀卿等奏曰：「陛下體至仁之德，廣推恩之道，將弘引進，以示睦親，再發德音，更令詳議。
entries.en: Xuanzong again composed a personal reply: "There are six kinds of derivative mourning, and this is one of them. As for the rules of lowering and reducing, the ritual has no clear text. These all proceed from oneself in leading kin and are used to make mourning dress. What is preserved and restrained is entirely a pushing outward of grace. My feeling is not settled, and therefore I ordered detailed deliberation; I did not wish merely to seek alteration of antiquity in order to show difference. You and the others consider that 'for kin of the external clan, ritual has no suppressing reduction, and the reciprocal mourning system is drawn from very distant cases.' But maternal aunts and uncles belong to the closest of derivative kin. Speaking by kinship, they also match paternal aunts and uncles. How could the examples cited be distant, while the mourning for close kin is reduced? Also, a wife follows her husband. Since the husband has mourning for his maternal aunts and uncles, she wears mourning by following her husband, and in this way kinship is harmonized. I truly wish to make the unworthy reach upward and the worthy bend downward. You and the others should examine this thoroughly." Yaoqing and the others memorialized: "Your Majesty embodies utmost benevolence and extends the Way of grace broadly, intending to enlarge drawing-in and show harmony among kin; you have again issued virtuous words and again ordered detailed deliberation.
entries.literal: Xuanzong again composed a personal reply: "There are six kinds of derivative mourning, and this is one of them. As for the rules of lowering and reducing, the ritual has no clear text. These all proceed from oneself in leading kin and are used to make mourning dress. What is preserved and restrained is entirely a pushing outward of grace. My feeling is not settled, and therefore I ordered detailed deliberation; I did not wish merely to seek alteration of antiquity in order to show difference. You and the others consider that 'for kin of the external clan, ritual has no suppressing reduction, and the reciprocal mourning system is drawn from very distant cases.' But maternal aunts and uncles belong to the closest of derivative kin. Speaking by kinship, they also match paternal aunts and uncles. How could the examples cited be distant, while the mourning for close kin is reduced? Also, a wife follows her husband. Since the husband has mourning for his maternal aunts and uncles, she wears mourning by following her husband, and in this way kinship is harmonized. I truly wish to make the unworthy reach upward and the worthy bend downward. You and the others should examine this thoroughly." Yaoqing and the others memorialized: "Your Majesty embodies utmost benevolence and extends the Way of grace broadly, intending to enlarge drawing-in and show harmony among kin; you have again issued virtuous words and again ordered detailed deliberation.

entries.zh: 臣等按《大唐新禮》：親舅加至小功，與從母同服。
entries.en: We have reviewed the New Tang Rites: a mother's brother was raised to xiao gong, matching the mother's sister.
entries.literal: Your servants examine the New Tang Rites: the mother's brother increased to xiao gong, the same mourning as the mother's sister.

entries.zh: 此蓋當時特命，不以輕重遞增，蓋不欲參於本宗，慎於變禮者也。
entries.en: That was a special order of the time, not a ladder of ever-heavier grades—chiefly to keep external kin from merging with the main line, a cautious change of ritual.
entries.literal: This was at that time a special command, not increasing grade by grade, broadly not wishing to mix with the root lineage—caution in altering ritual.

entries.zh: 今聖制親姨舅小功，更制舅母緦麻，堂姨舅袒免等服，取類《新禮》，垂示將來，通於物情，自我作則。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty sets mother's brothers and sisters at xiao gong, an aunt by marriage at si hemp, and cousins on the mother's side at tan mian—following the New Rites as a type, showing the future a rule that fits human feeling and is made here and now.
entries.literal: Now the sage regulation makes mother's brothers and sisters xiao gong, further regulating the mother's brother's wife as si hemp, hall mother's brothers and sisters as tan mian, and the like—taking categories from the New Rites, displaying them for the future, penetrating common feeling, making the rule oneself.

entries.zh: 群儒風議，徒有稽留。
entries.en: The Confucian debaters had only delayed.
entries.literal: The multitude of Confucians in discussion merely had delay.

entries.zh: 並望准制施行。」
entries.en: We all hope the regulation will be approved and put into practice."
entries.literal: We all hope the regulation will be approved and put into practice."

entries.zh: 制從之。
entries.en: The regulation was approved.
entries.literal: The regulation was approved.

entries.zh: 天寶六載正月，出嫁母宜終服三年。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Tianbao, first month: a married-out mother should observe the full three-year mourning.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, in the first month, a mother who has married out her son should complete the three-year mourning.

entries.zh: 上元元年，天后上表曰：「至如父在為母服止一期，雖心喪三年，服由尊降。
entries.en: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu submitted a memorial, saying: "As for when the father is alive, mourning for the mother stops at one cycle—though heart mourning is three years, the garment is reduced by reverence for the father.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu submitted a memorial, saying: "As for when the father is alive, mourning for the mother stops at one cycle—though heart mourning is three years, the garment is reduced by reverence for the father.

entries.zh: 竊謂子之於母，慈愛特深，非母不生，非母不育。
entries.en: A child owes the mother a singular depth of love: without her there is no birth, without her no rearing.
entries.literal: I venture to say that in a child's relation to the mother, affection is especially deep—without the mother one is not born, without the mother one is not reared.

entries.zh: 推燥居濕，咽苦吐甘，生養勞瘁，恩斯極矣！
entries.en: She tended his dryness and wetness, swallowed bitterness and gave sweetness—the labor of nurture exhausts what kindness can mean.
entries.literal: Tending dryness and wetness, swallowing bitterness and spitting sweetness—the toil of bearing and rearing, kindness reaches its utmost!

entries.zh: 所以禽獸之情，猶知其母，三年在懷，理宜崇報。
entries.en: Even beasts know their dam; three years in the womb demand a commensurate return.
entries.literal: Therefore even beasts in feeling know their mother; three years in the womb—by principle one ought to honor her in return.

entries.zh: 若父在為母服止一期，尊父之敬雖周，報母之慈有闕。
entries.en: Stopping at one cycle while the father lived honored him fully but left the mother's kindness short.
entries.literal: If when the father is alive mourning for the mother stops at one cycle, reverence for the father is complete yet requital of the mother's kindness is lacking.

entries.zh: 且齊斬之制，足為差減，更令周以一期，恐傷人子之志。
entries.en: Hemmed sackcloth already graded the mourning; shrinking three years to one cycle would wound a son's intent.
entries.literal: Moreover the hemmed-and-cut garment system is sufficient for graduated reduction; to make one cycle suffice where three years should apply would wound the son's intent.

entries.zh: 今請父在為母終三年之服。」
entries.en: We now request that when the father is alive mourning for the mother run the full three years."
entries.literal: We now request that when the father is alive mourning for the mother run the full three years."

entries.zh: 高宗下詔，依議行焉，
entries.en: Gaozong decreed and put her proposal into practice.
entries.literal: Gaozong issued a decree and followed the proposal in practice,

entries.zh: 開元五年，右補闕盧履冰上言：「准禮，父在為母一週除靈，三年心喪。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, Right Remonstrator Lu Lübing submitted a memorial: "According to ritual, when the father is alive, for the mother one cycle until removal of the spirit tablet, three years' heart mourning.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, Right Remonstrator Lu Lübing submitted a memorial: "According to ritual, when the father is alive, for the mother one cycle until removal of the spirit tablet, three years' heart mourning.

entries.zh: 則天皇后請同父沒之服，三年然始除靈。
entries.en: Empress Wu had asked for the same garment as when the father was dead—three years before tablet removal.
entries.literal: Empress Wu Zetian requested mourning the same as when the father is dead—three years before removal of the spirit tablet.

entries.zh: 雖則權行，有紊彝典。
entries.en: That expedient had been carried out, but it tangled the standing canon.
entries.literal: Though it was provisionally carried out, it disorderly violated the constant canon.

entries.zh: 今陛下孝理天下，動合禮經，請仍舊章，庶葉通典。」
entries.en: Now Your Majesty filially governs the realm and moves in accord with ritual classics; we request return to the old articles, that it may accord with the comprehensive canon."
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty filially governs the realm and moves in accord with ritual classics; we request return to the old articles, that it may accord with the comprehensive canon."

entries.zh: 於是下制令百官詳議；
entries.en: A decree ordered the bureaucracy to deliberate.
entries.literal: Thereupon a decree was issued ordering the hundred officials to deliberate in detail;

entries.zh: 並舅及嫂叔服不依舊禮，亦合議定。
entries.en: Mourning for uncles, aunts, sisters-in-law, and younger uncles that no longer matched the old ritual was to be settled in the same review.
entries.literal: mourning for mother's brothers and sisters-in-law and younger uncles not following the old ritual should also be settled by deliberation.

entries.zh: 刑部郎中田再思建議曰：干尊坤卑，天一地二，陰陽之位分矣，夫婦之道配焉。至若死喪之威，隆殺之等，禮經五服之制，齊斬有殊，考妣三年之喪，貴賤無隔，以報免懷之慈，以酬罔極之恩者也。稽之上古，喪期無數，暨乎中葉，方有歲年。《禮》云：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異代，不相襲禮。」《白虎通》云：「質文再變，正朔三而復。」自周公制禮之後，孔父刊經已來，爰殊厭降之儀，以標服紀之節。重輕從俗，斟酌隨時。故知禮不從天而降，不由地而出也，在人消息，為適時之中耳。春秋諸國，魯最知禮，以周公之後，孔子之邦也。晉韓起來聘，言「周禮盡在魯矣。」齊仲孫來盟，言「魯猶秉周禮。」尚有子張問高宗諒陰三年，子思不聽其子服出母，子游謂同母異父昆弟之服大功，子夏謂合從齊衰之制。此等並四科之數，十哲之人，高步孔門，親承聖訓，及遇喪事，猶此致疑，即明自古已來，升降不一者也。三年之制，說者紛然。鄭玄以為二十七月，王肅以為二十五月。又改葬之服，鄭云服緦三月，王云訖葬而除。又繼母出嫁，鄭云皆服，王云從於繼育，乃為之服。又無服之殤，鄭云子生一月，哭之一日；王云以哭之一日易服之月。鄭、王祖經宗傳，各有異同；荀摯采古求遺，互為損益。方知去聖漸遠，殘缺彌多。故曰會禮之家，名為聚訟，寧有定哉！而父在為母三年，行之已逾四紀，出自高宗大帝之代，不從則天皇后之朝。大帝御極之辰，中宮獻書之日，往時參議，將可施行，編之於格，服之已久。前王所是，疏而為律；後王所是，著而為令。何必乖先帝之旨，阻人子之情，虧純孝之心，背德義之本？有何妨於聖化，有何紊於彝倫，而欲服之週年，與伯叔母齊焉，與姑姊妹同焉？夫三年之喪，如白駒之過隙，君子喪親，有終身之憂，何況再周乎！夫禮者，體也，履也，示之以跡。孝者，畜也，養也，因之以心。小人不恥不仁，不畏不義。服之有制，使愚人企及；衣之以衰，使見之摧痛。以此防人，人猶有朝死而夕忘者；以此制人，人猶有釋服而從吉者。方今漸歸古樸，須敦孝義，抑賢引愚，理資寧戚，食稻衣錦，所不忍聞。若以庶事朝儀，一依周禮，則古之人臣見君也，公卿大夫贄羔雁、珪璧，今何故不依乎？周之用刑也，墨、劓、宮、刖，今何故不行乎？周則侯、甸、男、衛，朝聘有數，今何故不行乎？周則不五十不仕，七十不入朝，今何故不依乎？周則井、邑、丘、甸，以立徵稅，今何故不行乎？周則三老五等，父死子及，今何故不行乎？周則冠冕衣裘，乘車而戰，今何故不行乎？周則分土五更，膠序養老，今何故不行乎？諸如此例，不可勝述。何獨孝思之事，愛一年之服於其母乎？可為痛心，可為慟哭者！《詩》云：「哀哀父母，生我劬勞。」《禮》云：「父之親子也，親賢而下無能；母之親子也，賢則親之，無能則憐之。」阮嗣宗晉代之英才，方外之高士，以為母重於父。據齊斬升數，粗細已降，何忍服之節制，減至於周？豈後代之士，盡慚於古。循古未必是，依今未必非也。又同爨服緦，禮經明義。嫂叔遠別，同諸路人。引而進之，觸類而長。猶子咸衣苴枲，季父不服緦麻，推遠之情有餘，睦親之義未足。又母之昆弟，情切渭陽，翟酺訟舅之冤，甯氏宅甥之相，我之出也，義亦殷焉。不同從母之尊，遂降小功之服，依諸古禮，有爽俗情。今貶舅而宗姨，是陋今而榮古。此並太宗之制也，行之百年矣，輒為刊復，實用有疑。
entries.en: Tian Zaisi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice, made a proposal: Qian is honored and kun is lowly; Heaven is one and earth is two. The positions of yin and yang are divided, and the way of husband and wife is paired with them. As for the awe of death and mourning and the grades of fullness and reduction, the ritual classics have the system of the five mourning grades. Trimmed and unhemmed mourning differ, but the three-year mourning for father and mother has no barrier between noble and base, because it repays the kindness of bearing and cherishing and answers boundless grace. Examining high antiquity, mourning terms had no fixed number; by middle antiquity, only then were there years and months. The Ritual says: "The Five Emperors differed in time and did not follow one another in music; the Three Kings differed in age and did not inherit one another's rites." The Baihu Tong says: "Plainness and refinement change twice, and the first month changes through three and returns." Since the Duke of Zhou made ritual and since Confucius edited the classics, there have been different rules of suppression and reduction to mark the divisions of mourning regulations. Heavy and light follow custom; deliberation and adjustment follow the time. Thus we know ritual does not descend from Heaven or come out from earth; it lies in human increase and decrease, making what fits the time and the mean. Among the states of the Spring and Autumn, Lu best knew ritual, because it was the descendants of the Duke of Zhou and the state of Confucius. When Han Qi of Jin came on a visit, he said, "The rites of Zhou are all in Lu." When Zhongsun of Qi came to make a covenant, he said, "Lu still holds the rites of Zhou." Yet Zizhang asked about Gaozong's three years of silent mourning; Zisi did not allow his son to wear mourning for his divorced mother; Ziyou said that brothers with the same mother but different fathers should wear great-work mourning; Zixia said they should follow the trimmed-mourning rule. These were all among the numbered disciples of the four categories and the ten philosophers, men of high rank in Confucius's gate who personally received the sage teaching; yet when they encountered mourning matters, they still produced doubts like this. This makes clear that since antiquity increases and reductions have not been uniform. As for the three-year system, explanations are confused. Zheng Xuan considered it twenty-seven months; Wang Su considered it twenty-five months. Again for mourning after reburial, Zheng says one wears fine hemp for three months, while Wang says one removes it when burial is completed. Again for a stepmother who remarries, Zheng says all wear mourning, while Wang says that only if one followed and was raised by her does one wear mourning. Again for a child who died young and for whom there is no mourning, Zheng says that for a child born one month, one cries one day; Wang says one day of crying replaces one month of mourning. Zheng and Wang each take the classics as ancestor and the commentaries as lineage, and each has differences. Xun Zhi collected antiquity and sought what was left, alternately reducing and increasing. From this we know that as the sages recede farther away, gaps and losses become more numerous. Therefore it is said that houses that assemble ritual are called gathered lawsuits; how could there be a fixed answer? Yet the three-year mourning for a mother while the father is alive has been practiced for more than forty years. It came from the generation of Gaozong the Great Emperor, not from the court of Empress Zetian. When the Great Emperor ruled and the palace submitted the document, the former deliberations could be put into practice; it was compiled into the regulations, and the mourning has been worn for a long time. What a former king approved was set out as law; what a later king approved was written as ordinance. Why must we oppose the former emperor's intent, block the feeling of a person's son, diminish a pure filial heart, and turn against the root of virtue and obligation? What harm is there to sage transformation? What disorder is there to the constant human order, that one would make the mourning one year, equal to that for paternal uncles' wives, and the same as for paternal aunts and sisters? The three-year mourning passes like a white colt through a crack; a gentleman mourning his parent has lifelong grief, how much more for two full cycles! Ritual is embodiment, practice, showing it by traces. Filial piety is storing up, nourishing, following it by the heart. Petty people are not ashamed of inhumanity and do not fear unrighteousness. Mourning dress has regulations to make foolish people reach upward; they are clothed in mourning garments so that seeing them produces crushing pain. Using this to guard people, there are still those who forget by evening one who died in the morning. Using this to regulate people, there are still those who remove mourning and follow auspicious affairs. Now we are gradually returning to ancient simplicity and must deepen filial piety and obligation. Restraining the worthy and drawing in the foolish, in principle, depends on Ning Qi; eating rice and wearing brocade are things one cannot bear to hear. If ordinary affairs and court ceremony are all to follow the Zhou rites, then when ancient ministers saw the ruler, dukes, ministers, and great officers presented lambs, geese, jade tablets, and disks; why do we not follow this now? Zhou punishments used tattooing, nose-cutting, castration, and foot-cutting; why do we not carry them out now? Zhou had hou, dian, nan, and wei domains, and audiences and visits had fixed numbers; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou did not let one serve before fifty, and at seventy one did not enter court; why do we not follow this now? Zhou used jing, yi, qiu, and dian to establish taxation; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou had three elders and five grades, father dying and son succeeding; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou used caps, robes, fur garments, and chariots in battle; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou divided land and had five geng, and in village and school nourished the aged; why do we not carry this out now? Examples such as these cannot be fully stated. Why only in the matter of filial thought begrudge one year of mourning for one's mother? This can make the heart ache; this can make one wail. The Odes says: "Alas, alas, my father and mother, who bore me with toil." The Ritual says: "When a father loves his child, he loves the worthy and lowers the incapable; when a mother loves her child, if worthy she loves him, and if incapable she pities him." Ruan Sizong, an outstanding talent of Jin and lofty man beyond the world, considered the mother weightier than the father. Based on the thread counts of trimmed and unhemmed mourning, coarseness and fineness already descend. How can one bear for the term of mourning to be reduced to one year? Surely later men are not all ashamed before antiquity. Following antiquity is not necessarily right; following the present is not necessarily wrong. Again, those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp; this is a clear meaning of the ritual classics. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law are kept distant and treated like people on the road. Drawing them in and advancing them extends by analogy. Nephews all wear hemp mourning, but a younger uncle does not wear fine hemp; the feeling of pushing away is more than enough, and the obligation of harmonizing kin is insufficient. Again the mother's brothers have feeling as close as Weiyang; Di Pu litigated his uncle's injustice, and the Ning family housed a nephew as minister. Since I come from them, obligation too is deep. Not sharing the honor of a mother's sister, they are thereby lowered to small-work mourning. According to the ancient rites, this conflicts with common feeling. Now lowering the maternal uncle while honoring the maternal aunt is to scorn the present and glorify antiquity. These are all Taizong's regulations and have been practiced for a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring them truly creates doubt.

entries.zh: 至七年八月，下敕曰：「惟周公制禮，當歷代不刊；況子夏為《傳》，乃孔門所受。格條之內，有父在為母齊衰三年，此有為而為，非尊厭之義。與其改作，不如師古，諸服紀宜一依《喪服》文。」自是卿士之家，父在為母行服不同：或既周而禫，禫服六十日釋服，心喪三年者；
entries.en: By the eighth month of the seventh year, an edict was issued: "Only the rites made by the Duke of Zhou should remain unaltered through successive ages; how much more since Zixia made the commentary, receiving it from Confucius's school. Within the regulations there is three-year trimmed mourning for a mother while the father is alive; this is something done for a particular purpose, not the meaning of honored suppression. Rather than changing and remaking it, it is better to take antiquity as teacher. The various mourning regulations should all follow the text of the Mourning Dress." From this time, in the households of ministers and grandees, mourning for a mother while the father was alive was carried out differently: some, after one cycle and the end-of-mourning rite, wore end-of-mourning garments for sixty days and then removed mourning, while observing inner mourning for three years;
