entries.zh: 或有既周而禫服終三年者；
entries.en: some kept end-of-mourning dress the full three years after one cycle;
entries.literal: some, having completed one cycle, wore end-of-mourning garments for the full three years;

entries.zh: 或有依上元之制，齊衰三年者。
entries.en: some followed Shangyuan's hemmed sackcloth for three years.
entries.literal: some followed the Shangyuan system of hemmed sackcloth three years.

entries.zh: 時議者是非紛然，元行沖謂人曰：「聖人制厭降之禮，豈不知母恩之深也，以尊祖貴祢，欲其遠別禽獸，近異夷狄故也。
entries.en: Debaters of the time right and wrong were clamorous; Yuan Xingchong said to people: "The sage instituted the ritual of honored reduction—how could he not know the depth of a mother's kindness? It is because one honors the grandfather and values the temple founder, wishing people to keep far from beasts and near yet distinct from barbarians.
entries.literal: Debaters of the time right and wrong were clamorous; Yuan Xingchong said to people: "The sage instituted the ritual of honored reduction—how could he not know the depth of a mother's kindness? It is because one honors the grandfather and values the temple founder, wishing people to keep far from beasts and near yet distinct from barbarians.

entries.zh: 人情易搖，淺識者眾。
entries.en: Feeling sways easily; shallow views are common.
entries.literal: Human feeling is easy to sway; those of shallow understanding are many.

entries.zh: 一紊其度，其可止乎！」
entries.en: Once the measure is disorderly, how can it be stopped!"
entries.literal: Once the measure is disorderly, how can it be stopped!"

entries.zh: 二十年，中書令蕭嵩與學士改修定五禮，又議請依上元敕，父在為母齊衰三年為定。
entries.en: Year twenty: Secretariat Director Xiao Song and the academicians revised the Five Rites and again asked to fix Shangyuan's rule—hemmed sackcloth three years for a mother while the father lived.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, Secretariat Director Xiao Song and academicians again revised and fixed the Five Rites, and again deliberated requesting that according to the Shangyuan decree, when the father is alive hemmed sackcloth three years for the mother be made fixed.

entries.zh: 及頒禮，乃一依行焉。
entries.en: When the rites were issued, everyone followed them.
entries.literal: When the rites were promulgated, all followed it in practice.

entries.zh: 於是太子賓客崔沔建議曰：「竊聞大道既隱，天下為家。
entries.en: Then Mentor of the Heir Apparent Cui Mian memorialized: "I have heard that once the Great Way was hidden, the realm became a single household.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Mentor of the Heir Apparent Cui Mian submitted a recommendation, saying: "Your servant has heard that when the Great Way was concealed, all under Heaven became one's household.

entries.zh: 聖人因之，然後製禮。
entries.en: The sages took that as their basis and then fashioned ritual.
entries.literal: The sages followed this and thereafter fashioned rites.

entries.zh: 禮教之設，本為正家，家道正而天下定矣。
entries.en: Ritual teaching was instituted chiefly to set the household in order; when the household is right, the realm is stable.
entries.literal: The establishment of ritual teaching was fundamentally to rectify the family; when the family way is rectified, all under Heaven is settled.

entries.zh: 正家之道，不可以貳，總一定議，理歸本宗。
entries.en: The way to order a household cannot be divided in two: one settled rule, with principle anchored in the main line.
entries.literal: The way to rectify the family cannot be twofold; to gather and fix one deliberation, reason returns to the root lineage.

entries.zh: 父以尊崇，母以厭降，豈忘愛敬，宜存倫序。
entries.en: The father is exalted and the mother reduced in rank—not to forget love and respect, but to keep relational order.
entries.literal: The father is honored and elevated; the mother is suppressed and demoted—how could one forget love and respect? One should preserve the order of human relations.

entries.zh: 是以內有齊斬，外服皆緦麻，尊名所加，不過一等，此先王不易之道也。
entries.en: Hence within the family are the heaviest grades of mourning; for outside kin all wear the lightest hemp; added honor never exceeds one step—this is the former kings' unchanging rule.
entries.literal: Therefore within there is zhan and cui; for external relations all wear si hemp; where honored names are added, it does not exceed one grade—this is the unchanging way of the former kings.

entries.zh: 前聖所志，後賢所傳，其來久矣。
entries.en: What the ancient sages set down and later worthies handed on has stood for ages.
entries.literal: What former sages recorded, later worthies transmitted—their coming has long been so.

entries.zh: 昔辛有適伊川，見被髮而祭於野者，曰：『不及百年，此其戎乎？
entries.en: Long ago Xin You went to Yichuan and saw people with loose hair sacrificing in the open country, and said, 'In less than a hundred years, will this be the Rong?'
entries.literal: Long ago Xin You went to Yichuan and saw people with loose hair sacrificing in the open country, and said, 'In less than a hundred years, will this be the Rong?'

entries.zh: 其禮先亡矣！』
entries.en: Their ritual will die first!
entries.literal: Their rites will perish first!

entries.zh: 貞觀修禮，時改舊章，漸廣渭陽之恩，不遵洙、泗之典。
entries.en: When Zhenguan revised ritual, old statutes were altered, maternal kin were favored ever more widely, and the standards of Confucius's homeland were left aside.
entries.literal: In Zhenguan's revision of rites the times altered the old statutes, gradually widening the affection of the Wei-yang ode and not following the canons of Zhu and Si.

entries.zh: 及弘道之後，唐隆之間，國命再移於外族矣。
entries.en: After Hongdao and in the Tanglong years, the dynastic mandate twice passed to outsiders.
entries.literal: Reaching after Hongdao and in the Tanglong era, the nation's mandate twice shifted to alien clans.

entries.zh: 禮亡徵兆，儻或斯見，天人之際，可不誡哉！
entries.en: The death of ritual had its omens—perhaps we see them here; at the meeting of Heaven and humanity, ought we not take warning!
entries.literal: The perishing of rites had its omens—perhaps this is seen; at the juncture of Heaven and man, can one not be warned!

entries.zh: 開元初，補闕盧履冰嘗進狀論喪服輕重，敕令僉議。
entries.en: Early in Kaiyuan, Remonstrance Councillor Lu Lübing had memorialized on the grades of mourning dress, and an edict ordered joint deliberation.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Remonstrance Councillor Lu Lübing once submitted a memorial discussing the light and heavy grades of mourning garments; an edict ordered collective deliberation.

entries.zh: 於時群議紛拏，各安積習，太常禮部，奏依舊定。
entries.en: Debate then was tangled, each side clinging to habit; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites urged keeping the old rules.
entries.literal: At that time the multitude of discussions were tangled; each clung to accumulated custom; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites memorialized to follow the old fixings.

entries.zh: 陛下運稽古之思，發獨斷之明，至開元八年，特降別敕，一依古禮。
entries.en: Your Majesty, drawing on antiquity and acting with decisive clarity, in Kaiyuan 8 issued a special edict restoring the ancient mourning rules in full.
entries.literal: Your Majesty, exercising reflection on antiquity and issuing independent, clarifying judgments, by the eighth year of Kaiyuan specially promulgated a separate edict, wholly following the ancient rites.

entries.zh: 事符故實，人知向方，式固宗盟，社稷之福。
entries.en: That matched ancient precedent, gave the people a clear standard, and strengthened the clan bond—a blessing to the state.
entries.literal: The matter accords with former facts; people know the direction; it firmly secures the clan bond—the fortune of the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 更圖異議，竊所未詳。
entries.en: To reopen dispute on this point is, in my view, hard to understand.
entries.literal: To plot further divergent discussion—your servant has not yet understood.

entries.zh: 願守八年明旨，以為萬代成法。」
entries.en: We hope to preserve the clear directive of the eighth year as the enduring law for ten thousand generations."
entries.literal: We hope to preserve the clear directive of the eighth year as the enduring law for ten thousand generations."

entries.zh: 二十三年，藉田禮畢，正制曰：「服制之紀，或有所未通，宜令禮官學士詳議聞奏。」太常卿韋縚奏曰：「謹按《儀禮喪服》：舅，緦麻三月。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year, after the plowing rite was completed, a formal ordinance said: "In the regulations of mourning dress, some points may not yet be fully understood. Let ritual officials and scholars deliberate in detail and report." Wei Tao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized: "Respectfully according to the Ceremonies and Rites, Mourning Dress: for a maternal uncle, fine hemp for three months.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year, after the plowing rite was completed, a formal ordinance said: "In the regulations of mourning dress, some points may not yet be fully understood. Let ritual officials and scholars deliberate in detail and report." Wei Tao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized: "Respectfully according to the Ceremonies and Rites, Mourning Dress: for a maternal uncle, fine hemp for three months.

entries.zh: 從母，小功五月。
entries.en: A mother's sister, five months' lesser accomplishment.
entries.literal: Mother's sister, five months' lesser accomplishment.

entries.zh: 《傳》曰：可以小功，以名加也。
entries.en: The Commentary: lesser accomplishment may apply—the name adds the grade.
entries.literal: The Commentary says: one may use lesser accomplishment—added by the name.

entries.zh: 堂姨舅、舅母，恩所不及。
entries.en: Hall cousins on the mother's side and uncles' wives—kindness does not reach them.
entries.literal: Hall mother's brothers and sisters, mother's brothers' wives—kindness does not reach.

entries.zh: 外祖父母。
entries.en: Maternal grandparents—
entries.literal: Maternal grandparents.

entries.zh: 小功五月。
entries.en: five months of lesser accomplishment mourning.
entries.literal: five months' lesser accomplishment.

entries.zh: 《傳》曰：何以小功，以尊加也。
entries.en: The Commentary asks why lesser accomplishment: honor raises the grade.
entries.literal: The Commentary says: why lesser accomplishment? Added by the honored status.

entries.zh: 舅，緦麻三月，並是情親而服屬疏者也。
entries.en: A mother's brother, three months' finest hemp—all close in feeling, distant in kin grade.
entries.literal: Mother's brother, three months' finest hemp—all are close in feeling yet distant in garment kinship.

entries.zh: 外祖正尊，同於從母之服。
entries.en: Maternal grandparents are primary elders, the same grade as a mother's sister.
entries.literal: Maternal grandparents are primary elders, the same as mourning for the mother's sister.

entries.zh: 姨舅一等，服則輕重有殊。
entries.en: Mother's sister and mother's brother are one class, yet the garments differ in weight.
entries.literal: Mother's sister and mother's brother are one class, yet garments differ in light and heavy.

entries.zh: 堂姨舅親即未疏，恩絕不相為服。
entries.en: Hall cousins are not yet distant kin, yet kindness is cut and they wear no mourning for each other.
entries.literal: Hall mother's brothers and sisters—the kin is not yet distant, yet kindness is severed and they do not wear mourning for one another.

entries.zh: 親舅母來承外族，同爨之禮不加。
entries.en: An uncle's wife who joins the outer clan does not receive the shared-hearth rite.
entries.literal: A mother's brother's wife who comes to join the outer clan—the ritual of sharing the hearth is not added.

entries.zh: 竊以古意猶有所未暢者也。
entries.en: Ancient intent, he ventured, was not yet fully expressed.
entries.literal: I venture that in ancient intent something is still not fully expressed.

entries.zh: 且為外祖小功，此則正尊情甚親而服屬疏者也，請加至大功九月。
entries.en: Maternal grandparents wore lesser accomplishment though feeling was very close and kin grade distant—he asked to raise them to nine months' greater accomplishment.
entries.literal: Moreover for maternal grandparents lesser accomplishment—this is primary elder, feeling very close yet garment kinship distant—we request increase to greater accomplishment nine months.

entries.zh: 姨舅儕類，親既無別，服宜齊等，請為舅加至小功五月。
entries.en: Mother's sister and mother's brother were the same class without kin distinction—the garment should match; he asked five months' lesser accomplishment for a mother's brother.
entries.literal: Mother's sister and mother's brother are the same class; the kin is without distinction—the garment ought to be equal; we request for the mother's brother increase to five months' lesser accomplishment.

entries.zh: 堂姨舅疏降一等，親舅母從服之例，先無制服之文，並望加至袒免。
entries.en: Hall cousins dropped one grade; an uncle's wife had no prior garment rule—he asked baring shoulder and untying the cap-band for them all.
entries.literal: Hall mother's brothers and sisters reduced one grade; a mother's brother's wife following-garment precedent—formerly no garment text existed—we together hope to add to baring shoulder and untying cap-band.

entries.zh: 臣聞禮以飾情，服從義制，或有沿革，損益可明。
entries.en: I have heard that ritual adorns emotion and mourning dress follows moral rule—where practice has shifted, what to add or trim can be stated plainly.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that rites adorn feeling and mourning garments follow righteous regulation; there may be continuations and changes, and what is to be reduced or increased can be made clear.

entries.zh: 事體既大，理資詳審。
entries.en: The matter is weighty and calls for careful deliberation.
entries.literal: The matter in its substance is already great; reason requires thorough deliberation.

entries.zh: 望付尚書省集眾官吏詳議，務從折衷，永為典則。」
entries.en: We hope it may be entrusted to the Department of State Affairs to assemble the multitude of officials for detailed discussion, striving for compromise, and made a perpetual standard."
entries.literal: We hope it may be entrusted to the Department of State Affairs to assemble the multitude of officials for detailed discussion, striving for compromise, and made a perpetual standard."

entries.zh: 禮部員外郎楊仲昌議曰：「謹按《儀禮》曰：『外服皆緦。』
entries.en: Yang Zhongchang, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, deliberated: "Respectfully according to the Ceremonies and Rites: "All mourning for external kin is fine hemp."
entries.literal: Yang Zhongchang, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, deliberated: "Respectfully according to the Ceremonies and Rites: "All mourning for external kin is fine hemp."

entries.zh: 又曰：『外祖父母以尊加，從母以名加，並為小功五月。』
entries.en: It also says: "Maternal grandparents, with honor added, and mothers' sisters, with the name added, both have small-work mourning for five months."
entries.literal: It also says: "Maternal grandparents, with honor added, and mothers' sisters, with the name added, both have small-work mourning for five months."

entries.zh: 其為舅緦，鄭文貞公魏徵已議同從母例，加至小功五月訖。
entries.en: For the maternal uncle, si hemp—Wei Zheng, Duke of Zhengwen, had already argued he should match the mother's sister at xiao gong for five months, and that was settled.
entries.literal: For the mother's brother, si hemp—Duke of Zheng Wen, Wei Zheng, already deliberated to follow the mother's-sister precedent, increasing to xiao gong for five months, and that is settled.

entries.zh: 今之所加，豈異前旨？
entries.en: What is now proposed to be added—how does it differ from that earlier ruling?
entries.literal: What is now to be added—how does it differ from the former intent?

entries.zh: 雖文貞賢也，而周、孔聖也，以賢改聖，後學何從？
entries.en: Wei Zheng was worthy, but Zhou and Confucius were sages; to let worthies revise sages—what should later students follow?
entries.literal: Though Wen was worthy, yet Zhou and Confucius were sages; to use the worthy to alter the sage—what are later students to follow?

entries.zh: 堂舅姨、堂舅母，並升為袒免，則何以祖述禮經乎？
entries.en: Cousins on the mother's side and their wives, all raised to tan mian—how then can we claim to follow the ritual canon?
entries.literal: Hall mother's brothers and sisters and hall mother's brothers' wives, all raised to tan mian—then how may one trace and transmit the ritual classics?

entries.zh: 如以外祖父母加至大功，則豈無加報於外孫乎？
entries.en: If maternal grandparents are raised to da gong, must not maternal grandsons also return the heavier mourning?
entries.literal: If for maternal grandparents one increases to da gong, then would there not also be added return mourning for maternal grandsons?

entries.zh: 如外孫為報，服大功，則本宗庶孫，何同等而相淺乎？
entries.en: If maternal grandsons wore da gong in return, how could patrilineal grandsons of the same degree wear less?
entries.literal: If maternal grandsons in return wore da gong, then the common grandsons of the root lineage—why are they equal in rank yet shallower in mourning?

entries.zh: 儻必如是，深所不便。
entries.en: If it must be so, the inconvenience is grave.
entries.literal: If it must be so, this is deeply inconvenient.

entries.zh: 竊恐內外乖序，親疏奪倫、情之所沿，何所不至，理必然也。
entries.en: I fear inner and outer kin will fall out of order and near and far will invert rank—where feeling leads, what limit will hold? That is inevitable.
entries.literal: Your servant fears inner and outer will lose their order, near and distant will usurp rank, and where feeling leads—what will not follow? Reason demands it.

entries.zh: 昔子路有姊之喪而不除，孔子問之，子路對曰：『吾寡兄弟而不忍也。』
entries.en: Long ago Zilu mourned a sister but would not leave off the garments; Confucius asked him, and Zilu said, 'I have few siblings and cannot bear to do so.'
entries.literal: In antiquity Zilu had mourning for a sister yet did not remove the garments; Confucius questioned him, and Zilu replied: 'I have few brothers and sisters and cannot bear it.'

entries.zh: 子曰：『先王制禮，行道之人皆不忍也。』
entries.en: The Master said, 'When the former kings made ritual, even passers-by felt the same reluctance.'
entries.literal: The Master said, 'When the former kings made ritual, even passers-by felt the same reluctance.'

entries.zh: 子路聞而除之。
entries.en: Zilu heard and removed the mourning.
entries.literal: Zilu heard this and removed the garments.

entries.zh: 此則聖人因言以立訓，援事抑情之明例也。
entries.en: Here the sage turned a remark into teaching—an explicit case of using precedent to curb excess of feeling.
entries.literal: This is the sage using words to establish instruction—an illuminating example of citing a case to restrain feeling.

entries.zh: 禮不云乎，無輕議禮。
entries.en: Does ritual not say, Do not lightly debate ritual?
entries.literal: Does ritual not say: do not lightly discuss ritual?

entries.zh: 明共蟠於天地，並彼日月，賢者由之，安敢小有損益也！
entries.en: It coils with Heaven and Earth and stands with sun and moon—the worthy follow it; who would dare trim it even slightly!
entries.literal: Brightness coiled with Heaven and Earth, equal to sun and moon—the worthy follow it; how dare one make small additions or subtractions!

entries.zh: 況夫《喪服》之紀，先王大猷，奉以周旋，以匡人道。
entries.en: Above all the Mourning Garments—the former kings' great design, carried in practice to set the human way right.
entries.literal: How much more the records of Mourning Garments—the great design of the former kings, upheld in practice to rectify the human way.

entries.zh: 一辭寧措，千載是遵，涉於異端，豈曰弘教。
entries.en: A single phrase is not lightly altered; a thousand years follow it; to wander into side paths is not to enlarge teaching.
entries.literal: One word is better left unchanged; for a thousand years it is followed; to touch heterodox paths—how may one call that broadening teaching?

entries.zh: 伏望各依正禮，以厚儒風。
entries.en: I beg that all adhere to the orthodox rites and strengthen Confucian practice.
entries.literal: We prostrate ourselves and hope each will follow the correct rites to thicken Confucian custom.

entries.zh: 太常所謂增加，愚見以為不可。」
entries.en: What the Court of Imperial Sacrifices calls increases, in my foolish view, cannot be accepted."
entries.literal: What the Court of Imperial Sacrifices calls increases, in my foolish view, cannot be accepted."

entries.zh: 又戶部郎中楊伯成、左監門錄事參軍劉秩並同是議，與沔等略同。
entries.en: Bureau Director Yang Bocheng in the Ministry of Revenue and Left Gate Recorder Liu Zhi also wrote in the same vein, broadly agreeing with Cui Mian and his allies.
entries.literal: Also Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue Yang Bocheng and Left Gate Recorder Liu Zhi all submitted the same opinion, broadly matching Mian and the others.

entries.zh: 議奏，上又手敕侍臣等曰：「朕以為親姨舅既服小功，則舅母於舅有三年之服，服是受我而厚，以服制情，則舅母之服，不得全降於舅也，宜服緦麻。堂姨舅古今未制服，朕思惇睦九族，引而親之，宜服袒免。又鄭玄注《禮記》云『同爨緦』，若比堂姨舅於同爨，親則厚矣。又《喪服傳》云『外親之服皆緦』，是亦不隔於堂姨舅也。若以所服不得過本，而須為外曾祖父母及外伯叔祖父母制服，亦何傷乎？是皆親親敦本之意，卿等更熟詳之。」
entries.en: When the deliberations were submitted, the emperor again personally instructed his attendants, saying: "I consider that since close maternal aunts and uncles already receive small-work mourning, and an uncle's wife has three-year mourning for the uncle, her mourning is thickened by receiving it from me. If mourning dress regulates feeling, then mourning for an uncle's wife cannot be wholly lowered from that for the uncle, and she should receive fine hemp. Second maternal aunts and uncles have never had mourning dress fixed in ancient or recent times, but I think of strengthening harmony among the nine kin, drawing them in and making them close, so they should receive bared-shoulder exemption. Also, Zheng Xuan's annotation to the Book of Rites says, "Those who share the cooking hearth receive fine hemp." If second maternal aunts and uncles are compared to those who share the hearth, this is thick in kinship. Again the Mourning Dress Tradition says, "Mourning for external kin is all fine hemp." This too does not exclude second maternal aunts and uncles. If one says that the mourning worn may not exceed the root, and therefore mourning dress must also be made for external great-grandparents and external great-uncles and great-aunts, what harm would that do? All this is the intention of loving kin and thickening the root. You should examine it further and carefully."
entries.literal: When the deliberations were submitted, the emperor again personally instructed his attendants, saying: "I consider that since close maternal aunts and uncles already receive small-work mourning, and an uncle's wife has three-year mourning for the uncle, her mourning is thickened by receiving it from me. If mourning dress regulates feeling, then mourning for an uncle's wife cannot be wholly lowered from that for the uncle, and she should receive fine hemp. Second maternal aunts and uncles have never had mourning dress fixed in ancient or recent times, but I think of strengthening harmony among the nine kin, drawing them in and making them close, so they should receive bared-shoulder exemption. Also, Zheng Xuan's annotation to the Book of Rites says, "Those who share the cooking hearth receive fine hemp." If second maternal aunts and uncles are compared to those who share the hearth, this is thick in kinship. Again the Mourning Dress Tradition says, "Mourning for external kin is all fine hemp." This too does not exclude second maternal aunts and uncles. If one says that the mourning worn may not exceed the root, and therefore mourning dress must also be made for external great-grandparents and external great-uncles and great-aunts, what harm would that do? All this is the intention of loving kin and thickening the root. You should examine it further and carefully."

entries.zh: 於是紛議不定。
entries.en: Debate deadlocked.
entries.literal: Thereupon debate was unsettled.

entries.zh: 履冰又上疏曰：「《禮》：父在，為母十一月而練，十三月而祥，十五月而禫，心喪三年。
entries.en: Lübing again submitted a memorial, saying: "The Ritual: when the father is alive, for the mother eleven months then practice; thirteenth month auspicious; fifteenth month end-of-mourning; heart mourning three years.
entries.literal: Lübing again submitted a memorial, saying: "The Ritual: when the father is alive, for the mother eleven months then practice; thirteenth month auspicious; fifteenth month end-of-mourning; heart mourning three years.

entries.zh: 上元中，則天皇后上表，請同父沒之服，亦未有行。
entries.en: In Shangyuan Wu had asked for mourning equal to a father's death, but it had not yet taken effect.
entries.literal: In the Shangyuan era Empress Wu Zetian submitted a memorial requesting mourning the same as when the father is dead, yet it was still not carried out.

entries.zh: 至垂拱年中，始編入格，易代之後，俗乃通行。
entries.en: Only in Chuigong was it written into the code; after the dynastic shift the custom spread.
entries.literal: By the Chuigong era it was first entered into the administrative code; after the change of dynasty the custom then spread in practice.

entries.zh: 臣開元五年，頻請仍舊。
entries.en: Your servant, in the fifth year of Kaiyuan, repeatedly asked to restore the old rule.
entries.literal: Your servant, in the fifth year of Kaiyuan, repeatedly asked to restore the old rule.

entries.zh: 恩敕並嫂叔舅姨之服，亦付所司詳議。
entries.en: The throne also sent mourning for sisters-in-law, younger uncles, and maternal kin to the relevant offices for review.
entries.literal: The gracious edict also entrusted mourning for sisters-in-law, younger uncles, and mother's brothers and sisters to the relevant offices for detailed deliberation.

entries.zh: 諸司所議，同異相參。
entries.en: The offices split.
entries.literal: The offices' deliberations mixed agreement and difference.

entries.zh: 所司惟執齊斬之文，又曰亦合典禮。
entries.en: One office clung to the hemmed-sackcloth articles and called that canonical.
entries.literal: The relevant office alone held to the text on hemmed and cut garments, and also said it accorded with canonical ritual.

entries.zh: 竊見新修之格，猶依垂拱之偽，致有祖父母安存，子孫之妻亡沒，下房筵幾，亦立再周，甚無謂也。
entries.en: The new code still followed Chuigong's error: with grandparents alive and a grandson's wife dead, lower apartments sometimes observed a second full cycle—absurd.
entries.literal: I observe that the newly revised code still follows the Chuigong error, so that when grandparents are alive and a grandson's wife dies, in the lower apartments a second full cycle is also observed—most meaningless.

entries.zh: 據《周易·家人》卦云：『利女貞女正位於內，男正位於外。
entries.en: The Changes, Family hexagram, says: constancy profits the woman; she holds correct position within, the man without.
entries.literal: According to the Changes, Family hexagram: 'It profits the woman's constancy; the woman holds correct position within, the man holds correct position without.

entries.zh: 男女正，天地之大義。
entries.en: Correct man and woman embody Heaven and Earth's great principle.
entries.literal: Man and woman correct—this is the great principle of Heaven and Earth.

entries.zh: 家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也。
entries.en: A household has a stern lord: father and mother.
entries.literal: The family has a stern lord—this means father and mother.

entries.zh: 父父、子子、兄兄、弟弟、夫夫、婦婦，家道正而天下正矣。』
entries.en: Let fathers be fathers, sons be sons, elder brothers be elder brothers, younger brothers be younger brothers, husbands be husbands, and wives be wives—right the family and the realm follows.
entries.literal: Father as father, son as son, elder brother as elder brother, younger brother as younger brother, husband as husband, wife as wife—the family way is correct and the realm is correct.'

entries.zh: 《禮》：『女在室，以父為天；
entries.en: The Ritual says: in the chamber a woman takes her father as Heaven;
entries.literal: The Ritual: 'A woman in the chamber takes the father as Heaven;

entries.zh: 出嫁，以夫為天。』
entries.en: after marriage she takes her husband as Heaven.
entries.literal: after marriage, she takes the husband as Heaven.'

entries.zh: 又：『在家從父，出嫁從夫，夫死從子。』
entries.en: Again: at home she follows the father, in marriage the husband, in widowhood the son.
entries.literal: Again: 'At home she follows the father; after marriage she follows the husband; when the husband dies she follows the son.

entries.zh: 本無自專抗尊之法。
entries.en: There is no charter for defying elders on one's own.
entries.literal: Fundamentally there is no law of self-willed defiance of elders.

entries.zh: 即《喪服四制》云：『天無二日，土無二王，國無二君，家無二尊，以一理之也。
entries.en: The Mourning Dress Four Principles says: Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings, a state no two lords, a family no two elders—one principle rules all.
entries.literal: The Mourning Dress Four Principles says: 'Heaven has no two suns, earth no two kings, the state no two lords, the family no two elders—one principle governs.

entries.zh: 故父在為母服周者，避二尊也。』
entries.en: Hence while the father lives, mourning for the mother is one cycle—to avoid two elders in one house.
entries.literal: Therefore when the father is alive mourning for the mother is one cycle—to avoid two elders.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下正持家國，孝理天下，而不斷在宸衷，詳正此禮，無隨末俗，顧念兒女之情。
entries.en: Your Majesty rightly orders family and state by filial rule, yet has not settled this rite in the imperial heart—do not follow custom and indulge a child's feeling alone.
entries.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty rightly holds family and state and filially governs the realm, yet does not decide in the imperial heart and correct this ritual in detail—do not follow vulgar custom and indulge children's feelings.

entries.zh: 臣恐後代復有婦奪夫政之敗者。」
entries.en: Your servant fears that later ages will again have women who usurp their husbands' government."
entries.literal: Your servant fears that later ages will again have women who usurp their husbands' government."

entries.en: The memorial closed.
entries.literal: The memorial concluded."

entries.zh: 疏奏未報。
entries.en: No answer came.
entries.literal: The memorial was submitted and not answered.

entries.zh: 履冰又上奏曰：臣聞夫婦之道，人倫之始。尊卑法於天地，動靜合於陰陽，陰陽和而天地生成，夫婦正而人倫式序。自家刑國，牝雞無晨，四德之禮不愆，三從之義斯在。即《喪服四制》云：「天無二日，土無二王，國無二君，家無二尊，以一理之也。故父在為母服周者，見無二尊也。」准舊儀，父在為母一週除靈，再周心喪。父必三年而後娶者，達子之志焉。豈先聖無情於所生，固有意於家國者矣。原夫上元肇年，則天已潛秉政，將圖僭篡，預自崇先。請升慈愛之喪，以抗尊嚴之禮，雖齊斬之儀不改，而几筵之制遂同。數年之間，尚未通用。天皇晏駕，中宗蒙塵。垂拱之末，果行聖母之偽符；載初之元，遂啟易代之深釁。孝和雖名反正，韋氏復效晨鳴。孝和非意暴崩，韋氏旋即稱制。不蒙陛下英算，宗廟何由克復？《易》云：「臣弒其君，子弒其父，非一朝一夕之故。」其斯之謂矣。臣謹尋禮意，防杜實深，若不早圖刊正，何以垂戒於後？所以薄言禮教，請依舊章，恩敕通明，蒙付所司詳議。且臣所獻者，蓋請正夫婦之綱，豈忘母子之道。諸議多不討其本源，所非議者，大凡只論罔極之恩；喪也寧戚；禽獸識母而不識父；秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑；豈得與伯叔母服同，豈得與姑姊妹制等；三王不相襲禮，五帝不相沿樂；齊斬足為升降，歲年何忍不同：此並道聽途說之言，未習先王之旨，又安足以議經邦理俗之禮乎？臣請據經義以明之。所云「罔極之恩」者，春秋祭祀，以時思之。君子有終身之憂，霜露之感，豈止一二周之服哉！故聖人恐有朝死而夕忘，曾鳥獸之不若，為立中制，使賢不肖共成文理而已。所云「喪也寧戚」者，孔子答林放之問。至如太奢太儉，太易太戚，皆非禮中。苟不得中，名為俱失，不如太儉太戚焉。毀而滅性，猶愈於朝死夕忘焉。此論臨喪哀毀之容，豈比於同宗異姓之服？所云「禽獸識母而不識父」者，禽獸群居而聚筜，而無家國之禮，少雖知親愛其母，長不解尊嚴其父。引此為諭則亦禽獸之不若乎！所云「秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑」者，人間或有遺逸，豈亦家戶到而燔之？假若盡燔，苟不可信，則墳黃都謬，庠序徒立，非聖之談，復云安屬？所云「與伯叔姑姊服同」者，伯叔姑姊有筵杖之制、三年心喪乎？所云「五帝不相沿樂，不相襲禮」，誠哉是言！此是則天懷私苞禍之情，豈可復相沿樂襲禮乎？所云「齊斬足為升降」者，母齊父斬，不易之禮。按《三年問》云：「將由修飾之君子與，三年之喪，若駟之過隙，遂之，則是無窮也。然則何以周也？曰：至親以周斷。是何也？曰：天地則已易矣，四時則已變矣，其在天地之者，莫不更始焉，以是象之也。然則何以三年？曰：加重焉耳。」故父加至再周，父在為母加三年心喪。今者還同父沒之制，則尊厭之律安施？《喪服四制》又曰：「凡禮之大體，體天地，法四時，則陰陽，順人情，故謂之禮。」訾之者是不知禮之所由生。非徒不識禮之所由制，亦恐未達孝子之通義。臣謹按《孝經》，以明陛下孝治之合至德要道，請論世欲訾禮之徒。夫至德謂孝悌，要道謂禮樂。「移風易俗，莫善於樂，安上治民，莫善於禮。」又《禮》有「無體之禮，無聲之樂。」按《孝經援神契》云：「天子孝曰就，就之為言成也。天子德被天下，澤及萬物，始終成就，則其親獲安，故曰就也。諸侯孝曰度，度者法也。諸侯居國，能奉天子法度，得不危溢，則其親獲安，故曰度也。卿大夫孝曰譽，譽之為言名也。卿大夫言行佈滿，能無惡稱，譽達遐邇，則其親獲安，故曰譽也。士孝曰究，究者以明審為義。士始升朝，辭親入仕，能審資父事君之禮，則其親獲安，故曰究也。庶人孝曰畜，畜者含畜為義。庶人含情受朴，躬耕力作，以畜其德，則其親獲安，故曰畜也。」陛下以韋氏構逆，中宗降禍，宸衷哀憤，睿情卓烈。初無一旅之眾，遂殄九重之妖，定社稷於阽危，拯宗枝於塗炭。此陛下孝悌之至，通於神明，光於四海，無所不通。使諸侯得守其法度，卿大夫得盡其言行，士得資親以事君，庶人得用天而分地。此陛下無體之禮，以安上理人也。上元以來，政由武氏，文明之後，法在凶人。賊害宗親，誅滅良善，勳階歲累，酺赦年頻。佞之則榮華，正之則遷謫。神龍、景雲之際，其事尤繁；先天、開元之間，斯弊都革。此陛下之無聲之樂，以移風易俗也。臣前狀單略，議者未識臣之懇誠。謹具狀重進，請付中書門下商量處分。臣言若讜，然敢側足於軒墀；臣言不忠，伏請竄跡於荒裔。
entries.en: Lu Lubing again submitted a memorial: Your servant has heard that the way of husband and wife is the beginning of human relations. Honored and lowly take law from Heaven and earth; movement and stillness accord with yin and yang. When yin and yang are harmonious, Heaven and earth generate and complete; when husband and wife are correct, human relations are thereby ordered. From regulating the family to governing the state, the hen has no morning cry; the rites of the four virtues do not fail, and the obligation of the three followings is here. The Four Mourning Systems says: "Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings, the state has no two rulers, and the household has no two honored ones; these are ordered by one principle. Therefore when the father is alive, one wears one-year mourning for the mother, showing that there are not two honored ones." According to the old ritual, when the father was alive, for the mother one removed the spirit seat after one cycle and observed inner mourning for two cycles. That the father must wait three years before marrying again expresses the son's intent. How could the former sages have had no feeling for the one who gave birth, when they were certainly intent on household and state? Looking back, in the first year of Shangyuan, Zetian had already secretly taken hold of government. Planning usurpation, she first honored her ancestors. She requested raising compassionate mourning to oppose the rites of reverence; although the forms of trimmed and unhemmed mourning were not changed, the system of mats and seats became the same. For several years it still was not generally used. The Heavenly Emperor died, and Zhongzong suffered dust and exile. At the end of Chuigong, the false tally of the Sage Mother was indeed carried out; in the first year of Zaichu, the deep provocation for changing dynasties was opened. Although Xiaohe was called a return to correctness, the Wei clan again imitated the morning cry. Xiaohe suddenly died contrary to expectation, and the Wei clan immediately took charge. Had it not been for Your Majesty's heroic planning, how could the ancestral temples have been restored? The Changes says: "When a minister murders his ruler or a son murders his father, it is not the cause of one morning or one evening." This is what it means. Your servant has carefully sought the meaning of ritual, and its guard and prevention are truly deep. If we do not early plan to cut and correct this, how can we transmit warning to later times? Therefore I briefly spoke of ritual teaching and requested following the old statutes. The gracious edict was penetrating and clear, and I received referral to the responsible offices for detailed deliberation. What your servant submitted was a request to correct the bond of husband and wife; how could it forget the way of mother and son? Most deliberations do not examine the root and source. What they criticize generally only discusses boundless grace, that in mourning one should prefer grief, that birds and beasts know their mothers but not their fathers, that after Qin burned the books the ritual classics were damaged and later Confucians compiled them and are not reliable, that how could it be the same mourning as for paternal uncles' wives, how could it equal the rules for paternal aunts and sisters, that the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites and the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music, and that trimmed and unhemmed garments are enough for increase and reduction while one cannot bear for the years to differ. These are all words heard on the road, not practiced in the former kings' intent. How are they enough to discuss the rites that order the state and regulate custom? Your servant requests to rely on classic meaning to clarify it. As for what is called "boundless grace," spring and autumn sacrifices remember it by season. A gentleman has lifelong grief and the feeling of frost and dew; how could it stop with one or two cycles of mourning dress? Therefore sages feared that some would have a morning death and evening forgetfulness, worse than birds and beasts, and established a middle regulation, so that worthy and unworthy together completed pattern and principle. As for what is called "in mourning, prefer grief," this is Confucius answering Lin Fang's question. As for too extravagant and too frugal, too easy and too grief-stricken, all are not within the ritual mean. If one cannot attain the mean, both are called losses, though too frugal and too grief-stricken are better. Destroying oneself and extinguishing one's nature is still better than morning death and evening forgetfulness. This discusses the appearance of grief and self-damage when facing mourning; how can it be compared to mourning dress for the same lineage and different surnames? As for "birds and beasts know the mother but not the father," birds and beasts live in flocks and gather without the rites of household and state. When young, they may know to love their mothers, but when grown they do not understand honoring their fathers. If this is cited as an analogy, are we not worse than birds and beasts? As for "after Qin burned the books, the ritual classics were damaged, and later Confucians compiled them, so they cannot be relied upon," among people there may have been texts left or lost; did Qin burn them from house to house? Suppose they were all burned. If they cannot be trusted, then the ancient classics are all mistaken, schools stand in vain, and to what does talk that rejects the sages belong? As for "the same mourning as paternal uncles' wives and paternal aunts and sisters," do paternal uncles' wives, paternal aunts, and sisters have a system of mats and staffs or three years of inner mourning? As for "the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music and did not inherit one another's rites," true indeed are these words! This was Zetian's feeling of harboring selfishness and wrapping disaster; how could one again follow her music and inherit her rite? As for "trimmed and unhemmed are enough for increase and reduction," trimmed for mother and unhemmed for father is unchanging ritual. According to Questions on Three Years: "Is it because of cultivated gentlemen? Three years of mourning is like a team of four horses passing a crack; if one extended it, it would be endless. Then why stop with one year? It says: the closest kin are cut off by a year. Why is this? It says: Heaven and earth have already changed; the four seasons have already changed; among what is within Heaven and earth, nothing has not begun anew, and this is used to model it. Then why three years? It says: weight is added." Therefore for the father it is increased to two full cycles, and while the father is alive, for the mother it is increased by three years of inner mourning. If now it is returned to the rule for when the father has died, where will the law of honored suppression be applied? The Four Mourning Systems also says: "In general, the great body of ritual embodies Heaven and earth, takes law from the four seasons, follows yin and yang, and accords with human feeling; therefore it is called ritual." Those who criticize this do not know from what ritual is born. Not only do they not understand from what ritual is made; I also fear they have not grasped the general obligation of a filial son. Your servant has carefully examined the Classic of Filial Piety to make clear that Your Majesty's filial governance accords with utmost virtue and the essential way, and I request to discuss those in the age who wish to criticize ritual. Utmost virtue means filial piety and fraternal respect; the essential way means rites and music. "For changing customs, nothing is better than music; for securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual." Also, the Ritual has "formless ritual and soundless music." According to the Filial Piety apocryphon Yuan Shen Qi: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called completion; completion means accomplishing. When the Son of Heaven's virtue covers All Under Heaven and his grace reaches the myriad things, beginning and end are accomplished, and then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called completion. A feudal lord's filial piety is called measure; measure means law. When a feudal lord resides in his state and can uphold the Son of Heaven's laws and measures, not becoming endangered or overflowing, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called measure. A minister or great officer's filial piety is called reputation; reputation means name. When a minister or great officer's words and conduct spread fully and can have no evil name, and his reputation reaches far and near, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called reputation. A shi's filial piety is called investigation; investigation takes clarity and examination as its meaning. When a shi first enters court, leaves his parents and enters service, and can examine the rite of using the father as resource to serve the ruler, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called investigation. A commoner's filial piety is called storing up; storing up takes containing and preserving as its meaning. When a commoner contains feeling and receives simplicity, personally plowing and laboring in order to store up his virtue, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called storing up." Because the Wei clan plotted rebellion and Zhongzong suffered disaster, Your Majesty's imperial heart was grieved and angered, and your sagely feeling was outstanding and fierce. At first you had not even one brigade of troops, yet you destroyed the monster in the ninefold palace, fixed the altars of soil and grain in danger, and rescued the imperial branches from mire and ashes. This is the utmost of Your Majesty's filial piety and fraternal respect, penetrating to spirits and brightness, shining over the four seas, with nothing it does not reach. It lets feudal lords keep their laws and measures, ministers and great officers exhaust their words and conduct, shi use kinship to serve the ruler, and commoners use Heaven and divide earth. This is Your Majesty's formless ritual, by which you secure superiors and order the people. Since Shangyuan, government came from the Wu clan; after Wenming, law lay with cruel people. They harmed imperial kin, killed the good, accumulated merit ranks every year, and frequently held feasts and amnesties. To flatter them brought glory; to correct them brought demotion and exile. During Shenlong and Jingyun, these affairs were especially numerous; between Xiantian and Kaiyuan, these abuses were all reformed. This is Your Majesty's soundless music, by which you changed customs. Your servant's previous statement was brief, and the debaters did not understand my earnest sincerity. I have carefully prepared this statement and present it again, requesting that it be sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery for deliberation and disposition. If your servant's words are honest, then I dare stand beside the palace steps. If your servant's words are not loyal, I humbly request exile to the distant borders.

Those who criticize this do not know from what ritual is born. Not only do they not understand from what ritual is made; I also fear they have not grasped the general obligation of a filial son. Your servant has carefully examined the Classic of Filial Piety to make clear that Your Majesty's filial governance accords with utmost virtue and the essential way, and I request to discuss those in the age who wish to criticize ritual. Utmost virtue means filial piety and fraternal respect; the essential way means rites and music. "For changing customs, nothing is better than music; for securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual." Also, the Ritual has "formless ritual and soundless music." According to the Filial Piety apocryphon Yuan Shen Qi: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called completion; completion means accomplishing. When the Son of Heaven's virtue covers All Under Heaven and his grace reaches the myriad things, beginning and end are accomplished, and then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called completion. A feudal lord's filial piety is called measure; measure means law. When a feudal lord resides in his state and can uphold the Son of Heaven's laws and measures, not becoming endangered or overflowing, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called measure. A minister or great officer's filial piety is called reputation; reputation means name. When a minister or great officer's words and conduct spread fully and can have no evil name, and his reputation reaches far and near, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called reputation. A shi's filial piety is called investigation; investigation takes clarity and examination as its meaning. When a shi first enters court, leaves his parents and enters service, and can examine the rite of using the father as resource to serve the ruler, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called investigation. A commoner's filial piety is called storing up; storing up takes containing and preserving as its meaning. When a commoner contains feeling and receives simplicity, personally plowing and laboring in order to store up his virtue, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called storing up." Because the Wei clan plotted rebellion and Zhongzong suffered disaster, Your Majesty's imperial heart was grieved and angered, and your sagely feeling was outstanding and fierce. At first you had not even one brigade of troops, yet you destroyed the monster in the ninefold palace, fixed the altars of soil and grain in danger, and rescued the imperial branches from mire and ashes. This is the utmost of Your Majesty's filial piety and fraternal respect, penetrating to spirits and brightness, shining over the four seas, with nothing it does not reach. It lets feudal lords keep their laws and measures, ministers and great officers exhaust their words and conduct, shi use kinship to serve the ruler, and commoners use Heaven and divide earth. This is Your Majesty's formless ritual, by which you secure superiors and order the people. Since Shangyuan, government came from the Wu clan; after Wenming, law lay with cruel people. They harmed imperial kin, killed the good, accumulated merit ranks every year, and frequently held feasts and amnesties. To flatter them brought glory; to correct them brought demotion and exile. During Shenlong and Jingyun, these affairs were especially numerous; between Xiantian and Kaiyuan, these abuses were all reformed. This is Your Majesty's soundless music, by which you changed customs. Your servant's previous statement was brief, and the debaters did not understand my earnest sincerity. I have carefully prepared this statement and present it again, requesting that it be sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery for deliberation and disposition. If your servant's words are honest, then I dare stand beside the palace steps. If your servant's words are not loyal, I humbly request exile to the distant borders.

entries.zh: 左散騎常侍元行沖奏議曰：「天地之性，惟人最靈者，蓋以智周萬物，惟睿作聖，明貴賤，辨尊卑，遠嫌疑，分情理也。
entries.en: Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Yuan Xingchong submitted a deliberation, saying: "Of Heaven and Earth's nature, only the human is most spiritual—because wisdom encompasses the ten thousand things, only the perspicacious become sage, discerning noble and base, distinguishing honored and humble, keeping distant what is suspect, dividing feeling and principle.
entries.literal: Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Yuan Xingchong submitted a deliberation, saying: "Of Heaven and Earth's nature, only the human is most spiritual—because wisdom encompasses the ten thousand things, only the perspicacious become sage, discerning noble and base, distinguishing honored and humble, keeping distant what is suspect, dividing feeling and principle.

entries.zh: 是以古之聖人，征性識本，緣情制服，有申有厭。
entries.en: Ancient sages read nature for the root and followed feeling to set garments—sometimes extending, sometimes reducing.
entries.literal: Therefore the ancient sages examined nature to know the root, followed feeling to set garments—there is extension and there is reduction.

entries.zh: 天父、天夫，故斬衰三年，情理俱盡者，因心立極也。
entries.en: Heaven is father, Heaven is husband—hence three years' full sackcloth where feeling and principle are both spent, the heart sets the utmost limit.
entries.literal: Heaven as father, Heaven as husband—therefore full sackcloth three years; where feeling and principle are both exhausted, the heart establishes the utmost.

entries.zh: 生則齊體，死則同穴，比陰陽而配合，同兩儀而成化。
entries.en: Alive they share one body; dead one grave—yin and yang paired, the two principles made whole.
entries.literal: In life they share one body; in death one grave—matching yin and yang in union, forming transformation with the two principles.

entries.zh: 而妻喪杖期，情禮俱殺者，蓋以遠嫌疑，尊乾道也。
entries.en: Yet a wife's death brings staff for one year—feeling and ritual both cut—to keep distance from suspicion and honor the yang way.
entries.literal: Yet for a wife's mourning, staff for one year—where feeling and ritual are both reduced—is because one keeps distant what is suspect and honors the yang way.

entries.zh: 父為嫡子三年斬衰，而不去職者，蓋尊祖重嫡，崇禮殺情也。
entries.en: A father wears three years' full sackcloth for a legitimate son yet does not leave office—honoring the grandfather, weighting the legitimate line, exalting ritual over feeling.
entries.literal: A father for the legitimate son wears three years' full sackcloth yet does not leave office—because one honors the grandfather and values the legitimate line, exalting ritual and reducing feeling.

entries.zh: 資於事父以事君，孝莫大於嚴父。
entries.en: Serving the lord as one serves the father—no filial piety exceeds honoring the father.
entries.literal: Taking service to the father as service to the lord—no filial piety is greater than honoring the father.

entries.zh: 故父在，為母罷職齊周而心喪三年，謂之尊厭者，則情申而禮殺也。
entries.en: So while the father lives, for the mother one leaves office, wears hemmed sackcloth one cycle, and heart-mourns three years—honored reduction: feeling extended, ritual cut.
entries.literal: Therefore when the father is alive, for the mother one leaves office for hemmed sackcloth one cycle and heart mourning three years—called honored reduction: feeling is extended but ritual is reduced.

entries.zh: 斯制也，可以異於飛走，別於華夷。
entries.en: That system separates humans from beasts and the civilized from the barbarian.
entries.literal: This system can distinguish one from birds and beasts and set one apart from the civilized and the barbarian.

entries.zh: 羲、農、堯、舜，莫之易也；
entries.en: Xi, Nong, Yao, and Shun never altered it;
entries.literal: Xi, Nong, Yao, and Shun—none altered it;

entries.zh: 文、武、周、孔，同所尊也。
entries.en: Wen, Wu, the Zhou, and Confucius honored it alike.
entries.literal: Wen, Wu, Zhou, and Confucius honored it alike.

entries.zh: 今若舍尊厭之重，虧嚴父之義，略純素之嫌，貽非聖之責，則事不師古，有傷名教矣。
entries.en: To cast off honored reduction, wound reverence for the father, ignore the suspicion plain garments guard against, and invite the charge of defying the sages would abandon the ancients and harm moral teaching.
entries.literal: If now one abandons the weight of honored reduction, injures the principle of honoring the father, overlooks the suspicion of plain white garments, and invites the blame of being un-sage-like, then affairs do not take the ancients as teachers and name-teaching is wounded.

entries.zh: 姨兼從母之名，即母之女黨，加於舅服，有理存焉。
entries.en: A mother's sister shares the mother's sister's name—she is the mother's female line; raising mourning for a mother's brother has its reason.
entries.literal: The mother's sister shares the name of the mother's sister—she is the mother's female kindred; increasing mourning for the mother's brother has reason in it.

entries.zh: 嫂叔不服，避嫌疑也。
entries.en: Sisters-in-law and younger uncles wore no mourning—to avoid suspicion.
entries.literal: Sister-in-law and younger uncle do not wear mourning—to avoid suspicion.

entries.zh: 若引同爨之緦，以忘推遠之跡，既乖前聖，亦謂難從。
entries.en: To cite finest hemp for sharing a hearth and forget the rule of pushing kin distant both departs from the sages and is hard to follow.
entries.literal: If one cites finest hemp for sharing the hearth and forgets the trace of pushing distant, it both departs from former sages and is hard to follow.

entries.zh: 謹詳三者之疑，並請依古為當。」
entries.en: We respectfully examine the doubts in all three cases and together request that following the ancient is correct."
entries.literal: We respectfully examine the doubts in all three cases and together request that following the ancient is correct."

entries.zh: 自是百僚議意不決。
entries.en: The bureaucracy still could not settle.
entries.literal: From this the hundred officials' deliberations did not decide.

entries.zh: 志第七禮儀七，
entries.en: Treatise Seven: Rites Seven
entries.literal: Treatise 7: Rites 7,

entries.zh: 文明元年八月，奉高宗神主祔於太廟中，始遷宣皇帝神主于夾室。
entries.en: Wenming 1, eighth month: Gaozong's tablet was enshrined in the Grand Temple, and Xuan's tablet was moved to the side chamber for the first time.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Wenming, Gaozong's spirit tablet was enshrined within the Grand Temple; for the first time, Emperor Xuan's spirit tablet was moved to the side chamber.

entries.zh: 垂拱四年正月，又於東都立高祖、太宗、高宗三廟，四時享祀，如京廟之儀。
entries.en: Chuigong 4, first month: the eastern capital gained temples to Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong, with seasonal rites matching the capital.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Chuigong, three temples for Gaozu, Taizong, and Gaozong were also established in the eastern capital; the four seasonal offerings followed the rites of the capital temples.

entries.zh: 別立崇先廟以享武氏祖考。
entries.en: A separate Chongxian Temple was built for Wu clan ancestors.
entries.literal: A separate Chongxian Temple was established to offer to the Wu clan ancestors.

entries.zh: 則天尋又令所司議立崇先廟室數，司禮博士、崇文館學士周忭希旨，請立崇先廟為七室，其皇室太廟，減為五室。
entries.en: Zetian soon ordered debate on Chongxian's chamber count; Zhou Ping of Spring Rites, courting her wish, urged seven chambers for Chongxian and five for the imperial temple.
entries.literal: Empress Zetian soon again ordered the offices to deliberate on how many chambers the Chongxian Temple should have; Court of Spring Rites erudite and Scholar of the Chongwen Institute Zhou Ping, to please her intent, requested seven chambers for Chongxian Temple and reduction of the imperial ancestral temple to five chambers.

entries.zh: 春官侍郎賈大隱奏曰：「臣竊准秦、漢皇太后臨朝稱制，並據禮經正文，天子七廟，諸侯五廟。
entries.en: Jia Dayin of Spring Rites wrote: "Qin and Han dowagers who ruled from court all cited canon—the Son of Heaven keeps seven temples, lords five.
entries.literal: Vice Minister of the Court of Spring Rites Jia Dayin memorialized, saying: "Your subject ventures to cite Qin and Han, when empress dowagers held court and exercised regulatory power—all followed the canonical ritual texts: the Son of Heaven has seven temples, feudal lords five temples.

entries.zh: 蓋百王不易之義，萬代常行之法，未有越禮違古而擅裁儀注者也。
entries.en: That is the immovable rule of kings and ages—none has broken ritual to rewrite ceremony at will.
entries.literal: This is the unchanging meaning of the hundred kings, the constant law of myriad generations—never has anyone transgressed ritual and antiquity to arrogate regulation of ceremony.

entries.zh: 今周悰別引浮議，廣述異文，直崇臨朝權儀，不依國家常度，升崇先之廟而七，降國家之廟而五。
entries.en: Zhou Cong now cites loose opinion and stray texts, exalting a regent's provisional rite over state norm—seven for Chongxian, five for the realm.
entries.literal: Now Zhou Cong cites floating opinions and broadly sets forth heterodox texts, directly elevating provisional rites of holding court, not relying on the state's constant norms—raising Chongxian temple to seven while lowering the state temple to five.

entries.zh: 臣聞皇圖廣辟，實崇宗社之尊；
entries.en: I have heard: when the throne's design is wide, the altars of state gain honor;
entries.literal: Your subject has heard: when the imperial design is broadly opened, it truly honors the altars of state;

entries.zh: 帝業弘基，實等山河之固。
entries.en: when its foundation is vast, it matches mountains and rivers in firmness.
entries.literal: when the imperial enterprise has a vast foundation, it truly equals the solidity of mountains and rivers.

entries.zh: 伏以天步多艱，時逢遏密，代天理物，自古有之。
entries.en: Heaven's course has been hard; times of mourning seclusion came; regents who govern for Heaven are ancient.
entries.literal: Your subject observes: the heavenly steps have been many times arduous; times encountered mourning seclusion; one who substitutes for Heaven and governs things has existed since antiquity.

entries.zh: 伏惟皇太后親承顧托，憂勤黎庶，納孝慈之請，垂矜撫之懷，實所謂光顯大猷，恢崇聖載。
entries.en: The Dowager took the trust, toiled for the people, heard pleas of filial mercy, and soothed the realm—truly glorifying the great design and widening the sage charge.
entries.literal: Your subject respectfully considers: the Empress Dowager personally received the entrustment, labored in care for the common people, accepted the request of filial piety and compassion, extended a cherishing and soothing heart—this truly is what is called to glorify the great plan and expand the sage burden.

entries.zh: 其崇先廟室，合同諸侯之數，國家宗廟，不合輒有移變。
entries.en: Chongxian should match a lord's count; the state temple must not be casually altered.
entries.literal: Chambers of Chongxian Temple should accord with the feudal lord count; the state ancestral temple must not casually be shifted.

entries.zh: 臣之愚直，並依正禮，周忭之請，實乖古儀。」
entries.en: Your subject's stubborn directness wholly follows orthodox ritual; Zhou Ping's request truly contravenes ancient ceremony."
entries.literal: Your subject's stubborn directness wholly follows orthodox ritual; Zhou Ping's request truly contravenes ancient ceremony."

entries.zh: 則天由是且止，
entries.en: Zetian held off for the moment.
entries.literal: Zetian therefore stopped for the time being,

entries.zh: 中宗即位，神龍元年正月，改享德廟依舊為京太廟。
entries.en: After Zhongzong's accession, Shenlong 1, first month restored Xiangde Temple as the capital Grand Temple.
entries.literal: After Zhongzong took the throne, in the first month of the first year of Shenlong, Xiangde Temple was changed back into the capital Grand Temple as before.

entries.zh: 五月，遷武氏七廟神主於西京之崇尊廟，東都創置太廟。
entries.en: Fifth month: seven Wu tablets went to western Chongzun; a new Great Temple rose at the eastern capital.
entries.literal: Fifth month: moved the seven Wu clan temple spirit tablets to western capital Chongzun Temple; newly established Great Temple at eastern capital.

entries.zh: 太常博士張齊賢建議曰：昔孫卿子云：「有天下者事七代，有一國者事五代。」
entries.en: Grand Ritual Erudite Zhang Qixian cited Xunzi: "The ruler of All Under Heaven serves seven generations; the ruler of one state serves five."
entries.literal: Grand Ritual Erudite Zhang Qixian cited Xunzi: "The ruler of All Under Heaven serves seven generations; the ruler of one state serves five."

entries.zh: 則天子七廟，古今達禮。
entries.en: Thus the emperor has seven temples, a ritual standard accepted across antiquity and the present.
entries.literal: Thus the emperor has seven temples, a ritual standard accepted across antiquity and the present.

entries.zh: 故《尚書》稱「七代之廟，可以觀德」。
entries.en: 《Documents》 says, "Through seven generations of temples, one may observe virtue."
entries.literal: 《Documents》 says, "Through seven generations of temples, one may observe virtue."

entries.zh: 《祭法》稱「王立七廟，一壇一墠」。
entries.en: 《Sacrificial Regulations》 says, "The king establishes seven temples, one altar, and one open ground."
entries.literal: 《Sacrificial Regulations》 says, "The king establishes seven temples, one altar, and one open ground."

entries.zh: 《王制》云：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」
entries.en: The 《Wang System》 says, "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."
entries.literal: The 《Wang System》 says, "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."

entries.zh: 莫不尊始封之君，謂之太祖。
entries.en: All such systems honor the first enfeoffed lord as Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: All such systems honor the first enfeoffed lord as Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 太祖之廟，百代不遷。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor's temple remains unmoved for a hundred generations.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor's temple remains unmoved for a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 袷祭之禮，毀廟之主陳於太祖，未毀廟之主，皆升合食于太祖之室。
entries.en: At the xia sacrifice, removed temple tablets are arrayed at the Grand Ancestor, while unremoved tablets are raised to share offerings in the Grand Ancestor's chamber.
entries.literal: At the xia sacrifice, removed temple tablets are arrayed at the Grand Ancestor, while unremoved tablets are raised to share offerings in the Grand Ancestor's chamber.

entries.zh: 太祖東向，昭南向，穆北向。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor faces east; zhao face south, and mu face north.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor faces east; zhao face south, and mu face north.

entries.zh: 太祖者，商之玄王、周之后稷是也。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestors are exemplified by Xuan Wang of Shang and Hou Ji of Zhou.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestors are exemplified by Xuan Wang of Shang and Hou Ji of Zhou.

entries.zh: 太祖之外，更無始祖。
entries.en: Beyond the Grand Ancestor there is no additional founding ancestor.
entries.literal: Beyond the Grand Ancestor there is no additional founding ancestor.

entries.zh: 但商自玄王以後，十有四代，至湯而有天下。
entries.en: From Shang's Xuan Wang to Tang's possession of the realm lay fourteen generations.
entries.literal: From Shang's Xuan Wang to Tang's possession of the realm lay fourteen generations.

entries.zh: 周自后稷已後，十有七代，至武王而有天下。
entries.en: From Zhou's Hou Ji to King Wu's possession of the realm lay seventeen generations.
entries.literal: From Zhou's Hou Ji to King Wu's possession of the realm lay seventeen generations.

entries.zh: 其間代數既遠，遷廟親廟，皆出太祖之後，故得合食有序，尊卑不差。
entries.en: Since those lines were remote, both removed temples and kin temples stood after the Grand Ancestor, so joint offerings had proper order and rank was not confused.
entries.literal: Since those lines were remote, both removed temples and kin temples stood after the Grand Ancestor, so joint offerings had proper order and rank was not confused.

entries.zh: 其後漢高祖受命，無始封祖，即以高皇帝為太祖。
entries.en: When Han Gaozu received the mandate without a first-enfeoffed ancestor, he himself became Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu received the mandate without a first-enfeoffed ancestor, he himself became Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 太上皇高帝之父，立廟享祀，不在昭穆合食之列，為尊于太祖故也。
entries.en: Gaozu's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor, received a temple and sacrifices but was not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings, because he was honored above the Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: Gaozu's father, the Grand Supreme Emperor, received a temple and sacrifices but was not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings, because he was honored above the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 魏武創業，文帝受命，亦即以武帝為太祖。
entries.en: Cao Cao founded Wei's enterprise, so when Emperor Wen received the mandate, Emperor Wu likewise became Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: Cao Cao founded Wei's enterprise, so when Emperor Wen received the mandate, Emperor Wu likewise became Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 其高皇、太皇、外處君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
entries.en: Gao Huang, Tai Huang, Waichu Jun, and the others were honored as kin and not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings.
entries.literal: Gao Huang, Tai Huang, Waichu Jun, and the others were honored as kin and not included in the zhao-mu shared offerings.

entries.zh: 晉宣創業，武帝受命，亦即以宣帝為太祖。
entries.en: Sima Yi founded Jin's enterprise, so when Emperor Wu received the mandate, Emperor Xuan likewise became Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: Sima Yi founded Jin's enterprise, so when Emperor Wu received the mandate, Emperor Xuan likewise became Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 其征西、豫章、潁川、京兆府君等並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
entries.en: The Zhengxi, Yuzhang, Yingchuan, Jingzhao, and other lords were honored as kin and excluded from the zhao-mu shared offerings.
entries.literal: The Zhengxi, Yuzhang, Yingchuan, Jingzhao, and other lords were honored as kin and excluded from the zhao-mu shared offerings.

entries.zh: 歷茲已降，至於有隋，宗廟之制，斯禮不改。
entries.en: From those dynasties through Sui, the ancestral-temple rule remained unchanged.
entries.literal: From those dynasties through Sui, the ancestral-temple rule remained unchanged.

entries.zh: 故宇文氏以文皇帝為太祖，隋室以武元皇帝為太祖。
entries.en: Thus Northern Zhou treated Emperor Wen as Grand Ancestor, and Sui treated Emperor Wuyuan as Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: Thus Northern Zhou treated Emperor Wen as Grand Ancestor, and Sui treated Emperor Wuyuan as Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 國家誕受在命，累葉重光。
entries.en: Our dynasty received the mandate, and successive generations have renewed its brilliance.
entries.literal: Our dynasty received the mandate, and successive generations have renewed its brilliance.

entries.zh: 景皇帝始封唐公，實為太祖。
entries.en: Emperor Jing, first enfeoffed as Duke of Tang, is truly the Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing, first enfeoffed as Duke of Tang, is truly the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 中間代數既近，列在三昭三穆之內，故皇家太廟，唯有六室。
entries.en: Because the line is still close and Emperor Jing falls within the three zhao and three mu, the Tang Grand Temple has only six chambers.
entries.literal: Because the line is still close and Emperor Jing falls within the three zhao and three mu, the Tang Grand Temple has only six chambers.

entries.zh: 其弘農府君、宣、光二帝，尊于太祖，親盡則遷，不在昭穆合食之數。
entries.en: The Hongnong Lord, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Guang stand in honor above the Grand Ancestor; once kinship is exhausted they are moved and are not part of the zhao-mu shared offerings.
entries.literal: The Hongnong Lord, Emperor Xuan, and Emperor Guang stand in honor above the Grand Ancestor; once kinship is exhausted they are moved and are not part of the zhao-mu shared offerings.

entries.zh: 今皇極再造，孝思匪寧。
entries.en: Now the imperial order has been restored, and filial concern remains unsettled.
entries.literal: Now the imperial order has been restored, and filial concern remains unsettled.

entries.zh: 奉二月二十九日敕：「七室已下，依舊號尊崇。」
entries.en: The edict of the twenty-ninth day of the second month said, "For the seven chambers and below, keep the old titles and honors."
entries.literal: The edict of the twenty-ninth day of the second month said, "For the seven chambers and below, keep the old titles and honors."

entries.zh: 又奉三月一日敕：「既立七廟，須尊崇始祖，速令詳之」者。
entries.en: The edict of the first day of the third month added, "Since seven temples are being established, the founding ancestor must be honored. Examine this quickly."
entries.literal: The edict of the first day of the third month added, "Since seven temples are being established, the founding ancestor must be honored. Examine this quickly."

entries.zh: 伏尋禮經，始祖即是太祖，太祖之外，更無始祖。
entries.en: Looking through the ritual classics, I find that the founding ancestor is the Grand Ancestor, and outside the Grand Ancestor there is no separate founder.
entries.literal: Looking through the ritual classics, I find that the founding ancestor is the Grand Ancestor, and outside the Grand Ancestor there is no separate founder.

entries.zh: 周朝太祖之外，以周文王為始祖，不合禮經。
entries.en: For Zhou to set King Wen as a founding ancestor beyond the Grand Ancestor does not fit the ritual classics.
entries.literal: For Zhou to set King Wen as a founding ancestor beyond the Grand Ancestor does not fit the ritual classics.

entries.zh: 或有引《白虎通義》云「后稷為始祖、文王為太祖、武王為太宗」，及鄭玄注《詩·雍》序云「太祖謂文王」以為說者。
entries.en: Some explain this by citing 《Baihu tongyi》, "Hou Ji was founding ancestor, King Wen Grand Ancestor, and King Wu Grand Zong," and Zheng Xuan's note to the 《Shi: Yong》 preface, "Grand Ancestor means King Wen."
entries.literal: Some explain this by citing 《Baihu tongyi》, "Hou Ji was founding ancestor, King Wen Grand Ancestor, and King Wu Grand Zong," and Zheng Xuan's note to the 《Shi: Yong》 preface, "Grand Ancestor means King Wen."

entries.zh: 其義不然。
entries.en: That interpretation is wrong.
entries.literal: That interpretation is wrong.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 彼以禮「王者祖有功，宗有德，周人祖文王而宗武王」，故謂文王為太祖耳，非袷祭群主合食之太祖。
entries.en: They call King Wen Grand Ancestor because ritual says, "Rulers make ancestors of those with merit and zong of those with virtue; Zhou made King Wen ancestor and King Wu zong." But this is not the Grand Ancestor who receives all rulers in shared xia offerings.
entries.literal: They call King Wen Grand Ancestor because ritual says, "Rulers make ancestors of those with merit and zong of those with virtue; Zhou made King Wen ancestor and King Wu zong." But this is not the Grand Ancestor who receives all rulers in shared xia offerings.

entries.zh: 今之議者，或有欲立涼武昭王為始祖者，殊為不可。
entries.en: Some now wish to make Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor, but this is especially wrong.
entries.literal: Some now wish to make Liang Wuzhao Wang the founding ancestor, but this is especially wrong.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 昔在商、周，契、稷始封，湯、武之興，祚由契、稷，故以契、稷為太祖，即皇家之景帝是也。
entries.en: In Shang and Zhou, Xie and Hou Ji were the first enfeoffed ancestors. Tang and Wu rose from their fortune, so Xie and Hou Ji became Grand Ancestors. For our imperial house, that role belongs to Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: In Shang and Zhou, Xie and Hou Ji were the first enfeoffed ancestors. Tang and Wu rose from their fortune, so Xie and Hou Ji became Grand Ancestors. For our imperial house, that role belongs to Emperor Jing.

entries.zh: 涼武昭王勳業未廣，後主失國，土宇不傳。
entries.en: Liang Wuzhao Wang's merit was limited, his successor lost the state, and the territory did not continue.
entries.literal: Liang Wuzhao Wang's merit was limited, his successor lost the state, and the territory did not continue.

entries.zh: 景皇始封，實基明命。
entries.en: Emperor Jing's first enfeoffment truly founded the Tang mandate.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing's first enfeoffment truly founded the Tang mandate.

entries.zh: 今乃舍封唐之盛烈，崇西涼之遠構，考之前古，實乖典禮。
entries.en: To abandon the great enfeoffment in Tang and exalt distant Western Liang violates ancient ritual precedent.
entries.literal: To abandon the great enfeoffment in Tang and exalt distant Western Liang violates ancient ritual precedent.

entries.zh: 魏氏不以曹參為太祖，晉氏不以殷王仰為太祖，宋氏不以楚元王為太祖，齊、梁不以蕭何為太祖，陳、隋不以胡公、楊震為太祖，則皇家安可以涼武昭王為太祖乎？
entries.en: Wei did not ancestralize Cao Shen, Jin did not ancestralize the King of Yin, Song did not ancestralize King Yuan of Chu, Qi and Liang did not ancestralize Xiao He, and Chen and Sui did not ancestralize Duke Hu or Yang Zhen. How could Tang make Liang Wuzhao Wang Grand Ancestor?
entries.literal: Wei did not ancestralize Cao Shen, Jin did not ancestralize the King of Yin, Song did not ancestralize King Yuan of Chu, Qi and Liang did not ancestralize Xiao He, and Chen and Sui did not ancestralize Duke Hu or Yang Zhen. How could Tang make Liang Wuzhao Wang Grand Ancestor?

entries.zh: 漢之東京，大議郊祀，多以周郊后稷，漢當郊堯。
entries.en: In Eastern Han, a major debate over suburban sacrifice held that because Zhou offered to Hou Ji, Han should offer to Yao.
entries.literal: In Eastern Han, a major debate over suburban sacrifice held that because Zhou offered to Hou Ji, Han should offer to Yao.

entries.zh: 制上公卿議，議者多同，帝亦然之。
entries.en: The court sent the issue to the ministers; most agreed, and the emperor was inclined to agree as well.
entries.literal: The court sent the issue to the ministers; most agreed, and the emperor was inclined to agree as well.

entries.zh: 杜林正議，獨以為「周室之興，祚由后稷。
entries.en: Only Du Lin argued correctly: "The rise of Zhou came through Hou Ji.
entries.literal: Only Du Lin argued correctly: "The rise of Zhou came through Hou Ji.

entries.zh: 漢業特起，功不緣堯。
entries.en: Han arose on its own; its merit did not derive from Yao.
entries.literal: Han arose on its own; its merit did not derive from Yao.

entries.zh: 祖宗故事，所宜因循。」
entries.en: The old precedents for ancestors and zong should be followed."
entries.literal: The old precedents for ancestors and zong should be followed."

entries.zh: 竟從林議。
entries.en: The court ultimately followed Du Lin.
entries.literal: The court ultimately followed Du Lin.

entries.zh: 又傳稱，「欲知天上，事問長人」，以其近之。
entries.en: Another tradition says, "To know Heaven, ask the elders," because they stand closer to it.
entries.literal: Another tradition says, "To know Heaven, ask the elders," because they stand closer to it.

entries.zh: 武德、貞觀之時，主聖臣賢，其去涼武昭王蓋亦近於今矣。
entries.en: The Wude and Zhenguan rulers were sagely and their ministers worthy, and they were closer to Liang Wuzhao Wang's time than we are.
entries.literal: The Wude and Zhenguan rulers were sagely and their ministers worthy, and they were closer to Liang Wuzhao Wang's time than we are.

entries.zh: 當時不立者，必不可立故也。
entries.en: If they did not establish him then, he surely should not be established now.
entries.literal: If they did not establish him then, he surely should not be established now.

entries.zh: 今既年代浸遠，方復立之，是非三祖二宗之意。
entries.en: To establish him only after so many years would violate the intent behind the three ancestors and two zong.
entries.literal: To establish him only after so many years would violate the intent behind the three ancestors and two zong.

entries.zh: 實恐景皇失職而震怒，武昭虛位而不答，非社稷之福也。
entries.en: I fear Emperor Jing would be displaced and angered, while Wuzhao would hold an empty position and give no response; this would not benefit the state.
entries.literal: I fear Emperor Jing would be displaced and angered, while Wuzhao would hold an empty position and give no response; this would not benefit the state.

entries.zh: 宗廟事重，禘祫禮崇，先王以之觀德。
entries.en: Temple affairs are weighty, and the di and xia rites are exalted; through them the former kings observed virtue.
entries.literal: Temple affairs are weighty, and the di and xia rites are exalted; through them the former kings observed virtue.

entries.zh: 或者不知其說，既灌而往，孔子不欲觀之。
entries.en: Some fail to understand this. Confucius himself did not wish to watch after the libation had passed.
entries.literal: Some fail to understand this. Confucius himself did not wish to watch after the libation had passed.

entries.zh: 今朝命惟新，宜應慎禮，祭如神在，理不可誣。
entries.en: Now that the dynasty's mandate has been renewed, ritual must be handled carefully. Sacrifice is performed as if the spirits were present; it cannot be falsified.
entries.literal: Now that the dynasty's mandate has been renewed, ritual must be handled carefully. Sacrifice is performed as if the spirits were present; it cannot be falsified.

entries.zh: 請准敕加太廟為七室，享宣皇帝以備七代，其始祖不合別有尊崇。
entries.en: I request that the Grand Temple be expanded to seven chambers and Emperor Xuan be sacrificed to as the seventh generation; no separate honor should be given to another founding ancestor.
entries.literal: I request that the Grand Temple be expanded to seven chambers and Emperor Xuan be sacrificed to as the seventh generation; no separate honor should be given to another founding ancestor.

entries.zh: 太常博士劉承慶、尹知章又議云：謹按《王制》：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」
entries.en: Grand Ritual Erudites Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang also cited the 《Wang System》: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."
entries.literal: Grand Ritual Erudites Liu Chengqing and Yin Zhizhang also cited the 《Wang System》: "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."

entries.zh: 此載籍之明文，古今之通制。
entries.en: This is the clear written rule and the common system of antiquity and later ages.
entries.literal: This is the clear written rule and the common system of antiquity and later ages.

entries.zh: 皇唐稽考前範，詳采列辟，崇建宗靈，式遵斯典。
entries.en: Tang examined earlier models, drew carefully on past rulers, built up the ancestral spirits, and followed this canon.
entries.literal: Tang examined earlier models, drew carefully on past rulers, built up the ancestral spirits, and followed this canon.

entries.zh: 但以開基之主，受命之君，王跡有淺深，太祖有遠近。
entries.en: Yet founders and mandate-receiving rulers differ: royal traces may be deep or shallow, and Grand Ancestors may be remote or near.
entries.literal: Yet founders and mandate-receiving rulers differ: royal traces may be deep or shallow, and Grand Ancestors may be remote or near.

entries.zh: 湯、文祚基契、稷，太祖代遠，出乎昭穆之上，故七廟可全。
entries.en: Tang and King Wen were rooted in Xie and Hou Ji; because those Grand Ancestors were remote and stood above the zhao-mu line, the full seven temples were possible.
entries.literal: Tang and King Wen were rooted in Xie and Hou Ji; because those Grand Ancestors were remote and stood above the zhao-mu line, the full seven temples were possible.

entries.zh: 若夏繼唐、虞，功非由鯀；
entries.en: Xia succeeded Tang and Yu, but its merit did not derive from Gun;
entries.literal: Xia succeeded Tang and Yu, but its merit did not derive from Gun;

entries.zh: 漢除秦、項，力不因堯。
entries.en: Han destroyed Qin and Xiang, but its power did not come from Yao.
entries.literal: Han destroyed Qin and Xiang, but its power did not come from Yao.

entries.zh: 及魏、晉經圖，周、隋撥亂，皆勳隆近代，祖業非遠，受命始封之主，不離昭穆之親，故肇立宗祊，罕聞全制。
entries.en: Wei, Jin, Zhou, and Sui won their achievements in recent generations, not through remote ancestral enterprises; their mandate-receiving founders still lay within the zhao-mu kinship line, so their first temple systems were rarely complete.
entries.literal: Wei, Jin, Zhou, and Sui won their achievements in recent generations, not through remote ancestral enterprises; their mandate-receiving founders still lay within the zhao-mu kinship line, so their first temple systems were rarely complete.

entries.zh: 夫太祖以功建，昭穆以親崇，有功百代而不遷，親盡七葉而當毀。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor rests on merit; zhao and mu rest on kinship. Merit keeps a tablet unmoved for a hundred generations, while exhausted kinship after seven leaves requires removal.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor rests on merit; zhao and mu rest on kinship. Merit keeps a tablet unmoved for a hundred generations, while exhausted kinship after seven leaves requires removal.

entries.zh: 或以太祖代淺，廟數非備，更于昭穆之上，遠立合遷之君，曲從七廟之文，深乖迭毀之制。
entries.en: To force the seven-temple wording by adding a remote but movable ruler above the zhao-mu line, merely because the Grand Ancestor is near, would badly violate the rule of successive removal.
entries.literal: To force the seven-temple wording by adding a remote but movable ruler above the zhao-mu line, merely because the Grand Ancestor is near, would badly violate the rule of successive removal.

entries.zh: 皇家千齡啟旦，百葉重光。
entries.en: The imperial house opened a thousand-year dawn and renewed the brightness of a hundred generations.
entries.literal: The imperial house opened a thousand-year dawn and renewed the brightness of a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 景皇帝浚德基唐，代數猶近，號雖崇于太祖，親尚列于昭穆，且臨六室之位，未申七代之尊。
entries.en: Emperor Jing founded Tang in deep virtue, but his generation is still near. Though honored as Grand Ancestor, by kinship he remains within the zhao-mu line and one of the six chambers, not yet creating the honor of seven generations.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing founded Tang in deep virtue, but his generation is still near. Though honored as Grand Ancestor, by kinship he remains within the zhao-mu line and one of the six chambers, not yet creating the honor of seven generations.

entries.zh: 是知太廟當六，未合有七。
entries.en: Thus the Grand Temple should have six chambers and not yet seven.
entries.literal: Thus the Grand Temple should have six chambers and not yet seven.

entries.zh: 故先朝惟有宣、光、景、元、神、堯、文武六代親廟。
entries.en: The former court therefore had only six generations of kin temples: Xuan, Guang, Jing, Yuan, Shenyao, and Wenwu.
entries.literal: The former court therefore had only six generations of kin temples: Xuan, Guang, Jing, Yuan, Shenyao, and Wenwu.

entries.zh: 大帝登遐，神主升祔於廟室，以宣皇帝代數當滿，准禮復遷。
entries.en: When the Great Emperor died and his tablet was enshrined, Emperor Xuan's generations were complete, so ritual moved him out again.
entries.literal: When the Great Emperor died and his tablet was enshrined, Emperor Xuan's generations were complete, so ritual moved him out again.

entries.zh: 今止有光皇帝已下六代親廟，非是天子之廟數不當有七，要由太祖有遠近之異，故初建有多少之殊。
entries.en: Now there are only six generations of kin temples from Emperor Guang down. This does not mean the emperor should not have seven temples; it means the number at establishment varies because Grand Ancestors may be remote or near.
entries.literal: Now there are only six generations of kin temples from Emperor Guang down. This does not mean the emperor should not have seven temples; it means the number at establishment varies because Grand Ancestors may be remote or near.

entries.zh: 敬惟三后臨朝，代多儒雅，神祊事重，禮豈虛存，規模可沿，理難變革。
entries.en: The three former reigns had many learned classicists, and temple affairs were weighty. Their ritual model was not empty; it can be followed, and principle does not favor changing it.
