entries.literal: The three former reigns had many learned classicists, and temple affairs were weighty. Their ritual model was not empty; it can be followed, and principle does not favor changing it.

entries.zh: 宣皇既非始祖，又廟無祖宗之號，親盡既遷，其在不合重立。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan is not the founder, and his temple has no zu or zong title. Since his kinship line was exhausted and he was moved, he should not be restored.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan is not the founder, and his temple has no zu or zong title. Since his kinship line was exhausted and he was moved, he should not be restored.

entries.zh: 若禮終運往，建議復崇，實違《王制》之文，不合先朝之旨。
entries.en: To exalt him again after the ritual order has moved on would violate the 《Wang System》 and the former court's intent.
entries.literal: To exalt him again after the ritual order has moved on would violate the 《Wang System》 and the former court's intent.

entries.zh: 請依貞觀之故事，無改三聖之宏規，光崇六室，不虧古議。
entries.en: We request following Zhenguan precedent, preserving the grand rule of the Three Sages, and honoring the six chambers without impairing the ancient judgment.
entries.literal: We request following Zhenguan precedent, preserving the grand rule of the Three Sages, and honoring the six chambers without impairing the ancient judgment.

entries.zh: 時有制令宰相更加詳定，禮部尚書祝欽明等奏言：「博士三人，自分兩議：張齊賢以始同太祖，不合更祖昭王；
entries.en: An edict sent chancellors to refine the question; Zhu Qinming of Rites reported: "Three erudites split two ways—Zhang Qixian said they were already Great Founder and King Zhao should not be added as ancestor;
entries.literal: Then there was an edict ordering the chief ministers to deliberate further; Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming and others memorialized, saying: "Three erudites divided into two opinions: Zhang Qixian held that from the first they were the same as the Great Founder, and it was not fitting to further take King Zhao as ancestor;

entries.zh: 劉承慶以《王制》三昭三穆，不合重崇宣帝。
entries.en: Liu Chengqing cited the 《Wang System》's three zhao and three mu: no double honor for Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: Liu Chengqing held that the three zhao and three mu of the 《Wang System》 did not permit doubly honoring Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 臣等商量，請依張齊賢以景皇帝為太祖，依劉承慶尊崇六室。」
entries.en: Your subjects deliberated and request: follow Zhang Qixian in taking Emperor Jing as Great Founder, follow Liu Chengqing in honoring with six chambers."
entries.literal: Your subjects deliberated and request: follow Zhang Qixian in taking Emperor Jing as Great Founder, follow Liu Chengqing in honoring with six chambers."

entries.zh: 制從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: The decree followed this.

entries.zh: 尋有制以孝敬皇帝為義宗，升祔於太廟。
entries.en: Soon an edict made the Filial and Respectful Emperor the Righteous Ancestor and elevated him into the Great Temple.
entries.literal: Soon there was an edict making Filial and Respectful Emperor the Righteous Ancestor, elevated enshrinement in the Great Temple.

entries.zh: 其年八月，崇祔光皇帝、太祖景皇帝、代祖元皇帝、高祖神堯皇帝、太宗文武聖皇帝、皇考高宗天皇大帝、皇兄義宗孝敬皇帝于東都之太廟，躬行享獻之禮。
entries.en: That eighth month at the eastern Great Temple: elevated enshrinement for Guang, Jing as Great Founder, Yuan as dynastic ancestor, Shenyao Gaozu, sage Taizong, heavenly Gaozong, and Righteous Ancestor Filial and Respectful—the emperor offered in person.
entries.literal: That year eighth month: elevated enshrinement of Emperors Guang, Jing as Great Founder, Yuan as Dynastic Ancestor, Gaozu as Emperor Shenyao, Taizong as the Civil and Martial Sage Emperor, father Emperor Gaozong the Great Heavenly Emperor, elder brother Righteous Ancestor Filial and Respectful Emperor at the eastern capital Great Temple; the emperor in person performed the offering rite.

entries.zh: 時太常卿姜皎復與禮官上表曰：「臣聞敬宗尊祖，享德崇恩，必也正名，用光時憲，禮也。
entries.en: Director Jiang Jiao and the ritual officials again memorialized: "We hear that revering ancestors and exalting grace require correct titles to honor the age's laws—that is ritual.
entries.literal: At that time Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao again, with ritual officials, submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that revering the clan and honoring ancestors, enjoying virtue and exalting grace, must rectify names to illuminate the statutes of the age—this is ritual.

entries.zh: 伏見太廟中則天皇后配高宗天皇大帝，題云『天后聖帝武氏』。
entries.en: In the Grand Temple Empress Zetian shares sacrifice with Emperor Gaozong, inscribed as "Holy Emperor Wu of the Heavenly Empress."
entries.literal: We note in the Grand Temple Empress Zetian is enshrined with Emperor Gaozong Tianhuang Dadi, the inscription reading "Holy Emperor Wu of the Heavenly Empress."

entries.zh: 伏尋昔居寵秩，親承顧托，因攝大政，事乃從權。
entries.en: She once held favored rank, received the late emperor's trust, and took power as an expedient measure.
entries.literal: We trace how in the past she held favored rank and personally received the entrustment; she then assumed great government, the affair being one of expedient power.

entries.zh: 神龍之初，已去帝號。
entries.en: At the start of Shenlong her imperial title had already been removed.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong the imperial title was already removed.

entries.zh: 岑羲等不閑政體，復題帝名。
entries.en: Cen Xi and others, ignorant of governance, restored an imperial title on the inscription.
entries.literal: Cen Xi and others were unversed in the body of government and again inscribed an imperial name.

entries.zh: 若又使帝號長存，恐非聖朝通典。
entries.en: To let an imperial title stand again would violate court precedent.
entries.literal: If the imperial title is again made to endure long, I fear it is not the general statute of the sagely court.

entries.zh: 夫七廟者，高祖神堯皇帝之廟也。
entries.en: The seven temples are those of the High Ancestor, Emperor Shen Yao.
entries.literal: The seven temples are the temples of the High Ancestor, the Divine Yao Emperor.

entries.zh: 父昭子穆，祖德宗功，非夫帝子天孫，乘乾出震者，不得升祔於斯矣。
entries.en: Father-zhao, son-mu, ancestral merit—only imperial sons and heaven's grandsons who received the mandate may be enshrined there.
entries.literal: Father zhao, son mu; ancestral virtue and clan achievement—none but sons of emperors and grandsons of Heaven, those who mount Qian and issue from Zhen, may ascend to enshrinement there.

entries.zh: 但皇后祔廟，配食高宗，位號舊章，無宜稱帝。
entries.en: Yet as consort sharing Gaozong's sacrifices, her old titles should not include "emperor.
entries.literal: But the empress enshrined in the temple, sharing sacrifice with Gaozong, by old title and statute ought not be called emperor.

entries.zh: 今山陵日近，陞祔非遙，請申陳告之儀，因除『聖帝』之字，直題云『則天皇后武氏』。」
entries.en: With her enshrinement near, we ask to perform the announcement rite, drop "Holy Emperor," and inscribe only "Empress Zetian Wu."
entries.literal: Now the imperial tomb day draws near and ascent to enshrinement is not distant; we ask to declare the announcement rite and remove the words "Holy Emperor," inscribing simply "Empress Zetian Wu."

entries.zh: 詔從之。
entries.en: The emperor approved.
entries.literal: The edict followed it.

entries.zh: 時既另造義宗廟，將作大匠韋湊上疏曰：「臣聞王者制體，是曰規模；
entries.en: A separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou wrote: "A king's institutions are his model;
entries.literal: At that time a separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that the king establishes the body—this is called the model;

entries.zh: 規模之興，實資師古；
entries.en: and models must learn from antiquity;
entries.literal: the rise of the model in fact relies on taking antiquity as teacher;

entries.zh: 師古之道，必也正名；
entries.en: which requires correct names;
entries.literal: the Way of taking antiquity as teacher must rectify names;

entries.zh: 惟名與實，固當相副。
entries.en: name and fact must agree.
entries.literal: names and reality solidly ought to match each other.

entries.zh: 其在宗廟，禮之大者，豈可失哉！
entries.en: In the ancestral temple, the greatest rite—how can it be neglected!
entries.literal: As for the ancestral temple, the greatest of rites—how can it be lost!

entries.zh: 禮，祖有功而宗有德。
entries.en: Ritual holds that ancestors have merit and clan lords have virtue.
entries.literal: Ritual: the ancestor has merit, the clan lord has virtue.

entries.zh: 祖宗之廟，百代不毀。
entries.en: Ancestor and clan-lord temples stand for a hundred generations.
entries.literal: The temples of ancestor and clan lord are not destroyed for a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 故殷太甲曰太宗，太戊曰中宗，武丁曰高宗。
entries.en: Yin's Tai Jia was styled Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, and Wu Ding Gaozong.
entries.literal: Thus Yin's Tai Jia was called Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, Wu Ding Gaozong.

entries.zh: 周宗文王、武王。
entries.en: Zhou honored Kings Wen and Wu.
entries.literal: Zhou honored King Wen and King Wu.

entries.zh: 漢則文帝為太宗，武帝為世宗。
entries.en: Han styled Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.
entries.literal: Han made Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.

entries.zh: 其後代有稱宗，皆以方制海內，德澤可宗，列于昭穆，期於不毀。
entries.en: Later rulers styled "zong" when their virtue filled the realm and merited lasting place in the zhao-mu sequence.
entries.literal: Afterward generations had those styled "zong," all because they regulated the realm within the four seas and their virtue and grace could be honored; ranked in zhao and mu, they were expected not to be destroyed.

entries.zh: 祖宗之義，不亦大乎！
entries.en: The weight of "ancestor" and "zong" is immense!
entries.literal: Is the meaning of "ancestor" and "zong" not also great!

entries.zh: 況孝敬皇帝位止東宮，未嘗南面，聖道誠冠于儲副，德教不被於寰瀛，立廟稱宗，恐非合體。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaojing never ruled; though his virtue surpassed other heirs, his teaching did not reach the realm—calling him "zong" does not fit ritual.
entries.literal: Moreover Emperor Xiaojing's position stopped at the Eastern Palace; he never faced south. His sagely Way indeed topped the heir, yet his moral teaching did not spread through the realm—establishing a temple and styling him zong, I fear, is not fitting the body of ritual.

entries.zh: 況別起寢廟，不入昭穆，稽諸祀典，何義稱宗？
entries.en: A separate shrine outside the zhao-mu line: how can it be called "zong" under the sacrifice canon?
entries.literal: Moreover, if a separate sleeping temple is erected and he does not enter the zhao-mu sequence, then when this is checked against the sacrifice canon, by what principle can he be called zong?

entries.zh: 而廟號義宗，稱之萬代。
entries.en: Yet the temple name Yizong would stand for ages.
entries.literal: Yet the temple name Yizong would be spoken for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 以臣庸識，竊謂不可。
entries.en: In my humble view it should not be done.
entries.literal: By your servant's shallow knowledge, I privately deem it impossible.

entries.zh: 望更令有司詳定，務合於禮。」
entries.en: I hope you will further order the relevant offices to examine in detail and ensure conformity with ritual."
entries.literal: I hope you will further order the relevant offices to examine in detail and ensure conformity with ritual."

entries.zh: 於是太常請以本諡「孝敬」為廟稱。
entries.en: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices then proposed "Xiaojing," his posthumous title, as the temple name.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested using the original posthumous title "Xiaojing" as the temple name.

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: Approved.
entries.literal: It was approved.

entries.zh: 唐禮：四時各以孟月享太廟，每室用太牢，季冬蠟祭之後，以辰日臘享於太廟，用牲如時祭。
entries.en: Tang ritual: each season's first month, offerings at the Great Temple—tai lao per chamber. After twelfth-month wax and la, a chen-day la feast at the temple used seasonal victims.
entries.literal: Tang rites: In each of the four seasons, in the first month of the season, offerings were made to the Great Ancestral Temple; for each chamber the great offering was used. After the wax sacrifices following the twelfth month's la rites, on a chen day a la offering was presented at the Great Temple, with victims as at the seasonal sacrifices.

entries.zh: 三年一祫，以孟冬。
entries.en: A he rite every three years, in mid-winter's opening month.
entries.literal: Every three years a he sacrifice, in the first month of winter.

entries.zh: 五年一禘，以孟夏。
entries.en: A di rite every five years, in mid-summer's opening month.
entries.literal: Every five years a di sacrifice, in the first month of summer.

entries.zh: 又時享之日，修七祀於太廟西門內之道南：司命，戶以春，灶以夏；
entries.en: On seasonal offering days the Seven Sacrifices were kept on the lane south of the temple's west gate—Spirit of Fate; Household Spirit in spring, Stove Spirit in summer;
entries.literal: On days of seasonal offerings, the Seven Sacrifices were maintained on the road south within the western gate of the Great Temple: Spirit of Fate; the Household Spirit in spring, the Stove Spirit in summer;

entries.zh: 門，厲以秋，行以冬，中溜則于季夏迎氣日祀之。
entries.en: Gate and Pestilence Spirits in autumn, Road Spirit in winter; Central Gutter on the last-summer qi-reception day.
entries.literal: the Gate Spirit and the Pestilence Spirit in autumn, the Road Spirit in winter; the Central Gutter was sacrificed on the day of receiving seasonal qi in the last month of summer.

entries.zh: 若品物時新堪進御者，所司先送太常，與尚食相知，簡擇精好者，以滋味與新物相宜者配之。
entries.en: Seasonal delicacies fit for the throne went first to the Court of Sacrifices and the Provisioners, who picked the best and matched flavor to the new offering.
entries.literal: If seasonal novelties were fit to present to the sovereign, the responsible office first sent them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and coordinated with the Imperial Provisioners, selecting the finest and pairing them with flavors suited to the new goods.

entries.zh: 太常卿奉薦於太廟，不出神主。
entries.en: The Minister of Sacrifices presented at the Great Temple without removing the tablets.
entries.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices presented offerings at the Great Temple without bringing out the spirit tablets.

entries.zh: 仲春薦冰，亦如之。
entries.en: Mid-spring ice offerings followed the same rule.
entries.literal: In mid-spring ice was presented—in the same manner.

entries.zh: 《貞觀禮》，祫享，功臣配享于廟庭，禘享則不配。
entries.en: The Zhenguan Ritual: at xia, meritorious ministers share in the temple court; at di they do not.
entries.literal: The Zhenguan Ritual: at xia sharing, meritorious ministers share in the temple court; at di they do not.

entries.zh: 當時令文，祫禘之日，功臣並得配享。
entries.en: At that time regulations allowed meritorious ministers to share on both xia and di days.
entries.literal: Then regulations had meritorious ministers share on both xia and di days.

entries.zh: 貞觀十六年，將行禘祭，有司請集禮官學士等議，太常卿韋挺等一十八人議曰：「古之王者，富有四海，而不朝夕上膳於宗廟者，患其禮過也。
entries.en: Zhenguan 16, before di sacrifice, offices requested ritualists and scholars to debate; Director Wei Ting and seventeen others argued: "Ancient kings possessing the four seas did not daily present food at the temple—fearing excessive ritual.
entries.literal: Zhenguan 16, before di sacrifice, offices requested ritualists and scholars to debate; Director Wei Ting and seventeen others argued: "Ancient kings possessing the four seas did not daily present food at the temple—fearing excessive ritual.

entries.zh: 故曰：'春秋祭祀，以時思之。
entries.en: Hence: Spring and Autumn sacrifice—think of them in season.
entries.literal: Hence: Spring and Autumn sacrifice—think of them in season.

entries.zh: '至於臣有大功享祿，其後孝子率禮，潔粢豐盛，禮、祀、烝、嘗，四時不輟，國家大祫，又得配焉。
entries.en: When a minister has great merit and enjoys emolument, later filial sons observe ritual with pure offerings in abundance—li, si, zheng, and xiang without cease through the four seasons; at the great xia he may also share.
entries.literal: When a minister has great merit and enjoys emolument, later filial sons observe ritual with pure offerings in abundance—li, si, zheng, and xiang without cease through the four seasons; at the great xia he may also share.

entries.zh: 所以昭明其勳，尊顯其德，以勸嗣臣也。
entries.en: Thus his merit is displayed and virtue honored to encourage successor ministers.
entries.literal: Thus his merit is displayed and virtue honored to encourage successor ministers.

entries.zh: 其禘及時享，功臣皆不應預。
entries.en: At di and seasonal sharing, meritorious ministers should not participate.
entries.literal: At di and seasonal sharing, meritorious ministers should not participate.

entries.zh: 故周禮六功之官，皆配大烝而已。
entries.en: Thus in Zhou ritual officials of the six merits share only at the great zheng.
entries.literal: Thus in Zhou ritual officials of the six merits share only at the great zheng.

entries.zh: 先儒皆取大烝為祫祭。
entries.en: Former scholars all take great zheng as the xia sacrifice.
entries.literal: Former scholars all take great zheng as the xia sacrifice.

entries.zh: 高堂隆、庾蔚之等多遵鄭學，未有將為時享。
entries.en: Gao Tanglong, Yu Weizhi, and others mostly follow Zheng Xuan's school—none took it as seasonal sharing.
entries.literal: Gao Tanglong, Yu Weizhi, and others mostly follow Zheng Xuan's school—none took it as seasonal sharing.

entries.zh: 又漢、魏祫祀，皆在十月，晉朝禮官，欲用孟秋殷祭，左僕射孔安國啟彈，坐免者不一。
entries.en: Again, Han and Wei xia sacrifices were all held in the tenth month. Jin ritual officers wished to use the mid-autumn yin sacrifice; Left Vice Director Kong Anguo memorialized impeachment, and more than one was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: Again, Han and Wei xia sacrifices were all held in the tenth month. Jin ritual officers wished to use the mid-autumn yin sacrifice; Left Vice Director Kong Anguo memorialized impeachment, and more than one was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 梁初誤禘功臣，左丞何佟之駁議，武帝允而依行。
entries.en: Early in Liang, meritorious ministers were mistakenly included in the di sacrifice; Left Assistant Minister He Tongzhi submitted a rebutting deliberation, and Emperor Wu approved and followed it.
entries.literal: Early in Liang, meritorious ministers were mistakenly included in the di sacrifice; Left Assistant Minister He Tongzhi submitted a rebutting deliberation, and Emperor Wu approved and followed it.

entries.zh: 降洎周、齊，俱遵此禮。
entries.en: Down through Zhou and Qi, all followed this rite.
entries.literal: Down through Zhou and Qi, all followed this rite.

entries.zh: 竊以五年再殷，合諸天道，一大一小，通人雅論，小則人臣不預，大則兼及功臣。
entries.en: Your subject holds that two yin sacrifices in five years accord with Heaven's Way—a great and a small; refined scholars agree that in the small, ministers do not participate, while in the great, meritorious ministers are also included.
entries.literal: Your subject holds that two yin sacrifices in five years accord with Heaven's Way—a great and a small; refined scholars agree that in the small, ministers do not participate, while in the great, meritorious ministers are also included.

entries.zh: 今禮禘無功臣，誠謂禮不可易。」
entries.en: Now the rite has di without meritorious ministers; your subject truly holds the rite cannot be altered."
entries.literal: Now the rite has di without meritorious ministers; your subject truly holds the rite cannot be altered."

entries.zh: 乃詔改令從禮。
entries.en: An edict ordered the rules brought into line with ritual.
entries.literal: An edict then ordered the regulations changed to follow the rite.

entries.zh: 至開元中改修禮，復令禘祫俱以功臣配饗焉。
entries.en: When Kaiyuan revised the rites, di and xia again both assigned meritorious ministers accompanying offerings.
entries.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, when the rites were revised, di and xia were again both made to include meritorious ministers in accompanying offerings.

entries.zh: 志第六禮儀六
entries.en: Treatise 6: Rites 6.
entries.literal: Treatise Six, Rites Six.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，遵貞觀故事，務在恤刑。
entries.en: When Gaozong ascended the throne, he followed the Zhenguan precedents and strove to show compassion in the administration of justice.
entries.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, he followed the precedents of Zhenguan, striving to show compassion in punishments.

entries.zh: 嘗問大理卿唐臨在獄系囚之數，臨對曰：「見囚五十餘人，惟二人合死。」
entries.en: He once asked Grand Judge Tang Lin how many prisoners were detained. Lin replied, "There are somewhat more than fifty prisoners; only two merit the death penalty."
entries.literal: He once asked Grand Judge Tang Lin the number of prisoners detained in the prisons; Lin replied: "Prisoners currently seen are more than fifty persons; only two merit death."

entries.zh: 帝以囚數全少，怡然形於顏色。
entries.en: The emperor, pleased that the number of prisoners was so low, showed his satisfaction openly.
entries.literal: The emperor, because the number of prisoners was altogether few, showed contentment in his countenance.

entries.zh: 永徽初，敕太尉長孫無忌、司空李勣、左僕射于志寧、右僕射行成、侍中高季輔、黃門侍郎宇文節柳奭、右丞段寶玄、太常少卿令狐德棻、吏部侍郎高敬言、刑部侍郎劉燕客、給事中趙文恪，中書舍人李友益、少府丞張行實、大理丞元紹、太府丞王文端、刑部郎中賈敏行等，共撰定律令格式。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Yonghui era the emperor charged Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Vice Directors Yu Zhining and Xing Cheng, Attendant-in-ordinary Gao Jifu, Vice Directors Yu Wenjie and Liu Shi, Assistant Director Duan Baoxuan, Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Linghu Defen, Vice Director of Personnel Gao Jingyan, Vice Director of Justice Liu Yanke, Attending Gentleman Zhao Wenke, Secretariat drafter Li Youyi, Assistant Director Zhang Xingshi of the Court of Imperial Manufactories, Assistant Grand Judge Yuan Shao, Assistant Director Wang Wenduan of the Imperial Treasury, Bureau Director Jia Minxing of the Ministry of Justice, and others to compile the statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui, he ordered Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, Right Vice Director Xing Cheng, Attendant-in-ordinary Gao Jifu, Yellow Gate Vice Directors Yu Wenjie and Liu Shi, Right Assistant Director Duan Baoxuan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Linghu Defen, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Gao Jingyan, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Liu Yanke, Attending Gentleman Zhao Wenke, Secretariat Drafter Li Youyi, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Manufactories Zhang Xingshi, Assistant Grand Judge Yuan Shao, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Treasury Wang Wenduan, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Justice Jia Minxing, and others jointly to compile and fix statutes, ordinances, regulations, and forms.

entries.zh: 舊制不便者，皆隨刪改。
entries.en: Provisions of the old code found inconvenient were revised or deleted.
entries.literal: Where old institutions were inconvenient, all were deleted and revised as they went.

entries.zh: 遂分格為兩部：曹司常務為《留司格》，天下所共者為《散頒格》。
entries.en: The supplementary regulations were divided into two parts: routine bureau affairs became the Retained Bureau Regulations, and regulations applicable empire-wide became the Broadly Promulgated Regulations.
entries.literal: They then divided the regulations into two parts: routine affairs of the bureaus became the Retained Bureau Regulations; what was shared throughout the realm became the Broadly Promulgated Regulations.

entries.zh: 其《散頒格》下州縣，《留司格》但留本司行用焉。
entries.en: The Broadly Promulgated Regulations were distributed to prefectures and counties; the Retained Bureau Regulations were kept by the originating offices for their own use.
entries.literal: The Broadly Promulgated Regulations were sent down to prefectures and counties; the Retained Bureau Regulations were retained only by the originating offices for use.

entries.zh: 三年，詔曰：「律學未有定疏，每年所舉明法，遂無憑准。
entries.en: In the third year an edict declared, "Legal studies lack an authoritative commentary, leaving candidates for the legal examinations without a standard of reference.
entries.literal: In the third year, an edict said: "Legal studies have no fixed commentary; each year those presented for expertise in law thus have no basis for judgment.

entries.zh: 宜廣召解律人條義疏奏聞。
entries.en: Let scholars versed in the law be summoned to prepare commentaries on each article and submit them for imperial review.
entries.literal: It is fitting broadly to summon those who understand the law to set forth article meanings in commentary and memorialize for the throne's knowledge.

entries.zh: 仍使中書、門下監定。」
entries.en: The Secretariat and Chancellery were charged with supervising and approving the work."
entries.literal: They were also to have the Secretariat and Chancellery supervise and fix them."

entries.zh: 於是太尉趙國公無忌、司空英國公勣、尚書左僕射兼太子少師監修國史燕國公志寧、銀青光祿大夫刑部尚書唐臨、太中大夫守大理卿段寶玄、朝議大夫守尚書右丞劉燕客、朝議大夫守御史中丞賈敏行等，參撰《律疏》，成三十卷，四年十月奏之，頒於天下。
entries.en: Thereupon Wuji, Duke of Zhao and Grand Preceptor; Li Ji, Duke of Ying and Minister of Works; Xu Zhining, Duke of Yan, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and supervisor of the national history; Tang Lin, Minister of Justice; Duan Baoxuan, Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; Liu Yanke, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; Jia Minxing, Vice Censor-in-Chief; and others jointly drafted the Statutory Commentary in thirty scrolls, submitted it in the tenth month of the fourth year, and had it promulgated throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Thereupon Grand Preceptor Zhao, Duke of Zhao, Wuji; Minister of Works Li, Duke of Ying, Ji; Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince, supervising the compilation of the national history, Yan, Duke of Yan, Zhining; Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness with Silver Seal, Minister of Justice Tang Lin; Grand Master Duan Baoxuan, acting Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; Gentleman for Discussing Affairs Liu Yanke, acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; Gentleman for Discussing Affairs Jia Minxing, acting Vice Censor-in-Chief; and others jointly compiled the Statutory Commentary, completing thirty scrolls; in the tenth month of the fourth year they submitted it, and it was promulgated throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 自是斷獄者皆引疏分析之。
entries.en: Henceforth, all who adjudicated cases cited the commentary in their analysis.
entries.literal: From then on, those who decided cases all cited the commentary to analyze them.

entries.zh: 永徽五年五月，上謂侍臣曰：「獄訟繁多，皆由刑罰枉濫，故曰刑者成也，一成而不可變。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yonghui, the emperor told his ministers: "Prison cases and lawsuits abound, all because punishments are misapplied. As the saying goes, punishment means a settled judgment—once rendered, it must not be altered.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yonghui, the emperor said to his attendants: "Prison cases and lawsuits are numerous, all because punishments are wrongly applied; hence it is said that punishment means completion—once fixed it must not be changed.

entries.zh: 末代斷獄之人，皆以苛刻為明，是以秦氏網密秋荼，而獲罪者眾。
entries.en: In later ages, judges took harshness for clarity; thus the Qin wove its laws tight as autumn bitter herb, and multitudes were condemned.
entries.literal: Those who decided cases in later ages all took harsh severity as clarity; hence the Qin dynasty's nets were dense as autumn bitter herb, and those who incurred guilt were many.

entries.zh: 今天下無事，四海乂安，欲與公等共行寬政。
entries.en: Now that the realm is untroubled and the four seas at peace, I wish to join you in practicing lenient governance.
entries.literal: Now the realm is at peace and the four seas tranquil; I wish to practice lenient governance together with you.

entries.zh: 今日刑罰，得無枉濫乎？」
entries.en: Are there no wrongful applications in today's punishments?"
entries.literal: Today's punishments—are they not wrongly applied?"

entries.zh: 無忌對曰：「陛下欲得刑法寬平，臣下猶不識聖意。
entries.en: Wuji answered: "Your Majesty wishes the penal code to be lenient and fair, yet your officials still fail to grasp your intent.
entries.literal: Wuji replied: "Your Majesty wishes to have the penal code lenient and equitable, yet your subjects still do not understand the sage intent.

entries.zh: 此法弊來已久，非止今日。
entries.en: These abuses of the law have persisted for a long time; they did not begin only today.
entries.literal: These evils in the law have long persisted; they did not begin only today.

entries.zh: 若情在體國，即共號癡人，意在深文，便稱好吏。
entries.en: If one sought the welfare of the state, all would call him a fool; if one pursued harsh textual penalties, he was hailed as a capable official.
entries.literal: If one's feeling lay in serving the state, together they would call one a fool; if one's intent lay in strict textual construction of charges, one was called a good official.

entries.zh: 所以罪雖合杖，必欲遣徒，理有可生，務入於死，非憎前人，陷於死刑。
entries.en: Thus though an offense merited beating, they would push for penal servitude; though logic allowed sparing a life, they pressed for death—not from personal hatred, but to trap the accused in a capital sentence.
entries.literal: Therefore though the offense warranted the cudgel, they would insist on banishment; though reason allowed life, they strove to put one to death—not from hatred of the person, but to ensnare him in the death penalty.

entries.zh: 陛下矜而令放，法司亦宜固請，但陛下喜怒不妄加於人，刑罰自然適中。」
entries.en: When Your Majesty shows mercy and orders release, the courts should press their petitions as well; if Your Majesty does not capriciously vent favor or wrath upon others, punishments will naturally be balanced."
entries.literal: When Your Majesty pities and orders release, the law officers ought likewise to press their petitions firmly; only if Your Majesty does not capriciously impose joy or anger upon people will punishments naturally become fitting."

entries.zh: 上以為然。
entries.en: The emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The emperor considered this correct.

entries.zh: 永徽六年七月，上謂侍臣曰：「律通比附，條例太多。」
entries.en: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yonghui, the emperor told his ministers: "The statutes rely too heavily on analogical application, and the articles are too numerous."
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yonghui, the emperor said to his attendants: "The statutes rely extensively on analogical application, and the articles are too numerous."

entries.zh: 左僕射志寧等對：「舊律多比附斷事，乃稍難解。
entries.en: Left Vice Director Zhining and others answered: "The old statutes relied heavily on analogical judgment, which made cases somewhat difficult to understand.
entries.literal: Left Vice Director Zhining and others replied: "The old statutes relied much on analogical judgment in deciding cases, which was somewhat hard to understand.

entries.zh: 科條極眾，數至三千。
entries.en: The statutory articles were extremely numerous, numbering as many as three thousand.
entries.literal: The statutory articles were extremely numerous, reaching three thousand in count.

entries.zh: 隋日再定，惟留五百。
entries.en: Under the Sui they were revised again, leaving only five hundred articles.
entries.literal: The Sui daily revised and fixed them again, retaining only five hundred.

entries.zh: 以事類相似者，比附科斷。
entries.en: Similar cases were adjudicated by analogical application of the relevant articles.
entries.literal: Similar matters were punished by analogical application of articles.

entries.zh: 今日所停，即是參取隋律修易。
entries.en: The code now in force was revised with reference to the Sui statutes.
entries.literal: What stops today is precisely taking the Sui statutes as reference for revision.

entries.zh: 條章既少，極成省便。」
entries.en: With so few articles and chapters, the code is far more convenient and economical."
entries.literal: Since the articles and chapters are few, they are extremely convenient and economical."

entries.zh: 志第三十刑法
entries.en: Treatise 30: Punishment and Law
entries.literal: Treatise 30: Punishment and Law

entries.zh: 尋與中書侍郎褚遂良受詔重撰《晉書》，於是奏取太子左庶子許敬宗、中書舍人來濟、著作郎陸元仕、劉子翼、前雍州刺史令狐德棻、太子舍人李義府、薛元超、起居郎上官儀等八人，分功撰錄，以臧榮緒《晉書》爲主，參考諸家，甚爲詳洽。
entries.en: Soon afterward he and Vice Director of the Secretariat Chu Suiliang were ordered to rewrite the Book of Jin. He asked that eight men share the work: Xu Jingzong, Left Mentor of the Crown Prince; Lai Ji, Drafter of the Secretariat; the editorial directors Lu Yuanshi and Liu Ziyi; Linghu Defen, former Prefect of Yongzhou; the crown prince's secretaries Li Yifu and Xue Yuanchao; and the court diarist Shangguan Yi. They took Zang Rongxu's Book of Jin as the base, compared the other traditions, and made a full and careful text.
entries.literal: Soon after, together with Vice Director of the Secretariat Chu Suiliang, he received an edict to rewrite the Book of Jin; he then memorialized to take eight men—Xu Jingzong, Left Mentor of the Crown Prince; Lai Ji, Drafter of the Secretariat; Lu Yuanshi and Liu Ziyi, Editorial Directors; Linghu Defen, former Prefect of Yongzhou; Li Yifu and Xue Yuanchao, Secretaries of the Crown Prince; and Shangguan Yi, Court Diarist—to divide the work of compiling the record, taking Zang Rongxu's Book of Jin as the principal text and consulting the various other families, and it was very detailed and complete.

entries.zh: 然史官多是文詠之士，好採詭謬碎事，以廣異聞；
entries.en: But most of the historians were men of verse, fond of gathering strange, dubious scraps to swell the store of oddities;
entries.literal: Yet the historians were mostly men of literary verse, fond of gathering strange, false, and trivial matters in order to broaden curious hearsay;

entries.zh: 又所評論，競爲綺豔，不求篤實，由是頗爲學者所譏。
entries.en: and their judgments vied in ornate color rather than solid truth, so scholars rather mocked the work.
entries.literal: and the comments they made competed in ornate beauty and did not seek solid substance; for this they were rather ridiculed by scholars.

entries.zh: 唯李淳風深明星曆，善於著述，所修《天文》、《律曆》、《五行》三志，最可觀採。
entries.en: Only Li Chunfeng knew the stars and the calendar thoroughly and wrote well. His three treatises—Heavenly Patterns, Pitch-pipes and the Calendar, and the Five Phases—are the parts most worth reading.
entries.literal: Only Li Chunfeng was deeply versed in the stars and the calendar and skilled at writing; the three treatises he compiled—Heavenly Patterns, Pitch-pipes and the Calendar, and the Five Phases—are the most worth viewing and adopting.

entries.zh: 太宗自著宣、武二帝及陸機、王羲之四論，於是總題云「御撰」。
entries.en: Taizong himself wrote the four discourses on Emperors Xuan and Wu and on Lu Ji and Wang Xizhi, and the whole work was then titled 'Imperially Compiled.'
entries.literal: Taizong himself wrote the four discourses on Emperors Xuan and Wu and on Lu Ji and Wang Xizhi, and thereupon the work was titled as a whole 'Imperially Compiled.'

entries.zh: 至二十年，書成，凡一百三十捲，詔藏於秘府，頒賜加級各有差。
entries.en: In the twentieth year the book was finished, one hundred thirty juan in all. An edict stored it in the imperial library, and gifts and promotions were given in differing degrees.
entries.literal: By the twentieth year the book was completed, in all one hundred thirty scrolls; an edict stored it in the secret archives, and grants and advancements of rank were each according to difference.

entries.zh: 武德八年，慶州總管楊文幹作亂，辭連東宮，歸罪於淹及王珪、韋挺等，並流於越巂。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Wude, Area Commander Yang Wengan of Qingzhou rebelled; his words implicated the Eastern Palace, and blame was laid on Yan together with Wang Gui, Wei Ting, and others; all were sent into exile in Yuexi.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Wude, Area Commander Yang Wengan of Qingzhou rebelled; his words implicated the Eastern Palace, and blame was laid on Yan together with Wang Gui, Wei Ting, and others; all were sent into exile in Yuexi.

entries.zh: 太宗知淹非罪，贈以黃金三百兩。
entries.en: Taizong knew Yan was not guilty and sent him three hundred bolts of yellow gold.
entries.literal: Taizong knew Yan was not guilty and sent him three hundred bolts of yellow gold.

entries.zh: 及即位，徵拜御史大夫，封安吉郡公，賜實封四百戸。
entries.en: When Taizong took the throne, Yan was summoned as Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed Duke of Anji, and granted a substantial fief of four hundred households.
entries.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Yan was summoned as Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed Duke of Anji, and granted a substantial fief of four hundred households.

entries.zh: 以淹多識典故，特詔東宮儀式簿領，並取淹節度。
entries.en: Because Yan knew many precedents and statutes, a special edict took the Eastern Palace's ritual forms and ledgers and had Yan direct them all.
entries.literal: Because Yan knew many precedents and statutes, a special edict took the Eastern Palace's ritual forms and ledgers and had Yan direct them all.

entries.zh: 尋判吏部尚書，參議朝政。
entries.en: Soon he was assigned Minister of Personnel and took part in deliberating court governance.
entries.literal: Soon he was assigned Minister of Personnel and took part in deliberating court governance.

entries.zh: 前後表薦四十餘人，後多知名者。
entries.en: Before and after he submitted memorials recommending more than forty men; many later became well known.
entries.literal: Before and after he submitted memorials recommending more than forty men; many later became well known.

entries.zh: 房玄齡 玄齡子遺直 遺愛 杜如晦 弟楚客 叔淹
entries.en: Fang Xuanling; his sons Yizhi and Yiai; Du Ruhui, with Ruhui's younger brother Chuke and uncle Yan.
entries.literal: Fang Xuanling; Xuanling's sons Yizhi and Yiai; Du Ruhui; younger brother Chuke; uncle Yan.

entries.zh: 褚遂良，散騎常侍亮之子也。
entries.en: Chu Suiliang was the son of Chu Liang, who had served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
entries.literal: Chu Suiliang was the son of the Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Chu Liang.

entries.zh: 太業末，隨父在隴右，薛舉僭號，署為通事舍人。
entries.en: In the final years of the Sui Daye era, he accompanied his father to Longyou. When Xue Ju declared himself ruler, he appointed Chu Suiliang Master of Communications.
entries.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, he followed his father to Longyou; Xue Ju usurped a title and appointed him Master of Communications.

entries.zh: 舉敗歸國，授秦州都督府鎧曹參軍。
entries.en: After Xue Ju's defeat, he submitted to the Tang and was appointed aide in the Armor Section of the Qinzhou Area Command headquarters.
entries.literal: When Ju was defeated he returned to the state and was granted the post of Army Armor Section aide in the Qinzhou Area Command.

entries.zh: 貞觀十年，自秘書郎遷起居郎。
entries.en: In 636, he was promoted from Secretary to Attendant of the Bedchamber.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan, he moved from Secretary to Attendant of the Bedchamber.

entries.zh: 遂良博涉文史，尤工隸書，父友歐陽詢甚重之。
entries.en: Suiliang was widely read in literature and history and was especially accomplished in clerical script. Ouyang Xun, a friend of his father, held him in high regard.
entries.literal: Suiliang was broadly versed in literature and history and especially skilled in clerical script; his father's friend Ouyang Xun greatly valued him.

entries.zh: 太宗嘗謂侍中魏徵曰：「虞世南死後，無人可以論書。」
entries.en: Emperor Taizong once told Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, "Since Yu Shinan died, I have had no one with whom to discuss calligraphy."
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor once said to the Palace Attendant Wei Zheng: "After Yu Shinan died, there is no one with whom to discuss calligraphy."

entries.zh: 徵曰：「褚遂良下筆遒勁，甚得王逸少體。」
entries.en: Wei Zheng replied, "Chu Suiliang's brushwork is vigorous and powerful, and it captures Wang Xizhi's style remarkably well."
entries.literal: Zheng said: "Chu Suiliang's brushwork is forceful and vigorous and very much captures Wang Yishao's style."

entries.zh: 太宗即日召令侍書。
entries.en: That same day, Taizong summoned him to serve at court as a calligrapher.
entries.literal: That same day the Taizong Emperor summoned him and ordered him to attend at writing.

entries.zh: 太宗嘗出御府金帛購求王羲之書跡，天下爭齎古書詣闕以獻，當時莫能辯其真偽，遂良備論所出，一無舛誤。
entries.en: Taizong once used gold and silk from the imperial treasury to buy works attributed to Wang Xizhi. People across the empire rushed ancient books to court as offerings, and at the time no one could tell which were genuine. Suiliang identified the provenance of each piece without a single mistake.
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor once issued gold and silk from the imperial treasury to purchase traces of Wang Xizhi's writing; all under Heaven vied to bring ancient books to the palace to present, and at the time none could distinguish true from false—Suiliang discussed in full their provenance, without a single error.

entries.zh: 十五年，詔有事太山，先幸洛陽，有星孛於太微，犯郎位。
entries.en: In 641, an edict ordered rites at Mount Tai. The emperor first visited Luoyang, where a comet appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure constellation and trespassed upon the Retinue stars.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, an edict ordered rites at Mount Tai; first he visited Luoyang; a broom star appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure and encroached on the Retinue positions.

entries.zh: 遂良言於太宗曰：「陛下撥亂反正，功超前烈，將告成東嶽，天下幸甚。
entries.en: Suiliang said to Taizong, "Your Majesty quelled chaos and restored order, and your achievements surpass those of former sages. You are about to complete the rites at the Eastern Peak, to the great fortune of the realm.
entries.literal: Suiliang spoke to the Taizong Emperor, saying: "Your Majesty has quelled disorder and restored the right, your achievements surpassing former worthies; you are about to announce completion at the Eastern Peak—the realm is greatly fortunate.

entries.zh: 而行至洛陽，彗星輒見，此或有所未允合者也。
entries.en: Yet upon reaching Luoyang, a comet appeared at once. This may mean that something is not yet in accord with Heaven's will.
entries.literal: Yet upon reaching Luoyang the comet promptly appeared—this perhaps indicates something not yet in accord.

entries.zh: 且漢武優柔數年，始行岱禮，臣愚伏願詳擇。」
entries.en: Moreover, Emperor Wu of Han deliberated for years before he finally performed the rites at Mount Tai. In my humble view, I beg Your Majesty to choose the timing with great care."
entries.literal: Moreover Emperor Wu of Han hesitated for several years before performing the Dai rites; this subject in his folly prostrates himself wishing Your Majesty to deliberate carefully."

entries.zh: 太宗深然之，下詔罷封禪之事。
entries.en: Taizong strongly agreed and issued an edict canceling the feng and shan ceremonies.
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor deeply approved this and issued an edict halting the feng and shan affairs.

entries.zh: 其年，遷諫議大夫，兼知起居事。
entries.en: That year he was promoted to Grand Master of Remonstrance and was also put in charge of the bedchamber records.
entries.literal: That year he was transferred to Grand Master of Remonstrance and concurrently managed bedchamber affairs.

entries.zh: 太宗嘗問：「卿知起居，記錄何事，大抵人君得觀之否？」
entries.en: Taizong once asked, "As keeper of the bedchamber records, what do you write down? May a ruler generally read them?"
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor once asked: "You manage the bedchamber records—what affairs do you record? Can a ruler in general view them?"

entries.zh: 遂良對曰：「今之起居，古左右史，書人君言事，且記善惡，以為鑑誡，庶幾人主不為非法。
entries.en: Suiliang answered, "The bedchamber records of today are the ancient Left and Right Historians. They record the ruler's words and deeds, noting good and evil alike, so that they may serve as a mirror and a warning and keep the sovereign from unlawful acts.
entries.literal: Suiliang replied: "Today's bedchamber records are the ancient Left and Right Historians; they write the ruler's words and affairs, and also record good and evil, to serve as mirror and warning, so that perhaps the sovereign will not do what is unlawful.

entries.zh: 不聞帝王躬自觀史。」
entries.en: I have never heard of an emperor reading his own history himself."
entries.literal: One does not hear of emperors and kings personally viewing the histories."

entries.zh: 太宗曰：「朕有不善，卿必記之耶？」
entries.en: Taizong said, "If I do something wrong, will you record that too?"
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor said: "If I have what is not good, will you surely record it?"

entries.zh: 遂良曰：「守道不如守官，臣職當載筆，君舉必記。」
entries.en: Suiliang said, "Upholding moral principle is less binding than upholding one's office. My duty is to hold the brush: whatever Your Majesty does, I must record it."
entries.literal: Suiliang said: "Keeping the Way is not as good as keeping one's office; this subject's duty is to bear the brush—whatever the ruler does must be recorded."

entries.zh: 黃門侍郎劉洎曰：「設令遂良不記，天下亦記之矣。」
entries.en: Yellow Gate Attendant Liu Ji said, "Even if Suiliang did not record it, the realm would still record it."
entries.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Liu Ji said: "Suppose Suiliang did not record it—the realm would still record it."

entries.zh: 太宗以為然。
entries.en: Taizong agreed that this was so.
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor considered this correct.

entries.zh: 時魏王為太宗所愛，禮秩如嫡。
entries.en: At that time the Prince of Wei was a favorite of Taizong, and his ceremonial standing was treated like that of the legitimate heir.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Wei was loved by the Taizong Emperor, his ritual rank like that of the legitimate heir.

entries.zh: 其年，太宗問侍臣曰：「當今國家何事最急？」
entries.en: That year Taizong asked his ministers, "What is the most urgent matter facing the state today?"
entries.literal: That year the Taizong Emperor asked his attending ministers: "In the state today, what matter is most urgent?"

entries.zh: 中書侍郎岑文本曰：「《傳》稱『導之以德，齊之以禮』，由斯而言。
entries.en: Central Secretariat Attendant Cen Wende said, "The Analects say, 'Lead them with virtue and harmonize them with ritual.' From that perspective—
entries.literal: Central Secretariat Attendant Cen Wende said: "The Documents say 'Lead them with virtue, regulate them with ritual'—speaking from this.

entries.zh: 禮義為急。」
entries.en: ritual and righteousness are the most urgent matters."
entries.literal: Ritual and righteousness are urgent."

entries.zh: 遂良進曰：「當今四方仰德，誰敢為非？
entries.en: Suiliang stepped forward and said, "Today the four quarters look up to Your Majesty's virtue. Who would dare do wrong?
entries.literal: Suiliang advanced and said: "Today the four quarters look up to virtue—who would dare do wrong?

entries.zh: 但太子、諸王，須有定分，陛下宜為萬代法以遺子孫。」
entries.en: But the Crown Prince and the other princes must have fixed ranks and roles. Your Majesty should establish a precedent for ten thousand generations to pass on to your descendants."
entries.literal: But the Crown Prince and the various princes must have fixed distinctions; Your Majesty should make a law for ten thousand generations to bequeath to descendants."

entries.zh: 太宗曰：「此言是也。
entries.en: Taizong said, "That is true.
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor said: "This statement is correct.

entries.zh: 朕年將五十，已覺衰怠。
entries.en: I am nearly fifty and already feel my strength failing.
entries.literal: I am nearing fifty years and already feel decline and weariness.

entries.zh: 既以長子守器東宮，弟及庶子數將五十，心常憂慮，頗在此耳。
entries.en: I have already installed my eldest son as heir in the Eastern Palace, but I have nearly fifty younger sons and sons by concubines. What weighs on my mind most is precisely this.
entries.literal: Having already installed the eldest son to guard the vessel in the Eastern Palace, younger brothers and sons by concubines number nearly fifty—I constantly worry in my heart, and it lies largely in this.

entries.zh: 但自古嫡庶無良佐，何嘗不傾敗國家？
entries.en: Yet since antiquity, when legitimate and illegitimate lines lacked good advisers, when did they not bring ruin upon a state?
entries.literal: Yet since antiquity legitimate and illegitimate lines without good assistants—when have they not overturned and ruined states?

entries.zh: 公等為朕搜訪賢德，以傅儲宮，爰及諸王，咸求正士。
entries.en: Search out worthy men for me to tutor the Heir Apparent, and find upright men for all the princes as well.
entries.literal: You gentlemen should for me search out the worthy and virtuous to tutor the Heir Apparent, and extending to the various princes, all seek upright men.

entries.zh: 且事人歲久，即分義情深，非意窺窬，多由此作。」
entries.en: Moreover, when men serve a prince for many years, their bond of loyalty grows deep. Unintended ambitions for the throne often arise from just such circumstances."
entries.literal: Moreover, serving a person for many years, then the bond of duty grows deep—unintended coveting of the throne often arises from this."

entries.zh: 於是限王府官僚不得過四考。
entries.en: Thereupon he limited officials in princely establishments to no more than four terms of service.
entries.literal: Thereupon he limited princely establishment officials to no more than four performance reviews.

entries.zh: 十七年，太宗問遂良曰：「舜造漆器，禹雕其俎，當時諫舜、禹者十餘人。
entries.en: In 643, Taizong asked Suiliang, "Shun made lacquer vessels, and Yu carved his sacrificial stands. More than ten men remonstrated with them at the time.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year the Taizong Emperor asked Suiliang: "Shun made lacquer vessels; Yu carved his sacrificial stands—at the time more than ten persons remonstrated with Shun and Yu.

entries.zh: 食器之間，苦諫何也？」
entries.en: Why such strenuous remonstrance over mere eating vessels?"
entries.literal: Among eating vessels, why such strenuous remonstrance?"

entries.zh: 遂良對曰：「雕琢害農事，纂組傷女工。
entries.en: Suiliang answered, "Carving and polishing harm farming, and brocade work injures women's labor.
entries.literal: Suiliang replied: "Carving and polishing harm agricultural affairs; brocade and embroidery injure women's work.

entries.zh: 首創奢淫，危亡之漸。
entries.en: To be the first to indulge in luxury is the first step on the road to ruin.
entries.literal: First creating extravagance and dissipation is the gradual approach of peril and ruin.

entries.zh: 漆器不已，必金為之；
entries.en: If lacquer vessels are not enough, one will make them of gold;
entries.literal: If lacquer vessels do not stop, they must be made of gold;

entries.zh: 金器不已，必玉為之。
entries.en: and if gold is not enough, one will make them of jade.
entries.literal: if gold vessels do not stop, they must be made of jade.

entries.zh: 所以諍臣必諫其漸，及其滿盈，無所復諫。」
entries.en: That is why remonstrating ministers must speak at the first sign of excess. Once luxury has overflowed, there is nothing left to remonstrate about."
entries.literal: Therefore remonstrating ministers must remonstrate at the gradual stage; when it reaches fullness and overflow, there is nothing further to remonstrate about."

entries.zh: 太宗以為然，因曰：「夫為人君，不憂萬姓而事奢淫，危亡之機可反掌而待也。」
entries.en: Taizong agreed and added, "For a ruler of men, to neglect the welfare of the people and pursue luxury instead is to invite ruin with a turn of the hand."
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor considered this correct and then said: "For one who is ruler of men, not to worry for the myriad people but to pursue extravagance and dissipation—the moment of peril and ruin can be awaited with a turn of the palm."

entries.zh: 時皇子年幼者多任都督、刺史，遂良上疏曰：「昔兩漢以郡國理人，除郡以外，分立諸子。
entries.en: At that time many young princes were appointed as area commanders and prefects. Suiliang submitted a memorial: "In the two Han dynasties, the realm was governed through commanderies and kingdoms. Apart from the commanderies, the emperor's sons were granted separate domains.
entries.literal: At the time many young princes were appointed area commanders and prefects; Suiliang submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly the two Han used commanderies and kingdoms to govern people; apart from commanderies they separately established the various sons.

entries.zh: 割土分疆，雜用周制。
entries.en: They divided territory and apportioned domains, mixing in institutions from the Zhou.
entries.literal: Dividing territory and apportioning borders, they mixed in Zhou institutions.

entries.zh: 皇唐州縣，祖依秦法。
entries.en: Great Tang's prefectures and counties follow the Qin model as their foundation.
entries.literal: Great Tang's prefectures and counties follow the Qin law as ancestor.

entries.zh: 皇子幼年，或授刺史，陛下豈不以王之骨肉，鎮扞四方？
entries.en: When princes are still young, some are made prefects. Does Your Majesty not intend your own flesh and blood to guard the four quarters?
entries.literal: When princes are young, some are granted prefectures—is not Your Majesty using the king's flesh and bone to guard and defend the four quarters?

entries.zh: 此之造制，道高前烈。
entries.en: In creating this system, Your Majesty's principle surpasses that of former sages.
entries.literal: This institution surpasses former worthies in principle.

entries.zh: 如臣愚見，有小未盡。
entries.en: In my humble view, however, one small matter remains incomplete.
entries.literal: In this subject's foolish view, there is something small not yet complete.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: What is it?
entries.literal: What is it?

entries.zh: 刺史郡帥，民仰以安。
entries.en: A prefect is the commander of a commandery, and the people depend on him for their security.
entries.literal: Prefects are commanders of commanderies; the people look up to them for security.

entries.zh: 得一善人，部內蘇息；
entries.en: With one good man in office, the district revives;
entries.literal: Obtain one good man and the district revives;

entries.zh: 遇一不善，合州勞弊。
entries.en: but with one bad man, the whole prefecture is worn down and exhausted.
entries.literal: meet one who is not good and the whole prefecture is worn and exhausted.

entries.zh: 是以人君愛恤百姓，常為擇賢。
entries.en: That is why a ruler who loves his people constantly selects worthy men for office.
entries.literal: Therefore the ruler of men loves and cherishes the hundred names and constantly selects the worthy for them.

entries.zh: 或稱河潤九里，京師蒙福；
entries.en: Some say that when a river nourishes the land for nine li, the capital shares in the blessing;
entries.literal: Some say the river moistens for nine li and the capital receives blessing;

entries.zh: 或人興歌詠，生為立祠。
entries.en: or the people sing his praises and build shrines to him while he still lives.
entries.literal: or the people rise in song and praise and while living build shrines for him.

entries.zh: 漢宣帝云：『與我共理者，惟良二千石。』
entries.en: Emperor Xuan of Han said, 'Those who govern with me are only good prefects.'
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han said: 'Those who govern with me are only good two-thousand-dan officials.'

entries.zh: 如臣愚見，陛下兒子內年齒尚幼、未堪臨人者，且留京師，教以經學。
entries.en: In my humble view, among Your Majesty's sons, those who are still too young to govern people should remain in the capital for now and be taught the classics.
entries.literal: In this subject's foolish view, among Your Majesty's sons those whose years are still young and not yet able to oversee people should for the present remain in the capital and be taught the classics.

entries.zh: 一則畏天之威，不敢犯禁；
entries.en: First, they will fear Heaven's majesty and not dare break the law;
entries.literal: First, they will fear Heaven's majesty and not dare violate prohibitions;

entries.zh: 二則觀見朝儀，自然成立。
entries.en: second, they will observe court ritual and naturally learn how to conduct themselves.
entries.literal: second, they will observe and see court ritual and naturally be formed.

entries.zh: 因此積習，自知為人。
entries.en: Through such accumulated habit, they will learn on their own how to be men.
entries.literal: Through this accumulated practice they will themselves know how to be human.

entries.zh: 審堪臨州，然後遣出。
entries.en: Only when they are truly fit to govern a prefecture should they be sent out.
entries.literal: When it is verified that they can oversee a prefecture, then send them out.

entries.zh: 臣謹按漢明、章、和三帝，能友愛於弟，自茲已降，取為準的。
entries.en: I respectfully note that Emperors Ming, Zhang, and He of Han were able to treat their younger brothers with affection. Let us take them as our standard from this point forward.
entries.literal: This subject respectfully notes that the Ming, Zhang, and He emperors of Han were able to be friendly and loving toward their younger brothers; from this down, take them as the standard.

entries.zh: 封立諸王，雖各有國土，年尚幼小者，召留京師，訓以禮法，垂以恩惠。
entries.en: When they enfeoffed the various kings, each received his own domain, but those who were still young were summoned to remain in the capital, instructed in ritual and law, and showered with favor.
entries.literal: Enfeoffing and establishing the various kings, although each had his own territory, those whose years were still young were summoned to remain in the capital, instructed in ritual and law, and bestowed with favor.

entries.zh: 訖三帝世，諸王數十百人，唯二王稍惡，自余餐和染教，皆為善人。
entries.en: Through the reigns of those three emperors, the princes numbered in the tens and hundreds. Only two princes turned out badly; the rest, nourished by harmony and shaped by instruction, all became good men.
entries.literal: Through the three emperors' reigns, the various kings numbered in the tens and hundreds—only two kings were somewhat bad; the rest, nourished by harmony and dyed by instruction, all became good men.

entries.zh: 則前事已驗，惟陛下詳察。」
entries.en: The precedent has already been tested. I beg Your Majesty to consider it carefully."
entries.literal: Then former affairs have already been verified—only may Your Majesty examine carefully."

entries.zh: 太宗深納之。
entries.en: Taizong accepted this advice wholeheartedly.
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor deeply accepted this.

entries.zh: 其年，太子承乾以罪廢，魏王泰入侍，太宗面許立為太子。
entries.en: That year Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed for his crimes. The Prince of Wei, Li Tai, attended the emperor in person, and Taizong openly promised to make him crown prince.
entries.literal: That year the Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed for crime; the Prince of Wei Tai entered attendance; the Taizong Emperor to his face promised to establish him as Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「昨青雀自投我懷云：『臣今日始得與陛下為子，更生之日也。
entries.en: He then told his ministers, "Yesterday the Green Sparrow threw himself into my arms and said, 'Today I have at last become Your Majesty's son in truth. It is like being born again.
entries.literal: He then said to his attending ministers: "Yesterday the Green Sparrow threw himself into my embrace, saying: 'Your subject today for the first time obtains to be a son with Your Majesty—it is a day of rebirth.

entries.zh: 臣唯有一子，臣百年之後，當為陛下殺之，傳國晉王。』
entries.en: I have only one son. After I die, I will kill him for Your Majesty's sake and pass the realm to the Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: Your subject has only one son; after Your subject's hundred years I shall for Your Majesty kill him and pass the state to the Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 父子之道，故當天性，我見其如此，甚憐之。」
entries.en: The bond between father and son is a matter of nature. When I saw him speak so, I was deeply moved.'"
entries.literal: The way of father and son ought by nature to be thus—I saw him like this and greatly pitied him.'"

entries.zh: 遂良進曰：「陛下失言。
entries.en: Suiliang stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty has spoken unwisely.
entries.literal: Suiliang advanced and said: "Your Majesty has misspoken.

entries.zh: 伏願審思，無令錯誤也。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to think this through carefully and not make a mistake.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself wishing Your Majesty to deliberate carefully and not let there be error.

entries.zh: 安有陛下百年之後，魏王執權為天下之主，而能殺其愛子，傳國於晉王者乎？
entries.en: After Your Majesty is gone, when the Prince of Wei holds power as ruler of the realm, would he truly kill his own beloved son and pass the throne to the Prince of Jin?
entries.literal: How could there be, after Your Majesty's hundred years, the Prince of Wei holding power as lord of all under Heaven yet able to kill his beloved son and pass the state to the Prince of Jin?

entries.zh: 陛下昔立承乾為太子，而復寵愛魏王，禮數或有逾於承乾者，良由嫡庶不分，所以至此。
entries.en: Your Majesty once made Chengqian crown prince, yet continued to favor the Prince of Wei, sometimes treating him with honors that exceeded Chengqian's. This came about because legitimate and illegitimate lines were not kept distinct.
entries.literal: Your Majesty formerly established Chengqian as Crown Prince, yet again showed favor to the Prince of Wei, ritual count sometimes exceeding Chengqian's—truly because legitimate and illegitimate were not distinguished, therefore it came to this.

entries.zh: 殷鑑不遠，足為龜鏡。
entries.en: The lesson of the recent past is close at hand and should serve as a mirror for Your Majesty.
entries.literal: The Yin mirror is not far—sufficient to serve as tortoise mirror.

entries.zh: 陛下今日既立魏王，伏願陛下別安置晉王，始得安全耳。」
entries.en: Now that Your Majesty has chosen the Prince of Wei, I beg Your Majesty to make separate arrangements for the Prince of Jin. Only then will he be safe."
entries.literal: Your Majesty today having already established the Prince of Wei, I prostrate myself wishing Your Majesty to separately settle the Prince of Jin—only then can there be security."

entries.zh: 太宗涕泗交下曰：「我不能。」
entries.en: Taizong wept openly and said, "I cannot do that."
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor, tears and mucus crossing his face, said: "I cannot."

entries.zh: 即日召長孫無忌、房玄齡、李勣與遂良等定策，立晉王為皇太子。
entries.en: That same day he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, Suiliang, and others to settle the succession and install the Prince of Jin as crown prince.
entries.literal: That same day he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, and Suiliang and others to fix the policy and establish the Prince of Jin as Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 時頻有飛雉集於宮殿之內，太宗問群臣曰：「是何祥也？」
entries.en: At that time wild pheasants were frequently seen gathering inside the palace. Taizong asked his ministers, "What omen does this signify?"
entries.literal: At the time pheasants frequently gathered within the palace halls; the Taizong Emperor asked his ministers: "What omen is this?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「昔秦文公時，有童子化為雉，雌者鳴於陳倉，雄者鳴於南陽。
entries.en: They answered, "In the time of Duke Wen of Qin, a boy transformed into a pheasant. The female cried at Chencang, and the male cried at Nanyang.
entries.literal: They replied: "Formerly in the time of Duke Wen of Qin, a boy transformed into a pheasant; the female cried at Chencang, the male cried at Nanyang.

entries.zh: 童子曰：得雄者王，得雌者霸。
entries.en: The boy said, 'He who obtains the male will become king; he who obtains the female will become hegemon.'
entries.literal: The boy said: He who obtains the male will be king; he who obtains the female will be hegemon.

entries.zh: 文公遂以為寶雞。
entries.en: Duke Wen thereupon took it as an auspicious sign from Chen.
entries.literal: Duke Wen thereupon took it as the treasured cock of Chen.

entries.zh: 後漢光武得雄，遂起南陽而有四海。
entries.en: Later, Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male pheasant, rose from Nanyang, and won the realm.
entries.literal: Later Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male and thereupon rose from Nanyang to possess the four seas.

entries.zh: 陛下舊封秦王，故雄雉見於秦地，此所以彰表明德也。」
entries.en: Your Majesty was once enfeoffed as Prince of Qin, so the male pheasant has appeared in Qin territory. This is a sign that your bright virtue is being made manifest."
entries.literal: Your Majesty was formerly enfeoffed as Prince of Qin, therefore the male pheasant appeared in Qin territory—this is how bright virtue is made manifest."

entries.zh: 太宗悅曰：「立身之道，不可無學，遂良博識，深可重也。」
entries.en: Taizong said with pleasure, "The way to establish oneself in the world cannot be learned without study. Suiliang is deeply learned and truly worthy of respect."
entries.literal: The Taizong Emperor, pleased, said: "The Way of establishing oneself cannot be without learning—Suiliang is broadly knowledgeable and deeply to be valued."

entries.zh: 尋授太子賓客。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was appointed Guest of the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Shortly he was appointed Guest of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 臣聞有國家者譬諸身，兩京等於心腹，四境方乎手足，他方絕域，若在身外。
entries.en: I have heard that one who possesses a state may be compared to the body. The two capitals are like the heart and belly, the four borders like the hands and feet, and other regions and distant realms are as if outside the body.
entries.literal: This subject has heard that one who has a state is compared to the body—the two capitals equal the heart and belly, the four borders are like the hands and feet, other regions and distant realms are as if outside the body.

entries.zh: 臣近於坐下，伏奉口敕，布語臣下，雲自欲伐遼。
entries.en: Recently below Your seat I received an oral edict, promulgated to your ministers below, saying that you yourself wish to attack Liao.
entries.literal: This subject recently below Your seat, prostrate received oral edict, promulgated words to ministers below, saying you yourself wish to attack Liao.

entries.zh: 臣數夜思量，不達其理。
entries.en: For several nights I have pondered this and cannot understand its rationale.
entries.literal: This subject for several nights pondered and could not reach its principle.

entries.zh: 高麗王為陛下之所立，莫離支輒殺其主，陛下討逆收地，斯實乘機。
entries.en: The King of Goryeo was established by Your Majesty. Yeon Gaesomun abruptly killed his lord. For Your Majesty to punish the rebel and recover the territory is truly to seize the opportune moment.
entries.literal: The King of Goryeo was established by Your Majesty; Yeon Gaesomun abruptly killed his lord—Your Majesty punishing rebellion and recovering territory is truly seizing the opportunity.

entries.zh: 關東賴陛下德澤，久無征戰，但命二、三勇將，發兵四、五萬，飛石輕梯，取如回掌。
entries.en: Guandong relies on Your Majesty's virtue and grace and has long been free of warfare. You need only command two or three brave generals and send forth forty or fifty thousand troops. With flying stones and light ladders, taking it would be like turning the palm.
entries.literal: Guandong relies on Your Majesty's virtue and favor, long without campaigns and battles—only command two or three brave generals, send forth forty or fifty thousand troops, flying stones and light ladders, taking it like turning the palm.

entries.zh: 夫聖人有作，必履常規，貴能克平凶亂，駕馭才傑。
entries.en: When a sage acts, he must follow constant norms, valuing the ability to overcome fierce disorder and to drive and control talented heroes.
entries.literal: The sage when he acts must tread constant norms, valuing the ability to overcome and pacify fierce disorder and to drive and control talented heroes.

entries.zh: 惟陛下弘兩儀之道，扇三五之風，提厲人物，皆思效命。
entries.en: Your Majesty alone expands the Way of the Two Principles and fans the wind of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, lifting and sharpening men of talent, all of whom wish to offer their lives.
entries.literal: Only Your Majesty expands the Way of the Two Principles, fans the wind of the Three and Five, lifts and sharpens men and things—all think to offer their lives.

entries.zh: 昔侯君集、李靖，所謂庸夫，猶能掃萬里之高昌，平千載之突厥，皆是陛下發蹤指示，聲歸聖明。
entries.en: Formerly Hou Junji and Li Jing, so-called mediocre men, still swept Gaochang ten thousand li away and pacified the Turks of a thousand years—all because Your Majesty set them on the track and gave directions, and the credit returned to your sagely brilliance.
entries.literal: Formerly Hou Junji and Li Jing, so-called mediocre men, still could sweep ten-thousand-li Gaochang and pacify thousand-year Turks—all were Your Majesty issuing tracks and giving directions, reputation returning to sagely brilliance.

entries.zh: 臣旁求史籍，訖乎近代，為人之主，無自伐遼，人臣往征，則有之矣。
entries.en: I have searched the histories on every side down to recent times. As ruler of men, none has personally campaigned against Liao, though as ministers going on campaign there have been such cases.
entries.literal: This subject searched history on every side down to recent times—as ruler of men, none personally campaigned against Liao; as ministers going on campaign, there have been such cases.

entries.zh: 漢朝則荀彘、楊僕，魏代則毋丘儉、王頎；
entries.en: In the Han dynasty there were Xun Yi and Yang Pu; in the Wei era there were Wuqiu Jian and Wang Qi;
entries.literal: Han dynasty then Xun Yi and Yang Pu; Wei era then Wuqiu Jian and Wang Qi;

entries.zh: 司馬懿猶為人臣，慕容真僭號之子，皆為其主長驅高麗，虜其人民，削平城壘。
entries.en: Sima Yi was still a minister of men, and Murong Zhen was the son of a usurper—all of them for their lords drove deep into Goryeo, captured its people, and leveled walls and ramparts.
entries.literal: Sima Yi was still a minister of men; Murong Zhen was a son who usurped a title—all for their lords drove far into Goryeo, captured its people, and leveled walls and ramparts.

entries.zh: 陛下立功同於天地，美化包於古昔，自當超邁於百王，豈止俯同於六子？
entries.en: Your Majesty's achievements equal Heaven and Earth, and your civilizing transformation embraces antiquity. You should naturally surpass the hundred kings—how could you merely bow to match the six sons?
entries.literal: Your Majesty's establishment of achievement equals Heaven and Earth, civilizing transformation embraces antiquity—you should naturally surpass the hundred kings, how only bow to match the six sons?

entries.zh: 陛下昔翦平寇逆，大有爪牙，年齒未衰，猶堪任用，匪唯陛下之所使，亦何行而不克。
entries.en: Your Majesty formerly cut down bandit rebels and greatly possessed capable men. Your years are not yet declined and they are still fit for employment. Not only can Your Majesty employ them—what undertaking would they not succeed in?
entries.literal: Your Majesty formerly cut down and pacified bandit rebels, greatly possessing claws and fangs; years not yet declined, still fit for employment—not only those Your Majesty can employ, what undertaking would not succeed?

entries.zh: 方今太子新立，年實幼少，自余籓屏，陛下所知。
entries.en: Just now the crown prince has been newly established and is truly young. As for the rest of the princely screen, Your Majesty knows them well.
entries.literal: Just now the Crown Prince is newly established, years truly young and small; the rest of the screen of vassals Your Majesty knows.

entries.zh: 今一旦棄金湯之全，渡遼海之外，臣忽三思，煩愁並集。
entries.en: Now, in a single morning, to abandon the completeness of metal and boiling water and cross beyond the Liao Sea—when I think of it three times over, worry and sorrow gather together.
entries.literal: Now in one morning abandoning the completeness of metal and boiling water, crossing beyond the Liao Sea—this subject suddenly thrice thinks, worry and sorrow together gather.

entries.zh: 大魚依於巨海，神龍據於川泉，此謂人君不可輕而遠也。
entries.en: Great fish rely on the vast sea, and the divine dragon occupies streams and springs. This means that the ruler of men cannot lightly go far from home.
entries.literal: Great fish rely on the vast sea; divine dragon occupies streams and springs—this means the ruler of men cannot be lightly made distant.

entries.zh: 且以長遼之左，或遇霖淫，水潦騰波，平地數尺。
entries.en: Moreover, along the left bank of the long Liao, one may meet prolonged rain, when floods surge in waves and the level ground stands several feet deep.
entries.literal: Moreover along the left of long Liao, one may meet prolonged rain; floods surge in waves, level ground several feet.

entries.zh: 夫帶方、玄菟，海途深渺，非萬乘所宜行踐。
entries.en: Daifang and Xuantu lie along a sea route deep and vast—not a path that the Son of Heaven should tread.
entries.literal: Daifang and Xuantu—the sea route deep and vast, not what ten-thousand chariots should tread.

entries.zh: 東京太原，謂之中地，東捴可以為聲勢，西指足以摧延陀，其於西京，逕路非遠，為其節度，以設軍謀，系莫離支頸，獻皇家之廟。
entries.en: The Eastern Capital at Taiyuan is called the central land. A gathering to the east can serve as momentum, and a thrust to the west suffices to crush Xueyantuo. As for the Western Capital, the direct route is not far. Make dispositions from there, set military plans, tie Yeon Gaesomun by the neck, and present his head in the imperial clan temple.
entries.literal: Eastern Capital Taiyuan is called the central land—eastward gathering can serve as sound and momentum, westward pointing suffices to crush Xueyantuo; as for Western Capital, the direct route is not far, make dispositions for it, set military plans, tie Yeon Gaesomun's neck, present to the imperial clan temple.

entries.zh: 此實處安全之上計，社稷之根本，特乞天慈，一垂省察。
entries.en: This is truly the best plan for dwelling in security and the root of the altars of state. I specially beg your heavenly kindness to examine it once.
entries.literal: This is truly the upper plan for dwelling in security, the root of altars of soil and grain—I specially beg heavenly kindness, once to extend examination.

entries.zh: 臣聞古者哲後，必先事華夏而後夷狄，務廣德化，不事遐荒。
entries.en: I have heard that in antiquity wise rulers first attended to the Hua-Xia and afterward to the Yi-Di, striving to extend virtue and transformation rather than serving distant wilds.
entries.literal: This subject has heard that in antiquity wise rulers first attended to the Hua-Xia and afterward to the Yi-Di, striving to extend virtue and transformation, not serving distant wilds.

entries.zh: 是以周宣薄伐，至境而止；
entries.en: Therefore King Xuan of Zhou made a light campaign, reaching the border and stopping;
entries.literal: Therefore King Xuan of Zhou made a light campaign, reaching the border and stopping;

entries.zh: 始皇遠塞，中國分離。
entries.en: the First Emperor made distant barriers, and China was divided.
entries.literal: the First Emperor made distant barriers, and China was divided.

entries.zh: 漢武負文、景之聚財，玩士馬之餘力，始通西域，初置校尉。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Han relied on the accumulated wealth of Emperors Wen and Jing and played with the remaining strength of soldiers and horses. He first opened the Western Regions and first established commandants.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Han relied on Wen and Jing's accumulated wealth, played with remaining strength of soldiers and horses, first opened the Western Regions, first established commandants.

entries.zh: 軍旅連出，將三十年。
entries.en: Armies went forth in succession for nearly thirty years.
entries.literal: Armies and brigades went forth in succession for nearly thirty years.

entries.zh: 復得天馬於宛城，采蒲萄於安息。
entries.en: He obtained heavenly horses at Wancheng and gathered grapes at Parthia.
entries.literal: He again obtained heavenly horses at Wancheng and gathered grapes at Parthia.

entries.zh: 而海內虛竭，生人失所，租及六畜，算至舟車，因之凶年，盜賊並起，搜粟都尉桑弘羊復希主意，遣士卒遠田輪台，築城以威西域。
entries.en: Yet the realm was emptied and exhausted, the living lost their homes, levies reached even the six livestock, and assessments reached boats and chariots. Because of this there were famine years and bandits rose together. Search-for-Grain Commandant Sang Hongyang again hoped for the ruler's intent and sent soldiers to farm Luntai from afar and build walls to awe the Western Regions.
entries.literal: Yet within the seas was emptied and exhausted, living people lost their places, levies reaching the six livestock, assessments reaching boats and chariots—because of this there were famine years, bandits and robbers rose together; Search-for-Grain Commandant Sang Hongyang again hoped for the ruler's intent, sent soldiers to farm Luntai from afar, built walls to awe the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 帝翻然追悔，情發於中，棄輪台之野，下哀痛之詔，人神感悅，海內乃康。
entries.en: The emperor suddenly turned and regretted, feeling arising from within. He abandoned the fields of Luntai and issued the edict of mournful pain. Men and spirits were moved and pleased, and the realm then knew peace.
entries.literal: The Emperor suddenly turned and regretted, feeling arising from within, abandoned the fields of Luntai, issued the edict of mournful pain—men and spirits were moved and pleased, within the seas then was peace.

entries.zh: 向使武帝復用弘羊之言，天下生靈皆盡之矣。
entries.en: If Emperor Wu had again used Hongyang's words, all living beings under Heaven would have been exhausted.
entries.literal: If formerly Emperor Wu had again used Hongyang's words, all living spirits under Heaven would have been exhausted.

entries.zh: 是以光武中興，不逾蔥嶺，孝章即位，都護來歸。
entries.en: Therefore Guangwu's restoration did not cross the Onion Range, and when Emperor Zhang assumed the throne, the Protector came to submit.
entries.literal: Therefore Guangwu's restoration did not cross the Onion Range; when Emperor Zhang assumed the throne, the Protector came to submit.

entries.zh: 古之聖王，立諫鼓，設謗木，冀欲聞逆耳之言，甘苦口之議，發揚大化，裨益洪猷，垂令譽於將來，播休聲於不朽者也。
entries.en: The sage kings of antiquity established remonstrance drums and set up slander posts, hoping to hear ear-offending words and welcome bitter counsel, to extend great transformation and benefit vast plans, to hang fine reputation on the future and spread excellent fame for eternity.
entries.literal: The sage kings of antiquity established remonstrance drums and set up slander posts, hoping to hear ear-offending words and sweet bitter-mouth discussions, to extend great transformation and benefit vast plans, to hang fine reputation on the future and spread excellent sound in imperishability.

entries.zh: 伏見詔書以褚遂良為潭州都督，臣夙夜思之，用增感激。
entries.en: I see the edict making Chu Suiliang Area Commander of Tanzhou. Day and night I have pondered it, and my emotion and gratitude have only increased.
entries.literal: I prostrate and see the edict making Chu Suiliang Area Commander of Tanzhou—this subject day and night pondered it, thereby increasing emotion and gratitude.

entries.zh: 臣識慚知遠，業謝通經，載撫愚情，誠為未可。
entries.en: My knowledge is ashamed before knowing the far, and my craft declines before mastering the classics. Bearing my foolish feelings, I truly cannot remain silent.
entries.literal: This subject's knowledge is ashamed before knowing the far, my craft declines before mastering the classics—bearing and stroking foolish feeling, truly it cannot be done.

entries.zh: 遂良運偶昇平，道昭前烈，束髮從宦，方淹累稔。
entries.en: Suiliang's fate met an age of ascending peace, and his Way illuminated former worthies. From binding his hair he followed office, submerged in service for many accumulated years.
entries.literal: Suiliang's fate met ascending peace, his Way illuminated former worthies; binding hair he followed office, just submerged for accumulated years.

entries.zh: 趨侍陛下，俄歷歲年，不聞涓滴之愆，常睹勤勞之效。
entries.en: Hastening to attend Your Majesty, he has shortly passed many years. Not a drop's fault has been heard of him, and the effects of his diligent toil are constantly seen.
entries.literal: Hastening to attend Your Majesty, shortly passing years and years—not heard a drop's fault, constantly seen diligent toil's effect.

entries.zh: 竭忠誠於早歲，罄直道於茲年。
entries.en: He exhausted his loyalty in early years and spent the straight Way in this year.
entries.literal: He exhausted loyalty in early years, spent the straight Way in this year.

entries.zh: 體國忘家，捐身徇物，風霜其操，鐵石其心。
entries.en: He embodied the state and forgot his family, casting away his body to follow public affairs. Wind and frost were his conduct, and iron and stone his heart.
entries.literal: Embodying the state and forgetting family, casting away the body to follow affairs—wind and frost his conduct, iron and stone his heart.

entries.zh: 誠可重於皇明，詎專方於曩昔？
entries.en: Truly he can be valued in your imperial brilliance—how could he be valued only in former times?
entries.literal: Truly he can be valued in imperial brilliance—how only specialized in former times?

entries.zh: 且先帝納之於帷幄，寄之以心膂，德逾水石，義冠舟車，公家之利，言無不可。
entries.en: Moreover the former emperor admitted him into the tent curtains and entrusted him with heart and backbone. His virtue exceeded water and stone, and his righteousness crowned boats and chariots. For the public family's benefit, in speech nothing was not permissible.
entries.literal: Moreover the former emperor admitted him into the tent curtains, entrusted him with heart and backbone—virtue exceeding water and stone, righteousness crowning boats and chariots; the public family's benefit, in speech nothing not permissible.

entries.zh: 及纏悲四海，遏密八音，竭忠國家，親承顧托，一德無二，千古懍然。
entries.en: When grief enveloped the four seas and the eight tones were stilled, he exhausted his loyalty for the state and personally received the dying entrustment. One virtue without duality—for a thousand ages awe-inspiring.
entries.literal: When grief enveloped the four seas and eight tones were stilled, he exhausted loyalty for the state, personally received the dying entrustment—one virtue without duality, for a thousand ages awe-inspiring.

entries.zh: 此不待臣言，陛下備知之矣。
entries.en: This does not await my words—Your Majesty is fully aware of it.
entries.literal: This does not await this subject's words—Your Majesty is fully aware.

entries.zh: 臣嘗有此心，未敢聞奏。
entries.en: I once had this thought in my heart but dared not memorialize it.
entries.literal: This subject once had this heart but dared not hear and memorialize.

entries.zh: 且萬姓失業，旰食忘勞；
entries.en: Moreover the myriad people have lost their occupations, and you eat late and forget fatigue;
entries.literal: Moreover the myriad names lose their occupations, eating late and forgetting fatigue;

entries.zh: 一物不安，納隍軫慮，在於微細，寧得過差。
entries.en: if one thing is not at peace, you receive it into the moat and turn your care. In what is minute and fine, how can there be excess error?
entries.literal: one thing not at peace, receiving the moat and turning care—in what is minute and fine, how can there be excess error.
