entries.zh: 況社稷之舊臣，陛下之賢佐，無聞罪狀，斥去朝廷，內外氓黎，咸嗟舉措。
entries.en: How much more a former minister of the altars of state and Your Majesty's worthy assistant—no crime heard of, yet expelled from court. Inner and outer common folk all sigh at this action.
entries.literal: How much more a former minister of the altars of state, Your Majesty's worthy assistant—no crime heard, expelled from court; inner and outer common folk all sigh at the action.

entries.zh: 觀其近日言事，披誠懇切，詎肯後陛下之德，異於堯、舜；
entries.en: Observing his recent words on affairs, spreading sincerity earnest and cutting—how would he lag behind Your Majesty's virtue or differ from Yao and Shun;
entries.literal: Observing his recent days' speaking on affairs, spreading sincerity earnest and cutting—how would he lag behind Your Majesty's virtue, differ from Yao and Shun;

entries.zh: 懼陛下之過，塵於史冊。
entries.en: he fears only that Your Majesty's excess will stain the historical records.
entries.literal: he fears Your Majesty's excess will dust the historical records.

entries.zh: 而乃深遭厚謗，重負丑言，可以痛志士之心，損陛下之明也。
entries.en: Yet he deeply suffers thick slander and heavily bears ugly words. This can pain the heart of a determined scholar and diminish Your Majesty's brilliance.
entries.literal: Yet he deeply suffers thick slander, heavily bears ugly words—this can pain the determined scholar's heart and diminish Your Majesty's brilliance.

entries.zh: 臣聞晉武弘裕，不貽劉毅之誅；
entries.en: I have heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was vast and generous and did not bequeath punishment to Liu Yi;
entries.literal: This subject has heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was vast and generous, not bequeathing Liu Yi's punishment;

entries.zh: 漢祖深仁，無恚周昌之直。
entries.en: the Han Founder was deeply benevolent and bore no resentment toward Zhou Chang's straightness.
entries.literal: the Han Founder was deeply benevolent, without resentment toward Zhou Chang's straightness.

entries.zh: 而遂良被遷，已經寒暑，違忤陛下，其罰塞焉。
entries.en: Yet Suiliang has been transferred and has already passed through cold and heat. Having offended Your Majesty, his punishment is sufficient.
entries.literal: Yet Suiliang was transferred, already passing cold and heat; having offended Your Majesty, his punishment is sufficient.

entries.zh: 伏願纟面鑑無辜，稍寬非罪，俯矜微款，以順人情。
entries.en: I beg you to look down with compassion on the innocent, slightly loosen what is not truly a crime, bow to cherish his slight sincerity, and accord with human feeling.
entries.literal: I prostrate myself wishing to look down and examine the innocent, slightly loosen non-crime, bowing to cherish slight sincerity, to accord with human feelings.

entries.zh: 疏奏，帝謂瑗曰：「遂良之情，朕亦知之矣。
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor told Yuan, "I also know Suiliang's feelings.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor told Yuan: "Suiliang's feeling—I also know it.

entries.zh: 然其悖戾犯上，以此責之，朕豈有過，卿言何若是之深也！」
entries.en: Yet he was perverse and violent in offending his superiors. For this he is blamed. How could I be at fault? Why are your words so extreme!"
entries.literal: Yet his perversity and violence offended superiors—for this he is blamed. How could I have fault? Why are your words so deep as this!"

entries.zh: 瑗對曰：「遂良可謂社稷忠臣，臣恐以諛佞之輩，蒼蠅點白，損陷忠貞。
entries.en: Yuan replied, "Suiliang can be called a loyal minister of the altars of state. I fear that flatterers and sycophants, like flies spotting white cloth, will harm and trap the loyal and upright.
entries.literal: Yuan replied: "Suiliang can be called a loyal minister of the altars of state. I fear that with flatterers and sycophants, blue flies spotting white, the loyal and upright will be harmed and trapped.

entries.zh: 昔微子去之而殷國以亡，張華不死而綱紀不亂，國之慾謝，善人其衰。
entries.en: Formerly when Weizi left, the Yin state perished; when Zhang Hua did not die, institutions and law were not disordered. When a state is about to decline, good men decay with it.
entries.literal: Formerly when Weizi left, the Yin state thereby perished; when Zhang Hua did not die, institutions and law were not disordered—a state about to decline, good men thereby decay.

entries.zh: 今陛下富有四海，八紘清泰，忽驅逐舊臣，而不垂省察乎！
entries.en: Now Your Majesty possesses the four seas and the eight cords are clear and peaceful. Will you suddenly drive out old ministers and not extend examination and consideration!
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty possesses the four seas, the eight cords clear and peaceful—suddenly driving out old ministers, yet not extending examination and consideration!

entries.zh: 伏願違彼覆車，以收往過，垂勸誡於事君，則群生幸甚。」
entries.en: I beg you to avoid that overturned cart, recover from former excess, and hang admonition on serving the ruler. Then the myriad living would be greatly fortunate."
entries.literal: I prostrate myself wishing to avoid that overturned cart, to recover former excess, to hang admonition on serving the ruler—then the myriad living would be greatly fortunate."

entries.zh: 帝竟不納。
entries.en: The emperor in the end did not accept it.
entries.literal: The Emperor in the end did not accept it.

entries.zh: 瑗以言不見用，憂憤上表，請歸田裡，詔不許。
entries.en: Because his words were not employed, Yuan in worry and anger submitted a memorial requesting to return to his fields and village, but the edict did not permit it.
entries.literal: Yuan because his words were not employed, in worry and anger submitted a memorial requesting to return to his fields and village—the edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 顯慶二年，許敬宗、李義府希皇后之旨，誣奏瑗與褚遂良潛謀不軌，以桂州用武之地，故授遂良桂州刺史，實以為外援。
entries.en: In 657 Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, hoping to please the empress, falsely memorialized that Yuan and Chu Suiliang had secretly plotted treason. Because Guizhou was a place of military importance, Suiliang had been made Prefect of Guizhou in reality to serve as external support.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu hoping for the empress's intent falsely memorialized that Yuan and Chu Suiliang secretly plotted irregularity—because Guizhou was a place of military use, therefore Suiliang was granted Prefect of Guizhou, in reality to serve as external aid.

entries.zh: 於是更貶遂良為愛州刺史，左授瑗振州刺史。
entries.en: Thereupon Suiliang was again demoted to Prefect of Aizhou, and Yuan was demoted to Prefect of Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: Thereupon Suiliang was again demoted to Prefect of Aizhou, and Yuan was demoted left to Prefect of Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 四年，卒官，年五十四。
entries.en: In 659 he died in office at the age of fifty-four.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he died in office, age fifty-four.

entries.zh: 明年，長孫無忌死，敬宗等又奏瑗與無忌通謀，遣使殺之。
entries.en: The next year Zhangsun Wuji died. Jingzong and others again memorialized that Yuan had communicated plots with Wuji and sent envoys to kill him.
entries.literal: The next year Zhangsun Wuji died; Jingzong and others again memorialized that Yuan had communicated plots with Wuji and sent envoys to kill him.

entries.zh: 及使至，瑗已死，更發棺驗屍而還，籍沒其家，孫配徙嶺表。
entries.en: When the envoy arrived, Yuan was already dead. They opened the coffin and examined the corpse and returned, registered and confiscated his household, and his grandsons were sentenced to exile beyond the Ling range.
entries.literal: When the envoy arrived, Yuan was already dead; they again opened the coffin and examined the corpse and returned, registered and confiscated his household, and grandsons were sentenced to exile beyond the Ling range.

entries.zh: 神龍元年，則天遺制令復其官爵。
entries.en: In 705 Empress Zetian's testamentary institution ordered restoration of his offices and titles.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Empress Zetian's testamentary institution ordered restoration of his offices and titles.

entries.zh: 褚遂良 韓瑗 來濟 上官儀
entries.en: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and Shang Guanyi
entries.literal: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, Shang Guanyi

entries.zh: 臨孫紹，博學，善《三禮》。
entries.en: Lin's grandson Shao was learned and expert in the Three Rites.
entries.literal: Lin's grandson Shao was erudite and skilled in the Three Rites.

entries.zh: 神龍中為太常博士，
entries.en: During the Shenlong era he served as Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: In the Shenlong era he was Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices,

entries.zh: 景龍二年，韋庶人上言：“自妃、主及命婦、宮官，葬日請給鼓吹。”
entries.en: In the second year of Jinglong, Empress Wei petitioned that consorts, princesses, titled ladies, and palace women be granted martial music at their funerals.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jinglong, the Deposed Empress Wei submitted a memorial: "From consorts and princesses down to titled ladies and palace officers, on burial days request that martial music be granted.

entries.zh: 中宗特製許之。
entries.en: Emperor Zhongzong specially approved it.
entries.literal: Zhongzong by special edict permitted it.

entries.zh: 紹上疏諫曰：“竊聞鼓吹之樂，本為軍容。
entries.en: Shao remonstrated: "Martial pipe-and-drum music was created for armies.
entries.literal: Shao submitted a remonstrance, saying: "I have heard that the music of martial pipes and drums was originally for military array.

entries.zh: 昔黃帝涿鹿有功，以為警衛。
entries.en: The Yellow Emperor instituted it as a guard of honor after Zhuolu.
entries.literal: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor, for merit at Zhuolu, made it a guard of honor.

entries.zh: 故棡鼓曲有《靈夔吼》、《雕鶚爭》、《石墜崖》、《壯士怒》之類，自昔功臣備禮，適得用之。
entries.en: Its drum pieces—Spirit Kui Roars, Eagle and Goshawk Contend, Stone Falls from the Cliff, Hero's Wrath—were reserved for meritorious ministers.
entries.literal: Therefore the rattle-drum tunes have such titles as Spirit Kui Roars, Eagle and Goshawk Contend, Stone Falls from the Cliff, and Hero's Wrath; from old meritorious ministers received full ritual and only then might use it.

entries.zh: 丈夫有四方之功，以恩加寵錫。
entries.en: Men who won the realm received such honors by imperial grace.
entries.literal: A man with merit in the four directions received favor and bestowal of gifts by grace.

entries.zh: 假如郊天祀地，誠是重儀，惟有宮懸，本無案據。
entries.en: Even at the greatest sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, only the palace bells are prescribed—no precedent for martial music there.
entries.literal: Suppose sacrificing to Heaven and Earth—truly this is a weighty rite; only the palace suspended bells exist, and originally there is no precedent for the other.

entries.zh: 故知軍樂所備，尚不洽於神祇；
entries.en: Military music does not even belong at rites for the gods;
entries.literal: Thus one knows that what military music prepares still does not extend to the spirits;

entries.zh: 鉦鼓之音，豈能接於閨閫。
entries.en: how could gongs and drums enter the women's quarters?
entries.literal: how could the sound of bells and drums be joined to inner chambers?

entries.zh: 準式，公主、王妃已下葬禮，惟有團扇、方扇、彩帷、錦鄣之色。
entries.en: Regulations for princesses and consorts allow only fans, canopies, and brocade screens at burial.
entries.literal: By regulation, for burial rites of princesses and imperial consorts and below, there are only round fans, square fans, colored canopies, and brocade screens.

entries.zh: 加之鼓吹，曆代未聞。
entries.en: Adding martial music has no precedent in any dynasty.
entries.literal: Adding martial music—no age has heard of it.

entries.zh: 又準令，五品官婚葬，元無鼓吹，惟京官五品，得借四品鼓吹為儀。
entries.en: Statute gives fifth-rank officials no martial music at all; only metropolitan fifth-rank officials may borrow fourth-rank music.
entries.literal: Moreover by regulation, for fifth-rank officials' weddings and funerals there originally was no martial music; only capital officials of fifth rank might borrow fourth-rank martial music as ceremony.

entries.zh: 令特給五品以上母妻，五品官則不當給限，便是班秩本因夫子，儀飾乃復過之。
entries.en: Granting it to fifth-rank mothers and wives while denying fifth-rank officials themselves inverts rank, which derives from husband or son.
entries.literal: Now to grant specially to mothers and wives above fifth rank, while fifth-rank officials ought not receive the limit—then rank originally derives from husband and son, yet ceremonial display again surpasses them.

entries.zh: 事非倫次，難為定制，參詳義理，不可常行。
entries.en: The order is wrong, the rule unworkable, and the rite should not become routine.
entries.literal: The matter is not in proper order; it is hard to make a fixed rule; examining the meaning and principle, it cannot be regularly practiced.

entries.zh: 請停前敕，各依常典。”
entries.en: I ask that the recent edict be revoked and old custom restored."
entries.literal: I request to stop the prior edict and each follow the usual canon."

entries.zh: 疏奏不納。
entries.en: The memorial went unheeded.
entries.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.

entries.zh: 文琮從父弟文收，隋內史舍人虔威子也。
entries.en: Wenzong's cousin Wenshou was the son of the Sui interior secretary Qianwei.
entries.literal: Wenzong's paternal cousin Wenshou was son of Sui Interior Secretary Attendant Qianwei.

entries.zh: 尤善音律，嚐覽蕭吉《樂譜》，以為未甚詳悉，更博采群言及曆代沿革，裁竹為十二律吹之，備盡旋宮之義。
entries.en: Skilled in music theory, he found Xiao Ji's treatise incomplete, studied wider sources, cut bamboo pipes for the twelve pitches, and demonstrated full cyclical modulation.
entries.literal: He was especially skilled in pitch and mode; once he perused Xiao Ji's Music Treatise and thought it not very detailed, and further broadly gathered many statements and successive ages' changes and reforms, cut bamboo for the twelve modes and blew them, fully completing the meaning of cyclical modes.

entries.zh: 時太宗將創製禮樂，召文收於太常，令與少卿祖孝孫參定雅樂。
entries.en: When Taizong was creating court music, Wenshou was called to the Imperial Sacrifices office to work with Zu Xiaosun.
entries.literal: At the time Taizong was about to create ritual music; he summoned Wenshou to the Imperial Sacrifices office and ordered him with Vice Director Zu Xiaosun to fix the elegant music.

entries.zh: 太樂有古鍾十二，近代惟用其七，餘有五，俗號啞鍾，莫能通者。
entries.en: The court had twelve ancient bells; only seven were used in recent times—the other five, called mute bells, could not be sounded.
entries.literal: The Grand Music had twelve ancient bells; in recent times only seven were used; the remaining five, commonly called mute bells, none could make sound.

entries.zh: 文收吹律調之，聲皆響徹，時人咸服其妙。
entries.en: Wenshou tuned them with his pipes until all rang clear, to general admiration.
entries.literal: Wenshou blew modes to tune them; all sounds rang clear; people of the time all submitted to his subtlety.

entries.zh: 尋授協律郎。
entries.en: He was soon made harmonizing officer.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Harmonizing Officer.

entries.zh: 十一年，文收表請厘正太樂，上謂侍臣曰：“樂本緣人，人和則樂和。
entries.en: In year eleven he asked to reform court music; the emperor told his ministers, "Music follows the people—when people are at peace, music is in harmony.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year Wenshou memorialized requesting to rectify Grand Music; the emperor told attendant officials: "Music fundamentally follows people; if people are harmonious then music is harmonious.

entries.zh: 至如隋煬帝末年，天下喪亂，縱令改張音律，知其終不和諧。
entries.en: At the end of Sui Yangdi's reign the realm was in chaos; even if you changed the pitches, they would not harmonize.
entries.literal: As for late in Sui Yangdi's reign, the realm was in disorder and mourning; even if one changed and spread pitch and mode, one knows in the end it would not be harmonious.

entries.zh: 若使四海無事，百姓安樂，音律自然調和，不藉更改。”
entries.en: When the realm is tranquil and the people content, music harmonizes of itself without reform."
entries.literal: If the four seas had no affairs and the common people were at ease and happy, pitch and mode would naturally be harmonious without relying on change."

entries.zh: 竟不依其請。
entries.en: His request was denied.
entries.literal: In the end he did not follow his request.

entries.zh: 十四年，景雲見，河水清，文收采《朱雁天馬》之義，製《景雲河清》樂，名曰“燕樂”，奏之管弦，為樂之首，今元會第一奏者是也，
entries.en: In year fourteen, when auspicious clouds and a clear Yellow River appeared, he composed "Auspicious Clouds and Clear River," called Yan Music—the piece still opened the New Year court.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, auspicious clouds appeared and the Yellow River ran clear; Wenshou took the meaning of Vermilion Goose and Heavenly Horse and composed the music "Auspicious Clouds and Clear River," named "Yan Music"; played on pipes and strings, it was first among music—what is now first played at the New Year assembly is this,

entries.zh: 咸亨元年，遷太子率更令，卒官。
entries.en: In the first year of Xianheng, He was then made rate master of the heir apparent and died in office.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianheng, he was moved to Rate Master of the Heir Apparent and died in office.

entries.zh: 撰《新樂書》十二卷。
entries.en: He wrote New Music Book in twelve scrolls.
entries.literal: He compiled New Music Book in twelve scrolls.

entries.zh: 徐有功，國子博士文遠孫也。
entries.en: Xu Yougong, grandson of National University erudite Xu Wenyuan.
entries.literal: Xu Yougong was grandson of Erudite of the National University Xu Wenyuan.

entries.zh: 舉明經，累轉蒲州司法參軍，紹封東莞男。
entries.en: He passed the Mingjing exam, served as judicial officer in Puzhou, and inherited the barony of Dongguan.
entries.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was repeatedly promoted to Judicial Staff Officer of Puzhou, inheriting the enfeoffment Baron of Dongguan.

entries.zh: 為政寬仁，不行杖罰。
entries.en: He governed with leniency and never used the beating staff.
entries.literal: In governing he was lenient and benevolent and did not apply the staff penalty.

entries.zh: 吏人感其恩信，遞相約曰：“若犯徐司法杖者，眾必斥罰之。”
entries.en: Officials and people, trusting him, agreed among themselves that anyone who forced Xu to use the staff would be shamed by the community.
entries.literal: Officials and people were moved by his grace and trust and in turn agreed: "If anyone violates Staff Officer Xu's staff, the multitude will surely reprove and punish him."

entries.zh: 由是人爭用命，終於代滿，不戮一人，
entries.en: They competed to obey the law, and when his term ended not a single person had been executed.
entries.literal: Therefore people vied to fulfill orders; by the end of his term of replacement not one was put to death,

entries.zh: 載初元年，累遷司刑丞。
entries.en: In the first year of Zaichu, He was then promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zaichu, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Punishments.

entries.zh: 時酷吏周興、來俊臣、丘神勣、王弘義等構陷無辜，皆抵極法，公卿震恐，莫敢正言。
entries.en: Cruel officials such as Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, and Wang Hongyi framed the innocent to extreme punishments while the court fell silent.
entries.literal: At the time the cruel officials Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wang Hongyi, and others framed the innocent; all reached extreme law; dukes and ministers trembled in fear and none dared speak straight.

entries.zh: 有功獨存平恕，詔下大理者，有功皆議出之，前後濟活數十百家。
entries.en: Yougong alone remained fair and lenient; cases sent to the Grand Court he argued to release, saving dozens of families.
entries.literal: Yougong alone preserved fairness and leniency; those sent down to the Grand Court by edict Yougong all deliberated to release; before and after he saved several tens of families.

entries.zh: 常於殿庭論奏曲直，則天厲色詰之，左右莫不悚栗，有功神色不撓，爭之彌切。
entries.en: He often argued cases in court; Wu Zetian questioned him angrily while attendants trembled, but he did not flinch and argued all the harder.
entries.literal: He often in the palace hall debated right and wrong in cases; Wu Zetian with stern countenance interrogated him; those left and right were all fearful, yet Yougong's expression did not bend and he contended all the more keenly.

entries.zh: 尋轉秋官員外郎，轉郎中。
entries.en: He soon became vice director and then director of the Autumn Office.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved to Vice Director of the Autumn Office, then Director.

entries.zh: 俄而鳳閣侍郎任知古、冬官尚書裴行本等七人被構陷當死，則天謂公卿曰：“古人以殺止殺，我今以恩止殺。
entries.en: Soon Ren Zhigu, Pei Xingben, and five others were framed for death; Wu Zetian told the court, "The ancients stopped killing by killing; I stop killing by grace.
entries.literal: Soon Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Ren Zhigu, Winter Office Minister Pei Xingben, and seven others were framed and should die; Wu Zetian told the dukes and ministers: "The ancients used killing to stop killing; I now use grace to stop killing.

entries.zh: 就群公乞知古等，賜以再生，各授以官，佇申來效。”
entries.en: I ask you to spare Zhigu and the rest, give them office, and await their service."
entries.literal: I approach the assembled lords to beg Zhigu and the others, grant them renewed life, each confer office, and wait to declare future merit."

entries.zh: 俊臣、張知默等又抗表請申大法，則天不許之。
entries.en: Lai Junchen and Zhang Zhimou protested for harsh law, but she refused.
entries.literal: Junchen, Zhang Zhimou, and others again submitted memorials requesting application of the great law; Wu Zetian did not permit it.

entries.zh: 俊臣乃獨引行本，重驗前罪，奏曰：“行本潛行悖逆，告張知蹇與廬陵王反不實，罪當處斬。”
entries.en: Junchen alone brought Xingben back, re-examined the case, and said Xingben had falsely reported the Prince of Luling's rebellion and deserved death.
entries.literal: Junchen then alone led out Xingben, again verified the former crime, and submitted: "Xingben secretly acted in rebellion, reporting to Zhang Zhijian that the Prince of Luling's rebellion was untrue—the crime should be execution."

entries.zh: 有功駁奏曰：“俊臣乖明主再生之賜，虧聖人恩信之道。
entries.en: Yougong rebutted: "Junchen defies your gift of life and betrays imperial grace.
entries.literal: Yougong rebutted the memorial, saying: "Junchen violates the enlightened ruler's gift of renewed life and damages the sage's path of grace and trust.

entries.zh: 為臣雖當嫉惡，然事君必將順其美。”
entries.en: A minister must hate evil, yet serve the ruler by following his good intent."
entries.literal: As a minister one must hate evil, yet in serving the ruler one must follow his excellence.

entries.zh: 行本竟以免死。
entries.en: Xingben was spared after all.
entries.literal: Xingben in the end was spared death.

entries.zh: 道州刺史李仁褒及弟榆次令長沙，又為唐奉一所構，高宗末私議吉凶，謀復李氏，將誅之。
entries.en: Li Renbao, prefect of Dao, and his younger brother Changsha, magistrate of Yuci, were framed by Tang Fengyi for private divination plotting to restore the Li house.
entries.literal: Dao Prefecture Inspector Li Renbao and his younger brother, Magistrate of Yuci Changsha, were again framed by Tang Fengyi; at the end of Gaozong they privately discussed fortune and misfortune, plotting to restore the Li clan, and were about to be executed.

entries.zh: 有功又固爭之，不能得。
entries.en: Yougong argued fiercely but could not save them.
entries.literal: Yougong again firmly contended but could not succeed.

entries.zh: 秋官侍郎周興奏有功曰：“臣聞兩漢故事，附下罔上者腰斬，麵欺者亦斬。
entries.en: Zhou Xing memorialized against Yougong, saying, "I have heard that in Han precedents, those who fawn on subordinates and deceive superiors are cut at the waist.
entries.literal: Autumn Office Vice Minister Zhou Xing memorialized against Yougong, saying: "Your servant has heard that in the two Han stories, those who fawn on subordinates and deceive superiors are cut at the waist, and those who deceive to the face are also beheaded.

entries.zh: 又《禮》云：析言破律者殺。
entries.en: The Rites also say those who twist words to break the law are killed.
entries.literal: Moreover the Rites say: those who analyze words to break statutes are killed.

entries.zh: 有功故出反囚，罪當不赦，請推按其罪。”
entries.en: Yougong released rebels and should not be forgiven; investigate him."
entries.literal: Yougong deliberately released rebel prisoners—the crime should not be pardoned; I request investigation and prosecution of his crime."

entries.zh: 則天雖不許係問，然竟坐免官。
entries.en: She did not imprison him but removed him from office.
entries.literal: Although Wu Zetian did not permit binding and interrogation, in the end he sat and was removed from office.

entries.zh: 久之，起為左台侍御史，則天特褒異之。
entries.en: After a time he was restored as left censor, which Wu Zetian specially praised.
entries.literal: After a long time he was raised as Attending Censor of the Left Terrace; Wu Zetian especially praised and distinguished him.

entries.zh: 時遠近聞有功授職，皆欣然相賀。
entries.en: Near and far rejoiced at his appointment.
entries.literal: At the time near and far, hearing Yougong received appointment, all gladly congratulated one another.

entries.zh: 中宗即位，製曰：“忠正之臣，自昔攸尚；
entries.en: When Zhongzong succeeded, an edict said, "Loyal ministers have always been honored;
entries.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, an edict said: "Loyal and upright ministers have from old been honored;

entries.zh: 褒贈之典，舊章所重。
entries.en: Honoring the dead with praise and gifts was always esteemed in precedent.
entries.literal: The canon of praise and posthumous gift is what old regulations esteem.

entries.zh: 故贈大理卿徐有功，節操貞勁，器懷亮直，徇古人之誌業，實一代之賢良，司彼刑書，深存敬慎。
entries.en: The late Grand Justice Xu Yougong was firm in integrity, bright and upright in character, devoted to the ancients' ideals, a true worthy of his age who handled the penal codes with deep reverent care.
entries.literal: Therefore the posthumously given Grand Justice Xu Yougong, whose integrity was firm and strong and whose capacity embraced brightness and uprightness, followed the ancients' aims and work, truly a worthy of his generation; he managed those penal writings and deeply preserved reverent caution.

entries.zh: 周興、來俊臣等性惟殘酷，務在誅夷，不順其情，立加誣害。
entries.en: Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and their ilk were cruel by nature, bent on slaughter, and would fabricate charges without regard to truth.
entries.literal: Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others by nature were only cruel; they strove to exterminate and slay; not following the facts, they immediately added false harm.

entries.zh: 有功卓然守法，雖死不移，無屈撓之心，有忠烈之議。
entries.en: Yougong stood out in upholding the law, unshaken even before death, never yielding, and spoke with loyal fierceness.
entries.literal: Yougong outstandingly upheld law; though death he did not shift; he had no heart of bending or yielding and had loyal and fierce deliberation.

entries.zh: 當其執斷，並遇平反，定國、釋之，何以加此。
entries.en: In his judgments he repeatedly secured reversals of wrongful convictions—what more could Ding Guo or Shi Zhi have added?
entries.literal: When he held judgment and decided, all met reversal of wrongful cases; how could Ding Guo and Shi Zhi surpass this?

entries.zh: 朕惟新庶政，追想前跡，其人既歿，其德可稱。
entries.en: As I renew the government, I recall his path: though he is gone, his virtue deserves praise.
entries.literal: We alone renew the multitude of policies, recall former traces; the man has already died, yet his virtue can be praised.

entries.zh: 追往贈終，慰茲泉壤。
entries.en: Let posthumous honors comfort him in the grave.
entries.literal: Pursue the past and gift the end, comfort these springs and soil.

entries.zh: 可贈越州刺史，仍遣使就家吊祭，賜物百段，授一子官。”
entries.en: Let him be posthumously made prefect of Yuezhou; send envoys to mourn at his home, grant a hundred gifts, and give office to one son."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously given Prefect of Yuezhou; still send envoys to his home to mourn and sacrifice, bestow a hundred items, and confer office on one son."

entries.zh: 今上踐祚，竇孝諶之子希瑊等請以身之官爵讓有功子惀，以報舊恩。
entries.en: When the present emperor succeeded, Dou Xiaochen's son Xizhen and others asked to yield their own offices to Yougong's son Lun in repayment of old kindness.
entries.literal: When the present emperor trod the throne, Dou Xiaochen's son Xizhen and others requested to yield their own offices and ranks to Yougong's son Lun, to repay old grace.

entries.zh: 惀由是自太子司議郎、恭陵令累遷申王府司馬，卒。
entries.en: Lun rose from admonisher to the crown prince and magistrate of Gongling to major of the Prince of Shen's household, and died.
entries.literal: Lun from this was from Crown Prince Admonishing Attendant, Magistrate of Gongling, repeatedly promoted to Prince of Shen's Household Major, and died.

entries.zh: 【論贊】史臣曰：文法，理具之大者，故舜命皋陶為士，昌言誡敕，勤亦至焉。
entries.en: [Discussion] The historian writes: Penal law is among the great instruments of governance; Shun appointed Gao Yao minister of crime and exhorted him with clear admonitions—such was the diligence required.
entries.literal: [Discussion and Praise] The historiographer says: Literary law is among the great instruments of principle; therefore Shun appointed Gao Yao as minister of crime, and with bright words admonished and instructed—diligence also reached there.

entries.zh: 蓋人命所懸，一失其平，冤不可復，聖王所以疚心也。
entries.en: Human lives hang in the balance; one lapse from fairness leaves injustice beyond repair—this is why sage rulers grieve.
entries.literal: For human lives hang upon it; once balance is lost, injustice cannot be restored—the sage king therefore is pained in heart.

entries.zh: 如臨之守法，文瓘之議刑，時屬哲王，可以理奪。
entries.en: Men such as Lin, who upheld the law, and Wenjun, who weighed punishments, flourished under wise rulers who could be swayed by reason.
entries.literal: Such as Lin's upholding law and Wenjun's deliberating punishments—when the time belonged to a wise king, one could prevail by reason.

entries.zh: 當賊後遷鼎之際，酷吏羅織之辰，徐有功獨抗群邪，持平不撓，此所以為難也。
entries.en: In the age after rebellion and the move of the capital, when cruel officials wove false charges, Xu Yougong alone stood against the wicked and held the scales level—no small feat.
entries.literal: At the time after the rebel moved the tripod, in the hour when cruel officials wove nets, Xu Yougong alone resisted the multitude of evil, held balance and did not bend—this is why it was difficult.

entries.zh: 比釋之、定國，徐又過之。
entries.en: Beside Shi Zhi and Ding Guo, Xu Yougong was greater still.
entries.literal: Compared to Shi Zhi and Ding Guo, Xu again surpassed them.

entries.zh: 希瑊讓爵酬恩，可知遺愛。
entries.en: Xizhen's yielding of rank to repay kindness shows how deeply he was loved.
entries.literal: Xizhen yielded rank to repay grace—one can know the love he left behind.

entries.zh: 紹尋遷左台侍御史，兼太常博士。
entries.en: Shao was soon made Left Censor and still served as ritual erudite.
entries.literal: Shao was soon moved to Attending Censor of the Left Terrace, concurrently Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 中宗將親拜南郊，國子祭酒祝欽明等希旨皇后為亞獻，紹與博士蔣欽緒固爭以為不可。
entries.en: When Zhongzong prepared to sacrifice at the southern suburb, Zhu Qinming and others flattered Empress Wei as secondary offerer; Shao and Jiang Qinxu protested.
entries.literal: Zhongzong was about to perform the southern suburban sacrifice in person; the National University Rector Zhu Qinming and others, to please the empress, wished her to be secondary offerer; Shao and Erudite Jiang Qinxu firmly contended that this could not be.

entries.zh: 又則天父母二陵各置守戶五百人，武三思及子崇訓墓各置守戶六十人。
entries.en: Wu Zetian's parents' tombs each received five hundred guard households; Wu Sansi and his son Chongxun each received sixty.
entries.literal: Moreover at the two tombs of Wu Zetian's parents five hundred tomb-guard households were established each; at the tombs of Wu Sansi and his son Chongxun sixty guard households each were established.

entries.zh: 以武氏外戚乃與昭陵禮同，三思等復逾親王之製，又上疏切諫。
entries.en: Equating Wu kin with Taizong's Zhaoling and outdoing princely rites, Shao remonstrated again.
entries.literal: Because the Wu clan as maternal kin were made equal in ritual to Zhaoling, and Sansi and others again exceeded the regulations for imperial princes, he again submitted a sharp remonstrance.

entries.zh: 當時雖皆不從，深為議者所美。
entries.en: None of it was adopted, but contemporaries admired his stand.
entries.literal: Although at the time all were not followed, he was deeply praised by discussants.

entries.zh: 睿宗即位，又數陳時政損益，累轉給事中，仍知禮儀事。
entries.en: Under Ruizong he repeatedly advised on policy, rose to Drafting Attendant, and still oversaw ritual.
entries.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he again several times stated gains and losses of current policy, was repeatedly promoted to Drafting Attendant, and still managed ritual matters.

entries.zh: 文瓘性嚴正，諸司奏議，多所糾駁，高宗甚委之。
entries.en: Stern and upright, he corrected many memorials from other offices; Gaozong relied on him heavily.
entries.literal: Wenjun's nature was stern and upright; the various offices' submitted deliberations he many times criticized and rejected; Gaozong greatly relied on him.

entries.zh: 或時臥疾在家，朝廷每有大事，上必問諸宰臣曰：“與文瓘議未？”
entries.en: When ill at home, on great affairs the emperor asked his chancellors, "Have you consulted Wenjun?"
entries.literal: Sometimes lying ill at home, whenever the court had a great matter the emperor would ask the chief ministers: "Have you deliberated with Wenjun?"

entries.zh: 奏雲未者，則遣共籌之。
entries.en: If they had not, he sent them to confer with him.
entries.literal: If the reply was not yet, he would send them to plan together.

entries.zh: 奏雲已議者，皆報可從之。
entries.en: If they had, he approved their decision.
entries.literal: If the reply was already deliberated, all were reported as acceptable to follow.

entries.zh: 其後，新羅外叛，高宗將發兵討除。
entries.en: Later Silla rebelled abroad, and Gaozong prepared to send troops against them.
entries.literal: After this, Silla rebelled externally and Gaozong was about to send troops to punish and eliminate them.

entries.zh: 時文瓘疾病在家，乃輿疾請見，奏曰：“比為吐蕃犯邊，兵屯寇境，新羅雖未即順，師不內侵。
entries.en: Wenjun was ill at home but had himself carried in to see the emperor. He said, "Tibetans are raiding the frontier and troops are massed there. Silla has not yet submitted, but their armies are not marching inland.
entries.literal: At the time Wenjun was ill at home; he had himself carried in illness to request an audience and submitted: "Recently because Tibetans violated the border, troops are stationed on the frontier; although Silla has not yet immediately submitted, their armies do not invade inward.

entries.zh: 若東西俱事征討，臣恐百姓不堪其弊。
entries.en: If we fight on both fronts at once, the people will not endure the burden.
entries.literal: If east and west both undertake campaigns, your servant fears the common people cannot bear the harm.

entries.zh: 請息兵修德以安百姓。”
entries.en: I beg you to halt the armies and cultivate virtue to give the people peace."
entries.literal: I request to cease troops and cultivate virtue to settle the common people."

entries.zh: 高宗從之。
entries.en: Gaozong agreed.
entries.literal: Gaozong followed this.

entries.zh: 儀鳳二年卒，年七十三，贈幽州都督，諡曰懿。
entries.en: In the second year of Yifeng, he died at seventy-three, was posthumously made governor of Youzhou, and given the posthumous name Yi.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, he died at age seventy-three, was posthumously given Governor of Youzhou, and his posthumous title was Yi.

entries.zh: 以其經事孝敬皇帝，特敕陪葬恭陵。
entries.en: For having served Emperor Xiaojing, he was specially ordered buried at Gongling.
entries.literal: Because he had served the Filial and Respectful Emperor, a special edict ordered him buried with honor at Gongling.

entries.zh: 四子：潛、沛、洽、涉。
entries.en: He had four sons: Qian, Pei, Qia, and She.
entries.literal: Four sons: Qian, Pei, Qia, and She.

entries.zh: 中宗時，潛官至魏州刺史，沛同州刺史，洽衛尉卿，涉殿中監。
entries.en: Under Zhongzong, Qian became prefect of Wei, Pei of Tong, Qia commandant of the guards, and She director of the palace directorate.
entries.literal: In the Zhongzong era, Qian reached Prefect of Weizhou, Pei Tong Prefecture, Qia Commandant of the Guards, and She Director of the Palace.

entries.zh: 父子兄弟五人皆至三品官，時人謂之“萬石張家”。
entries.en: Father and four sons all reached third rank; contemporaries called them the Zhang family of ten thousand stone.
entries.literal: Father, sons, and brothers—five men—all reached third-rank office; people of the time called them the "Wanshi Zhang family."

entries.zh: 及韋溫等被誅之際，涉為亂兵所殺。
entries.en: When Wei Wen and his faction were killed, She died at the hands of mutinous troops.
entries.literal: When Wei Wen and others were executed, She was killed by mutinous soldiers.

entries.zh: 兄文琮，貞觀中為持書侍御史。
entries.en: His elder brother Wenzong was an attending censor in Zhenguan.
entries.literal: His elder brother Wenzong, in Zhenguan served as Attending Censor holding the imperial writing.

entries.zh: 三遷毫州刺史，為政清簡，百姓安之。
entries.en: Promoted thrice to prefect of Bozhou, he governed plainly and the people were content.
entries.literal: Three times moved to Prefect of Bozhou; his governance was clear and simple and the common people were at peace.

entries.zh: 永徽初，表獻《太宗文皇帝頌》，優製褒美，賜絹百匹，征拜戶部侍郎。
entries.en: In early Yonghui he presented an eulogy to Taizong; the emperor praised it, gave a hundred bolts of silk, and made him Vice Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: Early in Yonghui he submitted a memorial offering Eulogy for Emperor Taizong, Wen; an excellent edict praised him, bestowed a hundred bolts of silk, and summoned him as Vice Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 從母弟房遺愛以罪貶授房州刺史，文琮作詩祖餞。
entries.en: His cousin Fang Yiai, convicted, was demoted to Fangzhou; Wenzong wrote a farewell poem.
entries.literal: His maternal cousin Fang Yiai, for a crime, was demoted and appointed Prefect of Fangzhou; Wenzong composed a poem to send him off.

entries.zh: 及遺愛誅，坐是出為建州刺史。
entries.en: When Yiai was executed, Wenzong was posted out as prefect of Jianzhou.
entries.literal: When Yiai was executed, for this he was sent out as Prefect of Jianzhou.

entries.zh: 州境素尚淫祀，不修社稷。
entries.en: The region favored improper cults and neglected the state altars.
entries.literal: The prefecture had long favored licentious sacrifices and did not repair the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 文琮下教書曰：“春秋二社，蓋本為農，惟獨此州，廢而不立。
entries.en: He issued an instruction: "The spring and autumn communal rites exist for farming; this prefecture alone has abandoned them.
entries.literal: Wenzong issued an instruction, saying: "The two seasonal communal sacrifices of spring and autumn are fundamentally for agriculture; only this prefecture abolished them and did not establish them.

entries.zh: 禮典既闕，風俗何觀？
entries.en: With ritual neglected, what custom remains to follow?
entries.literal: The ritual canon is already lacking—what is there to model in custom?

entries.zh: 近年已來，田多不熟，抑不祭先農所致乎！
entries.en: In recent years the fields have often failed—is this not because the god of agriculture goes unhonored?
entries.literal: In recent years fields have often not ripened—is this perhaps because the Former Farmer is not sacrificed to!

entries.zh: 神在於敬，何以邀福？”
entries.en: Spirits respond to reverence, not to bribery."
entries.literal: The spirits lie in reverence—how seek blessing?"

entries.zh: 於是示其節限條製，百姓欣而行之。
entries.en: He then published the seasonal rules, and the people gladly obeyed.
entries.literal: Thereupon he displayed the seasonal limits and regulations, and the common people gladly carried them out.

entries.zh: 尋卒。
entries.en: He soon died.
entries.literal: Soon he died.

entries.zh: 文集二十卷。
entries.en: His collected works ran to twenty scrolls.
entries.literal: Collected writings in twenty scrolls.

entries.zh: 子戩，官至江州刺史，撰《喪儀纂要》七卷，行於時。
entries.en: His son Jian became prefect of Jiangzhou and wrote Essentials of Mourning Rites in seven scrolls, widely used in his day.
entries.literal: His son Jian reached Prefect of Jiangzhou and compiled Essentials of Mourning Rites in seven scrolls, current in the age.

entries.zh: 戩弟錫，則天時為鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。
entries.en: Jian's brother Xi under Wu Zetian was vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and chancellor.
entries.literal: Jian's younger brother Xi, in Wu Zetian's time was Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Tower.

entries.zh: 先是，姊子李嶠知政事，錫拜官，而嶠罷相出為國子祭酒，舅甥相代為相，時人榮之。
entries.en: Earlier his nephew Li Qiao had been chancellor; when Xi was appointed, Qiao left office as rector of the National University—uncle and nephew succeeding each other as chief ministers, to the admiration of the age.
entries.literal: Previously his sister's son Li Qiao managed government affairs; when Xi received appointment, Qiao ceased being chancellor and went out as Rector of the National University—maternal uncle and nephew succeeding each other as chancellor; people of the time honored this.

entries.zh: 錫與鄭杲俱知天官選事，坐贓，則天將斬之以徇，臨刑而特赦之。
entries.en: Xi and Zheng Gao oversaw personnel selection; convicted of bribery, they were about to be executed when Wu Zetian pardoned them at the block.
entries.literal: Xi together with Zheng Gao both managed Celestial Office selection affairs; for bribery Wu Zetian was about to behead them as a warning, but at execution they received special pardon.

entries.zh: 中宗時，累遷工部尚書，兼修國史，尋令於東都留守。
entries.en: Under Zhongzong he rose to Minister of Works, helped revise the national history, and was left to guard the eastern capital.
entries.literal: In the Zhongzong era he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works, concurrently revised the national history, and soon was ordered to remain at the eastern capital.

entries.zh: 中宗崩，韋庶人臨朝，詔錫與刑部尚書裴談並同中書門下三品。
entries.en: After Zhongzong's death Empress Wei ruled; Xi and Pei Tan were made chancellors of the third rank.
entries.literal: When Zhongzong died, the Deposed Empress Wei held court; an edict made Xi and Minister of Punishments Pei Tan both Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

entries.zh: 旬日，出為絳州刺史。
entries.en: Ten days later he was posted as prefect of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: Within ten days he was sent out as Prefect of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 累封平原郡公，以年老致仕而卒。
entries.en: Enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan, he retired for age and died.
entries.literal: Repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan, he retired for old age and died.

entries.zh: 先天二年冬，今上講武於驪山，紹以修儀注不合旨，坐斬。
entries.en: In the second year of Xiantian, that winter the emperor drilled troops at Lishan; Shao's ritual directions displeased him and he was sentenced to death.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, in winter the present emperor held martial exercises at Lishan; Shao, because the revised ritual regulations did not match the intent, was punished with execution.

entries.zh: 時今上既怒講武失儀，坐紹於纛下，右金吾將軍李邈遽請宣敕，遂斬之。
entries.en: Already angry at the disorderly drill, the emperor had Shao sit beneath the command banner; General Li Miao rushed the edict and he was beheaded.
entries.literal: At the time the present emperor was already angry that the drill had been disorderly; he seated Shao beneath the banner; the Right Golden Crow General Li Miao hastily requested proclamation of the edict, and he was beheaded.

entries.zh: 時人既痛惜紹，而深咎於邈。
entries.en: The court mourned Shao and blamed Li Miao.
entries.literal: People of the time both grieved for Shao and deeply blamed Miao.

entries.zh: 尋有敕罷邈官，遂擯廢終其身。
entries.en: An edict soon stripped Miao of office and he never served again.
entries.literal: Soon an edict dismissed Miao from office, and he was cast out and idle to the end of his life.

entries.zh: 張文瓘，貝州武城人。
entries.en: Zhang Wenjun, a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenjun was a man of Wucheng in Beizhou.

entries.zh: 大業末徙家魏州之昌樂。
entries.en: Late in the Daye era his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.
entries.literal: Late in Daye his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.

entries.zh: 瓘幼孤，事母兄以孝友聞。
entries.en: Orphaned young, he was known for devotion to his mother and elder brother.
entries.literal: Wenjun was orphaned young; he served mother and elder brother and was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.

entries.zh: 貞觀初，舉明經，補并州參軍。
entries.en: In early Zhenguan he passed the Mingjing exam and became a Bingzhou staff officer.
entries.literal: Early in Zhenguan he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Staff Officer of Bingzhou.

entries.zh: 時英國公李勣為長史，深禮之。
entries.en: Li Ji, Duke of Ying, was then regional commander and treated him with great respect.
entries.literal: At the time the Duke of Ying Li Ji was Administrator; he deeply honored him.

entries.zh: 累遷水部員外郎。
entries.en: He rose to vice director of the Water Bureau.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Water Bureau.

entries.zh: 時兄文琮為戶部侍郎，舊制兄弟不許並居台閣，遂出為雲陽令。
entries.en: His brother Wenzong was Vice Minister of Revenue; regulations barred brothers from the central secretariat, so Wenjun was posted as magistrate of Yunyang.
entries.literal: At the time his elder brother Wenzong was Vice Minister of Revenue; by old regulation brothers were not permitted to hold office together in the Censorate and Secretariat, so he was sent out as Magistrate of Yunyang.

entries.zh: 龍朔年，累授東西台舍人、參知政事。
entries.en: In Longshuo he became a drafting officer on the Eastern and Western Terrace and joined the council of state.
entries.literal: In the Longshuo year he was repeatedly appointed Eastern and Western Terrace Drafting Officer and Participant in Governance.

entries.zh: 尋遷東台侍郎、同東西台三品，兼知左史事。
entries.en: He soon became Eastern Terrace vice minister with third-rank standing and oversaw the left historiographer.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved to Vice Minister of the Eastern Terrace, Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Eastern and Western Terrace, and concurrently managed Left Historiographer affairs.

entries.zh: 時初造蓬萊、上陽、合璧等宮，又征討四夷，廄馬有萬匹，倉庫漸虛。
entries.en: New palaces—Penglai, Shangyang, Hebi—were rising, campaigns against the four quarters continued, ten thousand horses filled the stables, and the treasuries thinned.
entries.literal: At the time they were first building the Penglai, Shangyang, and Hebi palaces, and also campaigning against the four barbarians; the stables had ten thousand horses and the granaries gradually emptied.

entries.zh: 文瓘因進諫曰：“人力不可不惜，百姓不可不養，養之逸則富以康，使之勞則怨以叛。
entries.en: Wenjun remonstrated: "Do not waste labor or neglect the people. Ease makes them prosperous; overwork breeds resentment and revolt.
entries.literal: Wenjun therefore submitted a remonstrance, saying: "Human labor must not be unspared; the common people must not be unfed; if fed in ease then they grow rich and healthy, if made to labor then they resent and rebel.

entries.zh: 秦皇、漢武，廣事四夷，多造宮室，使士崩瓦解，戶口減半。
entries.en: Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi campaigned widely and built endlessly until armies shattered and the population halved.
entries.literal: Qin Huang and Han Wu, extensively serving the four barbarians and building many palaces, made knights collapse and disintegrate and household registers halved.

entries.zh: 臣聞製化於未亂，保邦於未危，人罔常懷，懷於有仁。
entries.en: Order is made before chaos, safety before peril; people cling to whoever shows benevolence.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard: establish transformation before disorder, preserve the state before danger; people have no constant hold—they hold to benevolence.

entries.zh: 陛下不製於未亂之前，安能救於既危之後？
entries.en: If you do not act before disorder, how will you rescue the realm once danger arrives?
entries.literal: If Your Majesty does not establish rule before disorder, how can you save after danger has come?

entries.zh: 百姓不堪其弊，必構禍難，殷鑒不遠，近在隋朝。
entries.en: The people cannot endure such burdens; disaster will follow. The lesson is close—the Sui fell only yesterday.
entries.literal: The common people cannot bear these harms and will surely bring calamity; the mirror is not far—near at hand is the Sui dynasty.

entries.zh: 臣願稍安撫之，無使生怨。”
entries.en: I beg you to soothe them and give no cause for anger."
entries.literal: Your servant wishes slightly to soothe them and not let resentment arise."

entries.zh: 上深納其言，於是節減廄馬數千匹，賜文瓘繒錦百段，
entries.en: The emperor took this to heart, cut thousands of horses from the stables, and gave Wenjun a hundred bolts of brocade.
entries.literal: The emperor deeply accepted his words; thereupon he reduced the stables by several thousand horses and bestowed on Wenjun a hundred lengths of silk brocade,

entries.zh: 唐臨，京兆長安人，周內史瑾孫也。
entries.en: Tang Lin, a native of Chang'an in the capital district of Jingzhao, was the grandson of Tang Jin, who had served Zhou as Interior Secretary.
entries.literal: Tang Lin. Tang Lin was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao; he was the grandson of Jin, Interior Secretary of Zhou.

entries.zh: 其先自北海徙關中。
entries.en: His family had originally come from Beihai and later relocated to the Guanzhong region.
entries.literal: His forebears had moved from Beihai to Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 伯父令則，開皇末為左庶子，坐諂事太子勇誅死。
entries.en: His uncle Tang Lingze had served as Left Vice Heir Apparent at the end of the Kaihuang era and was put to death for toadying to Crown Prince Yong.
entries.literal: His paternal uncle Lingze, late in Kaihuang served as Left Vice Heir Apparent, and was executed for the crime of flattering Crown Prince Yong.

entries.zh: 臨少與兄皎俱有令名。
entries.en: In youth, Lin and his elder brother Jiao were both famed for their character.
entries.literal: When young, Lin together with his elder brother Jiao both had an excellent reputation.

entries.zh: 武德初，隱太子總兵東征，臨詣軍獻平王世充之策，太子引直典書坊，尋授右衛率府鎧曹參軍。
entries.en: Early in the Wude era, when the crown prince led the eastern campaign, Lin went to the camp and offered a plan to defeat Wang Shichong. The prince installed him in the crown prince's document office, and he was soon made a staff officer in the Right Guard's armor bureau.
entries.literal: Early in Wude, the Hidden Crown Prince commanded troops on the eastern campaign; Lin went to the army and presented a strategy for pacifying Wang Shichong; the Crown Prince brought him in to straighten the Classic Books Workshop, and soon he was appointed Armor-Cauldron Staff Officer of the Right Guard's Rate Command.

entries.zh: 宮殿廢，出為萬泉丞。
entries.en: After the crown prince's fall, he was posted out as assistant magistrate of Wanquan County.
entries.literal: The Eastern Palace was abolished, and he was sent out to serve as Assistant Magistrate of Wanquan.

entries.zh: 縣有輕囚十數人，會春暮時雨，臨白令請出之，令不許。
entries.en: The county held a dozen-odd light offenders. Late spring brought seasonal rains, and Lin asked the magistrate to release them for planting; the magistrate refused.
entries.literal: The county had more than ten minor prisoners; it happened to be late spring with seasonal rains, and Lin reported to the magistrate requesting to release them; the magistrate did not permit it.

entries.zh: 臨曰：“明公若有所疑，臨請自當其罪。”
entries.en: Lin said, "If you have doubts, I will answer for this myself."
entries.literal: Lin said: "If Your Honor has any doubt, Lin asks to bear the guilt himself."

entries.zh: 令因請假，臨召囚悉令歸家耕種，與之約，令歸係所。
entries.en: The magistrate took leave, and Lin sent every prisoner home to farm under bond to return when called.
entries.literal: The magistrate then took leave; Lin summoned the prisoners and ordered them all to return home to farm, made an agreement with them, and ordered them to return to custody.

entries.zh: 囚等皆感恩貸，至時畢集詣獄，臨因是知名。
entries.en: The prisoners were grateful for the trust; when the deadline came they all presented themselves at the jail, and Lin's name spread.
entries.literal: The prisoners all were grateful for the loan, and when the time came all assembled at the prison; Lin thereby became known.

entries.zh: 義府貌狀溫恭，與人語必嬉怡微笑，而褊忌陰賊。
entries.en: Yifu looked mild and courteous. When he spoke with others he always smiled pleasantly, yet he was narrow-minded, jealous, and secretly malicious.
entries.literal: Yifu in appearance was mild and courteous. When speaking with others he always smiled pleasantly, yet he was narrow-minded, jealous, and secretly malicious.

entries.zh: 既處權要，欲人附己，微忤意者，輒加傾陷。
entries.en: Once he held power, he wanted others to attach themselves to him; whoever slightly displeased him, he would at once bring down and ruin.
entries.literal: Once he held a position of power, he wanted others to attach themselves to him; whoever slightly displeased him, he would at once bring down and ruin.

entries.zh: 故時人言義府笑中有刀，又以其柔而害物，亦謂之「李貓。」
entries.en: Therefore people of the time said that Yifu had a knife hidden in his smile, and because he was soft yet harmed others, they also called him "Li the Cat."
entries.literal: Therefore people of the time said that Yifu had a knife hidden in his smile, and because he was soft yet harmed others, they also called him "Li the Cat."

entries.zh: 顯慶元年，以本官兼太子右庶子，進爵為侯。
entries.en: In the first year of Xianqing, retaining his original post, he was additionally made Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and advanced in rank to marquis.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, in his original post he was additionally made Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and advanced in rank to marquis.

entries.zh: 有洛州婦人淳于氏，坐奸繫於大理，義府聞其姿色，囑大理丞畢正義求為別宅婦，特為雪其罪。
entries.en: There was a woman of Luozhou named Lady Chunyu, imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review on a charge of adultery. Yifu heard of her beauty and instructed Vice Director Bi Zhengyi of the Court of Judicial Review to obtain her as a concubine for his separate residence, and specially had her crime cleared.
entries.literal: There was a woman of Luozhou named Lady Chunyu, imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review on a charge of adultery. Yifu heard of her beauty and instructed Vice Director Bi Zhengyi of the Court of Judicial Review to obtain her as a woman for his separate residence, and specially had her crime cleared.

entries.zh: 卿段寶玄疑其故，遽以狀聞，詔令按其事，正義惶懼自縊而死。
entries.en: Senior Director Duan Baoxuan suspected the reason and hurriedly reported the matter in a memorial. An edict ordered an investigation, and Zhengyi, in fear and panic, hanged himself.
entries.literal: Senior Director Duan Baoxuan suspected the reason and hurriedly reported the matter in a memorial. An edict ordered an investigation of the affair, and Zhengyi, in fear and panic, hanged himself.

entries.zh: 侍御史王義方廷奏義府犯狀，因言其初容貌為劉洎、馬周所幸，由此得進，言詞猥褻。
entries.en: Attending Censor Wang Yifang memorialized in court on Yifu's offenses, and further said that at first his handsome appearance had been favored by Liu Ji and Ma Zhou, by which he had advanced; his language was obscene and lewd.
entries.literal: Attending Censor Wang Yifang memorialized in court Yifu's offenses, and further said that at first his appearance had been favored by Liu Ji and Ma Zhou, by which he had advanced; his language was obscene and lewd.

entries.zh: 帝怒，出義方為萊州司戶，而不問義府奸濫之罪。
entries.en: The emperor was angry and sent Yifang out as registrar of Laizhou, but did not inquire into Yifu's crimes of adultery and abuse.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry and sent Yifang out as registrar of Laizhou, but did not inquire into Yifu's crimes of adultery and abuse.

entries.zh: 義府云：「王御史妄相彈奏，得無愧乎？」
entries.en: Yifu said, "Censor Wang recklessly memorialized against me—should he not feel ashamed?"
entries.literal: Yifu said: "Censor Wang recklessly memorialized against me—should he not feel ashamed?"

entries.zh: 義方對云：「仲尼為魯司寇七日，誅少正卯於兩觀之下；
entries.en: Yifang replied, "Confucius, as Minister of Crime of Lu, within seven days executed Shaozheng Mao beneath the twin watchtowers;
entries.literal: Yifang replied: "Confucius, as Minister of Crime of Lu, within seven days executed Shaozheng Mao beneath the twin watchtowers;

entries.zh: 義方任御史旬有六日，不能去奸邪於雙闕之前，實以為愧。」
entries.en: I have served as censor for sixteen days and could not remove the wicked and corrupt before the twin palace gates—I truly feel ashamed."
entries.literal: Yifang has served as censor for sixteen days and could not remove the wicked and corrupt before the twin palace gates—I truly feel ashamed."

entries.zh: 尋兼太子左庶子。
entries.en: Soon Yifu was additionally made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Soon [Yifu] was additionally made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 二年，代崔敦禮為中書令，兼檢校御史大夫，監修國史、學士並如故。
entries.en: In the second year he replaced Cui Dunli as Director of the Secretariat, additionally serving as acting Censor-in-Chief; his charge over compilation of the national history and his status as academician remained as before.
entries.literal: In the second year [of Xianqing] he replaced Cui Dunli as Director of the Secretariat, additionally serving as acting Censor-in-Chief; his charge over compilation of the national history and his status as academician remained as before.

entries.zh: 尋加太子賓客，進封河間郡公。
entries.en: Soon he was additionally made Mentor to the Heir Apparent and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Hejian Commandery.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally made Mentor to the Heir Apparent and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Hejian Commandery.

entries.zh: 三年，又追贈其父德晟為魏州刺史，諸子孩抱者並列清官，詔為造甲第，榮寵莫之能比。
entries.en: In the third year his father Desheng was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Weizhou; all his sons, even those still in arms, were given posts in the pure offices. An edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—honor and favor none could match.
entries.literal: In the third year his father Desheng was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Weizhou; all his sons, even those still in arms, were given posts in the pure offices. An edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—honor and favor none could match.

entries.zh: 而義府貪冒無厭，與母、妻及諸子、女婿賣官鬻獄，其門如市。
entries.en: Yet Yifu was greedy and insatiable. Together with his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law he sold offices and traded in judicial verdicts; his gate was like a market.
entries.literal: Yet Yifu was greedy and insatiable. Together with his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law he sold offices and traded in judicial verdicts; his gate was like a market.

entries.zh: 多引腹心，廣樹朋黨，傾動朝野。
entries.en: He brought in many trusted intimates and widely planted factions, shaking court and countryside.
entries.literal: He brought in many trusted intimates and widely planted factions, shaking court and countryside.

entries.zh: 初，杜正倫為中書侍郎，義府時任典儀，至是乃與正倫同為中書令。
entries.en: Earlier, Du Zhenglun had been Vice Director of the Secretariat while Yifu had held the post of Ceremonial Officer; now the two of them served together as Directors of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Earlier, Du Zhenglun had been Vice Director of the Secretariat while Yifu had held the post of Ceremonial Officer; now the two of them served together as Directors of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 正倫每以先進自處，不下義府，而中書侍郎李友益密與正倫共圖議義府，更相伺察。
entries.en: Zhenglun always placed himself as the senior man and would not defer to Yifu, while Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi secretly joined Zhenglun in plotting against Yifu; they watched and investigated each other in turn.
entries.literal: Zhenglun always placed himself as the senior man and would not defer to Yifu, while Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi secretly joined Zhenglun in plotting against Yifu; they watched and investigated each other in turn.

entries.zh: 義府知而密令人封奏其事。
entries.en: Yifu learned of this and secretly had someone submit a sealed memorial reporting the affair.
entries.literal: Yifu learned of this and secretly had someone submit a sealed memorial reporting the affair.

entries.zh: 正倫與義府訟於上前，各有曲直。
entries.en: Zhenglun and Yifu argued their case before the emperor; each had points in his favor and against.
entries.literal: Zhenglun and Yifu argued their case before the emperor; each had points in his favor and against.

entries.zh: 上以大臣不和，兩責之，左貶義府為普州刺史，正倫為橫州刺史，友益配流峰州。
entries.en: Because the great ministers were not in harmony, the emperor rebuked them both and demoted Yifu to prefect of Puzhou and Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou; Youyi was sentenced to exile in Feng Prefecture.
entries.literal: Because the great ministers were not in harmony, the emperor rebuked them both and demoted Yifu to prefect of Puzhou and Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou; Youyi was sentenced to exile in Feng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 四年，復召義府兼吏部尚書、同中書門下三品，自余官封如故。
entries.en: In the fourth year Yifu was recalled and additionally made Minister of the Civil Service with chancellor rank; his other offices and enfeoffments remained as before.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Yifu was recalled and additionally made Minister of the Civil Service with the same rank as the three chancellors; his other offices and enfeoffments remained as before.

entries.zh: 龍朔元年，丁母憂去職。
entries.en: In the first year of Longshuo he left office upon mourning for his mother.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longshuo he left office upon mourning for his mother.

entries.zh: 二年，起復為司列太常伯、同東西台三品。
entries.en: In the second year he was recalled from mourning as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with chancellor rank in the Eastern and Western Offices.
entries.literal: In the second year he was recalled from mourning as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with the same rank as the three chancellors of the Eastern and Western Offices.

entries.zh: 義府尋請改葬其祖父，營墓於永康陵側。
entries.en: Yifu soon requested to reinter his grandfather and built a tomb beside Yongkang Mausoleum.
entries.literal: Yifu soon requested to reinter his grandfather and built a tomb beside Yongkang Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 三原令李孝節私課丁夫車牛，為其載土築墳，晝夜不息。
entries.en: Magistrate Li Xiaojie of Sanyuan privately levied corvée laborers, carts, and oxen to haul earth and build the mound for him, working day and night without cease.
entries.literal: Magistrate Li Xiaojie of Sanyuan privately levied corvée laborers, carts, and oxen to haul earth and build the mound for him, working day and night without cease.

entries.zh: 於是高陵、櫟陽、富平、雲陽、華原、同官、涇陽等七縣，以孝節之故，懼不得已，悉課丁車赴役。
entries.en: Thereupon the seven counties of Gaoling, Liyang, Fuping, Yunyang, Huayuan, Tongguan, and Jingyang, fearing they had no choice because of Xiaojie, all levied corvée laborers and carts to go to the work.
entries.literal: Thereupon the seven counties of Gaoling, Liyang, Fuping, Yunyang, Huayuan, Tongguan, and Jingyang, because of Xiaojie, fearing they had no choice, all levied corvée laborers and carts to go to the work.

entries.zh: 高陵令張敬業恭勤怯懦，不堪其勞，死於作所。
entries.en: Magistrate Zhang Jingye of Gaoling, though respectful and diligent, was timid and weak and could not endure the labor; he died at the work site.
entries.literal: Magistrate Zhang Jingye of Gaoling, though respectful and diligent, was timid and weak and could not endure the labor; he died at the work site.

entries.zh: 王公已下，爭致贈遺，其羽儀、導從、轜輶、器服，並窮極奢侈。
entries.en: From princes and dukes downward, all vied to send gifts. The ceremonial guards, escorts, carriages, and accoutrements were all pushed to the utmost extravagance.
entries.literal: From princes and dukes downward, all vied to send gifts. The ceremonial guards, escorts, carriages, and accoutrements were all pushed to the utmost extravagance.

entries.zh: 又會葬車馬祖奠供帳，自灞橋屬於三原，七十里間，相繼不絕。
entries.en: Moreover, at the joint burial the funeral carriages, roadside offerings, and provision tents stretched from Ba Bridge to Sanyuan—a distance of seventy li—unbroken in succession.
entries.literal: Moreover, at the joint burial the funeral carriages, offerings at the roadside, and provision tents stretched from Baa Bridge to Sanyuan—a distance of seventy li—unbroken in succession.

entries.zh: 武德已來，王公葬送之盛，未始有也。
entries.en: Since the Wude era, the splendor of princely and ducal funerals had never been seen before.
entries.literal: Since Wude, the splendor of princely and ducal funerals had never been seen before.

entries.zh: 義府本無藻鑑才，怙武後之勢，專以賣官為事。
entries.en: Yifu originally had no talent for discerning men. Relying on Empress Wu's power, he devoted himself solely to selling offices.
entries.literal: Yifu originally had no talent for discerning men. Relying on Empress Wu's power, he devoted himself solely to selling offices.

entries.zh: 銓序失次，人多怨讟。
entries.en: The order of appointments was disrupted and many people complained and cursed.
entries.literal: The order of appointments was disrupted and many people complained and cursed.

entries.zh: 時殷王初出閣，又以義府兼王府長史。
entries.en: At that time Prince Yin had just left the palace precinct, and Yifu was additionally made chief administrator of the princely household.
entries.literal: At that time Prince Yin had just left the palace precinct, and Yifu was additionally made chief administrator of the princely household.

entries.zh: 三年，遷右相，殷王府長史仍知選事並如故。
entries.en: In the third year he was transferred to Right Chancellor; his post as chief administrator of the princely household and his charge over appointments remained as before.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Right Chancellor; his post as chief administrator of the princely household and his charge over appointments remained as before.

entries.zh: 義府入則諂言自媚，出則肆其奸宄，百僚畏之，無敢言其過者。
entries.en: Yifu, when inside, flattered with fawning words; when outside, he gave free rein to his wickedness. The hundred officials feared him, and none dared speak of his faults.
entries.literal: Yifu, when inside, flattered with fawning words; when outside, he gave free rein to his wickedness. The hundred officials feared him, and none dared speak of his faults.

entries.zh: 帝頗知其罪失，從容誡義府云：「聞卿兒子、女婿皆不謹慎，多作罪過，我亦為卿掩覆，未即公言，卿可誡勖，勿令如此。」
entries.en: The emperor was quite aware of his faults and offenses. He calmly admonished Yifu, saying, "I hear that your sons and sons-in-law are all careless and commit many offenses. I have also covered for you and have not spoken of it publicly. You should warn and encourage them—do not let them go on this way."
entries.literal: The emperor was quite aware of his faults and offenses. He calmly admonished Yifu, saying: "I hear that your sons and sons-in-law are all careless and commit many offenses. I have also covered for you and have not spoken of it publicly. You should warn and encourage them—do not let them go on this way."

entries.zh: 義府勃然變色，腮頸俱起，徐曰：「誰向陛下道此？」
entries.en: Yifu suddenly flushed with anger; his cheeks and neck both reddened. He said slowly, "Who told Your Majesty this?"
entries.literal: Yifu suddenly changed color in anger; his cheeks and neck both flushed. He said slowly: "Who told Your Majesty this?"

entries.zh: 上曰：「但我言如是，何須問我所從得耶！」
entries.en: The emperor said, "But I speak thus—why must you ask where I heard it from!"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "But I speak thus—why must you ask where I heard it from!"

entries.zh: 義府睆然，殊不引咎，緩步而去。
entries.en: Yifu stared blankly, showed no sign of accepting blame, and walked away at an unhurried pace.
entries.literal: Yifu stared blankly, showed no sign of accepting blame, and walked away at an unhurried pace.

entries.zh: 上亦優容之。
entries.en: The emperor also treated him with forbearance.
entries.literal: The emperor also treated him with forbearance.

entries.zh: 初，五禮儀注，自前代相沿，吉凶畢舉。
entries.en: Earlier, the ceremonial regulations for the Five Rites, handed down from former ages, included both auspicious and inauspicious rites in full.
entries.literal: Earlier, the ceremonial regulations for the Five Rites, handed down from former ages, included both auspicious and inauspicious rites in full.

entries.zh: 太常博士蕭楚材、孔志約以皇室凶禮為預備凶事，非臣子所宜言之。
entries.en: Academicians Xiao Chucai and Kong Zhiyue of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that the imperial mourning rites, as preparations for inauspicious events, were not what subjects should speak of.
entries.literal: Academicians Xiao Chucai and Kong Zhiyue of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that the imperial mourning rites, as preparations for inauspicious events, were not what subjects should speak of.

entries.zh: 義府深然之。
entries.en: Yifu deeply agreed with this.
entries.literal: Yifu deeply agreed with this.

entries.zh: 於是悉刪而焚焉。
entries.en: Thereupon he had them all deleted and burned.
entries.literal: Thereupon he had them all deleted and burned.

entries.zh: 義府既貴之後，又自言本出趙郡，始與諸李敘昭穆，而無賴之徒苟合，藉其權勢，拜伏為兄叔者甚眾。
entries.en: After Yifu had risen to high rank, he also declared that his family originally came from Zhao Commandery and began to arrange senior and junior relations with various members of the Li clan. Many rascals who attached themselves to him, relying on his power, bowed and called him elder brother or uncle.
entries.literal: After Yifu had risen to high rank, he also declared that his family originally came from Zhao Commandery and began to arrange senior and junior relations with various members of the Li clan. Rascals who attached themselves to him, relying on his power, were many who bowed and called him elder brother or uncle.

entries.zh: 給事中李崇德初亦與同譜敘昭穆，及義府出為普州刺史，遂即除削。
entries.en: Attendant Li Chongde had at first also joined him in arranging their clan genealogy, but when Yifu was demoted to Prefect of Puzhou, Chongde was immediately struck from the roll.
entries.literal: Attendant Li Chongde at first also joined with him in arranging the clan genealogy and seniority, but when Yifu was sent out as Prefect of Puzhou, he was at once struck from the roll.

entries.zh: 義府聞而銜之，及重為宰相，乃令人誣構其罪，竟下獄自殺。
entries.en: Yifu heard of this and bore a grudge. When he again became chief minister, he had charges fabricated against Chongde, who was thrown into prison and took his own life.
entries.literal: Yifu heard of this and bore a grudge; when he again became chief minister, he had someone fabricate charges against him, and in the end he was thrown into prison and committed suicide.

entries.zh: 初，貞觀中，太宗命吏部尚書高士廉、御史大夫韋挺、中書侍郎岑文本、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等及四方士大夫諳練門閥者修《氏族志》，勒成百卷，升降去取，時稱允當，頒下諸州，藏為永式。
entries.en: Earlier, during the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong ordered Gao Shilian, Wei Ting, Cen Wenben, Linghu Defen, and other officials, together with scholars versed in distinguished clans from across the realm, to compile the Genealogies of Clans. The work ran to a hundred scrolls, and its rankings were widely judged fair. It was distributed to all prefectures and preserved as a permanent standard.
entries.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenguan era, the Taizong Emperor ordered Minister of Personnel Gao Shilian, Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, Secretariat Vice Director Cen Wenben, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others, together with gentlemen from all quarters versed in distinguished clans, to compile the Genealogies of Clans. The work was completed in a hundred scrolls; promotions and demotions in rank were at the time called fair and appropriate. It was distributed to all prefectures and preserved as a permanent standard.

entries.zh: 義府恥其家代無名，乃奏改此書，專委禮部郎中孔志約、著作郎楊仁卿、太子洗馬史玄道、太常丞呂才重修。
entries.en: Ashamed that his family had for generations lacked renown, Yifu memorialized to revise the work and entrusted Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, and Lü Cai with a full revision.
entries.literal: Yifu was ashamed that his family for generations had been without renown and therefore memorialized to revise this book, specially entrusting Section Director of Rites Kong Zhiyue, Compiler Yang Renqing, Crown Prince's Libationer Shi Xuandao, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lü Cai to revise it anew.

entries.zh: 志約等遂立格云：「皇朝得五品官者，皆升士流。」
entries.en: Zhiyue and the others then established a rule: "In our dynasty, all who obtain office of the fifth rank are to be entered among the gentry."
entries.literal: Zhiyue and the others thereupon established a rule saying: "In our dynasty, all who obtain office of the fifth rank are to be raised into the gentry stream."

entries.zh: 於是兵卒以軍功致五品者，盡入書限，更名為《姓氏錄》。
entries.en: Thereupon soldiers who through military merit reached the fifth rank were all entered in the register, which was renamed the Register of Surnames.
entries.literal: Thereupon soldiers and commoners who through military merit reached the fifth rank all entered the limits of the book, and it was renamed the Register of Surnames.

entries.zh: 由是搢紳士大夫多恥被甄敘，皆號此書為「勳格」。
entries.en: Because of this, many gentry and scholar-officials were ashamed to be listed in it and called the book the "Merit Register."
entries.literal: Because of this, many gentry and scholar-officials were ashamed to be entered in the selection and all called this book the "Merit Register."

entries.zh: 義府仍奏收天下《氏族志》本焚之。
entries.en: Yifu also memorialized to collect all copies of the Genealogies of Clans throughout the realm and burn them.
entries.literal: Yifu still memorialized to collect all copies of the Genealogies of Clans throughout the realm and burn them.

entries.zh: 關東魏、齊舊姓，雖皆淪替，猶相矜尚，自為婚姻。
entries.en: The old families of Wei and Qi east of the Pass, though fallen from power, still prided themselves on their standing and married only among themselves.
entries.literal: The old surnames of Wei and Qi east of the Pass, though all had fallen from power, still prided themselves on one another and formed marriages among themselves.

entries.zh: 義府為子求婚不得，乃奏隴西李等七家，不得相與為婚。
entries.en: When Yifu failed to secure a marriage for his son, he memorialized that the seven great families, including the Li of Longxi, must not intermarry with one another.
entries.literal: When Yifu could not obtain a marriage for his son, he memorialized that the seven families including the Li of Longxi must not intermarry with one another.

entries.zh: 許敬宗
entries.en: Xu Jingzong
entries.literal: Xu Jingzong

entries.zh: 貞觀二十年，封為陳王。
entries.en: In 646 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year of Zhenguan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.

entries.zh: 永徽元年，拜雍州牧。
entries.en: In 650 he was appointed Governor of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, he was appointed Governor of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 時王皇后無子，其舅中書令柳奭說後謀立忠為皇太子，以忠母賤，冀其親己，後然之。
entries.en: Empress Wang was childless, and her uncle Liu Shi, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, urged her to have Zhong named crown prince, arguing that because his mother was of humble birth he would remain close to the empress. She agreed.
entries.literal: At that time Empress Wang had no son; her uncle, Chief Minister of the Secretariat Liu Shi, urged the empress to plot making Zhong crown prince, reasoning that because Zhong's mother was of low status he would be drawn close to her; the empress agreed.

entries.zh: 奭與尚書右僕射褚遂良、侍中韓瑗諷、太尉長孫無忌、右僕射於誌寧等，固請立忠為儲後，高宗許之。
entries.en: Liu Shi joined Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Zhangsun Wuji, Yu Zhining, and others in pressing Gaozong to name Zhong heir apparent, and the emperor agreed.
entries.literal: Liu Shi, together with Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Chu Suiliang, Palace Attendant Han Yuan, Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Right Vice Director Yu Zhining, and others, earnestly petitioned to establish Zhong as heir apparent, and Emperor Gaozong consented.

entries.zh: 三年，立忠為皇太子，大赦天下，五品已上子為父後者賜勳一級。
entries.en: In 652 Zhong was named crown prince. A general amnesty was declared, and heirs of officials of fifth rank and above received one grade of merit.
entries.literal: In the third year, Zhong was established as crown prince; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm, and sons of fifth rank and above who were heirs to their fathers were granted one grade of merit.

entries.zh: 六年，加元服，製大辟罪已下並降一等，大酺三日。
entries.en: In 655 he came of age. Capital crimes and all lesser offenses were reduced by one degree, and the court held three days of public celebration.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he received the cap of manhood; an edict reduced all crimes below capital punishment by one degree, and great feasting was held for three days.

entries.zh: 其年，王皇后被廢，武昭儀所生皇子弘年三歲。
entries.en: That year Empress Wang was deposed, and Lady Wu's son Hong was three years old.
entries.literal: That same year Empress Wang was deposed, and the prince Hong born to Lady Wu Zhaoyi was three years old.

entries.zh: 禮部尚書許敬宗希旨上疏曰：“伏惟陛下憲章千古，含育萬邦，爰立聖慈，母儀天下。
entries.en: Xu Jingzong, Minister of Rites, submitted a flattering memorial: "Your Majesty's laws illumine the ages and nurture all lands; you have raised a sage and loving consort who embodies motherhood for the realm.
entries.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong, seeking to please, submitted a memorial saying: "I humbly consider that Your Majesty's statutes illumine the ages and nurture the myriad realms; you have established a sage and loving consort who embodies motherhood for the world.

entries.zh: 既而皇后生子，合處少陽。
entries.en: Now that the empress has borne a son, he rightly belongs in the eastern palace of the heir.
entries.literal: Now that the empress has borne a son, he ought to occupy the position of lesser yang.

entries.zh: 出自塗山，是謂吾君之胤；
entries.en: Born of Tushan, he is truly our sovereign's heir;
entries.literal: Born from Tushan, he is truly the heir of our lord;

entries.zh: 夙聞胎教，宜展問豎之心。
entries.en: reared from the womb in virtue, he should show the mind eager to learn from his teachers.
entries.literal: long versed in prenatal instruction, he should display the heart of one who inquires after his tutor.

entries.zh: 乃復為孽奪宗，降居藩邸，是使前星匿彩，瑤嶽韜峰。
entries.en: Yet a lesser son again holds the succession while the true heir is sent to a princely residence, dimming the heir's star and hiding the jade mountain's peak.
entries.literal: yet again a bastard has seized the succession and been demoted to a princely residence, causing the former star to hide its brilliance and the jade peak to veil its splendor.

entries.zh: 臣以愚誠，竊所未喻。
entries.en: In my humble sincerity I cannot understand this.
entries.literal: Your servant, in his foolish sincerity, privately fails to understand this.

entries.zh: 且今之守器，素非皇嫡，永徽爰始，國本未生，權引彗星，越升明兩。
entries.en: Moreover, the present heir was never the legitimate son. From the start of Yonghui, before the true heir was born, a comet was provisionally elevated above the rightful pair.
entries.literal: Moreover, the present holder of the vessel was never the legitimate imperial son; from the beginning of Yonghui, when the foundation of the state had not yet been born, a comet was provisionally drawn forth to ascend beyond the bright pair.

entries.zh: 近者元妃載誕，正胤降神，重光日融，爝暉宜息。
entries.en: Lately the chief consort has borne a son; the true heir has come down from heaven. The sun's doubled light should shine as one, and the lesser flame ought to be put out.
entries.literal: Recently the primary consort has given birth; the legitimate heir has descended as a spirit; the doubled radiance of the sun should merge, and the torchlight ought to be extinguished.

entries.zh: 安可以茲傍統，叨據溫文？
entries.en: How can this collateral line presumptuously hold the heir's place?
entries.literal: How can this collateral succession presumptuously occupy the gentle and cultured role?

entries.zh: 國有諍臣，孰逃其責！
entries.en: When the state has ministers who speak plainly, who can shirk this duty!
entries.literal: When the state has remonstrating ministers, who can escape this duty!

entries.zh: 竊惟息姑克讓，可以思齊；
entries.en: I reflect that Xigong's willingness to yield offers a model to follow;
entries.literal: I privately reflect that Xigong's capacity for yielding offers a model for emulation;

entries.zh: 劉強守藩，宜遵往軌。
entries.en: and Liu Qiang's holding to his fief should follow precedent.
entries.literal: Liu Qiang's guarding of his fief ought to follow the former track.

entries.zh: 追跡太伯，不亦休哉？
entries.en: To follow Taibo's example—would that not be excellent?
entries.literal: To follow in the footsteps of Taibo—would that not be excellent?

entries.zh: 踵武延陵，故常安矣。
entries.en: Following Yanling's path, all would remain secure.
entries.literal: Treading in the martial wake of Yanling, one would ever be secure.

entries.zh: 寧可反植枝幹，久易位於天庭；
entries.en: How can branches be planted upside down and positions in the court long be reversed;
entries.literal: How can one plant branches upside down and long exchange positions in the celestial court;

entries.zh: 倒襲衣裳，使違方於震位？
entries.en: or garments be worn inside out so that the improper occupies the heir's place?
entries.literal: invert upper and lower garments and set what is improper in the position of Zhen?

entries.zh: 蠢爾黎庶，雲誰係心？
entries.en: The common people—upon whom will their hearts depend?
entries.literal: Your dull common people—upon whom do their hearts depend?

entries.zh: 垂裕後昆，將何播美？”
entries.en: What glory will you leave to posterity?"
entries.literal: In bestowing abundance on later generations, what beauty will you spread abroad?"

entries.zh: 高宗從之。
entries.en: Gaozong accepted the memorial.
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozong followed this advice.

entries.zh: 顯慶元年，廢忠為梁王，授梁州都督，賜實封二千戶，物二萬段，甲第一區。
