entries.en: In 656 Zhong was deposed and made Prince of Liang, with appointment as commissioner of Liangzhou, a substantive fief of two thousand households, twenty thousand bolts of goods, and a suit of first-rank armor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, Zhong was deposed and made Prince of Liang, appointed Military Commissioner of Liangzhou, granted a substantive fief of two thousand households, twenty thousand bolts of goods, and one first-rank suit of armor.

entries.zh: 其年，轉房州刺史。
entries.en: That year he was transferred to Prefect of Fangzhou.
entries.literal: That same year he was transferred to be Prefect of Fangzhou.

entries.zh: 讚曰：父子天性，嬖能害正。
entries.en: In praise: Father and son share nature's bond, yet favorites can destroy what is right.
entries.literal: In praise it is said: Father and son share heaven's nature, yet favorites can harm what is right.

entries.zh: 宜臼、申生，翻為不令。
entries.en: Yijiu and Shensheng were turned into unworthy sons.
entries.literal: Yijiu and Shensheng were turned into unworthy sons.

entries.zh: 唐年鈞德，章懷最仁。
entries.en: In Tang's age of measured virtue, Zhanghuai was the most humane.
entries.literal: In Tang's years of balanced virtue, Zhanghuai was most humane.

entries.zh: 凶母畏明，取樂於身。
entries.en: The vicious mother feared the bright prince and sought only her own pleasure.
entries.literal: The vicious mother feared the bright; she took pleasure for herself alone.

entries.zh: 高宗中宗諸子
entries.en: Sons of Emperor Gaozong and Emperor Zhongzong
entries.literal: The sons of Emperor Gaozong and Emperor Zhongzong

entries.zh: 自春秋之後，禮義漸頹，風俗塵昏，愧恥心盡，疾走先得者爲上，奪攘投會者爲能。
entries.en: After the Spring and Autumn period, ritual and righteousness gradually collapsed, custom grew dusty and dim, and the heart of shame was exhausted. Those who ran fastest and arrived first were esteemed; those who seized by force and seized opportunity were deemed capable.
entries.literal: After the Spring and Autumn period, ritual and righteousness gradually collapsed, custom grew dusty and dim, and the heart of shame was exhausted. Those who ran fastest and arrived first were esteemed; those who seized by force and seized opportunity were deemed capable.

entries.zh: 加以八世專齊，三家分晉，子貢之亂五國，蘇秦之鬥七雄，苛刻繁興，經籍道息，莫不長詐術，貴攻戰，萬姓皆戴爪牙，無人不屬觜距。
entries.en: Moreover, the eight generations monopolized Qi, the three families divided Jin, Zigong threw five states into chaos, and Su Qin set seven powers at odds. Harshness and severity flourished, the way of the classics ceased, and all prized deceit and stratagem and value attack and warfare. The myriad people all wore claws and fangs; there was no one who did not possess beak and spur.
entries.literal: Moreover, the eight generations monopolized Qi, the three families divided Jin, Zigong threw five states into chaos, and Su Qin set seven powers at odds. Harshness and severity flourished, the way of the classics ceased, and all prized deceit and stratagem and value attack and warfare. The myriad people all wore claws and fangs; there was no one who did not possess beak and spur.

entries.zh: 所以商鞅欺故友，李斯囚舊交，孫臏喪足於龐涓，張儀得誌於陳軫。
entries.en: Therefore Shang Yang deceived an old friend, Li Si imprisoned a former associate, Sun Bin lost his feet at the hands of Pang Juan, and Zhang Yi achieved his wish over Chen Zhen.
entries.literal: Therefore Shang Yang deceived an old friend, Li Si imprisoned a former associate, Sun Bin lost his feet at the hands of Pang Juan, and Zhang Yi achieved his wish over Chen Zhen.

entries.zh: 一旅之眾，便欲稱王；
entries.en: A single company of men then wished to declare themselves kings;
entries.literal: A single company of men then wished to declare themselves kings;

entries.zh: 再戰之雄，爭來奉帝。
entries.en: heroes who had fought twice contended to offer allegiance to an emperor.
entries.literal: heroes who had fought twice contended to offer allegiance to an emperor.

entries.zh: 先王會盟之禮，昔時樽俎之容，三代玄風，掃地至盡。
entries.en: The alliance rites of former kings and the bearing of former times at the feast — the mysterious customs of the Three Dynasties were swept clean to the ground.
entries.literal: The alliance rites of former kings and the bearing of former times at the feast — the mysterious customs of the Three Dynasties were swept clean to the ground.

entries.zh: 況始皇削平區宇，殊非至公，李斯之作股肱，罕循大道，人無見德，唯虐是聞。
entries.en: Moreover, when the First Emperor pacified the realm, it was by no means supremely fair. When Li Si served as his right arm, he rarely followed the great way. The people saw no virtue — they heard only cruelty.
entries.literal: Moreover, when the First Emperor pacified the realm, it was by no means supremely fair. When Li Si served as his right arm, he rarely followed the great way. The people saw no virtue — they heard only cruelty.

entries.zh: 當此時也，主猜於上，人駭於下，父不能保之於子，君不能得之於臣。
entries.en: At that time the ruler was suspicious above and the people terrified below. Fathers could not preserve their sons; lords could not obtain their ministers.
entries.literal: At that time the ruler was suspicious above and the people terrified below. Fathers could not preserve their sons; lords could not obtain their ministers.

entries.zh: 欲使始皇分土奸雄，建侯薄俗，若喻晉、鄭之可依，便借賊兵而資盜糧，寄龍魚而助風雨，不可行也。
entries.en: To wish to make the First Emperor divide territory among treacherous heroes and establish marquisates amid shallow custom — if one were to say that Jin and Zheng could be relied upon, it would be like lending weapons to bandits and supplying grain to robbers, entrusting dragons and fish and aiding wind and rain. It could not be done.
entries.literal: To wish to make the First Emperor divide territory among treacherous heroes and establish marquisates amid shallow custom — if one were to say that Jin and Zheng could be relied upon, it would be like lending weapons to bandits and supplying grain to robbers, entrusting dragons and fish and aiding wind and rain. It could not be done.

entries.zh: 是以秦鑒周德之綿深，懼己圖之不遠，罷侯置守，高下在心，天下製在一人，百姓不聞二主。
entries.en: Therefore Qin took warning from Zhou's virtue extending deep and long, feared that its own design would not reach far, abolished marquisates and established governors. High and low were in its heart; the realm was controlled by one man, and the common people heard not of two masters.
entries.literal: Therefore Qin took warning from Zhou's virtue extending deep and long, feared that its own design would not reach far, abolished marquisates and established governors. High and low were in its heart; the realm was controlled by one man, and the common people heard not of two masters.

entries.zh: 直是不得行其世封，非薄功臣而賤骨肉也。
entries.en: It was simply that hereditary enfeoffment could not be practiced — not that it slighted meritorious ministers or despised kin.
entries.literal: It was simply that hereditary enfeoffment could not be practiced — not that it slighted meritorious ministers or despised kin.

entries.zh: 王及善，洺州邯鄲人也。
entries.en: Wang Jishan was a native of Handan in Mozhou.
entries.literal: Wang Jishan was a native of Handan in Mozhou.

entries.zh: 父君愕。
entries.en: His father was Jun'e.
entries.literal: His father was Jun'e.

entries.zh: 隋大業末，并州人王君廓掠邯鄲，君愕往說君廓曰：「方今萬乘失禦，英雄競起，誠宜撫納遺氓，保全形勝，按甲以觀時變，擁眾而歸真主，此富貴可圖也。
entries.en: At the end of the Sui Emperor Yang's reign, Wang Junguo of Bingzhou raided Handan. Jun'e went to persuade Junguo, saying, "At present the throne has lost its guidance and heroes are rising in rivalry. You truly ought to win over the scattered populace, secure your strategic strongholds, hold your forces in check to observe how affairs change, gather followers and return them to the true sovereign — then wealth and honor can be pursued.
entries.literal: At the end of the Sui Emperor Yang's reign, Wang Junguo of Bingzhou raided Handan. Jun'e went to persuade Junguo, saying, "At present the imperial throne has lost its guidance and heroes are rising in rivalry. You truly ought to win over the scattered populace, secure your strategic strongholds, hold your forces in check to observe how affairs change, gather followers and return them to the true sovereign — then wealth and honor can be pursued.

entries.zh: 今足下居無尺土之地，守無兼旬之糧，恣行殘忍，所過攘奪，竊爲足下寒心矣。」
entries.en: Now you possess not a foot of territory, nor food enough for even ten days. You indulge in cruelty wherever you go and plunder as you pass. I fear for you on your account."
entries.literal: Now you possess not a foot of territory, nor food enough for even ten days. You indulge in cruelty wherever you go and plunder as you pass. I fear for you on your account."

entries.zh: 君廓曰：「計將安出？」
entries.en: Junguo said, "What plan do you propose?"
entries.literal: Junguo said, "What plan do you propose?"

entries.zh: 君愕爲陳井陘之險，可先往據之。
entries.en: Jun'e explained the strategic advantages of Jingxing Pass and advised that he go there first to seize it.
entries.literal: Jun'e explained the strategic advantages of Jingxing Pass and advised that he go there first to seize it.

entries.zh: 君廓從其言，乃屯井陘山。
entries.en: Junguo followed his advice and encamped on Mount Jingxing.
entries.literal: Junguo followed his advice and encamped on Mount Jingxing.

entries.zh: 歲餘，會義師入定關中，乃與君廓率所部萬餘人來降，拜大將軍。
entries.en: After more than a year, when the righteous army entered and pacified Guanzhong, he and Junguo led their more than ten thousand followers to surrender and were appointed Grand General.
entries.literal: After more than a year, when the righteous army entered and pacified Guanzhong, he and Junguo led their more than ten thousand followers to surrender and were appointed Grand General.

entries.zh: 頻以戰功封新興縣公，累遷左武衛將軍。
entries.en: For repeated military achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing County and was promoted in succession to General of the Left Martial Guards.
entries.literal: Repeatedly for military achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing County and was promoted in succession to General of the Left Martial Guards.

entries.zh: 從太宗征遼東，兼領左屯營兵馬。
entries.en: When he followed Emperor Taizong on the campaign against Liaodong, he also commanded the troops of the Left Encampment.
entries.literal: When he followed Emperor Taizong on the campaign against Liaodong, he also commanded the troops of the Left Encampment.

entries.zh: 與高麗戰於駐蹕山，君愕先鋒陷陣，力戰而死。
entries.en: Fighting the Goguryeo at Mount Zhubi, Jun'e led the vanguard in breaking the enemy lines and died fighting fiercely.
entries.literal: Fighting the Goguryeo at Mount Zhubi, Jun'e led the vanguard in breaking the enemy lines and died fighting fiercely.

entries.zh: 太宗深痛悼之，贈左衛大將軍、幽州都督、邢國公，賜東園秘器，陪葬昭陵。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong deeply mourned him, posthumously appointing him Grand General of the Left Guard, Military Governor of Youzhou, and Duke of Xing State, granting him the Eastern Garden funerary vessels and permitting burial at Zhaoling.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizong deeply mourned him, posthumously appointing him Grand General of the Left Guard, Military Governor of Youzhou, and Duke of Xing State, granting him the Eastern Garden funerary vessels and permitting burial at Zhaoling.

entries.zh: 其年秋，柬之表請歸襄州養疾。
entries.en: That autumn Jianzhi asked to return to Xiang Prefecture to recover from illness.
entries.literal: That autumn Jianzhi memorialized requesting to return to Xiang Prefecture to nurse his illness.

entries.zh: 許之，仍特授襄州刺史，又拜其子漪爲著作郎，令隨父之任。
entries.en: The request was granted; he was specially appointed prefect of Xiang, and his son Yi was made drafting official and sent with him to his post.
entries.literal: The request was granted; he was specially appointed prefect of Xiang Prefecture, and his son Yi was appointed drafting official and ordered to accompany his father to his post.

entries.zh: 上親賦詩祖道，又令群公餞送於定鼎門外。
entries.en: The emperor personally composed a farewell poem and had the assembled ministers see him off with a feast outside the Dingding Gate.
entries.literal: The emperor personally composed a poem to send him off on the road, and also ordered the assembled lords to give a farewell feast outside the Dingding Gate.

entries.zh: 柬之至襄州，有鄉親舊交抵罪者，必深文致法，無所縱舍。
entries.en: Once in Xiang Prefecture, Jianzhi prosecuted kinsmen and old friends who had run afoul of the law with the utmost severity and showed no mercy.
entries.literal: When Jianzhi reached Xiang Prefecture, if kinsmen or old acquaintances were charged with crimes, he always applied the law with the utmost severity and showed no leniency.

entries.zh: 其子漪恃以立功，每見諸少長，不以禮接，時議以爲不能易荊楚之剽性焉。
entries.en: His son Yi, relying on his father's standing, treated elders and juniors without proper courtesy; people said he could not change the fierce Jing-Chu temperament.
entries.literal: His son Yi, relying on his father's achievements, whenever he met elders or juniors did not receive them with proper courtesy; contemporary opinion held that he could not change the fierce nature of Jing-Chu.

entries.zh: 尋爲武三思所構，貶授新州司馬。
entries.en: Soon Wu Sansi framed him, and he was demoted to military adjutant of Xin.
entries.literal: Soon he was framed by Wu Sansi and demoted to military adjutant of Xin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 柬之至新州，憤恚而卒，年八十餘，景雲元年，製曰：「褒德紀功，事華典冊；
entries.en: Jianzhi reached Xin Prefecture, died in anger and resentment at over eighty, and in the first year of Jingyun an edict declared, "To honor virtue and record merit adorns the canonical records;
entries.literal: When Jianzhi reached Xin Prefecture he died in anger and resentment, aged over eighty. In the first year of Jingyun an edict said, "To honor virtue and record merit is the splendor of canonical records;

entries.zh: 飾終追遠，理光名教。
entries.en: to adorn the end and recall the distant past illuminates the principles of moral teaching.
entries.literal: to adorn the end and recall the distant past illuminates the principles of name and teaching.

entries.zh: 故吏部尚書張柬之翼戴興運，謨明帝道，經綸謇諤，風範猶存。
entries.en: The late Minister of Personnel Zhang Jianzhi aided the rising fortune, counseled with clarity on the imperial way, ordered the realm with forthright remonstrance, and his exemplary bearing still endures.
entries.literal: The late Minister of Personnel Zhang Jianzhi aided and upheld the rising fortune, counseled with clarity on the imperial way, ordered the realm with forthright remonstrance, and his exemplary bearing still endures.

entries.zh: 往屬回邪，構成釁咎，無辜放逐，淪沒荒遐。
entries.en: Through perverse wickedness a cause of offense was fabricated; he was banished without guilt and lost in distant exile.
entries.literal: Formerly, through perverse wickedness, a cause of offense was fabricated; he was banished without guilt and sank into distant exile.

entries.zh: 言念勳賢，良深軫悼，宜加寵贈，式賁幽泉。
entries.en: Remembering his merit, I am deeply grieved; he should receive added posthumous honors to adorn the realm below.
entries.literal: Thinking on his meritorious worth, I am deeply grieved; he should receive added posthumous honors to adorn the hidden realm.

entries.zh: 可贈中書令，封漢陽郡公。」
entries.en: Let him be posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang."
entries.literal: He may be posthumously given the post of Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang commandery."

entries.zh: 建中初，又贈司徒。
entries.en: Early in Jianzhong he was again posthumously made Minister of Education.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he was again posthumously given the title Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 桓彥範敬暉崔玄暐張柬之袁恕己
entries.en: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, and Yuan Shuji
entries.literal: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuji

entries.zh: 及安祿山反，上以封常清、高仙芝喪敗，召翰入，拜為皇太子先鋒兵馬元帥，以田良丘為御史中丞，充行軍司馬，以王思禮、鉗耳大福、李承光、蘇法鼎、管崇嗣及蕃將火拔歸仁、李武定、渾萼、契苾寧等為裨將，河隴、朔方兵及蕃兵與高仙芝舊卒共二十萬，拒賊於潼關。
entries.en: When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated, the emperor summoned Han and appointed him Vanguard Commander of the Heir Apparent's Army; Tian Liangqiu was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Campaigning Major; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the barbarian generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, Qibi Ning, and others were made deputy generals — Hexi, Longyou, and Shuofang troops and barbarian soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops, two hundred thousand in all, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.
entries.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and lost, the emperor summoned Han and appointed him Vanguard Commander of the Heir Apparent's Army; Tian Liangqiu was made Censor-in-Chief and Campaigning Major; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and barbarian generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, Qibi Ning, and others were made deputy generals — Hexi, Longyou, Shuofang troops and barbarian soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops, two hundred thousand in all, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.

entries.zh: 上御勤政樓勞遣之，百僚出餞於郊。
entries.en: The emperor saw them off from the Hall of Diligent Government; the officials feasted them outside the walls.
entries.literal: The emperor attended at the Hall of Diligent Government to comfort and send them off; the hundred officials went out to feast them at the suburbs.

entries.zh: 十五載，加翰尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was made Left Vice Director and Associate Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Han was given Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and made Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 先是，翰數奏祿山雖竊河朔，而不得人心，請持重以弊之，彼自離心，因而翦滅之，可不傷兵擒茲寇矣。
entries.en: Han had repeatedly urged that though Lushan had seized Hebei he lacked popular support — hold firm and wear them down, let them split of themselves, and destroy this bandit without heavy losses.
entries.literal: Earlier Han had repeatedly memorialized that though Lushan had seized Hebei and Shuofang he had not won men's hearts; he asked to hold firm and wear them down — they would split of themselves, and thus he could cut them off and capture this bandit without harming the troops.

entries.zh: 賊將崔乾祐於陜郡潛鋒蓄銳，而覘者奏雲「賊殊無備」，上然之，命悉眾速討之。
entries.en: Rebel general Cui Qianyu was secretly massing at Shan, but scouts reported "the rebels were unprepared"; the emperor believed it and ordered a full assault at once.
entries.literal: The rebel general Cui Qianyu at Shan commandery secretly sharpened his edge and stored his strength, but scouts reported "the rebels are quite unprepared"; the emperor agreed and ordered the whole force to attack quickly.

entries.zh: 翰奏曰：「賊既始為AT逆，祿山久習用兵，必不肯無備，是陰計也。
entries.en: Han memorialized, "The rebels have risen in treason; Lushan is a veteran commander — he will not be unprepared; this is a trap.
entries.literal: Han memorialized: "Since the rebels have begun treason, Lushan has long practiced warfare — he will certainly not be without preparation; this is a hidden stratagem.

entries.zh: 且賊兵遠來，利在速戰。
entries.en: The rebels have marched far — they need a quick fight.
entries.literal: Moreover the rebel troops have come from afar — their advantage lies in swift battle.

entries.zh: 今王師自戰其地，利在堅守，不利輕出；
entries.en: Our army fights on its own ground — we should hold firm, not sally lightly;
entries.literal: Now the imperial army fights on its own ground — the advantage lies in stubborn defense, not in sallying lightly;

entries.zh: 若輕出關，是入其算。
entries.en: to leave the pass lightly is to fall into their trap.
entries.literal: if we lightly leave the pass, we enter their calculation.

entries.zh: 乞更觀事勢。」
entries.en: I beg to watch the situation longer."
entries.literal: I beg to observe the situation further."

entries.zh: 楊國忠恐其謀己，屢奏使出兵。
entries.en: Yang Guozhong, fearing Han plotted against him, repeatedly urged an advance.
entries.literal: Yang Guozhong feared Han plotted against him and repeatedly memorialized to make the army advance.

entries.zh: 上久處太平，不練軍事，既為國忠眩惑，中使相繼督責。
entries.en: The emperor, long at peace and unused to war, was swayed by Guozhong; palace envoys pressed Han in succession.
entries.literal: The emperor had long dwelt in peace and did not practice military affairs; having been dazzled and misled by Guozhong, palace envoys came in succession to supervise and reproach.

entries.zh: 翰不得已，引師出關。
entries.en: Han had no choice and led the army out.
entries.literal: Han had no choice and led the army out of the pass.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：大盜作梗，祿山亂常，詞雖欲誅國忠，誌則謀危社稷。
entries.en: Commentary. The historiographer writes: The great rebel rose; Lushan overturned the order — he spoke of punishing Guozhong but aimed at the throne itself.
entries.literal: Commentary. The historiographer says: The great bandit raised obstruction; Lushan disturbed the norms — in words he wished to execute Guozhong, but in intent he plotted to endanger the altars of state.

entries.zh: 於時承平日久，金革道消，封常清、高仙芝相次率不教之兵，募市人之眾，以抗AT寇，失律喪師。
entries.en: Peace had lasted so long that warcraft had faded; Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi in turn led untrained troops and market rabble against the rebels — and lost their armies.
entries.literal: At that time peace had lasted long and the way of arms and armor had faded; Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi in succession led untrained troops and recruited crowds of market folk to resist the rebel band — they lost discipline and lost their armies.

entries.zh: 哥舒翰廢疾於家，起專兵柄，二十萬眾拒賊關門，軍中之務不親，委任又非其所。
entries.en: Ge Shuhan, invalid at home, was raised to sole command; two hundred thousand held the pass — yet he did not lead in person and his deputies were unfit.
entries.literal: Ge Shuhan, disabled by illness at home, was raised to monopolize military power; two hundred thousand resisted the rebels at the pass gate — he did not personally handle army affairs, and those entrusted were not fit for their posts.

entries.zh: 及遇羯賊，旋致敗亡，天子以之播遷，自身以之拘執，此皆命帥而不得其人也。
entries.en: They met the rebels and were swiftly destroyed — the emperor fled, they were captured — all because the wrong men were given command.
entries.literal: When they met the Jie rebels they quickly met defeat and ruin — the Son of Heaven was driven to wander, they themselves were seized and held — all this from appointing commanders and not getting the right men.

entries.zh: 《禮》曰：「大夫死眾。」
entries.en: The Rites says, "A grandee dies for the multitude."
entries.literal: The Rites says: "A grandee dies for the multitude."

entries.zh: 又曰：「謀人之軍師敗則死之。」
entries.en: It also says, "The strategist who fails must die."
entries.literal: It also says: "One who plots as another's military adviser — if defeated, dies for it."

entries.zh: 翰受署賊庭，茍延視息，忠義之道，即可知也，豈不愧於顏杲卿乎！
entries.en: Han took office under the rebels and clung to life — his loyalty is plain; how could he not blush before Yan Gaoqing!
entries.literal: Han accepted appointment in the rebel court and clung to life drawing breath — the way of loyalty and righteousness can be known from this; how is he not ashamed before Yan Gaoqing!

entries.zh: 抑又聞之，古之命將者，推轂而謂之曰：「閫外之事，將軍裁之。」
entries.en: We also hear that ancient emperors, appointing a general, would push the chariot wheel and say, "Beyond the gate, the general decides."
entries.literal: Moreover it is heard that in antiquity when appointing generals, they would push the chariot wheel and say: "Matters outside the gate — the general decides."

entries.zh: 觀楊國忠之奏事，邊令誠之護戎，又掣肘於軍政者也，未可偏責三帥，不尤伊人。
entries.en: Consider Yang Guozhong's interference and Bian Lingcheng's supervision — the court hamstrung its generals; one cannot blame the three commanders alone.
entries.literal: Considering Yang Guozhong's memorials, Bian Lingcheng's supervision of the army — again hamstringing military affairs — one cannot lay all blame on the three commanders alone or reproach those men only.

entries.zh: 後之君子，得不深鑒！
entries.en: Let later ages take this deeply to heart!
entries.literal: Gentlemen of later ages — can they not take this as a deep mirror!

entries.zh: 翰至潼關，或勸翰曰：「祿山阻兵，以誅楊國忠為名，公若留兵三萬守關，悉以精銳回誅國忠，此漢挫七國之計也，公以為何如？」
entries.en: At Tong Pass someone advised him, "Lushan marches under the banner of punishing Yang Guozhong — leave thirty thousand to hold the pass and march your best troops back to kill Guozhong, as the Han did against the Seven States — what say you?"
entries.literal: When Han reached Tong Pass, someone advised him: "Lushan blocks the army and takes punishing Yang Guozhong as his pretext — if you leave thirty thousand to guard the pass and bring all your elite back to execute Guozhong, this is the Han plan for breaking the Seven States — what do you think?"

entries.zh: 翰心許之，未發。
entries.en: Han agreed in his heart but did not act.
entries.literal: Han agreed in his heart but did not set out.

entries.zh: 有客泄其謀於國忠，國忠大懼，及奏曰：「兵法『安不忘危』，今潼關兵眾雖盛，而無後殿，萬一不利，京師得無恐乎！
entries.en: Someone leaked the plan to Guozhong, who in terror memorialized, "In peace forget not danger — Tong Pass is strong but has no reserve; if things go wrong, will not the capital tremble?
entries.literal: A guest leaked the plan to Guozhong; Guozhong was greatly afraid and memorialized: "In military law, 'In peace do not forget danger' — now Tong Pass has a great host but no rear guard; if by chance things go ill, will not the capital be in fear!

entries.zh: 請選監牧小兒三千人訓練於苑中。」
entries.en: He asked to train three thousand boys from the horse herds in the imperial park."
entries.literal: He asked to select three thousand boys of the horse herds to train in the imperial park."

entries.zh: 詔從之，遂遣劍南軍將李福、劉光庭分統焉。
entries.en: The emperor agreed and sent Jiannan generals Li Fu and Liu Guangting to command them.
entries.literal: An edict approved this; Li Fu and Liu Guangting of the Jiannan army were then sent to command them separately.

entries.zh: 又奏召募一萬人，屯於灞上，令其腹心杜乾運將之。
entries.en: He also recruited ten thousand men at Bashang under his confidant Du Qianyun.
entries.literal: He also memorialized to recruit ten thousand men to encamp at Bashang, putting his confidant Du Qianyun in command.

entries.zh: 翰慮為所圖，乃上表請乾運兵隸於潼關，遂召乾運赴潼關計事，因斬之。
entries.en: Han feared a plot against him, asked that Qianyun's troops be attached to Tong Pass, summoned Qianyun there on pretense of consultation, and executed him.
entries.literal: Han feared he was being plotted against; he therefore memorialized asking that Qianyun's troops be placed under Tong Pass, then summoned Qianyun to Tong Pass to discuss affairs and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 自是，翰心不自安。
entries.en: From then on Han was uneasy.
entries.literal: From this Han's heart was ill at ease.

entries.zh: 又素有風疾，至是頗甚，軍中之務，不復躬親，委政於行軍司馬田良丘。
entries.en: His old stroke had worsened; he no longer managed army affairs himself but left them to Tian Liangqiu.
entries.literal: He had long had a wind ailment; by now it was quite severe — military affairs he no longer handled in person but entrusted government to Campaigning Major Tian Liangqiu.

entries.zh: 良丘復不敢專斷，教令不一，頗無部伍。
entries.en: Liangqiu dared not decide alone; orders conflicted and discipline collapsed.
entries.literal: Liangqiu in turn did not dare decide alone; orders and teachings were not unified — discipline was quite lacking.

entries.zh: 其將王思禮、李承光又爭長不葉，人無鬥志。
entries.en: Generals Wang Sili and Li Chengguang vied for command and would not cooperate — the men lost heart.
entries.literal: His generals Wang Sili and Li Chengguang also vied for precedence and would not cooperate — men had no fighting spirit.

entries.zh: 高仙芝，本高麗人也。
entries.en: Gao Xianzhi was ethnically Korean.
entries.literal: Gao Xianzhi was originally a man of Koguryo.

entries.zh: 父舍雞，初從河西軍，累勞至四鎮十將、諸衛將軍。
entries.en: His father Sheji had first served with the Hexi armies and, through long service, rose to become a Ten-General of the Four Garrisons and a palace guard general.
entries.literal: His father Sheji at first followed the Hexi army; through accumulated labors he rose to Ten-General of the Four Garrisons and a general of the Palace Guards.

entries.zh: 仙芝美姿容，善騎射，勇決驍果。
entries.en: Xianzhi was handsome, an expert horseman and archer, and bold, decisive, and ferocious in battle.
entries.literal: Xianzhi had a handsome appearance, was skilled at mounted archery, and was brave, resolute, fierce, and daring.

entries.zh: 少隨父至安西，以父有功授遊擊將軍。
entries.en: As a young man he accompanied his father to Anxi and, thanks to his father's service record, was granted the rank of General of Resist-the-Enemy.
entries.literal: In youth he followed his father to Anxi; because of his father's merit he was appointed General of Resist-the-Enemy.

entries.zh: 年二十餘即拜將軍，與父同班秩。
entries.en: By his twenties he already held general's rank, equal in grade to his father.
entries.literal: Before he was twenty-some years old he was already appointed as a general, sharing rank with his father.

entries.zh: 事節度使田仁琬、蓋嘉運，未甚任用，後夫蒙靈察累拔擢之。
entries.en: Under commissioners Tian Renwan and Gai Jiayun he saw little use; Fumeng Lingcha later promoted him again and again.
entries.literal: He served under Military Commissioners Tian Renwan and Gai Jiayun and was not much employed; afterward Fumeng Lingcha repeatedly promoted and advanced him.

entries.zh: 開元末，為安西副都護、四鎮都知兵馬使。
entries.en: Near the end of the Kaiyuan reign he was made Deputy Protector of Anxi and overall commander of the Four Garrisons' forces.
entries.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he became Deputy Protector-General of Anxi and Commander-in-Chief of the Military Forces of the Four Garrisons.

entries.zh: 初，無量與馬懷素俱為侍讀，顧待甚厚；
entries.en: Earlier, when Wuliang and Ma Huai Su had both served as imperial readers, they had been favored and treated with great generosity;
entries.literal: Earlier, when Wuliang and Ma HuaiSu had both served as imperial readers, they were favored and treated very generously;

entries.zh: 及無量等卒後，秘書少監康子原、國子博士侯行果等又入侍講，雖屢加賞賜，而禮遇不逮褚焉。
entries.en: after Wuliang and the others died, Secretariat vice director Kang Ziyuan, National University erudite Hou Xingguo, and others again served as lecturers. Although they were repeatedly rewarded, the courtesy shown them did not equal what had been accorded Chu.
entries.literal: after Wuliang and the others died, Secretariat vice director Kang Ziyuan, National University erudite Hou Xingguo, and others again entered to lecture, and although rewards were repeatedly increased, the courtesy shown did not reach that given to Chu.

entries.zh: 劉子玄，本名知幾，楚州刺史胤之族孫也。
entries.en: Liu Zixuan, whose original name was Zhiji, was a clansman of Chu Prefecture governor Liu Yinzhi.
entries.literal: Liu Zixuan—Liu Zixuan, original name Zhiji, was a clansman of Chu Prefecture governor Yinzhi.

entries.zh: 少與兄知柔俱以詞學知名，弱冠舉進士，授獲嘉主簿。
entries.en: In his youth he and his elder brother Zhirou were both famed for literary learning. At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Huojia.
entries.literal: In youth he and his elder brother Zhirou were both famed for literary learning; at the capping age he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Huojia chief clerk.

entries.zh: 證聖年，有制文武九品已上各言時政得失，知幾上表陳四事，詞甚切直。
entries.en: In the Zhengsheng year an edict required civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above to comment on current policy. Zhiji submitted a memorial on four matters in very blunt and direct language.
entries.literal: In the Zhengsheng year an edict ordered civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above each to speak on the gains and losses of current policy; Zhiji submitted a memorial setting forth four matters, his wording very blunt and direct.

entries.zh: 是時官爵僭濫而法網嚴密，士類競為趨進而多陷刑戮，知幾乃著《思慎賦》以刺時，且以見意。
entries.en: At that time offices and titles were lavished without restraint while the law was harsh; scholars scrambled for advancement and many fell victim to punishment. Zhiji therefore wrote Reflections on Caution to satirize the age and make his views known.
entries.literal: At that time offices and titles were excessively bestowed while the legal net was strict; gentlemen strove to advance and many fell into punishment and execution. Zhiji therefore composed Reflections on Caution to satirize the age and also to express his intent.

entries.zh: 鳳閣侍郎蘇味道、李嶠見而嘆曰：「陸機《豪士》所不及也。」
entries.en: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Ministers Su Weidao and Li Jiao, on reading it, exclaimed, "Even Lu Ji's Bold Heroes does not equal this."
entries.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Su Weidao and Li Jiao, on reading it, sighed and said: "Even Lu Ji's Bold Heroes does not reach this."

entries.zh: 馬懷素，潤州丹徒人也。
entries.en: Ma Huai Su was a native of Dantu in Run Prefecture.
entries.literal: Ma HuaiSu—Ma HuaiSu was a native of Dantu in Run Prefecture.

entries.zh: 寓居江都，少師事李善。
entries.en: He lived in Jiangdu and in his youth studied under Li Shan.
entries.literal: He resided in Jiangdu and in his youth took Li Shan as his teacher.

entries.zh: 家貧無燈燭，晝采薪蘇，夜燃讀書，遂博覽經史，善屬文。
entries.en: His family was too poor to afford lamps or candles; by day he gathered firewood and brush, and by night he burned them to read by their light. In this way he came to be widely versed in the classics and histories and skilled at writing.
entries.literal: His family was poor and had no lamps or candles; by day he gathered firewood and kindling, by night he burned them to read, and thus came to read broadly in the classics and histories and was skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 舉進士，又應制舉，登文學優贍科，拜郿尉，四遷左臺監察御史。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination and also took the special imperial literary examination, placing in the Literary Excellence and Abundant Talent category. He was appointed magistrate of Mei district and was promoted four times to investigating censor of the Left Censorate.
entries.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, also responded to the imperial examination, attained the Literary Excellence and Abundant Talent category, was appointed Mei district magistrate, and was transferred four times to Left Censorate investigating censor.

entries.zh: 初，肅宗在鳳翔，喪亂之後，綱紀未立，兵吏三銓，簿籍煨燼，南曹選人，文符悉多偽濫。
entries.en: Earlier, when Suzong's court was at Fengxiang after the rebellion, government discipline had collapsed. The personnel registers of the three selection boards had been burned, and candidates at the southern bureau submitted largely forged credentials.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Suzong was at Fengxiang, after the calamity of rebellion discipline had not yet been established; the three boards for military and civil selection had their registers burned to ashes, and among candidates at the southern bureau documents were largely forged and spurious.

entries.zh: 上以凶醜未滅，且示招懷，據到註擬，一無檢括。
entries.en: Because the rebels had not yet been crushed and the emperor wished to win support, he approved appointments on whatever papers were submitted, without any review.
entries.literal: The emperor, because the wicked enemy had not yet been destroyed and wishing to show conciliation, approved appointments on the basis of whatever documents arrived, with no examination at all.

entries.zh: 見素曰：「臣典選歲久，周知此弊。
entries.en: Jiansu said, "I presided over appointments for many years and know this abuse well.
entries.literal: Jiansu said, "Your servant has presided over selections for many years and knows this abuse thoroughly.

entries.zh: 今寰區未復，員闕不多。
entries.en: The empire is not yet recovered, and vacant posts are still few.
entries.literal: The realm is not yet restored and vacant posts are not numerous.

entries.zh: 若總無條綱，恐難持久。」
entries.en: If we have no standards at all, I fear the practice cannot last."
entries.literal: If there are no rules at all, I fear this cannot last."

entries.zh: 上然之，未暇釐革。
entries.en: The emperor agreed but had no time yet to reform the system.
entries.literal: The emperor agreed but had no leisure to reform the system.

entries.zh: 及還京，選人數千，補授無所，喧訴於朝，由是行見素之言。
entries.en: After the return to the capital thousands of candidates had no posts to fill and protested loudly at court, and Jiansu's advice was finally adopted.
entries.literal: When they returned to the capital thousands of candidates had no posts to which they could be appointed and clamored in protest at court; because of this Jiansu's advice was put into practice.

entries.zh: 及房琯以敗軍左降，崔圓、崔渙等皆罷知政事，上皇所命宰臣，無知政事者。
entries.en: When Fang Guan was demoted after his military defeat and Cui Yuan, Cui Huan, and others were removed from office, none of the chief ministers appointed by the retired emperor still held real power.
entries.literal: When Fang Guan was demoted to the left for military defeat and Cui Yuan, Cui Huan, and others were all removed from participation in government, among the chief ministers appointed by the Retired Emperor none remained in charge of state affairs.

entries.zh: 五月，遷見素太子太師。
entries.en: In the fifth month Jiansu was made grand preceptor of the crown prince.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Jiansu was transferred to Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 十一月，肅宗自右輔還京，詔見素入蜀奉迎太上皇。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, when Suzong returned to the capital from the western capital, he ordered Jiansu into Shu to escort the retired emperor home.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, when Suzong returned to the capital from the western capital region, he ordered Jiansu to enter Shu to escort the Retired Emperor back.

entries.zh: 十二月，上皇至京師，肅宗禦樓大赦。
entries.en: In the twelfth month the retired emperor reached the capital, and Suzong proclaimed a general amnesty from the palace tower.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month the Retired Emperor reached the capital and Suzong proclaimed a great amnesty from the palace tower.

entries.zh: 見素以奉上皇幸蜀功，加開府儀同三司，食實封三百戶。
entries.en: For accompanying the retired emperor to Shu, Jiansu was granted the honor of opening an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and a fief of three hundred households.
entries.literal: For his merit in attending the Retired Emperor on his journey to Shu, Jiansu was granted the honor of opening an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and an actual fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 上元中，以足疾上表請致仕，許之。
entries.en: During the Shangyuan era he petitioned to retire on account of a foot ailment, and his request was granted.
entries.literal: In the Shangyuan era, citing illness of the feet, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and was permitted to withdraw.

entries.zh: 寶應元年十二月卒，年七十六，贈司空，謚曰忠貞，喪事官給。
entries.en: He died in the twelfth month of Baoying 1 at the age of seventy-six. He was posthumously made minister of works, given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright, and his funeral was paid for by the state.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoying he died at the age of seventy-six; he was posthumously made Minister of Works, given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright, and his funeral expenses were supplied by the state.

entries.zh: 子倜、諤、益、丱。
entries.en: His sons were Ti, E, Yi, and Guan.
entries.literal: His sons were Ti, E, Yi, and Guan.

entries.zh: 倜、諤皆位至給事中，益終刑部員外郎，丱終秘書丞。
entries.en: Ti and E both rose to Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as a vice-director in the ministry of justice, and Guan as a secretary in the imperial archives.
entries.literal: Ti and E both reached the post of Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as vice-director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guan as assistant director of the Palace Library.

entries.zh: 倜子頌。
entries.en: Ti had a son named Song.
entries.literal: Ti's son was Song.

entries.zh: 杜鴻漸
entries.en: Du Hongjian
entries.literal: Du Hongjian

entries.zh: 晉卿幼好學，善屬文，進士擢第。
entries.en: Jinqing had loved study from childhood, wrote well, and passed the jinshi civil examination.
entries.literal: Jinqing from youth loved learning, excelled at literary composition, and was selected in the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 初授懷州修武縣尉，歷奉先縣尉，坐累貶徐州司戶參軍。
entries.en: He was first made magistrate's assistant at Xiuwu in Huai, then served at Fengxian, but was demoted to registrar at Xu prefecture after being implicated in an affair.
entries.literal: Initially appointed magistrate's assistant of Xiuwu County in Huai Prefecture, served as magistrate's assistant of Fengxian County, and because of entanglement in a case was demoted to Registrar of Xu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 秩滿隨調，判入高等，授萬年縣尉。
entries.en: At the end of his term he entered the routine reassignment pool, scored in the top tier on his evaluation, and received appointment as assistant magistrate of Wannian.
entries.literal: When his term ended he joined the regular transfer; his written evaluation was graded in the upper rank, and he was appointed magistrate's assistant of Wannian County.

entries.zh: 遷侍御史，歷度支、兵、吏部三員外郎。
entries.en: He rose to attending censor and then held vice-director posts in the revenue, war, and personnel ministries in turn.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor and served successively as Vice Director in the ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.

entries.zh: 開元二十三年，遷吏部郎中。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 23 (735), he was made a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 二十四年，與吏部郎中孫逖並拜中書舍人。
entries.en: The next year he and Sun Ti of the personnel ministry were both promoted to drafter in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, together with Sun Ti, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, he was jointly appointed Secretariat Drafter.

entries.zh: 二十七年，以本官權知吏部選事。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 27 he was given his existing rank but charged with directing the ministry's selection examinations.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, with his existing office he was temporarily put in charge of personnel selection matters.

entries.zh: 晉卿性謙柔，選人有訴訟索好官者，雖至數千言，或聲色甚厲者，晉卿必含容之，略無慍色。
entries.en: Jinqing was modest and even-tempered: when examinees petitioned or quarreled for better appointments, sometimes at great length or with angry outbursts, he always listened patiently and never showed annoyance.
entries.literal: Jinqing's nature was modest and gentle; when candidates lodged complaints or sued for good posts, even if to several thousand words, or their voice and bearing were very fierce, Jinqing always bore with them, without a trace of anger.

entries.zh: 二十九年，拜吏部侍郎。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 29 he was made vice minister of personnel.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 前後典選五年，政既寬弛，胥吏多因緣為奸，賄賂大行。
entries.en: He oversaw the examinations for five years in all; his rule was lenient and slack, so clerks seized every opening for graft and bribes became rampant.
entries.literal: Over five years before and after in charge of selection, because administration was already lax, clerks often took advantage to commit wrongdoing, and bribery flourished greatly.

entries.zh: 時天下承平，每年赴選常萬余人。
entries.en: Peace reigned under heaven, and more than ten thousand candidates presented themselves each year.
entries.literal: At the time the empire enjoyed peace, and those who came each year to selection often exceeded ten thousand.

entries.zh: 李林甫為尚書，專任廟堂，銓事唯委晉卿及同列侍郎宋遙主之。
entries.en: Li Linfu held the ministerial post but kept his grip on court power, leaving the actual running of selections to Jinqing and his fellow vice minister Song Yao alone.
entries.literal: Li Linfu as Minister devoted himself solely to the court altar, and selection affairs were solely entrusted to Jinqing and his colleague Vice Minister Song Yao to preside.

entries.zh: 選人既多，每年兼命他官有識者同考定書判，務求其實。
entries.en: With so many candidates, each year other capable officials were also assigned to grade the written examinations, so that the results might reflect real merit.
entries.literal: Because candidates were numerous, each year additional appointment was made of other officials with discernment to join in evaluating written judgments, striving to seek the real quality.

entries.zh: 天寶二年春，御史中丞張倚男奭參選，晉卿與遙以倚初承恩，欲悅附之，考選人判等凡六十四人，分甲乙丙科，奭在其首。
entries.en: In the spring of Tianbao 2 (743), Zhang Yi's son Shi entered the examinations. Jinqing and Yao, eager to curry favor with the newly favored Zhang Yi, ranked sixty-four candidates in three tiers and placed Shi at the top.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year of Tianbao, Zhang Yi, Vice Censor-in-Chief, his son Shi participated in selection; Jinqing and Yao because Yi had newly received favor wished to please and attach to him—they evaluated candidates' written grades totaling sixty-four persons, dividing into First, Second, and Third classes, with Shi at their head.

entries.zh: 眾知奭不讀書，論議紛然。
entries.en: Everyone knew Shi was unlettered, and protest swirled through the capital.
entries.literal: The crowd knew Shi did not read books, and discussion was in uproar.

entries.zh: 有蘇孝慍者，嘗為范陽薊令，事安祿山，具其事告之。
entries.en: A former magistrate of Ji in Fanyang named Su Xiaoyin, now in An Lushan's service, reported the whole affair to him in detail.
entries.literal: There was one Su Xiaoyin, who had once been magistrate of Ji in Fanyang, served An Lushan, and reported the full matter to him.

entries.zh: 祿山恩寵特異，謁見不常，因而奏之。
entries.en: Lushan enjoyed unusual imperial favor and did not often attend court, so he used this occasion to lay the matter before the throne.
entries.literal: Lushan enjoyed exceptional grace and favor; audiences were not regular, and so through this he memorialized it.

entries.zh: 玄宗大集登科人，禦花萼樓親試，登第者十無一二；
entries.en: Xuanzong convened all the newly accredited candidates and personally examined them at the Hua'e Tower; fewer than one or two in ten of those already listed as passed could meet the test.
entries.literal: Xuanzong greatly gathered those who had passed the examinations, personally tested them at the Hua'e Pavilion; of those who had received degrees, not one or two in ten [passed].

entries.zh: 而奭手持試紙，竟日不下一字，時謂之「曳白」。
entries.en: Shi held his examination slip and wrote not a single character all day long, and contemporaries dubbed him "the dragged blank."
entries.literal: But Shi, holding the examination paper, all day did not write a single character; they at the time called it "dragging the blank."

entries.zh: 上怒，晉卿貶為安康郡太守，遙為武當郡太守，張倚為淮陽太守。
entries.en: The emperor's rage sent Jinqing to Ankang as prefect, Yao to Wudang, and Zhang Yi to Huaiyang.
entries.literal: The Emperor was angry; Jinqing was demoted to Prefect of Ankang commandery, Yao to Prefect of Wudang commandery, Zhang Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 敕曰：「門庭之間，不能訓子；
entries.en: The edict read: "In his own household he could not discipline his son;
entries.literal: Edict said: "Within one's gate and courtyard, unable to instruct his son;

entries.zh: 選調之際，仍以托人。」
entries.en: and at the time of civil selection he still had to plead on his son's behalf."
entries.literal: at the time of selection and appointment, still relied on entrusting it to others."

entries.zh: 時士子皆以為戲笑。
entries.en: Scholars of the day repeated it as a bitter joke.
entries.literal: At the time scholars all took it as jest and ridicule.

entries.zh: 數日，肅宗晏駕，代宗踐祚，又詔晉卿攝冢宰。
entries.en: Within days Suzong died and Daizong ascended the throne; he again ordered Jinqing to serve as regent.
entries.literal: Several days later Suzong died; Daizong ascended the throne and again ordered Jinqing to act as regent.

entries.zh: 晉卿上表懇辭曰：「臣以昔者天子居喪之時，百官聽於冢宰者，蓋君幼小，禦極事殷，情理當然。
entries.en: Jinqing memorialized again in earnest refusal: "In former times, when the Son of Heaven mourned and officials obeyed a regent, it was because the ruler was a child and the throne's burdens were overwhelming—that was only natural.
entries.literal: Jinqing submitted a memorial earnestly declining, saying: "Your servant considers that in former times when the Son of Heaven dwelt in mourning and the hundred officials listened to the regent, it was because the ruler was young and small, the throne's affairs were pressing—reason and sentiment made it natural.

entries.zh: 沿革不一，今古異同，而周武、漢文，合於通變，垂範作則，可舉而行。
entries.en: Custom has varied from age to age, yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han adapted wisely to circumstance and left examples we may follow.
entries.literal: Change and continuation are not uniform; present and ancient differ in sameness and difference—yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han conformed to flexible adaptation, handed down models and made standards that may be raised up and carried out.

entries.zh: 又士或墨缞，時遇金革，豈非銜恤，謂義在斷恩。
entries.en: A gentleman may wear mourning garb yet take up arms when the state is at war—he grieves inwardly but knows that duty must override private sorrow.
entries.literal: Again, a gentleman may wear black hemp mourning, yet when the time meets arms and armor, is it not that he harbors grief yet holds that righteousness lies in cutting off private feeling?

entries.zh: 且百善之至，無加於孝也，其有容瘁心絕，指景悼生，此匹夫守節之常情，殊王者嗣續之大計。
entries.en: Filial piety is the highest of virtues, yet to waste away in grief and mourn one's own life is the conduct of a private man—not the great duty of one who must carry on the royal line.
entries.literal: Moreover, among the hundred virtues none surpasses filial piety; yet there are those whose countenance is haggard and heart broken, who point to the sun and mourn life—this is the ordinary sentiment of a common man keeping integrity, quite different from the great plan of a king's succession.

entries.zh: 昨二十日，陛下於大行皇帝柩前即位，是承先帝遺顧之言，亦前代不易之典。
entries.en: Only yesterday, on the twentieth, Your Majesty took the throne before the late emperor's bier—fulfilling his final charge and following an immemorial precedent.
entries.literal: Yesterday, the twentieth day, Your Majesty at the bier of the late emperor ascended the throne—this carries out the late emperor's parting charge and is also an unchanging canon of former ages.

entries.zh: 則知所略不為害，所存是適權，防威滅端，所利者大。
entries.en: What is set aside does no harm; what is preserved is timely expedience—cutting danger at the root brings the greater good.
entries.literal: Then one knows that what is set aside does no harm and what is preserved is fitting expedience—warding off peril and extinguishing the source; the benefit is great.

entries.zh: 陛下因心純至，天地明察。
entries.en: Your Majesty's heart is utterly sincere; Heaven and Earth discern it.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's heart follows purity to the utmost; Heaven and Earth see clearly.

entries.zh: 伏以報劬勞之恩，申罔極之思，終身之痛，豈計朝夕！
entries.en: To repay a parent's toil and express boundless grief is a lifelong sorrow—not a matter of days alone!
entries.literal: Your servant considers that repaying toilsome labor's grace and expressing boundless longing—lifelong pain, how could one reckon by days and nights!

entries.zh: 但以一日之內，萬務在中，須達宸聰，始成國政。
entries.en: Yet within a single day ten thousand affairs press in; only when they reach Your Majesty's ear can the state be governed.
entries.literal: Yet within a single day the myriad affairs lie at the center; the imperial ear must be reached before state government can be accomplished.

entries.zh: 百僚萬姓及僧道耆壽等，相顧聚言，以臣老且無能，愚豈測聖，況久無居攝，臣不敢奉詔。
entries.en: Officials, common people, monks, Daoists, and elders alike say I am old and incapable—how could a fool measure a sage? Regency has long been obsolete; I dare not accept the charge.
entries.literal: The hundred officials, myriad people, monks and Daoists, elders of long years, and others look at one another and gather in speech, saying your servant is old and without ability—how could stupidity measure sagehood? Moreover, for long there has been no regency; your servant dares not accept the edict.

entries.zh: 特乞陛下遵遺命，三日而政。
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty only to follow the testament and take up government after three days.
entries.literal: I specially beg Your Majesty to follow the testamentary command and govern after three days.

entries.zh: 臣博聽眾情，不勝懇願，伏望割痛抑哀，則天下悲幸。」
entries.en: Having heard the people's voice, I cannot state their wish strongly enough: I pray you set aside private grief, and the realm will be overwhelmed with sorrow and relief together."
entries.literal: Your servant has broadly listened to the multitude's feelings and cannot bear the earnest wish; I bow and hope you will cut pain and restrain grief—then all under Heaven will be overwhelmed with grief and good fortune."

entries.zh: 上號泣從之。
entries.en: The emperor wept aloud and assented.
entries.literal: The Emperor wailed and wept and followed it.

entries.zh: 時晉卿年已衰暮，又患兩足，上特許肩輿至中書，入閣不趨，累日一視事。
entries.en: Jinqing was then advanced in years and afflicted in both legs; the emperor specially allowed him a sedan chair to the Secretariat, exemption from hurrying into court, and attendance at affairs only every few days.
entries.literal: At the time Jinqing's years were already declining in old age and he also suffered in both feet; the Emperor specially permitted him to be carried in a litter to the Secretariat, to enter the pavilion without hurrying, and to attend to affairs once every several days.

entries.zh: 歷三朝，皆以謹密見稱。
entries.en: Through three reigns he was praised for caution and discretion.
entries.literal: Through three reigns he was in each case praised for caution and discretion.

entries.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
entries.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

entries.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
entries.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
entries.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
entries.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
entries.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 未幾，換戶部侍郎、同平章事。
entries.en: Before long he was switched to vice minister of revenue and co-ordinating minister.
entries.literal: Before long he was switched to Vice Minister of Revenue and co-ordinating minister.

entries.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。
entries.en: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made minister of works.
entries.literal: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 天子自岐下還宮，以樞檢校右僕射、同平章事，出為廣南節度使。
entries.en: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made acting right vice director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.
entries.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made Acting Right Vice Director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.

entries.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
entries.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
entries.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

entries.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
entries.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
entries.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

entries.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。
entries.en: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hongwen Academy, commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and commissioner for salt and iron transport across all circuits.
entries.literal: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Academy, Commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport across all circuits.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：晉卿謹身蒞事，足為純臣，避寇全忠，固彰大節。
entries.en: Appraisal: The historiographer writes: Jinqing conducted himself with care and served faithfully—he was truly a loyal minister; in fleeing the rebels he preserved his integrity, and that alone shows his great moral stature.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Jinqing was cautious in person and attended to affairs—fully a pure minister; avoiding the bandits he preserved his loyalty, which indeed displayed great integrity.

entries.zh: 然博達精審，豈不知寬猛之道哉！
entries.en: Yet he was learned and discerning—how could he not have known the balance of lenience and severity!
entries.literal: Yet broadly versed and keenly discriminating—could he not have known the way of lenience and severity!

entries.zh: 奉林甫之旨，順胥吏之意，悅附張倚，欺罔時君。
entries.en: He followed Li Linfu's wishes, indulged the clerks, curried favor with Zhang Yi, and deceived his sovereign.
entries.literal: He followed Linfu's intent, complied with the clerks' wishes, pleased and attached to Zhang Yi, and deceived the sovereign of the time.

entries.zh: 生為重臣，諂林甫之勢也；
entries.en: In life he was a great minister who flattered Li Linfu's power;
entries.literal: In life a great minister—this was fawning on Linfu's power;

entries.zh: 歿改美謚，引元載之恩焉。
entries.en: after death his posthumous name was improved through Yuan Zai's favor.
entries.literal: in death his fine posthumous title was changed—this drew on Yuan Zai's grace.

entries.zh: 或言晉卿不為巧宦者，誠不信也。
entries.en: Those who say Jinqing was no crafty courtier simply cannot be believed.
entries.literal: Some say Jinqing was not a crafty office-seeker—truly one cannot believe it.

entries.zh: 冕力贊中興，名居大位，奉公抱義，可以致身；
entries.en: Mian vigorously aided the restoration and rose to the highest rank; devoted to the public good and upright in principle, he might have made a name for himself—
entries.literal: Mian vigorously aided the restoration, his name occupied the great position, devoted to the public and embracing righteousness—by this one might establish oneself;

entries.zh: 賣官度僧，是何為政？
entries.en: yet he sold offices and sold ordinations—what sort of government was that?
entries.literal: yet selling offices and ordaining monks—what kind of government is this?

entries.zh: 及其老也，貪冒尤深。
entries.en: In old age his greed grew worse still.
entries.literal: When he grew old, his greed and presumption were especially deep.

entries.zh: 遵慶學術貞明，為國忠所出；
entries.en: Zunqing's learning was upright and clear, yet Yang Guozhong posted him out of the capital;
entries.literal: Zunqing's learning was upright and clear, yet he was sent out by Guozhong;

entries.zh: 恭儉謹密，遇蕭華素知。
entries.en: respectful, frugal, and discreet—he won the long-standing regard of Xiao Hua.
entries.literal: respectful, frugal, cautious, and discreet—he met Xiao Hua, who had long known him.

entries.zh: 位重行純，老而彌篤，彼二公固有慚德。
entries.en: He held high office with pure conduct and grew more steadfast in old age—the other two men might well have felt shame beside him.
entries.literal: His position was weighty and his conduct pure; in old age he grew ever more steadfast—those two lords indeed had cause for shame beside him.

entries.zh: 向克荷堂構，不墜門風。
entries.en: Xiang upheld the family estate and did not let its reputation fall.
entries.literal: Xiang was able to bear the hall's beams and did not let the family's reputation fall.

entries.zh: 樞因盜而振，盜憎而亡，宜哉！
entries.en: Shu rose through the usurper, and when the usurper turned against him he died—as was fitting!
entries.literal: Shu rose through the bandit, the bandit came to hate him and he perished—fitting indeed!

entries.zh: 君子守道遠刑，蓋慮此也。
entries.en: The gentleman holds to the Way and keeps clear of punishment—perhaps he had this in mind.
entries.literal: The gentleman keeps the Way and keeps punishment far off—perhaps he takes thought for this.

entries.zh: ○苗晉卿裴冕裴遵慶子向向子寅寅子樞=苗晉卿=苗晉卿，上黨壺關人。
entries.en: This section covers Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, and Pei Zunqing, together with Pei Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, and Yin's son Shu. Miao Jinqing was from Huguan in Shangdang.
entries.literal: [Section:] Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, his son Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, Yin's son Shu. = Miao Jinqing = Miao Jinqing was a native of Huguan in Shangdang.

entries.zh: 世以儒素稱。
entries.en: His lineage was known for upright Confucian learning and modest living.
entries.literal: His family for generations was famed for Confucian simplicity.

entries.zh: 祖夔，高道不仕，追贈禮部尚書。
entries.en: His grandfather Kui, a man of exalted principle who never held office, was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: His grandfather Kui, of lofty virtue and did not take office, was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 父殆庶，官至絳州龍門縣丞，早卒，以晉卿贈太子少保。
entries.en: His father Dai-shu rose only to assistant magistrate of Longmen in Jiang prefecture and died young; on account of Jinqing's eminence he was posthumously granted the title Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: His father Dai-shu, reached office as Assistant Magistrate of Longmen County in Jiang Prefecture, died early; because of Jinqing he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 十五年六月，玄宗蒼黃幸蜀，大臣陳希烈、張倚等銜於失恩，不時赴難。
entries.en: In the sixth month of year 15 Xuanzong fled in panic to Shu; ministers Chen Xilie and Zhang Yi, bitter over lost favor, did not hurry to his side.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year Xuanzong fled in haste to Shu; grandees Chen Xilie and Zhang Yi and others, resentful at lost favor, did not hurry to the crisis.

entries.zh: 琯結張均、張垍兄弟與韋述等行至城南十數里山寺，均、垍同行，皆以家在城中，逗留不進，琯獨馳蜀路。
entries.en: Guan joined Zhang Jun and Zhang Ya with Wei Shu and reached a mountain temple south of the city; the Zhang brothers, with kin in the capital, hung back, while Guan alone raced toward Shu.
entries.literal: Guan joined Zhang Jun and Zhang Ya and brothers with Wei Shu and others and went to a mountain temple ten-odd li south of the city; Jun and Ya, whose families were in the city, lingered and would not advance, but Guan alone galloped along the road to Shu.

entries.zh: 七月，至普安郡謁見，玄宗大悅，即日拜文部尚書、同中書門下平章事，賜紫金魚袋。
entries.en: In the seventh month he presented himself at Pu'an; Xuanzong was delighted and that day made him Minister of Culture, Grand Councillor, and gave him the gold-and-purple fish bag.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he presented himself at Pu'an Commandery; Xuanzong was greatly pleased and that same day appointed him Minister of Culture, Grand Councillor with the Secretariat, and granted the gold and purple fish bag.

entries.zh: 從幸成都，加銀青光祿大夫，仍與一子官。
entries.en: He followed the court to Chengdu, received Silver and Blue Glory Grandee rank, and an office for one son.
entries.literal: Following the court to Chengdu, he was given the silver and blue glory grandee rank and an office for one son.

entries.zh: 其年八月，與左相韋見素、門下侍郎崔渙等奉使靈武，冊立肅宗。
entries.en: That eighth month, with Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu and Vice Director Cui Huan, he went to Lingwu to invest Suzong.
entries.literal: That eighth month, with Left Chancellor Wei Jiansu and Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Huan and others, he was sent as envoy to Lingwu to invest Suzong.

entries.zh: 至順化郡謁見，陳上皇傳付之旨，因言時事，詞情慷慨，肅宗為之改容。
entries.en: At Shunhua he delivered the retired emperor's charge and spoke on affairs of the day with passion, and Suzong's face changed.
entries.literal: Presenting himself at Shunhua Commandery, he declared the retired emperor's transmitted charge and spoke on current affairs with passionate words; Suzong's expression changed.

entries.zh: 時潼關敗將王思禮、呂崇賁、李承光等引於纛下，將斬之，琯從容救諫，獨斬承光而已。
entries.en: Defeated Tong Pass generals Wang Sili, Lü Chongben, and Li Chengguang were brought to the standards for execution; Guan calmly argued them down, and only Chengguang was killed.
entries.literal: At that time the defeated generals from Tong Pass—Wang Sili, Lü Chongben, Li Chengguang, and others—were brought before the banners to be executed; Guan calmly remonstrated and only Chengguang was beheaded.

entries.zh: 肅宗以琯素有重名，傾意待之，琯亦自負其才，以天下為己任。
entries.en: Suzong, knowing Guan's long-standing fame, favored him wholeheartedly; Guan in turn trusted his own gifts and took the realm as his responsibility.
entries.literal: Suzong, because Guan had long enjoyed a great reputation, treated him with full favor; Guan too relied on his talent and took the empire as his charge.

entries.zh: 時行在機務，多決之於琯，凡有大事，諸將無敢預言。
entries.en: At the mobile court most affairs were settled by Guan; on major matters the generals hardly dared speak.
entries.literal: At the mobile court most business was decided by Guan; on great matters the generals did not dare speak.

entries.zh: 尋抗疏自請將兵以誅寇孽，收復京都，肅宗望其成功，許之。
entries.en: He soon asked in a memorial to lead troops against the rebels and recover the capital; Suzong hoped he would succeed and agreed.
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized asking to lead troops to destroy the rebels and recover the capital; Suzong hoped for success and assented.

entries.zh: 詔加持節、招討西京兼防禦蒲潼兩關兵馬節度等使，乃與子儀、光弼等計會進兵。
entries.en: He was given full powers to reconnoiter the western capital and command the Pu and Tong garrisons, and planned advances with Ziyi and Guangbi.
entries.literal: An edict added full powers as commissioner to reconnoiter the western capital and defend the armies of Pu and Tong passes, and he consulted with Ziyi, Guangbi, and others on advancing.

entries.zh: 琯請自選參佐，乃以禦中史中丞鄧景山為副，戶部侍郎李揖為行軍司馬，中丞宋若思、起居郎知制誥賈至、右司郎中魏少遊為判官，給事中劉秩為參謀。
entries.en: Guan chose his staff: Vice Censor-in-Chief Deng Jingshan as deputy, Vice Minister Li Yi as army marshal, Song Ruosi, Jia Zhi, and Wei Shaoyou as judges, and Liu Zhi as adviser.
entries.literal: Guan asked to choose his own staff: Vice Censor-in-Chief Deng Jingshan as deputy, Vice Minister of Revenue Li Yi as army marshal, censors Song Ruosi and Jia Zhi and Right Department Director Wei Shaoyou as judges, and supervising secretary Liu Zhi as staff adviser.

entries.zh: 既行，又令兵部尚書王思禮副之。
entries.en: After he marched, Minister of War Wang Sili was added as deputy.
entries.literal: After setting out, Minister of War Wang Sili was also made his deputy.

entries.zh: 琯分為三軍：遣楊希文將南軍，自宜壽入；
entries.en: Guan divided his force: Yang Xiwen would lead the southern army in from Yishou;
entries.literal: Guan divided into three armies: Yang Xiwen was to lead the southern army in from Yishou;

entries.zh: 劉悊將中軍，自武功入；
entries.en: Liu Ti the central army from Wugong;
entries.literal: Liu Ti was to lead the central army in from Wugong;

entries.zh: 李光進將北軍，自奉天入。
entries.en: Li Guangjin the northern army from Fengtian.
entries.literal: Li Guangjin was to lead the northern army in from Fengtian.

entries.zh: 琯自將中軍，為前鋒。
entries.en: Guan himself commanded the central army as vanguard.
entries.literal: Guan himself led the central army as vanguard.

entries.zh: 十月庚子，師次便橋。
entries.en: On gengzi in the tenth month the army camped at Bian Bridge.
entries.literal: On the gengzi day of the tenth month the army halted at Bian Bridge.

entries.zh: 辛丑，二軍先遇賊於咸陽縣之陳濤斜，接戰，官軍敗績。
entries.en: On xinchou two armies met the rebels at Chentaoxie in Xianyang and were routed.
entries.literal: On xinchou the two armies first met the rebels at Chentaoxie in Xianyang County; they joined battle and the government troops were defeated.

entries.zh: 時琯用春秋車戰之法，以車二千乘，馬步夾之。
entries.en: Guan fought by Spring and Autumn chariot rules, with two thousand chariots flanked by infantry and cavalry.
entries.literal: At that time Guan used Spring and Autumn chariot warfare, with two thousand chariots and horse and foot on either side.

entries.zh: 既戰，賊順風揚塵鼓噪，牛皆震駭，因縛芻縱火焚之，人畜撓敗，為所傷殺者四萬余人，存者數千而已。
entries.en: In battle the rebels, wind at their backs, raised dust and clamor; oxen panicked, fodder was fired, men and beasts broke, more than forty thousand were killed or hurt, and only thousands remained.
entries.literal: Once battle was joined the rebels, with the wind at their backs, raised dust and shouted; the oxen were terrified, fodder was bound and set afire, men and beasts were thrown into chaos, more than forty thousand were killed or wounded, and only a few thousand survived.

entries.zh: 癸卯，琯又率南軍即戰，復敗，希文、劉悊並降於賊。
entries.en: On guimao Guan led the southern army again, lost again, and Xiwen and Liu Ti surrendered.
entries.literal: On guimao Guan again led the southern army into battle, was again defeated, and Xiwen and Liu Ti both surrendered to the rebels.

entries.zh: 琯等奔赴行在，肉袒請罪，上並宥之。
entries.en: Guan and his party rushed to the mobile court, stripped to the waist to beg punishment, and were all pardoned.
entries.literal: Guan and the others ran to the mobile court, bared their torsos to ask punishment, and the emperor pardoned them all.

entries.zh: 崔光遠，滑州靈昌人也。
entries.en: Cui Guangyuan came from Lingchang in Huazhou.
entries.literal: Cui Guangyuan was a native of Lingchang in Huazhou.

entries.zh: 本博陵舊族。
entries.en: He was descended from the old Boling aristocracy.
entries.literal: His clan was originally of the old Boling aristocracy.

entries.zh: 祖敬嗣，好樗蒱飲酒。
entries.en: His grandfather Jingsi was fond of gambling at chuck-a-luck and of wine.
entries.literal: His grandfather Jingsi loved playing chuck-a-luck and drinking wine.

entries.zh: 則天初，為房州刺史。
entries.en: In the early years of Empress Wu, he served as prefect of Fangzhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Empress Wu's reign, he served as prefect of Fang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 中宗為廬陵王，安置在州，官吏多無禮度，敬嗣獨以親賢待之，供給豐贍，中宗深德之。
entries.en: When Zhongzong was Prince of Luling and was kept at Fangzhou, most officials treated him without proper respect; only Jingsi received him as kin and as a man of worth and provided for him lavishly, and Zhongzong never forgot his kindness.
entries.literal: When Zhongzong was Prince of Luling and was placed in that prefecture, most officials showed him no proper courtesy; Jingsi alone treated him with the affection due a kinsman and worthy, supplied him generously, and Zhongzong was deeply grateful.

entries.zh: 及登位，有益州長史崔敬嗣，既同姓名，每進擬官，皆御筆超拜之者數四。
entries.en: After Zhongzong took the throne, a chief administrator of Yizhou named Cui Jingsi shared the same name, and on four separate occasions when appointments were proposed the emperor personally marked him for extraordinary promotion.
entries.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, there was a Yizhou chief administrator named Cui Jingsi who bore the same name; whenever proposed appointments were submitted, the emperor four times used his own brush to promote him beyond the normal rank.

entries.zh: 後引與語，始知誤寵。
entries.en: Only when he later summoned the man to court did he discover his mistake.
entries.literal: Later he summoned the man to speak with him and only then realized he had favored the wrong man.

entries.zh: 訪敬嗣已卒，乃遣中書令韋安石授其子汪官。
entries.en: On learning that Jingsi was dead, he sent Chief Minister Wei Anshi to grant an office to his son Wang.
entries.literal: Learning that Jingsi had already died, he sent Chief Minister Wei Anshi to confer an office on his son Wang.

entries.zh: 汪嗜酒不堪職任，且授洛州司功，又改五品。
entries.en: Wang drank heavily and could not hold office, so he was first made Registrar of Luozhou and later demoted to fifth rank.
entries.literal: Wang was addicted to wine and unfit for office; he was therefore given the post of Registrar of Luozhou, then reduced to fifth rank.

entries.zh: 晉卿幼好學，善屬文，進士擢第。
entries.en: From boyhood Jingqing was devoted to study and gifted at writing; he passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: Jingqing from youth loved learning, was skilled at literary composition, and passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 初授懷州修武縣尉，歷奉先縣尉，坐累貶徐州司戶參軍。
entries.en: He was first appointed county defender of Xiuwu in Huai prefecture, later served as county defender of Fengxian, and was eventually demoted to registrar of Xu prefecture after a series of entanglements.
entries.literal: At first he was appointed County Defender of Xiuwu in Huai prefecture, served as County Defender of Fengxian, and through accumulated offenses was demoted to Registrar of Xu prefecture.

entries.zh: 秩滿隨調，判入高等，授萬年縣尉。
entries.en: When his term ended he entered the regular reassignment process, received a top evaluation, and was appointed county defender of Wannian county.
entries.literal: When his term expired he followed the regular transfer, was judged in the upper grade, and was appointed County Defender of Wannian.

entries.zh: 遷侍御史，歷度支、兵、吏部三員外郎。
entries.en: He rose to the post of attending censor and then served in turn as vice director in the ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor and successively served as Vice Director in the Ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.

entries.zh: 開元二十三年，遷吏部郎中。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 23 (735) he was made a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 二十四年，與吏部郎中孫逖並拜中書舍人。
entries.en: The following year he and Sun Di of the Ministry of Personnel were jointly appointed drafting attendants at the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he and Sun Di, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, were together appointed Drafting Attendants at the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 二十七年，以本官權知吏部選事。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 27 (739) he was given temporary charge of civil-service selection while retaining his secretariat post.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, in his existing post he was temporarily charged with managing personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 晉卿性謙柔，選人有訴訟索好官者，雖至數千言，或聲色甚厲者，晉卿必含容之，略無慍色。
entries.en: Jingqing was by nature modest and mild-mannered. When candidates came with petitions or demands for favorable appointments—even haranguing him at length or raising their voices in anger—he always received them patiently and never showed irritation.
entries.literal: Jingqing's nature was modest and gentle; when candidates brought lawsuits or demanded good posts, even if they spoke thousands of words or their voices and expressions were very fierce, Jingqing always bore with them and showed not the least anger.

entries.zh: 二十九年，拜吏部侍郎。
entries.en: In Kaiyuan 29 (741) he was appointed vice minister of personnel.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 前後典選五年，政既寬弛，胥吏多因緣為奸，賄賂大行。
entries.en: He oversaw selection for five years in all. Because his administration was lenient, clerks found countless openings for abuse and bribery became rampant.
entries.literal: Over five years in charge of selection, administration grew lax, clerks widely used opportunities for villainy, and bribery flourished.

entries.zh: 時天下承平，每年赴選常萬余人。
entries.en: The empire was at peace, and each year more than ten thousand candidates typically presented themselves for examination.
entries.literal: At the time the realm enjoyed peace; each year more than ten thousand commonly came for selection.

entries.zh: 李林甫為尚書，專任廟堂，銓事唯委晉卿及同列侍郎宋遙主之。
entries.en: Li Linfu, as minister of personnel, kept his grip on court power and left the business of selection entirely to Jingqing and his colleague Song Yao.
entries.literal: Li Linfu was Minister and monopolized court affairs; selection matters were entrusted solely to Jingqing and his fellow Vice Minister Song Yao.

entries.zh: 選人既多，每年兼命他官有識者同考定書判，務求其實。
entries.en: With so many candidates, each year other knowledgeable officials were also assigned to grade the written examinations together, so that the results might be as fair as possible.
entries.literal: Because candidates were numerous, each year other officials of discernment were also ordered to examine and grade written judgments jointly, striving for truth.

entries.zh: 天寶二年春，御史中丞張倚男奭參選，晉卿與遙以倚初承恩，欲悅附之，考選人判等凡六十四人，分甲乙丙科，奭在其首。
entries.en: In the spring of Tianbao 2 (743), Zhang Yi's son Shi sat for the examinations. Jingqing and Yao, wishing to curry favor with Yi, who had only recently risen in the emperor's grace, ranked sixty-four candidates in three grades—and placed Shi at the top.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year of Tianbao, Zhang Yi's son Shi entered selection; Jingqing and Yao, because Yi had newly received favor, wished to please and attach themselves to him; they graded sixty-four candidates in written judgment into jia, yi, and bing classes, with Shi at the head.

entries.zh: 眾知奭不讀書，論議紛然。
entries.en: Everyone knew that Shi was barely literate, and public outcry spread.
entries.literal: The multitude knew Shi did not read books, and debate arose in confusion.

entries.zh: 有蘇孝慍者，嘗為范陽薊令，事安祿山，具其事告之。
entries.en: A man named Su Xiaoyin, who had once been magistrate of Ji in Fanyang and was now in An Lushan's service, reported the whole affair to him in detail.
entries.literal: There was one Su Xiaoyin who had once been Magistrate of Ji in Fanyang, served An Lushan, and reported the whole affair to him in detail.

entries.zh: 祿山恩寵特異，謁見不常，因而奏之。
entries.en: Lushan enjoyed extraordinary favor at court and was not often granted audience; he seized the occasion to present a memorial on the matter.
entries.literal: Lushan enjoyed exceptional favor and was not often received in audience; he therefore memorialized it.

entries.zh: 玄宗大集登科人，禦花萼樓親試，登第者十無一二；
entries.en: Emperor Xuanzong summoned all the newly passed candidates to the Hua'e Tower for a personal examination; fewer than one in ten proved able to pass;
entries.literal: Xuanzong greatly assembled those who had passed the examinations, personally tested them at the Hua'e Tower, and of those who had passed, not one or two in ten [succeeded];

entries.zh: 而奭手持試紙，竟日不下一字，時謂之「曳白」。
entries.en: Shi, holding his examination paper, could not write a single character all day long—people at the time called it 'dragging a blank sheet.'
entries.literal: but Shi held the examination paper and for a whole day did not write a single character; at the time they called it 'dragging the blank.'

entries.zh: 上怒，晉卿貶為安康郡太守，遙為武當郡太守，張倚為淮陽太守。
entries.en: The emperor was furious. Jingqing was demoted to prefect of Ankang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Zhang Yi to prefect of Huaiyang.
entries.literal: The emperor was angry; Jingqing was demoted to Prefect of Ankang commandery, Yao to Prefect of Wudang commandery, and Zhang Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 敕曰：「門庭之間，不能訓子；
entries.en: An edict declared: 'At home he could not teach his son;
entries.literal: An edict said: 'Within one's own gate and courtyard, one cannot instruct one's son;

entries.zh: 選調之際，仍以托人。」
entries.en: at selection time he still had to rely on pulling strings for others.'
entries.literal: at the time of selection and transfer, he still relied on entrusting others.'

entries.zh: 時士子皆以為戲笑。
