entries.literal: During the rebellion of Li Lingyao, the military governors holding Henan mostly did not obey laws and edicts, and tax collection followed suit;

entries.zh: 州縣雖益減，晏以羨余相補，人不加賦，所入仍舊，議者稱其能。
entries.en: though local revenues fell further, Yan used surpluses to make up the shortfall so the people paid no extra levies and state intake held steady; observers praised his skill.
entries.literal: though prefectures and counties were further reduced, Yan used surplus revenue to compensate so the people were not charged extra levies and intake remained as before; commentators praised his ability.

entries.zh: 自諸道巡院距京師，重價募疾足，置遞相望，四方物價之上下，雖極遠不四五日知，故食貨之重輕，盡權在掌握，朝廷獲美利而天下無甚貴甚賤之憂，得其術矣。
entries.en: From his circuit inspection offices to the capital he hired swift couriers at high pay and set relay stations in chains; price movements even in the remotest regions were known within four or five days. He thus controlled the weight of grain and goods—the court gained handsome profit while the realm avoided extreme inflation or collapse; he had mastered the art.
entries.literal: From the circuit inspection offices to the capital he paid high prices to recruit swift runners and set relay stations in sight of one another; the rise and fall of prices in the four quarters, however remote, was known within four or five days; thus the weight of grain and goods lay entirely in his grasp—the court gained fine profit while the realm had no fear of extreme dearth or cheapness; he had mastered the method.

entries.zh: 凡所任使，多收後進有幹能者。
entries.en: In appointments he mostly favored capable younger men.
entries.literal: In all appointments he mostly recruited younger men of ability and competence.

entries.zh: 其所總領，務乎急促，趨利者化之，遂以成風。
entries.en: His departments stressed speed and efficiency; profit-seekers took his example until it became the prevailing style.
entries.literal: What he oversaw stressed urgency; those who sought profit were transformed by him, and this became the prevailing style.

entries.zh: 當時權勢，或以親戚為托，晏亦應之，俸給之多少，命官之遲速，必如其誌，然未嘗得親職事。
entries.en: Powerful men sometimes asked favors for relatives; Yan complied on salary and appointment timing as they wished, yet never gave them substantive duties.
entries.literal: Powerful men of the time sometimes asked favors for relatives; Yan also complied—the amount of salary and the speed of appointment always matched their wishes, yet they never obtained substantive duties.

entries.zh: 其所領要務，必一時之選，故晏沒後二十余年，韓洄、元琇、裴腆、包佶、盧征、李衡繼掌財賦，皆晏故吏。
entries.en: For key posts he always chose the best men of the day; more than twenty years after his death Han Hui, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Bao Ji, Lu Zheng, and Li Heng in turn ran fiscal affairs—all his former subordinates.
entries.literal: For key duties under his charge he always chose men of the moment; thus more than twenty years after Yan's death Han Hui, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Bao Ji, Lu Zheng, and Li Heng successively managed fiscal affairs—all were Yan's former subordinates.

entries.zh: 其部吏居數千里之外，奉教令如在目前，雖寢興宴語，而無欺紿，四方動靜，莫不先知，事有可賀者，必先上章奏。
entries.en: Subordinates thousands of li away obeyed his orders as if he stood before them; even in private moments there was no deceit. He learned of events across the empire before anyone else, and good news was always reported to the throne first.
entries.literal: His subordinates, though thousands of li away, obeyed orders as if before his eyes; even in sleep, rising, feasting, or conversation there was no deception; movements in the four quarters were all known to him first; when something merited congratulation, a memorial was always submitted first.

entries.zh: 江淮茶、橘，晏與本道觀察使各歲貢之，皆欲其先至。
entries.en: Jianghuai tea and oranges were presented yearly as tribute by Yan and the circuit commissioners alike, each vying to arrive first.
entries.literal: Tea and oranges from Jianghuai—Yan and the circuit observation commissioners each presented them yearly as tribute, all wanting theirs to arrive first.

entries.zh: 有土之官，或封山斷道，禁前發者，晏厚以財力致之，常先他司，由是甚不為籓鎮所便。
entries.en: Local officials sometimes blocked roads to prevent early shipment; Yan used ample funds to secure delivery and usually beat other offices—making him deeply unpopular with the military governors.
entries.literal: Local officials sometimes sealed mountains and blocked roads to forbid early dispatch; Yan used ample funds to secure delivery and usually arrived before other offices—hence he was greatly disliked by the military governors.

entries.zh: 晏理家以儉約稱，而重交敦舊，頗以財貨遺天下名土，故人多稱之。
entries.en: Yan ran his household frugally but valued old friendships and often gave money to famous scholars; many spoke well of him for it.
entries.literal: Yan managed his household with a reputation for frugality, yet valued friendship and old ties and often gave wealth to famous scholars of the realm; therefore many praised him.

entries.zh: 善訓諸子，鹹有學藝。
entries.en: He trained his sons well; all were accomplished scholars.
entries.literal: He trained his sons well; all had learning and arts.

entries.zh: 任事十余年，權勢之重，鄰於宰相，要官重職，頗出其門。
entries.en: After more than ten years in office his power rivaled a chancellor's; many key posts went to his protégés.
entries.literal: In office more than ten years, his power and influence neared that of a chancellor; many key posts and heavy offices came from his faction.

entries.zh: 既有材力，視事敏速，乘機無滯，然多任數，挾權貴，固恩澤，有口者必利啖之。
entries.en: Talented and energetic, he handled affairs swiftly and seized every opportunity; yet he often used stratagem, leveraged the powerful, secured imperial favor, and bribed anyone who could speak for him.
entries.literal: He had both talent and force, handled affairs swiftly, seized opportunities without delay; yet he often relied on stratagem, leveraged the powerful, secured favor and grace, and anyone with a voice he surely fed with profit.

entries.zh: 當大歷時，事貴因循，軍國之用，皆仰於晏，未嘗檢轄。
entries.en: During the Dali era the court valued routine; military and state expenses all depended on Yan, and no one ever audited him.
entries.literal: During the Dali era affairs valued routine compliance; military and state expenses all depended on Yan, and no one ever audited him.

entries.zh: 張滂先善於宏，宏薦為司農少卿，及參欲以滂分掌江淮鹽鐵，詢之於宏，宏以滂嫉惡，慮以法繩徐粲，因曰：「滂強戾難制，不可用。」
entries.en: Zhang Pang had once been Ban Hong's ally, and Hong had helped make him vice director of agriculture. When Dou Can proposed splitting Jiang-Huai salt-and-iron duties with Pang, he asked Hong's view. Hong knew Pang was fierce and incorruptible and feared he would prosecute Xu Can, so he said, "Pang is harsh and unmanageable—he cannot be used."
entries.literal: Zhang Pang had first been on good terms with Hong; Hong recommended him as vice director of agriculture; when Can wished Pang to share management of Jiang-Huai salt-and-iron, he consulted Hong; Hong, because Pang hated evil and was severe, and fearing he would bind Xu Can with the law, therefore said: "Pang is violent and obstinate, hard to control—not usable."

entries.zh: 滂知之。
entries.en: Zhang Pang learned of the slight.
entries.literal: Pang knew of this.

entries.zh: 八年三月，參遂為上所疏，乃讓度支使，遂以宏專判，而參不欲使務悉歸於宏，問計京兆尹薛玨，玨曰：「二子交惡，而滂剛決，若分鹽鐵轉運於滂，必能制宏。」
entries.en: In the third month of 792 Dou Can fell from imperial favor and surrendered the finance commission to Ban Hong—but Can did not want Hong controlling everything. He consulted Metropolitan Prefect Xue Jue, who advised: "Those two are enemies, and Pang is tough and resolute; give him salt-and-iron transport and he can check Hong."
entries.literal: Third month of year eight, Can was therefore denounced to the emperor; he yielded the disbursement commission; Hong was then given sole judgment; yet Can did not wish all affairs to fall wholly to Hong; he consulted Metropolitan Prefect Xue Jue; Jue said: "The two men are mutually hostile, and Pang is firm and decisive; if salt-and-iron transport is divided to Pang, he will surely be able to restrain Hong."

entries.zh: 參乃薦滂為戶部侍郎、鹽鐵使、判轉運，尚隸於宏以悅之。
entries.en: Dou Can accordingly recommended Zhang Pang as vice minister of revenue, salt commissioner, and transport supervisor—formally under Hong, to keep him appeased.
entries.literal: Can then recommended Pang as vice minister of revenue, salt-and-iron commissioner, judging transport, still subordinate to Hong to please him.

entries.zh: 江淮兩稅，悉宏主之，置巡院，然令宏、滂共擇其官。
entries.en: Ban Hong kept control of the Jiang-Huai land tax and set up inspection offices, but both men were told to jointly appoint their staff.
entries.literal: Jiang-Huai double tax was entirely managed by Hong; inspection depots were established; yet Hong and Pang together were to select their officials.

entries.zh: 滂請鹽鐵舊簿書於宏，宏不與之。
entries.en: Zhang Pang asked Ban Hong for the old salt-and-iron account books; Hong refused to hand them over.
entries.literal: Pang requested old salt-and-iron ledgers from Hong; Hong would not give them.

entries.zh: 每署院官，宏、滂更相是非，莫有用者。
entries.en: Every time one of them nominated a depot official, the other vetoed the choice, and positions stayed empty.
entries.literal: Each time depot officials were appointed, Hong and Pang alternately negated each other; none could be used.

entries.zh: 滂乃奏曰：「班宏與臣相戾，巡院多闕官。
entries.en: Zhang Pang memorialized: "Ban Hong and I are at loggerheads, and many inspection posts stand unfilled.
entries.literal: Pang then memorialized: "Ban Hong is at odds with me; inspection depots have many vacant posts.

entries.zh: 臣掌財賦，國家大計，職不修，無所逃罪。
entries.en: I oversee revenue—the lifeblood of the state. If I fail in my duties, I cannot escape blame.
entries.literal: I manage finance and taxation—the great plan of the state; if duties are not maintained, there is no escaping guilt.

entries.zh: 今宏若此，何以輯事？」
entries.en: With Hong acting like this, how can the work get done?"
entries.literal: Now if Hong is like this, how can affairs be assembled?"

entries.zh: 遂令分掌之。
entries.en: The emperor ordered them to split the duties between them.
entries.literal: Thereupon an order was issued to divide management.

entries.zh: 無幾，宏言於宰相趙憬、陸贄曰：「宏職轉運，年運江淮米五十萬斛，前年增七十萬斛，以實太倉，幸無過。
entries.en: Before long Ban Hong told Chancellors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi: "In my transport duties I once moved five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai grain each year, and two years ago seven hundred thousand shi to fill the Great Storehouse—and I met every target.
entries.literal: Before long Hong spoke to chancellors Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi: "Hong's duty is transport—each year five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice shipped; the year before last increased to seven hundred thousand shi to fill the Great Storehouse; fortunately without fault.

entries.zh: 今職移於人，不知何謂？」
entries.en: Now my duties have been handed to someone else—what am I to make of that?"
entries.literal: Now duties shifted to another—what is this to mean?"

entries.zh: 滂時在側，忿然曰：「尚書失言甚矣！
entries.en: Zhang Pang, who was present, snapped: "Director, you go too far!
entries.literal: Pang was then at the side; angrily he said: "Director, you misspeak greatly!

entries.zh: 若運務畢舉，朝廷固不奪之，蓋由喪公錢、縱奸吏故也。
entries.en: If you had truly done your job, the court would never have taken transport away from you. You lost it because you squandered public funds and protected crooked subordinates.
entries.literal: If transport duties were fully accomplished, the court naturally would not strip them; it is because of losing public money and indulging corrupt clerks.

entries.zh: 且凡為度支胥吏，不一歲，資累鉅萬，僮馬第宅，僭於王公，非盜官財何以致是？
entries.en: And every clerk in the finance office amasses fortunes of tens of thousands within a year—slaves, horses, mansions fit for princes. How else could they afford it except by robbing the treasury?
entries.literal: Moreover all who are disbursement clerks, within one year assets accumulate in the tens of thousands; slaves, horses, mansions surpassing kings and dukes—if not stealing official wealth, how attain this?

entries.zh: 道呼喧喧，無不知之，聖上故令滂分掌。
entries.en: Everyone on the road knows it, which is exactly why His Majesty ordered me to share the duties.
entries.literal: Along the roads the clamor is loud—none do not know; the sage emperor therefore had Pang divide management.

entries.zh: 公向所言，無乃歸怨於上乎、」宏默然不對。
entries.en: Are you not pinning the blame on the emperor himself?" Ban Hong fell silent.
entries.literal: What the lord just said—might it not shift blame onto the sovereign?" Hong silently did not reply.

entries.zh: 是日，宏稱疾於第，滂往問之，宏不見，憬、贄乃以宏、滂之言上聞。
entries.en: That day Ban Hong feigned illness at home. When Zhang Pang came to visit, Hong refused to see him. Zhao Jing and Lu Zhi reported both men's words to the throne.
entries.literal: That day Hong claimed illness at his residence; Pang went to inquire; Hong would not see him; Jing and Zhi then reported Hong and Pang's words to the emperor.

entries.zh: 由是遵大歷故事，如劉晏、韓滉所分。
entries.en: The court then reverted to the Dali-era arrangement, dividing finance as Liu Yan and Han Huang once had.
entries.literal: Thereby following Dali precedent, as Liu Yan and Han Huang had divided duties.

entries.zh: 滂至揚州按徐粲，逮仆妾子侄，得贓鉅萬，乃徙嶺表。
entries.en: Zhang Pang went to Yangzhou to prosecute Xu Can, seized his household and kin, uncovered bribes totaling tens of thousands, and had him banished to the far south.
entries.literal: Pang reached Yangzhou to investigate Xu Can; arrested maids, concubines, sons and nephews; obtained bribes in the tens of thousands; then Xu was exiled beyond the Ling passes.

entries.zh: 故參得罪，宏頗有力焉。
entries.en: When Dou Can finally fell, Ban Hong had played no small part in bringing him down.
entries.literal: Thus when Can incurred guilt, Hong contributed considerable force to it.

entries.zh: 勤恪官署，晨入夕歸，下吏勞而未嘗厭苦，清白勤幹，稱之於時。
entries.en: He was tireless at his desk, arriving at dawn and leaving at dusk; though his staff toiled endlessly he never complained. His honesty and industry won wide praise.
entries.literal: Diligent at office, entering at dawn and returning at evening; subordinates labored yet he never showed weariness; pure, white, diligent, capable—praised in his time.

entries.zh: 貞元八年七月卒，年七十三，廢朝，加贈，謚曰敬。
entries.en: He died in the seventh month of 792, aged seventy-three. Court audiences were suspended, extra honors granted, and he was posthumously titled "Reverent."
entries.literal: Seventh month Zhenyuan eighth year he died, age seventy-three; court mourning suspended; additional posthumous honors; posthumous title Jing (Reverent).

entries.zh: 李巽，字令叔，趙郡人。
entries.en: Li Xun, courtesy name Ling Shu, came from Zhao Commandery.
entries.literal: Li Xun, courtesy name Ling Shu, was a native of Zhao Commandery.

entries.zh: 少苦心為學，以明經調補華州參軍，拔萃登科，授鄠縣尉。
entries.en: In his youth he applied himself rigorously to learning. He passed the classics examination and was appointed aide in Huazhou. After winning selection in the superior examination he was made assistant magistrate of E County.
entries.literal: In youth he painstakingly studied; through the classics examination he was appointed Huazhou aide; selected in the superior examination and passed; granted Assistant Magistrate of E County.

entries.zh: 周歷臺省，由左司郎中出為常州刺史。
entries.en: He served in various posts in the Secretariat and Chancellery, and left the capital from his post as Director in the Left Bureau to become prefect of Changzhou.
entries.literal: He passed through the Secretariat and Chancellery offices; from Director in the Left Bureau he went out as Prefect of Changzhou.

entries.zh: 逾年，召為給事中，出為湖南觀察使，銳於為理。
entries.en: A year later he was recalled to serve as a Supervising Secretariat Drafter, then sent out as commissioner of Hunan, where he governed with sharp efficiency.
entries.literal: After a year he was summoned as Supervising Secretary, sent out as Hunan Observation Commissioner; he was keen on governance.

entries.zh: 五年，改江西觀察使，加檢校散騎常侍、兼御史大夫。
entries.en: In his fifth year he was transferred to Jiangxi as observation commissioner, with the additional titles of Acting Regular Palace Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Jiangxi Observation Commissioner, with additional Acting Regular Palace Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 巽持下以法，吏不敢欺，而動必察之。
entries.en: Li Xun governed his subordinates strictly by law. Clerks did not dare cheat him—and he scrutinized every move they made.
entries.literal: Xun held subordinates by law; clerks did not dare deceive, yet every movement he surely investigated.

entries.zh: 順宗即位，入為兵部侍郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Li Xun was brought back to serve as Vice Minister of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 司徒杜佑判度支鹽鐵轉運使，以巽幹治，奏為副使。
entries.en: Situ Du You headed the finance, salt, iron, and transport commission. Impressed by Li Xun's administrative skill, he recommended him as deputy commissioner.
entries.literal: Situ Du You presided over finance, salt, iron, and transport; because Xun was capable in administration, he memorialized him as vice commissioner.

entries.zh: 佑辭重位，巽遂專領度支鹽鐵使。
entries.en: When Du You stepped down from the heavy office, Li Xun took sole charge of the finance and salt commission.
entries.literal: You declined the heavy post; Xun then solely headed the Finance and Salt Commissioner.

entries.zh: 榷筦之法，號為難重，唯大歷中僕射劉晏雅得其術，賦入豐羨。
entries.en: The state monopoly system was notoriously difficult to manage. Only in the Dali era had Vice Director Liu Yan truly mastered it, yielding abundant revenue.
entries.literal: The monopoly-and-control laws were called difficult and heavy; only in the Dali era Vice Director Liu Yan elegantly mastered their technique, and tax revenue was abundant.

entries.zh: 巽掌使一年，征課所入，類晏之多歲，明年過之，又一年加一百八十萬貫。
entries.en: In his first year in office Li Xun's tax collections matched Liu Yan's best years. The next year he exceeded that total, and in the following year he added another 1.8 million strings of cash.
entries.literal: Xun held the commission one year; revenue collected matched Yan's many plentiful years; the next year surpassed it; in another year he added one million eight hundred thousand strings.

entries.zh: 舊制，每歲運江淮米五十萬斛抵河陰，久不盈其數，唯巽三年登焉。
entries.en: By regulation five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai grain were shipped each year to Heyin, a quota long unmet—until Li Xun fulfilled it three years running.
entries.literal: By old regulation, each year five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice were transported to Heyin; for a long time the quota was not filled; only Xun in three years achieved it.

entries.zh: 遷兵部尚書，明年改吏部尚書，使任如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to Minister of Military Affairs, and the following year transferred to Minister of Personnel while retaining his commission unchanged.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Military Affairs; the next year changed to Minister of Personnel; his commissioner duties remained as before.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：歷代操利柄為國計者，莫不損下益上，危人自安，變法以弄權，斂怨以構禍，皆有之矣。
entries.en: The historian writes: Throughout history, those who held the reins of fiscal power in service of state finance have invariably enriched the throne at the people's expense, endangered others to save themselves, changed the laws to play politics, and stockpiled resentments that bred disaster—all of this has happened before.
entries.literal: The historian says: In every age those who grasped the profit lever for state planning, without exception harmed the lower to benefit the upper, endangered others to secure themselves, changed laws to wield power, and gathered resentments to bring on calamity—all have had these.

entries.zh: 如劉晏通擁滯，任才能，富其國而不勞於民，儉於家而利於眾。
entries.en: Liu Yan was different: he cleared bottlenecks, put talent to use, enriched the state without overburdening the people, kept his household frugal, and brought benefit to all.
entries.literal: Such as Liu Yan, who cleared congestion, employed talent and ability, enriched the state without burdening the people, was frugal in his household and beneficial to the multitude.

entries.zh: 或問曰：鄭子產吏不能欺，宓子賤吏不忍欺，西門豹吏不敢欺。
entries.en: One might ask: "With Zichan of Zheng, clerks could not cheat him; with Master Fu Ziqian, they could not bear to cheat him; with Ximen Bao, they did not dare cheat him."
entries.literal: Someone asked: "Zi Chan of Zheng—clerks could not deceive him; Mi Zi Jian—clerks could not bear to deceive him; Xi Men Bao—clerks did not dare deceive him."

entries.zh: 三子者，古之賢人也，吏皆懷其欺而不能、不忍、不敢也。
entries.en: These three were sages of old. Their clerks may have wished to cheat them, but found themselves unable, unwilling, or too afraid.
entries.literal: These three men were worthy men of antiquity; clerks all harbored deception but could not, could not bear to, and did not dare.

entries.zh: 晏之吏，遠近自不欺者何也？
entries.en: Why was it that Liu Yan's subordinates, near and far, simply did not cheat?
entries.literal: Yan's clerks, near and far, naturally did not deceive—why?

entries.zh: 答曰：蓋任其才而得其人也。
entries.en: The answer: because he put the right people in the right roles and let them apply their talents.
entries.literal: The answer: Probably because he employed their talents and obtained the right men.

entries.zh: 晏歿，故吏二十余年繼掌財賦，不其是哉！
entries.en: After Liu Yan's death, his former subordinates continued to manage the treasury for more than twenty years—is that not proof enough?
entries.literal: When Yan died, his former clerks for more than twenty years successively managed finance and taxation—is this not proof!

entries.zh: 《史記貨殖》云：「平糶齊物，關市不乏，治國之道也。」
entries.en: The "Wealth and Profit" chapter of the Records of the Historian says, "Regulating grain prices to stabilize goods, keeping markets and frontier passes supplied—this is the art of governing."
entries.literal: The "Wealth and Profit" chapter of the Records of the Historian says: "Evening out grain purchases to equalize goods, markets and passes not lacking—this is the way of governing a state."

entries.zh: 晏治天下，無甚貴甚賤之物，泛言治國者，其可及乎！
entries.en: Under Liu Yan's administration the realm saw neither ruinously high nor ruinously low prices. How many who speak of governing a nation can match that?
entries.literal: Yan governed the realm; there were no extremely expensive or extremely cheap goods; speaking broadly of those who govern states, can they reach this!

entries.zh: 舉真卿才，忠也，減王縉罪，正也，忠正之道，復出於人，嗚呼！
entries.en: To recommend Yan Zhenqing showed loyalty; to lighten Wang Jin's punishment showed integrity. The virtues of loyalty and righteousness lived again in a single man—alas!
entries.literal: Recommending Zhenqing's talent was loyalty; reducing Wang Jin's punishment was righteousness; the way of loyalty and righteousness again emerged in a person—alas!

entries.zh: 本秀於林，風必摧之，常袞見忌於前，楊炎致冤於後，可為長嘆息矣！
entries.en: A tree that stands above the forest is sure to be broken by the wind. Chang Gun resented him first; Yang Yan engineered his ruin afterward—enough to draw a long sigh.
entries.literal: Timber outstanding in the forest—wind is sure to break it; Chang Gun envied him earlier; Yang Yan brought wrongful death later—one can only sigh long!

entries.zh: 時譏有口者以利啖之，茍不塞讒口，何以持重權？
entries.en: At the time, critics with wagging tongues were bought off with profit. Unless you silenced those tongues, how could you hold real power?
entries.literal: At the time slanderers with mouths were fed with profit; if one does not stop slanderous mouths, how can one hold heavy power?

entries.zh: 即無以展其才，濟其國矣。
entries.en: Without that, there was no way to deploy one's abilities or serve the nation.
entries.literal: Then there is no way to display one's talent and save the state.

entries.zh: 是其術也，又何譏焉。
entries.en: That was his approach—and what is there to condemn in it?
entries.literal: This was his method—what is there to slander?

entries.zh: 第五琦促辦應卒，民不加賦，而國豐饒，亦庶幾矣。
entries.en: Fifth Qi mobilized resources swiftly in crisis without raising taxes on the people, and the treasury still grew flush—a feat nearly as admirable.
entries.literal: Fifth Qi rushed preparations to meet emergencies; the people were not increased in taxes, yet the state was abundant—this too nearly succeeds.

entries.zh: 然鑄錢變法，物貴身危，其何陋哉！
entries.en: Yet his recoinage and legal tinkering drove up prices and put his own life at risk—how crude!
entries.literal: Yet casting coins and changing laws made goods expensive and himself endangered—how base!

entries.zh: 凡利國者，農商之外，不可為也。
entries.en: As a rule, anything that enriches the state beyond agriculture and commerce should not be attempted.
entries.literal: Generally what benefits the state—outside agriculture and commerce—cannot be done.

entries.zh: 宏、滂爭權樹黨，皆非令人。
entries.en: Ban Hong and Zhang Pang schemed for power and built factions—neither was a man one could respect.
entries.literal: Hong and Pang fought for power and built factions—neither was a man to be admired.

entries.zh: 紹之謹密幹事，巽之皦察精辨，亦足可稱。
entries.en: Wang Shao's caution and efficiency, Li Xun's sharp-eyed precision—these too deserve recognition.
entries.literal: Shao's discretion in handling affairs, Xun's clear scrutiny and precise discernment—also sufficient to praise.

entries.zh: 贊曰：豐財忠良，晏道為長。
entries.en: In praise: Enriching the treasury through loyal service—Liu Yan's way stands foremost.
entries.literal: Eulogy: Abundant wealth and loyal integrity—Yan's way is foremost.

entries.zh: 琦、宏、滂、巽，鹹以利彰。
entries.en: Fifth Qi, Ban Hong, Zhang Pang, and Li Xun—all won fame through fiscal mastery.
entries.literal: Qi, Hong, Pang, and Xun—all alike were famed through profit.

entries.zh: 張鎰，蘇州人，朔方節度使齊丘之子也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi was a native of Suzhou and the son of Qi Qiu, military governor of Shuofang.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi was a native of Suzhou and the son of Qi Qiu, military governor of Shuofang.

entries.zh: 以門廕授左衛兵曹參軍。
entries.en: He received appointment as Left Guards Army Office Record Officer through hereditary privilege.
entries.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed Left Guards Army Office Record Officer.

entries.zh: 郭子儀為關內副元帥，以嘗伏事齊丘，辟鎰為判官。
entries.en: When Guo Ziyi served as vice commander-in-chief of Guannei, he recruited Zhang Yi as a staff judge, having once served under Qi Qiu himself.
entries.literal: When Guo Ziyi served as vice commander-in-chief of Guannei, because he had once served under Qi Qiu, he recruited Yi as staff judge.

entries.zh: 授大理評事，遷殿中侍御史。
entries.en: He was appointed a reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and later promoted to Palace Censor.
entries.literal: He was appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and promoted to Palace Censor.

entries.zh: 乾元初，華原令盧樅以公事呵責邑人內侍齊令詵，令詵銜之，構誣。
entries.en: Early in the Qianyuan era, Lu Cong, magistrate of Huayuan, publicly rebuked the local eunuch Qi Lingshen over official business. Lingshen nursed a grudge and fabricated charges against him.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, Lu Cong, magistrate of Huayuan, publicly rebuked the local eunuch Qi Lingshen over official business; Lingshen harbored resentment and fabricated charges.

entries.zh: 外發鎰按驗，樅當降官，及下有司，樅當杖死。
entries.en: Zhang Yi was sent from outside to investigate the case. Lu Cong should have been demoted, but once the matter reached the judicial offices, he faced death by beating.
entries.literal: An external investigation was dispatched with Yi to examine the case; Cong should have been demoted, but once the case reached the judiciary, Cong faced death by beating.

entries.zh: 鎰其公服白其母曰：「上疏理樅，樅必免死，鎰必坐貶。
entries.en: Still in his official robes, Zhang Yi told his mother, "If I submit a memorial to clear Lu Cong, he will surely escape death, but I will surely be demoted in punishment.
entries.literal: Yi, still in his official robes, told his mother, saying: 'If I submit a memorial to vindicate Cong, Cong will surely escape death, but Yi will surely suffer demotion.

entries.zh: 若以私則鎰負於當官，貶則以太夫人為憂，敢問所安？」
entries.en: If I act from private feeling, I fail in my duty as an official; if I accept demotion, I will cause you, my lady, great worry. May I ask where your peace lies?"
entries.literal: If I act from private feeling, then Yi fails in his duty as an official; if I accept demotion, then the Lady Dowager will be troubled—dare I ask where you find peace?'

entries.zh: 母曰：爾無累於道，吾所安也。」
entries.en: His mother replied, "You will not be burdened in the Way—that is where I find my peace."
entries.literal: His mother said: 'You will not be burdened in the Way—this is where I find peace.'

entries.zh: 遂執奏正罪，樅獲配流，鎰貶撫州司戶。
entries.en: He then submitted a memorial insisting on the proper penalty. Lu Cong was sentenced to exile, and Zhang Yi was demoted to registrar of Fuzhou.
entries.literal: Thereupon he firmly submitted a memorial to establish the proper penalty; Cong was sentenced to exile, and Yi was demoted to registrar of Fuzhou.

entries.zh: 量移晉陵令，未之官，洪吉觀察張鎬辟為判官，奏授殿中侍御史。
entries.en: He was transferred by degree to magistrate of Jinling, but before he took up the post, Zhang Hao, observation commissioner of Hong-Ji, recruited him as a staff judge and memorialized for his appointment as Palace Censor.
entries.literal: He was transferred by degree to be magistrate of Jinling but had not taken up the post when Zhang Hao, observation commissioner of Hong-Ji, recruited him as staff judge and memorialized for his appointment as Palace Censor.

entries.zh: 遷屯田員外郎，轉祠部、右司二員外。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Public Lands and then transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and vice director of the Right Office.
entries.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Public Lands and transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and vice director of the Right Office.

entries.zh: 母憂居喪有聞，免喪，除司勛員外。
entries.en: He became known for the propriety with which he observed mourning for his mother. When the mourning period ended, he was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Merits.
entries.literal: During mourning for his mother he conducted the rites with such renown that, once the mourning ended, he was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Merits.

entries.zh: 交遊不雜，與楊綰、崔祐甫相善。
entries.en: He kept his associations selective and was on good terms with Yang Wan and Cui Youfu.
entries.literal: His associations were not mixed; he was on good terms with Yang Wan and Cui Youfu.

entries.zh: 大歷五年，除濠州刺史，為政清凈，州事大理。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Dali, he was appointed prefect of Hao. His administration was pure and restrained, and the affairs of the prefecture were brought into good order.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Dali, he was appointed prefect of Hao; his governance was pure and clean, and the affairs of the prefecture were greatly ordered.

entries.zh: 乃招經術之士，講訓生徒，比去郡，升明經者四十余人。
entries.en: He recruited scholars of the classics to instruct students, and by the time he left the prefecture, more than forty had passed the Mingjing examination.
entries.literal: He then recruited scholars of the classics to instruct students, and by the time he left the prefecture, more than forty had passed the Mingjing examination.

entries.zh: 撰《三禮圖》九卷、《五經微旨》十四卷、《孟子音義》三卷。
entries.en: He authored Three Rites Illustrations in nine fascicles, Subtle Meanings of the Five Classics in fourteen fascicles, and Phonological Glosses on Mencius in three fascicles.
entries.literal: He compiled Three Rites Illustrations in nine fascicles, Subtle Meanings of the Five Classics in fourteen fascicles, and Phonological Glosses on Mencius in three fascicles.

entries.zh: 李靈曜反於汴州，鎰訓練鄉兵，嚴守禦之備，詔書褒異，加侍御史、沿淮鎮守使。
entries.en: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou, Zhang Yi trained local militia and rigorously prepared the defenses. An imperial edict singled him out for praise and added the posts of attendant censor and commissioner for defense along the Huai.
entries.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou, Yi trained local militia and strictly prepared defenses; an imperial edict praised him with distinction and added the posts of attendant censor and commissioner for defense along the Huai.

entries.zh: 尋遷壽州刺史，使如故。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to prefect of Shouzhou while retaining his commissioner post.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to prefect of Shouzhou, retaining his commissioner post as before.

entries.zh: 德宗即位，除江南西道都團練觀察使、洪州刺史、兼御史中丞，征拜吏部侍郎，尋除河中晉絳都防禦觀察使。
entries.en: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Zhang Yi was appointed overall training and observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit, prefect of Hongzhou, and concurrently vice censor-in-chief. He was then summoned to serve as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and soon afterward appointed defense and observation commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Yi was appointed overall training and observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit, prefect of Hongzhou, and concurrently vice censor-in-chief; he was summoned and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and soon afterward made defense and observation commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang.

entries.zh: 到官數日，改汴滑節度觀察使、汴州刺史、兼御史大夫，以疾辭，逗留於中路，征入，養疾私第。
entries.en: Within days of reaching his post, he was reassigned as military governor and observation commissioner of Bian-Hua, prefect of Bianzhou, and concurrently censor-in-chief. He declined on grounds of illness, lingered en route, was recalled to court, and convalesced at his private residence.
entries.literal: Within days of reaching his post, he was reassigned as military governor and observation commissioner of Bian-Hua, prefect of Bianzhou, and concurrently censor-in-chief; he declined on grounds of illness, lingered on the road, was recalled to court, and convalesced at his private residence.

entries.zh: 未幾，拜中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿學士，修國史。
entries.en: Before long he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and compiler of the national history.
entries.literal: Before long he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and compiler of the national history.

entries.zh: 建中三年正月，太仆卿趙縱為奴當千發其陰事，縱下御史臺，貶循州司馬，留當千於內侍省。
entries.en: In the first month of the third year of Jianzhong, Grand Stable Master Zhao Zong was denounced by his slave Dangqian for secret misconduct. Zhao Zong was sent to the Censorate and demoted to military adjutant of Xunzhou, while Dangqian was retained in the Palace Domestic Service.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jianzhong, Grand Stable Master Zhao Zong was denounced by his slave Dangqian for secret misconduct; Zong was sent to the Censorate, demoted to military adjutant of Xunzhou, and Dangqian was retained in the Palace Domestic Service.

entries.zh: 鎰上疏論之曰：
entries.en: Zhang Yi submitted a memorial on the matter, saying:
entries.literal: Yi submitted a memorial discussing the matter, saying:

entries.zh: 伏見趙縱為奴所告下獄，人皆震懼，未測聖情。
entries.en: I observe that Zhao Zong was reported by a slave and sent to prison. Everyone is shaken with fear, unable to discern Your Majesty's intent.
entries.literal: I humbly observe that Zhao Zong was reported by a slave and sent to prison; all are shaken with fear and cannot fathom the sage mind.

entries.zh: 貞觀二年，太宗謂侍臣曰：「比有奴告其主謀逆，此極弊法，特須禁斷。
entries.en: In the second year of Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong told his attending ministers, "Lately slaves have been reporting their masters for plotting rebellion. This is an extremely corrupt practice and must be strictly forbidden.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong told his attending ministers: 'Recently there have been slaves reporting their masters for plotting rebellion—this is an extremely corrupt practice and must be specially forbidden and cut off.

entries.zh: 假令有謀反者，必不獨成，自有他人論之，豈藉其奴告也。
entries.en: Even if someone were plotting rebellion, he would surely not accomplish it alone; others would naturally report it. Why rely on a slave's accusation.
entries.literal: Even if there were one plotting rebellion, he would surely not accomplish it alone; others would naturally report it—why rely on a slave's report.

entries.zh: 自今已後，奴告主者皆不受，盡令斬決。」
entries.en: From this time forward, no report by a slave against his master shall be accepted, and all such slaves shall be executed by decapitation."
entries.literal: From this time forward, reports by slaves against masters shall none be accepted, and all such slaves shall be ordered executed by decapitation.'

entries.zh: 由是賤不得幹貴，下不得陵上，教化之本既正，悖亂之漸不生。
entries.en: By this the lowly could not interfere with the noble and the inferior could not encroach upon the superior. The foundation of moral instruction was set right, and the seeds of rebellion did not take root.
entries.literal: By this the lowly could not interfere with the noble, and the inferior could not encroach upon the superior; the root of instruction was corrected, and the beginnings of rebellion did not arise.

entries.zh: 為國之經，百代難改，欲全其事體，實在防微。
entries.en: As a fundamental principle of statecraft, it is difficult to alter across generations. To preserve the integrity of the system truly depends on guarding against small beginnings.
entries.literal: As a constant of governing the state, it is hard to alter for a hundred generations; to preserve the integrity of the matter truly lies in guarding against the minute.

entries.zh: 頃者長安令李濟得罪因奴，萬年令霍晏得罪因婢，愚賤之輩，悖慢成風，主反畏之，動遭誣告，充溢府縣，莫能斷決。
entries.en: Recently Chang'an magistrate Li Ji and Wannian magistrate Huo Yan both fell afoul of the law because of slaves and maids. Among the foolish and base, insolence became the fashion; masters instead feared their servants and were constantly subjected to false accusations. Cases overflowed the prefectures and counties, and none could be resolved.
entries.literal: Recently Chang'an magistrate Li Ji offended because of a slave, and Wannian magistrate Huo Yan offended because of a maid; among the foolish and base, insolence became the fashion, masters instead feared them, and at every turn suffered false accusations—the cases overflowed prefectures and counties and none could decide them.

entries.zh: 建中元年五月二十八日，詔曰：準鬥競律，諸奴婢告主，非謀叛已上者，同自首法，並準律處分。」
entries.en: On the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month of the first year of Jianzhong, an edict declared, "According to the statute on brawling and litigation, any slave or maid who reports a master for an offense short of plotting rebellion shall be treated under the law on voluntary surrender and punished according to statute."
entries.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month of the first year of Jianzhong, an edict said: 'According to the statute on brawling and litigation, all slaves and maids reporting masters for offenses other than plotting rebellion or above shall be treated under the law on voluntary surrender and punished according to statute.'

entries.zh: 自此奴婢復順，獄訴稍息。
entries.en: From this point slaves and maids again became compliant, and litigation gradually subsided.
entries.literal: From this the slaves and maids again became compliant, and prison litigation gradually subsided.

entries.zh: 今趙縱非叛逆，奴實奸兇，奴在禁中，縱獨下獄，考之於法，或恐未正。
entries.en: Zhao Zong is not a rebel, while the slave is truly treacherous and vicious. The slave remains in the palace while Zhao Zong alone is sent to prison. Examined under the law, I fear this may not be correct.
entries.literal: Now Zhao Zong is not a rebel, while the slave is truly treacherous and vicious; the slave remains in the palace confines while Zong alone is sent to prison—in examination under law, I fear this may not be correct.

entries.zh: 將帥之功，莫大於子儀；
entries.en: Among generals, none has greater merit than Guo Ziyi;
entries.literal: Among generals, no merit is greater than that of Ziyi;

entries.zh: 人臣之位，莫大於尚父。
entries.en: and among subjects, none holds a rank higher than Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Among subjects, no rank is greater than Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 歿身未幾，墳土僅乾，兩婿先已當辜，趙縱今又下獄。
entries.en: Not long after his death, the earth on his grave had barely dried. Two sons-in-law had already been found guilty, and now Zhao Zong has been sent to prison as well.
entries.literal: Not long after his death, the grave earth had barely dried; two sons-in-law had already been found guilty, and now Zhao Zong is again sent to prison.

entries.zh: 設令縱實抵法，所告非奴，才經數月，連罪三婿。
entries.en: Even if Zhao Zong truly merited punishment under the law, the accuser was not a slave, and within only a few months three sons-in-law have been punished in succession.
entries.literal: Even if Zong truly merited punishment under law, the accuser was not a slave, and within only a few months three sons-in-law have been punished in succession.

entries.zh: 錄勛念舊，猶或可容，況在章程，本宜宥免。
entries.en: Recording merit and remembering old ties might still allow forbearance; moreover, under the regulations, pardon and exemption would be appropriate.
entries.literal: Recording merit and remembering old ties might still allow forbearance; moreover, under the regulations, pardon and exemption were originally appropriate.

entries.zh: 陛下方誅群賊，大用武臣，雖見寵於當時，恐息望於他日。
entries.en: Your Majesty is now executing rebels and greatly employing military ministers. Though they are favored in the present, I fear their hopes will be extinguished hereafter.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is now executing the band of rebels and greatly employing military ministers; though they are favored in the present, I fear their hopes will be extinguished hereafter.

entries.zh: 太宗之令典尚在，陛下之明詔始行，一朝偕違，不與眾守，於教化恐失，於刑法恐煩，所益悉無，所傷至廣。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong's authoritative precedent still stands, and Your Majesty's enlightened edict has only just been promulgated. To violate both at once and not abide with the rest—in moral instruction there will likely be loss, and in penal law there will likely be trouble. The benefit is entirely absent, while the harm is far-reaching.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizong's authoritative precedent still stands, and Your Majesty's enlightened edict has only just been promulgated; to violate both at once and not abide with the multitude—in instruction there will likely be loss, in penal law there will likely be trouble; the benefit is entirely none, the harm extremely broad.

entries.zh: 臣非私趙縱，非惡此奴，叨居股肱，職在匡弼，斯昌大體，敢不極言。
entries.en: I am not acting privately for Zhao Zong, nor do I bear personal hatred toward this slave. Occupying a place at Your Majesty's right hand, my duty is to assist and correct. On a matter of such broad principle, I dare not speak less than fully.
entries.literal: Your servant is not acting privately for Zhao Zong, nor does he hate this slave; occupying the place of arm and thigh, my duty is to assist and correct—on this great principle I dare not speak less than fully.

entries.zh: 伏乞聖慈，納臣愚懇。
entries.en: I humbly beg Your Majesty's compassion to accept my earnest plea.
entries.literal: I humbly beg the sage compassion to accept your servant's earnest plea.

entries.zh: 上深納之，縱於是左貶而已，當千杖殺之。
entries.en: The emperor deeply accepted the memorial. Zhao Zong was merely demoted, and Dangqian was beaten to death.
entries.literal: The emperor deeply accepted it; Zong was therefore merely demoted to the left, and Dangqian was beaten to death.

entries.zh: 鎰乃令召子儀家僮數百人，以死奴示之。
entries.en: Zhang Yi then summoned several hundred of Guo Ziyi's household slaves and showed them the dead slave.
entries.literal: Yi then ordered several hundred of Ziyi's household slaves summoned and showed them the dead slave.

entries.zh: 盧杞忌鎰名重道直，無以陷之，以方用兵西邊，杞乃偽請行，上固以不可，因薦鎰以中書侍郎為鳳翔隴右節度使代硃泚，與吐蕃相尚結贊等盟於清水。
entries.en: Lu Qi resented Zhang Yi's great reputation and upright conduct and had no means to entrap him. As troops were then being deployed on the western frontier, Qi falsely offered to go in person. The emperor firmly refused, and Qi therefore recommended Zhang Yi, with the title of vice director of the Secretariat, as military governor of Fengxiang-Longyou to replace Zhu Ci. Zhang Yi then entered into an alliance with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan and others at Qingshui.
entries.literal: Lu Qi resented Yi's great reputation and upright conduct and had no means to entrap him; as troops were then being used on the western frontier, Qi falsely requested to go himself; the emperor firmly held it impossible, and therefore recommended Yi, with the title vice director of the Secretariat, as military governor of Fengxiang-Longyou to replace Zhu Ci, and Yi allied with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan and others at Qingshui.

entries.zh: 將盟，鎰與結贊約各以二千人赴壇所，執兵者半之，列於壇外二百步；
entries.en: Before the alliance, Zhang Yi and Jiezan agreed that each side would bring two thousand men to the altar site. Half would bear arms and be arrayed two hundred paces outside the altar;
entries.literal: Before the alliance, Yi and Jiezan agreed that each would bring two thousand men to the altar site; half would bear arms and be arrayed two hundred paces outside the altar;

entries.zh: 散從者半之，分立壇下。
entries.en: and half would be unarmed attendants stationed separately below the altar.
entries.literal: half would be unarmed attendants and be stationed separately below the altar.

entries.zh: 鎰與賓佐齊映、齊抗及盟官崔漢衡、樊澤、常魯、於頔等七人，皆朝服；
entries.en: Zhang Yi, his staff members Qi Ying and Qi Kang, and alliance officials Cui Hanheng, Fan Ze, Chang Lu, Yu Di, and others—seven men in all—were all in court dress;
entries.literal: Yi with his staff members Qi Ying and Qi Kang and alliance officials Cui Hanheng, Fan Ze, Chang Lu, Yu Di, and others—seven men in all—were all in court dress;

entries.zh: 結贊與其本國將相論悉頰藏、論臧熱、論利陁、斯官者、論力徐等亦七人，俱升壇為盟。
entries.en: Jiezan, together with his country's generals and ministers Lun Xibizang, Lun Zangre, Lun Lituo, Siguanzhe, Lun Lixu, and others—also seven men—all ascended the altar to make the alliance.
entries.literal: Jiezan with his own country's generals and ministers Lun Xibizang, Lun Zangre, Lun Lituo, Siguanzhe, Lun Lixu, and others—also seven men—all ascended the altar to make the alliance.

entries.zh: 初，約漢以牛，蕃以馬為牲，鎰恥與之盟，將殺其禮，乃請結贊曰：「漢非牛不田，蕃非馬不行，今請以羊豕犬三物代之。」
entries.en: At first it was agreed that the Han side would use an ox and the Tibetan side a horse as sacrificial victims. Ashamed to ally on those terms, Zhang Yi sought to diminish the rite and requested of Jiezan, "The Han cannot plow without oxen, and Tibet cannot travel without horses. I request that sheep, pigs, and dogs be substituted instead."
entries.literal: At first it was agreed that Han would use an ox and Tibet a horse as sacrificial victims; Yi was ashamed to ally with them and, intending to diminish the rite, therefore requested of Jiezan, saying: 'Han cannot plow without oxen, and Tibet cannot travel without horses—now I request that the three animals sheep, pigs, and dogs be substituted for them.'

entries.zh: 結贊許諾。
entries.en: Jiezan agreed.
entries.literal: Jiezan agreed.

entries.zh: 時塞外無豕，結贊請以羝羊，鎰出犬、白羊，乃坎於壇北刑之，雜血一器而歃，盟文曰：
entries.en: At that time there were no pigs beyond the frontier, so Jiezan requested a ram in place of a pig. Zhang Yi produced a dog and a white sheep. They dug a pit north of the altar and executed the victims there, mixed the blood in one vessel and drank it, and the alliance text read:
entries.literal: At that time there were no pigs beyond the frontier; Jiezan requested a ram in place of a pig, Yi produced a dog and a white sheep, and they then dug a pit north of the altar and executed the victims there, mixed the blood in one vessel and drank it, and the alliance text said:

entries.zh: 德宗將幸奉天，鎰竊知之，將迎鑾駕，具財貨服用獻行在。
entries.en: Emperor Dezong was about to proceed to Fengtian. Zhang Yi learned of it privately and prepared to welcome the imperial carriage, assembling wealth, goods, and clothing to present at the traveling palace.
entries.literal: Emperor Dezong was about to proceed to Fengtian; Yi learned of it privately and prepared to welcome the imperial carriage, assembling wealth, goods, and clothing to present at the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 李楚琳者，嘗事硃泚，得其心。
entries.en: Li Chulin had once served Zhu Ci and won his confidence.
entries.literal: Li Chulin had once served Zhu Ci and won his heart.

entries.zh: 軍司馬齊映等密謀曰：「楚琳不去，必為亂。」
entries.en: Army marshal Qi Ying and others secretly plotted, saying, "If Li Chulin is not removed, he will surely cause disorder."
entries.literal: Army marshal Qi Ying and others secretly plotted, saying: 'If Chulin is not removed, he will surely cause disorder.'

entries.zh: 乃遣楚琳屯於隴州。
entries.en: They then dispatched Li Chulin to garrison at Long prefecture.
entries.literal: They then dispatched Chulin to garrison at Long prefecture.

entries.zh: 楚琳知其謀，乃托故不時發。
entries.en: Li Chulin learned of their plot and, pleading some excuse, did not depart on time.
entries.literal: Chulin knew their plot and, pleading some excuse, did not depart on time.

entries.zh: 鎰始以迎駕心憂惑，以楚琳承命去矣，殊不促其行。
entries.en: Zhang Yi, preoccupied with welcoming the imperial carriage, assumed Li Chulin had accepted the order and departed, and did not press him to go.
entries.literal: Yi, at first preoccupied and troubled in mind over welcoming the imperial carriage, thought Chulin had accepted the order and departed, and did not at all press him to go.

entries.zh: 鎰修飾邊幅，不為軍士所悅。
entries.en: Zhang Yi was fastidious in dress and deportment and was not liked by the soldiers.
entries.literal: Yi was fastidious in dress and deportment and was not liked by the soldiers.

entries.zh: 是夜，楚琳遂與其黨王汾、李卓、牛僧伽等作亂。
entries.en: That night Li Chulin, together with his followers Wang Fen, Li Zhuo, Niu Sengqie, and others, raised a rebellion.
entries.literal: That night Chulin then with his faction Wang Fen, Li Zhuo, Niu Sengqie, and others raised a rebellion.

entries.zh: 鎰夜縋而走，判官齊映自水竇出，齊抗為傭保負荷而逃，皆獲免。
entries.en: Zhang Yi lowered himself by rope and fled by night. Staff judge Qi Ying escaped through a water conduit, and Qi Kang fled disguised as a hired porter carrying loads. All escaped harm.
entries.literal: Yi lowered himself by rope and fled by night; staff judge Qi Ying escaped through a water conduit; Qi Kang fled disguised as a hired porter carrying loads—all escaped harm.

entries.zh: 鎰出鳳翔三十里，及二子皆為候騎所得，楚琳俱殺之；
entries.en: When Zhang Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, he and his two sons were all seized by scouting cavalry, and Li Chulin killed them all;
entries.literal: When Yi had gone thirty li out of Fengxiang, he and his two sons were all seized by scouting cavalry, and Chulin killed them all;

entries.zh: 判官王沼、張元度、柳遇、李漵被殺。
entries.en: Staff judges Wang Zhao, Zhang Yuandu, Liu Yu, and Li Qin were killed.
entries.literal: staff judges Wang Zhao, Zhang Yuandu, Liu Yu, and Li Qin were killed.

entries.zh: 尋贈太子太傅，葬事官給。
entries.en: He was soon posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and funeral arrangements were supplied by the state.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and funeral arrangements were supplied by the state.

entries.zh: 唐有天下，恢奄禹跡，舟車所至，莫不率俾。
entries.en: Tang possesses All Under Heaven, broadly covering the traces of Yu; wherever boat and carriage reach, none fail to submit and serve.
entries.literal: Tang possesses All Under Heaven, broadly covering the traces of Yu; wherever boat and carriage reach, none fail to submit and serve.

entries.zh: 以累聖重光，卜年惟永，恢王者之丕業，被四海以聲教。
entries.en: Through successive sage emperors and renewed glory, the years are divined to be everlasting. The king's great enterprise is restored, and the four seas are covered with civilizing instruction.
entries.literal: Through successive sage emperors and renewed glory, the years are divined to be everlasting; the king's great enterprise is restored, and the four seas are covered with civilizing instruction.

entries.zh: 與吐蕃贊普，代為婚姻，因結鄰好，安危同體，甥舅之國，將二百年。
entries.en: With the Tibetan tsenpo, generation after generation there has been marriage alliance, and neighborly friendship has been formed. Safety and danger have been shared as one body—a nephew-and-uncle state for nearly two hundred years.
entries.literal: With the Tibetan tsenpo, generation after generation there has been marriage alliance; thereby neighborly friendship was formed, safety and danger shared as one body—a nephew-and-uncle state for nearly two hundred years.

entries.zh: 其間或因小忿，棄惠為仇，封疆騷然，靡有寧歲。
entries.en: In the interval, at times small resentments led grace to be cast aside and enmity to be made. The borders were disturbed, and there were no years of peace.
entries.literal: In the interval, at times because of small resentments, grace was cast aside and enmity made; the borders were disturbed and there were no years of peace.

entries.zh: 皇帝踐阼，湣茲黎元，乃釋俘囚悉歸蕃落。
entries.en: The emperor ascended the throne, pitying the common people, and released captives and prisoners, returning them all to Tibetan settlements.
entries.literal: The emperor ascended the throne, pitying these common people, and released captives and prisoners, all returning them to Tibetan settlements.

entries.zh: 二國展禮，同茲協和，行人往復，累布成命。
entries.en: The two states exchanged ritual courtesies and harmonized together. Envoys went back and forth, and repeated edicts were promulgated.
entries.literal: The two states extended ritual courtesies, harmonized together in this, envoys went back and forth, and repeated edicts were promulgated.

entries.zh: 是必詐謀不起，兵革不用矣。
entries.en: By this treacherous plots will surely not arise, and arms and armor will not be used.
entries.literal: By this treacherous plots surely will not arise, and arms and armor will not be used.

entries.zh: 彼猶以兩國之要，求之永久，古有結盟，今請用之。
entries.en: They still seek permanence in the essentials of the two states. Alliance-making existed in antiquity, and I request that it be used now.
entries.literal: They still, regarding the essentials of the two states, seek permanence; anciently there was alliance-making—now I request that it be used.

entries.zh: 國家務息邊人，外其故地，棄利蹈義，堅盟從約。
entries.en: The state is intent on giving peace to the frontier people, ceding its former territory, abandoning profit and treading righteousness, and firmly allying under the agreement.
entries.literal: The state is intent on giving peace to the frontier people, ceding its former territory, abandoning profit and treading righteousness, firmly allying and following the agreement.

entries.zh: 今國家所守界：涇州西至彈箏峽西口，隴州西至清水縣，鳳州西至同谷縣，暨劍南西山、大渡河東，為漢界。
entries.en: The boundaries the state now holds are as follows: from Jing prefecture west to the western mouth of Tansheng Gorge, from Long prefecture west to Qingshui county, from Feng prefecture west to Tonggu county, and including the western mountains of Jiannan and the area east of the Dadu River—this is the Han boundary.
entries.literal: Now the boundaries the state holds: from Jing prefecture west to the western mouth of Tansheng Gorge, from Long prefecture west to Qingshui county, from Feng prefecture west to Tonggu county, and including the western mountains of Jiannan and east of the Dadu River—this is the Han boundary.

entries.zh: 蕃國守鎮在蘭、渭、原、會，西至臨洮，又東至成州，抵劍南西界磨些諸蠻、大渡水西南，為蕃界。
entries.en: Tibet's garrison posts are at Lan, Wei, Yuan, and Hui, west to Lintao, and east again to Cheng prefecture, reaching the western border of Jiannan, the Mosuo tribes, and the area southwest of the Dadu River—this is the Tibetan boundary.
entries.literal: Tibet's garrison posts are at Lan, Wei, Yuan, and Hui, west to Lintao, and east again to Cheng prefecture, reaching the western border of Jiannan, the Mosuo tribes, and southwest of the Dadu River—this is the Tibetan boundary.

entries.zh: 其兵馬鎮守之處州縣見有居人，彼此兩邊見屬漢諸蠻，以今所分見住處依前所有不載者，蕃有兵馬處蕃守，漢有兵馬處漢守，不得侵越。
entries.en: At places where troops and horses are stationed, in prefectures and counties where inhabitants presently dwell, and among the various tribes on both sides presently subject to Han—as to present divisions of residence according to prior holdings not recorded—where Tibet has troops and horses, Tibet shall guard; where Han has troops and horses, Han shall guard. Neither side may encroach or overstep.
entries.literal: At places where troops and horses are stationed and garrisoned, in prefectures and counties where inhabitants presently dwell, and among the various tribes on both sides presently subject to Han—as to present divisions of residence according to prior holdings not recorded—where Tibet has troops and horses, Tibet shall guard; where Han has troops and horses, Han shall guard; neither may encroach or overstep.

entries.zh: 其先未有兵馬處，不得雜置並築城堡耕種。
entries.en: At places where previously there were no troops and horses, none may be mixed in, nor may fortresses be built or fields cultivated.
entries.literal: At places where previously there were no troops and horses, none may be mixed in, nor may fortresses and castles be built or fields cultivated.

entries.zh: 今二國將相受辭而會，齋戒將事，告天地山川之神，惟神昭臨，無得衍墜。
entries.en: Now the generals and ministers of the two states, having received the words, meet. Having fasted and purified themselves, they shall perform the rite, announcing to the spirits of Heaven, Earth, mountains, and rivers. May the spirits brightly oversee, and may none be neglected or abandoned.
entries.literal: Now the generals and ministers of the two states, having received the words, meet; having fasted and purified themselves they shall perform the rite, announcing to the spirits of Heaven, Earth, mountains, and rivers—may the spirits brightly oversee and may none be neglected or abandoned.

entries.zh: 其盟文藏於郊廟，副在有司，二國之誠，其永保之。
entries.en: The alliance text shall be stored in the suburban and ancestral temples, with a copy held by the relevant offices. May the sincerity of the two states be forever preserved.
entries.literal: The alliance text shall be stored in the suburban and ancestral temples, with a copy held by the relevant offices; the sincerity of the two states—may it be forever preserved.

entries.zh: 結贊亦出盟文，不加於坎，但埋牲而已。
entries.en: Jiezan also produced an alliance text. He did not add it to the pit but merely buried the sacrificial victims.
entries.literal: Jiezan also produced an alliance text, not adding it to the pit but merely burying the victims.

entries.zh: 盟畢，結贊請鎰就壇之西南隅佛幄中焚香為誓，誓畢，復升壇飲酒。
entries.en: When the alliance was complete, Jiezan requested that Zhang Yi go to the Buddha pavilion at the southwest corner of the altar and burn incense to swear. When the oath was complete, they again ascended the altar and drank wine.
entries.literal: When the alliance was complete, Jiezan requested that Yi go to the Buddha pavilion at the southwest corner of the altar and burn incense to swear; when the oath was complete, they again ascended the altar and drank wine.

entries.zh: 獻酬之禮，各用其物，以將厚意而歸。
entries.en: In the rites of offering and return, each side used its own gifts, thereby conveying generous intent before departing.
entries.literal: In the rites of offering and return, each used his own gifts, thereby conveying generous intent before departing.

entries.zh: 先時，淮南節度陳少遊首稱臣於李希烈，鳳翔將李楚琳殺節度使張鎰以應硃泚，鎰判官韋臯先知隴州留後，首殺豳叛卒數百人，不應楚琳。
entries.en: Earlier, Huainan military governor Chen Shaoyou was the first to declare himself subject to Li Xilie. Fengxiang general Li Chulin killed military governor Zhang Yi to join Zhu Ci. Zhang Yi's staff judge Wei Gao, who had earlier served as acting rear commander of Long prefecture, was the first to kill several hundred mutinous soldiers from Bin and refused to follow Chulin.
entries.literal: Earlier, Huainan military governor Chen Shaoyou was the first to declare himself subject to Li Xilie; Fengxiang general Li Chulin killed military governor Zhang Yi to respond to Zhu Ci; Yi's staff judge Wei Gao, who had earlier been acting rear commander of Long prefecture, was the first to kill several hundred mutinous soldiers from Bin and did not respond to Chulin.

entries.zh: 復江南使回，與宰相同對訖，復獨留，奏曰：「陛下自返宮闕，勛臣已蒙官爵，唯旌善懲惡，未有區分。
entries.en: When Fu returned from his Jiangnan mission, after answering together with the chief ministers he alone remained and memorialized, saying, "Since Your Majesty returned to the palace, meritorious ministers have already received ranks and titles, yet in honoring good and punishing evil there has been no distinction.
entries.literal: When Fu returned from his Jiangnan mission, after answering together with the chief ministers he alone remained and memorialized, saying: 'Since Your Majesty returned to the palace, meritorious ministers have already received ranks and titles, yet in honoring good and punishing evil there has been no distinction.

entries.zh: 陳少遊將相之寄最崇，首敗臣節；
entries.en: Chen Shaoyou held the highest trust of general and minister and was the first to destroy loyal integrity;
entries.literal: Chen Shaoyou held the highest trust of general and minister and was the first to destroy loyal integrity;

entries.zh: 韋臯名宦最卑，特建忠義。
entries.en: Wei Gao's official rank was the most humble, yet he specially established loyalty and righteousness.
entries.literal: Wei Gao's official name and rank were the most humble, yet he specially established loyalty and righteousness.

entries.zh: 請令韋臯代少遊，則天下明然知逆順之理。」
entries.en: I request that Wei Gao be ordered to replace Chen Shaoyou, so that All Under Heaven will clearly understand the principle of rebellion and submission."
entries.literal: I request that Wei Gao be ordered to replace Shaoyou, and then All Under Heaven will clearly know the principle of rebellion and submission.'

entries.zh: 上許之。
entries.en: The emperor approved.
entries.literal: The emperor approved.

entries.zh: 復出，宰相李勉、盧翰、劉從一方同歸中書，中使馬欽緒至，揖從一，附耳語而退，諸相各歸閣。
entries.en: Fu went out. Chief ministers Li Mian, Lu Han, and Liu Congyi together returned to the Secretariat. Palace envoy Ma Qinxu arrived, bowed to Liu Congyi, whispered in his ear, and withdrew. The ministers each returned to their offices.
entries.literal: Fu went out; chief ministers Li Mian, Lu Han, and Liu Congyi together returned to the Secretariat; palace envoy Ma Qinxu arrived, bowed to Congyi, whispered in his ear, and withdrew; the ministers each returned to their offices.

entries.zh: 從一詣復曰：「適欽緒宣旨，令與公商量朝來所奏便進，勿令李勉、盧翰知。」
entries.en: Liu Congyi went to Fu and said, "Just now Qinxu announced the imperial intent, ordering me to consult with you and immediately advance this morning's memorial. Do not let Li Mian and Lu Han know."
entries.literal: Congyi went to Fu and said: 'Just now Qinxu announced the imperial intent, ordering me to consult with you and immediately advance this morning's memorial; do not let Li Mian and Lu Han know.'

entries.zh: 復曰：「適來奏對，亦聞斯旨，然未諭聖心，已面陳述，上意尚爾，復未敢言其事。」
entries.en: Fu said, "In the audience just now I also heard this intent, but I had not yet understood the emperor's mind. I already stated it face to face, and the emperor's intent is still unchanged, so I did not dare speak of the matter."
entries.literal: Fu said: 'In the audience just now I also heard this intent, but I had not yet understood the sage mind; I already stated it face to face, and the emperor's intent is still thus—I did not dare speak of the matter.'

entries.zh: 復又曰：「唐、虞有僉曰之論，朝廷有事，尚合與公卿同議。
entries.en: Fu also said, "Tang and Yu had the doctrine of collective assent. When the court has business, it ought still to be jointly deliberated with the high ministers.
entries.literal: Fu also said: 'Tang and Yu had the doctrine of collective assent; when the court has business, it ought still to be jointly deliberated with the high ministers.

entries.zh: 今勉、翰不可在相位，即去之；
entries.en: If Li Mian and Lu Han ought not be in chief minister posts, then remove them;
entries.literal: If Mian and Han ought not be in chief minister posts, then remove them;

entries.zh: 既在相位，合同商量，何故獨避此之一節？
entries.en: since they are in chief minister posts, they ought to deliberate together. Why alone avoid this one matter?
entries.literal: since they are in chief minister posts, they ought to deliberate together—why alone avoid this one matter?

entries.zh: 且與公行之無爽，但恐浸以成俗，此政之大弊也。」
entries.en: Moreover, to carry it out with you would be without error, but I fear it will gradually become custom. This is a great defect in government."
entries.literal: Moreover, to carry it out with you would be without error, but I fear it will gradually become custom—this is a great defect in government.'

entries.zh: 竟不言於從一。
entries.en: In the end he did not speak of it to Liu Congyi.
entries.literal: In the end he did not speak of it to Congyi.

entries.zh: 從一奏之，上浸不悅。
entries.en: Liu Congyi reported it, and the emperor gradually became displeased.
entries.literal: Congyi reported it, and the emperor gradually became displeased.

entries.zh: 復累表辭疾，請罷知政事，從之，守太子左庶子。
entries.en: Fu repeatedly memorialized citing illness and requested to be relieved of participation in government. The request was granted, and he remained as left assistant to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Fu repeatedly memorialized citing illness, requesting to be relieved of participation in government; the request was granted, and he remained as left assistant to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 三年，坐郜國公主親累，檢校左庶子，於饒州安置。
entries.en: In the third year, because of kinship entanglement with Princess Guo, he was made provisional left assistant to the Heir Apparent and settled at Raozhou.
entries.literal: In the third year, because of kinship entanglement with Princess Guo, he was made provisional left assistant to the Heir Apparent and settled at Raozhou.

entries.zh: 四年，終於饒州，時年五十七。
entries.en: In the fourth year he died at Raozhou at the age of fifty-seven.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he died at Raozhou at age fifty-seven.

entries.zh: 渾母兄識，，篤意文章，有重名於開元、天寶間，與蕭穎士、元德秀、劉迅相亞。
entries.en: Hun's elder maternal brother Shi was devoted to literature and had a great reputation during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, ranking alongside Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun.
entries.literal: Hun's elder maternal brother Shi was devoted to literature and had a great reputation during Kaiyuan and Tianbao, ranking alongside Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun.

entries.zh: 其練理創端往往詣極，當時作者，鹹伏其簡拔，而趣尚辨博。
entries.en: In refining principles and opening beginnings he often reached the utmost. Writers of the time all submitted to his concise elevation, yet his bent favored disputation and breadth.
entries.literal: In refining principles and opening beginnings he often reached the utmost; writers of the time all submitted to his concise elevation, yet his bent favored disputation and breadth.

entries.zh: 渾亦善為文，然趨時向功，非沈思之所及。
entries.en: Hun also wrote well, yet he bent to the times and sought achievement—not what deep reflection could reach.
entries.literal: Hun also wrote well, yet he bent to the times and sought achievement—not what deep reflection could reach.

entries.zh: 渾警辯，好諧謔放達，與人交，豁然無隱。
entries.en: Hun was alert in debate and fond of jest and free openness. In dealing with people he was expansive and hid nothing.
entries.literal: Hun was alert in debate, fond of jest and free openness; in dealing with people he was expansive and hid nothing.

entries.zh: 性節儉，不治產業，官至丞相，假宅而居。
entries.en: By nature he was frugal and did not manage estates. Though he reached chief minister, he borrowed a residence to live in.
entries.literal: By nature he was frugal and did not manage estates; though he reached chief minister, he borrowed a residence to live in.

entries.zh: 罷相數日，則命親族尋勝，宴醉方歸，陶陶然忘其黜免。
entries.en: Within days of leaving the chief ministry he would order kin to seek scenic spots, feast until drunk before returning, and forget his dismissal in contentment.
entries.literal: Within days of leaving the chief ministry he would order kin to seek scenic spots, feast until drunk before returning, and forget his dismissal in contentment.

entries.zh: 時李勉、盧翰皆退罷居第，相謂曰：「吾輩方柳宜城，悉為拘俗之人也。」
entries.en: At that time Li Mian and Lu Han had both retired and lived at their residences. They said to each other, "Compared with Liu of Yicheng, we are all people bound by convention."
entries.literal: At that time Li Mian and Lu Han had both retired and lived at their residences; they said to each other: 'Compared with Liu of Yicheng, we are all people bound by convention.'

entries.zh: 史臣曰：張鎰、蕭復、柳渾，節行才能訏謨亮直，皆足相明主，平泰階，而盧杞忌之於前，延賞排之於後，管仲有言：「任君子，使小人間之，害霸也。」
entries.en: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun—in integrity, conduct, talent, and outspoken, bright uprightness—all were sufficient to assist an enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway. Yet Lu Qi envied them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said, "Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between—this harms hegemony."
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun—in integrity, conduct, talent, and outspoken, bright uprightness—all were sufficient to assist an enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway; yet Lu Qi envied them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said: 'Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between—this harms hegemony.'

entries.zh: 德宗黜賢相，位奸臣，致硃泚、懷光之亂，是失其人也，豈尤其時哉！
entries.en: Emperor Dezong dismissed worthy chief ministers and placed treacherous ministers in rank, bringing about the disorders of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang. This was losing the right men. How can one blame the times alone!
entries.literal: Emperor Dezong dismissed worthy chief ministers and placed treacherous ministers in rank, bringing about the disorders of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang—this was losing the right men; how can one blame the times alone!

entries.zh: 河清歿於王事，乃顯忠貞；
entries.en: Heqing died in royal service and thereby displayed loyalty and steadfastness;
entries.literal: Heqing died in royal service and thereby displayed loyalty and steadfastness;

entries.zh: 從一舉自奸人，固宜循默。
entries.en: Liu Congyi was raised by treacherous men and properly ought to have kept silent.
entries.literal: Congyi was raised by treacherous men and properly ought to have followed silence.

entries.zh: 贊曰：得人則興，失人則亡。
entries.en: The encomium says: Gain the right men and flourish; lose them and perish.
entries.literal: The encomium says: Gain the right men and flourish; lose them and perish.

entries.zh: 鎰、復、渾去，宗社其殃。
entries.en: When Yi, Fu, and Hun departed, the altars of state met calamity.
entries.literal: When Yi, Fu, and Hun departed, the altars of state met calamity.

entries.zh: 盧鸑，幽州范陽人也，貞觀中工部侍郎義恭玄孫也。
entries.en: Lu Yue was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou and the great-great-grandson of Yigong, vice minister of works under Emperor Taizong.
entries.literal: Lu Yue was a man of Fanyang in Youzhou, the great-great-grandson of Yigong, vice minister of works in the Zhenguan era.

entries.zh: 父子騫，潁王府諮議參軍，以鸑贈秘書少監。
entries.en: His father Ziqian had been advisory staff officer in the Prince of Ying's household and was posthumously honored as vice director of the Secretariat through Yue's promotions.
entries.literal: His father Ziqian was advisory staff officer of the Prince of Ying's establishment; through Yue he was posthumously honored as vice director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 鸑少以門廕入仕，在職以幹局稱。
entries.en: Yue entered office young through hereditary privilege and was known in service for practical competence.
entries.literal: Yue in youth entered office by yin privilege and in service was known for practical ability.

entries.zh: 累授閬州錄事參軍、監察殿中御史、侍御史、金州刺史。
entries.en: He rose through posts as recorder of Langzhou, investigating and palace censor, attendant censor, and prefect of Jinzhou.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly appointed recorder of Langzhou, investigating censor and palace censor, attendant censor, and prefect of Jinzhou.

entries.zh: 宰相楊炎遇之頗厚，召入左司郎中、京兆少尹，遷大尹。
entries.en: Chief Minister Yang Yan favored him, recalled him as director in the Left Secretariat and junior metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, then promoted him to metropolitan governor.
entries.literal: Chief Minister Yang Yan treated him quite generously, summoned him in as director in the Left Secretariat and junior metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, then promoted him to metropolitan governor.

entries.zh: 鸑無術學，善事權要，為政苛躁。
entries.en: Yue had no scholarly training, cultivated the powerful, and governed with harsh impatience.
entries.literal: Yue had no learning in the arts, was good at serving the powerful, and in governing was harsh and impatient.

entries.zh: 盧杞甚惡之，諷有司彈奏，坐貶撫州司馬同正，改饒州刺史，遷福州刺史、福建觀察使。
entries.en: Lu Qi detested him, had him impeached, and demoted him to secretary of Fuzhou. He was later made prefect of Raozhou, then of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.
entries.literal: Lu Qi greatly hated him, prompted the relevant offices to impeach him, and he was demoted to secretary of Fuzhou with the same nominal rank, then changed to prefect of Raozhou, and transferred to prefect of Fuzhou and observation commissioner of Fujian.

entries.zh: 貞元二年七月，以疾終。
entries.en: He died of illness in the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyuan.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyuan he died of illness.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：李揆發言沃心，幸遇明主；
entries.en: The historiographer writes: Li Kui's counsel enriched the emperor's mind, and he was fortunate to serve an enlightened ruler;
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Li Kui's words enriched the imperial heart, and he was fortunate to meet an enlightened ruler;

entries.zh: 蔽賢固位，終非令人。
entries.en: yet in blocking the worthy to hold his post he proved in the end no admirable man.
entries.literal: yet in screening the worthy and holding fast to office he was in the end not a man to be approved.

entries.zh: 少遊逐勢利隨時，盧惎事權要巧宦，察言觀行，皆無可稱。
entries.en: Shaoyou chased profit with the times; Lu Yue curried favor with the powerful through crafty office-seeking. Judging their words and conduct, none deserves praise.
entries.literal: Shaoyou chased profit and power as times changed; Lu Yue served the powerful in crafty office-seeking—examining their words and observing their conduct, none is praiseworthy.

entries.zh: 涵節行著聞，谞和易為理，庶幾近仁也。
entries.en: Han was renowned for restraint and integrity; Xu governed with mild ease. Both nearly approached true benevolence.
entries.literal: Han was renowned for his restraint and conduct; Xu governed with mild ease—they nearly approached benevolence.

entries.zh: 贊曰李、陳、盧鸑，言行非真。
entries.en: The encomium reads: Li, Chen, and Lu Yue—their words and conduct were not genuine.
entries.literal: The encomium says: Li, Chen, and Lu Yue—their words and conduct were not true.

entries.zh: 涵、谞和易，庶乎近仁。
entries.en: Han and Xu were mild in manner—they nearly approached true benevolence.
entries.literal: Han and Xu were mild and easy—they nearly approached benevolence.

entries.zh: 李揆字端卿，隴西成紀人，而家於鄭州，代為冠族。
entries.en: Li Kui, whose courtesy name was Duanqing, came from Chengji in Longxi, though his family had long lived in Zhengzhou and ranked among the foremost lineages of the age.
entries.literal: Li Kui, courtesy name Duanqing, was a native of Chengji in Longxi, but his family had settled in Zhengzhou, and for generations they were a leading clan.

entries.zh: 秦府學士、給事中玄道玄孫，秘書監、贈吏部尚書成裕之子。
entries.en: He was descended from Xuantao, who had served as an academician in the Prince of Qin's household and as a supervising censor, and was the son of Chengyu, director of the Secretariat, who after death was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was the great-great-grandson of Xuantao, academician of the Prince of Qin's establishment and supervising censor, and the son of Chengyu, director of the Secretariat, posthumously honored as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 少聰敏好學，善屬文。
entries.en: As a youth he was quick-witted and devoted to learning, and showed a gift for writing.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever and fond of study, and skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 開元末，舉進士，補陳留尉，獻書闕下，詔中書試文章，擢拜右拾遺。
entries.en: Near the close of the Kaiyuan reign he took the jinshi degree, served as assistant magistrate of Chenliu, and submitted a work to the court. The emperor ordered the Secretariat to examine his prose, after which he was elevated to Right Reminder.
entries.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Chenliu, presented a book at the palace gates, and by imperial order the Secretariat tested his writings; he was then promoted and appointed Right Reminder.

entries.zh: 改右補闕、起居郎，知宗子表疏。
entries.en: He was next made Right Supplementation Censor and Imperial Diarist, with responsibility for memorials from members of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and Imperial Diarist, and was charged with imperial-clan memorials and reports.

entries.zh: 遷司勛員外郎、考功郎中，並知制誥。
entries.en: He rose to vice director in the Bureau of Merits and director in the Bureau of Evaluations, holding in each office the duty of drafting imperial edicts.
entries.literal: He was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Merits and to director in the Bureau of Evaluations, and in both posts he drafted imperial edicts.

entries.zh: 扈從劍南，拜中書舍人。
entries.en: Accompanying the court into Jiannan, he was appointed drafting secretary of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When he followed the emperor to Jiannan, he was appointed Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 臯生知音律，嘗觀彈琴，至《止息》，嘆曰：「妙哉！
entries.en: Gao had an innate understanding of pitch and musical law. Once, watching someone play the zither, when the player reached "Stopping and Resting," he sighed, "Marvelous!
entries.literal: Gao from birth understood pitch and law; once watching someone play the zither, when they reached "Stopping and Resting," he sighed: "Wonderful!

entries.zh: 嵇生之為是曲也，其當晉、魏之際乎！
entries.en: When Master Ji composed this piece, must it not have been at the turning point between Jin and Wei!
entries.literal: When Master Ji composed this piece, must it not have been at the juncture of Jin and Wei!

entries.zh: 其音主商，商為秋聲。
entries.en: Its tone is dominated by the shang mode, and shang is the sound of autumn.
entries.literal: Its tone is dominated by shang; shang is the sound of autumn.

entries.zh: 秋也者，天將搖落肅殺，其歲之晏乎！
entries.en: Autumn is when heaven shakes the leaves down in bleak severity—is it not the year's decline!
entries.literal: Autumn—heaven about to shake down, wither, and kill in severity—is it not the year's decline!

entries.zh: 又晉乘金運，商，金聲，此所以知魏之季而晉將代也。
entries.en: Jin, moreover, rode the fortune of metal, and shang is the sound of metal—by this one knows that Wei was in its last days and Jin was about to replace it.
entries.literal: Also Jin rode the fortune of metal; shang is the sound of metal—by this one knows the end of Wei and Jin about to replace it.

entries.zh: 慢其商弦，與宮同音，是臣奪君之義也，所以知司馬氏之將篡也。
entries.en: Loosen the shang strings until they match the palace tone, and that is the image of a subject seizing his lord—by this one knows the Sima clan was about to usurp the throne.
entries.literal: If one loosens its shang strings to match palace in tone, that is the meaning of subject seizing lord—by this one knows the Sima clan was about to usurp.

entries.zh: 司馬懿受魏明帝顧托後嗣，反有篡奪之心，自誅曹爽，逆節彌露。
entries.en: Sima Yi had received Wei Emperor Ming's deathbed charge to protect the successor, yet harbored thoughts of usurpation; from the killing of Cao Shuang onward, his treasonous intent showed ever more plainly.
entries.literal: Sima Yi received Wei Emperor Ming's deathbed charge for the successor, yet harbored usurpation in mind; from killing Cao Shuang, his rebellious intent showed ever more.

entries.zh: 王陵都督揚州，謀立荊王彪；
entries.en: Wang Ling, governor of Yang province, plotted to install Prince Jing Biao;
entries.literal: Wang Ling as governor of Yang province plotted to install Prince Jing Biao;
