entries.zh: 毋丘儉、文欽、諸葛誕前後相繼為揚州都督，咸有匡復魏室之謀，皆為懿父子所殺。
entries.en: Wuqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan served in succession as governors of Yang province, each with plans to restore the house of Wei, and each was killed by Yi and his sons.
entries.literal: Wuqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan in succession governed Yang—each had plans to restore the Wei house—all were killed by Yi and his sons.

entries.zh: 叔夜以揚州故廣陵之地，彼四人者，皆魏室文武大臣，咸敗散於廣陵，《散》言魏氏散亡，自廣陵始也。
entries.en: Jiye took Yangzhou's old territory of Guangling—those four men were all great civil and military ministers of Wei, all defeated and scattered at Guangling; "Scatter" means the dispersal and ruin of Wei, beginning at Guangling.
entries.literal: Jiye took Yangzhou's former Guangling territory—those four men were all Wei civil and military great ministers, all defeated and scattered at Guangling; "Scatter" speaks of Wei's dispersal and ruin, beginning from Guangling.

entries.zh: 《止息》者，晉雖暴興，終止息於此也。
entries.en: "Stopping and Resting" means that though Jin rose violently, it would in the end come to rest here.
entries.literal: "Stopping and Resting"—though Jin rose violently, it would in the end stop and rest here.

entries.zh: 其哀憤躁蹙，憯痛迫脅之旨，盡在於是矣。
entries.en: Its grief, rage, agitation, compression, bitter pain, and sense of forced constraint—all of that intent is contained in this piece.
entries.literal: Its grief, rage, agitation, compression, bitter pain, and forced constraint—all intent is in this.

entries.zh: 永嘉之亂，其應乎！
entries.en: The Yongjia disaster—is this its fulfillment!
entries.literal: The Yongjia disorder—is this its response!

entries.zh: 叔夜撰此，將貽後代之知音者，且避晉、魏之禍，所以托之神鬼也。」
entries.en: Jiye composed this to bequeath it to later generations who would understand, and also to avoid the disasters of Jin and Wei—therefore he entrusted it to spirits and ghosts."
entries.literal: Jiye composed this to bequeath to later generations who understand tone, and also to avoid Jin-Wei disaster—therefore he entrusted it to spirits and ghosts."

entries.zh: 韓滉，字太沖，太子少師休之子也。
entries.en: Han Huang, courtesy name Taichong, was the son of Xiu, who had served as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Han Huang, styled Taichong, was a son of Xiu, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 少貞介好學，以廕解褐左威衛騎曹參軍，出為同官主簿。
entries.en: As a young man he was upright and studious; through hereditary privilege he began his career as cavalry adjutant in the Left Weiming Guard and was later posted as registrar at Tongguan.
entries.literal: In youth he was upright and fond of learning; through yin privilege he entered service as Cavalry Army Adjutant of the Left Weiming Guard, and went out as registrar at Tongguan.

entries.zh: 至德初，青齊節度鄧景山辟為判官，授監察御史、兼北海郡司馬，以道路阻絕，因避地山南。
entries.en: Early in the Zhide era, Deng Jingshan, military governor of Qing and Qi, took him on as aide; he received appointment as investigative censor and concurrent militia marshal of Beihai commandery; when travel routes were cut off, he withdrew to the Shannan region.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era, Deng Jingshan, commissioner of Qing-Qi, recruited him as aide; he was appointed Investigative Censor and concurrently Militia Marshal of Beihai; because roads were blocked, he took refuge in Shannan.

entries.zh: 采訪使李承昭奏充判官，授通州長史、彭王府諮議參軍。
entries.en: The investigation commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized that he serve as aide; he was granted the posts of tongzhou administrator and staff adviser in the Prince of Peng's establishment.
entries.literal: Investigation Commissioner Li Chengzhao memorialized appointing him aide; he was appointed Administrator of Tongzhou and Staff Adviser of the Prince of Peng's household.

entries.zh: 鄧景山移鎮淮南，又表為賓佐，未行，除殿中侍御史，追赴京師。
entries.en: When Deng Jingshan moved his headquarters to Huainan, he again nominated Huang as a staff aide; before Huang could take up the post, he was appointed palace attendant censor and ordered to the capital.
entries.literal: When Deng Jingshan transferred his command to Huainan, he again memorialized for him as staff aide; before he could go, he was appointed Palace Attendant Censor and summoned to the capital.

entries.zh: 先是，滉兄法知制誥，草王玙拜官之詞，不加虛美，玙頗銜之。
entries.en: Earlier, Huang's elder brother Fa had been responsible for drafting edicts; when he composed the text appointing Wang Yu, he had not padded it with empty praise, and Yu took strong offense.
entries.literal: Earlier, Huang's elder brother Fa had charge of edict drafting; when drafting Wang Yu's appointment text, he did not add empty flattery, and Yu deeply resented it.

entries.zh: 及其秉政，諸使奏滉兄弟者，必以冗官授之。
entries.en: Once Yu was in power, whenever memorials came in concerning the Huang brothers, he always assigned them to nominal posts.
entries.literal: When Yu held power, whenever envoys memorialized about the Huang brothers, he always gave them idle appointments.

entries.zh: 玙免相，群議稱其屈，累遷至祠部、孝功、吏部三員外郎。
entries.en: After Yu was removed from the chancellorship, opinion held that they had been treated unjustly; Huang rose in succession through external vacancies in the ministries of rites, filial achievement, and personnel.
entries.literal: When Yu left the chancellorship, public comment held that they had been wronged; Huang was successively promoted to external vacancy in the Rites, Filial Achievement, and Personnel ministries.

entries.zh: 建中初，張鎰為河中少尹。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Jianzhong reign, Zhang Yi served as Vice Governor of Hezhong.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Zhang Yi was Vice Governor of Hezhong.

entries.zh: 鎰尋入相，二年七月，遷播給事中。
entries.en: Zhang Yi soon entered the chancellorship. In the seventh month of Jianzhong 2, Guan Bo was promoted to Supervising Secretary.
entries.literal: Yi soon entered the chancellorship; in the seventh month of the second year, Bo was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

entries.zh: 舊例，諸司甲庫，皆是胥吏掌知，為弊頗久，播始建議並以士人知之，至今稱當。
entries.en: By longstanding custom, the personnel archives of the various ministries had been managed by low-level clerks—a source of chronic abuse. Guan Bo was the first to propose placing educated officials in charge of them, a reform still praised as apt.
entries.literal: By old precedent, the archives of the various offices were all managed by clerks and runners—a abuse long standing; Bo first proposed that gentlemen-scholars manage them jointly, and to this day it is called appropriate.

entries.zh: 轉刑部侍郎、奉迎皇太后副使。
entries.en: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Commissioner for Welcoming the Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Commissioner for Welcoming the Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 盧杞以播柔緩，冀其易制，驟稱薦之。
entries.en: Lu Qi, judging Guan Bo gentle and pliable, hoped to control him easily and suddenly began praising and recommending him.
entries.literal: Lu Qi, because Bo was gentle and mild, hoped he would be easy to control and abruptly praised and recommended him.

entries.zh: 尋遷吏部侍郎，轉刑部尚書、知刪定。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Minister of Justice with charge over statutory revision.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Minister of Justice and placed in charge of statutory revision.

entries.zh: 奏上元中，詔擇古今名將十人於武成王廟配享，如文宣王廟之儀。
entries.en: He reported that during the Shangyuan reign an edict had selected ten famous generals from history for companion worship in the Temple of the Martial Accomplishment King, patterned after the rites of Confucius's temple.
entries.literal: He memorialized that in the Shangyuan era an edict had chosen ten famous generals from ancient and modern times for companion worship at the Temple of the Martial Accomplishment King, following the ritual of the Temple of the Literary Sage King.

entries.zh: 播以「太公古稱大賢，今其下稱亞聖，於義不安。
entries.en: Guan Bo argued, "The Grand Duke was called a great sage in antiquity; to designate those beneath him as 'lesser sages' is improper in principle.
entries.literal: Bo argued: "The Grand Duke was anciently called a great sage; now beneath him they are called sub-sages—in propriety this is unsettling.

entries.zh: 又孔子十哲，皆是當時弟子，今所擇名將，年代不同，於義既乖，於事又失。
entries.en: Moreover, Confucius's Ten Worthies were all disciples of his own day. The generals now chosen belong to different ages. This violates principle and misses the point in practice as well.
entries.literal: Moreover Confucius's Ten Worthies were all disciples of his own time; the famous generals now chosen belong to different ages—in principle this already conflicts, and in practice it is also wrong.

entries.zh: 臣請刪去名將配享之儀及十哲之稱。」
entries.en: I therefore request that the rite of companion worship for famous generals and the designation 'Ten Worthies' be abolished."
entries.literal: Your subject requests deletion of the rite of companion worship for famous generals and the title of Ten Worthies.

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was granted.
entries.literal: This was approved.

entries.zh: 王璵 道士李國禎附
entries.en: Wang Yu — with an appended account of the Daoist Li Guozhen
entries.literal: Wang Yu; appended: the Daoist Li Guozhen

entries.zh: 其載，補剡縣尉，改會稽尉。
entries.en: He was then appointed supplemental magistrate of Shan County and transferred to magistrate of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was appointed supplemental magistrate of Shan County and transferred to magistrate of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 宣州觀察使殷日用奏為判官，宣慰使李季卿又以表薦，連授大理評事、兼監察御史。
entries.en: Yin Riyong, commissioner observing Xuanzhou, memorialized to make him judge; pacification commissioner Li Jiqing also recommended him, and he was successively made evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent investigating censor.
entries.literal: Yin Riyong, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou, memorialized to appoint him judge; the pacification commissioner Li Jiqing also recommended him by memorial, and he was successively made Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent Investigating Censor.

entries.zh: 轉運使劉晏奏令巡覆江西，多所蠲免。
entries.en: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan had him tour and review Jiangxi, and many tax remissions were granted.
entries.literal: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan memorialized to have him tour and review Jiangxi, and many remissions were granted.

entries.zh: 改殿中侍御史、檢校倉部員外、民部郎中，並充浙西留後。
entries.en: He became Palace Attendant Censor, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He was changed to Palace Diarist, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, all while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 佐晏征賦，頗有裨益，晏甚任之。
entries.en: Assisting Yan in tax collection, he proved of considerable benefit, and Yan relied on him greatly.
entries.literal: Assisting Yan in collecting taxes, he was of considerable benefit, and Yan greatly relied on him.

entries.zh: 姚南仲，華州下邽人。
entries.en: Yao Nanzhong came from Xiaji in Hua Prefecture.
entries.literal: Yao Nanzhong was a native of Xiaji in Hua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 乾元初，制科登第，授太子校書，歷高陵、昭應、萬年三縣尉。
entries.en: In the early Qianyuan period he passed the special examination, was made collator to the Crown Prince, and served in turn as county defender (wei) of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian counties.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, he passed the special examination and was appointed Crown Prince's collator; he served successively as county defender of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.

entries.zh: 遷右拾遺，轉右補闕。
entries.en: He rose to Right Reminder and then became Right Rectifier of Omissions.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Right Reminder and then transferred to Right Rectifier of Omissions.

entries.zh: 大歷十三年，貞懿皇后獨孤氏崩，代宗悼惜不已，令於近城為陵墓，冀朝夕臨望於目前。
entries.en: In Dali 13 the Virtuous and Gracious Empress, née Dugu, died. Emperor Daizong grieved deeply and ordered a mausoleum built close to the capital so he could look upon it at every hour of the day.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of the Dali era, the Virtuous and Gracious Empress of the Dugu clan died; Emperor Daizong mourned her without cease and ordered a tomb built near the city, hoping to gaze upon it morning and evening before his eyes.

entries.zh: 南仲上疏諫曰：伏聞貞懿皇后今於城東章敬寺北以起陵廟，臣不知有司之請乎，陛下之意乎，陰陽家流希旨乎？
entries.en: Nanzhong submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "I have heard that a mausoleum and temple for the Virtuous and Gracious Empress are now being raised north of Zhangjing Temple, east of the city. I do not know whether this was requested by the responsible offices, reflects Your Majesty's own intent, or flatters geomancers seeking to please?"
entries.literal: Nanzhong submitted a memorial remonstrating: I have heard that a mausoleum and temple for the Virtuous and Gracious Empress are now being raised north of Zhangjing Temple east of the city. I do not know whether this was the request of the responsible offices, Your Majesty's own intent, or the flattery of geomancers seeking to please?

entries.zh: 臣愚以為非所宜也。
entries.en: In my humble opinion this is not fitting.
entries.literal: Your subject in his foolishness considers this not fitting.

entries.zh: 謹具疏陳論，伏願暫留天睠而省察焉。
entries.en: I respectfully submit these arguments and beg Your Majesty to pause and reflect.
entries.literal: I respectfully set forth this memorial in full argument and prostrate myself in hope that Your Majesty will briefly withhold heavenly regard and reflect upon it.

entries.zh: 臣聞人臣宅於家，君上宅於國。
entries.en: I have heard that ministers dwell in their homes and rulers dwell in the state.
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that ministers dwell in their homes and rulers dwell in the state.

entries.zh: 長安城，是陛下皇居也，其可穿鑿興動，建陵墓於其側乎？
entries.en: Chang'an is Your Majesty's imperial residence. How can one excavate and build a mausoleum beside it?
entries.literal: Chang'an is Your Majesty's imperial residence—how can one excavate and stir construction, building a mausoleum at its side?

entries.zh: 此非宜一也。
entries.en: This is the first impropriety.
entries.literal: This is the first point of impropriety.

entries.zh: 夫葬者藏也，欲人之不得見也。
entries.en: Burial means concealment; one wishes that the dead not be seen.
entries.literal: Burial means concealment; one wishes that people not see.

entries.zh: 是以古帝前王葬后妃，莫不憑丘原，遠郊郭。
entries.en: Therefore when ancient emperors and former kings buried their consorts, they all chose hills and plains far from the suburbs.
entries.literal: Therefore ancient emperors and former kings burying their consorts all relied on hills and plains, far from suburbs and walls.

entries.zh: 今則西臨宮闕，南迫康莊，若使近而可見，死而復生，雖在西宮待之可也。
entries.en: Now it faces the palace on the west and presses Kangzhuang on the south. If nearness and visibility meant she could die and live again, even waiting for her in the Western Palace would be acceptable.
entries.literal: Now it faces the palace gates on the west and presses Kangzhuang on the south. If being near and visible meant she could die and live again, even waiting for her in the Western Palace would be acceptable.

entries.zh: 如骨肉歸土，魂無不之，章敬之北，竟何所益？
entries.en: But if flesh and bones return to earth and the soul goes everywhere, what benefit is there in building north of Zhangjing?
entries.literal: But if flesh and bones return to earth and the soul roams everywhere, what use is there north of Zhangjing?

entries.zh: 視之兆庶，則彰溺愛；
entries.en: Seen by the common people, it exposes excessive doting;
entries.literal: Seen by the common people, it exposes excessive doting;

entries.zh: 垂之萬代，則累明德，此非所宜二也。
entries.en: passed down through ten thousand generations, it will burden bright virtue—this is the second impropriety.
entries.literal: passed down through ten thousand generations, it will burden bright virtue—this is the second point of impropriety.

entries.zh: 夫帝王者，居高明，燭幽滯。
entries.en: Emperors and kings occupy the heights and illuminate what is dark and stagnant.
entries.literal: Emperors and kings occupy high clarity and illuminate what is dark and stagnant.

entries.zh: 先皇所以因龍首建望春，蓋為此也。
entries.en: It was for this that the late emperor built Wangchun on Longshou.
entries.literal: It is for this that the late emperor built Wangchun on the basis of Longshou.

entries.zh: 今若起陵目前，動傷宸慮，天心一傷，數日不平。
entries.en: If a mausoleum is raised before your eyes, it will wound your imperial thoughts. Once the heavenly heart is wounded, it is unsettled for days.
entries.literal: If a mausoleum is now raised before your eyes, stirring and wounding your imperial thoughts, once the heavenly heart is wounded it is unbalanced for days.

entries.zh: 且匹夫向隅，滿堂為之不樂；
entries.en: When a common man faces a corner, the whole hall is made unhappy;
entries.literal: Moreover, when a common man faces a corner, the whole hall is made unhappy for it;

entries.zh: 萬乘不樂，人其可歡心乎？
entries.en: when the Son of Heaven is unhappy, how can the people rejoice?
entries.literal: when the Son of Heaven is unhappy, how can the people be joyful?

entries.zh: 又暇日起歌，動鐘於內，此地皆聞，此非宜三也。
entries.en: On leisure days when singing is raised and bells struck within, all this area hears it—this is the third impropriety.
entries.literal: Also, when on leisure days singing is raised and bells are struck within, all this place hears it—this is the third point of impropriety.

entries.zh: 伏以貞懿皇后，坤德合天，母慈逮下，陛下以切軫旒扆，久俟蓍龜。
entries.en: The Virtuous and Gracious Empress, in earthly virtue conformed to Heaven and motherly compassion reached those below. Your Majesty, deeply grieved at the throne, long awaited the divination of shell and stalks.
entries.literal: Prostrate myself in considering that the Virtuous and Gracious Empress, in her earthly virtue conformed to Heaven and her motherly compassion reached those below, Your Majesty, deeply grieved at the imperial throne, long awaited the divination of tortoise shell and yarrow stalks.

entries.zh: 始謚之以貞懿，終待之以褻近，臣竊惑焉，非所以稱述後德，光被下泉也。
entries.en: At first you honored her with the posthumous title Virtuous and Gracious, yet in the end you treat her with intimate proximity. I am privately perplexed; this is not how to proclaim her late virtue and spread its light below.
entries.literal: At first you honored her with the posthumous title Virtuous and Gracious, yet in the end you wait to treat her with intimate proximity—your subject is privately perplexed; this is not the way to proclaim her late virtue and spread its light to the netherworld.

entries.zh: 今國人皆曰：「貞懿皇后之陵邇於城下者，主上將日省而時望焉。」
entries.en: Now the people all say, "The mausoleum of the Virtuous and Gracious Empress near the walls below the city—the sovereign will visit it daily and gaze upon it from time to time."
entries.literal: Now the people all say: "The mausoleum of the Virtuous and Gracious Empress, being near below the city walls—the sovereign will visit it daily and gaze upon it from time to time."

entries.zh: 斯有損於聖德，無益於貞懿。
entries.en: This damages sagely virtue and does the Virtuous and Gracious Empress no good.
entries.literal: This damages sagely virtue and benefits not the Virtuous and Gracious Empress.

entries.zh: 將欲寵之，而反辱之，此非宜四也。
entries.en: Wishing to honor her, one instead dishonors her—this is the fourth impropriety.
entries.literal: Wishing to honor her, one instead dishonors her—this is the fourth point of impropriety.

entries.zh: 凡此數事，實玷大猷，天下鹹知，伏惟陛下熟計而取其長也。
entries.en: All these matters truly stain the great design, and all under Heaven know it. I beg Your Majesty to weigh them carefully and choose what is best.
entries.literal: All these matters truly stain the great plan; all under Heaven know them. I prostrate myself in hope that Your Majesty will carefully calculate and take what is best.

entries.zh: 陛下方將偃武靖人，一誤於此，其傷實多。
entries.en: Your Majesty is about to cease warfare and bring peace to the people. A single mistake here will cause much harm.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is about to cease warfare and bring peace to the people—a single mistake here will cause much harm.

entries.zh: 臣恐君子是非，史官褒貶，大明忽虧於掩蝕，至德翻後於堯、舜，不其惜哉！
entries.en: I fear that gentlemen's judgments and the historiographers' praise and blame will find sudden brilliance obscured and supreme virtue falling behind Yao and Shun—is this not lamentable!
entries.literal: Your subject fears that the judgments of gentlemen and the praise and blame of historiographers—sudden brilliance may be obscured and eroded, and supreme virtue may fall behind Yao and Shun—is this not to be regretted!

entries.zh: 今指日尚遙，改卜何害？
entries.en: The appointed day is still distant. What harm is there in choosing a new site?
entries.literal: The appointed day is still distant—what harm in changing the site?

entries.zh: 抑皇情之殊眷，成貞懿之美號。
entries.en: Rather, restrain your special affection and complete the Virtuous and Gracious Empress's beautiful posthumous honor.
entries.literal: Rather, restrain the emperor's special affection and complete the beautiful posthumous title of the Virtuous and Gracious Empress.

entries.zh: 茂元，幼有勇略，從父征伐知名。
entries.en: Maoyuan showed courage and tactical skill from youth and won fame campaigning with his father.
entries.literal: Maoyuan in his youth had courage and stratagem; following his father in campaigns he became renowned.

entries.zh: 元和中，為右神策將軍。
entries.en: During the Yuanhe reign he served as a general of the Right Shence Army.
entries.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was Right Shence Army general.

entries.zh: 太和中，檢校工部尚書、廣州刺史、嶺南節度使。
entries.en: In the Taihe era he became acting Minister of Works, prefect of Guangzhou, and military governor of Lingnan.
entries.literal: In the Taihe era he was acting Minister of Works, prefect of Guangzhou, and Lingnan military governor.

entries.zh: 在安南招懷蠻落，頗立政能。
entries.en: In Annan he won over the tribal peoples and governed with notable effectiveness.
entries.literal: In Annan he recruited and reassured the tribal settlements and established considerable administrative ability.

entries.zh: 南中多異貨，茂元積聚家財鉅萬計。
entries.en: The south abounded in exotic goods, and Maoyuan accumulated a family fortune of many millions.
entries.literal: The south had many exotic goods; Maoyuan amassed family wealth to the number of tens of millions.

entries.zh: 李訓之敗，中官利其財，掎摭其事，言茂元因王涯、鄭註見用。
entries.en: After Li Xun's downfall the eunuchs coveted his wealth and denounced him, claiming he had risen through the patronage of Wang Ya and Zheng Zhu.
entries.literal: When Li Xun's plot failed, the inner court eunuchs coveted his wealth and seized on his affairs, saying Maoyuan had been employed through Wang Ya and Zheng Zhu.

entries.zh: 茂元懼，罄家財以賂兩軍，以是授忠武軍節度、陳許觀察使。
entries.en: Fearing ruin, Maoyuan spent his entire fortune bribing the two armies and was transferred to military governor of the Zhongwu Army and observation commissioner of Chen and Xu.
entries.literal: Maoyuan feared this and exhausted his family wealth to bribe the two armies; because of this he was appointed Zhongwu Army military governor and Chenxu observation commissioner.

entries.zh: 會昌中，為河陽節度使。
entries.en: During the Huichang reign he served as military governor of Hanyang.
entries.literal: In the Huichang era he was Hanyang military governor.

entries.zh: 是時河北諸軍討劉稹，茂元亦以本軍屯天井，賊未平而卒。
entries.en: When the Hebei armies campaigned against Liu Zhen, Maoyuan encamped at Tianjing with his own troops but died before the rebellion was crushed.
entries.literal: At that time the Hebei armies attacked Liu Zhen; Maoyuan also encamped his own army at Tianjing, and before the rebels were pacified he died.

entries.zh: 馬璘，扶風人也。
entries.en: Ma Lin was a native of Fufeng.
entries.literal: Ma Lin was a man of Fufeng.

entries.zh: 祖正會，右威衛將軍。
entries.en: His grandfather Zheng Hui had served as general of the Right Martial Majesty Guard.
entries.literal: His grandfather Zheng Hui was Right Martial Majesty Guard general.

entries.zh: 父晟，右司禦率府兵曹參軍。
entries.en: His father Sheng was registrar of military affairs in the Right Imperial Guard Training Corps.
entries.literal: His father Sheng was military affairs registrar of the Right Imperial Guard Training Bureau.

entries.zh: 璘少孤，落拓不事生業。
entries.en: Lin lost his parents early and lived unconstrained, without taking up any regular occupation.
entries.literal: Lin was orphaned young, unrestrained and not pursuing any livelihood.

entries.zh: 年二十余，讀《馬援傳》至「大丈夫當死於邊野，以馬革裹屍而歸」，慨然嘆曰：「豈使吾祖勛業墜於地乎！」
entries.en: In his early twenties he read the biography of Ma Yuan as far as the line that a great man ought to die on the frontier, his body wrapped in horsehide for the journey home, and exclaimed with feeling, "Am I to let my forebears' achievements come to nothing?"
entries.literal: When he was a little over twenty, reading the biography of Ma Yuan to the passage "A great man ought to die on the frontier wilds, his corpse wrapped in horsehide for the return home," he sighed in emotion and said, "Shall I let my ancestors' achievements fall to the ground?"

entries.zh: 開元末，杖劍從戎，自效於安西。
entries.en: At the close of the Kaiyuan reign he took up the sword and entered military service, volunteering in the Anxi Protectorate.
entries.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he took sword in hand to join the army and offered himself in Anxi.

entries.zh: 以前後奇功，累遷至左金吾衛將軍同正。
entries.en: Through a series of remarkable feats he rose step by step to acting general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
entries.literal: Because of repeated extraordinary achievements he was promoted in succession to acting Left Golden Crow Guard general.

entries.zh: 其載，補剡縣尉，改會稽尉。
entries.en: He was then appointed supplemental magistrate of Shan County and transferred to magistrate of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was appointed supplemental magistrate of Shan County and transferred to magistrate of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 宣州觀察使殷日用奏為判官，宣慰使李季卿又以表薦，連授大理評事、兼監察御史。
entries.en: Yin Riyong, commissioner observing Xuanzhou, memorialized to make him judge; pacification commissioner Li Jiqing also recommended him, and he was successively made evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent investigating censor.
entries.literal: Yin Riyong, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou, memorialized to appoint him judge; the pacification commissioner Li Jiqing also recommended him by memorial, and he was successively made Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent Investigating Censor.

entries.zh: 轉運使劉晏奏令巡覆江西，多所蠲免。
entries.en: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan had him tour and review Jiangxi, and many tax remissions were granted.
entries.literal: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan memorialized to have him tour and review Jiangxi, and many remissions were granted.

entries.zh: 改殿中侍御史、檢校倉部員外、民部郎中，並充浙西留後。
entries.en: He became Palace Attendant Censor, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He was changed to Palace Attendant Censor, acting vice director of the Granaries Office, and director in the Ministry of Revenue, all while serving as acting governor of western Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 佐晏征賦，頗有裨益，晏甚任之。
entries.en: Assisting Yan in tax collection, he proved of considerable benefit, and Yan relied on him greatly.
entries.literal: Assisting Yan in collecting taxes, he was of considerable benefit, and Yan greatly relied on him.

entries.zh: 姚南仲，華州下邽人。
entries.en: Yao Nanzhong came from Xiaji in Hua Prefecture.
entries.literal: Yao Nanzhong was a native of Xiaji in Hua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 乾元初，制科登第，授太子校書，歷高陵、昭應、萬年三縣尉。
entries.en: In the early Qianyuan period he passed the special examination, was made collator to the Crown Prince, and served in turn as county defender of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, he passed the special examination and was appointed Crown Prince's collator; he served successively as county defender of Gaoling, Zhaoying, and Wannian.

entries.zh: 遷右拾遺，轉右補闕。
entries.en: He rose to Right Reminder and then became Right Supplementation Censor.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Right Reminder and then transferred to Right Supplementation Censor.

entries.zh: 大歷十三年，貞懿皇后獨孤氏崩，代宗悼惜不已，令於近城為陵墓，冀朝夕臨望於目前。
entries.en: In Dali 13 the Virtuous and Gracious Empress, née Dugu, died. Emperor Daizong grieved deeply and ordered a mausoleum built close to the capital so he could look upon it at every hour of the day.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of the Dali era, the Virtuous and Gracious Empress of the Dugu clan died; Emperor Daizong mourned her without cease and ordered a tomb built near the city, hoping to gaze upon it morning and evening before his eyes.

entries.zh: 南仲上疏諫曰：
entries.en: Nanzhong submitted a memorial of remonstrance, which read:
entries.literal: Nanzhong submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:

entries.zh: 裴度領太原，署為參謀。
entries.en: When Pei Du governed Taiyuan he appointed Rong staff planner.
entries.literal: When Pei Du governed Taiyuan he appointed him as staff planner.

entries.zh: 時王承宗據鎮州叛，度請戎單車往諭之，承宗感泣受教。
entries.en: When Wang Chengzong held Zhen Prefecture in rebellion, Du asked Rong to go alone to instruct him, and Chengzong wept and accepted instruction.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Chengzong held Zhen Prefecture in rebellion; Du asked Rong to go alone in a single carriage to instruct him, and Chengzong wept and accepted instruction.

entries.zh: 入為殿中侍御史，累拜吏部郎中，遷諫議大夫。
entries.en: He entered court as palace censor, rose to bureau director of personnel, and became censor.
entries.literal: He entered court as Palace Censor and was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel and then Censor.

entries.zh: 尋為劍南東、西兩川宣慰使。
entries.en: He was soon made pacification commissioner of Eastern and Western Sichuan.
entries.literal: He was soon made pacification commissioner of the Eastern and Western Sichuan circuits.

entries.zh: 西州承蠻寇之後，戎既宣撫，兼再定征稅，廢置得所，公私便之。
entries.en: Western prefectures, having suffered barbarian raids, were pacified by Rong; levies were reassessed, abolitions and establishments were appropriate, and public and private alike benefited.
entries.literal: The western prefectures, having suffered barbarian raids, were both pacified by Rong and had their levies reassessed; abolitions and establishments were appropriate, and public and private alike benefited.

entries.zh: 還，拜給事中，駁奏為當時所稱。
entries.en: On return he became drafting attendant; his memorials of rejection were praised at the time.
entries.literal: On his return he was appointed Drafting Attendant; his memorials of rejection were praised at the time.

entries.zh: 改華州刺史，遷兗海沂密都團練觀察等使。
entries.en: He became governor of Hua and overall training and surveillance commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.
entries.literal: He was changed to governor of Hua Prefecture and transferred to overall training and surveillance commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.

entries.zh: 將行，州人戀惜遮道，至有解靴斷登者。
entries.en: As he was about to depart, reluctant people blocked the road; some even pulled off boots and broke carriage steps.
entries.literal: As he was about to depart, the people, reluctant to part with him, blocked the road; some even pulled off boots and broke carriage steps.

entries.zh: 理兗一年，大和八年五月卒，贈禮部尚書。
entries.en: After governing Yan one year he died in the fifth month of Dahe 8 and was posthumously made minister of rites.
entries.literal: After governing Yan for one year he died in the fifth month of the eighth year of Dahe and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 毅夫，登進士第。
entries.en: Yifu passed the jinshi examination.
entries.literal: Yifu passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 初正甫兄式，大歷中進士登第，繼之以正甫，式子元夫、傑夫、征夫又相次登科。
entries.en: At first Zhengfu's elder brother Shi passed the jinshi in the Dalu era, followed by Zhengfu; Shi's sons Yuanfu, Jiefu, and Zhengfu passed in succession.
entries.literal: At first Zhengfu's elder brother Shi passed the jinshi in the Dalu era, followed by Zhengfu; Shi's sons Yuanfu, Jiefu, and Zhengfu in turn passed the examination in succession.

entries.zh: 太和中，文章之盛，世共稱之。
entries.en: In the Taihe era the flourishing of literary talent was praised by the age.
entries.literal: In the Taihe era the flourishing of literary talent was praised together by the age.

entries.zh: 元夫，太和初兵部郎中、知制誥，遷中書舍人，出為汝州刺史。
entries.en: Yuanfu, early in Taihe, was war bureau director and drafting drafter, rose to drafting attendant, and was sent out as governor of Ru.
entries.literal: Yuanfu, early in Taihe, was Bureau Director of the Ministry of War and drafting drafter, was promoted to Drafting Attendant, and was sent out as governor of Ru Prefecture.

entries.zh: 毅夫位至戶部侍郎、弘文館學士判院事。
entries.en: Yifu rose to vice minister of revenue and Hongwen Hall academician with charge of the academy.
entries.literal: Yifu rose to Vice Minister of Revenue and academician of the Hongwen Hall with charge of the academy.

entries.zh: 諸群從登第者數人，而毅夫子祎最知名。
entries.en: Several cousins passed the examination; among them Yifu's son Yi was most renowned.
entries.literal: Several cousins passed the examination; among them Yifu's son Yi was most renowned.

entries.zh: 祎，字冠章，釋褐汴州從事、戶部判官，入為藍田尉、集賢校理。
entries.en: Yi, styled Guanzhang, first served as staff in Bian and revenue judge, entered court as magistrate of Lantian and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
entries.literal: Yi, styled Guanzhang, on leaving office served as staff in Bian Prefecture and revenue judge, entered court as magistrate of Lantian and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

entries.zh: 趙隱鎮浙西，劉鄴鎮淮南，皆辟為賓佐。
entries.en: When Zhao Yin governed Zhexi and Liu Ye governed Huainan, both recruited him as staff.
entries.literal: When Zhao Yin governed Zhexi and Liu Ye governed Huainan, both recruited him as staff.

entries.zh: 入為監察御史，遷左補闕。
entries.en: He entered court as investigating censor and rose to left reminder.
entries.literal: He entered court as Investigating Censor and was promoted to Left Reminder.

entries.zh: 乾符中，詔入翰林為學士，累官至中書舍人。
entries.en: In the Qianfu era an edict summoned him to the Hanlin Academy; he rose repeatedly to drafting attendant.
entries.literal: In the Qianfu era an edict summoned him to the Hanlin Academy as academician; he rose repeatedly to Drafting Attendant.

entries.zh: 黃巢犯京師，從僖宗幸蜀，拜工部侍郎，判戶部事。
entries.en: When Huang Chao attacked the capital he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu and was appointed vice minister of works with charge of revenue.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu and was appointed Vice Minister of Works with charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 奉使江淮還，為當塗者不協，改太子賓客、左散騎常侍，轉吏部侍郎，歷刑部、兵部尚書。
entries.en: Returning from a Jianghuai mission he was at odds with the man in power and was changed to crown prince's mentor and left regular attendant, then vice minister of personnel, and successively minister of justice and minister of war.
entries.literal: On returning from a mission to the Jianghuai region he was at odds with the man in power and was changed to Crown Prince's Mentor and Left Regular Attendant, then Vice Minister of Personnel, and successively Minister of Justice and Minister of War.

entries.zh: 從昭宗在華，為韓建所構，貶衡州司馬。
entries.en: Following Emperor Zhaozong at Hua he was framed by Han Jian and demoted to vice magistrate of Heng.
entries.literal: Following Emperor Zhaozong at Hua he was framed by Han Jian and demoted to Vice Magistrate of Heng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 昭宗還京，征拜禮部尚書、太常卿，充禮儀使，遷兵部尚書。
entries.en: When Zhaozong returned to the capital he was summoned as minister of rites and grand minister of imperial sacrifices and ritual commissioner, then promoted to minister of war.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong returned to the capital he was summoned as Minister of Rites and Grand Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and made ritual commissioner, then promoted to Minister of War.

entries.zh: 祎苦心為文，老而益壯。
entries.en: Yi labored at writing; in old age his work grew stronger.
entries.literal: Yi labored at writing; in old age his work grew stronger.

entries.zh: 為刑部時，劉鄴子覃，當巢寇時避禍於金吾將軍張直方之第，被害。
entries.en: When he was minister of justice, Liu Ye's son Tan, during the Huang Chao rebellion, had taken refuge in Gold Crow Guard commander Zhang Zhifang's residence and was killed.
entries.literal: When he was Minister of Justice, Liu Ye's son Tan, during the Huang Chao rebellion, had taken refuge in the residence of Gold Crow Guard commander Zhang Zhifang and was killed.

entries.zh: 僖宗還京，而惡覃者以托附逆黨，死不以義，下三司詳罪。
entries.en: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital those who hated Tan accused him of attaching himself to rebels and dying without righteousness; the Three Offices were ordered to examine the crime.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital those who hated Tan accused him of attaching himself to the rebel party and dying without righteousness; the Three Offices were ordered to examine the crime in detail.

entries.zh: 祎上章申理，言覃父子並命於賊廷，豈附逆耶？
entries.en: Yi submitted a memorial in his defense, saying father and son both met death in the rebel court—how could this be joining rebellion?
entries.literal: Yi submitted a memorial in his defense, saying father and son both met their deaths in the rebel court—how could this be joining rebellion?

entries.zh: 其家竟獲洗雪，覃亦贈官。
entries.en: His family finally obtained rehabilitation and Tan was also posthumously granted office.
entries.literal: His family finally obtained rehabilitation and Tan was also posthumously granted office.

entries.zh: 其行義始終，皆如此類。
entries.en: His righteous conduct from beginning to end was all of this kind.
entries.literal: His righteous conduct from beginning to end was all of this kind.

entries.zh: 潘孟陽，禮部侍郎炎之子也。
entries.en: Pan Mengyang was the son of Yan, Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: Pan Mengyang was the son of Yan, Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 孟陽以父廕進，登博學宏辭科。
entries.en: Mengyang entered service through his father's privilege and passed the Boxue Hongci examination.
entries.literal: Mengyang advanced through his father's yin privilege and passed the Broad Learning and Eloquent Expression examination.

entries.zh: 累遷殿中侍御史，降為司議郎。
entries.en: He rose to Palace Censor, then was demoted to Secretariat Drafter.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Censor, then demoted to Secretariat Drafter.

entries.zh: 孟陽母，劉晏女也。
entries.en: Mengyang's mother was Liu Yan's daughter.
entries.literal: Mengyang's mother was a daughter of Liu Yan.

entries.zh: 公卿多父友及外祖賓從，故得薦用，累至兵部郎中。
entries.en: Many high officials were friends of his father or associates of his maternal grandfather, so he won recommendations and rose to bureau director in the Ministry of War.
entries.literal: Many ministers and officials were his father's friends and his maternal grandfather's associates and followers, so he was recommended for appointment and rose to Bureau Director of the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 先是，監軍使劉承偕恃寵淩節度使劉悟，三軍憤發大噪，擒承偕，欲殺之。
entries.en: Previously, the army supervisor Liu Chengjie, relying on imperial favor, looked down on the military commissioner Liu Wu. The three armies, inflamed with anger, raised a great clamor, seized Chengjie, and meant to kill him.
entries.literal: Previously, the army supervisor Liu Chengjie, relying on imperial favor, looked down on the military commissioner Liu Wu; the three armies, inflamed with anger, raised a great clamor, seized Chengjie, and meant to kill him.

entries.zh: 已殺其二傔，悟救之獲免，而囚承偕。
entries.en: They had already killed two of his attendants. Liu Wu rescued him and he escaped death, but Chengjie was imprisoned.
entries.literal: They had already killed two of his attendants; Wu rescued him and he escaped death, but Chengjie was imprisoned.

entries.zh: 詔遣歸京，悟托以軍情，不時奉詔。
entries.en: An edict ordered Chengjie sent back to the capital, but Liu Wu pleaded military circumstances and did not comply in good time.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Chengjie sent back to the capital, but Wu pleaded military circumstances and did not comply in good time.

entries.zh: 至是，宰臣延英奏事，度亦在列。
entries.en: At this point the chief ministers were reporting affairs at the Yanying Hall, and Du was among them.
entries.literal: At this point the chief ministers were reporting affairs at the Yanying Hall, and Du was among them.

entries.zh: 上顧謂度曰：「劉悟拘承偕而不遣，如何處置？」
entries.en: The emperor turned to Du and said: "Liu Wu is holding Chengjie and will not release him. How should this be handled?"
entries.literal: The emperor turned to Du and said: "Liu Wu is holding Chengjie and will not release him. How should this be handled?"

entries.zh: 度辭以蕃臣不合議軍國事。
entries.en: Du declined on the ground that as a frontier appointee he ought not debate state and military affairs.
entries.literal: Du declined on the ground that as a frontier appointee he ought not debate state and military affairs.

entries.zh: 上固問之，且曰：「劉悟負我，我以僕射寵之，近又賜絹五百萬疋，不思報功，翻縱軍眾淩辱監軍，我實難奈此事。」
entries.en: The emperor pressed him further and said: "Liu Wu has betrayed me. I showered him with the title of Vice Director of the Left and recently granted five million bolts of silk, yet instead of repaying me with loyal service he let his troops humiliate the army supervisor. I truly find this situation hard to bear."
entries.literal: The emperor pressed him further and said: "Liu Wu has betrayed me. I showered him with the title of Vice Director of the Left and recently granted five million bolts of silk, yet instead of repaying me with loyal service he let his troops humiliate the army supervisor. I truly find this situation hard to bear."

entries.zh: 度對曰：「承偕在昭義不法，臣盡知之，昨劉悟在行營與臣書，數論其事。
entries.en: Du replied: "Chengjie's misconduct in Zhaoyi is fully known to me. Not long ago Liu Wu wrote to me from the field camp, repeatedly discussing the matter.
entries.literal: Du replied: "Chengjie's misconduct in Zhaoyi is fully known to me. Not long ago Liu Wu wrote to me from the field camp, repeatedly discussing the matter.

entries.zh: 是時有中使趙弘亮在臣軍，仍持悟書將去，欲自奏，不知奏否？」
entries.en: At that time the envoy Zhao Hongliang was with my army, carrying Liu Wu's letter away and intending to report it himself. I do not know whether he reported it or not."
entries.literal: At that time the envoy Zhao Hongliang was with my army, carrying Wu's letter away, intending to report it himself — I do not know whether he reported it or not?"

entries.zh: 上曰：「我都不知，悟何不密奏其事，我豈不能處置？」
entries.en: The emperor said: "I knew nothing of this. Why did Liu Wu not report it secretly? Could I not have handled it?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I knew nothing of this. Why did Wu not report it secretly? Could I not have handled it?"

entries.zh: 度曰：「劉悟武臣，不知大臣體例。
entries.en: Du said: "Liu Wu is a military officer and does not know the protocols expected of high ministers.
entries.literal: Du said: "Liu Wu is a military officer and does not know the protocols expected of high ministers.

entries.zh: 雖然，臣竊以悟縱有密奏，陛下必不能處置。
entries.en: Even so, I privately believe that even had Liu Wu made a secret report, Your Majesty would certainly not have been able to act on it.
entries.literal: Even so, I privately believe that even had Wu made a secret report, Your Majesty would certainly not have been able to act on it.

entries.zh: 今日事狀如此，臣等面論，陛下猶未能決，悟單辭豈能動聖聽哉？」
entries.en: Today's situation is as you see. Even with us debating face to face Your Majesty still cannot decide — how could Liu Wu's word alone have moved the imperial ear?"
entries.literal: Today's situation is as you see. Even with us debating face to face Your Majesty still cannot decide — how could Wu's word alone have moved the imperial ear?"

entries.zh: 上曰：「前事勿論，直言此時如何處置？」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Do not discuss the past. Tell me plainly how it should be handled now."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Do not discuss the past. Tell me plainly how it should be handled now."

entries.zh: 度曰：「陛下必欲收忠義之心，使天下戎臣為陛下死節，唯有下半紙詔書，言任使不明，致承偕亂法如此，令悟集三軍斬之。
entries.en: Du said: "If Your Majesty truly wishes to win the hearts of the loyal and righteous and make military men throughout the realm die for you in faithful service, there is only one course: issue half a sheet of edict saying that your appointment was ill-chosen, that this caused Chengjie to break the law so flagrantly, and order Liu Wu to assemble the three armies and execute him.
entries.literal: Du said: "If Your Majesty truly wishes to win the hearts of the loyal and righteous and make military men throughout the realm die for you in faithful service, there is only one course: issue half a sheet of edict saying that your appointment was ill-chosen, that this caused Chengjie to break the law so flagrantly, and order Liu Wu to assemble the three armies and execute him.

entries.zh: 如此，則萬方畢命，群盜破膽，天下無事矣。
entries.en: If you do this, all the realm will pour out their lives for you, every rebel will lose heart, and the empire will be at peace.
entries.literal: If you do this, all the realm will pour out their lives for you, every rebel will lose heart, and the empire will be at peace.

entries.zh: 茍不能如此，雖與劉悟改官賜絹，臣亦恐於事無益。」
entries.en: If you cannot do this, then even if you change Liu Wu's titles and grant him more silk, I fear it will do no good."
entries.literal: If you cannot do this, then even if you change Liu Wu's titles and grant him more silk, I fear it will do no good.'

entries.zh: 上俛首良久，曰：「朕不惜承偕。
entries.en: The emperor bowed his head for a long while and said, "I would not begrudge Chengjie.
entries.literal: The emperor bowed his head for a long while and said, "I would not begrudge Chengjie.

entries.zh: 緣是太后養子，今被囚縶，太后未知，如卿處置未得，可更議其宜。」
entries.en: But he is the Empress Dowager's adopted son. He is now imprisoned and the Empress Dowager does not know. If your proposed handling will not do, we may discuss a more suitable course."
entries.literal: But he is the Empress Dowager's adopted son. He is now imprisoned and the Empress Dowager does not know. If your proposed handling will not do, we may discuss a more suitable course."

entries.zh: 度與王播等復奏曰：「但配流遠惡處，承偕必得出。」
entries.en: Du and Wang Bo and the others again reported: "If he is simply exiled to some remote and harsh place, Chengjie will surely be released."
entries.literal: Du and Wang Bo and the others again reported: "If he is simply exiled to some remote and harsh place, Chengjie will surely be released."

entries.zh: 上以為然，承偕果得歸。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, and Chengjie was indeed able to return.
entries.literal: The emperor agreed, and Chengjie was indeed able to return.

entries.zh: 裴度，字中立，河東聞喜人。
entries.en: Pei Du, whose courtesy name was Zhongli, came from Wenxi in Hedong.
entries.literal: Pei Du, styled Zhongli, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.

entries.zh: 祖有鄰，濮州濮陽令。
entries.en: His grandfather Youlin had served as magistrate of Puyang in Puzhou.
entries.literal: His grandfather Youlin was magistrate of Puyang in Puzhou.

entries.zh: 父漵，河南府澠池丞。
entries.en: His father Yin had been vice-prefect of Chi in the Henan prefectural administration.
entries.literal: His father Yin was vice-prefect of Chi in Henan prefecture.

entries.zh: 度，貞元五年進士擢第，登宏辭科。
entries.en: Du passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Zhenyuan reign and also qualified in the Hongci literary examination.
entries.literal: Du, in the fifth year of Zhenyuan, was selected in the jinshi examination and passed the Hongci examination.

entries.zh: 應制舉賢良方正、能直言極諫科，對策高等，授河陰縣尉。
entries.en: He entered the special imperial examination for worthy and upright men and for candid critics, placed high in the policy responses, and was appointed assistant magistrate of Heyin county.
entries.literal: He responded to the imperial summons for the examination of worthy and upright men and those able to speak bluntly with utmost remonstrance, ranked high in the policy answers, and was appointed county assistant of Heyin.

entries.zh: 遷監察御史，密疏論權幸，語切忤旨，出為河南府功曹。
entries.en: Promoted to investigating censor, he submitted a secret memorial attacking powerful favorites in language so sharp that it offended the throne, and he was transferred out to serve as recorder of Henan prefecture.
entries.literal: He was transferred to investigating censor; in a secret memorial he discussed powerful favorites, his words sharp and contrary to the imperial will, and he was sent out as recorder of Henan prefecture.

entries.zh: 遷起居舍人。
entries.en: He was then appointed attendant of the imperial diaries.
entries.literal: He was transferred to attendant of the diaries.

entries.zh: 元和六年，以司封員外郎知制誥，尋轉本司郎中。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he drafted imperial edicts as assistant director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments and was soon promoted to director within that bureau.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe, as assistant director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments he was charged with drafting edicts; soon he was transferred to director within the same bureau.

entries.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
entries.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
entries.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
entries.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
entries.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

entries.zh: 時可舉遣將李全忠攻易州。
entries.en: Keju then sent the general Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.
entries.literal: At that time Keju sent the general Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.

entries.zh: 有次將劉仁恭者，多權數；
entries.en: Among the deputy generals was Liu Rengong, a man of many stratagems.
entries.literal: Among the deputy generals was one Liu Rengong, full of stratagems.

entries.zh: 攻之彌月不下，乃穴地道以入。
entries.en: After a month of siege the city still held, so they dug a tunnel to enter it.
entries.literal: They besieged it for a full month without taking it, then dug a tunnel to enter.

entries.zh: 其城既下，易州士卒稍驕。
entries.en: After the city fell, the Yizhou soldiers grew somewhat overconfident.
entries.literal: Once the city had fallen, the soldiers of Yizhou grew somewhat arrogant.

entries.zh: 王處存引輕軍三千，以羊皮蒙之，夜伏於城外，仍別於間道以騎士伺之。
entries.en: Wang Chucun led three thousand light troops, covered them with sheepskins, and hid outside the city by night, while posting cavalry on a side road to watch for an opportunity.
entries.literal: Wang Chucun led three thousand light troops, covered them with sheepskins, and lay in ambush outside the city by night; he also posted cavalry on a side path to watch.

entries.zh: 燕軍望見，謂之群羊，爭趨焉。
entries.en: The Yan soldiers saw them from a distance, mistook them for a flock of sheep, and rushed to capture them.
entries.literal: When the Yan army saw them from afar, they took them for a flock of sheep and rushed to seize them.

entries.zh: 處存乘其無部伍，一擊大敗之，尋復其城。
entries.en: Chucun struck while they were disordered, routed them in a single blow, and soon recovered the city.
entries.literal: Chucun took advantage of their lack of formation, struck once and inflicted a great defeat, and soon recovered the city.

entries.zh: 全忠遁歸，懼可舉罪之，收其餘眾，反攻幽州。
entries.en: Quanzhong fled home, fearing Keju would punish him for the defeat. He gathered his remaining troops and turned against Youzhou.
entries.literal: Quanzhong fled back, fearing Keju would punish him; he gathered his remaining troops and counterattacked Youzhou.

entries.zh: 可舉危急，收集其族，登樓自燔而死。
entries.en: Keju, trapped and desperate, gathered his family, climbed a tower, and burned himself to death.
entries.literal: Keju was in dire straits; he gathered his clan, ascended a tower, and burned himself to death.

entries.zh: 李全忠，范陽人。
entries.en: Li Quanzhong was a native of Fanyang.
entries.literal: Li Quanzhong was a man of Fanyang.

entries.zh: 廣明中，為棣州司馬。
entries.en: During the Guangming era he served as defender of Dizhou.
entries.literal: During the Guangming reign he was defender of Dizhou.

entries.zh: 有蘆生於室，一尺三節，心惡之。
entries.en: Reeds sprouted in his room, one foot tall with three joints, and the omen troubled him.
entries.literal: Reeds sprouted in his room, one chi tall with three joints; he was troubled at heart.

entries.zh: 謂別駕張建曰：「吾室生蘆，無乃怪歟？」
entries.en: He said to the vice prefect Zhang Jian, "Reeds have sprouted in my room — could this be an ill omen?"
entries.literal: He said to the vice prefect Zhang Jian: "Reeds have sprouted in my room — could this be an omen?"

entries.zh: 建曰：「蘆，茅類，得澤而滋，公家有茅土之慶，殆天意乎！
entries.en: Jian replied, "Reeds are a kind of rush; given water they flourish. Your lordship has the blessing of a fief — could this be Heaven's intent?
entries.literal: Jian said: "Reeds belong to the rush family; given moisture they flourish. Your lordship has the blessing of fief and soil — could this be Heaven's intent!

entries.zh: 其生三節，必傳節鉞者三人。
entries.en: Three joints mean three generations will hold the commission of seals and credentials.
entries.literal: That it sprouted with three joints means three men will in succession receive seals and credentials.

entries.zh: 公勉樹功名，無忘斯言。」
entries.en: Strive to build your merit and fame, my lord, and do not forget these words."
entries.literal: My lord, strive to build merit and fame, and do not forget these words."

entries.zh: 全忠秩滿還鄉里，事節度使李可舉為牙將。
entries.en: When his term expired Quanzhong returned home and served the military governor Li Keju as a guard officer.
entries.literal: When Quanzhong's term expired he returned to his home district and served the military governor Li Keju as a guard officer.

entries.zh: 時可舉兵鋒方盛，欲與鎮人分易、定，遣全忠將兵攻之，為定州軍大敗於易水。
entries.en: At that time Keju's armies were at their peak. Seeking to divide Yizhou and Dingzhou with the forces of Zhenzhou, he sent Quanzhong to attack them, but the Dingzhou army routed his forces at the Yi River.
entries.literal: At that time Keju's military power was at its height; wishing to divide Yi and Ding with the men of Zhen, he sent Quanzhong to lead troops in attack, but the army of Dingzhou inflicted a great defeat on them at the Yi River.

entries.zh: 全忠懼，率其餘眾掩攻幽州。
entries.en: Quanzhong, fearing punishment, turned his remaining troops against Youzhou.
entries.literal: Quanzhong was afraid and led his remaining troops in a surprise attack on Youzhou.

entries.zh: 可舉死。
entries.en: Keju died.
entries.literal: Keju died.

entries.zh: 三軍推全忠為留後，朝廷因以節鉞授之，光啟元年春也。
entries.en: The three armies installed Quanzhong as acting administrator, and the court invested him with the commission in the spring of the first year of Guangqi.
entries.literal: The three armies pushed Quanzhong forward as acting administrator, and the court thereupon invested him with seals and credentials — it was spring of the first year of Guangqi.

entries.zh: 全忠卒，子匡威自襲父位，稱留後。
entries.en: When Quanzhong died, his son Kuangwei seized his father's position and styled himself acting administrator.
entries.literal: When Quanzhong died, his son Kuangwei seized his father's position on his own authority and styled himself acting administrator.

entries.zh: 匡威素稱豪爽，屬遇亂離，繕甲燕薊，有吞四海之志。
entries.en: Kuangwei had long been known for boldness and generosity. In those years of chaos he armed his forces in Yan and Ji and harbored ambitions to dominate the realm.
entries.literal: Kuangwei had long been known for bold generosity; encountering turmoil and separation, he readied armor in Yan and Ji and harbored the ambition to swallow the four seas.

entries.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
entries.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
entries.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

entries.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
entries.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

entries.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
entries.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
entries.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

entries.zh: 時鎔童幼，求援於燕；
entries.en: Rong was still young and appealed to Yan for help.
entries.literal: At that time Rong was still a child and sought aid from Yan.

entries.zh: 匡威親率軍應之。
entries.en: Kuangwei personally led an army to his aid.
entries.literal: Kuangwei personally led an army to respond.

entries.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
entries.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

entries.zh: 匡威弟匡籌，妻張氏有國色。
entries.en: Kuangwei's younger brother Kuangchou had a wife, Lady Zhang, whose beauty was famed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Kuangwei's younger brother Kuangchou had a wife, Lady Zhang, of unrivaled beauty.

entries.zh: 師將發，家人會別，匡威酒酣，留張氏報之。
entries.en: When the army was about to march, the family gathered to say farewell. Kuangwei, drunk, detained Lady Zhang and violated her.
entries.literal: As the army was about to depart, the family gathered for farewell; Kuangwei, deep in wine, detained Lady Zhang and violated her.

entries.zh: 匡籌私懷忿怒，匡威軍至博野，匡籌乃據城自為節度。
entries.en: Kuangchou nursed his anger in secret. When Kuangwei's army reached Boye, Kuangchou seized the city and declared himself military governor.
entries.literal: Kuangchou privately harbored rage; when Kuangwei's army reached Boye, Kuangchou seized the city and made himself military governor.

entries.zh: 匡威部下聞之，亡歸者半。
entries.en: When Kuangwei's troops heard the news, half of them deserted and returned home.
entries.literal: When Kuangwei's subordinates heard of it, half fled back.

entries.zh: 匡威退無歸路，將入覲京師。
entries.en: Kuangwei retreated with nowhere to go and prepared to travel to the capital to pay homage.
entries.literal: Kuangwei retreated with no way back and intended to go to court in the capital.

entries.zh: 時匡威留於深州，遣判官李抱貞奉章以聞。
entries.en: Kuangwei remained at Shenzhou and sent his judge Li Baozhen with a memorial to inform the court.
entries.literal: At that time Kuangwei remained at Shenzhou and sent the judge Li Baozhen with a memorial to report the matter.

entries.zh: 屬京師大亂之後，聞匡威來朝，市人震恐，咸曰「金頭王來謀社稷」，士庶有亡竄山谷者。
entries.en: This came after the great upheaval in the capital. When word spread that Kuangwei was coming to court, the people of the city were terrified. "The Golden-Headed King is coming to seize the realm," they cried, and officials and commoners fled into the mountains.
entries.literal: This came after the great chaos in the capital; when people heard Kuangwei was coming to court, the townspeople were terrified and all said, "The Golden-Headed King comes to plot against the state," and officials and commoners fled into the mountains.

entries.zh: 匡威其實不行，欲圖鎮州，示無留意。
entries.en: Kuangwei never actually went. He intended to seize Zhenzhou and made a show of having no further designs.
entries.literal: Kuangwei in fact did not go; he wished to seize Zhenzhou and showed no intention of proceeding.

entries.zh: 鎔以匡威再來援己，致其失師，遣使迎歸府第，父事之。
entries.en: Because Kuangwei had twice come to his aid and twice cost him his army, Rong sent envoys to welcome him to his mansion and treated him with the deference due a father.
entries.literal: Rong, because Kuangwei had twice come to aid him and thereby caused the loss of his army, sent envoys to welcome him back to the mansion and treated him as a father.

entries.zh: 匡威為鎔城郛繕甲，指陳方略，視鎔如子。
entries.en: Kuangwei fortified Rong's walls, readied his armor, laid out strategy, and treated Rong as a son.
entries.literal: Kuangwei fortified the walls and readied armor for Rong, laid out strategy, and regarded Rong as a son.

entries.zh: 每陰謀驟施，以悅人心。
entries.en: He constantly carried out sudden secret maneuvers to win the people's favor.
entries.literal: He constantly enacted sudden secret plots to win people's hearts.

entries.zh: 鎮之三軍，素忠於王氏，惡其所為。
entries.en: The three armies of Zhenzhou had long been loyal to the Wang clan and despised his conduct.
entries.literal: The three armies of Zhen had long been loyal to the Wang clan and hated what he was doing.

entries.zh: 會鎔過匡威第慰忌辰，匡威縞衣裹甲，伏兵劫鎔入牙城。
entries.en: When Rong came to Kuangwei's mansion to observe a mourning anniversary, Kuangwei wore mourning garments over his armor and used hidden troops to seize Rong and carry him into the headquarters.
entries.literal: When Rong happened to visit Kuangwei's mansion to observe a mourning anniversary, Kuangwei wore hemp mourning garments over armor and with hidden troops seized Rong and carried him into the headquarters.

entries.zh: 鎔兵逆戰，燔東偏門，軍士呼噪登屋，矢下如雨。
entries.en: Rong's troops fought back, burned the eastern gate, and soldiers shouting climbed onto the rooftops as arrows fell like rain.
entries.literal: Rong's troops fought back, burned the east side gate, and soldiers shouting climbed onto the roofs; arrows fell like rain.

entries.zh: 鎔僕墨君和亂中扶鎔登屋免難，而斬匡威以徇。
entries.en: In the chaos Rong's servant Mo Junhe helped him climb onto a roof to safety, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed his head.
entries.literal: Rong's servant Mo Junhe in the chaos helped Rong climb onto a roof and escape harm, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed the head.

entries.zh: 是歲，匡籌出師攻鎮之樂壽、武強以報恥。
entries.en: That year Kuangchou marched against Leshou and Wuqiang in Zhenzhou to avenge the humiliation.
entries.literal: That year Kuangchou marched out to attack Leshou and Wuqiang in Zhen to avenge the disgrace.

entries.zh: 匡威部曲劉仁恭歸於河東。
entries.en: Liu Rengong, formerly one of Kuangwei's officers, defected to Hedong.
entries.literal: Liu Rengong, a follower of Kuangwei, went over to Hedong.

entries.zh: 乾寧元年冬，河東聽仁恭之謀，出師進討。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianning, that winter Hedong adopted Rengong's plan and marched out to attack Yan.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianning, in winter Hedong heeded Rengong's plan and marched out to campaign against Yan.

entries.zh: 二月，敗燕軍於居庸，匡籌挈其族遁去，將赴京師。
entries.en: In the second month they routed the Yan army at Juyong. Kuangchou fled with his family, intending to go to the capital.
entries.literal: In the second month they defeated the Yan army at Juyong; Kuangchou fled with his clan and intended to go to the capital.

entries.zh: 至景城，為滄州節度使盧彥威所殺，掠其輜車、妓妾。
entries.en: At Jingcheng he was killed by Lu Yanwei, military governor of Cangzhou, who seized his baggage train and concubines.
entries.literal: When he reached Jingcheng he was killed by Lu Yanwei, military governor of Cangzhou, who plundered his baggage train and concubines.

entries.zh: 匡籌妻張氏產於路，不能進，劉仁恭獲之，獻於李克用，後立為夫人，嬖寵專房。
entries.en: Kuangchou's wife Lady Zhang gave birth on the road and could go no farther. Liu Rengong captured her and presented her to Li Keyong, who later made her his primary wife and favored her above all others.
entries.literal: Kuangchou's wife Lady Zhang gave birth on the road and could not proceed; Liu Rengong captured her and presented her to Li Keyong, who later made her his primary wife and favored her exclusively.

entries.zh: 李氏父子三葉，十年而亡。
entries.en: The Li clan, father and son across three generations, was destroyed within ten years.
entries.literal: The Li clan, father and sons across three generations, perished within ten years.

entries.zh: 【贊】史臣曰：大都偶國，亂之本也。
entries.en: 【Commentary】 The historian writes: When a great city rivals the throne, rebellion is never far behind.
entries.literal: 【Commentary】 The historian says: A great metropolis rivaling the state is the root of chaos.

entries.zh: 故古先哲王建國，公侯之封，不過千乘，所以強幹弱枝，防其悖慢。
entries.en: That is why the sage kings of antiquity, when founding their states, granted fiefs of no more than a thousand chariots — to strengthen the center and weaken the periphery and guard against rebellion.
entries.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity in establishing states granted marquis and duke fiefs of no more than a thousand chariots, thereby strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches to guard against insolence.

entries.zh: 彼幽州者，列九圍之一，地方千里而遙，其民剛強，厥田沃壤。
entries.en: Youzhou was one of the nine domains of the realm. Its territory stretched a thousand li, its people were hardy and fierce, and its land was rich.
entries.literal: That Youzhou was one of the nine domains; its territory extended a thousand li into the distance, its people were sturdy and strong, and its fields were rich soil.

entries.zh: 遠則慕田光、荊卿之義，近則染祿山、思明之風。
entries.en: From afar they admired the loyalty of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were infected with the rebellious spirit of An Lushan and Shi Siming.
entries.literal: From afar they admired the righteousness of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were infected with the spirit of Lushan and Siming.

entries.zh: 二百餘年，自相崇樹，雖朝廷有時命帥，而土人多務逐君。
entries.en: For more than two hundred years they constantly elevated their own leaders. Though the court sometimes appointed commanders, the local people mostly worked to drive them out.
entries.literal: For more than two hundred years they constantly elevated one another; though the court sometimes appointed commanders, the local people mostly sought to oust their lords.

entries.zh: 習苦忘非，尾大不掉，非一朝一夕之故也。
entries.en: Hardened by hardship, they forgot restraint; the tail had grown too large to control. This did not happen overnight.
entries.literal: Accustomed to hardship they forgot wrongdoing; the tail grew too large to wag — this was not the work of a single morning or evening.

entries.zh: 若李載義、張仲武、張允伸因利乘便，獲領旌旗，以仁守之，恭順朝旨，亦足多也。
entries.en: When men such as Li Zaiyi, Zhang Zhongwu, and Zhang Yunshen seized their opportunity, won command of the banners, ruled with benevolence, and obeyed the court, they too deserve praise.
entries.literal: If men such as Li Zaiyi, Zhang Zhongwu, and Zhang Yunshen seized the opportunity, obtained command of the banners, ruled with benevolence, and respectfully followed court directives, that too was praiseworthy.

entries.zh: 如硃克融、楊志誠、史元忠、張公素、李可舉、李全忠，以不仁得之，靡更曩志。
entries.en: Men such as Zhu Kerong, Yang Zhicheng, Shi Yuanzhong, Zhang Gongsu, Li Keju, and Li Quanzhong seized power through violence and never abandoned their old ambitions.
entries.literal: Men such as Zhu Kerong, Yang Zhicheng, Shi Yuanzhong, Zhang Gongsu, Li Keju, and Li Quanzhong obtained power through lack of benevolence and never changed their former ambitions.

entries.zh: 或尋為篡奪，或僅傳子孫，咸非令終，蓋其宜也。
entries.en: Some were soon overthrown, others held power only long enough to pass it to their sons — none came to a good end, and that was only to be expected.
entries.literal: Some were soon usurped, some passed power only to their descendants — none met good ends; that was only fitting.

entries.zh: 朱克融，賊泚之從孫也。
entries.en: Zhu Kerong was a grandnephew of the rebel Zhu Ci.
entries.literal: Zhu Kerong was the grandnephew of the rebel Zhu Ci.

entries.zh: 祖滔，父洄。
entries.en: His grandfather was Zhu Tao, and his father was Zhu Hui.
entries.literal: His grandfather was Tao; his father was Hui.

entries.zh: 克融少為幽州軍校，事節度使劉總。
entries.en: In his youth Kerong served as a military officer in Youzhou under the military governor Liu Zong.
entries.literal: Kerong in his youth was a military officer in Youzhou and served the military governor Liu Zong.

entries.zh: 總將歸朝，慮其有變，籍軍中素有異志者，薦之闕下，時克融亦在籍中。
entries.en: When Liu Zong prepared to return to court, fearing unrest he drew up a list of men in the army who had long harbored rebellious designs and sent them to the capital; Kerong was among them.
entries.literal: When Zong was about to return to court, fearing there might be trouble, he registered those in the army who had long harbored divergent intentions and recommended them to the capital; at that time Kerong was also on the register.

entries.zh: 宰相崔植、杜元穎不知兵，且無遠略，謂兩河無虞，遂奏勒歸鎮。
entries.en: The chancellors Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying knew nothing of war and had no long-term vision. Assuming the Two He regions were safe, they memorialized that the men be sent back to their garrisons.
entries.literal: The chancellors Cui Zhi and Du Yuanying knew nothing of military affairs and lacked long-range strategy; thinking the Two He regions were secure, they memorialized that the men be ordered back to their posts.

entries.zh: 長慶初，幽州軍亂，囚其帥張弘靖。
entries.en: Early in the Changqing era the Youzhou army mutinied and imprisoned their commander Zhang Hongjing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing reign, the Youzhou army mutinied and imprisoned its commander Zhang Hongjing.

entries.zh: 時洄廢疾於家，軍中素伏其謀略，至是眾欲立之。
entries.en: Zhu Hui was then confined at home by chronic illness, but the army had long admired his strategic ability, and the troops now wanted to make him their leader.
entries.literal: At that time Hui lay at home with chronic illness; the army had long respected his stratagems, and now the men wished to install him.

entries.zh: 洄自以老且病，推克融統軍務焉。
entries.en: Hui, deeming himself too old and ill to serve, put Kerong in charge of military affairs.
entries.literal: Hui, considering himself old and ill, yielded command of military affairs to Kerong.

entries.zh: 朝廷尋加檢校左散騎常侍，授以符節，
entries.en: The court soon appointed him acting Left Regular Attendant and invested him with the seals and credentials of office.
entries.literal: The court soon added the acting post of Left Regular Attendant and invested him with seals and credentials.

entries.zh: 列傳第一百三十一史憲誠史憲誠，其先出於奚虜，今爲靈武建康人。
entries.en: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. His ancestors originally sprang from the Xi people; in his day Shi Xiancheng was reckoned a man of Jiankang in Lingwu.
entries.literal: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. Shi Xiancheng — his ancestors came from the Xi barbarians; he is now registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.

entries.zh: 祖道德，開府儀同三司、試太常卿、上柱國、懷澤郡王。
entries.en: His grandfather Daode had served as Grand General of the Palace with the Honorary Three Excellencies, Acting Minister of Ceremonies, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Huaize.
entries.literal: His grandfather Daode held the titles of Kaifu Yitong Sansi, Acting Taichang Qing, Shangzhuguo, and Prince of Huaize commandery.

entries.zh: 父周洛，爲魏博軍校，事田季安，至兵馬大使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞、柱國、北海郡王。
entries.en: His father Zhouluo was a Weibo army officer under Tian Ji'an and eventually rose to command the army's horse and foot, with the ranks of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Beihai.
entries.literal: His father Zhouluo was an officer in the Weibo army, served Tian Ji'an, and rose to Grand Marshal of Cavalry and Infantry, Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, and Prince of Beihai commandery.

entries.zh: 憲誠始以材勇，隨父歷軍中右職，兼監察御史。
entries.en: Xiancheng first made his name through ability and valor, serving beside his father in senior army posts while also holding the post of Investigating Censor.
entries.literal: Xiancheng began by virtue of talent and courage; following his father he held senior posts in the army and concurrently served as Investigating Censor.

entries.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。
entries.en: During the Yuanhe reign, when Tian Hongzheng marched against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng ahead with four thousand vanguard troops to cross the Yellow River and take one fortified camp after another.
entries.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng to cross the river with four thousand vanguard troops, repeatedly capturing his fortified camps.

entries.zh: 復以大軍齊進，乘勢逐北，魏之全師迫於鄆之城下。
entries.en: The main army then advanced in concert, riding the momentum of victory in a northward pursuit until Wei's full force was pinned beneath the walls of Yan.
entries.literal: Then with the main force advancing together, they seized the momentum to pursue northward, pressing Wei's entire army to the walls of Yan prefecture.

entries.zh: 師道窮蹙，劉悟斬首投魏軍。
entries.en: With Shidao driven to desperation, Liu Wu cut off his head and presented it to the Wei forces.
entries.literal: Shidao was cornered; Liu Wu beheaded him and surrendered the head to the Wei army.

entries.zh: 錄功，超授憲誠兼中丞。
entries.en: When his merits were entered on the rolls, Xiancheng was promoted out of turn to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: His achievements were recorded, and Xiancheng was exceptionally promoted to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 孝章歷三鎮，雖無異績，而謹身畏法，以保初終。
entries.en: Xiaozhang held three commands; though he won no striking victories, he kept himself within the law and preserved his position from first to last.
entries.literal: Xiaozhang governed three commands; though he had no outstanding achievements, he was scrupulous in conduct and feared the law, thereby preserving himself from beginning to end.

entries.zh: 開成三年十月卒，贈右僕射。
entries.en: He died in the tenth month of the third year of Kaicheng and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He died in the tenth month of the third year of Kaicheng and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 何進滔，靈武人也。
entries.en: He Jintao came from Lingwu.
entries.literal: He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.

entries.zh: 曾祖孝物，祖俊，並本州軍校。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and his grandfather Jun had both been army officers in their home prefecture.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun were both army officers of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 父默，夏州衙前兵馬使，檢校太子賓客，試太常卿。
entries.en: His father Mo had served as horse-and-foot commissioner before the Xiazhou yamen, with the ranks of Acting Crown Prince's Guest and Acting Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: His father Mo was Cavalry and Infantry Commissioner before the Xiazhou yamen, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, and Acting Taichang Qing.

entries.zh: 以進滔之貴，贈左散騎常侍。
entries.en: When Jintao rose to high rank, Mo was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: Because of Jintao's eminence, Mo was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 進滔客寄於魏，委質軍門，事節度使田弘正。
entries.en: Jintao had settled in Wei as an outsider, pledged himself to the army, and served under the military governor Tian Hongzheng.
entries.literal: Jintao lived as a guest in Wei, pledged himself to the army gate, and served the military governor Tian Hongzheng.

entries.zh: 弘正奉詔討鄆州，破李師道，時進滔爲衙內都知兵馬使，以功授兼侍御史。
entries.en: When Hongzheng marched on Yanzhou by imperial order and broke Li Shidao, Jintao was chief controller of horse and foot in the headquarters guard and was made concurrent Attending Censor for his service.
entries.literal: Hongzheng received the edict to campaign against Yanzhou and defeated Li Shidao; at the time Jintao was Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry within the headquarters guard, and for his merit was appointed concurrent Attending Censor.

entries.zh: 太和三年，軍眾害史憲誠，連聲而呼曰：「得衙內都知兵馬使何端公知留後，即三軍安矣。」
entries.en: In the third year of Taihe the soldiers killed Shi Xiancheng and cried out together, "Let Lord He, the chief controller of the headquarters guard, take charge as acting governor, and the three armies will be settled."
entries.literal: In the third year of Taihe the troops killed Shi Xiancheng and shouted in unison: "If the Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry within the headquarters guard, Lord He of Duan, becomes acting military governor, the three armies will be at peace."

entries.zh: 推而立之。
entries.en: They pressed him forward and set him up as their leader.
entries.literal: They pushed him forward and installed him.

entries.zh: 朝廷因授進滔左散騎常侍、魏博等州節度觀察處置等使。
entries.en: The court thereupon appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Weibo and the associated prefectures.
entries.literal: The court accordingly appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Military Governor, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of Weibo and other prefectures.

entries.zh: 爲魏帥十餘年，大得民情，累官至司徒、平章事卒。
entries.en: He commanded Wei for more than ten years and won deep popular affection, rose through the ranks to Grand Tutor and Grand Councilor, and died in office.
entries.literal: He was military governor of Wei for more than ten years, greatly winning the people's hearts, rose in office to Grand Tutor and Grand Councilor, and died.

entries.zh: 進滔子 弘敬子弘敬襲其位。
entries.en: Jintao's son Hongjing succeeded to his father's post.
entries.literal: Jintao's son Hongjing — Hongjing succeeded to his position.

entries.zh: 朝廷時遣河中帥李執方、滄州帥劉約各遣使勸令歸闕，別俟朝旨。
entries.en: The court had Li Zhifang of Hezhong and Liu Yue of Cangzhou each send envoys urging him to come to court and await further imperial orders.
entries.literal: The court at the time had the commanders of Hezhong, Li Zhifang, and Cangzhou, Liu Yue, each send envoys urging him to return to court and await separate court orders.

entries.zh: 弘敬不從，竟就加節制。
entries.en: Hongjing refused, and in the end received the full command baton anyway.
entries.literal: Hongjing did not comply and in the end received the full military commission.

entries.zh: 及劉稹反，不時起兵。
entries.en: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he failed to mobilize his troops promptly.
entries.literal: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he did not raise troops at the proper time.

entries.zh: 鎮州王元逵下邢、洺二州，兵次上黨，弘敬方出師壓境。
entries.en: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou had already taken Xing and Ming and halted his army at Shangdang before Hongjing at last marched out to menace the frontier.
entries.literal: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou took the two prefectures of Xing and Ming; his troops halted at Shangdang, and only then did Hongjing march out to press the border.

entries.zh: 大中後，宣宗務其姑息，繼加官爵，亦至使相。
entries.en: After the Dazhong reign, Emperor Xuanzong treated him with deliberate indulgence, heaping rank upon rank until he too stood among the commissioners who held councilor titles.
entries.literal: After the Dazhong era, Emperor Xuanzong pursued a policy of indulgence toward him, repeatedly adding offices and titles until he too reached the rank of commissioner and councilor.

entries.zh: 咸通初，卒。
entries.en: Early in the Xiantong reign he died.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he died.

entries.zh: 子全皞嗣之。
entries.en: His son Quanhao succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Quanhao succeeded him.

entries.zh: 朝廷尋降符節，累官亦至同平章事。
entries.en: The court soon granted him the commander's seal and baton, and in time he too rose to Concurrent Grand Councilor.
