entries.literal: The court soon bestowed the seal and baton; through successive promotions he too reached Concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 十一年，爲軍人所害。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Xiantong his own soldiers killed him.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he was killed by the soldiers.

entries.zh: 子孫相繼，四十餘年。
entries.en: Father and son held the post in succession for more than forty years.
entries.literal: Father and son succeeded one another for more than forty years.

entries.zh: 韓允忠，魏州人也。
entries.en: Han Yunzhong came from Weizhou.
entries.literal: Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 舊名君雄，懿宗改賜今名。
entries.en: He had formerly been called Junxiong; Emperor Yizong granted him his present name.
entries.literal: His former name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong changed and bestowed his present name.

entries.zh: 父國昌，歷本州右職。
entries.en: His father Guochang had held senior posts in the prefecture.
entries.literal: His father Guochang held senior posts in the prefecture.

entries.zh: 會昌中，從何弘敬破劉稹，以功爲貝州刺史、兼御史中丞。
entries.en: During the Huichang reign he followed He Hongjing in the defeat of Liu Zhen and for his service was made prefect of Bei and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the Huichang era he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen and for his merit was made Prefect of Bei and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 以允忠故，累贈兵部尚書。
entries.en: On Yunzhong's account, Guochang was repeatedly promoted posthumously to Minister of War.
entries.literal: Because of Yunzhong, Guochang was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Minister of War.

entries.zh: 允忠少仕軍門，繼升裨校。
entries.en: Yunzhong entered military service young and rose through the ranks to staff officer.
entries.literal: Yunzhong entered the army gate in youth and was promoted in succession to staff officer.

entries.zh: 潞州之役，亦與其行。
entries.en: He also took part in the campaign against Luzhou.
entries.literal: In the Luzhou campaign he also marched with the army.

entries.zh: 咸通十一年，何全皞爲軍眾所殺，推允忠爲帥。
entries.en: In the eleventh year of Xiantong, when He Quanhao was killed by his soldiers, they set Yunzhong up as their leader.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Xiantong, He Quanhao was killed by the troops, and they pushed Yunzhong forward as commander.

entries.zh: 時僖宗爲普王，即降詔遙領節度，授允忠左散騎常侍、兼御史中丞，充節度觀察留後。
entries.en: Emperor Xizong was then still Prince of Pu; an edict at once named him to hold the command in absentia and appointed Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and acting military governor and observation commissioner.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was Prince of Pu; an edict was immediately issued appointing him to hold the military governorship in absentia, and Yunzhong was made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Acting Military Governor and Observation Commissioner.

entries.zh: 不數月，轉檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史、充魏博節度觀察等使。
entries.en: Within a few months he was made Acting Minister of Public Works, chief administrator of the superior prefecture of Weizhou, and military governor and observation commissioner of Weibo.
entries.literal: Within a few months he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of the Superior Prefecture of Weizhou, and Military Governor and Observation Commissioner of Weibo.

entries.zh: 累加至檢校司空、同平章事。
entries.en: He rose in time to Acting Grand Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Acting Grand Minister of Works and Concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 乾符元年十一月卒，年六十一。
entries.en: He died in the eleventh month of the first year of Qianfu, at the age of sixty-one.
entries.literal: He died in the eleventh month of the first year of Qianfu, aged sixty-one.

entries.zh: 累贈太尉。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted posthumously to Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 允忠子 簡子簡，自允忠初授戎帥，便爲節度副使。
entries.en: Yunzhong's son Jian had served as deputy military governor from the moment his father first took command.
entries.literal: Yunzhong's son Jian — Jian, from the time Yunzhong first received the military command, served as deputy military governor.

entries.zh: 乾符初，累官至檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: By the opening of the Qianfu reign he had risen to Acting Minister of Public Works.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu he had risen in office to Acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 允忠卒，即起復爲節度觀察留後。
entries.en: When Yunzhong died, Jian was recalled from mourning at once to serve as acting military governor and observation commissioner.
entries.literal: When Yunzhong died, Jian was immediately recalled from mourning to serve as Acting Military Governor and Observation Commissioner.

entries.zh: 逾月，加檢校右僕射。
entries.en: After a month he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: After more than a month he was added Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 其後累加至侍中，封昌黎郡王。
entries.en: He was later promoted to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli.
entries.literal: Thereafter he was promoted in succession to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli commandery.

entries.zh: 賊巢之亂，諸葛爽受其偽命河陽節度使。
entries.en: During Huang Chao's rebellion, Zhuge Shuang accepted a bogus appointment from him as military governor of Heyang.
entries.literal: During the rebellion of the bandit Huang Chao, Zhuge Shuang received from him a false appointment as military governor of Heyang.

entries.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，寇盜蜂起，簡據有六州，甲兵強盛，竊懷僭亂之志，且欲啟其封疆，乃舉兵攻河陽，爽棄城而走。
entries.en: The emperor was then in Shu while rebels swarmed the land. Jian held six prefectures and a powerful army; nursing secret ambitions of rebellion and eager to enlarge his domain, he marched on Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; bandits and robbers swarmed forth. Jian held six prefectures, his armor and troops were strong, and he secretly harbored ambitions of usurpation and wished to expand his territory; he therefore raised troops to attack Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 簡遂留兵保守，因北掠邢、洺而歸，遂移軍攻鄆。
entries.en: Jian left troops to hold Heyang, raided north through Xing and Ming, then turned his army against Yan.
entries.literal: Jian then left troops to hold and defend the place, raided north through Xing and Ming and returned, then shifted his army to attack Yan.

entries.zh: 鄆帥曹全晸出戰，爲簡所敗，死之。
entries.en: Cao Quanzhen, governor of Yan, marched out to meet him, was defeated, and was killed.
entries.literal: Cao Quanzhen, military governor of Yan, went out to battle and was defeated by Jian and killed.

entries.zh: 鄆將崔君裕收合殘眾，保鄆州。
entries.en: The Yan officer Cui Junyu rallied the survivors and held Yanzhou.
entries.literal: The Yan general Cui Junyu gathered the scattered remnants and held Yan prefecture.

entries.zh: 簡進攻其城，半年不下，河陽復爲諸葛爽所襲。
entries.en: Jian besieged the city for half a year without success, while Heyang was seized again by Zhuge Shuang.
entries.literal: Jian pressed the attack on the city for half a year without taking it; Heyang was again seized by Zhuge Shuang.

entries.zh: 簡因欲先討君裕，次及河陽，乃舉兵至鄆，君裕請降。
entries.en: Jian resolved to deal with Junyu first and Heyang afterward; he marched on Yan, and Junyu offered to surrender.
entries.literal: Jian therefore wished first to subdue Junyu and afterward deal with Heyang; he raised troops and came to Yan, and Junyu requested surrender.

entries.zh: 尋移軍復攻河陽，行及新鄕，爲爽軍逆擊，敗之。
entries.en: He soon marched on Heyang again, but near Xinxiang, Shuang's troops met him head-on and routed him.
entries.literal: Soon he shifted his army to attack Heyang again; when he reached Xinxing he was struck in counterattack by Shuang's army and defeated.

entries.zh: 簡單騎奔回，憂憤。
entries.en: Jian fled back alone on horseback, sick with grief and rage.
entries.literal: Jian fled back alone on horseback, stricken with grief and anger.

entries.zh: 疽發背而卒，時中和元年十一月也。
entries.en: A carbuncle broke out between his shoulders and he died, in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.
entries.literal: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died — this was in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.

entries.zh: 樂彥禎，魏州人也。
entries.en: Le Yanzhen came from Weizhou.
entries.literal: Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 父少寂，歷澶、博、貝三州刺史，贈工部尚書。
entries.en: His father Shaoji had governed Chan, Bo, and Bei in turn and was posthumously made Minister of Public Works.
entries.literal: His father Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei, and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 彥禎少爲本州軍校。
entries.en: Yanzhen began his career as an army officer in his home prefecture.
entries.literal: In youth Yanzhen was an army officer of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 韓簡之領節旄也，以彥禎爲馬歩軍都虞候，轉博州刺史。
entries.en: When Han Jian took command, he made Yanzhen chief commandant of the horse and foot armies and later made him prefect of Bo.
entries.literal: When Han Jian held the command baton, he made Yanzhen Chief Commandant of Horse and Foot Armies and then transferred him to be Prefect of Bo.

entries.zh: 下河陽，走諸葛爽。
entries.en: He captured Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang from the field.
entries.literal: He took Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang to flight.

entries.zh: 有功，遷澶州刺史。
entries.en: For this service he was transferred to Chan.
entries.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Prefect of Chan.

entries.zh: 簡再討河陽之敗也。
entries.en: This was during Han Jian's second, failed campaign against Heyang.
entries.literal: This was when Jian again campaigned against Heyang and was defeated.

entries.zh: 彥禎以一軍先歸，魏人遂共立之。
entries.en: Yanzhen brought one division home ahead of the rest, and the men of Wei promptly set him up as their leader.
entries.literal: Yanzhen returned first with one army, and the people of Wei thereupon jointly installed him.

entries.zh: 朝廷尋授檢校工部尚書，知魏博留後。
entries.en: The court soon made him Acting Minister of Public Works and acting governor of Weibo.
entries.literal: The court soon appointed him Acting Minister of Works and Acting Military Governor of Weibo.

entries.zh: 俄加戸部尚書，充節度觀察處置等使。
entries.en: He was soon made Minister of Revenue and full military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner.
entries.literal: Soon he was added Minister of Revenue and made Military Governor, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner.

entries.zh: 中和四年，累加至尚書左僕射、同平章事。
entries.en: By the fourth year of Zhonghe he had risen to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhonghe he was promoted in succession to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 僖宗自蜀回，加開府儀同三司，冊拜司徒。
entries.en: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen received the honorary rank of Grand General of the Palace with the Three Excellencies and was enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen was added Grand General of the Palace with the Honorary Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 彥禎危憤而卒，眾推都將趙文㺹知留後事。
entries.en: Yanzhen died, broken with anger and fear; the troops set up the chief commander Zhao Wenqing to manage affairs as acting governor.
entries.literal: Yanzhen died in distress and indignation; the masses pushed forward the chief commander Zhao Wenqing to handle affairs as acting governor.

entries.zh: 從訓自相州領兵三萬餘人至城下，文㺹按兵不出。
entries.en: Congxun marched from Xiang with more than thirty thousand men and halted beneath the walls; Wenqing kept his army inside and refused battle.
entries.literal: Congxun led more than thirty thousand men from Xiang to the city walls; Wenqing held his troops and would not come out.

entries.zh: 眾懷疑懼，復害文㺹，推羅弘信爲帥。
entries.en: The army grew fearful and restless; they killed Wenqing in turn and set up Luo Hongxin as commander.
entries.literal: The masses were suspicious and afraid; they again killed Wenqing and pushed Luo Hongxin forward as commander.

entries.zh: 弘信以兵出戰，敗之。
entries.en: Hongxin took the field and defeated him.
entries.literal: Hongxin went out to battle with troops and defeated him.

entries.zh: 從訓招集餘眾，次於洹水。
entries.en: Congxun rallied his survivors and encamped on the Huan River.
entries.literal: Congxun gathered the scattered remnants and encamped at the Huan River.

entries.zh: 弘信遣將程公佐領兵討擊，大敗之，梟從訓首於軍門，時文德元年春也。
entries.en: Hongxin sent Cheng Gongzuo in pursuit, routed him utterly, and displayed Congxun's head before the army gate in the spring of the first year of Wende.
entries.literal: Hongxin sent the general Cheng Gongzuo to lead troops in pursuit and attack; he inflicted a great defeat and displayed Congxun's head at the army gate — this was in the spring of the first year of Wende.

entries.zh: 羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄕人。
entries.en: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, came from Guixiang in Weizhou.
entries.literal: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, was a man of Guixiang in Weizhou.

entries.zh: 曾祖秀，祖珍，父讓，皆爲本州軍校。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been army officers in the prefecture.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been army officers of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 弘信少從戎役，歷事節度使韓簡、樂彥禎。
entries.en: Hongxin entered military service young and served in turn under Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.
entries.literal: In youth Hongxin followed military service and successively served the military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.

entries.zh: 光啟末，彥禎子從訓忌牙軍，出居於外，軍眾廢彥禎，推趙文㺹權主軍州事。
entries.en: Late in the Guangqi reign, Congxun, fearing the yajiun, withdrew to an outside post; the soldiers deposed Yanzhen and set Zhao Wenqing to govern the circuit provisionally.
entries.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun, fearing the yajiun, went out to live elsewhere; the troops deposed Yanzhen and pushed Zhao Wenqing to provisionally govern the army and prefecture.

entries.zh: 眾復以爲不便，因推弘信爲帥。
entries.en: The troops soon found this arrangement unsatisfactory and set up Hongxin instead.
entries.literal: The masses again found this unsuitable and therefore pushed Hongxin forward as commander.

entries.zh: 先是，有鄰人密謂弘信曰：「某嘗夜遇一白鬚翁，相告雲，君當爲土地主。
entries.en: Earlier a neighbor had told him in private, "One night I met a white-bearded old man who said you would become lord of this land.
entries.literal: Earlier a neighbor had secretly told Hongxin: "I once met a white-bearded old man at night who told me that you would become master of the land.

entries.zh: 如是者再三。」
entries.en: He said it again and again."
entries.literal: This happened again and again."

entries.zh: 弘信竊異之。
entries.en: Hongxin kept the story to himself and wondered at it.
entries.literal: Hongxin secretly marveled at this.

entries.zh: 及廢文㺹，軍人聚呼曰：「孰願爲節度使者？」
entries.en: When Wenqing was removed, the soldiers cried out together, "Who will be military governor?"
entries.literal: When Wenqing was deposed, the soldiers gathered and shouted: "Who wishes to be military governor?"

entries.zh: 弘信即應之曰：「白鬚翁早以命我。」
entries.en: Hongxin answered at once, "The white-bearded old man appointed me long ago."
entries.literal: Hongxin immediately answered: "The white-bearded old man long ago commanded me."

entries.zh: 眾乃環而視之，曰：「可也。」
entries.en: The men ringed him round and said, "He will do."
entries.literal: The masses then surrounded and looked at him, saying: "He will do."

entries.zh: 由是立之。
entries.en: So they set him up as their leader.
entries.literal: Thereupon they installed him.

entries.zh: 僖宗聞之，文德元年四月，詔加工部尚書，權知節度留後。
entries.en: When Emperor Xizong learned of it, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende he was made Minister of Public Works and authorized as acting military governor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xizong heard of this, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende an edict added the post of Minister of Works and authorized him to act as Acting Military Governor.

entries.zh: 七月，復加金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博節度觀察處置等使。
entries.en: In the seventh month he was further made Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Weibo.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he was again added Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Military Governor, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of Weibo.

entries.zh: 龍紀中，加檢校司空、同平章事，封豫章郡公。
entries.en: During the Longji reign he was made Acting Grand Minister of Works, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Duke of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: In the Longji era he was added Acting Grand Minister of Works, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang commandery.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，朱全忠急攻兗鄆，朱瑄求援於太原。
entries.en: During Qianning, Zhu Quanzhong pressed Yan and Yun hard, and Zhu Xuan appealed to Taiyuan for help.
entries.literal: In the Qianning era Zhu Quanzhong pressed the attack on Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 太原發軍，假道於魏，令大將李存信屯莘縣。
entries.en: Taiyuan marched an army through Wei and stationed the great general Li Cunxin at Shen county.
entries.literal: Taiyuan sent out an army and asked passage through Wei; the great general Li Cunxin was stationed at Shen county.

entries.zh: 存信御軍無法，侵魏之芻牧，弘信不平之。
entries.en: Cunxin kept poor discipline and plundered Wei's fodder and pasture, to Hongxin's anger.
entries.literal: Cunxin governed his troops without discipline and encroached on Wei's fodder and pasture; Hongxin was displeased.

entries.zh: 全忠復遣人謂之曰：「太原志吞河朔，回戈之日，貴道堪憂。」
entries.en: Quanzhong sent word again: "Taiyuan means to swallow the Hebei region; when it turns homeward, your circuit will be in peril."
entries.literal: Quanzhong again sent someone to tell him: "Taiyuan intends to swallow the Hebei region; on the day it turns its spears back, your circuit will be in peril."

entries.zh: 弘信乃托好於汴，出師三萬攻存信，敗之。
entries.en: Hongxin therefore courted Bian, marched out thirty thousand men against Cunxin, and defeated him.
entries.literal: Hongxin therefore made a show of friendship with Bian and marched out thirty thousand men to attack Cunxin and defeated him.

entries.zh: 太原怒，舉兵攻魏，營於觀音門外。
entries.en: Taiyuan was furious, marched on Wei, and encamped outside the Guanyin Gate.
entries.literal: Taiyuan was enraged and raised troops to attack Wei, encamping outside the Guanyin Gate.

entries.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。
entries.en: Ge Congzhou of Bian came to his relief and encamped on the Huan River.
entries.literal: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to his aid and encamped at the Huan River.

entries.zh: 李克用子落落時爲鐵林軍使，爲從周所擒，乃退歸。
entries.en: Li Keyong's son Luoluo, then commander of the Iron Forest Army, was captured by Congzhou, and Taiyuan withdrew.
entries.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo was then Iron Forest Army commander; he was captured by Congzhou and Taiyuan then withdrew.

entries.zh: 自是太原之師，每歲侵擾相、魏，魏人患之。
entries.en: Thereafter Taiyuan raided Xiang and Wei year after year, to the great distress of the Wei people.
entries.literal: From this time the armies of Taiyuan each year harassed Xiang and Wei, and the people of Wei suffered from them.

entries.zh: 朱全忠方事兗鄆，懼弘信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮答貺。
entries.en: Quanzhong was then busy with Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin might waver; every season he sent gifts, and Hongxin always replied with humble words and lavish return gifts.
entries.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then engaged with Yan and Yun and feared that Hongxin might turn aside; every year at the seasons he sent gifts, and Hongxin always answered with humble words and generous return gifts.

entries.zh: 全忠對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予倍年已上，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。」
entries.en: Quanzhong would face north and bow to receive Wei's gifts, saying, "Sixth Brother is more than twice my age; we are brothers in arms — how could I treat him as an ordinary neighbor?"
entries.literal: Quanzhong, facing Wei's envoy, bowed toward the north to receive the gifts and said: "Sixth Brother is more than twice my age; we are a state of brothers — how can I treat him as an ordinary neighbor?"

entries.zh: 弘信以爲厚己，亦推心焉。
entries.en: Hongxin took this as genuine regard and gave Quanzhong his full trust in return.
entries.literal: Hongxin thought he was treating him generously and also gave him his full trust.

entries.zh: 弘信累官至檢校太師、守侍中、臨清王。
entries.en: Hongxin rose in time to Acting Grand Preceptor, Defender Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.
entries.literal: Hongxin rose in office to Acting Grand Preceptor, Defender Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.

entries.zh: 光化元年九月卒，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。
entries.en: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua at sixty-three; the court posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, Prince of Beiping, with the posthumous title Zhuangsu.
entries.literal: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua, aged sixty-three; posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping, and given the posthumous title Zhuangsu.

entries.zh: 子威。
entries.en: His son was Wei.
entries.literal: His son was Wei.

entries.zh: 弘信子 威威，字端己。
entries.en: Hongxin's son Wei, styled Duanji.
entries.literal: Hongxin's son Wei — Wei, styled Duanji.

entries.zh: 文德初，授左散騎常侍，充天雄軍節度副使。
entries.en: At the opening of Wende he was made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and deputy military governor of the Tianxiong Army.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wende he was appointed Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and deputy military governor of the Tianxiong Army.

entries.zh: 自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中，累加官爵。
entries.en: From Longji through Qianning he accumulated rank upon rank for ten years.
entries.literal: From Longji through Qianning, within ten years he was repeatedly promoted in office and rank.

entries.zh: 弘信卒，襲父位爲留後，朝廷從而命之。
entries.en: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded as acting governor, and the court confirmed the appointment.
entries.literal: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded to his father's post as acting governor, and the court accordingly appointed him.

entries.zh: 天復末，累加至檢校太傅、兼侍中、長沙王。
entries.en: By the end of Tianfu he had risen to Acting Grand Tutor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianfu he was promoted in succession to Acting Grand Tutor, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.

entries.zh: 天祐初，授檢校太尉、守侍中，進封鄴王，賜號「忠勤宣力致理功臣」。
entries.en: Early in Tianyou he was made Acting Grand Preceptor and Defender Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence in Ordering the Realm."
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was appointed Acting Grand Preceptor, Defender Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence in Ordering the Realm."

entries.zh: 天祐二年七月十三日夜，牙軍裨校李公佺作亂，威僅以身免。
entries.en: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month in the second year of Tianyou, the yajiun officer Li Gongquan rebelled, and Wei barely escaped with his life.
entries.literal: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month of the second year of Tianyou, the yajiun staff officer Li Gongquan rebelled; Wei barely escaped with his life.

entries.zh: 公佺出奔滄州。
entries.en: Gongquan fled to Cangzhou.
entries.literal: Gongquan fled to Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 自是愈懼，遣使求援於全忠，密謀破之。
entries.en: Thereafter Wei grew ever more fearful, sent to Quanzhong for help, and secretly plotted their destruction.
entries.literal: From this Wei grew ever more afraid; he sent envoys to seek aid from Quanzhong and secretly plotted to destroy them.

entries.zh: 全忠遣李思安會魏博軍，再攻滄州。
entries.en: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to join the Weibo army in a renewed attack on Cangzhou.
entries.literal: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to join the Weibo army in again attacking Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 全忠女妻威子廷規，先是卒。
entries.en: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui and had died earlier.
entries.literal: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui; she had died earlier.

entries.zh: 全忠遣長直軍校馬嗣勳選兵千人，密於輿中實兵甲入魏，言助女葬事。
entries.en: Quanzhong sent Ma Cixun of the long-service guard to choose a thousand men and smuggle arms into Wei in funeral litters, under the pretext of helping bury his daughter.
entries.literal: Quanzhong sent the chief of the long-service guard Ma Cixun to select a thousand troops; arms and armor were secretly loaded in the palanquins that entered Wei, on the pretext of assisting with the daughter's funeral.

entries.zh: 三年正月五日，嗣勳至，全忠親率大軍濟河，言視行營於滄景。
entries.en: On the fifth day of the first month in the third year Cixun arrived; Quanzhong himself led a great army across the river, saying he meant to inspect the Cangjing front.
entries.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Cixun arrived; Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, saying he was going to inspect the camp at Cangjing.

entries.zh: 威欲因而出迎，至期，即假全忠帳下銳卒入而夾攻之。
entries.en: Wei planned to go out to meet him and, when the day came, borrow Quanzhong's crack troops to enter the city and strike the yajiun from within and without.
entries.literal: Wei wished to go out to meet him; when the day came he would borrow sharp troops from Quanzhong's camp to enter and strike them from both sides.

entries.zh: 牙軍頗疑，堅請不出。
entries.en: The yajiun grew suspicious and insisted he not leave the city.
entries.literal: The yajiun were quite suspicious and firmly begged him not to go out.

entries.zh: 威恐洩其事，慰納之。
entries.en: Fearing his plot would leak, Wei soothed and reassured them.
entries.literal: Wei feared the plot would leak and comforted and appeased them.

entries.zh: 是月十四日夜，率廝養百十輩，與嗣勳合攻之。
entries.en: On the night of the fourteenth he led a hundred-odd personal retainers to join Cixun in the assault.
entries.literal: On the night of the fourteenth day of that month he led a hundred or so personal attendants to join Cixun in a combined attack.

entries.zh: 時宿於牙城者千人，遲明殺之殆盡；
entries.en: A thousand yajiun were then quartered in the headquarters city; by dawn nearly all had been slaughtered;
entries.literal: At the time a thousand men were quartered in the yamen city; by dawn they had been killed almost to the last man;

entries.zh: 凡八千家，皆破其族。
entries.en: eight thousand households in all had their clans destroyed.
entries.literal: in all eight thousand households had their clans destroyed.

entries.zh: 魏軍攻滄州者，在歷亭聞有變，其將史仁遇擁之，保於高唐。
entries.en: The Wei troops besieging Cangzhou at Liting heard of the upheaval; their commander Shi Renyu held them together and defended Gaotang.
entries.literal: Those of the Wei army attacking Cangzhou, at Liting, heard of the disturbance; their commander Shi Renyu held them together and defended Gaotang.

entries.zh: 六州之內，皆爲讎敵，累月平之。
entries.en: Throughout the six prefectures every survivor became an enemy; months passed before order was restored.
entries.literal: Within the six prefectures all became enemies; it took months to pacify them.

entries.zh: 威仕梁數年後卒，年三十四，位至守太師、兼中書令，贈尚書令，謚曰貞壯。
entries.en: After several years in Liang service Wei died at thirty-four, having reached Defender Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat; the court posthumously made him Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Zhenzhuang.
entries.literal: After serving Liang for several years Wei died, aged thirty-four; in office he reached Defender Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat; posthumously he was made Director of the Secretariat and given the posthumous title Zhenzhuang.

entries.zh: 威嗣世之明年，正月，幽州劉仁恭擁兵十萬，謀亂河朔，進陷貝州，長驅攻魏。
entries.en: In the first month of the second year of Wei's rule, Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched a hundred thousand men to stir trouble in Hebei, seized Bei, and drove straight at Wei.
entries.literal: In the second year after Wei succeeded, in the first month, Liu Rengong of Youzhou gathered a hundred thousand troops, plotted disorder in the Hebei region, advanced and took Bei prefecture, and drove straight to attack Wei.

entries.zh: 威求援於汴。
entries.en: Wei appealed to Bian for help.
entries.literal: Wei sought aid from Bian.

entries.zh: 朱全忠遣將李思安屯於洹水。
entries.en: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to encamp on the Huan River.
entries.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent the general Li Si'an to encamp at the Huan River.

entries.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。
entries.en: Ge Congzhou marched in from Xing and Ming.
entries.literal: Ge Congzhou led troops from Xing and Ming into Wei.

entries.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及攻汴軍於內黃。
entries.en: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keyi attacked the Bian forces at Neihuang.
entries.literal: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keyi attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.

entries.zh: 思安逆戰，大敗之，乘勝追躡。
entries.en: Si'an met them in battle, routed them, and pursued in victory.
entries.literal: Si'an met them in battle and inflicted a great defeat, then pursued in victory.

entries.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。
entries.en: Congzhou came out to strike in concert, crushed the Yan army, and took thirty thousand heads.
entries.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a converging strike and annihilated the Yan army, beheading thirty thousand.

entries.zh: 三年，威引汴軍攻滄州以報之。
entries.en: In the third year Wei led Bian's army against Cangzhou in reprisal.
entries.literal: In the third year Wei led Bian troops to attack Cangzhou in retaliation.

entries.zh: 自是，威感全忠援助之恩，合從景附。
entries.en: From then on Wei, grateful for Quanzhong's aid, clung to him in alliance.
entries.literal: From this time Wei was moved by gratitude for Quanzhong's aid and drew close to him in alliance.

entries.zh: 史憲誠 子孝章 何進滔 子弘敬 韓允忠 子簡 樂彥禎 子從訓 羅弘信 子威
entries.en: Shi Xiancheng and his son Xiaozhang; He Jintao and his son Hongjing; Han Yunzhong and his son Jian; Le Yanzhen and his son Congxun; Luo Hongxin and his son Wei
entries.literal: Shi Xiancheng; his son Xiaozhang; He Jintao; his son Hongjing; Han Yunzhong; his son Jian; Le Yanzhen; his son Congxun; Luo Hongxin; his son Wei

entries.zh: 子簡，自允忠初授戎帥，便為節度副使。
entries.en: His son Jian had been made deputy military governor as soon as Yunzhong received his commission.
entries.literal: His son Jian, from when Yunzhong was first given military command, was made military governor's deputy.

entries.zh: 乾符初，累官至檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: By the beginning of the Qianfu era he had risen to Acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu, by successive offices he reached Acting Minister of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 允忠卒，即起復為節度觀察留後。
entries.en: When Yunzhong died, Jian was immediately recalled from mourning to serve as acting military governor.
entries.literal: When Yunzhong died, he was immediately recalled from mourning to be military governor, observation commissioner, and acting regent.

entries.zh: 逾月，加檢校右僕射。
entries.en: A month later he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: After more than a month he was additionally made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 其後累加至侍中，封昌黎郡王。
entries.en: He was subsequently promoted in stages to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as King of Changli.
entries.literal: Thereafter by successive additions he reached Palace Attendant and was enfeoffed as King of Changli commandery.

entries.zh: 賊巢之亂，諸葛爽受其偽命河陽節度使。
entries.en: During Huang Chao's rebellion, Zhuge Shuang accepted a bogus appointment from him as military governor of Heyang.
entries.literal: During the rebellion of the bandit Huang Chao, Zhuge Shuang received from him a false appointment as military governor of Heyang.

entries.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，寇盜蜂起，簡據有六州，甲兵強盛，竊懷僭亂之志，且欲啟其封疆，乃舉兵攻河陽，爽棄城而走。
entries.en: The emperor was then in Shu while rebels swarmed the land. Jian held six prefectures and a powerful army; nursing secret ambitions of rebellion and eager to enlarge his domain, he marched on Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; bandits and robbers swarmed forth. Jian held six prefectures, his armor and troops were strong, and he secretly harbored ambitions of usurpation and wished to expand his territory; he therefore raised troops to attack Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 簡遂留兵保守，因北掠邢、洺而歸，遂移軍攻鄆。
entries.en: Jian left troops to hold Heyang, raided north through Xing and Ming, then turned his army against Yan.
entries.literal: Jian then left troops to hold and defend the place, raided north through Xing and Ming and returned, then shifted his army to attack Yan.

entries.zh: 鄆帥曹全晸出戰，爲簡所敗，死之。
entries.en: Cao Quanzhen, governor of Yan, marched out to meet him, was defeated, and was killed.
entries.literal: Cao Quanzhen, military governor of Yan, went out to battle and was defeated by Jian and killed.

entries.zh: 鄆將崔君裕收合殘眾，保鄆州。
entries.en: The Yan officer Cui Junyu rallied the survivors and held Yanzhou.
entries.literal: The Yan general Cui Junyu gathered the scattered remnants and held Yan prefecture.

entries.zh: 簡進攻其城，半年不下，河陽復爲諸葛爽所襲。
entries.en: Jian besieged the city for half a year without success, while Heyang was seized again by Zhuge Shuang.
entries.literal: Jian pressed the attack on the city for half a year without taking it; Heyang was again seized by Zhuge Shuang.

entries.zh: 簡因欲先討君裕，次及河陽，乃舉兵至鄆，君裕請降。
entries.en: Jian resolved to deal with Junyu first and Heyang afterward; he marched on Yan, and Junyu offered to surrender.
entries.literal: Jian therefore wished first to subdue Junyu and afterward deal with Heyang; he raised troops and came to Yan, and Junyu requested surrender.

entries.zh: 尋移軍復攻河陽，行及新鄕，爲爽軍逆擊，敗之。
entries.en: He soon marched on Heyang again, but near Xinxing Shuang's troops met him head-on and routed him.
entries.literal: Soon he shifted his army to attack Heyang again; when he reached Xinxing he was struck in counterattack by Shuang's army and defeated.

entries.zh: 簡單騎奔回，憂憤。
entries.en: Jian fled back alone on horseback, sick with grief and rage.
entries.literal: Jian fled back alone on horseback, stricken with grief and anger.

entries.zh: 疽發背而卒，時中和元年十一月也。
entries.en: A carbuncle broke out between his shoulders and he died, in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.
entries.literal: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died — this was in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.

entries.zh: 樂彥禎，魏州人也。
entries.en: Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.
entries.literal: Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 父少寂，歷澶、博、貝三州刺史，贈工部尚書。
entries.en: His father Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei in turn and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
entries.literal: His father Shaoji passed through the three prefectures of Chan, Bo, and Bei as prefect, and was posthumously given Minister of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 彥禎少為本州軍校。
entries.en: Yanzhen had been a regimental officer in the local army from youth.
entries.literal: Yanzhen from youth was a military officer of the native prefecture.

entries.zh: 韓簡之領節旄也，以彥禎為馬步軍都虞候，轉博州刺史。
entries.en: When Han Jian took command, he made Yanzhen chief commandant of cavalry and infantry, then transferred him to prefect of Bo.
entries.literal: When Han Jian received the commander's banner and staff, he made Yanzhen Chief Commandant of Cavalry and Infantry, then transferred him to prefect of Bo.

entries.zh: 下河陽，走諸葛爽。
entries.en: He attacked Heyang and drove off Zhuge Shuang.
entries.literal: He descended on Heyang and drove off Zhuge Shuang.

entries.zh: 有功，遷澶州刺史。
entries.en: For this achievement he was transferred to prefect of Chan.
entries.literal: For merit he was transferred to prefect of Chan.

entries.zh: 簡再討河陽之敗也。
entries.en: This was during Han Jian's second failed campaign against Heyang.
entries.literal: This was when Jian again campaigned against Heyang and was defeated.

entries.zh: 彥禎以一軍先歸，魏人遂共立之。
entries.en: Yanzhen brought his division home first, and the Wei troops thereupon acclaimed him as their commander.
entries.literal: Yanzhen with one army returned first; the Wei people thereupon jointly installed him.

entries.zh: 朝廷尋授檢校工部尚書，知魏博留後。
entries.en: The court soon appointed him Acting Minister of Works and acting regent of Wei-Bo.
entries.literal: The court soon appointed him Acting Minister of Works and acting regent of Wei-Bo.

entries.zh: 俄加戶部尚書，充節度觀察處置等使。
entries.en: He was soon made Minister of Revenue and full military governor of Wei-Bo.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally made Minister of Revenue and military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner.

entries.zh: 中和四年，累加至尚書左僕射、同平章事。
entries.en: In Zhonghe 4 he rose in due course to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: In Zhonghe year four he was by successive additions made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 僖宗自蜀回，加開府儀同三司，冊拜司徒。
entries.en: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen was made Grand General with Honorary Staff of Three Offices and ceremonially appointed Minister of Education.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu he was additionally made Grand General with Honorary Staff of Three Offices and ceremonially appointed Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄉人。
entries.en: Luo Hongxin, courtesy name Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.
entries.literal: Luo Hongxin, style Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.

entries.zh: 曾祖秀，祖珍，父讓，皆為本州軍校。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been military officers in the local army.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang were all military officers of the native prefecture.

entries.zh: 弘信少從戎役，歷事節度使韓簡、樂彥禎。
entries.en: Hongxin entered military service young and served under the military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.
entries.literal: Hongxin from youth followed military service and successively served military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.

entries.zh: 光啟末，彥禎子從訓忌牙軍，出居於外，軍眾廢彥禎，推趙文㺹權主軍州事。
entries.en: At the end of the Guangqi era, Yanzhen's son Congxun, fearing the yamen guard, moved outside the city. The troops deposed Yanzhen and put Zhao Wenkan in charge of military and civil affairs.
entries.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun feared the yamen guard army, went out to reside elsewhere, the army masses deposed Yanzhen, and pushed Zhao Wenkan to hold military and prefectural affairs in authority.

entries.zh: 眾復以為不便，因推弘信為帥。
entries.en: The troops soon found this arrangement unsatisfactory and acclaimed Hongxin as their commander instead.
entries.literal: The masses again thought this inconvenient and therefore pushed Hongxin as commander.

entries.zh: 先是，有鄰人密謂弘信曰：「某嘗夜遇一白鬚翁，相告雲，君當為土地主。
entries.en: Earlier a neighbor had told Hongxin in secret, "One night I met a white-bearded old man who said to me, 'Your neighbor shall be lord of this land.
entries.literal: Earlier a neighbor secretly told Hongxin: "I once at night met a white-bearded old man who told me, saying, 'You shall be lord of this land.

entries.zh: 如是者再三。」
entries.en: This happened again and again.'"
entries.literal: It was like this three or four times.'"

entries.zh: 弘信竊異之。
entries.en: Hongxin had privately wondered at this.
entries.literal: Hongxin privately marveled at this.

entries.zh: 及廢文㺹，軍人聚呼曰：「孰願為節度使者？」
entries.en: When Wenkan was removed, the soldiers gathered and shouted, "Who will be military governor?"
entries.literal: When Wenkan was deposed the military men gathered and shouted: "Who wishes to be military governor?"

entries.zh: 弘信即應之曰：「白鬚翁早以命我。」
entries.en: Hongxin answered at once, "The white-bearded old man long ago destined me for it."
entries.literal: Hongxin at once responded: "The white-bearded old man long ago commanded me."

entries.zh: 眾乃環而視之，曰：「可也。」
entries.en: The men surrounded him and said, "He will do."
entries.literal: The masses then encircled and looked at him, saying: "He will do."

entries.zh: 由是立之。
entries.en: On that basis they installed him.
entries.literal: Thereby he was installed.

entries.zh: 僖宗聞之，文德元年四月，詔加工部尚書，權知節度留後。
entries.en: When Emperor Xizong learned of this, in the fourth month of Wende 1 he was made Minister of Works and acting military governor.
entries.literal: Emperor Xizong heard of it; in the fourth month of Wende year one an edict additionally made him Minister of Works and acting military governor regent.

entries.zh: 七月，復加金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博節度觀察處置等使。
entries.en: In the seventh month he was made Golden-Gleam Glory Grand Master, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and full military governor of Wei-Bo.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he was again given Golden-Gleam Glory Grand Master and Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, serving as Wei-Bo military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner.

entries.zh: 龍紀中，加檢校司空、同平章事，封豫章郡公。
entries.en: During the Longji era he was made Acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: In the Longji reign he was additionally made Acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang commandery.

entries.zh: 史憲誠，其先出於奚虜，今為靈武建康人。
entries.en: Shi Xiancheng's family originally came from the Xi people; he was registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.
entries.literal: Shi Xiancheng—his ancestors came from the Xi barbarians; he is now registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.

entries.zh: 祖道德，開府儀同三司、試太常卿、上柱國、懷澤郡王。
entries.en: His grandfather Daode had been Grand General with Honorary Staff of Three Offices, Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supreme Pillar of State, and Duke of Huaize.
entries.literal: His grandfather Daode held the titles Grand General with Honorary Staff of Three Offices, Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supreme Pillar of State, and Duke of Huaize commandery.

entries.zh: 父周洛，為魏博軍校，事田季安，至兵馬大使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞、柱國、北海郡王。
entries.en: His father Zhou Luo had served as a Wei-Bo regimental officer under Tian Ji'an, eventually reaching Army-and-Horse Commissioner, Silver-Gleam Glory Grand Master, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, and King of Beihai.
entries.literal: His father Zhou Luo was a Wei-Bo military officer serving Tian Ji'an, rising to Army-and-Horse Commissioner, Silver-Gleam Glory Grand Master, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, and King of Beihai commandery.

entries.zh: 憲誠始以材勇，隨父歷軍中右職，兼監察御史。
entries.en: Xiancheng first distinguished himself by talent and courage, rising through senior army posts alongside his father, and also held the post of Investigating Censor.
entries.literal: Xiancheng at first by talent and valor followed his father through senior military posts, and concurrently served as Investigating Censor.

entries.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。
entries.en: During the Yuanhe era, when Tian Hongzheng marched against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng with four thousand vanguard troops across the river; they took one enemy stockade after another.
entries.literal: In the Yuanhe reign, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng with four thousand vanguard troops to cross the river, repeatedly taking their walled stockades.

entries.zh: 復以大軍齊進，乘勢逐北，魏之全師迫於鄆之城下。
entries.en: The main army then advanced in force. Riding the momentum of victory, he pursued the enemy until the entire Wei force stood before the walls of Yan.
entries.literal: Again with the main army advancing together, seizing the momentum he pursued north; Wei's full army pressed to below the walls of Yan.

entries.zh: 師道窮蹙，劉悟斬首投魏軍。
entries.en: Shidao was cornered; Liu Wu cut off his head and turned it over to the Wei forces.
entries.literal: Shidao was driven to extremity; Liu Wu beheaded him and surrendered the head to the Wei army.

entries.zh: 錄功，超授憲誠兼中丞。
entries.en: For his merit he was specially promoted to concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: Recording merit, Xiancheng was exceptionally appointed concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 子弘敬襲其位。
entries.en: His son Hongjing succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Hongjing succeeded to his position.

entries.zh: 朝廷時遣河中帥李執方、滄州帥劉約各遣使勸令歸闕，別俟朝旨。
entries.en: The court repeatedly sent envoys through Li Zhifang of Hezhong and Liu Yue of Cangzhou urging him to come to the capital and await further orders.
entries.literal: The court at times sent Hezhong commander Li Zhifang and Cangzhou commander Liu Yue each to dispatch envoys urging him to return to court and await separate court instructions.

entries.zh: 弘敬不從，竟就加節制。
entries.en: Hongjing refused, and in the end received the full commission.
entries.literal: Hongjing did not comply, and in the end was given the commissioner's control.

entries.zh: 及劉稹反，不時起兵。
entries.en: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he failed to mobilize his troops promptly.
entries.literal: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he did not raise troops at the proper time.

entries.zh: 鎮州王元逵下邢、洺二州，兵次上黨，弘敬方出師壓境。
entries.en: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou had already taken Xing and Ming, and his army had reached Shangdang, before Hongjing finally marched out to threaten the border.
entries.literal: Zhenzhou's Wang Yuankui took Xing and Ming prefectures; troops reached Shangdang; only then did Hongjing march out to press the border.

entries.zh: 大中後，宣宗務其姑息，繼加官爵，亦至使相。
entries.en: After the Dazhong era Emperor Xuanzong indulged him with successive promotions until he too reached the rank of commissioner-councilor.
entries.literal: After the Dazhong reign, Emperor Xuanzong pursued indulgent treatment of him, successively adding offices and ranks until he too reached commissioner and councilor.

entries.zh: 咸通初，卒。
entries.en: He died early in the Xiantong era (860).
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he died.

entries.zh: 子全皞嗣之。
entries.en: His son Quanhao succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Quanhao succeeded him.

entries.zh: 朝廷尋降符節，累官亦至同平章事。
entries.en: The court soon issued him the commissioner's credentials, and he too rose in due course to concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: The court soon bestowed tally and staff; by successive offices he too reached concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 十一年，為軍人所害。
entries.en: In year eleven he was killed by his own troops.
entries.literal: In year eleven he was killed by the military men.

entries.zh: 子孫相繼，四十餘年。
entries.en: Father and son had held the post in succession for more than forty years.
entries.literal: Sons and grandsons succeeded one another for more than forty years.

entries.zh: 韓允忠，魏州人也。
entries.en: Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.
entries.literal: Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 舊名君雄，懿宗改賜今名。
entries.en: His original name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong gave him his present name.
entries.literal: His former name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong changed and bestowed the present name.

entries.zh: 父國昌，歷本州右職。
entries.en: His father Guochang had held senior posts in the local army.
entries.literal: His father Guochang passed through senior posts of the native prefecture.

entries.zh: 會昌中，從何弘敬破劉稹，以功為貝州刺史、兼御史中丞。
entries.en: During the Huichang era he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen and was made prefect of Bei and concurrent Censor-in-Chief for his service.
entries.literal: In the Huichang reign he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen; for merit he became prefect of Bei prefecture and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 以允忠故，累贈兵部尚書。
entries.en: Because of Yunzhong's eminence, Guochang was posthumously promoted in stages to Minister of War.
entries.literal: Because of Yunzhong, he was by successive gifts made Minister of War.

entries.zh: 允忠少仕軍門，繼升裨校。
entries.en: Yunzhong entered military service young and rose through the ranks to deputy commander.
entries.literal: Yunzhong from youth served at the army gates and successively rose to deputy commander.

entries.zh: 潞州之役，亦與其行。
entries.en: He also took part in the Luzhou campaign.
entries.literal: In the Luzhou campaign he also went with them.

entries.zh: 咸通十一年，何全皞為軍眾所殺，推允忠為帥。
entries.en: In Xiantong 11 (870) He Quanhao was killed by his troops, who acclaimed Yunzhong as their commander.
entries.literal: In Xiantong year eleven He Quanhao was killed by the army masses; they pushed Yunzhong as commander.

entries.zh: 時僖宗為普王，即降詔遙領節度，授允忠左散騎常侍、兼御史中丞，充節度觀察留後。
entries.en: Emperor Xizong was then Prince of Pu; he immediately issued an edict appointing Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief as acting military governor and observation commissioner.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was Prince of Pu; he immediately lowered an edict to hold the military governorship from afar, appointing Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, serving as military governor, observation commissioner, and acting regent.

entries.zh: 不數月，轉檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史、充魏博節度觀察等使。
entries.en: Within a few months he was made Acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Weizhou, and full military governor of Wei-Bo.
entries.literal: Within several months he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works in the Ministry of Revenue, Chief Administrator of the Great Capital Prefecture of Weizhou, and military governor and observation commissioner of Wei-Bo.

entries.zh: 累加至檢校司空、同平章事。
entries.en: He rose in due course to Acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: By successive additions he reached Acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 乾符元年十一月卒，年六十一。
entries.en: He died in the eleventh month of Qianfu 1 (874) at the age of sixty-one.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of Qianfu year one he died, age sixty-one.

entries.zh: 累贈太尉。
entries.en: He was posthumously promoted in stages to Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: By successive gifts he was made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 乾寧中，朱全忠急攻兗鄆，朱瑄求援於太原。
entries.en: During the Qianning era Zhu Quanzhong pressed his attack on Yan and Yanzhou, and Zhu Xuan sought help from Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the Qianning reign Zhu Quanzhong urgently attacked Yan and Yanzhou; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 太原發軍，假道於魏，令大將李存信屯莘縣。
entries.en: Taiyuan sent an army through Wei by permission and stationed the great general Li Cunxin at Shen county.
entries.literal: Taiyuan dispatched troops, borrowing passage through Wei, and ordered the great general Li Cunxin to encamp at Shen county.

entries.zh: 存信御軍無法，侵魏之芻牧，弘信不平之。
entries.en: Cunxin disciplined his troops poorly and encroached on Wei's fodder and pastures. Hongxin resented this.
entries.literal: Cunxin commanded the army without discipline, encroaching on Wei's fodder and pastures; Hongxin was displeased.

entries.zh: 全忠復遣人謂之曰：「太原志吞河朔，回戈之日，貴道堪憂。」
entries.en: Quanzhong sent another envoy to warn him, "Taiyuan means to swallow all of Hebei. When they turn their spears homeward, your circuit will be in peril."
entries.literal: Quanzhong again sent a man to tell him: "Taiyuan intends to swallow Hebei; on the day they turn their spears back, your honored circuit will be cause for worry."

entries.zh: 弘信乃托好於汴，出師三萬攻存信，敗之。
entries.en: Hongxin then feigned friendship with Bian, marched thirty thousand men against Cunxin, and defeated him.
entries.literal: Hongxin thereupon pretended friendship with Bian, marched out thirty thousand to attack Cunxin, and defeated him.

entries.zh: 太原怒，舉兵攻魏，營於觀音門外。
entries.en: Taiyuan was furious and marched on Wei, encamping outside Guanyin Gate.
entries.literal: Taiyuan was enraged, raised troops to attack Wei, and encamped outside Guanyin Gate.

entries.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。
entries.en: Ge Congzhou of Bian came to his aid and encamped on the Huan River.
entries.literal: Bian's general Ge Congzhou came to aid him and encamped at Huan River.

entries.zh: 李克用子落落時為鐵林軍使，為從周所擒，乃退歸。
entries.en: Li Keyong's son Luoluo, then commander of the Iron Forest Army, was captured by Congzhou, and the Taiyuan army withdrew.
entries.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo at the time was Iron Forest Army commissioner; he was captured by Congzhou, and they then withdrew and returned.

entries.zh: 自是太原之師，每歲侵擾相、魏，魏人患之。
entries.en: Thereafter the Taiyuan army raided Xiang and Wei year after year, to the great distress of the Wei people.
entries.literal: From this the Taiyuan army every year harassed Xiang and Wei; the Wei people suffered from it.

entries.zh: 硃全忠方事兗鄆，懼弘信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮答貺。
entries.en: Quanzhong was then occupied with Yan and Yanzhou and feared Hongxin might turn against him. Every year he sent gifts, and Hongxin always replied with humble words and lavish courtesy.
entries.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then engaged with Yan and Yanzhou, feared Hongxin would turn disloyal, and every year at the seasons sent gifts; Hongxin always answered with humble words and generous courtesy in return.

entries.zh: 全忠對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予倍年已上，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。」
entries.en: Quanzhong would bow northward to Wei's envoy as he received the gifts, saying, "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my age. As brother states, how can we treat each other as ordinary neighbors?"
entries.literal: Quanzhong toward Wei's envoy bowed facing north and received it, saying: "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my years; as brother states, how can we be treated as ordinary neighbors?"

entries.zh: 弘信以為厚己，亦推心焉。
entries.en: Hongxin took this as genuine regard for himself and gave Quanzhong his trust in return.
entries.literal: Hongxin thought this showed generosity toward himself and also gave his heart in return.

entries.zh: 弘信累官至檢校太師、守侍中、臨清王。
entries.en: Hongxin rose in due course to Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Palace Attendant, and King of Linqing.
entries.literal: Hongxin by successive offices reached Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Palace Attendant, and King of Linqing.

entries.zh: 光化元年九月卒，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。
entries.en: He died in the ninth month of Guanghua 1 at the age of sixty-three. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as King of Northern Ping, and given the posthumous title Zhuangsu.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of Guanghua year one he died, age sixty-three; posthumously given Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as King of Northern Ping, posthumous title Zhuangsu.

entries.zh: 子威。
entries.en: His son was Wei.
entries.literal: His son Wei.

entries.zh: 威嗣世之明年，正月，幽州劉仁恭擁兵十萬，謀亂河朔，進陷貝州，長驅攻魏。
entries.en: In the first month of the year after Wei succeeded his father, Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched a hundred thousand men to stir trouble in Hebei, seized Bei prefecture, and drove straight at Wei.
entries.literal: In the year after Wei succeeded to his line, in the first month, Youzhou's Liu Rengong held a hundred thousand troops, plotted disorder in Hebei, advanced and took Bei prefecture, and drove straight to attack Wei.

entries.zh: 威求援於汴。
entries.en: Wei sought help from Bian.
entries.literal: Wei sought aid from Bian.

entries.zh: 硃全忠遣將李思安屯於洹水。
entries.en: Zhu Quanzhong sent the general Li Si'an to encamp on the Huan River.
entries.literal: Zhu Quanzhong dispatched the general Li Si'an to encamp at Huan River.

entries.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。
entries.en: Ge Congzhou marched from Xing and Ming into Wei.
entries.literal: Ge Congzhou from Xing and Ming led troops into Wei.

entries.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及攻汴軍於內黃。
entries.en: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.
entries.literal: Yan's generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji attacked Bian's army at Neihuang.

entries.zh: 思安逆戰，大敗之，乘勝追躡。
entries.en: Si'an met them in battle, routed them, and pursued the fleeing army.
entries.literal: Si'an met them in battle and greatly defeated them, riding victory in pursuit.

entries.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。
entries.en: Congzhou came out to join the attack from ambush, crushed the Yan army, and took thirty thousand heads.
entries.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a concealed strike, overthrew and defeated the Yan army, and beheaded thirty thousand.

entries.zh: 三年，威引汴軍攻滄州以報之。
entries.en: In the third year Wei led Bian troops against Cangzhou in retaliation.
entries.literal: In year three Wei led Bian troops to attack Cangzhou in retaliation.

entries.zh: 自是，威感全忠援助之恩，合從景附。
entries.en: From then on Wei was grateful for Quanzhong's aid and drew ever closer to him in alliance.
entries.literal: From this Wei felt Quanzhong's grace in aiding him and joined in alliance and drew close in attachment.

entries.zh: 列傳第一百三十一
entries.en: Biography 131
entries.literal: Biography 131

entries.zh: 時又有獨孤武都，謀叛王世充歸國，事覺誅死。
entries.en: At the same time there was Dugu Wudu, who plotted to defect from Wang Shichong to the Tang; the plot was discovered and he was put to death.
entries.literal: At the same time there was Dugu Wudu, who plotted to rebel against Wang Shichong and return to the Tang; the affair was discovered and he was executed.

entries.zh: 武都子師仁，年始三歲，世充以其年幼不殺，使禁掌之。
entries.en: Wudu's son Shiren was only three years old; Shichong spared him because of his youth but had him imprisoned under guard.
entries.literal: Wudu's son Shiren was only three years old; Shichong, because he was young, did not kill him but had him imprisoned and guarded.

entries.zh: 乳母王氏，號蘭英，請髡鉗，求入保養，世充許之。
entries.en: His wet nurse, Lady Wang, known as Lanying, asked to be shorn and shackled so that she might enter the prison to care for him; Shichong consented.
entries.literal: His wet nurse Wang, called Lanying, requested to be shaved and shackled in order to enter and care for him; Shichong granted this.

entries.zh: 蘭英撫育提攜，備盡筋力。
entries.en: Lanying nursed and raised him, giving every ounce of her strength.
entries.literal: Lanying nursed and raised him, exhausting all her strength.

entries.zh: 時喪亂年饑，人多鋨死，蘭英扶路乞丐捃拾。
entries.en: In those years of chaos and famine, when many starved to death, Lanying went begging along the roads and gathered whatever she could find.
entries.literal: In those times of turmoil and famine many starved to death; Lanying supported herself along the roads, begging and gathering scraps.

entries.zh: 遇有所得，便歸與師仁；
entries.en: Whatever she obtained, she brought back for Shiren;
entries.literal: Whatever she obtained she brought back for Shiren;

entries.zh: 蘭英唯啖土飲水而已。
entries.en: Lanying herself ate only dirt and drank only water.
entries.literal: Lanying herself ate only earth and drank only water.

entries.zh: 後詐采拾，乃竊師仁歸於京師。
entries.en: Later, pretending to go out gathering, she stole Shiren away and fled with him to the capital.
entries.literal: Later, pretending to go gathering, she stole Shiren away and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 高祖嘉其義，下詔曰：「師仁乳母王氏，慈惠有聞，撫鞠無倦，提攜遺幼，背逆歸朝。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu commended her loyalty and issued an edict: "Shiren's wet nurse, Lady Wang, is renowned for her kindness and grace; she reared him without rest, carried off the orphaned child, and defied the rebel regime to bring him back to the court.
entries.literal: Gaozu commended her righteousness and issued an edict: "Shiren's wet nurse Wang is known for kindness and grace; she reared him without weariness, carried off the orphaned infant, and defied the rebel to return to the court.

entries.zh: 宜有褒隆，以錫其號。
entries.en: She deserves high honor and a title in recognition of her deeds.
entries.literal: She should receive lofty commendation and be granted a title.

entries.zh: 可封永壽郡君」。
entries.en: Let her be enfeoffed as Lady of Yongshou Commandery."
entries.literal: She may be enfeoffed as Lady of Yongshou Commandery."

entries.zh: 魏衡妻王氏，梓州郪人也。
entries.en: Wei Heng's wife, Lady Wang, was a native of Qi in Zizhou.
entries.literal: The wife of Wei Heng, née Wang, was a native of Qi in Zizhou.

entries.zh: 武德初，薛仁杲舊將房企地侵掠梁郡，因獲王氏，逼而妻之。
entries.en: Early in the Wude reign, Fang Qidi, a former general of Xue Rengao, raided Liang Commandery, captured Lady Wang, and forced her to marry him.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era, Fang Qidi, a former general of Xue Rengao, raided Liang Commandery, captured Wang, and forced her to become his wife.

entries.zh: 後企地漸強盛，衡謀以城應賊。
entries.en: As Qidi grew increasingly powerful, Heng plotted to surrender the city to the rebels.
entries.literal: Later, as Qidi grew increasingly powerful, Heng plotted to surrender the city to the rebels.

entries.zh: 企地領眾將趨梁州，未至數十里，飲酒醉臥。
entries.en: Qidi led his troops toward Liangzhou; when they were still several dozen li away, he drank himself into a stupor and fell asleep.
entries.literal: Qidi led his troops toward Liangzhou; when they were still several tens of li away, he drank wine, became drunk, and lay down to sleep.

entries.zh: 王氏取其佩刀斬之，攜其首入城，賊眾乃散。
entries.en: Lady Wang took his belt knife and killed him, carried his head into the city, and the rebel forces scattered.
entries.literal: Wang took his belt knife and slew him, carried his head into the city, and the rebel host dispersed.

entries.zh: 高祖大悅，封為崇義夫人，舍衡同賊之罪。
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased; he enfeoffed her as Lady of Chongyi and pardoned Heng for his collusion with the rebels.
entries.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased, enfeoffed her as Lady of Chongyi, and pardoned Heng's crime of colluding with the rebels.

entries.zh: 女子稟陰柔之質，有從人之義。
entries.en: Women are endowed with a yielding, feminine nature and are bound by the obligation to follow others.
entries.literal: Women receive the nature of yin and softness and have the duty of following others.

entries.zh: 前代誌貞婦烈女，蓋善其能以禮自防。
entries.en: Earlier dynasties recorded chaste wives and heroic women, chiefly to commend their power to protect themselves by observing ritual propriety.
entries.literal: Former ages recorded chaste wives and fierce women, generally praising their ability to guard themselves through ritual propriety.

entries.zh: 至若失身賊庭，不汙非義；
entries.en: Then there are those who fell into the power of rebel bands yet were not stained by wrongful acts—
entries.literal: As for those who lost their persons in the rebel camp yet were not defiled by unrighteous conduct—

entries.zh: 臨白刃而慷慨，誓丹衷而激發；
entries.en: who faced naked blades with unflinching resolve and pledged their loyal hearts in passionate defiance;
entries.literal: they faced naked blades with lofty resolve and pledged their loyal hearts in passionate defiance;

entries.zh: 粉身不顧，視死如歸，雖在壯夫，恐難守節，窈窕之操，不其賢乎！
entries.en: who thought nothing of being torn limb from limb and welcomed death as a homecoming—even strong men might fail to hold such constancy. How admirable is the moral fiber of these refined women!
entries.literal: they cared not if their bodies were ground to dust and regarded death as a homecoming; even stalwart men might struggle to keep such constancy—how worthy is the conduct of these gentle women!

entries.zh: 其次梁鴻之妻，無辭偕隱，共姜之誓，不踐二庭，婦道母儀，克彰圖史，又其長也。
entries.en: Next are figures such as Liang Hong's wife, who followed her husband into seclusion without a word of protest, and Gong Jiang, who vowed never to enter a second household—their wifely virtue and maternal example are fully celebrated in the histories, and this too is their highest merit.
entries.literal: Next come Liang Hong's wife, who shared seclusion without complaint, and Gong Jiang, who swore never to enter a second household—their wifely virtue and maternal exemplars shine fully in the historical records, and this too is their excellence.

entries.zh: 末代風靡，貞行寂寥，聊播椒蘭，以貽閨壺，彤管之職，幸無忽焉！
entries.en: In these latter days morals have declined and examples of constancy grown scarce; I offer here a brief bouquet of fragrant virtue for the women's quarters—may the historian's red brush never neglect this charge!
entries.literal: In the late age customs have declined and chaste conduct grown rare; I briefly scatter pepper and orchid to bestow upon the inner quarters—may the duty of the red brush not be neglected!

entries.zh: 頡利之敗也，其部落或走薛延陀，或走西域，而來降者甚眾。
entries.en: After Jieli's defeat, some of his tribes fled to Xueyantuo or the Western Regions, but vast numbers came over to surrender.
entries.literal: When Jieli was defeated, his tribes either fled to Xueyantuo or fled to the Western Regions, while those who came to surrender were very numerous.

entries.zh: 詔議安邊之術。
entries.en: The court was ordered to debate how best to secure the northern frontier.
entries.literal: An edict ordered deliberation on methods for securing the border.

entries.zh: 朝士多言突厥恃強，擾亂中國，為日久矣。
entries.en: Many officials argued that the Turks had long relied on their strength to harass China.
entries.literal: Many court officials said the Turks had relied on their strength and disturbed China for a long time now.

entries.zh: 今天實喪之，窮來歸我，本非慕義之心。
entries.en: Heaven has now abandoned them; they come to us in desperation, not from any love of our virtue.
entries.literal: Today Heaven has truly taken them away; coming in destitution to submit to us, it is fundamentally not a heart that admires righteousness.

entries.zh: 因其歸命，分其種落，俘之河南兗、豫之地，散居州縣，各使耕織，百萬胡虜可得化為百姓，則中國有加戶之利，塞北可常空矣。
entries.en: We should take advantage of their submission to break up their clans, resettle them south of the Yellow River in Yanzhou and Yuzhou, and scatter them among the prefectures to farm and weave. A million barbarian captives could become ordinary subjects, China would gain households, and the northern marches would stay empty.
entries.literal: Taking advantage of their submission, divide their tribes and clans, relocate them to the lands of Yanzhou and Yuzhou south of the Yellow River, scatter them among prefectures and counties and have each plow and weave—a million barbarian captives can be transformed into common people; then China will have the benefit of added households, and the northern frontier can remain forever empty.

entries.zh: 唯中書令溫彥博議請準漢建武時置降匈奴於五原塞下。
entries.en: Only Director of the Secretariat Wen Yanbo urged following the Han precedent under Emperor Guangwu of settling surrendered nomads below the Wuyuan pass.
entries.literal: Only Director of the Secretariat Wen Yanbo proposed following the Han Jianwu-era precedent of settling surrendered Xiongnu south of the Wuyuan frontier pass.

entries.zh: 全其部落，得為捍蔽，又不離其土俗，因而撫之，一則實空虛之地，二則示無猜心。
entries.en: Keep their tribes whole to serve as a frontier shield, let them keep their customs, and win them by kindness—thus filling empty lands and showing that we do not distrust them.
entries.literal: Keep their tribes intact so they can serve as a defensive screen, and without departing from their native customs, thereby comfort them—first, to solidify empty lands; second, to show a heart free of suspicion.

entries.zh: 若遣向河南兗、豫，則乖物性，故非含育之道。
entries.en: To send them deep into Yanzhou and Yuzhou south of the river would violate their nature and is no way to nurture subjects.
entries.literal: If sent south to Yanzhou and Yuzhou south of the Yellow River, it would run against their nature—therefore it is not the way of nurturing and cherishing.

entries.zh: 太宗將從之。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong was on the point of accepting this plan.
entries.literal: Emperor Taizong was about to follow this.

entries.zh: 秘書監魏征奏言：「突厥自古至今，未有如斯之破敗者也，此是上天剿絕，宗廟神武。
entries.en: Director of the Palace Library Wei Zheng memorialized: "Never in their history have the Turks been broken as they are now. Heaven has cut them off; our ancestral temple's divine might has done this.
entries.literal: Director of the Palace Library Wei Zheng memorialized: "From antiquity to the present the Turks have never suffered defeat such as this; this is Heaven cutting them off—the ancestral temple's divine martial prowess.

entries.zh: 且其世寇中國，百姓冤仇，陛下以其降伏，不能誅滅，即宜遣還河北，居其故土。
entries.en: They have raided China for generations, and the people bear deep grievances. Since Your Majesty will not destroy them now that they have surrendered, you should send them back north of the river to their old lands.
entries.literal: Moreover they have raided China generation after generation; the people harbor grievances and enmity. Your Majesty, because they have submitted, cannot wipe them out—you should send them back north of the Yellow River to dwell on their old lands.

entries.zh: 匈奴人面獸心，非我族類，強必寇盜，弱則卑服，不顧恩義，其天性也。
entries.en: These nomads have human faces and beasts' hearts; they are not of our kind. Strong, they raid; weak, they cringe. Grace and duty mean nothing to them—that is their nature.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu have human faces but beasts' hearts; they are not of our kind. When strong they must raid and plunder; when weak they humbly submit. They heed neither grace nor righteousness—such is their inborn nature.

entries.zh: 秦、漢患其若是，故發猛將以擊之，收取河南，以為郡縣，陛下奈何以內地居之！
entries.en: Qin and Han were vexed by just this and sent fierce generals to drive them out, taking the Henan region and making it into commanderies and counties. How can Your Majesty settle them in the interior!
entries.literal: Qin and Han were troubled by this, therefore they sent fierce generals to attack them, took Henan and made it commanderies and counties—Your Majesty, how can you settle them in the interior!

entries.zh: 且今降者幾至十萬，數年之間，孳息百倍，居我肘腋，密邇王畿，心腹之疾，將為後患，尤不可河南處也。」
entries.en: Nearly one hundred thousand have already surrendered; in a few years they will multiply a hundredfold. Placed at our very side, hard against the capital, they will become a disease of the heart and bowels—a calamity for the future. Above all, they must not be settled south of the river."
entries.literal: Moreover those who have surrendered now number nearly one hundred thousand; within a few years they will multiply a hundredfold. Dwelling in our armpit, close to the imperial capital—a malady of the heart and vitals, which will become a future calamity. It is especially impermissible to settle them south of the Yellow River."

entries.zh: 溫彥博奏曰：「天子之於物也，天覆地載，有歸我者，則必養之。
entries.en: Wen Yanbo replied: "The Son of Heaven shelters all beneath Heaven and bears all upon Earth. Whoever comes to us, we must sustain them.
entries.literal: Wen Yanbo memorialized: "As for things, the Son of Heaven covers them like Heaven and carries them like Earth; whoever returns to us, we must nurture them.

entries.zh: 今突厥破滅之余，歸心降附，陛下不加憐湣，棄而不納，非天地之道，阻四夷之意，臣愚甚謂不可。
entries.en: These are the broken remnants of the Turks, come in good faith to submit. If Your Majesty shows no pity but casts them away, that is not the way of Heaven and Earth and will turn the four quarters against us. I think it utterly wrong.
entries.literal: Now the remnant of the destroyed Turks have turned their hearts and submitted. If Your Majesty does not show pity and compassion but abandons and rejects them, it is not the way of Heaven and Earth; it would obstruct the intent of the four barbarians. I am very foolish and deem this impossible.

entries.zh: 遣居河南，所謂死而生之，亡而存之，懷我德惠，終無叛逆。」
entries.en: Settle them south of the river—give life to the doomed and restore the lost. Grateful for our kindness, they will never rebel."
entries.literal: Sending them to dwell south of the Yellow River—this is what is called giving life to the dead and preserving the perished; cherishing our virtue and kindness, they will in the end never rebel."

entries.zh: 魏征又曰：「晉代有魏時胡落，分居近郡，平吳已後，郭欽、江統勸武帝逐出塞外；
entries.en: Wei Zheng answered again: "Under Jin there were Wei-era barbarian tribes scattered through the neighboring commanderies. After Wu was pacified, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the passes;
entries.literal: Wei Zheng again said: "In the Jin era there were barbarian tribes from Wei times, scattered among neighboring commanderies; after Wu was pacified, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the frontier passes;

entries.zh: 不用欽等言，數年之後，遂傾瀍、洛。
entries.en: he ignored them, and within a few years the capitals at Chan and Luo were overturned.
entries.literal: He did not heed the words of Qin and the others; within a few years, then Chan and Luo were overturned.

entries.zh: 前代覆車，殷鑒不遠，陛下必用彥博之言，遣居河南，所謂養獸自遺患也！」
entries.en: The wreckage of earlier dynasties lies close at hand. If Your Majesty follows Yanbo and settles them south of the river, you will be raising beasts and storing up disaster for yourself!"
entries.literal: The overturned chariots of former generations—the clear mirror is not far off. If Your Majesty must use Yanbo's words and send them to dwell south of the Yellow River, this is what is called raising beasts and bequeathing calamity oneself!"

entries.zh: 彥博又曰：「聞聖人之道，無所不通，古先哲王，有教無類。
entries.en: Yanbo replied again: "I have heard that the sage's way knows no bounds; the ancient kings taught all alike.
entries.literal: Yanbo again said: "I have heard that the way of the sages knows no obstruction; ancient sage-kings had teaching that excluded no class.

entries.zh: 突厥余魂，以命歸我，我援護之，收居內地，稟我指麾，教以禮法，數年之後，盡為農民。
entries.en: These surviving Turks have entrusted their lives to us. Let us shelter them, settle them within the realm, teach them our rites and laws, and in a few years they will all become farmers.
entries.literal: The surviving souls of the Turks, entrusting their lives to us—we receive and protect them, gather them to dwell in the interior, receive our commands, teach them rites and laws; within a few years all will become farmers.

entries.zh: 選其酋首，遣居宿衛，畏威懷德，何患之有？
entries.en: Choose their chiefs for palace guard service. Awed by our might and grateful for our kindness—what is there to fear?
entries.literal: Select their chiefs and send them to serve in the palace guard; fearing our might and cherishing our virtue—what worry could there be?

entries.zh: 光武居南單于內郡，為漢籓翰，終乎一代，不有叛逆。」
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu settled the Southern Chanyu within the interior commanderies as a bulwark for Han, and through that whole dynasty there was no rebellion."
entries.literal: Guangwu settled the Southern Chanyu in the interior commanderies as a Han frontier bulwark; through the whole dynasty there was no rebellion."

entries.zh: 彥博既口給，引類百端，太宗遂用其計，於朔方之地，自幽州至靈州置順、祐、化、長四州都督府，又分頡利之地六州，左置定襄都督府，右置雲中都督府，以統其部眾。
entries.en: Yanbo, quick of tongue, argued from every angle, and Emperor Taizong adopted his plan. In Shuofang, from Youzhou to Lingzhou, he established the four area commands of Shun, You, Hua, and Chang; Jieli's lands were divided into six prefectures, with Dingxiang Area Command on the left and Yunzhong Area Command on the right to govern the tribes.
entries.literal: Yanbo, being quick with words, cited analogies on every side; Emperor Taizong thereupon adopted his plan. In the Shuofang region, from Youzhou to Lingzhou he established the four area commands of Shun, You, Hua, and Chang; also dividing Jieli's lands into six prefectures, on the left establishing the Dingxiang Area Command, on the right the Yunzhong Area Command, to govern their tribes.

entries.zh: 其酋首至者，皆拜為將軍、中郎將等官，布列朝廷，五品以上百餘人，因而入居長安者數千家。
entries.en: Chiefs who came to court were appointed generals, lieutenant generals, and the like; more than a hundred held fifth rank or higher, and several thousand households took up residence in Chang'an.
entries.literal: The chiefs who arrived were all appointed as generals, lieutenant generals, and the like, distributed throughout the court; more than a hundred of fifth rank and above, and consequently several thousand households came to dwell in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 自結社率之反也，太宗始患之。
entries.en: After Jieshe'er's revolt, Emperor Taizong began to have misgivings.
entries.literal: From Jieshe'er's rebellion onward, Emperor Taizong began to worry.

entries.zh: 又上書者多雲處突厥於中國，殊謂非便，乃徙於河北，立右武候大將軍、化州都督、懷化郡王思摩為乙彌泥孰侯利苾可汗，賜姓李氏，率所部建牙於河北。
entries.en: Many memorials also argued that settling Turks within China was a bad idea. They were therefore moved to Hebei, and Right Bulwark General, Area Commander of Huazhou, and Prince of Huaihua Simo was installed as Yimi Nishou Kelibo Khan, given the surname Li, and ordered to lead his followers and establish his headquarters in Hebei.
entries.literal: Also many who submitted memorials said that settling the Turks in China was especially inconvenient; thereupon they were moved to Hebei. They established Right Bulwark General, Area Commander of Huazhou, Prince of Huaihua Commandery Simo as Yimi Nishou Kelibo Khan, bestowed the surname Li, and had him lead his division to establish headquarters in Hebei.

entries.zh: 突厥之始，啟民之前，《隋書》載之備矣，只以入國之事而述之。
entries.en: The early history of the Turks, down to the time before Qimin Khan, is already set forth in full in the History of the Sui; the present account confines itself to their dealings with our state after that point.
entries.literal: As for the origins of the Turks, before Qimin Khan, the History of the Sui records them fully; here we treat only the matter of their entering the realm.

entries.zh: 德宗嗣位，加太子太師、鳳翔尹，實封至三百戶。
entries.en: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Zhu Ci was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Fengxiang, and his substantive fief was increased to three hundred households.
entries.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Ci was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Fengxiang, and his substantive fief was raised to three hundred households.

entries.zh: 建中元年，涇州將劉文喜阻兵為亂，加泚四鎮北庭行軍、涇原節度使，與諸軍討之。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianzhong, Jingzhou general Liu Wenxi mutinied and rebelled. Zhu Ci was made commander of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign and military commissioner of Jingyuan, and led the allied armies against him.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Jingzhou general Liu Wenxi blocked the army and made rebellion; Ci was made commander of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign and military commissioner of Jingyuan, and with the various armies punished him.

entries.zh: 涇州平，加泚中書令，還鎮鳳翔，而以舒王讓遙領涇原節度。
entries.en: After Jingzhou was pacified, Zhu Ci was made Grand Secretariat Director and returned to garrison Fengxiang, while Prince Shu Li Rang was given nominal command of Jingyuan.
entries.literal: When Jingzhou was pacified, Ci was made Grand Secretariat Director, returned to garrison Fengxiang, and Prince Shu Li Rang was made titular military commissioner of Jingyuan.

entries.zh: 二年，加泚太尉。
entries.en: In the second year Zhu Ci was made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: In the second year Ci was made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 朱滔將反叛，陰使人與泚計議，以帛書納蠟丸中，置髮髻間。
entries.en: Zhu Tao was plotting rebellion and secretly sent a messenger to consult with Zhu Ci, concealing a silk letter inside a wax pellet hidden in the messenger's hair bun.
entries.literal: Zhu Tao was about to rebel; secretly he sent a man to consult with Ci, placing a silk letter inside a wax pellet and hiding it in his hair bun.

entries.zh: 河東節度馬燧搜獲之，以聞，並送帛書及所遣使。
entries.en: Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui seized the messenger, reported to the throne, and forwarded both the silk letter and the envoy.
entries.literal: Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui searched and seized it, reported to the throne, and sent up both the silk letter and the envoy dispatched.

entries.zh: 泚惶懼，頓首乞歸罪有司。
entries.en: Zhu Ci was terrified and prostrated himself, begging to surrender himself to the authorities for judgment.
entries.literal: Ci was fearful and in panic, bowing his head and begging to surrender himself to the authorities for punishment.

entries.zh: 上勉之曰：「千里不同謀，非卿之過。」
entries.en: The emperor reassured him: "You were a thousand li apart and did not plot together—this is not your fault."
entries.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying: "A thousand li apart, you did not plot together—this is not your fault."

entries.zh: 三年四月，以張鎰代泚為鳳翔隴右節度留後，留泚京師，加實封至一千戶，與一子正員官，其幽州盧龍節度、太尉、中書令並如故。
