entries.en: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang Yi replaced Zhu Ci as acting military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou. Zhu Ci was kept at the capital, his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and one of his sons was given a regular official post; his titles as military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Secretariat Director remained unchanged.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang Yi replaced Ci as acting military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou; Ci was kept at the capital, his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and one son was given a regular official post; his posts as military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Secretariat Director remained as before.

entries.zh: 朱泚黃巢秦宗權
entries.en: Zhu Ci, Huang Chao, and Qin Zongquan.
entries.literal: Zhu Ci, Huang Chao, and Qin Zongquan.

entries.zh: 三年四月，遣葛從周以兗、鄆、滑、魏之師伐滄州。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou with troops from Yan, Yun, Hua, and Wei against Cangzhou.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou with armies from Yan, Yun, Hua, and Wei to attack Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 五月庚寅，攻德州，拔之，梟刺史傅公和於城上。
entries.en: On gengyin in the fifth month he stormed Dezhou, took it, and exposed Prefect Fu Gonghe's head on the ramparts.
entries.literal: On gengyin in the fifth month he attacked Dezhou, captured it, and displayed the head of Prefect Fu Gonghe on the wall.

entries.zh: 己亥，進攻浮陽。
entries.en: On jihai he pressed the attack on Fuyang.
entries.literal: On jihai he advanced to attack Fuyang.

entries.zh: 六月，燕帥劉仁恭大舉來援，從周與諸將逆戰于乾寧軍老鴉堤，大破之，殺萬餘眾，俘其將佐馬慎交已下百餘人。
entries.en: In the sixth month Liu Rengong marched to relieve the city; Congzhou met him at Laoya Embankment in Qianning Army, crushed his host, killed ten thousand, and took a hundred-odd officers including Ma Shenjiao.
entries.literal: In the sixth month the Yan commander Liu Rengong came in force to relieve them; Congzhou and the generals met them in battle at Laoya Embankment in Qianning Army, routed them greatly, killed more than ten thousand, and captured over a hundred of their officers including Ma Shenjiao.

entries.zh: 既而以連雨，遂班師。
entries.en: Relentless rain then forced a withdrawal.
entries.literal: Thereafter because of continuous rain, the army withdrew.

entries.zh: 八月，河東遣李進通襲陷洺州，執刺史硃紹宗。
entries.en: In the eighth month Hedong's Li Jintong raided and took Mingzhou, capturing Prefect Zhu Shaozong.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Hedong sent Li Jintong in a surprise attack that captured Mingzhou and seized Prefect Zhu Shaozong.

entries.zh: 帝遣葛從周自鄴縣渡漳水，屯於黃龍鎮，親領中軍涉洺而寨；
entries.en: The Emperor sent Ge Congzhou from Yexian across the Zhang to Huanglong Fort while he led the center across the Ming to encamp;
entries.literal: The Emperor sent Ge Congzhou from Yexian to cross the Zhang River and encamp at Huanglong Fort; he personally led the central army across the Ming River to make camp;

entries.zh: 晉人懼而宵遁，洺州復平。
entries.en: the Jin fled overnight in panic and Mingzhou was restored.
entries.literal: the Jin forces fled by night in fear, and Mingzhou was pacified again.

entries.zh: 九月，帝以仁恭、進通之入寇也，皆由鎮、定為其囊橐，即以葛從周為上將以伐鎮州，遂攻下臨城，渡滹沱以環其城。
entries.en: In the ninth month, blaming Zhen and Ding for supplying Rengong and Jintong, he made Ge Congzhou supreme commander against Zhenzhou, took Lincheng, and crossed the Hutuo to invest the city.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, because Rengong's and Jintong's invasions had both drawn on Zhen and Ding as their storehouses, he made Ge Congzhou supreme commander to attack Zhenzhou, captured Lincheng, and crossed the Hutuo to surround the city.

entries.zh: 帝親領軍繼至，鎮帥王熔俱，納質請盟，仍獻文繒二十萬以犒戎士，帝許之。
entries.en: The Emperor followed in person; Wang Rong of Zhen sent hostages, sued for peace, and offered two hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army—the Emperor agreed.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally led the army to follow; the Zhen commander Wang Rong submitted hostages and begged alliance, and also presented two hundred thousand bolts of figured silk to reward the troops; the Emperor consented.

entries.zh: 十月，晉人以帝宿兵于趙，遂南下太行，急攻河陽，留後侯言與都將閻寶力戰固守，僅而獲全。
entries.en: In the tenth month, with the Emperor camped in Zhao, the Jin rushed south through the Taihang and hammered Heyang; Hou Yan and Yan Bao held on by sheer force and barely kept the city.
entries.literal: In the tenth month the Jin, because the Emperor was encamped in Zhao, marched south through the Taihang in haste and attacked Heyang urgently; the acting governor Hou Yan and Commander Yan Bao fought stubbornly to hold firm and barely survived intact.

entries.zh: 十一月，以張存敬為上將，自甘陵發軍，北侵幽、薊，連拔瀛、莫二郡，遂移軍以攻中山。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Zhang Cunjing marched from Ganling north into You and Ji, took Ying and Mo in turn, then turned on Zhongshan.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he made Zhang Cunjing supreme commander, launched the army from Ganling, invaded You and Ji to the north, captured Ying and Mo in succession, and then shifted the army to attack Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 定帥王郜以精甲二萬戰於懷德亭，盡殪之。
entries.en: Ding's Wang Gao met him at Huaide Pavilion with twenty thousand elite armored troops and was annihilated.
entries.literal: The Ding commander Wang Gao fought with twenty thousand picked armored troops at Huaide Pavilion; they were utterly destroyed.

entries.zh: 郜懼，奔於太原。
entries.en: Gao fled in terror to Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Gao in fear fled to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 遲明，大軍集於城下，郜季父處直持印鑰乞降，亦以繒帛三十萬為獻，帝即以處直代郜領其鎮焉。
entries.en: By dawn the army stood before the walls; Gao's uncle Wang Chuzhi came out with seal and keys to surrender and gave three hundred thousand bolts of silk—the Emperor installed Chuzhi in Gao's place.
entries.literal: At daybreak the great army gathered below the city; Gao's uncle by descent Chuzhi held out the seal and keys to beg surrender, and also presented three hundred thousand bolts of silk as tribute; the Emperor at once had Chuzhi replace Gao in command of the circuit.

entries.zh: 是月，燕人劉守光赴援中山，寨于易水之上，繼為康懷英、張存敬等所敗，斬獲甚眾。
entries.en: That month Liu Shouguang of Yan marched to save Zhongshan and camped on the Yishui; Kang Huaiying and Zhang Cunjing broke him with heavy slaughter.
entries.literal: That month the Yan man Liu Shouguang came to relieve Zhongshan and encamped above the Yishui; he was thereafter defeated by Kang Huaiying, Zhang Cunjing, and others, and very many were killed or captured.

entries.zh: 由是河朔知懼，皆弭伏焉。
entries.en: Thereafter all Hebei submitted in fear.
entries.literal: From this the Hebei region knew fear and all submitted.

entries.zh: 光化元年正月，帝遣葛從周統諸將略地于山東，遂次於邢、洺。
entries.en: In the first month of Guanghua 1 the Emperor sent Ge Congzhou to lead the generals in raiding Shandong, and they halted at Xing and Ming.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Guanghua, the Emperor sent Ge Congzhou to command the generals in raiding Shandong, and they then halted at Xing and Ming.

entries.zh: 三月，昭宗以帝兼領天平軍節度使，余如故。
entries.en: In the third month Zhaozong made the Emperor concurrent military governor of the Tianping army; his other posts were unchanged.
entries.literal: In the third month Zhaozong had the Emperor additionally hold the post of military governor of the Tianping Army; the rest remained as before.

entries.zh: 四月，滄州節度使盧廷彥為燕軍所攻，棄城奔于魏，魏人送於汴。
entries.en: In the fourth month Lu Tingyan of Cangzhou, attacked by the Yan army, abandoned his city and fled to Wei, and the Wei garrison sent him on to Bian.
entries.literal: In the fourth month Lu Tingyan, military governor of Cangzhou, was attacked by the Yan army, abandoned the city and fled to Wei; the people of Wei sent him on to Bian.

entries.zh: 是月，帝以大軍至钜鹿，屯於城下，敗晉軍萬餘眾于青山口，俘馬千餘匹。
entries.en: That month the Emperor marched to Julu, camped beneath the walls, and at Qingshan Pass routed more than ten thousand Jin troops and seized a thousand horses.
entries.literal: That month the Emperor with a great army reached Julu, encamped below the city, and at Qingshan Pass defeated more than ten thousand Jin troops, capturing more than a thousand horses.

entries.zh: 丁卯，遣從周分兵攻洺州，斬刺史邢善益，擒將五十餘人。
entries.en: On dingmao he sent Congzhou to storm Mingzhou, killed Prefect Xing Shanyi, and took more than fifty officers.
entries.literal: On dingmao he sent Congzhou with a detachment to attack Ming Prefecture, beheaded Prefect Xing Shanyi, and captured more than fifty officers.

entries.zh: 五月己巳，邢州刺史馬師素棄城遁去。
entries.en: On jisi in the fifth month Xingzhou Prefect Ma Shisu abandoned the city and fled.
entries.literal: On jisi in the fifth month Ma Shisu, prefect of Xing Prefecture, abandoned the city and fled.

entries.zh: 辛未，磁州刺史袁奉滔自剄而死。
entries.en: On xinwei Cizhou Prefect Yuan Fengtao killed himself by cutting his throat.
entries.literal: On xinwei Yuan Fengtao, prefect of Ci Prefecture, cut his own throat and died.

entries.zh: 五日之內，連下三州。
entries.en: Within five days three prefectures fell in succession.
entries.literal: Within five days three prefectures fell in succession.

entries.zh: 因以葛從周兼邢州昭義軍節度使留後，帝遂班師。
entries.en: Ge Congzhou was made acting governor of Xingzhou and the Zhaoyi army, and the Emperor withdrew.
entries.literal: Thereupon Ge Congzhou was made acting military governor of Xing Prefecture and the Zhaoyi Army, and the Emperor then withdrew the army.

entries.zh: 是時，襄州節度使趙匡凝聞帝軍有清口之敗，密附於淮夷。
entries.en: Zhao Kuangning of Xiangzhou, hearing of the Emperor's defeat at Qingkou, secretly sided with the Huai rebels.
entries.literal: At this time Zhao Kuangning, military governor of Xiang Prefecture, hearing that the Emperor's army had suffered the defeat at Qingkou, secretly attached himself to the Huai barbarians.

entries.zh: 七月，帝遣氏叔琮率師伐之。
entries.en: In the seventh month the Emperor sent Shi Shuzong against him.
entries.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor sent Shi Shuzong to lead troops to attack him.

entries.zh: 未幾，泌州刺史趙璠越墉來降；
entries.en: Soon Bi Prefect Zhao Fan climbed the wall to surrender;
entries.literal: Before long Zhao Fan, prefect of Bi Prefecture, scaled the wall to come surrender;

entries.zh: 隨州刺史趙匡琳臨陣就擒。
entries.en: and Suizhou Prefect Zhao Kuanglin was taken in battle.
entries.literal: Zhao Kuanglin, prefect of Sui Prefecture, was captured on the spot in battle.

entries.zh: 二年正月，淮南楊行密舉全吳之眾，精甲五萬，以伐徐州，帝領大軍禦之。
entries.en: In the first month of the second year Yang Xingmi of Huainan mustered all Wu with fifty thousand elite armored troops and marched on Xuzhou; the Emperor took the field in force to meet him.
entries.literal: In the first month of the second year, Yang Xingmi of Huainan raised all the forces of Wu—fifty thousand picked armored men—to attack Xuzhou; the Emperor led a great army to resist him.

entries.zh: 行密聞帝親征，乃收軍而退。
entries.en: Hearing the Emperor had come in person, Xingmi pulled his army back.
entries.literal: When Xingmi heard the Emperor was campaigning in person, he withdrew his army.

entries.zh: 時幽州節度使劉仁恭大舉蕃漢兵號十萬以伐魏，遂攻陷貝州，州民萬餘戶，無少長悉屠之。
entries.en: Liu Rengong of Youzhou then raised a mixed tribal and Han host said to number one hundred thousand against Wei, took Beizhou, and slaughtered every soul among its ten thousand-odd households.
entries.literal: At that time Liu Rengong, military governor of Youzhou, raised a great force of tribal and Han troops numbering one hundred thousand to attack Wei, captured Beizhou, and of more than ten thousand households in the prefecture, none young or old was spared slaughter.

entries.zh: 進攻魏州，魏人來乞師，帝遣硃友倫、張存敬、李思安等先屯于內黃，帝遂親征。
entries.en: When Wei sought help against the siege, the Emperor sent Zhu Youlun, Zhang Cunjing, and Li Si'an ahead to Neihuang and followed in person.
entries.literal: Advancing to attack Weizhou, the people of Wei came to beg for aid; the Emperor sent Zhu Youlun, Zhang Cunjing, Li Si'an, and others to encamp first at Neihuang, then the Emperor himself campaigned.

entries.zh: 三月，與燕軍戰于內黃北，燕軍大敗，殺二萬餘眾，奪馬二千餘匹，擒都將單無敵已下七十餘人。
entries.en: In the third month he routed the Yan army north of Neihuang, killing twenty thousand, seizing two thousand horses, and capturing seventy-odd officers down to the famed commander Dan Wudi.
entries.literal: In the third month he fought the Yan army north of Neihuang; the Yan army was greatly defeated—more than twenty thousand killed, over two thousand horses captured, and more than seventy commanders from Commander Dan Wudi down were taken.

entries.zh: 《通鑒》：單可及，幽州驍將，號單無敵。
entries.en: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 notes that Dan Keji was a Youzhou champion known as Dan Wudi—"Peerless Dan."
entries.literal: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: Dan Keji was a fierce general of Youzhou, styled Dan Wudi ("Peerless Dan").

entries.zh: 是月，葛從周自山東領其部眾，馳以救魏。
entries.en: That same month Ge Congzhou raced from Shandong with his division to relieve Wei.
entries.literal: That month Ge Congzhou led his troops from Shandong at forced march to relieve Wei.

entries.zh: 翼日，乘勝，諸將張存敬以下連破八寨，遂逐燕軍，北至於臨清，壅其殘寇於御河，溺死者甚眾。
entries.en: The next day, riding the victory, Zhang Cunjing and the other generals stormed eight camps in a row, drove the Yan army to Linqing, and drowned masses of fugitives in the Imperial Canal.
entries.literal: The next day, pressing the victory, the generals from Zhang Cunjing downward broke eight camps in succession, pursued the Yan army north to Linqing, blocked the remnant bandits in the Imperial Canal, and very many drowned.

entries.zh: 仁恭奔於滄州。
entries.en: Rengong fled to Cangzhou.
entries.literal: Rengong fled to Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 六月，帝表丁會為潞州節度使，以李罕之疾亟故也。
entries.en: In the sixth month the Emperor recommended Ding Hui as governor of Luzhou, Li Hanzhi being gravely ill.
entries.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor memorialized to appoint Ding Hui military governor of Luzhou, because Li Hanzhi's illness was acute.

entries.zh: 又遣葛從周由固鎮路入於潞州，以援丁會。
entries.en: He also sent Ge Congzhou through Guzhen into Luzhou to reinforce Ding Hui.
entries.literal: He also sent Ge Congzhou by the Guzhen route into Luzhou to reinforce Ding Hui.

entries.zh: 七月壬辰朔，海州陳漢賓擁所部三千奔於淮南。
entries.en: On rengchen, the first of the seventh month, Haizhou's Chen Hanbin defected south with three thousand men.
entries.literal: On the first day of the seventh month (rengchen), Chen Hanbin of Haizhou led his three thousand troops in flight to Huainan.

entries.zh: 戊戌，晉人陷澤州。
entries.en: On wuxu the Jin took Zezhou.
entries.literal: On wuxu the Jin forces captured Zezhou.

entries.zh: 帝遣召葛從周於潞，留賀德倫以守之。
entries.en: The Emperor recalled Ge Congzhou from Luzhou and left He Delun to hold the city.
entries.literal: The Emperor summoned Ge Congzhou back from Luzhou and left He Delun to defend it.

entries.zh: 未幾，德倫為晉人所逼，遂棄潞而歸，由是潞州復為晉人所有。
entries.en: Soon pressed by the Jin, Delun abandoned Luzhou; the prefecture was Jin's again.
entries.literal: Before long Delun was pressed by the Jin forces, abandoned Luzhou and returned, and thus Luzhou again fell to the Jin.

entries.zh: 十一月，陝州都將硃簡殺留後李璠，自稱留後，送款於帝。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Shanzhou commander Zhu Jian killed acting governor Li Fan, seized the post, and submitted to the Emperor.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month Zhu Jian, garrison commander of Shanzhou, killed the acting governor Li Fan, declared himself acting governor, and submitted allegiance to the Emperor.

entries.zh: 四月，唐帝御劄敕宰臣張文蔚等備法駕奉迎梁朝。
entries.en: In the fourth month the Tang emperor sent an imperial decree ordering Zhang Wenwei and the other chief ministers to ready the imperial escort to receive the Liang.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, the Tang emperor issued an imperial decree commanding Zhang Wenwei and other chief ministers to prepare the imperial carriage to welcome the Liang court.

entries.zh: 宋州刺史王皋進赤烏一雙。
entries.en: Wang Gao, prefect of Songzhou, offered a pair of crimson crows.
entries.literal: Wang Gao, prefect of Songzhou, presented a pair of red crows.

entries.zh: 又，宰臣張文蔚正押傳國寶、玉冊、金寶及文武群官、諸司儀仗法物及金吾左右二軍離鄭州。
entries.en: Chief minister Zhang Wenwei meanwhile led the imperial seal, jade books, gold regalia, the full civil and military establishment, ceremonial equipage of every bureau, and the Left and Right Jinwu guards out of Zhengzhou.
entries.literal: Also, chief minister Zhang Wenwei personally escorted the dynastic seal, jade registers, gold seals, civil and military officials of all ranks, ritual regalia of every office, and the Left and Right Jinwu Armies as they departed Zhengzhou.

entries.zh: 丙辰，達上源驛。
entries.en: On bingchen they arrived at Shangyuan Post.
entries.literal: On bingchen they reached Shangyuan Post.

entries.zh: 是日，慶雲見。
entries.en: That day auspicious clouds were seen.
entries.literal: That day, auspicious clouds appeared.

entries.zh: 令曰：「王者創業興邦，立名傳世，必難知而示訓，從易避以便人。
entries.en: An edict declared: "Founders of dynasties who wish their names to endure must turn what is obscure into instruction and choose what is easy for the people to observe.
entries.literal: An edict said: "When kings found states and establish names to pass down through generations, they must turn what is hard to know into instruction and choose easy names for taboo avoidance so as to convenience the people.

entries.zh: 〈案：此下有闕文。〉
entries.en: 〈Note: Text is missing here.〉
entries.literal: 〈Note: Text is missing here.〉

entries.zh: 或稽其符命，應彼開基之義，垂諸象德之言。
entries.en: Some consult portents that match the moment of founding, or phrases that embody the virtue of their emblem.
entries.literal: Or they examine mandate tokens and respond to the meaning of founding a base, leaving words that embody symbolic virtue.

entries.zh: 爰考簡書，求於往代，周王昌、發之號，漢帝詢、衍之文，或從一德以徽稱，或為二名而更易。
entries.en: Looking to the records of old: Zhou's Kings Chang and Fa, Han's Emperors Xun and Yan—some took one virtue as a style, others changed names because they bore two characters.
entries.literal: Examining brief histories and seeking examples from past ages—the styles of King Chang and King Fa of Zhou, the inscriptions of Emperors Xun and Yan of Han—some took a single virtue as their emblem, others changed because they had two personal names.

entries.zh: 先王令典，布在縑緗。
entries.en: The precedents of former kings stand written in the classics.
entries.literal: The former kings' ordinances are set down in silk books.

entries.zh: 寡人本名，兼於二字，且異帝王之號，仍兼易之難，郡職縣官，多須改換。
entries.en: My birth name has two characters, unlike an emperor's style, and would be awkward to taboo—countless prefectural and county posts would need revision.
entries.literal: My original name combines two characters, differs from imperial styles, and still entails the difficulty of change—prefectural, circuit, and county offices would mostly need renaming.

entries.zh: 況宗廟不遷之業，憲章百世之規，事葉典儀，豈憚革易。
entries.en: Yet the ancestral rites and laws meant to last generations demand it—how could I refuse what ritual requires?
entries.literal: Moreover the enterprise of an undisturbed ancestral temple and institutions meant to last a hundred generations accord with canonical rites—how could one shrink from change?
